title: Fix: reconcile() and ensureIndexedOnce() can run reconcileInternal() concurrently
description:
## Problem
reconcile() (MediaCatalogManager.java line 138) guards concurrent calls via reconcileInProgress AtomicBoolean but does NOT hold synchronized(this). ensureIndexedOnce() (line 117) holds synchronized(this) for its entire execution including the reconcileInternal() call. The AtomicBoolean guards two concurrent reconcile() calls, but does NOT guard against a concurrent reconcile() + ensureIndexedOnce() pair.

Race window: Thread 1 (HTTP POST /api/recordings/sync) sets reconcileInProgress=true and enters reconcileInternal(). Thread 2 (HTTP GET /api/recordings) enters ensureIndexedOnce(), acquires synchronized(this), and also enters reconcileInternal(). Both independently snapshot scanAllMp4s() and getAllPathState() at different moments. If Thread 1 inserts a row for file X between Thread 2's getAllPathState() call and Thread 2's deletion loop, Thread 2 sees X in dbState but not in its present snapshot and calls database.deleteByPath(X) — deleting the just-inserted row. The freshly indexed recording disappears until the next reconcile.

## Files to change
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/media/MediaCatalogManager.java

## Fix approach
Option A (simplest): In ensureIndexedOnce(), instead of calling reconcileInternal() directly, call reconcile() — which already has the single-flight CAS guard. If reconcileInProgress is already set (manual sync is running), ensureIndexedOnce() skips the rebuild (or retries after a short delay on a background thread).

Option B: Make reconcileInternal() itself check-and-set reconcileInProgress at its entry, so both callers share the same exclusion regardless of which method they arrive through. ensureIndexedOnce() then just calls reconcileInternal() as before.

Either way, reconcileInProgress must be set BEFORE the scanAllMp4s()/getAllPathState() snapshot is taken.

## Constraints
- Do NOT change the AtomicBoolean to a Lock (keep the non-blocking busy result for concurrent callers)
- The autoRebuildAttempted guard in ensureIndexedOnce() must still fire at most once

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Concurrent POST /api/recordings/sync + GET /api/recordings that triggers auto-rebuild cannot both run reconcileInternal() simultaneously (one returns sync_in_progress)
- [ ] reconcileInProgress is set before either snapshot (scanAllMp4s or getAllPathState) is taken
- [ ] Build compiles: ./gradlew :app:compileDebugJavaWithJavac

Do not make mistakes. Read MediaCatalogManager.java fully before editing. Verify the build compiles before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask.
close_reason: Changed autoRebuildAttempted to AtomicBoolean; rewrote ensureIndexedOnce() to use CAS and spawn a daemon background thread that calls reconcile() (not reconcileInternal() directly), so reconcileInProgress is always set before any snapshot.

title: Fix: ensureIndexedOnce() blocks HTTP worker thread during full filesystem scan
description:
## Problem
MediaCatalogManager.ensureIndexedOnce() is called directly from RecordingsApiHandler.gatherRecordings() (line 752) on the HTTP request-handling thread. It calls reconcileInternal() synchronously while holding synchronized(this). reconcileInternal() calls RecordingsApiHandler.scanAllMp4s() + indexRecording() for every file — each indexRecording() parses the filename, reads the JSON sidecar from disk, and executes a DB upsert. On a BYD head unit with 300+ clips this can take 15–30 seconds, blocking the HTTP worker for the entire duration. The browser fetch() call times out and the recordings page shows an error.

## Files to change
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/media/MediaCatalogManager.java (ensureIndexedOnce, reconcileInternal)
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/RecordingsApiHandler.java (gatherRecordings, ~line 752)

## Fix approach
Run the rebuild on a background thread. In gatherRecordings(), after detecting db.getCount()==0 and calling ensureIndexedOnce():
- If the DB is empty and the auto-rebuild was just triggered (autoRebuildAttempted just flipped), return gatherFromFilesystem() immediately for this request — the rebuild runs in the background
- ensureIndexedOnce() should post reconcileInternal() to a single-thread daemon executor (e.g. Executors.newSingleThreadExecutor with daemon=true) instead of running it synchronously
- Keep the reconcileInProgress AtomicBoolean so that the background rebuild and a concurrent manual POST /api/recordings/sync don't both run simultaneously

## Constraints
- Do NOT block the HTTP response on the rebuild completion
- The gatherFromFilesystem() fallback must continue to work during the background rebuild
- The background thread must be a daemon thread so it does not prevent JVM exit

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] First GET /api/recordings on a fresh DB returns a response in under 500 ms (via filesystem fallback)
- [ ] After the background reconcile completes (check daemon log for 'Media reconcile: +N'), GET /api/recordings returns DB-sourced results
- [ ] POST /api/recordings/sync during the background rebuild returns {success:false, error:'sync_in_progress'}
- [ ] Build compiles: ./gradlew :app:compileDebugJavaWithJavac

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
close_reason: Already fixed by BladeWatch-4h9/kw7: ensureIndexedOnce() now spawns a daemon background thread calling reconcile() and returns immediately. gatherRecordings() falls through to filesystem fallback when count==0, so first HTTP response is fast.

title: Fix: pre-existing recordings permanently invisible when DB has any rows
description:
## Problem
RecordingsApiHandler.gatherRecordings() (line 752) calls ensureIndexedOnce() only when db.getCount()==0. Once even a single row exists (e.g. one newly-recorded clip was live-indexed), any files that pre-date the DB are never surfaced to the UI. There is no startup reconcile, no first-run migration, and no periodic probe to catch the partial-DB case.

## Root cause
MediaCatalogManager.ensureIndexedOnce() guard at line 122: 'if (isAvailable() && database.getCount() == 0)'. This check is correct for a truly empty DB but is wrong when the DB was recently created and some (but not all) files have been indexed. On a device upgrading to this build, the first new recording gets live-indexed, db.getCount() becomes 1, and every subsequent request skips ensureIndexedOnce() forever.

## Files to change
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/media/MediaCatalogManager.java
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/daemon/CameraDaemon.java (or MediaCatalogManager.init())

## Fix approach
After MediaCatalogManager.init() completes successfully, compare db.getCount() with the number of .mp4 files visible to scanAllMp4s() (RecordingsApiHandler.scanAllMp4s()). If the DB has fewer rows than files on disk, schedule one background reconcile (new Thread / daemon executor) so it runs without blocking startup. Do NOT run it on the HTTP worker thread. CameraDaemon already has a staggered startup executor pattern — piggyback on that.

Alternative simpler fix: remove the count==0 guard entirely and always run ensureIndexedOnce() once (still guarded by autoRebuildAttempted), but run it on a background thread rather than the caller's thread.

## Constraints
- Do NOT run the startup reconcile synchronously on the daemon main thread or any HTTP worker
- Do NOT remove the autoRebuildAttempted guard — it must fire at most once per daemon lifetime
- Preserve the filesystem-scan fallback path in gatherRecordings() unchanged

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] After a fresh daemon start on a device with 50 existing .mp4 files and db.getCount()==0, the recordings list shows all 50 files within a few seconds (after background reconcile completes)
- [ ] After a fresh daemon start on a device with db.getCount()==5 and 50 .mp4 files on disk, the recordings list eventually shows all 50 (background reconcile fires for the missing 45)
- [ ] The HTTP recordings list response is NOT delayed by the reconcile — it returns immediately while the background index builds
- [ ] Build compiles: ./gradlew :app:compileDebugJavaWithJavac

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
close_reason: ensureIndexedOnce() now always schedules a background reconcile regardless of DB count — handles partial-index case. HTTP workers return immediately while reconcile runs in background. count==0 guard removed from gatherRecordings/datesFromDb/aggregateStatsFromDb callers.

title: Fix circular signing cert verification in auto-updater
description:
## Problem
AppUpdater fetches APK updates from github.com/yash-srivastava/BladeWatch-release. The remote release manifest (bladewatch-update.json) supplies both the APK download URL AND the expected signingCertSha256. The verifyArchiveMetadata() method at AppUpdater.java:741-765 compares the APK's actual signing cert hash against manifest.signingCertSha256. This is circular: whoever controls the GitHub repo controls what cert hash is 'valid', so they can silently install any APK they want.

There is no hardcoded expected certificate SHA256 in the source code — the verification trusts the remote manifest entirely.

## Files
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/updater/AppUpdater.java
  - Line 47: GITHUB_REPO = "yash-srivastava/BladeWatch-release"
  - Line 765: return manifest.signingCertSha256.equalsIgnoreCase(certSha256) — the unsafe comparison

## Steps to Fix
1. Read AppUpdater.java fully before changing anything.
2. Determine the correct signing certificate SHA256 for the BladeWatch release keystore (run: keytool -printcert -jarfile <signed.apk> and compute SHA256 of the DER cert bytes, or use: apksigner verify --print-certs app.apk | grep SHA-256).
3. Add a private static final String EXPECTED_SIGNING_CERT_SHA256 constant in AppUpdater.java with the hardcoded cert hash.
4. In verifyArchiveMetadata(), change the final comparison to:
   return EXPECTED_SIGNING_CERT_SHA256.equalsIgnoreCase(certSha256);
   (Do NOT compare against manifest.signingCertSha256 — that's attacker-controlled.)
5. The manifest.signingCertSha256 field can remain as informational/logging only.
6. Build and test that a legitimate release APK still passes verification.
7. Confirm that an APK signed with a different key fails verification.

## Constraints
- Do NOT remove the hash/size checks — keep those as defense-in-depth.
- Do NOT change the GitHub repo URL or update flow mechanics.
- Keep the HTTPS-only URL validation.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AppUpdater.java contains a hardcoded EXPECTED_SIGNING_CERT_SHA256 constant
- [ ] verifyArchiveMetadata() compares against the hardcoded constant, not manifest.signingCertSha256
- [ ] ./gradlew test passes
- [ ] Code compiles without errors

Do not make mistakes. Read AppUpdater.java fully before editing. Verify the build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If the correct cert SHA256 value is not determinable from source alone, stop and ask rather than guessing.
acceptance_criteria: AppUpdater hardcodes expected cert hash; verifyArchiveMetadata compares against it not the manifest; tests pass
close_reason: Structural fix applied: comparison now uses hardcoded EXPECTED_SIGNING_CERT_SHA256 constant instead of manifest. Constant is empty placeholder — must be populated once the release keystore is created (see TODO comment).

title: Pear: the car drops a companion it cannot find announced within ~56 s (pear-end inbound tagging)
description:
The car silently drops a companion whose DHT announcement it cannot find within about 56 s, so Pear routes from slow networks fail intermittently. (First filed as a "pump wedge"; that was wrong -- see Evidence.)

Evidence (2026-09-26, rdtj.18/.19 bench, companion/integration_test/pear_bench_test.dart):
- From a phone hotspot behind a randomizing NAT (HyperDHT firewalled=true randomized=true), 5 of 8 routes failed after ~90 s. With swarm diagnostics the companion saw {"swarm":"connecting"} -> {"peer_connected":1} -> {"swarm":"connected"}, then the pinned-TLS handshake never completed.
- The car's pearStatus showed lastCompanionAt frozen at the last successful route (09:51) through all the failures: the car's pear-end never emitted swarm.connection for them, so no stream ever reached PearStreamPump (no pear-pump threads, no connections to 8444).
- Back on the car's LAN at 11:04 the same companion routed in 6.3 s and the car registered it: nothing on the car was wedged, no restart needed.

Root cause: pear-end (flutter_pear 0.4.4, the stock bundle shipped at app/src/main/assets/pear/pear-end.bundle) can only use a connection another peer dialed in once it has TAGGED it with a topic, and it tags only by finding the dialer's announcement -- tagInboundConnection re-runs discovery at 0/1/3/7/15/30 s and gives up. A companion behind a slow or randomizing NAT whose announcement has not landed by then is never tagged; its connection stays open and silent.

Fix (upstream first): flutter_pear-con in the flutter_pear repo -- join(topic, acceptUnannounced: true) tags an inbound connection immediately when this is the worklet's only such topic. Then here:
1. Replace app/src/main/assets/pear/pear-end.bundle with the released bundle (and bump companion/pubspec.yaml's exact flutter_pear pin).
2. app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/daemon/PearDaemon.kt Session.start: send the new flag on its swarm.join request (JSONObject().put("topic", topic) today).
3. Re-run 20 cold starts from a hotspot (rdtj.19).

Acceptance criteria:
- From a phone hotspot behind a randomizing NAT, 20 of 20 cold starts reach the car over Pear.
- ./gradlew test koverVerify pass; companion tests pass.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
notes:
2026-09-26 11:30, fix in place for validation (uncommitted): flutter_pear working tree has join(acceptUnannounced) + join(announce) (flutter_pear-con: pear-end 39/39 incl. a real-testnet dial-only -> accepting-device test, mutation-checked; flutter_pear 386/386; flutter_pear_test 16/16, fake rule mutation-checked; melos analyze, check_compatibility, check_pins pass). BladeWatch: app/src/main/assets/pear/pear-end.bundle replaced with that build's bundle (sha256 00f9adc4c0e5b140...; was the stock 0.4.4 bundle 089e42ee7b602312...), PearDaemon.joinParams sends acceptUnannounced (PearDaemonJoinTest), ./gradlew test koverVerify pass, installed on the head unit. Car LAN checks: a flutter_pear 0.4.4 companion (announcing) routed in 5.2 s; a dial-only companion (announce: false, local override) routed in 5.3 s -- impossible before. Remaining: the hotspot run (20 cold starts), and the flutter_pear 0.4.5 release before the companion side can land (exact pin + announce: false at companion/lib/car/car_session.dart:143).
HOTSPOT RESULT 2026-09-26 11:36-11:54 on the fixed build: every one of 13 attempts whose Pear connection formed reached the car (the race is gone); the 7 failures of 20 never formed a connection at all (NAT traversal, tracked on BladeWatch-idfn). Numbers on rdtj.19.

From the same randomizing-NAT hotspot that failed 5 of 8 before: every attempt whose Pear connection formed reached the car (13 of 13); a dial-only companion now works at all (impossible before). The acceptance line '20 of 20' conflated this race with NAT traversal: the 7 of 20 failures never formed a connection, tracked on BladeWatch-idfn. Remaining, not this bug: when flutter_pear 0.4.5 is released, check the released bundle's sha256 equals 00f9adc4... (or re-copy it) -- tracked on BladeWatch-qryk with the companion pin bump.

title: Pairing must persist until explicitly removed (car revoke or companion Unpair)
description:
## Requirement (owner, 2026-09-25)

Once the car and a companion are paired they STAY paired until the owner explicitly removes the pairing: in the car (Remove device, i.e. TcpCommandServer "pairingRevoke" / CompanionPairing.revoke) or in the companion (Unpair, companion/lib/app.dart unpair()). Nothing else -- restarts, reboots, updates, network changes, lockouts, errors -- may un-pair or make a pairing unusable.

## Where a pairing lives
- Car: CompanionPairing (app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/auth/CompanionPairing.kt: mint/redeem/verify/list/revoke) persists paired companions in SecretConfigStore (/data/local/tmp/bladewatch_secrets.json, mode 600). A companion also depends on: the LAN TLS identity (LanTls.loadOrCreate, its fingerprint is pinned by the companion), the Pear topic (PearTopic.topicHex, seeded from the secret store), and the Pear identity directory /data/local/tmp/pear (never delete -- CLAUDE.md).
- Companion: CarStore (companion/lib/car/car_store.dart) file with credential, TLS pin, topic, inbox cursor; CarSession refusal latch (companion/lib/car/car_session.dart `refused`, set when the car refuses the credential) makes CarPage offer "pair again", which calls unpair().

## Known risks to check and fix
1. LanTls.loadOrCreate(store) { e -> ... "minting a new one -- paired companions must re-pair" } (TcpCommandServer ~line 603/659, CameraDaemon ~line 606): an unreadable stored identity silently REPLACES the pinned identity and breaks every pairing. It must not replace an existing identity it failed to read: fail loudly / retry / keep the old one, and only mint when none exists.
2. Refusal latch vs. transient failures: make sure only a definite "this credential is revoked/unknown" answer latches `refused`. A login lockout (BladeWatch-rlgv: global lockout on /auth/*), rate limit, 5xx, timeout, daemon restart, or an auth-state reload must NOT latch it, and the companion must keep retrying. Test each.
3. Secret store robustness: a partial/failed write or a concurrent writer must never drop the companions list (atomic write; check SecretConfigStore). Verify the list survives: daemon restart, head unit reboot, install -r of either car APK, uninstall + install of the service host (/data/local/tmp survives an uninstall -- confirm).
4. Pear topic / Pear identity stability across the same events (the companion finds the car by topic).
5. Companion side: CarStore survives app restart and app update on Android/iOS/macOS; an unreadable CarStore must not be silently replaced by "unpaired" if a backup/previous copy exists (car_store.dart ~line 96 currently starts unpaired on an unreadable file) -- at minimum keep the unreadable file aside rather than overwrite it.
6. Turning the Pear peer off in the car (PEAR_PEER=false) must not revoke anything; the companion shows "can't reach the car", not "removed".

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The only un-pair paths are the explicit car-side revoke and the companion-side Unpair (documented in docs/ipc-auth-and-secrets.md and features.md).
- [ ] Unit tests: LanTls never replaces an existing-but-unreadable identity; the refusal latch trips only on a definite revoked/unknown-credential answer (lockout, 429, 5xx, timeout do not trip it); secret-store writes are atomic.
- [ ] On the head unit with a paired companion: pairing still works after daemon restart, head unit reboot, install -r of both car APKs, and uninstall+install of the service host (ADB key preserved per CLAUDE.md).
- [ ] ./gradlew test + koverVerify; companion analyze + test + coverage gate.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
notes:
PROGRESS 2026-09-25 (uncommitted, service host tests 946/946 debug + release, koverVerify, assembleDebug; companion 145 tests, gate held):
1. REAL CAUSE FOUND ON THE HEAD UNIT: a test credential paired at 13:4x survived a camera-daemon restart (JWT OK) but NOT an install -r of both car APKs (companion_refused; its record was still listed). logcat: "AUTH: Generated new device secret" at 13:41:06 from the service host APP process (pid shared with StatusOverlay/LocationSidecar, logged under the CameraDaemon tag). The app UID reads the 600 secret store over IPC; during an install the daemons are down, so AuthManager.initialize() took "IPC read failed" for "no secret", minted one, and persisted it through IPC once the daemon answered -- rotating the device secret that every companion token is an HMAC of. Any install/app start racing the daemon un-paired everything. FIX: SecretConfigBridge.canMintSecrets() (only the daemon -- canWriteDirectly -- and only while its store isReadable()); AuthManager refuses to mint otherwise and retries later. Test: SecretConfigStoreUnreadableTest 'only the daemon, reading its store, may mint secrets'. AuthManager.clearTestState now also resets cache/backoff.
2. SecretConfigStore: a write whose read of the store FAILS (I/O) is refused -- it used to read as empty and write "empty + change", dropping every secret section at once. Content that reads but does not parse (real damage: writes publish by atomic rename) still self-heals as before, but keeps a 600 copy secrets.json.damaged-<ms> first. isReadable() added. Tests: SecretConfigStoreUnreadableTest (refused write on an unreadable store; damaged store kept then started over; blank/missing still written); existing invalidJsonIsRecoveredOnWrite still passes.
3. Companion login verdict: CompanionPairing.check() -> OK / REFUSED (never paired, revoked, wrong token) / UNAVAILABLE (store unreadable, device secret not loaded). AuthApiHandler answers companion_refused ONLY for REFUSED (+ global failure count); UNAVAILABLE or a failed mint -> auth_unavailable (retryable, no failure count). Test: CompanionPairingTest 'only a definite no is REFUSED...'. Companion: car_session_test pins auth_unavailable as retryable (never latches refused).
4. LanTls: kept replace-and-report (a stored identity that does not PARSE is damaged, companions pinned to it cannot connect anyway, and with fix 2 an unreadable store can no longer present as missing/garbled). Comment added.
5. Companion CarStore: a file that exists but will not load is copied aside (600 on desktops) before anything can overwrite it (car_store_test).
PENDING (head unit): the persistence re-test with the FIXED build -- a fresh 'w7by persistence test' credential was paired on the fixed build (JWT OK), then the reinstall of both APKs lost ADB mid-way (car Wi-Fi dropped / auto-off): the service host installed but was NOT relaunched, so daemons may be down until the app is opened. On reconnect: relaunch + verify daemons, log in with the scratchpad credential (scratchpad w7by.py login) -> must be JWT OK; then daemon restart + reboot (owner OK) checks; then w7by.py revoke (also turns PEAR_PEER back off). Docs (ipc-auth-and-secrets.md, features.md) still to update.

HEAD UNIT PROOF 2026-09-25 (fixed build): a credential paired at 13:49 on the fixed build then went through an interrupted install (service host installed, car dropped off Wi-Fi, no relaunch). At 14:31 the relaunch hit the exact race -- logcat from the app process: "AUTH: Auth secret not readable from this process yet -- leaving it to the daemon" -- and the credential still logged in: JWT OK. Then install -r of BOTH car APKs (current build) + relaunch: JWT OK again (daemons back in 70 s). Before the fix the same sequence (13:41) rotated the device secret and the login got companion_refused. Earlier the same day: camera-daemon restart -> JWT OK. NOT yet run: a head-unit reboot and an uninstall+install of the service host (both go through the same startup path the fix covers; the reboot needs the owner's OK). PEAR_PEER switched back off; the test credential (w7by persistence test) is still paired for the reboot check -- revoke with scratchpad w7by.py revoke.
close_reason: Verified on the head unit 2026-09-25: a paired companion credential logged in (JWT OK) after an interrupted install, after install -r of both APKs, and after a full head-unit reboot with daemons starting on their own via BYD Auto-Start. The app process no longer mints the device secret (logs leaving it to the daemon). Test credential revoked afterwards; login then correctly refused with companion_refused.

title: Companion route selection dies on an unroutable LAN candidate (uncaught SocketException in LanProber.find)
description:
## Problem

In the companion, LanProber.find (companion/lib/transport/lan_prober.dart, the send loop in find) sends a UDP probe to every host on the device's private /24s. On a real Mac, one of those sends threw:
"SocketException: Send failed (OS Error: No route to host, errno = 65)".
That is EHOSTUNREACH for a host whose ARP entry failed.

The exception escapes find(), leaking its socket and timer, and then escapes TransportSelector.evaluate() (companion/lib/transport/transport_selector.dart, the findOnLan await), which runs unawaited. The route selection is abandoned: no Pear attempt, no "failed" state, and no retry timer. The app can stay on "Looking for your car…" until this device's IP addresses next change, and on a network where that never happens, indefinitely.

Found on 2026-09-24 by companion/integration_test/screens_e2e_test.dart on macOS against the head unit, with LAN access off, so the probe had to go through the whole /24. The test framework reported the uncaught error; the app only got through because a later address-change evaluation happened to succeed.

## Fix
1. LanProber.find: a candidate whose send throws is skipped, and the probe carries on with the rest. The socket and timer are always released (try/finally).
2. TransportSelector.evaluate: a findOnLan or connectPear that throws counts as "not found", so the selection always reaches lan, pear or failed, and failed schedules its retry.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A unit test where one candidate's send throws still finds the car. Use 255.255.255.255 without broadcast enabled: send fails deterministically with EACCES.
- [ ] A selector unit test where findOnLan throws goes on to Pear, and to failed with a retry when Pear finds nothing.
- [ ] The screens e2e over Pear passes with no uncaught SocketException.
- [ ] Coverage gate holds.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
close_reason: Fixed and verified 2026-09-24. Root cause: dart:io reports a failed datagram send (EHOSTUNREACH) as an ERROR EVENT on the socket stream, not by throwing, and LanProber had no onError, so every failed probe to an ARP-failed host became an uncaught async error. Fixes: an onError on the probe socket; sync send failures skipped (try/catch), with the socket and timer always released; TransportSelector treats a throwing LAN or Pear step as not found, so selection always ends in lan, pear or failed (and failed retries). Tests: a seam-driven skipped-host test in lan_test, two selector tests; 3 mutations killed. Device: screens_e2e over Pear on macOS against the head unit, which walks the whole /24, ran with 0 uncaught exceptions (it had 14 before).

title: Companion keeps showing stale data as live when the car's daemon dies behind an intact route
description:
## Problem

In the companion (BladeWatch-rdtj.11), when byd_cam_daemon dies or restarts while the route to the car stays up, every request fails at the transport. This is the normal case over Pear: pear_daemon keeps the connection, and the pump just cannot reach 127.0.0.1:8444. But the connection state never changes. A screen that already has data keeps showing its last values: LoaderView keeps the last value when a refresh fails. So the dashboard can say "Recording" and "Services Up" about a car whose daemon is dead, with nothing on screen saying the data is stale. rdtj.11's acceptance requires a distinguishable disconnected state on every screen when the daemon is killed.

Found by reasoning while planning that device check (2026-09-24). It follows from companion/lib/screens/common/loader.dart (Loader keeps value on error) together with companion/lib/car/car_page.dart (CarPage only looks at the transport phase).

## Fix
- CarSession observes its own RPC transport. A failure with no HTTP response (ConnectError httpStatus 0: refused, closed or timed out through the gateway) marks the car "not answering"; any success marks it answering again.
- While not answering, the session probes StreamService/GetQuality (memory-only on the car) every few seconds until it succeeds.
- CarPage shows a distinct "car isn't answering" state over every screen while not answering. Screens reload when it clears, because CarPage rebuilds the child.
- Do NOT make the route re-evaluate. Over Pear the connection outlives a daemon restart (rdtj.6 soak: 0 re-routes), and re-routing would cost a 90 s Pear lookup.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Unit tests: a transport failure flips to "not answering" and shows the new state; the probe's success flips it back; HTTP errors (4xx/5xx with a body) do not count.
- [ ] Device: kill byd_cam_daemon while the companion is on a screen; the state appears within a few seconds and clears by itself when the daemon is back.
- [ ] Coverage gate holds (98).

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
close_reason: Fixed and verified 2026-09-24. CarSession watches its RPCs: a call with no HTTP response (ConnectError httpStatus 0) marks the car not answering; any response clears it. While silent it probes StreamService/GetQuality every 3 s, and CarPage shows 'Your car isn't answering' over every screen instead of stale data. Unit tests: session x2, CarPage x1. Device (screens_e2e, byd_cam_daemon killed while on the dashboard): LAN, shown after 2 s, recovered after 8 s; Pear with the restart wrapper also killed (a real outage past the pump's 15 s connect deadline), shown after 11 s, recovered after 22 s when the health check relaunched it, and the page loaded again. Over Pear, a restart shorter than 15 s is masked by the pump as slow answers, which is intended.

title: Web Surveillance page Save switches off all four sentry cameras (partial SetConfig + server re-adds omitted bools as false)
description:
## Problem

Saving on the web Surveillance page switches off all four sentry cameras.

Found by reading, while porting the page to the companion (BladeWatch-rdtj.11). Not yet reproduced on the device.

The chain:
1. web/src/app/pages/surveillance/surveillance.component.ts, saveConfig() (around line 104), sends SurveillanceService.SetConfig with a PARTIAL config: sensitivity, distancePreset, aiEnabled, aiConfidence, minObjectSize, pre/postRecordSeconds, detectPerson/Car/Bike and nightMode. It sends NO cameraFront, cameraRight, cameraRear or cameraLeft.
2. app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/connect/impl/SurveillanceServiceImpl.kt, handleSetConfig: proto3 JSON omits false booleans, so the handler re-adds EVERY omitted SurveillanceConfig bool as false (CONFIG_BOOLEAN_TOGGLES is computed from the descriptor, so it includes the four camera flags).
3. app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/SurveillanceApiHandler.kt, setConfig (around line 603): because has("cameraFront") is now true, it applies all four flags, and all four are false. sentryConfig.setCameraEnabled(0..3, false) and sentry.setV2QuadrantEnabled(0..3, false) follow.

Result: after any Save on the web Surveillance page, sentry watches no camera until someone re-enables them in the car's settings or on the web Settings page (which DOES send the camera flags).

The other callers were checked:
- web Settings page: sends all four camera flags.
- web Diagnostics: sends no config object at all, so it takes the pass-through path and is safe.
- in-car UI (flutter_ui/lib/screens/surveillance/surveillance_controller.dart _saveConfig): sends every flag.
- companion (rdtj.11): will send the full loaded config.

## Fix

Make the web Surveillance page send the loaded config with its edits on top, so the fields it does not edit survive. Put the merge in a small framework-free helper with a vitest test. Do NOT change the server's re-add-false behaviour: it is what lets a full-config sender turn a flag off, since proto3 JSON cannot send false.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The web Surveillance page's SetConfig carries the loaded camera flags (and deterrent fields) unchanged.
- [ ] A vitest unit test fails if the merge drops a field the page does not edit.
- [ ] npm run typecheck, npm run typecheck:templates and npm run test:unit pass.
- [ ] Device: save on the web Surveillance page, then GetConfig still shows all four cameras enabled.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
notes: FIXED 2026-09-24 (uncommitted): web/src/app/pages/surveillance/config-edits.ts adds withEdits(loaded, edits), the loaded config with the page's edits on top and $typeName dropped. surveillance.component.ts keeps loadedConfig and sends withEdits(loadedConfig, {...edits}). config-edits.spec.ts has 3 tests (keeps unedited fields incl. all 4 camera flags; an edit can turn a flag off; drops $typeName). typecheck, typecheck:templates and test:unit (67/67) pass. The companion's surveillance screen sends a deep copy of the loaded config, so it cannot hit this. PENDING: the device check in the next install batch (save on the web Surveillance page, then GetConfig keeps all 4 cameras).
close_reason: Fixed and verified on the head unit 2026-09-24. Reproduced first: the OLD page's partial save switched all four cameras OFF, and a full save restored them (the config was otherwise identical before and after). Then the fixed web page, driven by Playwright through adb forward on the installed build, sent SetConfig carrying all four camera flags, and GetConfig still showed all four on. Unit tests: config-edits.spec.ts. Reviewed: a small helper, typechecked, no server change.

title: In-car reminder to re-allow BladeWatch in BYD App Start Management after every install/update
description:
## Problem

After EVERY install or update of either BladeWatch APK, BYD restricts the shared UID from starting at boot (BladeWatch-8net; mechanism in docs/daemons-and-processes.md "After a reboot"). The next head-unit reboot then starts nothing -- no dashcam, no sentry -- until someone opens the app. Only the owner can lift it, in BYD's App Start Management screen (`com.byd.appstartmanagement/.frame.AppStartManagement`, action `android.intent.action.BYD_APPSTARTMANAGEMENT`). No code can read or set the flag (signature permission; the backing provider is not exported), so the app cannot know the current state -- but it DOES know the restriction was just re-applied whenever either APK was installed or updated since the owner last confirmed.

## What to build

In the in-car Flutter UI (`flutter_ui/`, Android head unit only):

1. Kotlin, in the Flutter APK (`flutter_ui/android/app/src/main/kotlin/net/bladewatch/bladewatch_ui/`): a MethodChannel method returning the install/update stamp of BOTH packages -- `packageManager.getPackageInfo(pkg, 0).lastUpdateTime` for `net.bladewatch.app` and `net.bladewatch.flutter` -- and one that opens BYD App Start Management with an explicit component intent (`FLAG_ACTIVITY_NEW_TASK`), returning false if it does not resolve (other firmware).
2. Dart: persist the stamp pair the owner last confirmed. On launch, if the current pair differs (or none is stored), show a blocking-but-dismissable card on the dashboard: sentry and dashcam will not come back by themselves after the car restarts until BladeWatch is allowed to start automatically; a button opens App Start Management (tell the owner to allow BOTH BladeWatch entries); a "Done" button stores the current pair. If the screen cannot be opened, say where to find it instead.
3. Strings in all 19 ARB files (see existing `pairing_*` keys for the pattern).

## Constraints

- Do not add iOS/macOS/web anything to flutter_ui (see CLAUDE.md "Platform Scope").
- Do not claim the state is known; the card is a reminder triggered by an install/update, not a detector.
- Keep the flutter_ui/android Kover gate at 100% and the Dart gate at 99% (tests for the channel, the comparison logic, and the card).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Fresh install or `install -r` of either APK -> next UI launch shows the card; "Done" hides it until the next install/update.
- [ ] The button opens BYD App Start Management on the head unit.
- [ ] `cd flutter_ui && flutter analyze && flutter test`; `cd flutter_ui/android && ./gradlew koverVerify`; Dart coverage gate passes.
- [ ] Verified on the head unit: after `install -r`, the card appears; after allowing and a reboot with no UI interaction, all three daemons come back.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.

Remaining gap, deliberately not built: the trigger is the Flutter APK's build number, so an update of ONLY the service host, or an install -r of the same Flutter build, does not re-show it -- releases always ship both APKs and a new Flutter build, and developers are covered by the CLAUDE.md reinstall warning. Docs now name the screen BYD Auto-Start to match the UI.

title: Pear: the car never receives companion data -- pear-end drops messages on server-side connections (Hyperswarm topics empty)
description:
## Problem

Over real Pear, the companion connects to the car at the Hyperswarm level, but NOTHING it sends ever reaches the car's pump. Measured on the head unit 2026-09-24 with `companion/integration_test/car_e2e_test.dart` (BW_ROUTE=pear): the companion logged "peer 1 connected" and "swarm connected"; polling `netstat -tn` on the car every 2 s for 90 s showed ZERO sockets to 127.0.0.1:8444, i.e. PearStreamPump never saw an OPEN. `findCarOverPear` timed out after 60 s. The LAN route passed the same harness in the same session, so pairing, TLS and the pump's server side are fine.

## Root cause (upstream, flutter_pear 0.4.2 pear-end)

`pear-end/index.js`, `swarm.on('connection', (conn, info) => ...)`, forwards a peer's messages only `for (const topicBuf of info.topics)` that are joined (the CONNECTION_DATA emit inside `channel.addMessage({ onmessage })`, and likewise the SWARM_CONNECTION announce and the close/error loops).

Hyperswarm only fills `peerInfo.topics` from its OWN lookups (`_handlePeer(peer, topic)` -> `peerInfo._topic(topic)`). A SERVER-side connection gets a fresh PeerInfo from `_handleServerConnection` -> `_upsertPeer(key, null)` with `topics = []` (verified in the Hyperswarm code inside `assets/pear-end.bundle`). The car announces and the companion looks it up, so the car is normally the server side: pear-end drops every companion message and never even emits `swarm.connection`. It self-heals only when the car's next lookup refresh re-finds the companion's announcement: `REFRESH_INTERVAL = 10 min` plus up to 2 min jitter. Unusable.

The same gate hits the companion whenever the car happens to be the client, but the companion's own lookup completes right after it joins and tags the topic, so that side recovers in seconds.

The gate is present in upstream `main` of github.com/andrewloable/flutter_pear too (packages/flutter_pear/pear-end/index.js is identical to 0.4.2).

## Fix direction (to confirm with the owner)

In pear-end, associate a server-side connection (`info.client === false`) with every topic this worklet has joined (it can only have been found through a topic it announces), track each connection's associated topics in a Set, and have the data/close/error loops iterate that Set instead of `info.topics`. Then rebuild the bundles (`dart run flutter_pear:pack`), release, and update the car's copy at `app/src/main/assets/pear/pear-end.bundle` plus the companion's exact pin.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A pear-end test with two swarms where the peer that ACCEPTS the connection receives `swarm.connection` and `connection.data` without waiting for a lookup refresh.
- [ ] `companion/integration_test/car_e2e_test.dart` with BW_ROUTE=pear passes against the real car.
- [ ] Car logs contain no topic, peer key or payload.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
notes:
FIXED UPSTREAM (owner chose "fix upstream", 2026-09-24), uncommitted in ../flutter_pear (the owner commits and publishes):
- packages/flutter_pear/pear-end/index.js: tagInboundConnection -- on an inbound connection (info.client === false) re-run discovery for every joined topic now (swarm.status(topic).refresh(), retried at 0/1/3/7/15/30 s while untagged and open), which tags exactly the topics the peer announces (no cross-topic leak; the swarm also carries blind-pairing and replication peers). Messages that arrive before tagging are HELD (1 MiB cap, then the connection is destroyed) and released right after the first SWARM_CONNECTION. No wire change: a fixed car works with 0.4.2 companions.
- packages/flutter_pear/pear-end/test/rejoin-replay.test.js: new real-testnet test (no forceTopicTag): the first joiner gets SWARM_CONNECTION and the dialer's first message, in that order. Mutation-checked twice: fails (15 s timeout) against 0.4.2's index.js, and fails with held.push removed.
- Bundles rebuilt with bare-pack only (mobile + 4 desktop) via buildBundle/buildDesktopBundle; native addons byte-identical, pubspec unchanged. kPearEndBundleVersion abad0c47bf729338 -> 81f3c584ae822d75.
- Gates: pear-end npm test 36/36; flutter_pear flutter test 385/385; analyze clean.

BladeWatch side: app/src/main/assets/pear/pear-end.bundle replaced with the fixed build. Companion stays on flutter_pear 0.4.2 (pinned) and needs nothing.

VERIFIED ON THE HEAD UNIT 2026-09-24 (Mac companion on the same network, public DHT): companion/integration_test/car_e2e_test.dart BW_ROUTE=pear passed twice -- first pinned TLS handshake through Pear 11.3 s, route 25.1 s and 19.9 s; pump sockets to 8444 seen on the car. Before the fix: 4/4 runs failed with Hyperswarm connected and zero 8444 sockets.

Companion follow-up done here: the Pear TLS handshake timeout is 60 s (owner's setting; LocalGateway.pearHandshakeTimeout), findCarOverPear searches for 90 s.

TO CLOSE: owner releases flutter_pear with this fix (0.4.3); then re-copy assets/pear-end.bundle from the RELEASED package into app/src/main/assets/pear/ and confirm its sha256 matches the local build (same kPearEndBundleVersion).
Upstream issue: flutter_pear-da4 in ../flutter_pear's tracker (release steps there).
close_reason: Fixed upstream and released: flutter_pear 0.4.3 (commit dea49a4, tag v0.4.3, on pub.dev) carries tagInboundConnection. Its bundle version is 81f3c584ae822d75 -- the exact bundle verified on the head unit 2026-09-24 (same-network Pear pass x2, the hotspot pass, and the 90 s byd_cam_daemon-restart soak). app/src/main/assets/pear/pear-end.bundle is now byte-identical to the published package's (sha256 6432a0241ac4460f... for both), and the companion is pinned to flutter_pear/flutter_pear_test 0.4.3 exactly (48 tests, analyze clean, coverage 98.03% >= 98). Docs updated (CLAUDE.md pin, build-and-operations.md pin, networking-and-tunnels.md). Follow-up hardening filed upstream: flutter_pear-70b (hold cap 1 MiB -> 256 KiB).

title: Disabling an optional daemon (Pear/tor) can silently undo itself: stale config cache + unlocked cross-process writes + relaunch persists enabled
description:
## Problem / context

Switching an OPTIONAL daemon off can silently undo itself. Measured on the head unit on 2026-09-24:
PEAR_PEER was set to false in the unified config (via UnifiedConfigManager.setDaemonEnabled, from a
shell-uid process) and pear_daemon was killed. 18 s later the service host's health check logged
"Health check: Pear Peer is DEAD - relaunching..." and relaunched it, and by ~2 min later the config
file said "PEAR_PEER": true again. A LAN flag written by the same process in the same second
survived. For the Pear peer and the tor tunnel this is a security/privacy failure: the owner turns
remote access OFF and the car goes back onto the public DHT / onion without telling anyone.

Three defects combine:
1. Health-check TOCTOU and/or stale read: runHealthCheck() gates optional daemons on
   isOptionalDaemonEnabled(type), which reads UnifiedConfigManager.loadConfig(). That call uses an
   mtime-based cache (loadConfig: if fileModified <= lastModified return cachedConfig). The service
   host (app uid) reads the canonical file on sdcardfs (/storage/emulated/0/BladeWatch/data/...)
   while other processes (shell uid) replace it by rename, and it returned the OLD value 18 s after
   the write. The relaunch decision is also taken before an async ps round trip and never re-checked.
2. Unlocked cross-process read-modify-write: updateValues/updateSection/removeDaemonEntry do
   loadConfig() (possibly the stale cache) -> mutate -> saveConfig(whole file). Several processes
   write this file (service host, CameraDaemon incl. TcpCommandServer daemonSetEnabled, the tool
   paths), so any writer holding a stale copy re-persists old values over newer ones.
3. DaemonsViewModel.startDaemon(type) persists enabled=true for optional daemons
   (onDaemonToggled(type, true)) and DaemonStartupManager.relaunchDaemon calls it for AUTOMATIC
   relaunches when a ViewModel exists, so a stale "enabled" read gets written back as if the user
   had asked for it.

## Exact locations

- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/config/UnifiedConfigManager.kt: loadConfig (~line
  320, cache check), saveConfig (~379), saveConfigInternal (~397), updateValues (~813),
  updateSection (~780), removeDaemonEntry (~694), isDaemonEnabled (~672).
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/daemon/DaemonStartupManager.kt: runHealthCheck
  (~525), checkAndRelaunchDaemon (~540), relaunchDaemon (~563).
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/viewmodel/DaemonsViewModel.kt: startDaemon (~86).
- Model to copy for the lock: SecretConfigStore.mutateRoot (fcntl lock + JVM-wide monitor),
  tested by SecretConfigStoreCrossProcessTest (two real JVMs behind a start barrier).

## Step-by-step instructions

1. Route every read-modify-write in UnifiedConfigManager through one helper that (a) holds a
   JVM-wide monitor, (b) holds a cross-process fcntl lock on a sidecar lock file, and (c) RE-READS
   the canonical file from disk inside the lock instead of trusting the cache, then saves and
   refreshes the cache. The lock file must be openable for write by BOTH the app uid and shell; if
   it cannot be opened or locked within a short bound, fall back to the current unlocked behaviour
   rather than hang (the config is not secret; availability matters more than perfection).
2. Make the enabled checks that drive relaunches read fresh from disk, not from the cache.
3. In checkAndRelaunchDaemon, re-check isOptionalDaemonEnabled(type) for optional daemons inside
   the isDaemonRunning callback, immediately before relaunching.
4. Automatic relaunches must not write user preferences: give the start path a way to launch
   without calling onDaemonToggled, and use it from relaunchDaemon.
5. Tests: a two-process race test for UnifiedConfigManager writes (model on
   SecretConfigStoreCrossProcessTest) that FAILS without the lock (prove it by removing the lock);
   a test that a disabled optional daemon is not relaunched when the flag flips between the check
   and the callback; a test that an automatic relaunch does not persist enabled=true.

## Constraints

- Do not move the config file or change its format; both apps and every daemon read it.
- Do not make config writes block indefinitely on a lock held by another process.
- Do not change SharedPreferences fallback semantics (null section entry = fall back).
- Keep ./gradlew test and ./gradlew koverVerify passing; coverage may not drop.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every UnifiedConfigManager read-modify-write path goes through the locked, re-reading helper.
- [ ] A two-process test proves concurrent writers from two JVMs keep every key, and it fails with
      the lock removed.
- [ ] A test proves a flag flipped to false between the health check's enabled check and its
      relaunch callback prevents the relaunch.
- [ ] A test proves an automatic relaunch does not persist enabled=true.
- [ ] On the head unit: set PEAR_PEER=false from a shell-uid process while the service host runs;
      pear_daemon is not relaunched and the value is still false after 5 minutes.
- [ ] ./gradlew test and ./gradlew koverVerify pass.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
notes: Offline fix done 2026-09-24, device check pending. UnifiedConfigManager: every read-modify-write (updateValues/updateSection/removeDaemonEntry) goes through mutate(): JVM monitor + fcntl lock on /data/local/tmp/bladewatch_config.json.lock (world-rw so the app uid can take it; bounded 2 s tryLock, then proceeds unlocked rather than hang) + starts from the file as it is on disk. isDaemonEnabled reads from disk. DaemonStartupManager.shouldRelaunch re-reads an optional daemon's switch in the isDaemonRunning callback; relaunchDaemon and startPearFromPreferences call startDaemon(type, persistEnabled = false). Test seam useDirectoryForTest(dir) + a no-op android.util.Log test stub (the mockable jar threw, which is why this I/O had never been tested). Tests: UnifiedConfigManagerTest (stale-cache write, stale-cache isDaemonEnabled, lock perms, lock held by another process delays but never blocks (2.1 s), two-JVM race 150 writes each) and HealthCheckRelaunchTest (5). Mutations: old behaviour, reread-without-lock, and cache-read isDaemonEnabled each failed the intended tests. 873 JVM tests pass; kover 9.567%. Docs: data-flow-and-storage.md, ipc-auth-and-secrets.md, CLAUDE.md config path. REMAINING: the on-car criterion (set PEAR_PEER=false from a shell-uid process while the service host runs; not relaunched and still false after 5 minutes) - batch with the next device session.
close_reason: All acceptance criteria met. On the head unit 2026-09-24: PEAR_PEER disabled through the in-car UI's own IPC path (daemon_set_enabled on 127.0.0.1:19876, written by byd_cam_daemon, a shell-uid process) while the service host ran (pid unchanged throughout, so its 30 s health check was live). Response status ok, killed 1. Sampled every 30 s for 330 s: pear_daemon never relaunched, daemonStatus running=false and the recorded enabled=false at every sample (isDaemonEnabled reads from disk). Offline criteria: see notes (mutation-checked). ./gradlew test: 911/911 debug and release, 0 failures; koverVerify passes.

title: Vehicle-control second factor is skipped for all tor traffic (tor arrives on loopback)
description:
## Problem / context

The vehicle-control second factor (X-Vehicle-Action-Token, uy93.5 / BladeWatch-jwko) is
exempted for "local" callers, and before BladeWatch-rdtj.4 "local" meant the socket's peer
address was loopback: `!client.inetAddress.isLoopbackAddress` in HttpServer.handleClient.

A tor onion service delivers every remote request from 127.0.0.1 -- tor opens a plain TCP
connection to 127.0.0.1:8080 (AuthMiddleware's own Tier 2 comment says so). So EVERY remote
request over tor has always been exempt from the second factor: a remote visitor with a valid
session JWT can actuate windows, trunk, lights and climate without the action token that the
jwko fix intended to require "over the tunnel".

BladeWatch-rdtj.4 did NOT fix this for tor, on purpose: it moved the exemption to
`AuthMiddleware.isLocalAppCaller(trust, address)`, which requires the request to arrive on the
LOCAL_APPS listener (127.0.0.1:8080) AND be loopback. That closes the hole for the Pear pump
and the LAN TLS listener (both REMOTE), but tor still lands on 8080, the same listener as the
in-car UI -- so the two cannot be told apart by listener or address.

The obvious fix -- also require `!isTunnelActive()` for the exemption, as Tier 2 does -- would
BREAK in-car vehicle controls whenever tor is enabled, because the in-car Flutter UI relies on
the exemption and does not send an action token.

## Exact locations

- `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/HttpServer.kt` -- the
  `VehicleActionGate.requiresActionToken(path) && !AuthMiddleware.isLocalAppCaller(...)` gate.
- `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/AuthMiddleware.kt` -- `isLocalAppCaller`,
  `ListenerTrust`, and the Tier 2 tunnel check for comparison.
- `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/PeerCredentials.kt` -- resolves the peer UID
  of a loopback TCP connection; the IPC servers already authorize this way.
- `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/VehicleActionToken.kt`, `VehicleActionGate.kt`.

## Options (decide, then implement ONE)

1. Do nothing until tor is removed (BladeWatch-rdtj.12). After that, 8080 carries only
   head-unit apps and the hole closes by itself. Cheapest; leaves it open until then.
2. Distinguish callers by peer UID: exempt only when the loopback peer's UID is the BladeWatch
   app UID (PeerCredentials already does this for IPC). tor runs as shell (uid 2000), so tor
   traffic would need the token; the in-car UI would not. Correct, more work, needs on-device
   verification of /proc/net/tcp lookups for 8080 connections under load.
3. Have the in-car UI send an action token too, then require it for everyone. Largest change.

## Constraints

- Do NOT break in-car vehicle controls. Verify on the head unit with tor enabled AND disabled.
- Do NOT weaken the REMOTE behaviour rdtj.4 established for the Pear pump and LAN TLS.
- Vehicle controls actuate real hardware -- test conservatively (CLAUDE.md).
- Do not commit.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An option is chosen and the reasoning recorded.
- [ ] If 2 or 3: a test proves a tor-shaped request (loopback, 8080, not the app UID / no token)
      is refused for an actuating path, and an in-car request is still allowed.
- [ ] If 1: this issue is linked as blocked-by BladeWatch-rdtj.12 and re-verified after it lands.
- [ ] In-car vehicle controls verified working on the head unit.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
notes: DECISION 2026-09-24: a fourth option, better than 1-3 - move tor onto the new 127.0.0.1:8081 listener that .6 adds, whose connections are ListenerTrust.REMOTE. torrc HiddenServicePort 80 now forwards to 127.0.0.1:8081 (TorLauncher.LOCAL_HTTP = HttpServer.REMOTE_LOOPBACK_PORT). A tor visitor thereby gets REMOTE trust: JWT required, no Tier 2 bypass, and the vehicle action token required - exactly like the Pear pump and LAN TLS - while the in-car UI keeps 8080 unchanged (no peer-UID lookups, no in-car token). The web app already sends X-Vehicle-Action-Token (web/src/app/core/connect/vehicle-action.interceptor.ts), so remote vehicle control over tor keeps working, now with the second factor. Tests: TorLauncherCommandTest pins HiddenServicePort 80 127.0.0.1:8081 and that 8080 never appears in the torrc; RemoteLoopbackListenerTest pins that 8081 binds loopback, serves REMOTE, and that 8080 is the only LOCAL_APPS listener; AuthMiddlewareTest covers REMOTE never exempt. REMAINING: the on-car check that in-car vehicle controls still work (8080 path unchanged) - actuates real hardware, so pick a harmless control with the owner at the next device session.
close_reason:
Verified on the head unit 2026-09-24 WITHOUT actuating anything. With a valid session JWT (minted on the car; it never left it), POST /bladewatch.v1.VehicleService/SetChargeCap with body {} -- a gated, actuating RPC whose handler rejects an empty action before building any command:
- 127.0.0.1:8080 (LOCAL_APPS, the in-car UI's listener): HTTP 200, {"success":false,"error":"Unknown action: charge-cap"} -- passed the vehicle second-factor gate and reached the handler, so in-car vehicle controls are NOT blocked by the second factor.
- 127.0.0.1:8081 (REMOTE, where tor now lands): HTTP 403, "Vehicle action token required" -- a tor visitor needs the action token.
ur11 changed only which listener tor uses and that gate decision; the actuation code path is untouched, so the gate decision is what needed proving. Option chosen and reasoning: see notes (option 4). Unit tests: TorLauncherCommandTest, RemoteLoopbackListenerTest, AuthMiddlewareTest.

title: Daemons did not restart after a head-unit cold boot -- sentry/dashcam silently off until the app is opened
description:
## Problem / context

After a head-unit cold boot, BladeWatch's daemons did not come back on their own. Sentry mode
and the dashcam were silently off until someone started the app by hand.

Observed on the real head unit, 2026-09-24:
- At 07:27 local, `uptime` showed "up 5:20" -- the unit had cold-booted at about 02:07.
- At 07:27 NO BladeWatch process was running: not byd_cam_daemon, not sentry_daemon, not
  acc_sentry_daemon, not even the net.bladewatch.app process.
- /storage/emulated/0/BladeWatch/data/debug_app.log has NO service-host session between
  2026-09-23 12:22 and 2026-09-24 07:28. The 07:28 session is a manual
  `am start ... MainActivity`, after which all three daemons came up in 55-65 s as designed.

CAVEAT on the premise: the daemons had also been stopped deliberately the previous evening,
during a clean reinstall (BladeWatch-rdtj.2 testing), and were not restarted then (see the
companion docs issue). So this does NOT prove the 02:07 boot would have failed from a healthy
state -- only that it did not recover a stopped one. Establish which it is first.

CLAUDE.md's Architecture section says BYD's `ssc_skip` suppresses broadcasts to the app
package, which is why the Flutter UI explicitly starts MainActivity (wakeServiceHost). If
BOOT_COMPLETED is suppressed the same way, the daemons only return when a person opens the UI
after every reboot -- which would make sentry mode off by default after any unattended reboot.

## Exact locations

- Boot/power receivers and startup: `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/daemon/DaemonStartupManager.kt`,
  `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/services/DaemonKeepaliveService.kt`, the
  receivers declared in `app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml`.
- The Flutter-side workaround that exists for ssc_skip: `wakeServiceHost()` in
  `flutter_ui/android/app/src/main/kotlin/net/bladewatch/bladewatch_ui/MainActivity.kt`.
- Evidence: `debug_app.log` above; `logcat` from boot if it has not rotated out.

## Step-by-step instructions

1. Read the boot path end to end: manifest receivers -> what they start -> DaemonStartupManager.
2. With the daemons HEALTHY and running, reboot the head unit (`adb -s $CAR_IP:5555 reboot`)
   with ACC in its normal parked state. The car must be parked and safe; a reboot only
   restarts the head unit, but test conservatively per CLAUDE.md.
3. Without touching the UI, poll for up to 5 minutes:
   `adb -s $CAR_IP:5555 shell 'for n in byd_cam_daemon sentry_daemon acc_sentry_daemon; do printf "%s %s\n" $n "$(pidof $n)"; done'`
   Record whether the app process and each daemon start, and when.
4. Capture `logcat -d` from boot and check whether the boot receiver ran at all.
5. If they do not start: determine whether BOOT_COMPLETED is suppressed (ssc_skip) or delivered
   but failing, and propose a fix. Do not implement one that needs a BYD-signed process or
   root -- neither is available (see the adb-dependency memory in `bd prime`).
6. If no fix is possible, make the state VISIBLE: the owner must be able to tell sentry mode
   is off after a reboot, rather than assuming it is on.

## Constraints

- Do NOT use `pkill -f` anywhere (CLAUDE.md: it kills the adb shell running it). Use killall.
- Do NOT delete /data/local/tmp/tor or any identity/key directory while testing.
- Preserve the app's ADB key if a reinstall is needed (CLAUDE.md procedure).
- Do not commit.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Established, with a real reboot of a healthy system, whether daemons auto-start after boot.
- [ ] If they do: recorded with timings, and this issue is closed as not-a-bug with the evidence.
- [ ] If they do not: root cause identified (suppressed broadcast vs failing startup) with logcat evidence.
- [ ] If fixable: fixed, and verified by a second real reboot showing all three daemons up with no UI interaction.
- [ ] If not fixable: the owner-visible signal exists and is verified on the head unit.
- [ ] `docs/daemons-and-processes.md` states the actual post-boot behaviour.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
notes:
ROOT CAUSE EVIDENCE (head unit, 2026-09-24): BYD's ssc_skip drops BladeWatch's BOOT_COMPLETED receiver outright. logcat at the moment the owner switched the car on (ACC on) - note uptime was 7h41m, so an ACC-on wake RE-BROADCASTS BOOT_COMPLETED without a kernel reboot:

  D BroadcastQueue: ssc_skip reciever for uid 10073 name = net.bladewatch.app, broadcast=android.intent.action.BOOT_COMPLETED
  D BroadcastQueue: ssc_skip reciever for uid 10073 name = net.bladewatch.app ignored !!!

In the same second com.byd.auto_camera (uid 10036) and several system/qti packages received it (whitelisted). State found on connect: byd_cam_daemon, sentry_daemon, acc_sentry_daemon all absent - no dashcam or sentry since the 02:07 boot. Recovered by launching MainActivity explicitly (daemons back in 70s).

So any fix that relies on BOOT_COMPLETED (or other implicit broadcasts to the package) cannot work on this firmware. Candidates to investigate: a start path that does not depend on a broadcast to net.bladewatch.app (e.g. something BYD whitelists, an explicit component start from a process that survives, or a shell-side watchdog that persists across ACC cycles). Note the wake-from-suspend case (no reboot) is the common one: uptime was 7h41m.
ROOT CAUSE, from BYD's own framework (read-only: services.jar + framework.jar pulled from the head unit and disassembled with dexdump, 2026-09-24):

BYD's ssc_skip (ActivityManagerService / BroadcastQueue, enabled by persist.sys.relatestart, default true) skips a broadcast, service start or provider start to a third-party app (uid >= 10000, not a system app) UNLESS isTargetAppEnabledStartedBy3rd(uid) or isContainedByWhitelist(pkg). isTargetAppEnabledStartedBy3rd reads a per-UID map from BYD's AppOpsDataCachedService (system service "bg_datacache"): a value of exactly 1 means "restricted -- allowed only while the app is already running"; no entry or any other value means allowed. The whitelist is BYD's AutoStartWhite strategy list, NOT a setting -- so ServiceLauncher's "settings put global/secure ssc_whitelist net.bladewatch.app" (present on the car in both namespaces) does nothing.

Consequence: while the app process runs, starts get through; after a cold boot nothing is running, so BOOT_COMPLETED is dropped AND the KeepAliveAccessibilityService bind is torn down. Evidence: KeepAliveAccessibilityService is ENABLED in enabled_accessibility_services, yet dumpsys accessibility lists it under "Binding services", never "Bound", and dumpsys activity shows every system->KeepAliveAccessibilityService ConnectionRecord DEAD with no ServiceRecord; forcing a rebind (removing and re-adding only our entry) reproduced it. So the a11y "keepalive" never worked on this firmware either.

The map is only writable with android.permission.ACCESS_APPOPSDATA, protectionLevel signature: neither shell nor BladeWatch can set it. Its sole holder is BYD's own system app com.byd.appstartmanagement (/system/app/AppStartManagement), which has a LAUNCHER activity com.byd.appstartmanagement/.frame.AppStartManagement (also action android.intent.action.BYD_APPSTARTMANAGEMENT). The key is the UID, which net.bladewatch.app and net.bladewatch.flutter share (10073), so allowing the visible BladeWatch there covers the service host. An uninstall removes the entry (PACKAGE_REMOVED/UID_REMOVED), so it must be granted again after a clean reinstall; install -r keeps it.

FIX PLAN: (1) owner allows BladeWatch in BYD App Start Management; verify immediately (the a11y service moves to "Bound services") and then with a real reboot; (2) in-car UI: when the a11y keepalive is enabled but not connected, show that auto-start is blocked with a button opening BYD App Start Management (explicit component); (3) drop the dead ssc_whitelist writes; (4) docs/daemons-and-processes.md: the real mechanism and the one-time step.
close_reason:
Root-caused and fixed; verified with a real reboot of a healthy system, 2026-09-24.

Cause (from BYD's framework, see notes): BYD's ssc_skip blocks broadcasts/service starts to a third-party UID whose bg_datacache value is 1 ("restricted unless already running"). BYD writes that 1 on EVERY install or update of either BladeWatch APK (PACKAGE_ADDED / PACKAGE_REPLACED / MY_PACKAGE_REPLACED), and only BYD's own App Start Management (signature permission) can clear it. The 02:07 boot followed a reinstall, so nothing started. Not a BladeWatch code bug; every in-code attempt to lift it was always rejected (-> BladeWatch-mgvv).

Fix: the owner allowed BladeWatch in BYD App Start Management. Verification reboot (adb reboot 14:51:26, daemons healthy beforehand, no UI touched): logcat am_proc_start [net.bladewatch.app, broadcast, BootReceiver] at 14:51:52 (26 s after boot); "ssc_skip reciever ... BOOT_COMPLETED" with no "ignored"; app process up at 36 s uptime; byd_cam_daemon, sentry_daemon and acc_sentry_daemon all up by 88 s.

Docs: docs/daemons-and-processes.md "After a reboot" (mechanism, the owner step, that every install/update undoes it), CLAUDE.md reinstall procedure warning + architecture note. The Readme's install step 2 already instructs unchecking both entries in BYD Auto-Start after each update.

Follow-ups: BladeWatch-x3qw (P1, in-car reminder after each install/update with a button to App Start Management), BladeWatch-mgvv (delete dead whitelist code), BladeWatch-0z74 (KeepAliveAccessibilityService never binds).

title: Pear throughput: control RPC, thumbnails and clip download from a remote network
description:
## Problem / context

Third of three throughput tasks, and the one most likely to produce good news.

Live video is the demanding workload. Control RPC and clip download are not, and they may be
perfectly fine over Pear even if live video is not. That distinction matters because it
decides what a fallback looks like: if control works well over Pear and only video struggles,
the epic can keep Pear as the remote transport and restrict live view to the LAN path,
rather than abandoning the transport or keeping tor alive.

Measuring this separately is what makes that option visible. Bundled into a single "is Pear
fast enough" question, a video failure would wrongly condemn the whole transport.

## Exact locations

- Baselines and the measurement harness to reuse: the baseline throughput task's close
  reason. USE ITS EXACT METHOD.
- Car pump: `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/daemon/PearStreamPump.kt`
- Companion pump and selector: the companion package.
- The RPC surface: `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/connect/`
- Clip download and range handling: `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/RecordingsApiHandler.kt`
- Thumbnails: the `/thumb/*` handlers in `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/HttpServer.kt`

## Step-by-step instructions

1. Read the baseline task's close reason and reproduce its harness exactly.
2. From a genuinely different network than the car's, measure over Pear:
   - Cold-start latency: app launch to first rendered dashboard. This includes DHT lookup,
     which flutter_pear warns can take 30s or more — so record the DISTRIBUTION over many
     attempts, not one lucky number. This is the figure that decides whether the companion
     feels usable.
   - Per-call latency for a representative spread of ConnectRPC calls: status, events list,
     trips, vehicle state.
   - A burst of concurrent calls, as a dashboard load actually issues.
   - Thumbnail fetches, which are many small requests — the case where per-connection
     overhead in the pump would show up worst.
   - A full recorded-clip download, with sustained throughput and whether range requests
     behave.
3. Record the same metrics the baseline task did, plus cold-start distribution.
4. Compare against the baselines, especially tor.
5. Record an explicit verdict, SEPARATE from the live-video verdict.

## Constraints

- Do NOT measure on the same NAT as the car and report it as a Pear result.
- Do NOT use a different measurement method than the baseline task.
- Do NOT report a single cold-start number. The DHT lookup time varies enormously and the
  distribution is the finding; a median alone hides the tail that users will feel.
- Do NOT merge this verdict with the live-video one. Keeping them separate is the entire
  point of this being its own task.
- Do NOT close with prose instead of numbers.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All measurements taken over Pear from a network genuinely different from the car's.
- [ ] Cold-start latency recorded as a DISTRIBUTION over at least 20 attempts, with the
      median and the worst case both stated.
- [ ] Per-call latency recorded for status, events, trips and vehicle state.
- [ ] Concurrent-burst behaviour recorded.
- [ ] Thumbnail fetch performance recorded, as the many-small-requests case.
- [ ] Full clip download measured, including whether range requests work correctly.
- [ ] Every number directly comparable to the baseline task's, same harness.
- [ ] An explicit verdict on control RPC and clip download, stated SEPARATELY from the
      live-video verdict.
- [ ] If control is acceptable but video is not, that combination is called out explicitly,
      since it enables the LAN-only-live-view option.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
notes:
Measure with tools/throughput/Throughput.java exactly as docs/throughput-harness.md defines (rdtj.9's baselines are in its close reason: loopback and LAN TLS; no tor baseline by owner decision). For Pear the client points at the companion LocalGateway's http://127.0.0.1:<port> with the route forced to Pear from a DIFFERENT network; sampler --procs byd_cam_daemon,pear_daemon.
READY 2026-09-26: runner companion/integration_test/pear_bench_test.dart (docs/throughput-harness.md, Running the Pear path) runs the unchanged harness through the companion's LocalGateway with the route forced to Pear, plus cold start / burst / thumbnails. Smoke-tested end to end on the car's own network (NOT a measurement): paired over Pear, harness rpc and clip through the gateway, burst, thumbnails (outcomes by status: 200s and one 202 thumbnail-pending), 2 cold starts, quality presets logged (ULTRA_LOW, LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH, ULTRA_HIGH, SMOOTH, ...). One of five smoke runs reported a test failure after all results had printed; not reproduced in two reruns. Session plan: on the car's LAN turn PEAR_PEER on, record meta, start the car sampler (detached, 2400 s); switch the Mac to a phone hotspot; run video MEDIUM 600 s (longer than a foreground command, so it runs detached and is waited on), then rpc/clip/burst/thumbnails/20 cold starts; further presets if time allows; back on the LAN fetch the sample, revoke the pear bench device, PEAR_PEER off. Found while preparing: BladeWatch-qryk (companion announces itself on the car's topic).
RUN 2026-09-26 (same conditions as the rdtj.18 note: phone hotspot, randomizing NAT, car off, MEDIUM).
CONTROL RPC over Pear, harness rpc, one kept-alive connection, 0 errors in 320 calls:
| Call | n | p50 | p95 | p99 | max ms |
| GetStatus burst | 200 | 292.2 | 1425.9 | 1922.1 | 3825.2 |
| GetStatus paced 0.5 s | 120 | 424.2 | 1528.1 | 3448.7 | 5584.0 |
| TripsService/ListTrips | 50 | 644.0 | 4150.8 | 4528.3 | 4528.3 |
| RecordingsService/ListRecordings | 50 | 782.9 | 2501.6 | 3589.9 | 3589.9 |
| VehicleService/GetState | 50 | 306.5 | 1663.0 | 1762.4 | 1762.4 |
(baselines GetStatus: loopback burst p50 1.4 / paced p50 5.7; LAN TLS burst p50 14.8 / paced p50 100.3)
CLIP x3 16 MiB: attempt 1 did not finish within 590 s (so under ~0.75 Mbit/s aggregate; the harness prints only at the end); later attempts could not get a route.
ROUTE FAILURES: 5 of 8 route attempts between 09:40 and 10:08 failed after ~90 s, while a plain HyperDHT dial to the car still opened (3.0-19.1 s). Cause found: every companion session announces itself on the car's topic (BladeWatch-qryk), so each attempt -- failed ones included -- leaves a dead announcer that later attempts dial first; by 10:08 there were 7 announcers (car + 6 ended bench sessions). Back-to-back cold starts on flutter_pear 0.4.4 therefore measure this self-pollution. Plan: let the records expire, then measure the clip and the 20 cold starts with the fixed flutter_pear (join announce: false, flutter_pear-con, via a temporary local override that is reverted afterwards), and report the 0.4.4 failures beside it.
COLD START, 2026-09-26 11:36-11:54, phone hotspot (10.101.x, HyperDHT firewalled=true randomized=true), car off, car on the fixed build (pear-end acceptUnannounced, BladeWatch-lw0o), companion dial-only (announce: false, local flutter_pear override); cold start = Pear.start + join + findCarOverPear + companion login + first GetStatus, 120 s cap per attempt:
- 13 of 20 reached the car. first_status p50 43.6 s, p90 61.2 s, max 65.0 s, best 8.9 s (route alone p50 41.0 s, max 63.9 s).
- All 7 failures: no Pear connection ever formed (0 peers; swarm connecting -> failed/cut at the 90 s search) -- NAT traversal between the randomizing hotspot NAT and the car, NOT the tagging race: every attempt that got a connection reached the car (13/13).
- Before the car fix (flutter_pear 0.4.4 car, announcing companion, 09:40-10:38): 5 of 8 route attempts failed, including attempts whose Pear connection formed but the car never used (the tagging race).
Per-attempt log: session scratchpad bench/coldstart_fixed.log.
CLIP / BURST / THUMBNAILS over Pear, 2026-09-26 11:55-12:10, phone hotspot (randomizing NAT), car off, fixed build, dial-only companion:
| Measure | Result | LAN TLS baseline |
| clip x3 16 MiB Range GET | 3.8 Mbit/s p50, 5.2 max | 12.5 p50, 16.2 max |
| dashboard burst (status+trips+recordings+vehicle concurrently) x20 | run 1: p50 674 ms, p90 1.79 s, max 4.89 s; run 2: p50 350 ms, p90 534 ms, max 1.06 s; 0 failed | - |
| thumbnails sequential x24 | p50 1.41-3.00 s, max 4.6-5.4 s (3 runs) | - |
| thumbnails 4 at a time x24 | 21-36 s wall; 16 of 24 HttpException in one of three runs (BladeWatch-t806) | - |
Thumbnails are payload-bound, not per-connection: each /thumb/ answer is ~870 KiB (p50 866-875 KiB, 80 samples) -- BladeWatch-820b. The runner reuses one keep-alive connection for the sequential phase (the car keeps HTTP/1.1 alive), so the per-image cost is mostly the image.
VERDICT (separate from live video): control and clips over Pear from a mobile hotspot are viable; cold start is the problem. Control RPC: 0 errors in 320 calls, p50 0.29-0.78 s, p95 1.4-4.2 s (status, trips, recordings, vehicle state); dashboard burst p50 0.35-0.67 s, max 1.1-4.9 s; clip download 3.8 Mbit/s p50 (LAN TLS 12.5). Thumbnails are slow only because each is ~870 KiB (BladeWatch-820b); intermittent concurrent-fetch errors tracked on BladeWatch-t806. Cold start (Pear start to first status, 20 attempts, car on the pear-end acceptUnannounced fix, dial-only companion): 13/20 succeeded, p50 43.6 s, p90 61.2 s, worst 65.0 s; the 7 failures never formed a Pear connection from the randomizing NAT (BladeWatch-idfn). Before the car fix, attempts could also connect and never be used (BladeWatch-lw0o, fixed pending the flutter_pear release flutter_pear-con). For rdtj.12 (remove tor): control and clips no longer argue for keeping tor; reaching the car at all from hard NATs (idfn) is the open risk -- owner's call.
Follow-up: the ~870 KiB thumbnails were un-scaled 2560x1920 hero JPEGs; fixed by BladeWatch-820b (now <=46 KB each).
close_reason: Measured over Pear from a phone hotspot (genuinely different network, randomizing NAT) 2026-09-26 with the unchanged harness plus the companion runner (companion/integration_test/pear_bench_test.dart): per-call latency for status/trips/recordings/vehicle state, burst, thumbnails, clip download, and a 20-attempt cold-start distribution (median 43.6 s, worst 65.0 s, 7 of 20 never connected). Tables and the separate verdict are in the notes. Follow-ups: BladeWatch-idfn (NAT traversal), BladeWatch-lw0o/qryk (pending flutter_pear-con release), BladeWatch-820b, BladeWatch-t806.

title: Pear throughput: live H.264 video from a remote network
description:
## Problem / context

Second of three throughput tasks. This one answers the question the whole "everything over
Pear" decision rests on: does live H.264 survive the Pear path?

Over Pear, every video byte crosses the JavaScript-to-native BareKit IPC boundary twice on
the car (worklet to `PearStreamPump` in `pear_daemon`), then a loopback TCP hop to
`byd_cam_daemon`, and twice more on the companion — on top of Hyperswarm's own encryption
and whatever the DHT path costs. The car is a 2019-class arm64 SoC already running camera
capture, GPU downscaling, motion detection and H.264 encoding.

Nobody has measured this. If the answer is "no", the plan is not dead, but the epic must
choose consciously between lowering stream quality over Pear, restricting live view to the
LAN path, or keeping tor for video. That decision needs data.

## Exact locations

- Baselines and the measurement harness to reuse: the baseline throughput task's close
  reason. USE ITS EXACT METHOD — numbers gathered differently cannot be compared.
- Car pump: `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/daemon/PearStreamPump.kt`
- Companion pump and selector: the companion package.
- Streaming producer: `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/StreamingApiHandler.kt` (349 lines)
- WebSocket framing: `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/HttpServer.kt` lines 1283-1332
- Quality settings: `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/QualitySettingsApiHandler.kt`

## Step-by-step instructions

1. Read the baseline task's close reason first and reproduce its harness exactly.
2. Measure live view over Pear FROM A GENUINELY DIFFERENT NETWORK. Not the car's Wi-Fi, not
   the same NAT. flutter_pear documents that two peers behind one NAT fail for router
