title: v1.4.0.0 Epic: Replace Tor with Pear P2P transport and ship a companion app
description:
## Problem / context

BladeWatch's only remote-access path today is a Tor v3 onion service (`TorLauncher`,
`app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/launcher/TorLauncher.kt`, 347 lines) fronting
`127.0.0.1:8080`. Reaching it needs a Tor client on the viewer's device, which is why the
only practical remote client is the Angular SPA in `web/` opened in a browser.

v1.4.0.0 replaces that transport with Pear (Hyperswarm P2P) and ships a native companion app
for phone/desktop, retiring `web/` once the companion reaches parity.

THE COMPANION APP IS A FLUTTER APP USING THE FLUTTER_PEAR PLUGIN. That is a fixed decision.
flutter_pear lives at /Volumes/mandark-1Tb/projects/loabletech/flutter_pear and is published
on pub.dev at v0.4.0; it puts a typed Dart API over the same Pear stack (Bare worklet,
Hyperswarm, Hypercore family) that the car-side daemon runs via BareKit. Do not substitute a
different P2P library, a raw socket design, or a hand-rolled DHT on either side. Pin
flutter_pear to an EXACT version, never a caret: its README states minor versions may break
the API without notice before 1.0.

## The core architectural decision: tunnel, do not port

A Pear connection is a reliable, ordered, encrypted byte stream — the same shape tor
already provides. Pear therefore replaces tor AT THE SAME LAYER. Nothing above the
transport is rewritten:

- `HttpServer.kt` (1542 lines), including the WebSocket H.264 framing at
  `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/HttpServer.kt` lines 1283-1332
  (SPS/PPS caching, IDR requests, frame fragmenting) is UNTOUCHED.
- All ConnectRPC services are UNTOUCHED.
- `flutter_ui/lib/rpc/connect_client.dart` line 43 already takes baseUrl as a constructor
  parameter (default `http://127.0.0.1:8080`), so the companion just points it elsewhere.

Both stream pumps are written in Kotlin (car) and Dart (companion), NOT in the Bare
worklet JS. The daemon receives Pear bytes over BareKit IPC and opens the TCP socket to
8080 itself. This means the stock `pear-end.bundle` from
`flutter_pear/packages/flutter_pear/assets/pear-end.bundle` ships unmodified — no
`bare-pack`, no forked worklet JS, no `bare-tcp` dependency.

## Why BareKit works in the daemon

BladeWatch's HTTP server runs inside `CameraDaemon`, a shell-UID `app_process` process with
no Flutter engine. flutter_pear's Android host
(`packages/flutter_pear_bare/android/src/main/kotlin/tech/loable/flutter_pear_bare/FlutterPearBarePlugin.kt`,
355 lines) is a Flutter plugin, but it is only a relay: it wraps
`to.holepunch.bare.kit.Worklet` and `to.holepunch.bare.kit.IPC`, which come from upstream
holepunchto/bare-kit as a plain `classes.jar` plus `jni/<abi>/*.so`, downloaded at build
time (see `flutter_pear/packages/flutter_pear_bare/android/build.gradle` lines 86-90, 320).
Those classes have no Flutter dependency, and arm64-v8a is shipped. A plain Kotlin daemon
can therefore boot a worklet directly. THIS IS UNPROVEN AND IS THE FIRST TASK IN THIS EPIC.

## Same-LAN path (NAT hairpinning mitigation)

flutter_pear's own documented pairing matrix says two peers behind the same NAT FAIL —
router hairpinning breaks Hyperswarm's UDP hole punching. That case (car parked in the
driveway, phone on the same home Wi-Fi) is one of the most common remote-check moments, so
Pear alone is not sufficient.

The companion therefore does not try to detect the network — it probes for the car. It
broadcasts a UDP probe; the daemon replies UNICAST to the source address. If the car
answers, both are on the same segment by definition. This avoids ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION
(required on Android 10+ to read the SSID) and avoids needing a MulticastLock on the
companion.

The LAN path must NOT be plaintext. Today every remote byte is inside tor and therefore
encrypted; a plain-HTTP LAN path would put the Bearer JWT on the wire in the clear, and a
passive sniffer on a shared Wi-Fi who captured it would gain the full API including the
vehicle-control endpoints that actuate real hardware. Two listeners solve this:

| Bind | Transport | Clients |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `127.0.0.1:8080` | plain HTTP | in-car Flutter UI, Pear stream pump (Pear already encrypts) |
| `0.0.0.0:8443` | TLS, self-signed, fingerprint pinned at pairing | companion on the same LAN |

Nothing plaintext ever leaves the device.

## Child task order

Suffixes are this epic's child ids; the bd dependency graph encodes the real ordering.

1. `.1` Version bump to 1.4.0.0.
2. `.2` SPIKE: BareKit Worklet in a plain app_process. BLOCKS EVERYTHING ELSE.
3. `.3` PearLauncher in the daemon.
4. `.4` TLS listener on 8443.
5. `.5` LAN discovery probe responder.
6. `.6` Car-side Pear-to-TCP pump.
7. `.7` Unified pairing payload.
8. `.10` Melos workspace + Flutter companion scaffold with flutter_pear.
9. `.8` Companion-side pump + transport selector.
10. `.14` Sentry alert delivery to the companion. SEE THE OPEN PROBLEM BELOW.
11. `.9` Baseline throughput (loopback, LAN TLS, tor). RUN EARLY — the tor baseline is
    destroyed the moment tor is removed and cannot be recovered.
12. `.18` Pear throughput: live video. GATES TOR REMOVAL.
13. `.19` Pear throughput: control RPC and clips. GATES TOR REMOVAL.
14. `.11` Companion screens to parity.
15. `.17` In-car UI: Pear peer status, replacing the tunnel entry `.12` deletes.
16. `.16` Security review of the new network surface. GATES TOR REMOVAL.
17. `.15` Release workflow, build docs, upgrade notes.
18. `.12` Remove Tor.
19. `.13` web/ parity checklist and retirement gate.

`.4` MUST land before `.6`: `.4` builds the per-listener trust plumbing and `.6` adds the
8081 listener that depends on it. An agent doing `.6` first has nowhere to hang the policy
and will reach for 8080, which is exactly the P0 hole above. The dependency graph encodes
this; do not reorder around it.

## Open problem: sentry alerts may not be replaceable (`.14`)

Surveillance and proximity events reach the owner today through Web Push: the car POSTs an
encrypted payload straight to the browser's push subscription endpoint and the BROWSER's
service worker raises the notification (`PushSink.kt`, `PushTransport.kt`,
`VapidKeyStore.kt`; `docs/features.md` line 352).

A Flutter app has no service worker and cannot receive Web Push. Background delivery to a
Flutter app needs FCM or APNs — a central service, which cuts against the serverless premise
that motivated Pear. A held Pear connection is NOT a substitute: flutter_pear documents that
mobile OSes suspend background apps, that each suspend/resume resets the swarm to
`discovering`, and that a DHT lookup can take 30s or more.

This is unresolved by design, not an oversight. `.14` decides it and is a hard blocker on
`.13`. If alerts cannot reach the companion, retiring `web/` is a functional regression and
the browser PWA stays as the notification channel.

## The Pear peer is its own daemon process

`pear_daemon` is a standalone `app_process` daemon alongside `byd_cam_daemon`,
`sentry_daemon` and `acc_sentry_daemon` — NOT a thread inside CameraDaemon. Verified on the
head unit 2026-09-23, that launch shape is:

    sh -c CLASSPATH=/data/app/net.bladewatch.app-<hash>/base.apk \
      app_process /system/bin --nice-name=sentry_daemon \
      net.bladewatch.app.daemon.SentryDaemon

run as the `shell` user, outside the Activity lifecycle. The runtime class is
`net.bladewatch.app.daemon.*` while the source lives at `com/loabletech/bladewatch/daemon/*`;
the Gradle package rename makes them disagree on purpose.

The stream pump therefore lives in `pear_daemon` and reaches `HttpServer` — which lives in
`byd_cam_daemon` — over loopback TCP to 8081. That is a real cross-process hop: the pump
must retry if CameraDaemon is not yet listening, and close pumped connections cleanly if it
restarts. Process separation is NOT a security boundary here; the per-listener trust policy
below is what protects 8081.

`pear_daemon` must be added to CLAUDE.md's clean-reinstall daemon-stop block. A daemon
missing from that list survives an uninstall as a detached `app_process` and blocks the next
build with a stale lock.

## Cross-cutting security invariant: the Tier 2 loopback bypass

This spans `.4`, `.6`, `.12` and `.16`. Getting it wrong is a P0 vehicle-control hole, so it
is stated once here as well as in each task.

`AuthMiddleware` (lines 174-192) grants UNAUTHENTICATED access to callers from 127.0.0.1
when the build is debug, no tunnel-forwarding headers are present, and `isTunnelActive()`
is false. Debug is the build that actually ships to the car, because preserving the ADB key
across a reinstall needs `run-as`. `isTunnelActive()` (line 223) detects external
reachability by looking for ONE process name: `TorLauncher.TOR_PROCESS`, i.e.
`bladewatch_tor`.

The Pear stream pump opens a plain TCP connection to loopback — at the socket level
indistinguishable from an app on the head unit, exactly as tor was. And removing tor
deletes the only signal `isTunnelActive()` ever had. Left unaddressed, a debug build on the
car with the Pear peer up would hand full unauthenticated API access, vehicle control
included, to anyone who learned the Pear topic. That is the hole `BladeWatch-3lbz.2` closed
for tor.

The fix is STRUCTURAL, not stateful. `HttpServer` gets three listeners with per-listener
trust:

| Listener | Purpose | Tier 2 bypass |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `127.0.0.1:8080` | in-car Flutter UI | eligible in debug, as today |
| `127.0.0.1:8081` | Pear pump only | NEVER |
| `0.0.0.0:8443` | LAN companion over TLS | NEVER |

A new listener defaults to NOT bypass-eligible. Do not replace this with a global "a tunnel
is up" flag: that fails OPEN the moment someone forgets to set it, which is exactly the
failure mode being designed out.

## Constraints

- Do NOT commit. This project's CLAUDE.md forbids `git add`, `git commit`, `git push`.
- Do NOT modify `HttpServer.kt`'s WebSocket or ConnectRPC handling. The whole point is that
  the transport swap leaves it alone.
- Do NOT add iOS/macOS/Windows/Linux/web platform directories under `flutter_ui/`.
  `app/build.gradle.kts` line 1294 (`validateFlutterAndroidOnly`) fails the build if they
  appear. The companion is a SEPARATE Flutter project.
- Do NOT delete `/data/local/tmp/tor/hs` as part of any Tor work before the removal task
  explicitly says so — it holds the permanent onion identity key and deleting it silently
  breaks every QR code the owner has ever scanned.
- Do NOT rely on the loopback bypass being "debug-only" as a security argument. Debug is
  the build that ships to the car. See the cross-cutting invariant above.
- Do NOT widen the loopback auth bypass in `AuthMiddleware.kt`. LAN callers and Pear peers
  must keep full JWT enforcement.
- Do NOT lower any of the three coverage gates (repo-root koverVerify, flutter_ui/android
  koverVerify, Flutter coverage). They ratchet upward only.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All 19 child tasks are closed.
- [ ] `./gradlew test` and `./gradlew koverVerify` pass at the repo root.
- [ ] `cd flutter_ui/android && ./gradlew koverVerify` passes.
- [ ] `cd flutter_ui && flutter analyze && flutter test` pass.
- [ ] The companion is a Flutter app depending on flutter_pear at an exact pin.
- [ ] On a real DEBUG build on the head unit, a Pear peer with no JWT is denied every
      non-public endpoint including vehicle control, with the loopback bypass forced on.
- [ ] A companion app connects to a real head unit over Pear from a different network, and
      over TLS+LAN from the same network, with live view working on both.
- [ ] `docs/networking-and-tunnels.md`, `docs/architecture.md`,
      `docs/daemons-and-processes.md` and `docs/ipc-auth-and-secrets.md` describe the Pear
      transport, the 8443 TLS listener and the LAN probe, with no stale Tor claims.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.

title: Vehicle screen clips the 3D car and tyre cards in landscape
description:
## Problem

On the landscape head unit the Vehicle screen clipped the 3D car down to its roof and sliced
the four tyre pressure cards through the middle of their kPa line. The charge/fuel readout also
floated on top of the car and, being translucent, let the 3D render show through its own
numbers.

Not a styling problem. The screen was built for portrait and had no landscape arrangement.

## Root cause

The head unit rotates: landscape 960x540dp, portrait 540x960dp
(docs/ui-ux-design-language.md, "Target device"). The whole screen was one Stack whose three
parts had no shared constraint:

  - hero: Positioned.fill, so the WebView filled the entire Stack
  - tyre cards: Positioned(top: 60 ...) and Positioned(top: 156 ...), absolute pixels
  - controls: a Column with Spacer() and mainAxisSize.min, sized by its own content

The controls needed roughly 44 (appearance bar) + 48 (tab chips) + 360 (a hard-coded
ConstrainedBox maxHeight) = 452dp. A landscape head unit has 540dp of height. The tyre cards
needed 60 + 96 + 96 = 252dp from the top. Those do not both fit, and because nothing shared a
constraint the panel simply drew over the car and the cards.

It also violated the design language's own rule that layouts must reference tokens, never
hard-coded dp.

## Fix

Responsive split, chosen by the owner over two alternatives.

  - Landscape (>= 700dp wide): Row of hero pane 55% and controls 45%.
  - Portrait: Column, hero above controls, as before but with real constraints.

  - Tyre cards anchor to the hero pane's four CORNERS instead of screen pixel offsets. This is
    also a better map of the car: left column the right-hand wheels, right column the left-hand
    wheels, top row rear, bottom row front, which is exactly the arrangement the old offsets
    produced.
  - _StatusCard splits into _LockPill (lock state, stays over the hero, top-centre) and
    _ChargeCard (charge/range/fuel/fuel range as a solid card BELOW the car).
  - The appearance bar (colour swatches, model name) moves into the hero pane, since it
    describes the car rather than the controls.
  - The controls panel's ConstrainedBox(maxHeight: 360) becomes Flexible, so tab content takes
    whatever room its pane gives and scrolls inside it.
  - The climate tab's four two-across rows become a _pair(twoUp, a, b) helper that stacks below
    500dp. Necessary: a stepper's minus/value/plus cluster is rigid (two 48dp icon buttons plus
    the value), so at the landscape controls width of ~432dp the temperature and fan steppers
    overflowed by 16px.
  - The appearance bar's model label becomes Flexible with ellipsis; unbounded, it overflowed
    the narrower hero column by 7px.

## Constraints, do NOT change

- Do NOT change any ValueKey. The existing 180 widget tests assert on them.
- Do NOT change which RPC any control calls, or any user-visible string.
- Do NOT reintroduce absolute Positioned offsets for the tyre cards.
- Keep the controls panel OPAQUE. At alpha 0.92 the text behind it read through
  (BladeWatch-9c7d).
- The hero is a WebView and cannot be constructed in flutter test, so widget tests inject
  SizedBox.shrink() via heroBuilder. Anything that can only be seen against a real 3D render
  has to be checked on the device.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All four tyre cards are fully within the viewport at both 960x540 and 540x960.
- [ ] In landscape the controls sit beside the car, with every tyre card entirely left of the
      tab chips.
- [ ] In portrait the controls sit below the hero.
- [ ] The charge readout never overlaps a tyre card in either orientation.
- [ ] No RenderFlex overflow at either size.
- [ ] cd flutter_ui && flutter analyze passes, flutter test passes.
- [ ] Verified on the head unit: the car and all four tyre cards are visible and uncropped.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles
and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather
than guessing.
close_reason:
Fixed and verified on the head unit. Owner chose the responsive split over two alternatives.

Root cause: the screen was one Stack whose three parts shared no constraint -- hero at
Positioned.fill, tyre cards at absolute Positioned(top: 60) / (top: 156), and a control panel
sized by its own content with a hard-coded ConstrainedBox(maxHeight: 360). The panel needed
about 44 + 48 + 360 = 452dp, the tyre cards needed 252dp from the top, and nothing arbitrated.
In portrait there was room; in landscape the panel drew straight over the car and sliced the
tyre cards through their kPa line.

Changes:
- LayoutBuilder split at 700dp: landscape is a Row of hero pane 55% / controls 45%, portrait is
  the previous vertical stack, both now with real constraints.
- Tyre cards anchor to the hero pane's four corners instead of screen pixels. Also a better map
  of the car than the arithmetic it replaces: left column the right-hand wheels, right column
  the left-hand wheels, top row rear, bottom row front -- the same arrangement, stated as
  intent.
- _StatusCard split into _LockPill (stays over the hero, top-centre) and _ChargeCard
  (charge/range/fuel/fuel range as a solid card BELOW the car). The old readout was a
  translucent pill over the model, so the 3D render showed through its own numbers.
- The appearance bar moved into the hero pane; it describes the car, not the controls.
- ConstrainedBox(maxHeight: 360) -> Flexible.
- The climate tab's four two-across rows became a _pair(twoUp, a, b) helper that stacks below
  500dp. Required: a stepper's minus/value/plus cluster is rigid (two 48dp icon buttons plus
  the value), and at the landscape controls width the temperature and fan steppers overflowed
  by 16px. The appearance bar's model label likewise became Flexible with ellipsis after
  overflowing by 7px in the narrower hero column.

No ValueKey changed, so all 180 pre-existing widget tests passed untouched. Five new geometry
tests at both real device sizes; mutation-verified -- forcing the single-column layout
everywhere (the pre-fix behaviour) fails three of them.

Honest about coverage: two mutations SURVIVED. Restoring maxHeight: 360 no longer breaks
anything, because with the split in place 360 fits inside the landscape column -- the split is
the fix and Flexible is defence in depth, not the load-bearing part. Moving the charge card
back over the car also passes, because the hero is a WebView that cannot be constructed in
flutter test (heroBuilder injects SizedBox.shrink), so "overlaps the 3D model" is not
measurable in a widget test at all. Both were checked by eye on the device instead.

Gates: flutter analyze clean, full flutter test 1581 passed.

Verified on the car: two columns, the 3D model renders in full, all four tyre cards complete
and uncropped, charge/fuel in its own card below the car, controls in their own column.

Side finding, fixed in docs/ui-ux-design-language.md: the "Target device" line claimed
960x540dp landscape. Measured density is 240, so the device pixel ratio is 1.5 and the real
logical size is 1280x720dp. The old figure assumed density 320 and understated the height
budget by a third -- directly relevant to this class of bug.

title: Startup screen shows a raw PlatformChannelError instead of progress
description:
## Problem

The in-car startup screen prints a raw Dart exception across its header, in red, where the
progress message belongs. Seen on the head unit 2026-09-20 after a reboot:

  PlatformChannelError(daemonNotUp): connect to 127.0.0.1:19876 failed: failed to connect to
  /127.0.0.1 (port 19876) from /127.0.0.1 (port 42822) after 5000ms: isConnected failed:
  ECONNREFUSED (Connection refused)

File: flutter_ui/lib/screens/startup/startup_controller.dart line 98
  } catch (e) {
    _channelErrorMessage = e.toString();
  }

File: flutter_ui/lib/screens/startup/startup_screen.dart line 88
  c.channelErrorMessage ?? _headerText(l10n, c.phase)

## Why this is the wrong thing to show

daemonNotUp during startup is not an error, it is the normal state. The startup screen polls
daemon.processStatus roughly once a second while the daemons are still coming up, and the
daemon does not listen on 19876 until CameraDaemon is running. ECONNREFUSED is the expected
answer to every poll until then. The screen is literally named "Getting your dashcam ready"
and each row already reads "Waiting".

It is also unactionable. A socket errno, two loopback port numbers and an ephemeral source
port tell the driver nothing they can act on, and the information is already available in the
rows and over ADB.

## Fix

Stop surfacing channel exceptions on this screen at all.

1. startup_controller.dart: delete the _channelErrorMessage field and its getter. Keep the
   try/catch, which must still swallow the exception so tick() never throws, and leave a
   comment saying why nothing is surfaced: the rows plus the phase header already describe
   the state honestly, and daemonNotUp is expected here.
2. startup_screen.dart: the header Text becomes _headerText(l10n, c.phase) unconditionally,
   and the colour becomes theme.colorScheme.onSurfaceVariant unconditionally. Remove the
   error-colour branch.
3. Update the three tests in
   flutter_ui/test/screens/startup/startup_controller_test.dart (around lines 198 to 235)
   that assert on channelErrorMessage. Assert the real contract instead: a throwing channel
   does not throw out of tick(), leaves every row in the waiting state, and a later
   successful tick still promotes rows to ready.

## Constraints, do NOT change

- Do NOT add a new ARB key. app/build.gradle.kts validateArbCatalogs enforces strict key
  parity across all 19 locales in both directions, so one new English string means 19
  translations. A friendly replacement banner is a separate task if it is ever wanted.
- Do NOT add print or debugPrint. There is no logging call anywhere in flutter_ui/lib today
  and the poll runs about once a second, so it would be both a new convention and log spam.
- Do NOT stop catching the exception. tick() is driven by a Timer.periodic in the widget; an
  escaping exception would break the poll loop.
- Do NOT touch the "Continue anyway" escape hatch, the 120s delay, or StartupPhase.
- Rows already initialise to waiting (startup_controller.dart line 44), so a permanently
  broken channel shows "Getting things ready..." plus three Waiting rows plus Continue
  anyway. That is the intended degraded state, not a gap to fill.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] No raw exception text can reach the startup screen.
- [ ] channelErrorMessage no longer exists on StartupController.
- [ ] tick() still swallows PlatformChannelError and timeouts without throwing.
- [ ] Rows stay waiting while the channel is failing and still go ready after it recovers.
- [ ] No ARB file changed; no new localisation key.
- [ ] cd flutter_ui && flutter analyze passes with no new issues.
- [ ] cd flutter_ui && flutter test passes.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles
and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather
than guessing.
close_reason:
Removed rather than reworded, because daemonNotUp is not an error on this screen.

The startup screen polls daemon.processStatus about once a second, and nothing listens on
19876 until CameraDaemon is running, so ECONNREFUSED is the correct and expected answer to
every poll for roughly the first 45s after boot. The screen was printing its own normal
startup as a red fault, and the content was unactionable anyway: a socket errno and two
loopback port numbers including an ephemeral source port.

Changes:
- startup_controller.dart: deleted _channelErrorMessage and its getter. The catch still
  swallows, with a comment explaining why nothing is surfaced. Catching is still required
  because tick() is driven by a Timer.periodic in the widget.
- startup_screen.dart: header is now unconditionally the phase text in onSurfaceVariant. The
  error-colour branch is gone.

No new localisation string, deliberately. validateArbCatalogs enforces strict key parity in
both directions across all 19 locales, so one English string would mean 19 translations, and
the screen already describes the state honestly without one: rows initialise to waiting and
stay there while the channel is down, the phase header reads "Getting things ready...", and
the Continue anyway escape hatch still appears after 120s. A friendly banner for the genuinely
unexpected reasons, shellCallFailed and permissionDenied, is a separate task if wanted.

Tests: rewrote the three controller tests that asserted on the removed field plus the widget
test that asserted the raw text rendered. They now pin the real contract. The widget test
asserts the phase text is present and that none of "daemon not up", "PlatformChannelError",
"ECONNREFUSED" or "19876" reaches the screen.

Mutation-verified: restoring the raw exception to the header fails
"channel error: shows normal progress, never raw exception text", and both source files were
restored byte-identical afterwards.

One test bug caught on the way: my first version of the recovery test called stubStatuses()
with no arguments, which defaults every daemon to NOT running, so the rows correctly stayed
waiting and the assertion was wrong, not the code.

Gates: flutter analyze clean, full flutter test 1575 passed, validateArbCatalogs successful.

Deployed to the head unit and launched. The Flutter APK installs over itself so no uninstall,
no daemon restart and no ADB key handling was needed; shared UID still 10073 for both
packages. Launching it also woke the service host, which had not started after the 11:06
reboot because BYD ssc_skip suppressed BOOT_COMPLETED to the package; all four daemons are now
running and 19876 is listening.

Not visually reproduced on device after the fix: the error state only exists while the daemons
are down, and forcing it would disarm sentry on a parked car for a screenshot of something the
mutation-verified widget test already pins.

title: Sweep orphaned sidecars at daemon startup (retroactive companion to k3b0)
description:
## Problem

BladeWatch-k3b0 closed the two paths that STRAND sidecars (StorageManager.ensureSpace and
HardwareEventRecorderGpu.deleteSegmentSidecars). That fix is preventive only. Nothing anywhere
scans for a sidecar whose .mp4 is already gone, so every orphan created by an older build, a
crash between the sidecar write and the mp4 rename, or any future gap in a deletion path lives
forever.

Measured on the head unit 2026-09-20: 823 orphans (111 MB) accumulated over 9 days completely
undetected, and 9 more appeared within hours of the manual cleanup because the car still runs
the pre-k3b0 build.

The three existing automatic sweepers cannot see these:
  - StorageManager.startPeriodicCleanup (every 30s) is size-driven and deletes oldest-first; it
    cannot tell an orphan from real footage.
  - HardwareEventRecorderGpu.cleanupOrphanedTmpFiles (daemon startup) only matches .tmp/.broken.
  - TripDatabase.deleteOrphanedTrips reaps database rows, not files.

Orphans are not merely wasted space. The reaper measures the whole directory against
surveillanceLimitMb, so dead thumbnails consume quota and the reaper then deletes MORE real
footage to hit its target. The leak costs the owner video, not just disk.

## Fix

Add a companion function cleanupOrphanedSidecars(directory: File) to
app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/surveillance/HardwareEventRecorderGpu.kt, next to
the existing cleanupOrphanedTmpFiles (around line 2091), and call it from
app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/daemon/CameraDaemon.kt at the existing startup
cleanup block (lines 1473-1478) for both sm.recordingsDir and sm.surveillanceDir.

Algorithm:
  1. List the directory once.
  2. Build the set of live segment bases: strip ".mp4" from every mp4, and strip ".mp4.tmp"
     from every in-flight temp so a segment mid-write keeps its sidecars.
  3. For each candidate, derive its base:
       - "thumb_<base>_a...jpg"  -> the live base b for which the name starts with
         "thumb_" + b + "_a". This is the exact inverse of the forward rule
         deleteSegmentSidecars uses, so the two can never disagree.
       - "<base>.jpg" / "<base>.srt" / "<base>.json" -> the name minus its extension.
       - anything else (.mp4, .tmp, .broken, unknown) -> skip, not ours.
  4. Delete when the base is not in the live set AND the file is older than the same 5 minute
     window cleanupOrphanedTmpFiles uses. Promote that 5 minute value to a shared private const
     so the two functions cannot drift.
  5. Log a single summary line with the count and freed KB, only when something was deleted.

Startup-only is deliberate and sufficient: the leak accrues at roughly 12 MB/day, and
k3b0 stops new orphans at the source. Do NOT add a scheduler, a thread or a config knob.

## Constraints, do NOT change

- Do NOT touch which .mp4 files get selected for deletion anywhere.
- Do NOT widen the sweep beyond .jpg, .srt and .json. The device inventory for these two
  directories is exactly mp4, jpg, srt, json, tmp, and every jpg/srt/json in them is keyed to
  an mp4 basename. No config file lives there.
- Keep the "_a" anchor on the thumbnail rule, matching deleteSegmentSidecars,
  StorageManager line 1754 and RecordingsApiHandler line 1470.
- Do NOT change cleanupOrphanedTmpFiles behaviour; only swap its literal for the shared const.
- Do NOT delete a sidecar whose base has a live ".mp4.tmp" in flight.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] cleanupOrphanedSidecars deletes "<base>.jpg", "<base>.srt", "<base>.json" and
      "thumb_<base>_a*.jpg" when "<base>.mp4" is absent.
- [ ] It keeps every sidecar whose "<base>.mp4" is present.
- [ ] It keeps every sidecar whose "<base>.mp4.tmp" is present (segment mid-write).
- [ ] It keeps files younger than the 5 minute window even when orphaned.
- [ ] It leaves .mp4, .tmp and .broken files untouched.
- [ ] CameraDaemon calls it at startup for recordings and surveillance.
- [ ] A JVM unit test covers the cases above and fails if the logic is broken.
- [ ] ./gradlew :app:compileDebugJavaWithJavac compiles clean.
- [ ] ./gradlew test koverVerify passes with fresh test-result timestamps.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles
and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather
than guessing.
notes:
Follow-up review on 2026-09-20 found two things in the shipped change. Both fixed; gates green.

1. RATIONALE WAS WRONG. The KDoc on cleanupOrphanedSidecars claimed orphans consume the
   category quota and cost the owner real footage. StorageManager.getDirectoriesTotalSize
   counts only .mp4 and .json, so orphaned .jpg and .srt never inflate a limit. See the
   correction note on BladeWatch-k3b0 for the full detail. Comments and docs corrected.

2. COVERAGE GAP, AND A TRAP IN THE OBVIOUS FIX. cleanupOrphanedSidecars was called only on
   the active recordingsDir and surveillanceDir, while ensureSpace reaps across
   getReapableDirs -- the internal/SD mirror and the legacy path as well. An orphan left in
   the mirror after a storage switch was unreachable forever, and proximity was never swept
   at all.

   The obvious fix, passing getReapableDirs straight through, would have been destructive.
   getReapableDirs("recordings") includes the flat legacy base
   /storage/emulated/0/Android/data/net.bladewatch.app/files, which is not a media directory:
   it holds bladewatch_secrets.json, bladewatch_config.json and .bladewatch_device_id. The
   sweeper deletes any .json with no matching .mp4, so it would have deleted the device's
   legacy secrets and config. ensureSpace survives that directory only because it passes a
   category namePrefix, and a sweeper cannot use the same guard because per-actor thumbnails
   are named "thumb_<base>_a*.jpg" and carry no category prefix.

   Added StorageManager.sweepableDirs(category), which returns getReapableDirs minus that flat
   base and returns empty for "trips" (trip telemetry is <tripId>.jsonl.gz, nothing there is a
   sidecar). CameraDaemon now sweeps recordings, surveillance and proximity across every one of
   their directories, deduplicated by absolute path.

   The decision is extracted as a static, sweepableDirsFrom(category, reapableDirs), because a
   StorageManager cannot be constructed in a JVM test -- the same reason selectFilesToDelete
   was extracted. New SweepableDirsTest covers it, mutation-verified: removing the flat-base
   filter, letting trips through, and over-filtering the legacy subdirectory each fail a named
   assertion, and the source was restored byte-identical afterwards.

NOT changed, deliberately: cleanupOrphanedSidecars still has no listFilesViaShell /
deleteFileViaShell fallback, so it is a silent no-op on a directory whose listFiles() returns
null for UID reasons. cleanupOrphanedTmpFiles has the same shape, it works on the head unit
today, and those helpers are private to StorageManager. Latent, not active.
close_reason:
Added HardwareEventRecorderGpu.cleanupOrphanedSidecars(directory), called from CameraDaemon's
existing startup cleanup block for both recordingsDir and surveillanceDir, next to the two
cleanupOrphanedTmpFiles calls. The 5 minute grace window is now a shared private const
(ORPHAN_MIN_AGE_MS) used by both sweepers so they cannot drift.

Algorithm: list once, build the live base set from ".mp4" and from in-flight ".mp4.tmp", then
map each .jpg/.srt/.json back to a base -- plain sidecars by stripping the extension, per-actor
thumbnails by prefix-matching "thumb_" + base + "_a", which is the exact inverse of the forward
rule in deleteSegmentSidecars so the two cannot disagree. Delete when the base is not live and
the file is past the grace window. Everything else (.mp4, .tmp, .broken, unknown) is skipped.

Startup-only, deliberately. No scheduler, no thread, no config knob: k3b0 stops new orphans at
the source and the residue accrues at roughly 12 MB/day.

New JVM test OrphanedSidecarSweepTest, 8 cases. Mutation-verified -- every one of these breaks
a named assertion and was reverted byte-exact afterwards:
  - drop the .mp4.tmp in-flight guard   -> keepsSidecarsOfASegmentStillBeingWritten
  - drop the grace window               -> keepsOrphansYoungerThanTheGraceWindow
  - make the sweeper a no-op            -> reapsSidecarsWhoseSegmentIsGone
  - drop the "_a" thumbnail anchor      -> reapsADeadSiblingsThumbnailEvenWhenTheBaseSegmentIsLive

The anchor mutation is worth calling out: the first version of that test did not catch it. The
anchor's real failure mode is the reverse of the obvious one -- without it, a reaped segment's
thumbnail is misattributed to a live sibling whose name is a prefix of it and kept forever.
That is under-sweeping, i.e. the very leak this task exists to stop, not over-sweeping. The
test now covers both directions.

Validated against the live head unit as a dry run (exact port of the Kotlin logic run over the
real directory listing, nothing deleted): 2497 files / 590 segments in surveillance, 11 genuine
orphans identified, zero false positives; 259 files / 259 segments in recordings, zero orphans.
The in-flight ".mp4.tmp" guard was exercised by real data -- a segment was recording at the time
and its sidecars were correctly kept.

Gates green: :app:compileDebugJavaWithJavac clean, test and koverVerify pass.
docs/data-flow-and-storage.md updated with both sweepers and why an orphan costs video, not
just disk.

Not yet deployed -- the sweeper only runs at daemon startup, so it takes effect on the next
deploy to the car.

title: Retention reaper leaks sidecars: hero JPEG, per-actor thumbs and .srt survive mp4 deletion (823 orphans on device)
description:
## Problem

The surveillance retention reaper deletes an event `.mp4` and its `.json` timeline but leaves the
hero JPEG, the per-actor thumbnails and the `.srt` sidecar behind. Those files then live forever
with no `.mp4` to belong to.

Measured on the head unit 2026-09-20: 823 orphaned sidecars in
`/storage/<sd>/BladeWatch/surveillance`, totalling about 111 MB - 610 `.jpg` and 213 `.srt`.
They span 2026-09-11 through 2026-09-20, and the dates 09-16..09-20 still have surviving `.mp4`
files, which proves this is an ongoing leak rather than historical debris from an older build.

There are two separate deletion paths and each has a gap.

### Path 1 (the main leak): StorageManager.ensureSpace

File: app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/storage/StorageManager.kt
The deletion loop around lines 1719-1750 deletes:
  - the file itself (`.mp4`)
  - `<base>.json` (explicitly handled, with a comment)
  - invalidates the RecordingsApiHandler cache

It does NOT delete `<base>.jpg` (hero), `thumb_<base>_a*.jpg` (per-actor thumbs) or
`<base>.srt`. This is the path that runs when a category is over its storage limit, so it is
responsible for the bulk of the 823 orphans.

### Path 2: HardwareEventRecorderGpu.deleteSegmentSidecars

File: app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/surveillance/HardwareEventRecorderGpu.kt
around line 2117. It correctly removes `<base>.json`, `<base>.jpg` and `thumb_<base>_a*.jpg`,
but it does NOT remove `<base>.srt`. `.srt` files are written by SrtWriter.kt line 110 as
`File(mp4File.parentFile, "$base.srt")`.

## Why this matters beyond wasted space

The orphans still occupy the surveillance directory, and the reaper measures the directory
against `surveillanceLimitMb`. Dead thumbnails therefore consume quota, so to reach its target
the reaper deletes MORE real footage than it needs to. The leak costs the owner actual video,
not just disk.

## Fix

Do NOT make StorageManager call HardwareEventRecorderGpu.deleteSegmentSidecars.
HardwareEventRecorderGpu already imports StorageManager (line 14), so calling back the other way
creates a package cycle. Keep each path self-contained.

1. StorageManager.kt, in the `if (deleted) { ... }` block that currently handles the JSON
   sidecar: extend it to also remove, next to the deleted file, using the same
   `delete()`-then-`deleteFileViaShell()` fallback the JSON branch uses:
     - `<base>.jpg`
     - `<base>.srt`
     - every `thumb_<base>_a*.jpg` in the same directory

   Derive `<base>` by stripping a trailing `.mp4`, and skip the whole block when the deleted
   file is not an `.mp4`. Anchor the per-actor thumbnail prefix with `_a`
   (`"thumb_" + base + "_a"`) exactly as HardwareEventRecorderGpu does, so a sibling segment's
   thumbs are not swept.

2. HardwareEventRecorderGpu.kt `deleteSegmentSidecars`: add `<base>.srt` alongside the existing
   `.json` and `.jpg` handling, accumulating its length into the returned `freed` total.

## Constraints, do NOT change

- Do not change which `.mp4` files get selected for deletion; only the sidecars that accompany
  an already-deleted mp4.
- Keep the `_a` anchor on the thumbnail prefix. Without it, rotating `<base>` sweeps
  `<base>_2`'s thumbnails.
- Do not remove StorageManager's existing RecordingsApiHandler cache invalidation.
- Do not introduce an import of the surveillance package into StorageManager.
- Leave the `.tmp`/`.broken` orphan handling (HardwareEventRecorderGpu.cleanupOrphanedTmpFiles,
  5 minute age threshold) alone - it is correct.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] StorageManager's reaper removes `<base>.jpg`, `<base>.srt` and `thumb_<base>_a*.jpg`
      alongside the `.mp4` and `.json`.
- [ ] deleteSegmentSidecars also removes `<base>.srt` and counts its bytes in the freed total.
- [ ] Neither path sweeps a sibling segment's thumbnails.
- [ ] No surveillance-package import added to StorageManager.
- [ ] ./gradlew :app:compileDebugJavaWithJavac compiles clean.
- [ ] ./gradlew test koverVerify passes with fresh test-result timestamps.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles
and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather
than guessing.
notes:
CORRECTION to this issue's close reason, found in a follow-up review on 2026-09-20.

The close reason and the code comment both claimed orphaned sidecars consume the category
quota and therefore make the reaper delete more real footage. That is FALSE for .jpg and
.srt, which were 610 and 213 of the 823 orphans found, i.e. all of them.

StorageManager.getDirectoriesTotalSize counts only .mp4 and .json toward a category limit.
Orphaned .jpg and .srt are invisible to limit accounting; thumbnails are excluded twice over
since "thumb_..." also fails the "event_" name prefix. The real damage was 111 MB of a shared
SD card, not deleted footage.

The claim IS true for an orphaned .json, which is counted. Both deletion paths have always
handled .json, which is why none were found, but a crash between the .json write and the .mp4
rename can still strand one.

The fix itself is unchanged and still correct. Only its stated priority was overstated.
Comments in StorageManager.kt and HardwareEventRecorderGpu.kt, and
docs/data-flow-and-storage.md, have been corrected.

Related side effect now documented: because .jpg and .srt never count, a configured category
limit is not a cap on disk used. On the head unit that is 1462 jpg + 1180 srt sitting outside
the limit.
close_reason:
Both leak paths closed.

StorageManager.ensureSpace now removes "<base>.jpg", "<base>.srt" and "thumb_<base>_a*.jpg"
alongside the "<base>.mp4" and "<base>.json" it already handled, using the same
delete()-then-deleteFileViaShell() fallback. HardwareEventRecorderGpu.deleteSegmentSidecars
now also removes "<base>.srt" and counts its bytes into the freed total. Neither path gained a
cross-package import, so no cycle, and the "_a" thumbnail anchor is preserved in both.

Gates green: :app:compileDebugJavaWithJavac clean, test and koverVerify pass.

This fix is preventive only -- it stops new orphans at the source but never scans, so nothing
reaps what earlier builds already stranded. That retroactive half is BladeWatch-g8ee.

Not yet running on the head unit; the car is still on the pre-fix build. Confirmed still
leaking: a dry run of the g8ee sweeper against the live directory listing found 11 fresh
orphans from 2026-09-16, two of which appeared during this session.

title: GL render thread dies when cameraObj is released mid-open (null receiver in startCameraViaAvmReflection)
description:
## Problem

Observed live on the head unit on 2026-09-20 at 10:14:17 during a deploy:

    FATAL EXCEPTION: GL-RenderLoop
    java.lang.RuntimeException: java.lang.NullPointerException: null receiver
      at PanoramicCameraGpu.start$lambda$2(PanoramicCameraGpu.kt:384)
    Caused by: java.lang.NullPointerException: null receiver
      at java.lang.reflect.Method.invoke(Native Method)
      at PanoramicCameraGpu.startCameraViaAvmReflection(PanoramicCameraGpu.kt:799)
      at PanoramicCameraGpu.startCamera(PanoramicCameraGpu.kt:691)
      at PanoramicCameraGpu.start$lambda$2(PanoramicCameraGpu.kt:365)

The GL render thread died. The daemon process survived and a later retry brought the camera up
(it has since run stably at 14.6 FPS), so this is recoverable, but the recovery is timing
dependent and the failure takes out the render loop.

File: app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/camera/PanoramicCameraGpu.kt
Function: startCameraViaAvmReflection(cameraId: Int), roughly lines 724-810.

## Root cause

`cameraObj` is a `@Volatile` field (declared around line 138) that other threads null - see the
release path around line 1635, and the camera-yield path that hands the camera to the native BYD
app. `startCameraViaAvmReflection` opens the camera, assigns the handle to that field, and then
re-reads the FIELD at three separate reflective call sites:

    val fpsOk = AvmCameraHelper.setCameraFps(cameraObj, targetFps)          // ~line 787
    mAddSurface.invoke(cameraObj, cameraSurface, cameraSurfaceMode)         // ~line 799
    mStart.invoke(cameraObj)                                                // ~line 807

If another thread nulls `cameraObj` between the open and any of these, `Method.invoke` gets a
null receiver and throws NullPointerException("null receiver"). That propagates to the GL post
lambda, whose catch at line 383-384 logs and rethrows as RuntimeException, which kills the
HandlerThread.

This is NOT a conversion regression. The Java original is identical: it reads the `cameraObj`
field at the same three sites (lines 826, 837, 845 of the original) and rethrows the same way at
lines 421-423. The bug was carried across faithfully.

The existing null guard at line 770 does not cover this: it only runs inside the static-factory
fallback branch, and in any case it checks the field before the window in which the race occurs.

## Fix

Snapshot the handle into a local immediately after the open sequence, fail with a descriptive
message if it was already released, and use the local for all three reflective calls so the
sequence is internally consistent.

After the open block closes (just before the setCameraFps comment), add:

    val cam = cameraObj
        ?: throw RuntimeException("AVMCamera handle was released during open (id=$cameraId)")

Then replace `cameraObj` with `cam` in exactly these three places:

    AvmCameraHelper.setCameraFps(cam, targetFps)
    mAddSurface.invoke(cam, cameraSurface, cameraSurfaceMode)
    mStart.invoke(cam)

## Constraints, do NOT change

- Do NOT change the catch at lines 383-384 that logs and rethrows. That rethrow is what the
  existing retry/recovery path keys on, and it was verified working on the car - the camera
  recovered after this exact crash. Changing it would alter recovery behaviour on a live
  vehicle.
- Do NOT remove the existing `if (cameraObj == null) throw` guard in the static-factory branch.
- Do NOT stop assigning the `cameraObj` field; other code (renderLoop, setupEventCallback, the
  release path) depends on it.
- Do NOT touch the open/attempt-1/attempt-2 logic or the ordering
  open -> setCameraFps -> addPreviewSurface -> startPreview, which the BYD HAL state machine
  requires.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `startCameraViaAvmReflection` reads `cameraObj` once into a local after the open sequence.
- [ ] All three reflective calls (setCameraFps, addPreviewSurface, startPreview) use that local.
- [ ] When the handle was released mid-open, the thrown exception names the situation instead of
      surfacing as "null receiver".
- [ ] The catch/rethrow at lines 383-384 is unchanged.
- [ ] ./gradlew :app:compileDebugJavaWithJavac compiles clean.
- [ ] ./gradlew test koverVerify passes with fresh test-result timestamps.
- [ ] Redeployed to the head unit and the camera pipeline reaches a steady Stats line with a
      non-zero frame count and no FATAL EXCEPTION.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles
and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather
than guessing.
