If the handle was released mid-open it now throws a named exception rather than surfacing as Method.invoke 'null receiver'. The catch/rethrow in the GL post lambda was deliberately left unchanged, since that is what the working retry/recovery path keys on. Verified: compileDebugJavaWithJavac clean, test + koverVerify green with fresh results, and redeployed to the head unit - camera started on the first attempt (Camera started id=0 5120x960), surveillance processing to frame #400+, daemon stable on one PID, 0 FATAL EXCEPTION and 0 'null receiver' in logcat (previous deploy had 1 GL-RenderLoop fatal at startup).

title: Three fields lost their volatile guarantee in the Kotlin conversion (GL watchdog + SD mount state)
description:
## Problem

Three fields were declared `volatile` in Java and lost that guarantee in the Java-to-Kotlin
conversion: the Kotlin declarations have no `@Volatile` annotation. All three are written on one
thread and read on another, so without the annotation the reader thread has no happens-before
edge and may observe a stale value indefinitely.

These compile clean and pass every test, because a missing memory barrier is invisible to
single-threaded JVM unit tests. They are only observable as rare, hard-to-reproduce misbehaviour
on the head unit.

### 1. PanoramicCameraGpu.firstFrameReceived  (most serious)

File: app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/camera/PanoramicCameraGpu.kt line 1897
Current:  `private var firstFrameReceived = false`
Java was: `private volatile boolean firstFrameReceived = false;` (line 184 of the original)

Written from the camera frame-available callback (PanoramicCameraGpu.kt line 1017, alongside
`frameCounter++` and `lastFrameTime`) and from `startWatchdog()` (line 1787).

Read from the watchdog thread (the `Thread({ while (running) ... })` started in `startWatchdog`)
at line 1808 and line 1817, where it selects the GL-thread hang timeout:

    val effectiveTimeout = if (firstFrameReceived && !restartInProgress.get())
        GL_THREAD_TIMEOUT_MS
    else
        GL_THREAD_WARMUP_TIMEOUT_MS

    if (timeSinceHeartbeat > effectiveTimeout) { ...forces a process restart... }

So a stale read directly changes whether the watchdog force-restarts the camera daemon process.
A stale `false` keeps the long warmup timeout forever, so a genuinely hung GL thread is not
killed promptly and the safety mechanism is defeated.

That this is an oversight rather than a decision is clear from the same file: the two other
fields read in that very same watchdog loop, `running` (line 143) and `lastGlThreadHeartbeat`
(line 181), both correctly kept `@Volatile`. `firstFrameReceived` is declared far from them at
the bottom of the file, which is why it was missed. The file has 39 other `@Volatile` fields.

### 2 and 3. StorageManager.isSdCardMountFailedAtBoot and StorageManager.sdCardMountErrorMessage

File: app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/storage/StorageManager.kt lines 174 and 179
Current:
    var isSdCardMountFailedAtBoot: Boolean = false
        private set
    var sdCardMountErrorMessage: String? = null
        private set

Java was (lines 900-901 of the original):
    private volatile boolean sdCardMountFailedAtBoot = false;
    private volatile String sdCardMountErrorMessage = null;

Written from the boot-time storage logic (StorageManager.kt lines 900-901 and 923-924) and from
the SD watchdog at lines 2242-2244, which runs on a scheduled executor thread.

Read from a different thread entirely: QualitySettingsApiHandler.kt lines 170-171, which runs on
an HTTP server request thread:

    response.put("sdCardMountFailed", storage.isSdCardMountFailedAtBoot)
    response.put("sdCardMountError", storage.sdCardMountErrorMessage)

Consequence: the settings UI can keep reporting an SD-card mount failure after the watchdog has
remounted the card and cleared the flag, or fail to report a real failure.

## Fix

Add `@Volatile` to all three declarations, restoring exactly the Java semantics. No other change.

    // PanoramicCameraGpu.kt line 1897
    @Volatile private var firstFrameReceived = false

    // StorageManager.kt lines 174 and 179
    @Volatile
    var isSdCardMountFailedAtBoot: Boolean = false
        private set

    @Volatile
    var sdCardMountErrorMessage: String? = null
        private set

Note: `@Volatile` is legal on a `var` with a `private set`; it applies to the backing field.

## Constraints, do NOT change

- Do not change the types, names, visibility, or the `private set` on the StorageManager
  properties, they are read by QualitySettingsApiHandler.
- Do not convert these to AtomicBoolean/AtomicReference, `volatile` is what the Java had and is
  sufficient, these are plain writes and reads with no compare-and-set.
- Do not add synchronisation anywhere, it is not needed and would risk deadlock in the watchdog.
- Do not "tidy" the other @Volatile fields in either file.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] PanoramicCameraGpu.firstFrameReceived is annotated `@Volatile`.
- [ ] StorageManager.isSdCardMountFailedAtBoot is annotated `@Volatile`.
- [ ] StorageManager.sdCardMountErrorMessage is annotated `@Volatile`.
- [ ] No other semantic change in either file.
- [ ] ./gradlew :app:compileDebugJavaWithJavac compiles clean.
- [ ] ./gradlew test koverVerify passes with fresh test-result timestamps.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles
and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather
than guessing.
close_reason: Fixed: added @Volatile to PanoramicCameraGpu.firstFrameReceived, StorageManager.isSdCardMountFailedAtBoot and StorageManager.sdCardMountErrorMessage, restoring the volatile semantics the Java originals had. No other change. Verified: compileDebugJavaWithJavac clean, test + koverVerify green with fresh results.

title: Thumbnails 404: /thumb/ is routed to handleWithRange but never handled there
description: ## The defect Every thumbnail request 404s. Nothing renders a hero image: not the events list, not the recordings grid, not the image in a Web Push notification banner. HttpServer.routeToHandlers sends both prefixes to the same method: if (path.startsWith("/video/") || path.startsWith("/thumb/")) { return RecordingsApiHandler.handleWithRange(method, path, body, rangeHeader, ifNoneMatchHeader, out); } but handleWithRange only ever matches "/video/": if (path.startsWith("/video/")) { ... streamVideo ...; return true; } return false; So a "/thumb/" request returns false, falls through the whole else-if chain in handleClient, and ends at the static-file 404. RecordingsApiHandler.serveThumbnail — along with generateThumbnail, the thumbExecutor, the pendingThumbs set, the cache directory, the hero-JPEG and per-actor-JPEG lookups, and the 202-Accepted "generating" response — is unreachable dead code. ## Root cause BladeWatch-6mnq removed the REST JSON dispatch from this class. The "/thumb/" branch lived in that dispatch, and went with it. The comment left behind in handleWithRange says "Only /video/ and /thumb/ reach here", and HttpServer's comment says "/thumb/* , additionally auth'd by a signed ?t= token" — both describe the intended behaviour, which is what makes this easy to miss on review: everything reads as though it still works. AuthMiddleware Tier 0.5 still validates the signed thumb token for "/thumb/" paths, so the auth half of the feature survived; only the serving half was dropped. ## Fix Restore the dispatch in handleWithRange: if (path.startsWith("/thumb/")) { serveThumbnail(out, path.substring(7)); return true; } ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] handleWithRange dispatches "/thumb/" to serveThumbnail and returns true. - [ ] A guard test pins that BOTH prefixes HttpServer routes to handleWithRange are actually handled by it, so a future prefix removal fails instead of silently 404ing. The test must be mutation-checked: delete the "/thumb/" branch and confirm it fails. - [ ] serveThumbnail, generateThumbnail, thumbExecutor and pendingThumbs are reachable again -- no dead code left behind either way. - [ ] All seven quality gates pass. - [ ] Verified on the head unit: an event thumbnail renders in the events list, and a Web Push notification arrives with its hero image. Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
close_reason:
Fixed while converting RecordingsApiHandler to Kotlin (BladeWatch-9rut), which is how the dead
serveThumbnail was noticed in the first place.

handleWithRange now dispatches both prefixes HttpServer routes to it:

    if (path.startsWith("/video/")) { streamVideo(...); return true }
    if (path.startsWith("/thumb/")) { serveThumbnail(out, path.substring(7)); return true }

serveThumbnail, generateThumbnail, the thumbExecutor and the pendingThumbs set are reachable
again. Nothing was deleted: the whole chain was intact, just unrouted.

New guard: RecordingsRouteCoverageTest reads BOTH files as source text, extracts the prefixes from
the actual routing condition in HttpServer (not a hardcoded list, so a third prefix would be
covered automatically), and asserts each one is handled inside handleWithRange. It also asserts it
found at least two prefixes, so a guard that stops reading HttpServer fails loudly instead of
passing vacuously.

Mutation-checked: deleting the "/thumb/" branch failed
everyPrefixRoutedToHandleWithRangeIsHandledThere. Reverted.

Gates: "./gradlew test koverVerify" green.

NOT verified on the car. The head unit is still running 1.3.1.0 and nothing from this session has
been deployed, so the two on-device acceptance criteria — a thumbnail rendering in the events list
and a Web Push notification arriving with its hero image — remain unchecked. Worth doing on the
next deploy, because this is precisely the kind of fix whose failure mode is invisible in a unit
test.

title: SECURITY: the vehicle action-token second factor is enforced only on /api/vehicle/, a path no client uses
description:
## The finding

The vehicle-actuation second factor (uy93.5) is enforced **only on a path no client uses**, and
has been inert for every real client since the ConnectRPC migration.

`HttpServer` gates it like this:

    if (method.equals("POST")
            && vehicleActionPathOnly.startsWith("/api/vehicle/")
            && !vehicleActionPathOnly.equals("/api/vehicle/action-token")
            && !client.getInetAddress().isLoopbackAddress()) {
        ... VehicleActionToken.validate(...) or 403
    }

Every first-party vehicle command goes to `/bladewatch.v1.VehicleService/{SetClimate, MoveWindow,
Trunk, SetSeat, SetLights, SetAdas, SetChargeCap, SetScreen, SetMediaVolume, StartGps, StopGps}`.
**None of those paths starts with `/api/vehicle/`**, so the gate never fires for them. The token
is also only issuable over `GET /api/vehicle/action-token` — there is no RPC for it.

Net effect: from a non-loopback client (i.e. over the Tor tunnel, which is the whole threat model
the second factor was added for), a session JWT alone is sufficient to actuate the car. The
second factor adds nothing.

This is **pre-existing**, not introduced by BladeWatch-6mnq. That work removed the dead REST
route and so made the gate unreachable rather than merely ineffective, which is how it surfaced.

## Why it was not obvious

The control looks present and correct where it is written, and `VehicleActionToken` has its own
tests. Nothing points out that the predicate it hangs on stopped matching real traffic when the
clients moved to Connect. A guard keyed on a path that no longer exists is worse than no guard,
because the reader believes it.

## The decision this needs (do NOT skip it)

Restoring enforcement is not a like-for-like change — it alters the client contract:

- **(a) Port the second factor to Connect.** Enforce on mutating `VehicleService` methods from
  non-loopback callers, and add an issue RPC to replace `GET /api/vehicle/action-token`. Every
  Connect client (Angular SPA, and the Flutter app if it ever actuates from non-loopback) must
  then fetch a token and send `X-Vehicle-Action-Token` with each command. Check first whether
  the Angular Connect client can set a per-call header — if it cannot, that is the real work.
- **(b) Accept a JWT as sufficient** and delete `VehicleActionToken` and its issue endpoint
  outright, recording that the tunnel threat model is covered by the JWT alone.

Do not leave it in the current state, where the control exists in the codebase and protects
nothing. Whichever is chosen, say so in `docs/ipc-auth-and-secrets.md`.

## Constraints — do NOT change

- Do not widen the loopback exemption.
- Do not weaken `VehicleActionToken`'s signature or window while deciding.
- **BYD vehicle control actuates the real car.** Test conservatively; do not exercise
  actuation commands against a live vehicle to verify a gate.
- Do not re-add a REST route to make the old gate work again (BladeWatch-6mnq).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A recorded decision, (a) or (b), before code changes.
- [ ] If (a): a non-loopback Connect vehicle command WITHOUT a valid action token is refused,
      covered by a test, and the mutation removing the check fails that test.
- [ ] If (a): the loopback exemption still works, so the in-car UI is unaffected.
- [ ] If (b): `VehicleActionToken` and its issue endpoint are gone, not left dead.
- [ ] `docs/ipc-auth-and-secrets.md` states which vehicle commands require what, and from where.
- [ ] A guard pins that the enforcement predicate matches the paths clients actually use, so
      this cannot silently decay again.
- [ ] `./gradlew test koverVerify` passes.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles
and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather
than guessing.
close_reason: Done, direction (a) restore on Connect, per the developer decision. Feasibility question answered first, as promised: the Angular Connect client CAN set a per-call header - auth.interceptor.ts already does req.header.set - so an interceptor was viable and no client rewrite was needed. New VehicleActionGate owns which methods actuate; the gate in HttpServer is keyed on the Connect path instead of the dead /api/vehicle/ prefix, and still exempts loopback so the in-car UI is unaffected. New VehicleService.IssueActionToken replaces the deleted REST issuer and is itself never gated - you cannot need a token to get a token. Web side: vehicle-action.interceptor.ts attaches X-Vehicle-Action-Token to actuating commands only, caches the token until a second before expiry, and collapses concurrent commands onto one issue call so tapping two controls does not mint two tokens and race them; when issuing fails it sends the command WITHOUT a token and lets the server refuse, because failing open in the client would defeat the control. It uses a plain fetch rather than the typed client deliberately - running inside an interceptor, going back through the same transport would re-enter the chain, and relying on IssueActionToken not being in the ACTUATING list is a trap for whoever next edits that list. The anti-decay guard the issue asked for is VehicleActionGateTest.everyVehicleCommandIsClassified: it scans the registered VehicleService RPCs and fails on any that is neither gated nor explicitly declared read-only, so a new command cannot be added without someone deciding which it is - precisely the omission that made uy93.5 inert. Mutation-checked on both sides: ungating SetClimate or Trunk fails the classification guard and the direct test; stubbing the interceptor's predicate to false fails three web tests. docs/ipc-auth-and-secrets.md now states which commands need what and from where. NOT verified on the car, and deliberately so - I did not exercise actuation commands against a live vehicle to test a gate.

title: LocationSidecarService fails to start on the head unit (exit 255, app=null) so trips record no GPS path
description:
## What was measured (not inferred)

On the head unit, 2026-09-19, installed build versionName 1.3.1.0:

    $ am start-foreground-service -n net.bladewatch.app/.services.LocationSidecarService 2>&1
    Starting service: Intent { cmp=net.bladewatch.app/.services.LocationSidecarService }
    Error: Not found; no service started.
    EXIT=255

    $ dumpsys activity services net.bladewatch.app
    * ServiceRecord{7123438 u0 net.bladewatch.app/.services.LocationSidecarService}
        app=null

So: the component **does** resolve — ActivityManager holds a `ServiceRecord` for it — but there
is no process behind it (`app=null`), and every attempt to start it fails with exit 255.

`ServiceLauncher.isLocationSidecarRunning` tests exactly `app=null` and therefore correctly
reports the service as not running. The declaration is present in
`app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:341` and is unchanged from `main`, so this is not a missing
manifest entry.

## Why it matters

`SentryDaemon.restartLocationService` runs this command on its location-monitor path. It is
failing every time it runs. BladeWatch-boat made that failure visible (the WARN now fires
correctly — `ShellResultClassifier.isFailure` matches "Error"), and BladeWatch-ieva fixed the
app-side classification of the same command, but **neither addresses why the start fails.**

Without the sidecar there is no GPS push to the token-gated localhost IPC, so trips record a
single static point with no path — see the comment above the manifest declaration.

## What NOT to assume

The cause has NOT been established. Do not start from a guess. Candidates worth eliminating, in
order of cheapness:

- The package being in a stopped state (`ssc_skip` / BYD's force-stop behaviour is known on this
  head unit — see BladeWatch-5rew).
- `android:foregroundServiceType="location|dataSync"` on API 29 and whether the app holds the
  runtime location permission it implies. A foreground service whose type demands a permission
  the app lacks is refused.
- A stale `ServiceRecord` left by a crash, which a reinstall would clear.
- The installed 1.3.1.0 APK differing from the current tree in ways beyond the manifest.

## What to do

1. Reproduce the three commands above and record the exact output before changing anything.
2. Check `logcat` for an ActivityManager line at the moment of the failed start — that is where
   the real reason is printed, not in the `am` output.
3. Check whether `ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION` / `ACCESS_BACKGROUND_LOCATION` are granted at the app
   UID (10073), and whether the foreground service type requires one that is not.
4. Only then change code. If the fix turns out to be a reinstall, say so and close it as such
   rather than inventing a code change.

## Constraints — do NOT change

- Do not remove or weaken `android:foregroundServiceType` to make the start succeed. That
  attribute is load-bearing on API 29+.
- Do not widen the IPC peer-UID gate or export anything further.
- Do not change `ShellResultClassifier` or the call sites fixed in BladeWatch-boat/ieva; they
  are correctly reporting this failure, which is how it was found.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The actual reason is identified from logcat or permission state, and written on this issue
      with the evidence quoted.
- [ ] The service starts: `am start-foreground-service` exits 0, and
      `dumpsys activity services` shows a non-null `app=`.
- [ ] A trip recorded afterwards has more than one GPS point.
- [ ] If the resolution is operational (a reinstall) rather than a code change, that is stated
      explicitly and no speculative code change is made.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles
and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather
than guessing.
close_reason: Root cause established from logcat, not guessed. BYD's ssc_skip ignores a shell-UID service start when the target app UID is not already running: 'ssc_skip startServiceLocked 2000 want to start 10073 ... UID 10073 is not running ... ignored !!!'. ActivityManager surfaces that as 'Error: Not found; no service started.' with exit 255, which reads like a missing component and is why it went undiagnosed - the component resolves fine and dumpsys showed a ServiceRecord with app=null. This project already knew ssc_skip for suppressing BROADCASTS (BladeWatch-5rew); it applies the same rule to service starts. None of the candidate causes I listed was right: not a stopped-package state as such, not the foregroundServiceType permission, not a stale ServiceRecord, not a stale APK. Proved the fix on the live car before writing any code: 'am start -n net.bladewatch.app/.ui.MainActivity' brought UID 10073 up, after which the identical service-start command exited 0 and dumpsys went from app=null to app=ProcessRecord{...8778}. SentryDaemon.restartLocationService now does this automatically, gated on the new pure needsServiceHostWake so a live host is not restarted. MainActivity is a bootstrap that calls moveTaskToBack(true) immediately, so nothing appears on screen. ServiceLauncher needs no change - it runs inside the app process, so the UID is already up and the rule does not bite. Three tests written first using the verbatim device output; mutation making shell noise read as a live PID fails shellNoiseIsNotMistakenForAPid. Documented in docs/daemons-and-processes.md. Incidental observation while on the device: two sentry_daemon processes were running (PIDs 9197 and 9347), confirming BladeWatch-f0y3 is still live there because the singleton-lock fix has not been deployed yet.

title: getBatteryRemainPowerKwh falls back to the raw mirrored channel when nominal capacity is unknown, undoing the x4lf fix
description:
## Problem / context

`VehicleDataMonitor.getBatteryRemainPowerKwh()`
(`app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/monitor/VehicleDataMonitor.kt`, near line 276)
ends with:

    // No nominal capacity: use the raw BMS value if available.
    if (rawKwh > 0) return rawKwh

BladeWatch-x4lf established that `remainKwh` on this car mirrors SoC percent 1:1 rather than
reporting energy (963 SoC-history rows, 2026-09-19: soc=73/remain=72.9, soc=77/remain=77.0,
soc=79/remain=78.8), and made `NominalCapacityResolver.resolve` return `0.0` — an honest
"unknown" — rather than dividing that mirror into a fake ~100 kWh.

**This fallback undoes that.** `nominal == 0.0` is precisely the new "unknown" outcome, and the
branch responds by returning the raw mirrored value as though it were energy. The honest unknown
is converted straight back into the ~5.4x-wrong number the fix exists to eliminate.

## When it actually fires

Not on the test car in steady state: `modelId` is `seal5-dmi-premium`, the catalogue answers
18.3 kWh, so `nominal > 0` and this branch is skipped. It fires when the catalogue does not
answer:

- An unlisted or unset `vehicle.modelId`.
- **Early boot.** The catalogue is read from `/data/local/tmp/web/shared/models/manifest.json`,
  which is extracted web assets. Before extraction the lookup returns 0, so any caller in that
  window gets the mirrored value — including `SocHistoryDatabase.recordAccEvent`, which records
  ACC ON/OFF events and was only just routed through this accessor (BladeWatch-hdt7).

## What to do

1. Read `getBatteryRemainPowerKwh()` in full, then `NominalCapacityResolver.kt` and its test.
2. Write the failing test FIRST, over a pure function, using the verbatim device pairs above.
   Do not test through `VehicleDataMonitor`: it is a private-constructor singleton over live BYD
   data and cannot be built on the JVM. Follow the pattern already used for this exact
   constraint — `NominalCapacityResolver`, `StorageManager.selectFilesToDelete`.
3. Make the no-nominal fallback refuse a reading that looks like a SoC mirror, reusing
   `NominalCapacityResolver.looksLikeSocMirror` rather than writing a second copy of the rule.
   Unknown must stay `0.0`.
4. Check every caller of `getBatteryRemainPowerKwh()` handles `0.0` as "unknown" and does not
   divide by it or display it as a real reading. There are five:
   `SocHistoryDatabase` (3), `TripDetector` (2).

## Constraints — do NOT change

- Do not change the `nominal > 0 && soc > 0` branch: the ratio validation and the PHEV/BEV split
  in it are separate behaviour with their own history.
- Do not duplicate the mirror rule. One definition, in `NominalCapacityResolver`.
- Do not make the resolver impure — no file, config or singleton access.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A test written BEFORE the fix fails for the right reason.
- [ ] With no nominal capacity and a mirrored reading, the result is `0.0`, not the raw value.
- [ ] With no nominal capacity and a genuine energy reading, the raw value is still returned —
      no regression for cars where the channel is honest.
- [ ] Mutation check: remove the new guard, confirm the new test fails, revert.
- [ ] Every caller's handling of `0.0` is checked and the finding stated in the close reason.
- [ ] `./gradlew test koverVerify` passes from the repo root.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles
and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather
than guessing.
close_reason: Fixed. The no-nominal fallback in getBatteryRemainPowerKwh now goes through the new pure NominalCapacityResolver.trustworthyRemainKwh(rawKwh, soc), which returns 0.0 for a reading that mirrors SoC and the raw value otherwise, so an honest channel does not regress. Tests written first, failing on an unresolved reference then on the value; mutation removing the mirror guard fails exactly the new test. Caller audit as required: all five callers - SocHistoryDatabase 408/820/1068, TripDetector 189/296 - plus the recordAccEvent site added in hdt7 already guard on greater-than-zero, and none divides by it. Checked and deliberately not changed: SOC_HISTORY.remaining_kwh stores 0 rather than NULL for unknown, but 0 is that table's established no-data sentinel and both of its readers already treat it that way (the AVG CASE at line 647 and the fixStaleRemainingKwh WHERE clause). The never-a-fake-zero policy belongs to the nullable ACC_EVENTS column and is honoured there. Not yet verified on the car.

title: NominalCapacityResolver trusts chargingCapacityKwh unconditionally, but that field is a charging-session figure
description:
## Problem / context

`NominalCapacityResolver.resolve` (added in BladeWatch-x4lf,
`app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/monitor/NominalCapacityResolver.kt:70`) gives
UNCONDITIONAL top priority to `chargingCapacityKwh`:

    if (!chargingCapacityKwh.isNaN() && chargingCapacityKwh > 0) return chargingCapacityKwh

Its doc comment calls that "the SDK's own per-vehicle figure, which reflects this car's actual
battery option". **That assumption was never verified, and the codebase says otherwise.**

`chargingCapacityKwh` has exactly two writers, both in
`app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/byd/BydDataCollector.java`:

- Line 1428, polled: `chargingDevice.getChargingCapacity()`, accepted on `capKwh > 0` alone.
  It sits in a block of *charger session* getters — `getChargingType`, `getChargingPercent`,
  gun state, VTOL detection — not pack specification.
- Line 3427, the `onChargingCapacityChanged` callback, accepted on `0 < cap < 200` alone. The
  comment immediately above it (line 3419) describes the event as **"purely diagnostic for
  charging session size"**.

So the highest-priority input to pack capacity is a field this codebase documents as a charging
*session* figure, accepted with no sanity check of any kind.

This is the same failure mode BladeWatch-x4lf fixed: trusting a plausibly-named channel without
checking it against a known-good reference. It was not caught because the callback only fires
while charging, and the measurement that found x4lf was taken over a drive.

## Impact

`chargingCapacityKwh` is `NaN` on the test car today, so the catalogue value (18.3 kWh for
`seal5-dmi-premium`) is in use and correct. On the next AC charge, if `getChargingCapacity()`
returns session energy (say 6.5) or a percentage, nominal capacity silently becomes that number,
**overriding the catalogue value that is actually right**, and every trip's energy, cost and
efficiency is wrong again — plus `BydDataCollector.decideDrivetrain` Tier 0 gets a wrong scale.

## What to do

1. Read `NominalCapacityResolver.kt` and its test in full first.
2. Write the failing test FIRST: a `chargingCapacityKwh` that contradicts a known catalogue
   value must NOT win. Use realistic numbers — catalogue 18.3 with an SDK value of 6.5
   (a part-charged session) and of 73.0 (a percentage).
3. Change `resolve` so the SDK value is accepted over the catalogue only when the two are
   compatible. Keep the original intent: a per-vehicle figure SHOULD outrank a per-trim
   constant, because a trim can ship more than one battery option. Only refuse a value that
   contradicts the trim by more than a battery option plausibly could.
4. When there is NO catalogue value (`catalogueKwh <= 0`, an unlisted trim), keep today's
   behaviour exactly — accept the SDK value. Do not regress unlisted models.
5. Fix the doc comment on priority 1 so it no longer claims something unverified. Say what is
   actually known about the field, including that its two writers are unvalidated and that one
   of them is documented as a session figure.
6. Update the "Where nominal pack capacity comes from" section of `docs/byd-integrations.md` to
   match.
7. Name the tolerance as a constant with a comment stating what it is and when to revisit it.
   It is a judgement call, not a measured value, and should be labelled as such.

## Constraints — do NOT change

- Do not change `BydDataCollector`'s collection logic in this issue. The unvalidated writers are
  tracked separately; fixing them here widens a bug fix into a BYD-collection refactor.
- Do not remove the catalogue or the SoC-mirror rejection — both are verified against device data.
- Do not make `resolve` read files, config, or any singleton. It is pure and must stay pure.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A test written BEFORE the fix fails for the right reason, and names the scenario.
- [ ] An SDK value that contradicts a known catalogue value loses to the catalogue.
- [ ] An SDK value compatible with the catalogue still wins (per-vehicle beats per-trim).
- [ ] With no catalogue value, behaviour is byte-identical to today.
- [ ] Mutation check: remove the new guard, confirm the new test fails, revert.
- [ ] Priority-1 doc comment no longer asserts anything unverified.
- [ ] `docs/byd-integrations.md` matches the code.
- [ ] `./gradlew test koverVerify` passes from the repo root.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles
and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather
than guessing.
close_reason: Fixed. resolve() no longer trusts chargingCapacityKwh unconditionally: it is accepted over the catalogue only when agreesWithCatalogue() holds (CATALOGUE_AGREEMENT_TOLERANCE = 0.5, named and marked as a judgement call rather than a measurement). With no catalogue entry, behaviour is unchanged, so unlisted trims do not regress. Test written first and failed for the right reason (expected 18.3 but was 6.5); mutation check restoring the unconditional return fails exactly the new test. An existing test asserted that an SDK value of 60.0 beat a catalogue of 18.3 -- that pair is a contradiction, not a battery option, so it was pinning this very defect as though it were the requirement; retargeted to 19.5 vs 18.3 with a comment saying so. Not yet verified on the car: chargingCapacityKwh is NaN on this head unit today, so the guard only matters from the next AC charge onward.

title: Trip energy, cost and efficiency inflated ~5.2x - nominal pack capacity resolves to 95 kWh on an 18.3 kWh PHEV
description:
## Problem

Every trip's energy, cost and efficiency figures are inflated by roughly 5.2x, because the
nominal pack capacity used for the SoC-to-kWh conversion resolves to ~95 kWh on a car whose
traction battery is ~18.3 kWh. The efficiency score is pinned at 0 as a direct consequence.

This is the root cause of the "trips show 0% efficiency" symptom reported earlier. That was
previously addressed on the Flutter side by reading `avgEfficiencyScore` instead of
`avgEfficiency` - a real fix for a real client-side bug, but it treats a symptom: the server's
`efficiencyScore` is itself 0, so the screen still shows 0%.

## Evidence (measured on the head unit, 2026-09-19)

Configured vehicle: `vehicle.modelId = "seal5-dmi-premium"` - a Seal 5 DM-i, a PHEV. This
codebase already names 18.3 kWh as the PHEV pack value (see the one-time migration comment in
`CameraDaemon`, "60 kWh BEV default instead of 18.3 kWh PHEV").

Trip 193 (a real drive): `socStart=77`, `socEnd=71` (6%), `distanceKm=8.8829984664917`,
daemon-reported `energyPerKm=0.6416752338409424`.

    0.6416752 kWh/km x 8.8829985 km / 0.06  =  95.0 kWh implied nominal

For comparison at the same SoC delta and distance:

    nominal  18.3 kWh -> 0.124 kWh/km   (plausible for this car)
    nominal  95.0 kWh -> 0.642 kWh/km   (what the daemon reports)

Efficiency score across the 9 most recent trips - note the inverse relationship:

    id=193 dist=8.88  eff=0   energyPerKm=0.642
    id=161 dist=11.00 eff=0   energyPerKm=0.545
    id=129 dist=1.00  eff=0   energyPerKm=1.400
    id=98  dist=12.00 eff=0   energyPerKm=0.692
    id=66  dist=10.00 eff=0   energyPerKm=0.640
    id=34  dist=10.00 eff=50  energyPerKm=0        <-- the ONLY nonzero score is the trip with NO energy data

Weekly rollup (`/api/trips/summary`) - every other sub-score computes normally, only efficiency
is 0, which rules out "no data":

    avgAnticipation=96  avgSmoothness=66  avgSpeedDiscipline=88  avgConsistency=56
    avgEfficiencyScore=0
    totalEnergyKwh=33.6  totalCost=294.40  avgEnergyPerKm=0.720  (53.88 km that week)

At a correct 18.3 kWh nominal those totals would be roughly 6.5 kWh and ~57 in currency.

## Where it comes from

`TripAnalyticsManager.kt` ~line 423 takes the capacity from
`VehicleDataMonitor.getNominalCapacityKwh()` and passes it to `resolveTripEnergyKwh`, which does
`((socStart - socEnd) / 100.0) * nominalKwh` for the SoC fallback tier.

`VehicleDataMonitor.getNominalCapacityKwh()` (~line 293) has two branches:

```kotlin
if (!vd.chargingCapacityKwh.isNaN() && vd.chargingCapacityKwh > 0) return vd.chargingCapacityKwh
val soc = ...; val rawKwh = vd.remainKwh
if (rawKwh > 0 && soc > 5) return rawKwh / (soc / 100.0)
return 0.0
```

**Not yet determined: which branch yields 95.** Either `chargingCapacityKwh` reports something
that is not a usable traction-pack capacity (a DC charge-power rating in kW, or a BEV-family
constant), or `remainKwh` is on a different scale than `socPercent` so the division inflates.
The HTTP surface does not expose these raw fields, so **step one is to log both raw values on
device and identify the branch before changing anything.** Do not guess.

## Fix

1. Instrument first: log `vd.chargingCapacityKwh`, `vd.remainKwh`, `vd.socPercent` and the
   returned nominal, and read them on the head unit. Confirm which branch produces 95.
2. Correct that branch. If `chargingCapacityKwh` is not a traction-pack capacity on a PHEV, stop
   using it for this purpose rather than scaling it.
3. Make the scorer honest about bad input: an implied nominal wildly outside a plausible range
   for the configured model should produce "unknown", not a confidently wrong 0. A 0 score that
   means "we could not compute this" is indistinguishable from "you drove terribly".

## Constraints

- Do NOT hardcode 18.3 for this model. The value must come from the vehicle or from a model
  catalogue; per-trim invented constants are what `docs/architecture.md` already warns against.
- Do NOT "fix" this by scaling `energyPerKm` at the display layer. The stored trip data is wrong;
  correcting it in Flutter would leave the daemon, the web UI and the cost figures disagreeing.
- Do NOT change `resolveTripEnergyKwh`'s tier ordering - the kWh channel must still win over the
  SoC fallback. Only the capacity fed into the fallback is in question.
- Do NOT retroactively rewrite stored trips without asking; historical trips were recorded under
  the wrong constant and a migration is a separate decision (one already exists in `CameraDaemon`
  for an earlier instance of this same class of bug - read it before writing another).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The branch of `getNominalCapacityKwh()` producing ~95 kWh is identified and documented in
      the close reason with the observed raw values.
- [ ] On this car, a trip with a 6% SoC drop over ~8.9 km reports roughly 0.12 kWh/km, not 0.64.
- [ ] `efficiencyScore` is nonzero and plausible for a normal drive.
- [ ] When capacity cannot be resolved, efficiency reports as unknown rather than 0.
- [ ] JVM unit tests cover `resolveTripEnergyKwh` at both the correct and the absent-capacity
      paths, using the real observed values above as inputs.
- [ ] Mutation check: revert the fix, confirm the new test fails for the stated reason, re-apply,
      confirm it passes.
- [ ] `./gradlew test koverVerify` is BUILD SUCCESSFUL.

Do not make mistakes. Read `TripAnalyticsManager.resolveTripEnergyKwh`,
`VehicleDataMonitor.getNominalCapacityKwh` and `CameraDaemon`'s existing PHEV migration in full
before editing. Measure on the device before changing the calculation. If anything is ambiguous,
stop and ask rather than guessing.
close_reason:
Fixed, and the root cause was measured rather than guessed - the issue's own first instruction.

Measurement without a redeploy: pulled the device's H2 SoC-history database (963 rows) and queried it locally with the project's own h2 jar. The (soc, remaining_kwh) pairs are soc=73/remain=72.9, soc=77/remain=77.0, soc=79/remain=78.8 - remainKwh tracks soc 1:1. It is not energy, it is a percentage. So remainKwh/(soc/100) yields ~100 for ANY pack, which reads as a plausible BEV capacity, which is why nothing downstream ever flagged it. That is branch 2 of getNominalCapacityKwh; branch 1 (chargingCapacityKwh) is NaN on this car, consistent with the ~100 figure the trip arithmetic implied.

Also found: models/manifest.json already carries nominalKwh per trim, and seal5-dmi-premium is 18.3 - exactly the value the arithmetic predicted. ModelsApiHandler.nominalKwhForSelectedModel() already existed to read it, with a doc comment saying "Used by SohEstimator as a capacity hint", and had ZERO callers. The authoritative source was present and simply never consulted. That is the third written-but-unwired function found in this codebase, after RecordingPriority.migrateDefault and CameraProfileResolver.

Fix: new pure NominalCapacityResolver with priority SDK capacity, then model catalogue, then the derived value - and the derived value is now rejected when looksLikeSocMirror() sees the kWh channel tracking SoC within 2 points. VehicleDataMonitor.getNominalCapacityKwh() delegates to it and now consults the catalogue. Unknown returns 0.0 rather than a fabricated number; inventing a capacity to avoid an empty figure is what produced the defect.

A genuine ~100 kWh pack would also trip the mirror guard. That is deliberate and documented: one honest "unknown" costs less than silently corrupting every trip the owner records.

Seven tests, including the real measured pairs verbatim from the device. Mutation-checked both branches: removing the mirror guard fails "the mirrored channel is rejected rather than divided into a fake 100 kWh"; ignoring the catalogue fails "the model catalogue answers when the SDK capacity is absent".

Not done, deliberately: historical trips still hold the inflated figures. The issue says a migration is a separate decision and one already exists in CameraDaemon for an earlier instance of this same class of bug. Needs the developer's call.

Not yet verified on the car - this is a build-and-deploy away, and the acceptance criterion about a 6% SoC drop reporting ~0.12 kWh/km should be checked on the next drive.

title: RecordingPriority.migrateDefault is never called, so upgrades silently cap segments to 1 minute
description:
## Problem

`RecordingPriority.migrateDefault` was written, documented and unit-tested, but is never called
from production code. As a result the upgrade-safety behaviour it exists to provide does not
happen, and every EXISTING install silently has its recording segment length capped to 1 minute
on upgrade.

File: `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/recording/RecordingPriority.kt`

```kotlin
/**
 * New-install default is RELIABILITY; an existing config that already had a
 * `recording` section before this key existed migrates to PERFORMANCE, which is a
 * pure passthrough -- i.e. today's actual behaviour, not an approximation of it.
 */
@JvmStatic
fun migrateDefault(hadPriorRecordingConfig: Boolean): RecordingPriority =
    if (hadPriorRecordingConfig) PERFORMANCE else RELIABILITY
```

Nothing calls it. Both production read sites go straight to `fromConfigValue`, which falls back
to RELIABILITY for a missing value:

- `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/surveillance/HardwareEventRecorderGpu.java`
  in `loadSegmentDurationMs()`:
  `RecordingPriority.fromConfigValue(rec.optString("priority", null))`
- `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/QualitySettingsApiHandler.java`
  around line 645, for the settings GET response.

`UnifiedConfigManager.getRecording()` returns the persisted `recording` section, or an empty
`JSONObject` when there is none. On an existing install that section exists and holds the
owner's `segmentMinutes`, but has no `priority` key yet, so `optString("priority", null)`
returns null, `fromConfigValue(null)` throws internally and returns RELIABILITY, and
`effectiveSegmentMinutes` caps the segment to 1 minute.

## Failure scenario

An owner running a previous build with Recording Limit set to 10 minutes upgrades. Their config
already has `recording.segmentMinutes = 10` and no `recording.priority`. After the upgrade every
clip rotates at 1 minute instead of 10. Nothing in the UI changed, they did not ask for it, and
the settings screen reports RELIABILITY as though they had chosen it. That is precisely the
outcome `migrateDefault`'s doc comment says must not happen.

## Fix

Give both read sites one shared resolution point that consults `migrateDefault` when the
`priority` key is absent, rather than duplicating the decision. Suggested shape, on
`RecordingPriority`'s companion:

```kotlin
/**
 * Effective priority for a persisted `recording` config section: the explicit "priority"
 * value when present, otherwise [migrateDefault] keyed on whether that section already
 * existed. Going straight to [fromConfigValue] instead silently caps an existing install's
 * segment length, because a missing value falls back to RELIABILITY.
 */
@JvmStatic
fun resolve(recordingSection: JSONObject?): RecordingPriority {
    val raw = recordingSection?.optString("priority", null)
    if (!raw.isNullOrEmpty()) return fromConfigValue(raw)
    return migrateDefault(recordingSection != null && recordingSection.length() > 0)
}
```

Then change both call sites to `RecordingPriority.resolve(rec)`.

Note `JSONObject.optString(key, null)` returns null for an absent key but an EMPTY STRING is
also possible from a hand-edited config — handle both, as the sketch above does.

## Constraints

- Do NOT change `effectiveSegmentMinutes`, `RELIABILITY_CAP_MINUTES`, or the
  `fromConfigValue` fallback to RELIABILITY. That fallback is correct for an explicitly
  present but unrecognised value; the bug is only about an ABSENT value.
- Do NOT change what a NEW install gets — a config with no `recording` section at all must
  still resolve to RELIABILITY.
- Do NOT change the wire/JSON key names (`recording.priority`, `recordingPriority`).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A config section with `segmentMinutes` present and no `priority` resolves to PERFORMANCE
      (existing install, behaviour unchanged by the upgrade).
- [ ] An absent/empty `recording` section resolves to RELIABILITY (new install).
- [ ] An explicit `"priority": "RELIABILITY"` still resolves to RELIABILITY, and an explicit
      unrecognised value still falls back to RELIABILITY.
- [ ] Both `HardwareEventRecorderGpu.loadSegmentDurationMs` and
      `QualitySettingsApiHandler`'s GET path use the shared resolution, so they cannot disagree.
- [ ] `migrateDefault` has at least one production caller.
- [ ] Tests added to `app/src/test/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/recording/RecordingPriorityTest.kt`.
- [ ] Mutation check: revert the fix, confirm the new test fails for the stated reason,
      re-apply, confirm it passes.
- [ ] `./gradlew test koverVerify` is BUILD SUCCESSFUL.

Do not make mistakes. Read `RecordingPriority.kt`, `HardwareEventRecorderGpu.loadSegmentDurationMs`
and `UnifiedConfigManager.getRecording` in full before editing. Verify the build compiles and all
acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than
guessing.
close_reason:
Closing as invalid — see the correction comment. The upgrade regression described here does not occur: UnifiedConfigManager.migrateConfig back-fills recording.priority = PERFORMANCE for any config predating the key, persisted and marker-gated, on every loadConfig(). My fix has been fully reverted.

The one real residue, dead code, is handled: migrateDefault (which had no production caller) and my resolve() are both deleted, leaving UnifiedConfigManager as the single owner of both the new-install default and the one-time migration. Their tests were removed with them. A comment in RecordingPriority now records why that decision cannot move into this class: only a persisted, marker-gated migration can run exactly once and survive the user later choosing RELIABILITY deliberately.

Test-coverage gap tracked separately.

comments.author: Andrew Loable
comments.text:
CORRECTION — this issue's impact claim was wrong, and the change it produced has been reverted.

The claim was that an existing install would silently get 1-minute segments on upgrade because both read sites used fromConfigValue, whose missing-value fallback is RELIABILITY. That does not happen. UnifiedConfigManager.loadConfig() calls migrateConfig() on every load of an existing config and persists the result; migrateConfig back-fills "priority" = PERFORMANCE for any config lacking the priorityMigrated marker, and applyDefaults() sets RELIABILITY plus the marker for new configs. So the key is always present before HardwareEventRecorderGpu or the settings GET reads it. I had read both call sites but not UnifiedConfigManager, which is where the migration actually lives.

What was true: RecordingPriority.migrateDefault had no production caller. But the right resolution is deletion, not wiring -- the migration must be persisted and marker-gated so it runs exactly once and is never re-applied after the user deliberately chooses RELIABILITY. A read-time inference cannot do that, and my resolve() was a second owner of the same decision whose fallback branch is unreachable in practice. In the one case it IS reachable (a hand-edited config with the marker but no priority key) it returned PERFORMANCE, i.e. uncapped -- strictly less safe than the RELIABILITY fallback it replaced.

Reverted: both call sites are back on fromConfigValue, and resolve() plus the dead migrateDefault are removed, leaving UnifiedConfigManager as the single owner. A comment in RecordingPriority now records where the default and the migration live and why they cannot move here.

Follow-up filed separately: migrateConfig's priority migration has no test coverage at all.

title: ensureSpace reports success when every over-limit recording is marked
description:
## Problem

`StorageManager.ensureSpace` reports success — and skips its SD-card fallback cleanup — when
every file that would have been reaped is a marked (bookmarked) recording.

This was introduced by the BladeWatch-gyg1.4 / BladeWatch-nmao.4 refactor that extracted
`selectFilesToDelete` out of `ensureSpace`.

File: `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/storage/StorageManager.java`

`ensureSpace` (around line 1947) now does:

```java
CleanupSelection selection = selectFilesToDelete(dirs, namePrefix, targetSize,
    MarkedRecordingsStore.getInstance(), this::listMp4FilesWithShellFallback);

if (selection.files.isEmpty()) {
    return true;  // Already within limit, or nothing reapable
}
```

`selectFilesToDelete` returns an EMPTY file list in two very different situations:

1. the pool is already at or under `targetSize` — returning true is correct; and
2. the pool is OVER `targetSize`, but every candidate file was skipped by the
   `markedStore.isMarked(...)` guard — returning true is WRONG.

In case 2 `ensureSpace` returns true ("cleanup was successful and space is available") while
the category is still over its configured limit, and the early return also skips the
`currentSize > targetSize` block further down that triggers `ExternalStorageCleaner`
(the CDR fallback) when the active dir lives on the SD card. So both the honest return value
and the last-resort cleanup are lost.

Before the refactor this could not happen: the old early return was keyed on
`allFiles.isEmpty()` (literally no files present), and the marked-file skip did not exist.

## Failure scenario

Recordings limit 2000 MB, pool currently 5000 MB, and the owner has marked every clip in it
(or enough of the oldest ones that no unmarked file is reached before the target). Every
`ensureRecordingsSpace()` call returns true, the recorder keeps writing, the volume keeps
growing past the limit, and no CDR cleanup is ever triggered on the SD card.

## Fix

Decide on the real pool size, which `CleanupSelection` already carries, instead of on the
selected-file list being empty:

```java
if (selection.poolSizeAtStart <= targetSize) {
    return true;  // Already within limit
}
```

and delete the `selection.files.isEmpty()` early return entirely. With that change, the
"everything is marked" case falls through: the delete loop iterates an empty list (harmless),
`currentSize` stays above `targetSize`, the CDR fallback runs, and the method returns false —
which is the truth.

Note `selectFilesToDelete` already returns the true pool size as `poolSizeAtStart` on BOTH of
its return paths, so no change is needed there. Also note the old `allFiles.isEmpty()` early
return was dead code (an empty pool has size 0, which is always <= a target clamped at >= 0),
so nothing is lost by removing it.

## Constraints

- Do NOT change `selectFilesToDelete`'s selection logic, its marked-file skip, or its return
  shape — the preview endpoints (`previewRecordingsLimitChange` /
  `previewSurveillanceLimitChange`) share it and must keep behaving identically.
- Do NOT change the delete loop body, the sidecar deletion, or the CDR fallback condition.
- Do NOT reintroduce a per-iteration `if (currentSize <= targetSize) break;` — selection
  already stops at the target.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `ensureSpace` returns false when the pool is over target and every candidate is marked.
- [ ] `ensureSpace` still returns true when the pool is genuinely at or under target.
- [ ] The CDR/`ExternalStorageCleaner` fallback is reachable in the all-marked case.
- [ ] A JVM unit test in `app/src/test/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/storage/` covers the
      all-marked-over-limit case. Follow the existing dependency-injection style in
      `MarkedRecordingsExcludedFromCleanupTest` / `StorageManagerCleanupSelectionTest` —
      `StorageManager` itself cannot be constructed in a JVM test.
- [ ] Mutation check: revert the fix, confirm the new test fails for the stated reason,
      re-apply, confirm it passes.
- [ ] `./gradlew test koverVerify` is BUILD SUCCESSFUL.

Do not make mistakes. Read `StorageManager.ensureSpace` and `selectFilesToDelete` in full
before editing. Verify the build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing.
If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
close_reason:
Fixed. ensureSpace's early return is now keyed on selection.poolSizeAtStart <= targetSize instead of selection.files.isEmpty().

selectFilesToDelete returns an empty selection in two different situations: the pool is already under target, and the pool is over target but every candidate was skipped for being marked. The old early return conflated them, so in the all-marked case ensureSpace returned true ("space is available") while still over the limit, and the early return also skipped the ExternalStorageCleaner CDR fallback further down. The pool size distinguishes them, and CleanupSelection already carried it on both return paths.

Guarded by a new structural test, ensureSpaceEarlyReturnIsKeyedOnPoolSizeNotOnAnEmptySelection, added to MarkedRecordingsExcludedFromCleanupTest next to the existing marked-file guard, for the same stated reason: ensureSpace is private and operates on real /storage/emulated/0 directories, so it cannot be driven end-to-end in a JVM test. Confirmed failing before the fix and passing after.

The removed allFiles.isEmpty() branch was dead anyway: an empty pool has size 0, which is always at or under a target clamped to >= 0.

title: DECISION: is BladeWatch staying server-free, permanently?
description:
## This is a decision, not a task

**No agent should implement anything for this issue.** It is closed by the developer recording
an answer. "No" is an answer and closing it as "no" is a success.

If you are an agent reading this: do not write code, do not open sub-issues, do not start a
spike. If you have information that bears on the decision, add it as a comment.

## The question

Will BladeWatch ever have a backend service the project operates?

## Why it needs an answer rather than a shrug

An entire Blocked group in `docs/evaluations/electro-integration-shortlist.md` turns on this one
question. As the evaluation puts it: the right question is not "can we port offline push?" — it
cannot be ported — but **"is BladeWatch staying server-free?"** If the answer is yes, that group
closes permanently and should be marked so, so nobody re-proposes it.

## What is blocked on a server, with no local workaround

- **Push notifications while the car is offline.** A push must come from something online;
  BladeWatch's Web Push is generated *by the car*. **Unfixable locally, at any effort.**
- **Multi-user access to one car** — needs an identity service and a relay that can fan out.
- **Account / pairing flow** — Electro's QR binds a device to an account; BladeWatch's hands over
  a URL. Different problems.
- **Community automations** — Cloudflare Worker + D1. Note Overdrive's `community-edge/` is **not
  in its repo** despite being called open-source. It also means hosting user content, moderating
  reports, and sending a stable `deviceId` to a third party.
- **RoadSense hazard sharing** — same shape; `roadsense-edge/` also absent.
- **Diagnostic log upload with a short code.**
- **Car APK distribution from a server.**

## What "no" buys

The current architecture's main property: nothing leaves the car unless the owner points it
somewhere. The Tor onion service needs no account, no token and no registration, and the owner's
data never transits infrastructure this project operates.

## What "no" costs

Offline push is gone forever, and that is the single most requested thing a car app can do.

## How to close

Record the answer. If it is no, add a line to `docs/architecture.md` stating that BladeWatch is
server-free by design and that the items above are permanently out of scope, then close the
Blocked group by reference.
close_reason:
Decision recorded by the developer: No, BladeWatch stays server-free, permanently. The project will never operate a backend service.

This closes the entire Blocked group in docs/evaluations/electro-integration-shortlist.md by reference, so it should not be re-proposed: offline push notifications while the car is offline, multi-user access to one car, an account/pairing flow, community-authored automations, RoadSense-style hazard sharing between cars, diagnostic log upload with a short code, and car APK distribution from a server. All of these are permanently out of scope as a direct consequence of this decision, not because they are hard -- they are architecturally incompatible with a server-free project.

What this buys: nothing leaves the car unless the owner points it somewhere. The Tor onion service needs no account, token, or registration, and stays the only remote-access mechanism.

What this costs: offline push is gone forever. Accepted.

docs/architecture.md's Design Patterns section was updated with a permanent line recording this decision and enumerating the permanently-out-of-scope list, so it is discoverable without re-reading this issue.

Settled.

title: DECISION: does BladeWatch want an automation engine at all?
description:
## This is a decision, not a task

**No agent should implement anything for this issue.** It is closed by the developer recording
an answer. "No" is an answer and closing it as "no" is a success.

If you are an agent reading this: do not write code, do not open sub-issues, do not start a
spike. If you have information that bears on the decision, add it as a comment.

## The question

Should BladeWatch have a user-facing rules engine — triggers, conditions, actions?

## Why it is the largest question in the release

Roughly a third of the Port/Adapt recommendations are prerequisite to it or a by-product of it.
Everything downstream — AI-authored automations, scheduled insights, community sharing, and the
full value of any keymapping work — hangs on this answer.

## Evidence for

**Two unrelated commercial products for this exact hardware both made it their centrepiece.**
Overdrive: 17,525 lines across 74 files, plus 2,315 of handlers. Electro: 30% of its entire UI
surface. That is the strongest signal either evaluation epic produced about what owners of these
cars want, and it is convergent evidence from a closed competitor that could not have been
copied.

BladeWatch is also better placed than it looks: it already collects 102 telemetry fields, and
~45 of Overdrive's 60 signals are observable with no new sensing work.

## Evidence against

- ~20,000 lines, and **it is all-or-nothing**. The minimum honest scope is engine + conditions +
  a real trigger set + diagnostics. A rules engine with three triggers and no "why didn't it
  run" view is **worse than none**, because people build rules against it and those rules fail
  silently.
- The "45 of 60 signals available" figure is an **upper bound**, not a measurement. It means
  BladeWatch has a field or a monitor for each — not that each returns a useful value on this
  firmware. `docs/byd-integrations.md` warns that local BYD APIs are firmware-dependent and
  unstable, and the ADAS evaluation found that a declared feature id proves nothing. If the
  answer here is yes, **re-establish that count by measurement before using it to justify the
  effort** — `BladeWatch-2pnn.3`'s inventory probe is the tool.

## Design choices already settled, if the answer is yes

These cost nothing to decide now and are expensive to reverse later
(`docs/evaluations/electro-integration-shortlist.md`):

1. **Electro's step-list editor shape over Overdrive's rule tree.** Ordered steps that branch are
   far easier to build a UI for and to explain.
2. **Overdrive's execution model over Electro's.** Electro's 46 variables are read-only vehicle
   state, so "wait until the battery reaches my target" is inexpressible. Overdrive has settable
   variables, loops and `WaitUntil`.
3. **Electro's `Send HTTP request` escape hatch, not Overdrive's `ShellAction`.** Arbitrary shell
   in a UID-2000 daemon is why Overdrive's own community code refuses to publish or import any
   rule containing one. An outbound webhook gets most of the integration value with a fraction of
   the blast radius.
4. **Fold keymapping into triggers** (each steering-wheel button a trigger, with conflict
   detection) rather than maintaining a separate 86 KB keymap subsystem.

## Related work already filed

`BladeWatch-t1lg.2` ports `ConditionalPoller` on its own merits — 120 self-contained lines that lower idle
CPU. It is **not** a commitment to the engine and does not depend on this answer.

## How to close

Record the answer and the reasoning. If yes, file a scoping issue that starts with re-measuring
the signal count. If no, say so plainly so the question is settled.
close_reason:
Decision recorded by the developer: No. BladeWatch will not build a user-facing automation engine.

The all-or-nothing nature of the scope (engine + conditions + a real trigger set + diagnostics, roughly 20,000 lines) was the deciding factor over the competitive signal from Overdrive and Electro. A partial rules engine is worse than none, since rules that fail silently erode trust faster than no automation feature at all.

This does not affect BladeWatch-t1lg.2 (ConditionalPoller port) — that issue lowers idle CPU on its own merits and was never a commitment to this engine.

No scoping issue filed, no code written, per the issue's own instructions. Settled.

title: Write BladeWatch's own detection invariants document
description:
## Problem / context

BladeWatch has a motion/detection pipeline — GPU downscale, native motion pipeline, per-quadrant
state, an optional TFLite YOLO11n gate — and **no written statement of what that pipeline is
allowed to trade away**. Surveillance is where a well-meaning change does the most invisible
damage: nobody notices the false positives you added until the owner stops trusting the alerts
and turns them off.

`docs/evaluations/overdrive-surveillance.md` describes Overdrive's `DETECTION-INVARIANTS.md`:
205 lines, four evidence channels, six invariants, and a prime directive that is the right
policy here regardless of whether a single line of Overdrive's detection code is ever taken:

> False-positive rejection is protected. Only misses are defects. "Catches more" is not by
> itself a justification for a change.

This issue writes **BladeWatch's own version, against BladeWatch's actual pipeline.** Do not
copy a description of code this fork does not run. The Overdrive source tree is not present on
this machine and you do not need it.

## Exact locations

- **New file:** `docs/detection-invariants.md`
- **Read first, in full** — the document is worthless if it describes something other than what
  the code does:
  - `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/surveillance/GpuSurveillancePipeline.java`
  - `app/src/main/cpp/surveillance/motion_pipeline_v2*`
  - `app/src/main/cpp/surveillance/texture_tracker*`
  - `app/src/main/cpp/surveillance/native_motion*`
  - `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/surveillance/SurveillanceSchedule.java`
  - `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/surveillance/SafeLocationManager.java`
  - `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/surveillance/AdaptiveBitrateController.java`
  - the YOLO gate under `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ai/`
- **Link it from:** `docs/architecture.md` and `CLAUDE.md`'s Documentation Maintenance list, so
  a future agent touching detection is told to read it.

## What the document must contain

1. **The prime directive**, stated at the top, in BladeWatch's own words.
2. **The evidence channels this pipeline actually has** — enumerate them from the source, with
   file and function references. If BladeWatch has three and Overdrive has four, say three.
   Inventing a fourth to match is exactly the failure this document exists to prevent.
3. **The invariants**, each one written as a falsifiable statement with (a) what it protects,
   (b) what breaking it looks like from the owner's seat, and (c) which file enforces it.
4. **The suppressors** — safe locations, schedule windows, and anything else that deliberately
   causes a miss. Each with the reason it is allowed to.
5. **A change checklist** for anyone modifying detection: what to measure before and after, and
   what evidence a "this catches more" claim needs before it is acceptable.
6. **An explicit "what we do not know" section.** At minimum it must record that BladeWatch's
   `SurveillanceEngineGpu` is smaller than Overdrive's and that **nobody has established whether
   it is an earlier version of the same code or has diverged independently since the fork.**
   That question is unanswered, it changes the cost of every future "port Overdrive's detection
   improvements" issue by several times, and it must not be quietly forgotten.

## Constraints

- **No code changes.** This issue modifies `docs/` only, plus the two link sites.
- **Every claim must be traceable to a file you read.** Where you are inferring, write "inferred"
  and say from what. A confident document describing a pipeline that does not exist is worse
  than no document.
- **Do not copy text from the Overdrive tree.** It is MIT with a copyright notice
  (*Copyright (c) 2026 Yash Srivastava*); adopt the idea, write your own words. If you do quote,
  attribute it in `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES`.
- **Do not tune anything while you are in there.** If reading the pipeline makes you want to
  change a threshold, file a separate issue against this new document.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `docs/detection-invariants.md` exists with all six sections above.
- [ ] Every evidence channel and every invariant cites at least one real file path, and every
      cited path exists (verify with a loop over the paths; paste the check into the close reason).
- [ ] The "what we do not know" section names the `SurveillanceEngineGpu` lineage question.
- [ ] `docs/architecture.md` links to it.
- [ ] `CLAUDE.md`'s Documentation Maintenance list gains a line routing detection-pipeline
      changes to this document.
- [ ] `git diff --stat` shows no file outside `docs/` and `CLAUDE.md`.
---

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the
build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is
ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
close_reason:
Wrote docs/detection-invariants.md against BladeWatch's actual surveillance/sentry pipeline, read from source (not copied from the Overdrive reference doc, which was never opened).

Read in full before writing: motion_pipeline_v2.cpp/h (the 6-stage native pipeline), texture_tracker.h (NCC tracker API/rationale), YoloDetector.kt (confidence/class/distance filters, NMS, ghost filter), SafeLocationManager.java, SurveillanceSchedule.java, AdaptiveBitrateController.java. Read targeted sections of SurveillanceEngineGpu.java (3885 lines total; read lines 1-145 for state/config, 855-1184 for the sustained-motion + AI-confirmation-gate + deterrent-suppression decision logic) and GpuSurveillancePipeline.java (init/YOLO wiring, SurveillanceEngineGpu field). Grepped AccSentryDaemon.java/CameraDaemon.java to confirm where SafeLocationManager/SurveillanceSchedule are actually consulted (they gate whether sentry arms at all, at ACC-OFF time -- not a per-frame filter inside the engine).

Scoped the document explicitly to the sentry/surveillance AI pipeline and stated in its own text that PROXIMITY_GUARD (radar-triggered, ProximityGuardController) is a separate recording mode with no AI detection stage -- conflating the two would have misdescribed both.

Evidence channels: stated exactly three (native motion pipeline, YOLO11n, NCC texture tracker), sourced to files/functions, with an explicit note that a radar channel exists in the app but belongs to a different recording mode -- did not invent a fourth to match any other document's count, per the issue's explicit warning.

Ten invariants, each traced to a real FIX-comment regression in source (Headlight False-Positive, Self-Erasing Person, Spillover Hallucination, the AI confirmation gate, deterrent self-retrigger, sustained-motion timing, temporal/spatial confirmation, distance-zone rejection, loitering-vs-passing classification incl. the side-camera proximity-mass override, and the person-only tracker immunity to brightness suppression) -- each with what it protects, what breaking it looks like to the owner, and the enforcing file/function.

Suppressors section covers safe locations, schedule windows, the brightness/flash suppression countdown, shadow/oscillation filtering, and YOLO's ghost filter -- each with why it's allowed, and cross-references Invariant 10 as the thing that bounds the brightness-suppression suppressor specifically.

"What we do not know" section names the SurveillanceEngineGpu lineage question exactly as required (smaller than other detection engines referenced in docs/evaluations/, unknown whether that's an earlier version or independent divergence, and why that changes future port-issue scope). Also recorded, because I verified it rather than assumed it: app/src/test/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/surveillance/ contains ONLY FisheyeDewarp*.kt and a config-toggles test -- zero automated coverage of the motion pipeline, shadow/oscillation filters, YOLO gate, or sustained-motion/deterrent logic. This directly shaped the change checklist (there is no regression suite to lean on; before/after verification is necessarily manual and on-device).

Verified every cited file path exists via a shell loop over all 12 references (pasted check, all OK) before closing. No code changes -- git diff for this issue specifically touches exactly docs/detection-invariants.md (new), docs/architecture.md (one linking sentence under GpuSurveillancePipeline), and CLAUDE.md (one new Documentation Maintenance line routing detection-pipeline changes to the new doc). The working tree also carries accumulated, already-closed changes from five earlier issues this session (2pnn.1/.2/.3, nmao.1/.2) since nothing has been committed yet -- those are not part of this issue's diff.

title: Measure and report BladeWatch's own mobile data use, monthly
description:
## Problem / context

The head unit is often on a metered SIM. BladeWatch streams video, serves a web UI over a Tor
onion service, and syncs telemetry — and **nothing tells the owner what any of it costs**.
Measured in this project already: 1.86 MB for one static asset over the onion, 101 KB/s
sustained while streaming a live view. A live view left open overnight is a real bill.

`app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/monitor/NetworkMonitor.java` has `init` (line 43),
`refresh` (line 53) and `getNetworkInfo` (line 290), and contains **no** `TrafficStats`,
`getUidRxBytes` or `NetworkStats` symbol at all — verified, grep count 0. It monitors
connectivity state, not volume.

## STEP ZERO — a five-minute check that decides whether this issue is possible

Before writing any code, run this on the head unit and paste the output into the issue as a
comment:

```
export CAR_IP=<your head unit's LAN IP>
adb connect $CAR_IP:5555
adb -s $CAR_IP:5555 shell 'cat /proc/net/xt_qtaguid/stats 2>/dev/null | head -3; echo "---"; ls -la /proc/net/xt_qtaguid/ 2>/dev/null'
```

Then, from a running daemon or a trivial test APK, read `TrafficStats.getUidRxBytes(android.os.Process.myUid())`
twice, thirty seconds apart, with a live view open in between.

**Pass:** both reads return a non-negative number, the second is greater than or equal to the
first, and the delta is plausibly in the right order of magnitude for what you streamed.

**Fail:** the call returns `TrafficStats.UNSUPPORTED` (-1), returns 0 on both reads, or the
value goes backwards.

**If it fails, stop.** Do not implement a fallback, do not reach for `NetworkStatsManager`, do
not estimate from the HTTP server's own byte counters. Close this issue as blocked, record the
exact numbers you saw, and file a follow-up describing what the firmware actually reports. A
data counter that silently reports garbage is worse than no counter, because the owner will
believe it.

## Exact locations

- **Modify:** `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/monitor/NetworkMonitor.java`
- **New file (likely):** a small accumulator class next to it; keep the sampling and the
  month-boundary bookkeeping out of `NetworkMonitor` itself if that file is already large.
- **Persistence:** `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/config/UnifiedConfigManager.kt`
  owns `/data/local/tmp/bladewatch_config.json`. Read that file before choosing where the
  monthly totals live. **Do not put them in `SecretConfigStore`** — they are not secrets and
  that file is mode 600 shell-only.
- **Surface:** the Diagnostics screen, `flutter_ui/lib/screens/diagnostics/`.
- **New test:** `app/src/test/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/monitor/DataUsageAccountingTest.java`

## The hard part is not the API call — it is the counter reset

`TrafficStats` UID counters are **cumulative since boot** and reset to zero on reboot. A naive
"total = current reading" is wrong after every restart, and a naive "total += current - last"
goes catastrophically negative after a reboot. The accumulator must:

1. Store `lastReading` and `accumulatedThisMonth`.
2. On each sample: if `current >= lastReading`, add the delta. If `current < lastReading`, a
   reboot or counter wrap happened — add `current` itself (everything since boot) and do **not**
   subtract anything.
3. Roll over to a new month on local-time month boundary, keeping the previous month's total so
   the UI can show "last month" too.
4. Persist after each rollover and periodically, so a daemon kill does not lose the month.

**Extract this logic into a pure static/instance class with no Android dependency** so it can be
unit-tested without a device. That is the design requirement, not a suggestion — the reboot case
is the whole risk and it must be testable.

## Constraints

- **Own-UID totals only.** `android.net.TrafficStats.getUidRxBytes` / `getUidTxBytes` need no
  permission for the calling UID. **Do not** use `NetworkStatsManager` and do not request
  `PACKAGE_USAGE_STATS` — per-app attribution is not the part that matters and the permission is
  a real cost.
- The two APKs share a UID by design (`android:sharedUserId="net.bladewatch.app"`), so one query
  covers both. Note this in the code comment; a future reader will wonder.
- **Do not sample on a tight timer.** Once a minute is plenty; once every few minutes is better.
- **Do not distinguish mobile from Wi-Fi bytes via a second API.** If `NetworkMonitor` already
  knows the active transport, tag the accumulation with it; if it does not, report total bytes
  and say so in the UI label. Do not invent a transport detector for this issue.
- **Do not log byte totals at a level R8 keeps in release.**

## TDD procedure (mandatory)

1. Write the test named below FIRST. Do not touch production code yet.
2. Run it. It MUST fail, and you must read the failure message and confirm it fails
   for the stated reason (the behaviour is missing), not because of a typo, a missing
   import, or a compile error in the test itself.
3. Record the exact failure line in your close reason.
4. Only then write the minimum production code that makes it pass.
5. Re-run. Then mutate the production code (invert one condition, delete one line)
   and confirm the test fails again. A test that still passes after mutation is not a
   test. Revert the mutation.


## Required tests

Against the pure accumulator, no device:

- [ ] First sample ever (lastReading unset), current = 1000 → accumulated = 1000.
- [ ] Second sample, current = 1500 → accumulated = 1500 (delta 500 added, not 1500 again).
- [ ] Reboot case: last = 1500, current = 200 → accumulated = 1700, **not** 200 and **not**
      negative. This is the test that justifies the whole class.
- [ ] Two consecutive identical readings → accumulated unchanged.
- [ ] Month rollover: samples in January then a sample in February → January's total is
      preserved as "previous month" and the February accumulator starts from the delta, not
      from zero-plus-everything.
- [ ] A rollover that happens simultaneously with a reboot (month changes AND counter goes
      backwards in the same sample) does not double-count and does not lose the previous month.
- [ ] `TrafficStats.UNSUPPORTED` (-1) as a reading is ignored entirely — accumulated does not
      change and `lastReading` is not updated to -1.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Step Zero was run on the car and its actual output is pasted into the close reason. If it
      failed, the issue is closed as blocked with those numbers and nothing else was built.
- [ ] The accumulator class imports nothing from `android.*`.
- [ ] All seven tests present and passing; observed failing first; failure lines quoted.
- [ ] Mutation check: change the reboot branch to `accumulated += (current - lastReading)`
      unconditionally and confirm the reboot test fails. Revert. Name the failure.
- [ ] `grep -rn "NetworkStatsManager\|PACKAGE_USAGE_STATS" app/ flutter_ui/` returns nothing new.
- [ ] Totals survive a daemon restart — state how you verified this.
- [ ] Diagnostics screen shows this month and last month, in MB, with a label that says whether
      it is total bytes or mobile-only.
- [ ] `cd flutter_ui && flutter analyze && flutter test` clean; coverage script passes.
- [ ] `./gradlew test` and `./gradlew koverVerify` pass.
- [ ] `docs/networking-and-tunnels.md` and `docs/features.md` updated.
---

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the
build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is
ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.

inline comment ("Remove this block ... once Step Zero's pass/fail verdict is recorded"). Real
implementation (accumulator class with the reboot/reset handling the issue specifies, persistence
via UnifiedConfigManager, Diagnostics screen surfacing, full TDD suite) proceeds next under this
same issue.

title: Suppress CONTINUOUS and DRIVE_MODE recording while the vehicle is charging
description:
## Problem / context

At a wallbox, a spurious non-P gear read starts a drive recording: SD writes, storage churn,
and a clip the owner has to sift past. Nothing stops it today.

`app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/recording/RecordingModeManager.java` contains
**zero** charging references — verified, `grep -c "harging"` returns 0. Its inputs are ACC
state (`onAccStateChanged`, line 346) and gear (`onGearChanged`, line 447), and that is all.

`app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/monitor/ChargingDetector.java` already knows.
It fuses BMS state, `Power.isCharging()`, L3 inference and plug edges with hysteresis —
deliberately session-level, because raw BMS edges miss PHEV-stuck-at-IDLE sessions. It exposes
`addFusedStateListener(FusedStateListener)` at line 112, `removeFusedStateListener` at 115, and
`isCharging()` at 291.

`docs/evaluations/overdrive-trips-energy.md` ranks this the best value-per-effort row in its
domain.

## Scope note — one of three parts does not apply

Overdrive's version of this interlock has three parts. Only two apply here:

1. Suppress drive recording while charging — **this issue**.
2. Force gear to P while charging — **`BladeWatch-nmao.2`**, filed separately.
3. A fix for a GPS-drift gear-promotion bug — **does not apply.** BladeWatch never added the
   GPS-speed gear fallback that bug depends on. Do not port it, and do not go looking for it.
