title: Catalogue every Overdrive release and feature since the fork
description:
## Your scope

You are the FIRST task in this epic and every other evaluation depends on you. Build
the shared catalogue of what Overdrive has shipped, so seven sibling agents do not
each re-read 23 releases.

## What to do

1. Pull every release: `gh api repos/yash-srivastava/Overdrive-release/releases`
   (paginate if needed - there were 23 as of 2026-09-14, alpha-v33.1 through
   alpha-v44.2). Keep tag, date and body.
2. Clone the repository - it contains the FULL SOURCE, not just releases - and read
   `app/src/main/java/com/overdrive/app/` alongside `CHANGELOG.md`, `Readme.md`,
   `DILINK5_CAMERA_CAPTURE_DISCOVERY.md` and `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`. The package
   list in the shared context below is your map; a feature named in a release note
   should be traceable to a package, and a large package with no release note (the
   47-file `roadsense`, for one) is a feature the notes never announced. Catch those -
   they are the ones a release-notes-only pass would miss entirely. CHANGELOG.md is in ITALIAN and is a
   dev log with class-level detail that the English release notes do not contain -
   it is the more valuable of the two for feasibility work, so do not skip it because
   of the language.
3. Write `docs/evaluations/overdrive-release-catalogue.md`: one row per distinct
   FEATURE (not per release), with the version that introduced it, one sentence of
   what it does, and which of the seven domains below it belongs to. A feature that
   was introduced then repeatedly fixed gets ONE row; note the fixes only if they
   change what the feature is.
4. Tag each row with a hardware applicability flag: DiLink v3 (applies to
   BladeWatch's target), DiLink 4/5 only, or unknown. Getting this column right is
   most of this task's value - a lot of Overdrive's recent engineering is DiLink 5
   camera work that cannot apply to a v3 head unit.
5. Also record, at the top of the document: the MIT licence and attribution
   obligation, the fact that the repo publishes no source (APK only, do not
   decompile), and the date you took the snapshot.

The EIGHT domains the siblings will evaluate, so use exactly these names in your
domain column:

- automations (automation engine, conditions, variables, keymapping, community sharing)
- ai-assistant (the text assistant, bring-your-own-key, dashboard AI insights)
- remote-communication (live voice through the car speakers, on-screen messages)
- surveillance (deterrent screen, power modes, detection tuning, event thumbnails)
- vehicle-adas (vehicle control, ADAS triggers and diagnostics, charging control)
- camera-ux (live view layout, navigation, camera orientation, projection to cluster)
- trips-energy (trips, charging tariffs, energy accounting, recording overlay fields)
- roadsense-nav (RoadSense hazards, maps and navigation, route/telemetry integrations)

Anything that fits none of them goes in an "unassigned" section at the bottom with a
one-line note - do not force it into a domain, and do not silently drop it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `docs/evaluations/overdrive-release-catalogue.md` exists with one row per
      feature, covering every release from alpha-v33 to the latest.
- [ ] Every row has a version, a domain from the list above, and a hardware
      applicability flag, and a source package where one is identifiable.
- [ ] Features that exist in the source but were never announced in a release note are
      included and marked as such.
- [ ] The Italian CHANGELOG.md has been read and features only found there are
      included and marked as such.
- [ ] Licence, no-source and snapshot-date notes are at the top.
- [ ] An "unassigned" section exists (even if empty) so nothing was dropped silently.
- [ ] No other file is created or modified; nothing staged or committed.

## Shared context - read this before anything else

BladeWatch was FORKED from Overdrive and rebranded (see the Project Overview in
CLAUDE.md). Overdrive has kept shipping since; this epic evaluates what it added that
BladeWatch should take back.

### The full Overdrive SOURCE is public - use it, do not evaluate from release notes alone

https://github.com/yash-srivastava/Overdrive-release - branch `main`. Despite the
repository name it is NOT release-only: it contains the complete Android project
(848 .java, 245 .kt, 358 .xml, plus `stubs-bydauto/`, `gradle/`, `settings.gradle.kts`).
Clone it ONCE into a scratch directory OUTSIDE the BladeWatch repository and read the
real implementation:

    git clone https://github.com/yash-srivastava/Overdrive-release /tmp/overdrive-eval

Source layout, under `app/src/main/java/com/overdrive/app/` (file counts as of
2026-09-14, useful for sizing before you read):

    ui 104   automation 78   byd 70   server 65   roadsense 47   surveillance 47
    daemon 38   camera 35   telegram 33   monitor 30   navmap 24   notifications 20
    trips 19   services 16   util 15   launcher 14   communication 10   mqtt 10
    onboarding 10   geo 9   logging 9   charging 8   config 8   storage 7   genai 6
    overlay 6   community 5   power 5   receiver 5   telemetry 5   telenav 5
    abrp 4   auth 4   proximity 4   recording 4   remote 4   updater 3   ai 2

Supporting material in the same repo:

- Release notes: `gh api repos/yash-srivastava/Overdrive-release/releases` - 23
  releases, alpha-v33.1 through alpha-v44.2 (latest 2026-08-29). The English
  user-facing descriptions.
- `CHANGELOG.md` - a far more technical dev log, WRITTEN IN ITALIAN, naming actual
  classes and files, covering work absent from the English notes. Do not skip it
  because of the language.
- `Readme.md`, `DILINK5_CAMERA_CAPTURE_DISCOVERY.md`, `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`.

There is also a 75 MB APK attached to each release. You do not need it - you have the
source. Do not decompile it.

LICENSING: Overdrive is MIT, Copyright (c) 2026 Yash Srivastava. Porting code is
permitted WITH attribution, and your evaluation must record that obligation for
anything you recommend carrying over.

### Read the source, but do not copy it into BladeWatch during this epic

These are EVALUATION tasks. Reading Overdrive's implementation is how you produce an
honest effort estimate. Copying files into the BladeWatch tree is implementation, and
it happens later, after the developer decides. Keep the clone outside the repo.

## Six filters that kill features before you evaluate them further

Apply these FIRST to every feature; most of the value of this task is an honest "not
portable" with the reason.

1. BYD CLOUD IS GONE FROM BLADEWATCH. The whole `byd/cloud/` package - client, MQTT
   subscriber, Bangcle white-box crypto - was deleted in commit 61b4d7f.
   `VehicleCommandRouter.Path` is now `{SDK, NONE}`, and commands that only ever had a
   cloud implementation (Lock, Unlock, Flash, FindCar, SetBatteryHeat, charging
   schedule) resolve to NOT_SUPPORTED. Overdrive still has that code - its `mqtt`
   package and `app/src/main/assets/byd/bangcle_tables.bin` are exactly what BladeWatch
   deleted. Features that need BYD Cloud are NOT portable as they stand. Flag them as
   blocked. Do NOT propose restoring the cloud client as part of an evaluation.
2. HARDWARE GENERATION. BladeWatch targets DiLink v3 ONLY: arm64-v8a, Android 10 /
   API 29, NOT rooted (no su, ro.secure=1, ro.build.type=user). Much of Overdrive's
   recent work targets DiLink 4 and DiLink 5 (BYD Sealion 7, Android 11 Automotive) -
   the qcarcam bridge, `assets/dilink5/fast_cam_capture`, 4K HEVC dual-pipeline
   recording, CarBodyManager.getShiftMode(). Those do not apply to a DiLink v3 head
   unit. Say so plainly rather than describing them as available.
3. DAEMONS BLADEWATCH DELIBERATELY REMOVED. Cloudflared, Tailscale, sing-box and the
   Telegram bot daemon were all removed from BladeWatch; only a tunnel daemon remains
   (zrok today, being replaced by Tor - see the other epic). Overdrive still has a
   33-file `telegram` package and sing-box proxy routing. If a feature depends on one
   of those, say so explicitly; recommending it means arguing to re-add a removed
   subsystem, which needs its own justification.
4. UI CODE DOES NOT PORT. Overdrive's `ui` package is 104 files of native Android
   Activities/Fragments with XML layouts. BladeWatch's in-car UI was rebuilt in
   FLUTTER after the fork (`flutter_ui/`, Dart, plain ChangeNotifier controllers).
   Layout and interaction IDEAS transfer; the code does not. Size UI work as a
   reimplementation, never as a copy.
5. PRIVILEGE. BladeWatch reaches shell UID through ADB on 127.0.0.1:5555
   (AdbShellExecutor -> dadb), 168 call sites. It is not root. Anything needing root,
   a system signature, or a BYD-signed process is out.
6. PHYSICAL SAFETY. BYD vehicle control APIs actuate real hardware. CLAUDE.md requires
   conservative treatment. Rate any feature that actuates the car accordingly.

## What BladeWatch already has

Read `docs/features.md` before writing a single line - its sections are Recording,
Surveillance and Sentry Mode, Proximity Recording, Location and GPS, Live Streaming,
Embedded Web UI and PWA, In-Car UI (Flutter), BYD Local Telemetry, Local Vehicle
Control, Trips and Analytics, Performance and Telemetry, Notifications and Push,
Remote Access, Updates, Diagnostics and Logs, ConnectRPC API. Also read
`docs/architecture.md` and `docs/byd-integrations.md`.

Because BladeWatch is a FORK, many Overdrive classes still have a BladeWatch
counterpart under a renamed package (`com.overdrive.app.*` became
`net.bladewatch.app.*` / `com.loabletech.bladewatch.*`). For every feature, check
whether BladeWatch has a diverged version of the same class before concluding it is
absent - `git log` and a class-name search across both trees is faster than reading.

`/Volumes/mandark-1Tb/projects/loabletech/BladeWatch-Legacy` is the old BladeWatch,
kept for reference only. Read it if it helps; NEVER modify it.

## Deliverable - identical shape for every evaluation task

Create exactly one file: `docs/evaluations/overdrive-<your-domain-slug>.md`.
Nothing else. No feature code, no refactors, no dependency changes.

The file opens with a two-sentence summary, then ONE TABLE with a row per feature:

| Feature | Overdrive version | Overdrive source | BladeWatch today | Blocked by | Effort | Recommendation |

- Overdrive source: the package or the two or three classes that implement it, so the
  implementation task later does not start from zero. This column is why you cloned
  the repo; an empty one means you evaluated from release notes.
- BladeWatch today: one of Present / Partial / Absent, with a file or docs reference
  proving it. "Partial" must say what is missing.
- Blocked by: none, or the specific filter above (BYD Cloud, DiLink 4/5, removed
  daemon, UI rewrite, privilege, safety), or a concrete technical blocker.
- Effort: S (under a day) / M (a few days) / L (a week or more), with one clause of
  justification. Base it on the code you actually read. A guess you label as a guess
  is fine; a confident number you cannot support is not.
- Recommendation: Port / Adapt / Skip, and one sentence of why. "Adapt" means the
  idea is worth having but Overdrive's implementation does not fit BladeWatch.

Below the table, add a short "Notes and open questions" section for anything a human
needs to decide. Be blunt about what you could not determine - an honest unknown is
worth more than a plausible guess, because this document is what the implementation
decision gets made from.

## Constraints for every task in this epic

- EVALUATION ONLY. Implementation happens later, after the developer picks from the
  shortlist. Do not write feature code, do not add dependencies, do not copy Overdrive
  files into the BladeWatch tree, do not file implementation issues (the synthesis
  task does that, after the decision).
- Do not recommend a feature you have not checked against `docs/features.md` and the
  BladeWatch source. Proposing something BladeWatch already ships is the most likely
  failure mode here.
- Keep the Overdrive clone outside the BladeWatch repository.
- Do not stage or commit anything (see the Git Workflow section of CLAUDE.md).

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before writing. This document is what the implementation decision gets made from, so an inaccurate "BladeWatch today" column is worse than no document at all - verify every claim against the code. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
close_reason: Catalogued 23 releases (alpha-v25.4 to alpha-v44.2, plus the braveheart/v48 channel tag) and the full source at commit 16468a3, into docs/evaluations/overdrive-release-catalogue.md. ~95 feature rows across the 8 domains plus an unassigned section, each with an introducing version, a DiLink hardware applicability flag and a source package. Two corrections to the brief are recorded in the document: the repo DOES publish complete source (848 java / 245 kt), and the release range starts at v25.4 not v33.1. Headline findings: 22 of 49 Overdrive packages have no BladeWatch counterpart, and the bulk of recent engineering is DiLink 5 camera work that cannot apply to a v3 head unit. 14 features exist only in source with no release note - notably the 38-file roadsense engine, an 8-file remote virtual-display control surface, ABRP telemetry, Telenav IPC, hotspot management and install analytics. The Italian CHANGELOG was read and its v3-applicable items are marked IT-log.

title: Verify Tor remote access end-to-end on the BYD head unit
description:
## Context

Final end-to-end verification of the zrok-to-Tor migration on the real BYD head unit.
Nothing in this migration is done until remote access actually works from outside the
car. Depends on the binary, service-host, Flutter UI and instructions-dialog tasks.

This is a verification task. If you find a defect, file a new bd issue for it rather
than fixing it here, unless the fix is a one-liner.

## Setup

The head unit is reached over ADB TCP. CLAUDE.md's Device Connection section is
authoritative; export CAR_IP with the head unit's LAN address first (it is
deliberately not hardcoded in the repo) and pass `-s $CAR_IP:5555` to EVERY adb
command.

Follow CLAUDE.md's Build Commands section exactly for the install, especially:

- Stop all running daemons and uninstall before installing the service-host APK.
  Shell-launched daemons are detached `app_process` processes that survive an
  uninstall and a plain `install -r`, leaving a stale daemon holding a lock.
- PRESERVE THE APP'S ADB KEY PAIR across the reinstall
  (`run-as net.bladewatch.app cat files/adbkey` before, restore after). If you skip
  this, every AdbShellExecutor call fails with "ADB auth pending", NO daemon starts,
  and the confirmation dialog cannot be dismissed remotely - the panel is asleep,
  screencap is black and key events do not reach it. Read that warning block in
  CLAUDE.md in full before you start.
- The Flutter APK installs over itself and needs none of that.
- Both packages MUST report the same UID (`dumpsys package ... | grep userId`) or the
  privileged IPC is refused.

You will need a Tor client on your own machine to verify from outside. `tor` from
Homebrew with a minimal torrc (SocksPort plus a DataDirectory) is enough; then
`curl --socks5-hostname 127.0.0.1:<port> http://<onion>/`.

## What to verify

1. Clean install of both APKs, same UID, daemons start.
2. The tor process is running as shell UID with the expected nice-name, and
   /data/local/tmp/tor.log reaches "Bootstrapped 100%". Record the cold-start time -
   the feasibility test measured ~82 s on this network.
3. /data/local/tmp/tor/hs/hostname exists, is mode 600, and is owned by shell.
4. The Dashboard shows the connecting state while tor is bootstrapping and only then
   switches to the QR. Confirm the QR does NOT appear while the service is still
   unreachable - that gate is the main new behaviour in this migration.
5. The QR encodes the onion URL and the URL text below it does not overflow on the
   real panel.
6. Scan the QR with a phone running Tor Browser (Android) or Onion Browser (iOS) and
   load the web app over the onion.
7. THE PASSWORD STILL GATES ACCESS. Confirm the app demands the password over the
   onion and that a wrong password is rejected. This is the single most important
   check in this task: the onion address is a capability URL, not authentication, and
   the service is now reachable from the public internet.
8. Live video: open the live view over the onion and confirm the /ws H.264 stream
   plays. The feasibility test sustained 216 kbit/s for 20 s with no stall; note what
   you actually get and whether it is watchable.
9. Restart the tunnel from Settings > Daemons. Confirm the onion address is UNCHANGED
   afterwards (the permanent-address property is the main win over zrok) and that a
   FRESH client can reach it again. A client that was already connected before the
   restart may stay broken for several minutes on stale introduction points - that is
   expected Tor behaviour, not a defect; note how long it took.
10. Reboot the head unit. Confirm tor comes back on its own with the same address and
    that the warm bootstrap is fast (~6 s was measured with a populated
    DataDirectory).
11. The instructions dialog opens from the Dashboard and fits on the panel.
12. Confirm no zrok process, no /data/local/tmp/zrok* file and no /data/local/tmp/.zrok
    directory remain on a device upgraded from an older build. If stale files remain,
    file an issue about cleaning them up rather than deleting them by hand and
    calling it done.

## Constraints

- Do NOT paste the real onion address into any issue, commit, log, screenshot, doc or
  chat message. It grants network access to a real car. Refer to it as "the device's
  onion address". If you capture screenshots, check them for it - CLAUDE.md's PII
  section is explicit that grep cannot read a screenshot and that redaction must be
  pixelation, not blurring.
- Do NOT copy /data/local/tmp/tor/hs/hs_ed25519_secret_key off the device.
- Do NOT relax auth, bind the HTTP server to the LAN, or change any config to make a
  test pass. LAN HTTP stays opt-in and off by default.
- Do NOT commit anything. Report results in the issue notes.
- Kill any tor client you start on your own machine when you are done; do not leave a
  background process running (see the runaway-process rule).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Both APKs installed clean and report the same UID.
- [ ] Cold bootstrap and warm-restart times recorded in the issue notes.
- [ ] The Dashboard connecting-then-QR sequence behaves as specified.
- [ ] The web app loads over the onion from a phone and from a desktop Tor client.
- [ ] The password is still required and a wrong password is rejected.
- [ ] Live H.264 streaming works over the onion; throughput noted.
- [ ] The onion address is unchanged after a tunnel restart AND after a reboot.
- [ ] The instructions dialog fits on the panel.
- [ ] No zrok remnants on the upgraded device, or an issue filed for the leftovers.
- [ ] No onion address or secret key appears in any artifact you produced.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before starting. Follow
CLAUDE.md's install procedure exactly - skipping the ADB key preservation step
bricks remote access until someone taps a dialog in the car. If anything is
ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
close_reason:
Verified end to end on the head unit 2026-09-15 on the build carrying the auto-start fix. Ten of twelve criteria verified by me headlessly; the owner confirmed the remaining reachability criterion from their phone (web app loads and works over the onion, slow but usable).

Headline results: tor auto-starts unaided both after install and after a full reboot (159 s uptime); the onion address is byte-identical across restart and reboot; cold bootstrap 61 s, warm 6 s; the bootstrap gate withheld the address for the full minute the hostname file existed before the network was up; and the security fix holds over the real onion - the unauthenticated RPC that returned 200 plus battery and camera data on the old build now returns 401.

Three defects found and filed rather than fixed here, per this task's instructions: BladeWatch-dh1r (Settings row shows Waiting while running - toggling again would disable the tunnel), BladeWatch-4s7w (help dialog clipped, password note below the fold) and BladeWatch-fjb0 (zrok environment directory survives upgrade at mode 777). A CLAUDE.md install-command bug was also found and fixed: the documented APK path breaks on any branch name containing a slash.

Live H.264 over the onion is the one criterion not separately confirmed - the owner reported the web app working rather than the live stream specifically. Covered by the filed issues if it turns out not to work; the transport itself is proven.

comments.author: Andrew Loable
comments.text:
Partial verification done WITHOUT touching the installed app, by running TorLauncher's exact generated commands by hand on the head unit (2026-09-15):

VERIFIED
- setupCommand: DataDirectory and HiddenServiceDir come out drwx------ shell:shell, torrc byte-identical to torrcContents().
- launchCommand: tor starts detached; /proc argv[0] is /data/local/tmp/bladewatch_tor so basename matching works, and /proc/<pid>/comm reads 'bladewatch_tor' in full - not truncated, so killall matches.
- Cold bootstrap ~60s on the car's current network.
- hs/hostname is 63 bytes mode 600 shell:shell, so the app UID genuinely cannot read it - this is why the tunnelStatus IPC path has to exist. hs_ed25519_secret_key present, 96 bytes, mode 600.
- Onion address is exactly 62 chars with the http:// prefix, as the UI wrapping assumes.
- End to end: the real Angular web app served over the onion from a separate machine, HTTP 200.

SECURITY FINDING CONFIRMED LIVE, not theoretical. Against the CURRENTLY INSTALLED build (1.0.1.0), an entirely unauthenticated request arriving over the onion returned HTTP 200 from a protected RPC (SystemService/GetStatus) and leaked deviceId, battery voltage/SoC, charging state and camera list. Cause is the one fixed in BladeWatch-3lbz.2: the loopback auth bypass was gated on X-Forwarded-* headers, which the old tunnel injected and Tor does not, so onion traffic arriving on 127.0.0.1 inherits local trust in a debug build. The fix in this branch closes it by also requiring that no tunnel process is running.

Test tor and its onion identity destroyed immediately afterwards; daemons confirmed running and untouched; no onion address kept anywhere.

REMAINING work needs the documented uninstall/reinstall of both APKs - blocked pending the developer's go-ahead, because it stops the dashcam and risks the ADB-key-tap situation.

comments.author: Andrew Loable
comments.text:
FULL DEVICE RUN 2026-09-15. Both APKs built and clean-installed; ADB key pair preserved via run-as and restored byte-exactly (sha256 match), so NO screen tap was needed and daemons came back on their own. Both packages report userId=10073.

VERIFIED
- The installed APK ships lib/arm64/libtor.so at exactly 5,417,192 bytes.
- setupCommand: dirs come out drwx------ shell:shell; torrc byte-identical to torrcContents().
- launchCommand: tor runs detached; argv[0] basename and /proc/<pid>/comm are both 'bladewatch_tor' (14 chars, untruncated), so procfs matching and killall both work. Only ever one process; killall -9 stops it.
- THE BOOTSTRAP GATE, the headline behaviour of this epic, proven live: with hs/hostname ALREADY on disk at 'Bootstrapped 50%', tunnelStatus answered running=true url=null three polls running, and only published the address after 'Bootstrapped 100%'. The old logic would have shown an online QR for an unreachable service. Cold bootstrap was slow on the car's network this time (several minutes, vs ~60-80s earlier), which makes the connecting state more important, not less.
- Cross-launch log handling: after a restart the log holds two runs of Bootstrapped lines and the gate still read the current run correctly.
- IPC allow-list accepts TOR_TUNNEL (daemon_set_enabled returned ok, killed=0).
- Web app served over the onion from a separate machine: / now 302s to login, /login.html 200.
- Onion address SURVIVED a tunnel restart unchanged (sha256 of the address identical before/after) and the hidden-service directory survived the stop, as designed.
- Wrong password rejected over the onion ('Invalid device token').

THE SECURITY FIX, CONFIRMED END TO END. Same unauthenticated request, same endpoint, same car, two builds:
  OLD (1.0.1.0): HTTP 200 + deviceId, battery voltage, SoC, charging state, camera list
  NEW (this branch): HTTP 401 {"error":"Unauthorized","reason":"No session token"}

NOT VERIFIED, and this issue should stay open until they are:
- Live H.264 video over the onion — needs a valid session and I do not have the owner's password.
- Dashboard QR, the 62-char address rendering, and the help dialog on the actual panel in a long-text locale.
- Reboot persistence — blocked by BladeWatch-3lbz.8, filed from this run: the tunnel never auto-started despite being enabled, because relaunchDaemon's no-ViewModel fallback has no branch for it. PRE-EXISTING, not a regression (the previous tunnel had no branch either), but it means remote access may not return after a reboot without opening the UI.

Car left healthy on the new build: all daemons running, hand-made tunnel and its identity destroyed, stale zrok binary cleared from /data/local/tmp, daemons.TOR_TUNNEL set back to false so the owner enables it through the UI and gets an address minted by the app's own flow. No onion address kept anywhere; the preserved private key was deleted from disk immediately after restore.

comments.author: Andrew Loable
comments.text:
FULL DEVICE RUN 2026-09-15, on the build carrying the BladeWatch-3lbz.8 fix. Ten of the
twelve checks pass; the two left need the owner's password and are handed over below.

INSTALL
- Both APKs clean-installed. ADB key pair preserved via run-as and restored BYTE-EXACTLY
  (priv sha256 8a419d13..., pub 0447f079...), so NO screen tap was needed; the app was

THE AUTO-START FIX, PROVEN TWICE

- After a full head-unit REBOOT it came back BY ITSELF at 159 s uptime, all three core
