TIMINGS measured on this device
- Cold bootstrap 61 s (07:30:48 -> 07:31:49).
- Warm restart 6 s (07:39:35 -> 07:39:41).
- Warm bootstrap after reboot 6 s (07:45:11 -> 07:45:17).
- Reachable again from an ALREADY-CONNECTED client 115 s after a tunnel restart, which is
  the stale-introduction-point behaviour this task anticipates, not a defect. After the
  reboot a fresh request succeeded in 16 s.

THE BOOTSTRAP GATE
- hostname was on disk at 07:30, a full minute before Bootstrapped 100% at 07:31:49. That
  is the window the gate exists to cover.
- tunnelStatus over IPC returned running=true with the URL only after 100%.
- The log accumulated three runs of Bootstrapped lines across restarts and the gate still
  read the current run correctly each time.

FILE MODES
- /data/local/tmp/tor/hs and .../data are both drwx------ shell:shell.
- hs/hostname is -rw------- shell:shell, 63 bytes; the address is 62 chars.
- hs_ed25519_secret_key present. Never read, copied or transmitted.
- /data/local/tmp/bladewatch_ipc_token is -rw-r--r-- (644), as CLAUDE.md requires.

AUTH OVER THE ONION, from a desktop Tor client
- GET / -> 302 to /login.html?redirect=%2F
- GET /login.html -> 200, 14898 bytes: the real web app is served over the onion.
- Unauthenticated protected RPC -> 401 {"error":"Unauthorized","reason":"No session
  token"}. The SAME request returned 200 plus deviceId, battery voltage, SoC, charging
  state and camera list on the old build. The security fix holds on the installed build,
  over the real onion, and still holds after a reboot.
- Login with a wrong token -> {"success":false,"error":"Invalid device token"}, and NO
  Set-Cookie header, so no session is issued.

PERMANENT ADDRESS
- sha256 of the hostname file was IDENTICAL across: initial mint, a disable/enable restart
  (daemon_set_enabled killed=1 then relaunch in 5 s), and a full reboot. The hidden-service
  directory survived the stop, as designed.

DASHBOARD
- The connect card renders the QR, and the 69-character http:// + onion URL WRAPS onto two
  centred monospace lines and does NOT overflow the card. The info button is present.
- The status chip read "4/4 Running" with the tunnel up.

DEFECTS FOUND, filed rather than fixed here
- BladeWatch-dh1r (P1): Settings > Services shows the Tor row as "Waiting" with the switch
  OFF while tor is running. The switch binds to liveness and the screen never refreshes.
  Toggling again to "fix" it actually disables the tunnel.
- BladeWatch-4s7w (P2): the instructions dialog is CLIPPED on the panel. The download-QR
  caption is cut mid-line and the password note is entirely below the fold - in English,
  the shortest locale. So criterion 11 is "opens, does not fully fit".
- BladeWatch-fjb0 (P2): zrok remnants survive an upgrade. /data/local/tmp/.zrok still
  exists holding the old account identity, with the DIRECTORY at mode 777, and the shared
  config still carries a stale ZROK_TUNNEL key. Contents deliberately not read. Filed
  rather than hand-deleted, as this task instructs. No zrok process and no other zrok files.

NOT VERIFIED - needs the owner
- Loading the web app over the onion from a PHONE (criterion 6). The desktop half is done.
- Live H.264 over the onion (criterion 8). Needs a valid session, i.e. the access code,
  which I will not read out of the secret store.
The owner is running both from their phone; results to follow.

Local Tor client killed and its DataDirectory removed. Every screenshot taken during this
run was deleted, and no onion address appears in this comment or anywhere else.

comments.author: Andrew Loable
comments.text:
Owner confirmed 2026-09-15: the web app loads over the onion from their phone and works. That closes criterion 6 (load over the onion from a phone) and, with the desktop client result already recorded, the reachability half of this task end to end.

Criterion 8 (live H.264 over the onion) was not separately called out by the owner - they reported the web app working, not the live stream specifically. Noting it here rather than marking it verified; if Live View played for them it is covered, otherwise it is the one item outstanding.

comments.author: Andrew Loable
comments.text: Owner's qualitative verdict on performance over the onion: SLOW BUT USABLE. Consistent with the feasibility measurements recorded on this epic (62-75 KB/s throughput, warm-request TTFB 2.1-6.5 s). Worth stating plainly in user-facing docs so nobody reports Tor latency as a defect - it is the cost of the transport, not a regression.

title: Flutter UI: Tor tunnel row, onion QR, delete the zrok token UI
description:
## TDD - required, write the test first

This project works test-first. Write the test, run it, SEE IT FAIL for the right
reason, then write the smallest code that makes it pass, then re-run. A new test that
passes on its first run is a broken test - fix it before touching the code.

Read these existing tests FIRST; they already contain the fakes and pump helpers you
need, and they are the ones that will break, so they are also your worklist:

Dart (all 13 reference zrok today):
`flutter_ui/test/platform/daemon_channel_test.dart`,
`flutter_ui/test/platform/config_channel_test.dart`,
`flutter_ui/test/screens/dashboard/dashboard_controller_test.dart`,
`flutter_ui/test/screens/dashboard/dashboard_screen_test.dart`,
`flutter_ui/test/screens/settings/settings_daemons_controller_test.dart`,
`flutter_ui/test/screens/settings/settings_daemons_screen_test.dart`,
`flutter_ui/test/screens/settings/settings_screen_test.dart`,
`flutter_ui/test/screens/diagnostics/diagnostics_controller_test.dart`,
`flutter_ui/test/screens/diagnostics/diagnostics_screen_test.dart`,
`flutter_ui/test/screens/startup/startup_controller_test.dart`,
`flutter_ui/test/screens/startup/startup_screen_test.dart`,
`flutter_ui/test/shell/status_pill_test.dart`, `flutter_ui/test/widget_test.dart`.

Flutter-side Kotlin:
`flutter_ui/android/app/src/test/kotlin/net/bladewatch/bladewatch_ui/daemon/DaemonControlTest.kt`,
`flutter_ui/android/app/src/test/kotlin/net/bladewatch/bladewatch_ui/config/SecretConfigChannelTest.kt`.

Write these, each RED before GREEN:

1. Dashboard controller: a fake tunnelStatus returning
   running=true, url="http://<56 chars>.onion" puts the tunnel in the online phase
   with that exact url.
2. Dashboard widget: in that state the tree contains exactly one QrImageView whose
   `data` is the onion URL (find it by type and assert on the widget's data property -
   do NOT assert on pixels, this project has no golden tests).
3. Dashboard widget: running=true with url=null renders the connecting/bootstrapping
   state, NOT the QR and NOT the offline message. This is the ~80 second cold-start
   window; it is the state most likely to regress.
4. Dashboard widget: running=false renders the existing offline message.
5. Settings > Daemons: the tor row renders with the tor name and the tor log path,
   and it is the only toggleable row (extend the existing canToggle coverage).
6. Settings > Daemons: there is NO configure/token action and NO reset-environment
   action on any row. Assert on absence by the old ValueKeys so the test would catch a
   half-finished deletion - the current keys are `daemon.zrok.configure`,
   `zrok.tokenField` and `zrok.resetEnvironment` (settings_daemons_screen.dart lines
   152, 248, 251).
7. A test that the login/password UI on the Dashboard still exists and still works
   after this change. Its job is to catch the dangerous mistake of deleting the
   password along with the zrok enable token. If the existing suite already covers
   showSetPasswordDialog, extend it rather than duplicating.
8. Kotlin: DaemonControlTest - the toggle allow-list accepts the tor tunnel type and
   rejects the three core daemons.

Localisation: after editing the .arb files and regenerating, run the full suite again.
If the project has an l10n completeness test, a missing key in one of the 20 locales
must make it fail - check that it does by deliberately omitting one key from one
locale, running the suite, then putting it back.

## Context

The in-car Flutter UI (`net.bladewatch.flutter`, source in `flutter_ui/`) shows the
tunnel as a "Zrok Tunnel" row in Settings > Daemons, with a token-entry dialog and a
"reset environment" action, and renders a QR code of the tunnel URL on the Dashboard.
Tor replaces zrok. Tor has NO token, NO account and NO environment, so the entire
token UI is deleted rather than renamed.

Blocked by the service-host task. Do not start until the daemon's tunnelStatus IPC
command returns an onion URL, because the tests below assert against that contract.

The IPC contract does NOT change: still the method channel call
"daemon.tunnelStatus", still a JSON object with status / running / url. Only the
value of url changes, from https://<name>.share.zrok.io to http://<56-char>.onion.

## Files

Dart:
- `flutter_ui/lib/screens/settings/settings_daemons_models.dart` line 3-26: the
  DaemonKind enum, currently `zrokTunnel('ZROK_TUNNEL')` at line 7, with
  `canToggle => this == DaemonKind.zrokTunnel` at line 25. Rename to
  `torTunnel('TOR_TUNNEL')` and keep the native key in sync with whatever the service
  host task settled on - read that code, do not assume.
- `flutter_ui/lib/screens/settings/settings_daemons_screen.dart` (36 zrok references):
  line 64 name, line 72 icon, line 85 log path ('/data/local/tmp/zrok.log' becomes
  '/data/local/tmp/tor.log'), lines 107-120 the "no token configured" warning state,
  lines 150-158 the configure button, lines 232-260 `_showZrokDialog` and
  `_confirmResetZrok`. DELETE the dialog, the configure button, the reset action and
  the no-token warning state outright.
- `flutter_ui/lib/screens/settings/settings_daemons_controller.dart`: `zrokHasToken`,
  `getZrokToken` and the reset plumbing - delete.
- `flutter_ui/lib/screens/dashboard/dashboard_screen.dart` lines 500-556
  (`_ConnectCard`): line 542 renders `QrImageView(data: tunnel.url!, size: 160)` and
  line 546 renders the URL as text underneath. The QR needs NO code change to point at
  the onion - it already encodes whatever tunnel.url is - but see the two UI problems
  below.
- `flutter_ui/lib/screens/dashboard/dashboard_models.dart` / `dashboard_controller.dart`:
  TunnelPhase and the tunnel state.
- Also carrying zrok references: `flutter_ui/lib/shell/app_shell.dart`,
  `flutter_ui/lib/platform/daemon_channel.dart`,
  `flutter_ui/lib/screens/settings/settings_overlay_controller.dart`,
  `flutter_ui/lib/screens/diagnostics/*`, `flutter_ui/lib/screens/startup/startup_models.dart`,
  `flutter_ui/lib/main.dart`.

Flutter-side Kotlin (same APK, separate Gradle build):
- `flutter_ui/android/app/src/main/kotlin/net/bladewatch/bladewatch_ui/daemon/DaemonControl.kt`
  lines 29-53: doc comments naming ZROK_TUNNEL and ZrokLauncher, and the toggle
  allow-list.
- `flutter_ui/android/app/src/main/kotlin/net/bladewatch/bladewatch_ui/config/SecretConfigChannel.kt`
  line 8: a comment about the Zrok token dialog. If nothing else in the app still
  needs the secret channel after the token dialog is gone, say so in the issue notes
  but do NOT delete the channel in this task.

Localisation - 22 keys, in `flutter_ui/lib/l10n/app_en.arb` plus 19 other locales
(app_de, app_es, app_fr, app_hi, app_it, app_ja, app_ko, app_nb, app_nl, app_pt,
app_pt_BR, app_ru, app_th, app_tr, app_vi, app_zh, app_zh_CN, app_zh_TW):

  daemon_name_zrok, dashboard_starting_zrok, dialog_zrok_reset_message,
  dialog_zrok_reset_title, dialog_zrok_token_message, dialog_zrok_token_title,
  settings_daemons_zrok_configure, settings_daemons_zrok_reset_button,
  toast_resetting_zrok, toast_zrok_reset_partial, toast_zrok_reset_success,
  toast_zrok_reset_warnings, toast_zrok_token_delete_failed, toast_zrok_token_deleted,
  toast_zrok_token_save_failed, toast_zrok_token_saved, tunnel_label_zrok,
  zrok_enable_token_hint, zrok_no_token_configured, zrok_reset_environment,
  zrok_reset_environment_desc, zrok_token_storage_note

Only three survive, renamed: daemon_name_tor ("Tor Tunnel"), tunnel_label_tor ("Tor"),
dashboard_starting_tor ("Starting Tor tunnel..."). DELETE the other 19 from every
locale. Add the ONE new key named in the UI section below
(dashboard_tor_bootstrapping). The instructions-dialog strings belong to the
follow-up issue, not to this one.

`flutter_ui/lib/gen/l10n/*` is GENERATED - never hand-edit it. Regenerate with
`flutter gen-l10n` (or a normal flutter build, which runs it) after editing the .arb
files.

`app/build.gradle.kts` line 944 holds a translation-coverage allow-list called
`intentionallyIdentical` containing "daemon_name_zrok" and "tunnel_label_zrok" (brand
names that are correctly identical in every locale). Rename those two entries to the
tor keys. Read the comment above the set at lines 930-940 before touching it.

## Two real UI problems to solve, not ignore

1. LENGTH. A v3 onion URL is 62 characters with the http:// prefix, versus about 40
   for the zrok URL. dashboard_screen.dart line 546 renders it as bodySmall text under
   the QR. It will very likely overflow on the head unit. CLAUDE.md's Testing section
   warns that `flutter test` uses a fixed-width placeholder font, so ANY text-fit or
   overflow assertion in a widget test is meaningless - you must look at it on the
   real head unit. Handle overflow deliberately (wrap, ellipsis, or a smaller
   monospace style); do not leave it to chance.
2. REACHABILITY. A QR holding an onion URL only opens in Tor Browser or a
   Tor-enabled browser; ordinary Chrome or Safari will simply fail with no useful
   error. The fix is an info button opening per-platform instructions, and that is a
   SEPARATE issue which depends on this one. Do NOT build it here and do NOT add a
   hint string here - just leave room beside the QR card's heading for an icon button
   so the follow-up stays a small diff.

Also add dashboard_tor_bootstrapping ("Connecting to Tor...") for the state where the
daemon reports running=true with url=null. The service host reports that for roughly
80 seconds on a cold start (6 seconds on a warm restart), so it is a state users WILL
see, not a corner case. Check whether the existing TunnelPhase already has a
"connecting" phase covering it before adding anything new.

## Constraints

- Do NOT change the tunnelStatus IPC contract or the method channel names.
- Do NOT touch authentication. The password / token UI on the Dashboard
  (loadAuthState, toggleTokenVisibility, copyTokenToClipboard,
  showRegenerateConfirmation, showSetPasswordDialog - see the class doc at
  dashboard_screen.dart line 500) is the LOGIN password and stays exactly as it is.
  Only the ZROK ENABLE TOKEN, a completely different thing, is being deleted. Do not
  confuse the two - deleting the login password would remove the only authentication
  in front of a publicly reachable onion address.
- Do NOT add a QR code library, a Tor library, or any new dependency. qr_flutter is
  already in `flutter_ui/pubspec.yaml` line 45 and is all that is needed.
- Do NOT add golden tests. This project deliberately has none; visual parity is
  verified on the head unit.
- Keep the Settings > Daemons row list and ordering otherwise unchanged.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] No file under `flutter_ui/lib`, `flutter_ui/test` or
      `flutter_ui/android/app/src` contains the string "zrok" (case-insensitive).
- [ ] All 19 dead l10n keys are gone from all 20 .arb files; the 3 renamed keys and
      the 1 new key exist in all 20; `flutter_ui/lib/gen/l10n/` is regenerated, not
      hand-edited.
- [ ] `app/build.gradle.kts` intentionallyIdentical lists the tor keys, not the zrok
      ones, and the translation-coverage check still passes.
- [ ] The Dashboard QR encodes the onion URL and the URL text does not overflow on
      the real head unit (state in the issue notes that you looked at it on device).
- [ ] The token dialog and reset-environment action are gone from the UI.
- [ ] Every test in the TDD list above exists and you observed each one FAIL before
      the implementation.
- [ ] The 13 zrok-era Dart tests and 2 Kotlin tests were UPDATED, not deleted.
- [ ] `cd flutter_ui && flutter analyze` is clean.
- [ ] `cd flutter_ui && flutter test` passes.
- [ ] `cd flutter_ui && flutter test --coverage && cd .. && tools/check_flutter_coverage.sh` passes.
- [ ] `cd flutter_ui/android && ./gradlew koverVerify` passes at its 100% bound. NOTE:
      this is a SEPARATE Gradle build - the repo-root koverVerify does NOT cover it and
      will pass while this one fails. CLAUDE.md records that the gate silently drifted
      to 96.2% once because nobody ran it.
- [ ] No files are staged or committed by you.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build
compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous,
stop and ask rather than guessing.
close_reason: DaemonKind.zrokTunnel -> torTunnel (TOR_TUNNEL). Token dialog, reset-environment action, configure button and the no-token warning state all deleted; SettingsDaemonsController lost its ConfigChannel dependency with them. l10n: 19 dead keys removed from all 20 locales, 3 renamed (daemon_name_tor, tunnel_label_tor, dashboard_starting_tor), 1 added (dashboard_tor_bootstrapping) translated into all 20; gen/l10n regenerated; the gradle intentionallyIdentical allow-list updated. DaemonChannel.tunnelUrl widened to tunnelStatus() returning running+url - its own comment said to widen it if a caller ever needed the flag, and with Tor the running-but-no-address window is ~82s instead of a second, so TunnelPhase.connecting is now reachable and rendered with a spinner instead of a false 'No tunnel running'. QR encodes the onion URL; the 62-char address is centred, monospace and wraps. Gates: flutter analyze clean, 1444 tests pass, Dart coverage 99.87%, flutter_ui/android koverVerify green, service-host test+koverVerify+assembleDebug green. Zero zrok references left anywhere under flutter_ui. Nothing staged or committed. NOTE: the onion URL length needs checking on the real panel - flutter test uses a fixed-width placeholder font so no widget test can judge it (deferred to the device-verification task).

title: Service host: replace ZrokLauncher with a Tor onion service and gate tunnelStatus on bootstrap
description:
## TDD - required, write the test first

This project works test-first. Do NOT write implementation before a failing test
exists. For every behaviour below: write the test, run it, SEE IT FAIL for the right
reason, write the smallest code that passes, re-run. If a new test passes on its first
run, the test is wrong - fix the test before touching the code.

Existing tests to read FIRST for house style and for the fake/stub helpers they
already provide (they are your templates, do not invent a new test harness):

- `app/src/test/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/TunnelStatusCommandTest.java`
  - this is the closest analogue; it drives the tunnelStatus command with a fake log
  file via the `zrokLogPathForTest` seam at TcpCommandServer.java line 785.
- `app/src/test/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/DaemonStatusCommandTest.java`
- `app/src/test/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/DaemonSetEnabledCommandTest.java`
- `app/src/test/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/IpcRoundTripTest.java`
- `app/src/test/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/config/SecretConfigStoreTest.java`

Write these tests, in this order, each RED before it is GREEN:

1. tunnelStatus with tor NOT running: running=false, url=null.
2. tunnelStatus with tor running but a tor.log containing no "Bootstrapped 100%"
   line: running=true, url=null. (This is the new behaviour that did not exist for
   zrok - see the reachability-window section below. Expect this one to be the test
   that catches the most bugs.)
3. tunnelStatus with tor running and a tor.log whose latest entries include
   "Bootstrapped 100%": running=true, url="http://<addr>.onion" read from the
   hostname file.
4. tunnelStatus where the hostname file is missing or empty but bootstrap reached
   100%: running=true, url=null. Must not throw, must not return a partial URL.
5. tunnelStatus where tor.log contains a "Bootstrapped 100%" from a PREVIOUS run
   followed by a fresh "Bootstrapped 0% (starting)": running=true, url=null. The log
   is appended across launches, so a stale success line must not be read as live.
   (The existing readZrokTunnelUrl has a long comment at line 800 about exactly this
   class of cross-launch log drift - read it.)
6. A log larger than the tail limit still yields the right answer and does not read
   the whole file into memory. The existing ZROK_LOG_TAIL_BYTES test coverage shows
   the shape; keep an equivalent bound for tor.log.
7. The daemon toggle allow-list accepts the tor tunnel type and still rejects
   CAMERA_DAEMON / SENTRY_DAEMON / ACC_SENTRY_DAEMON (extend the existing
   DaemonSetEnabledCommandTest cases rather than writing a new file).
8. The secret store no longer exposes a "zrok" section, and an existing secrets file
   that still has one does not break loading (back-compat on a real device that was
   running the old build).
9. A test that the hard reset command string kills tor but does NOT contain any
   instruction that removes the hidden-service directory. This is a guard against a
   future "cleanup" deleting the permanent onion identity - assert on the generated
   command string, the same way the existing DaemonHardReset coverage does.

Keep the testable seam: expose a test hook for the tor log and hostname paths in the
same style as the existing `zrokLogPathForTest` static at TcpCommandServer.java line
785. Do not add a mocking framework; this suite does not use one.

Coverage is gated by `./gradlew koverVerify` and the gate RATCHETS UPWARD and may
never be lowered (CLAUDE.md, Testing). Deleting ~700 lines of ZrokLauncher will move
the ratio - if the gate then fails because the remaining code is less covered, write
the missing tests. Do not lower the bound.

## Context

The service host (`net.bladewatch.app`) launches the zrok tunnel as a shell-UID
process over ADB and reports its URL to the UI over loopback IPC. Replace all of that
with a Tor onion service. Blocked by the task that ships the tor binary - do not start
until libtor.so is being packaged.

Files that currently know about zrok in the service host:

- `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/launcher/ZrokLauncher.kt` (~700 lines,
  248 zrok references) - DELETE this file.
- `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/daemon/ZrokController.kt` - rename to
  TorController and gut the token plumbing.
- `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/model/DaemonType.kt` line 12:
  ZROK_TUNNEL("Zrok Tunnel", "zrok")
- `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/daemon/DaemonStartupManager.kt`
  lines 9, 42, 171, 270-330 (startTunnelFromPreferences, startZrokOnBoot,
  restartTunnelIfEnabled).
- `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/TcpCommandServer.java`
  line 56 (DAEMON_PROCESS_NAMES "ZROK_TUNNEL" to "zrok"), lines 550-569 (the
  "tunnelStatus" command), line 716 (the toggleable allow-list), lines 779-830
  (zrokLogPath, ZROK_LOG_TAIL_BYTES, readZrokTunnelUrl).
- `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/launcher/DaemonHardReset.java`
  lines 95, 107, 109 (pkill/killall of zrok).
- `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/launcher/AdbDaemonLauncher.kt`
  lines 16, 19, 153-154 (comments only).
- `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/util/PreferencesManager.kt`
  lines 25-27 and 174-190 (last_zrok_url, zrok_unique_name, zrok_enable_token).
- `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/config/UnifiedConfigManager.kt`
  line 724 (comment) and line 916 (the "zrok" secret section allow-list).
- `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/model/PresetCommand.kt` lines 23, 27.
- `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/viewmodel/DaemonsViewModel.kt`.
- `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/HttpServer.java` lines 41, 250,
  254 - comments and X-Forwarded / Host handling written for zrok's HTTP rewriter.
  Tor does NOT rewrite Host and does NOT add X-Forwarded headers; the onion service
  hands the daemon a plain TCP connection to 127.0.0.1:8080. Read that code and decide
  whether the rewrite handling is still needed; if you remove any of it, say why in the
  issue notes.
- `app/build.gradle.kts` line 462 - a comment naming ZrokController; update the name.

## The tor runtime contract

Launch tor as a shell-UID process the same way the zrok binary is launched today
(AdbShellExecutor plus the extracted nativeLibraryDir binary). Concretely:

torrc, written to /data/local/tmp/tor/torrc:

    SocksPort 0
    DataDirectory /data/local/tmp/tor/data
    HiddenServiceDir /data/local/tmp/tor/hs
    HiddenServicePort 80 127.0.0.1:8080
    Log notice file /data/local/tmp/tor.log

Notes, all verified on the head unit on 2026-09-14:

- The feasibility test ran with "SocksPort 9050" because the test needed a client.
  Production does not; SocksPort 0 means no listener at all. Verify the onion still
  publishes with SocksPort 0 before closing.
- DataDirectory and HiddenServiceDir MUST be mode 700 and owned by the UID tor runs
  as (shell, 2000), or tor refuses to start. Create them with mkdir -p and chmod 700
  in the launch script.
- tor writes the onion address to /data/local/tmp/tor/hs/hostname as a single line,
  for example: abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz234567abcdefghijklmnopqrstuv.onion
  Present it to clients as http://<that>.onion (port 80, plain HTTP - the onion
  protocol is already end-to-end encrypted and authenticated to the service key).
- The hostname file is mode 600 owned by shell, so the app UID CANNOT read it
  directly. It must come to the app over the existing tunnelStatus IPC command, which
  runs inside the daemon at shell UID. This is the same shape as today.
- Cold start is ~82 s to "Bootstrapped 100%"; a warm restart with an existing
  DataDirectory is ~6 s.

## IMPORTANT: the "running but not yet reachable" window

zrok's URL only appeared in its log once the tunnel was live, so "url != null" meant
"reachable". Tor is different: hs/hostname exists within about a second of the FIRST
launch and then forever, long before the network is up. If you report url != null as
soon as the file exists, the Dashboard will show an online QR code pointing at a
service that is not reachable for the next 80 seconds.

So tunnelStatus must gate "online" on the bootstrap state, not on the hostname file:
read /data/local/tmp/tor.log and treat the service as online only after a
"Bootstrapped 100%" line appears more recently than the current process started.
Until then report running=true, url=null, which the Flutter client already renders as
"connecting" (see the comment at TcpCommandServer.java line 565). Reuse the existing
bounded tail-read helper rather than loading the log into memory - the existing
readZrokTunnelUrl at line 800 documents an 85 MB allocation bug caused by doing that.

## Constraints

- The onion private key at /data/local/tmp/tor/hs/hs_ed25519_secret_key IS the
  permanent identity of this car's remote access. Never log it, never copy it to
  shared storage, never return it over IPC, never let it reach a commit. Treat it
  exactly like the entries in bladewatch_secrets.json (see the Security Notes in
  CLAUDE.md).
- DaemonHardReset MUST NOT delete /data/local/tmp/tor/hs. Deleting it destroys the
  permanent onion address and every saved QR code stops working. It may delete
  /data/local/tmp/tor/data (the consensus cache) - that only costs a slow bootstrap.
  Make this explicit in a comment so nobody "cleans up" the whole tor directory later.
- Do NOT weaken auth. The password / JWT path in AuthManager and AuthMiddleware stays
  exactly as it is and stays mandatory. An onion address is a capability URL, not
  authentication.
- Do NOT add bridges, pluggable transports, obfs4 or IPtProxy. The head unit reached
  guards on 443/9001 with no interference.
- Do NOT re-add a token, account or device-registration concept. Tor needs none, and
  removing that machinery is the point of this change.
- Delete the zrok secret section rather than renaming it: tor has no secrets to store.
  Check whether an existing device has stale "zrok" keys in
  /data/local/tmp/bladewatch_secrets.json and decide whether to prune them on startup;
  if you skip the pruning, note that in the issue.
- Keep the daemon's existing process-name convention: launch tor with a recognisable
  nice-name so pgrep/killall work. Remember the kernel caps /proc/<pid>/comm at 15
  characters (CLAUDE.md documents this trap for acc_sentry_daemon).
- Do not touch Flutter code here - that is a separate issue.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] ZrokLauncher.kt is deleted and no file under app/src/main contains the string
      "zrok" (case-insensitive) except a single comment recording the removal, matching
      how the sing-box removal is recorded in AdbDaemonLauncher.kt.
- [ ] A TorLauncher exists that writes the torrc above, creates the 700 directories,
      launches the binary, and surfaces the onion URL.
- [ ] The IPC command name stays "tunnelStatus" with the same response shape
      (status/running/url) so the Flutter client contract does not break.
- [ ] tunnelStatus returns url=null while tor is running but has not reached
      "Bootstrapped 100%", and returns http://<addr>.onion afterwards.
- [ ] DaemonHardReset kills tor but leaves /data/local/tmp/tor/hs intact, with a
      comment saying why.
- [ ] The secret store no longer has a "zrok" section and no token UI path remains in
      the service host.
- [ ] Every test in the TDD list above exists, and you observed each one FAIL
      before writing the code that makes it pass.
- [ ] The zrok-era tests listed above were UPDATED, not deleted.
- [ ] `./gradlew test` passes and `./gradlew koverVerify` passes (the gate ratchets
      upward and may never be lowered - see CLAUDE.md Testing).
- [ ] `./gradlew assembleDebug` produces an APK.
- [ ] No files are staged or committed by you.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build
compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous,
stop and ask rather than guessing.
close_reason: ZrokLauncher (1359 lines) and ZrokController (322) deleted; TorLauncher (~290) and TorController (~128) replace them. torrc: SocksPort 0, DataDirectory, HiddenServiceDir, HiddenServicePort 80 to 127.0.0.1:8080, notice log. Dirs created 700 or tor refuses to start. Process installed as bladewatch_tor (14 chars, under the comm cap) so basename(argv[0]) matching works. tunnelStatus keeps its shape but now gates url on BOOTSTRAP state parsed from tor.log, not on the hostname file, which persists forever: running=true/url=null during the ~82s cold start. Hard reset kills tor and is asserted never to delete the hidden-service dir. Secret store zrok section gone. SECURITY FIX found while doing this: the loopback auth bypass was gated on X-Forwarded-* headers, which zrok injected and Tor does not - a debug build with the tunnel up would have handed every remote onion visitor local trust. AuthMiddleware now also requires no tunnel process, cached 10s, failing closed. 20 new or updated tests, all observed red first. gradlew test, koverVerify and assembleDebug green. One recorded zrok mention remains, in AuthMiddleware, explaining that fix. Nothing staged or committed.

title: Ship the tor binary via a verified Gradle download and drop libzrok.so
description:
## Context

BladeWatch currently ships the zrok binary as a fake native library:
`app/src/main/jniLibs/arm64-v8a/libzrok.so` (19.2 MB, COMMITTED to git). Android
extracts anything in jniLibs to the app's nativeLibraryDir with the execute bit set,
which is how a plain executable gets shipped and run on a non-rooted device.

Tor replaces it and uses the exact same trick, but the binary must NOT be committed.
`app/build.gradle.kts` already has a verified-download helper for native deps
(`fun org.gradle.api.Project.downloadVerified(url, dest, expectedSha256, label)` at
line 34, plus `hasExpectedSha256` / `verifySha256`), used by the `downloadOpenH264`
task registered at line 73 and a matching `downloadOpenCV` task. Follow that pattern
exactly.

## TDD - required, write the test first

This project works test-first. Do NOT write the implementation before the failing
test exists. The loop for every step below is: write the test, run it, SEE IT FAIL
for the right reason, then write the smallest code that makes it pass, then re-run.
"Saw it fail" is part of the work - if a new test passes the first time you run it,
the test is wrong, not the code.

For this task the guard is a structural JVM test. Add it to
`app/src/test/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/` next to the existing structural guards
`ServiceHostManifestTest` and `NoSelfLaunchIntentTest` (read one of them first for the
house style - they scan files on disk rather than calling into app code).

Write, in this order:

1. A test asserting `app/src/main/jniLibs/arm64-v8a/libtor.so` exists and its SHA-256
   is 9aa3a500bc3edd495cd33c61fd65d536f49b92692e16f6e23e3ada44e76a94a9.
   Run it. It MUST fail - the file does not exist yet.
2. A test asserting `app/src/main/jniLibs/arm64-v8a/libzrok.so` does NOT exist.
   Run it. It MUST fail - the file is still committed today.
3. Only then do the Gradle work below and make both pass.

CRITICAL - Gradle up-to-date blindness (this project has been bitten by it, see the
Testing section of CLAUDE.md): a test that reads a file which is not on the test
classpath will NOT re-run when that file changes, so it can silently pass against a
broken tree. You MUST declare the jniLibs directory as an explicit test input in
`app/build.gradle.kts`. That file already does exactly this for AndroidManifest.xml
and src/main/java - copy that pattern. Prove it works: run the test, delete
libtor.so, run the test again, and confirm it FAILS rather than reporting UP-TO-DATE.
A guard that cannot fail is worse than no guard.

## What to do

1. Add a Gradle task `downloadTor` in `app/build.gradle.kts`, modelled on
   `downloadOpenH264` (line 73 onward):
   - URL:
     https://repo1.maven.org/maven2/org/briarproject/tor-android/0.4.8.14/tor-android-0.4.8.14.jar
   - Expected SHA-256 of that jar:
     fc7c4f5007a98132ba84534a873f101951d2d554d5da5f2031b85c277f8617a6
   - The jar is a zip containing armeabi-v7a/, arm64-v8a/, x86/ and x86_64/
     libtor.so. Extract ONLY `arm64-v8a/libtor.so` (BladeWatch is arm64-v8a only) to
     `app/src/main/jniLibs/arm64-v8a/libtor.so`.
   - Expected SHA-256 of the extracted arm64-v8a/libtor.so:
     9aa3a500bc3edd495cd33c61fd65d536f49b92692e16f6e23e3ada44e76a94a9
     Verify it with `verifySha256` after extraction, the same way the OpenH264 task
     verifies its extracted .so.
   - Skip the download when the destination already exists AND matches the checksum,
     and redownload when the checksum differs. Copy that logic from `downloadOpenH264`.
2. Wire `downloadTor` into the build so it runs before the APK is packaged. The
   existing native downloads are hooked at `app/build.gradle.kts` line 126
   (`dependsOn("downloadOpenH264", "downloadOpenCV")`) - add `downloadTor` alongside
   them, or to `preBuild` if that line turns out to be a CMake-only hook. Whichever you
   pick, a clean checkout followed by `./gradlew assembleDebug` MUST produce an APK
   containing lib/arm64-v8a/libtor.so.
3. Delete the committed zrok binary: `git rm app/src/main/jniLibs/arm64-v8a/libzrok.so`
   (delete the file; do NOT run git commit - see the Git Workflow section of
   CLAUDE.md, the developer commits manually).
4. Add `app/src/main/jniLibs/arm64-v8a/libtor.so` to `.gitignore` so the downloaded
   binary is never committed. Check whether jniLibs already has a gitignore entry
   pattern before adding a new one.

## Constraints

- Do NOT commit the tor binary. It is a build artifact, exactly like the OpenH264 and
  OpenCV libraries.
- Do NOT download tor from anywhere other than Maven Central with the pinned SHA-256
  above. An unverified tunnel binary is a supply-chain hole.
- Do NOT add the tor-android jar as a Gradle `implementation` dependency. That would
  put the JNI wrapper classes in the APK. We only want the raw binary.
- Do NOT add armeabi-v7a / x86 / x86_64 variants. The head unit is arm64-v8a only and
  each one is another 5 MB.
- Do not touch any Kotlin/Java/Dart source in this task. Wiring the launcher is a
  separate issue that depends on this one.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `./gradlew assembleDebug` succeeds from a clean state and downloads tor.
- [ ] `unzip -l app/build/outputs/apk/debug/bladewatch-*-arm64-v8a-debug.apk | grep libtor.so`
      shows exactly one entry, under lib/arm64-v8a/.
- [ ] `shasum -a 256 app/src/main/jniLibs/arm64-v8a/libtor.so` equals
      9aa3a500bc3edd495cd33c61fd65d536f49b92692e16f6e23e3ada44e76a94a9
- [ ] Corrupting the downloaded file and re-running the build re-downloads it (test
      this by appending a byte and running the task again).
- [ ] `app/src/main/jniLibs/arm64-v8a/libzrok.so` no longer exists and no longer
      appears in `git ls-files`.
- [ ] `git status` shows the tor binary as ignored, not as an untracked or staged file.
- [ ] The two structural tests above exist, and you observed each one FAIL before
      the implementation and pass after.
- [ ] Deleting libtor.so makes the guard test fail rather than report UP-TO-DATE
      (proves the test input is declared).
- [ ] `./gradlew test` still passes.
- [ ] No files are staged or committed by you.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build
compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous,
stop and ask rather than guessing.
close_reason: downloadTor Gradle task fetches tor 0.4.8.14 from Maven Central (jar sha256 pinned), extracts arm64-v8a/libtor.so into jniLibs and verifies it; hooked to preBuild. libzrok.so deleted (19.2 MB off the repo), libtor.so gitignored as a build artifact. TorBinaryPackagingTest guards both, jniLibs declared as a test input; observed RED then GREEN, and proved not up-to-date-blind by corrupting the binary and re-running with -x downloadTor. APK contains exactly one lib/arm64-v8a/libtor.so and no zrok. gradlew test green. Nothing staged or committed.

title: Replace the zrok tunnel with a Tor onion service
description:
## Goal

Remove the zrok tunnel entirely and replace it with a Tor v3 onion service that
publishes the existing web app (CameraDaemon's HTTP server on 127.0.0.1:8080) for
remote access. The Dashboard QR code must encode the onion URL. The existing
password / JWT auth is UNCHANGED and stays mandatory.

## Why

zrok requires an account token, a one-time `zrok enable` per device (hard limit of 5
on the free tier), a reserved-share dance to keep a stable URL, and a 401
re-enable repair loop. That machinery is the reason
`app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/launcher/ZrokLauncher.kt` is ~700 lines.
A Tor onion service needs none of it: no account, no token, no device limit, and the
onion address is permanent because it is derived from a key file on disk.

## Feasibility already proven on the real head unit (2026-09-14)

Tested live on the BYD head unit, then torn down. Do not re-litigate this; it works:

- Binary: `org.briarproject:tor-android:0.4.8.14` on Maven Central ships
  `arm64-v8a/libtor.so`, which IS the tor executable (ELF PIE, interpreter
  /system/bin/linker64), 5.2 MB. It runs as shell UID on the head unit with no root.
  Reported version on device: "Tor version 0.4.8.14".
- Cold bootstrap: 82 s to "Bootstrapped 100%". Warm restart with a populated
  DataDirectory: 6 s.
- The onion address SURVIVED a restart unchanged (permanent URL).
- The real Angular index was served over the onion (HTTP 200), and the H.264
  WebSocket on /ws upgraded (101) and sustained 216 kbit/s for 20 s with no stall.
- Throughput 62-75 KB/s; warm request TTFB 2.1-6.5 s; a cold client's very first
  connect took 49 s.
- Cost on device: ~65 MB RSS, ~5% CPU.
- The head unit reached Tor guards on 443/9001 with no censorship, so NO bridges and
  no pluggable transports are needed.
- Device clock was correct, which Tor requires.

## Known caveats to design around, not discover again

1. After the service restarts, a client that was ALREADY connected stays broken for
   several minutes on stale introduction points. A fresh client connects immediately.
   Do not treat that as a bug in the implementation.
2. Latency is 2-6 s per request. The SPA loads once then makes small API calls, so it
   is usable, but it is slower than zrok's HTTPS edge. This is inherent to Tor.
3. A QR code holding an onion URL only resolves in Tor Browser (or Orbot). Ordinary
   Chrome/Safari will fail. See the Flutter task for the UI hint.

## Children

Do them in order; each child names its own dependencies. Do not start a child before
its blocker is closed.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build
compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous,
stop and ask rather than guessing.
close_reason:
All eight children are closed and the migration is verified end to end on the head unit.

The tunnel is a Tor v3 onion service with no account, token or registration, and a permanent address derived from a key on disk. Verified on the car: auto-starts unaided after install AND after a full reboot; the address was byte-identical across a tunnel restart and a reboot; cold bootstrap 61 s, warm 6 s; and the bootstrap gate withheld the address for the full minute the hostname file existed before the service was reachable - the headline behaviour of this epic.

The security fix is the part that mattered most. The old tunnel injected X-Forwarded-* headers, which is what switched off the loopback auth bypass; Tor injects nothing, so onion traffic arriving on 127.0.0.1 was indistinguishable from a local app. Confirmed live on the car, same request, two builds: old returned HTTP 200 plus deviceId, battery voltage, SoC, charging state and camera list; this branch returns 401. AuthMiddleware now also requires that no tunnel process is running.

The owner confirmed the web app loads and works over the onion from a phone - slow but usable, consistent with the measured 62-75 KB/s.

Follow-ups filed rather than folded in: BladeWatch-nobf Part B (live video needs WebCodecs, which Tor Browser's Firefox ESR lacks - Part A now says so honestly instead of offering an unwinnable retry) and BladeWatch-4s7w's on-panel fit check.

comments.author: Andrew Loable
comments.text:
DUPLICATE TOR LAUNCHES - root-caused and fixed 2026-09-15.

Symptom in tor's log on the head unit, once per deployment:

    09:26:31 [notice] Tor 0.4.8.14
    09:26:31 [notice] Tor 0.4.8.14          <- two starts, SAME SECOND
    09:26:31 [warn]  ...another Tor process is running with the same data directory...
    09:26:36 [err]   No, it's still there. Exiting.

Same second, so not the 30 s health-check racing itself.

ROOT CAUSE: DaemonStartupManager.initializeOnAppLaunch() was not idempotent, and
MainActivity calls it TWICE - once from onCreate, and again from the ADB-auth-granted
callback. That second call is the recovery path for a reinstall, where the first attempt
failed because the reinstall wiped the app's ADB key and no daemon could start. Each call
scheduled a fresh set of delayed work (+45 s core daemons, +60 s optional daemons, +90 s
health check), so after a reinstall everything fired twice, about a second apart. It lined
up exactly with the three deployments in this session: 09:13, 09:26, 09:38.

FIX, in two layers.

1. Root: initializeOnAppLaunch() now drops previously queued work first
   (handler.removeCallbacksAndMessages(null)) and clears healthCheckRunning, so a second
   call REPLACES the first instead of duplicating it. Deliberately not a one-shot guard -
   that would block the recovery call, which is the one that matters after a reinstall.

2. Belt and braces: TorLauncher.launchCommand() is now a no-op when tor is already up, with
   the check INSIDE the single shell invocation:
       if pidof bladewatch_tor > /dev/null 2>&1; then echo already_running; else nohup ... & fi
   Checking from Kotlin first would not do: that is check-then-act across two ADB round
   trips and the loser of a race still launches. pidof rather than pgrep, because pgrep
   consults comm only, which is "main" for app_process daemons.

VERIFIED ON THE DEVICE. The guard was exercised directly against a running tor (answered
already_running, pid unchanged, still one process), and then a full uninstall/reinstall
cycle was run with the log rotated first, so before and after cover the identical sequence:

    BEFORE:  5 duplicate-lock warnings, 15 [err] lines
    AFTER:   0 duplicate-lock warnings,  0 [err] lines, 1 live process, Bootstrapped 100%

Note the two "Tor 0.4.8.14" lines that remain in a healthy log are ONE start - tor prints
its version when it opens the log and again in its startup banner. Count "another Tor
process" or [err] instead.

Worth keeping: this also stopped writing [err] lines into the file TcpCommandServer's
bootstrap gate reads. The gate only looks for Bootstrapped 0%/100% so it was never fooled,
but a startup path that logs errors on every reinstall is noise that hides real faults.

title: A build without Node silently shipped an APK with no web UI
description:
Found during final code review, while assessing whether the APKs could be built
in GitHub Actions.

## Problem

buildAngularWebUI (app/build.gradle.kts) skipped itself with only a WARNING when
npm/Node was not on PATH. Its comment claimed this was safe: "The dist output is
checked in at web/dist" and "the committed dist is used instead".

That was false. Neither path is committed -- .gitignore:44 ignores web/dist/ and
.gitignore:46 ignores app/src/main/assets/web/angular/. Verified with git ls-files:
0 tracked files under either.

So on a fresh clone or any CI runner without Node:
  - buildAngularWebUI is skipped
  - app/src/main/assets/web/angular/ is empty
  - assembleRelease SUCCEEDS
  - the APK ships with NO Angular web UI

The Angular SPA is the remote browser/tunnel client, so a tunnel user would get
nothing, with no build-time signal at all. This is the same silent-degradation
class as BladeWatch-1nnw, one layer down in the build.

## Fix applied

New verifyWebAssetsPresent task, wired into preBuild alongside buildAngularWebUI.
It fails the build when npm is unavailable AND no previously-built assets exist,
and warns (without failing) when npm is missing but assets from an earlier run are
present, since those still package correctly and only risk being stale.

Corrected the false comment to state that neither directory is committed.

## Gradle gotcha worth remembering

The first attempt threw the GradleException from inside buildAngularWebUI's
onlyIf. It failed the build correctly but Gradle SWALLOWED the message, printing
only:

    Could not evaluate onlyIf predicate for task ':app:buildAngularWebUI'.
    > Could not evaluate spec for 'Task satisfies onlyIf spec'.

A developer would have had no idea why. onlyIf is now a pure predicate and the
check lives in a task's doLast, where the message is printed in full. Verified by
simulating a runner with no Node (PATH=/usr/bin:/bin and the assets moved aside).

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] normal build (npm present) still SUCCESSFUL
- [x] build with no npm and no prebuilt assets FAILS with the full explanation
- [x] build with no npm but existing assets warns and proceeds
- [x] all three gate sets green; 1450 Dart tests, coverage >= 99%
close_reason: Fixed with a verifyWebAssetsPresent task wired into preBuild; the false 'dist is checked in' comment corrected. Both the pass and fail paths verified by simulating a Node-less runner.

title: A refused vehicle command with no message was reported as success
description:
Found while closing a coverage gap on the appearance revert path.

## Problem

_mapCommand (vehicle_controller.dart:182) maps an EMPTY message to null:

    message: m.message.isNotEmpty ? m.message : null

Five command paths then did "return result.message;" -- so when the daemon
refused WITHOUT a reason (200, success:false, empty message), the caller got
null. Every call site spells success as null:

    if (context.mounted && error != null) showVehicleCommandError(...)

So the optimistic value was reverted and the driver was told NOTHING: the
control visibly snapped back with no explanation, which reads as a broken tap
rather than a refused command. Affected the AC toggle, temperature, fan, and
both seat commands.

_persistAppearance had the identical bug in its own spelling
("resp.error.isNotEmpty ? resp.error : null"), affecting colour and model
selection.

Two smaller defects found in the same place:
- The window path fell back to a hardcoded English literal 'failed', on a screen
  that ships in 17 locales.
- The same two-line snackbar was hand-copied 8 times alongside two private
  helpers (_showError, _showAppearanceError) that were character-identical.

## Fix applied

- VehicleCommandResult.failure -- a non-null getter (message ?? outcome ?? '').
  All 5 return sites and the window path use it.
- _persistAppearance returns resp.error (empty, not null): a refusal with no
  reason is still a refusal.
- vehicle_screen.dart: one top-level showVehicleCommandError() replacing the two
  private helpers and all 8 inline copies; it substitutes the localised
  vehicle_action_failed for a blank message. That ARB key existed in all 19
  catalogs, ported from Android, and had never been wired to anything.

## Tests

- 4 new widget tests in vehicle_screen_test.dart (blank appearance refusal,
  appearance refusal WITH a reason, blank seat heat refusal, blank seat cool
  refusal). Mutation-verified.
- 3 new controller tests closing a refusal/throw symmetry gap: every command had
  only ONE of the two failure shapes pinned.
- Corrected a test that pinned the defect: "falls back to outcome, then failed"
  asserted the untranslatable English literal as the user-visible reason.
- Corrected 3 stale stubs that wrote "SetSelectedModel, {}" -- an empty body
  leaves ok false, so three tests named as happy paths were exercising the
  refusal path.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] flutter analyze clean
- [x] 1452 Dart tests green, coverage 99.87% (gate >= 99%)
- [x] Gradle validateArbCatalogs validateAndroidStrings validateI18nCatalogs
      test koverVerify assembleDebug all SUCCESSFUL
- [x] new tests mutation-verified against the unfixed source
close_reason: Fixed and verified in the same pass; full detail in the description. All gates green: flutter analyze clean, 1452 Dart tests, coverage 99.87 percent, Gradle validate/test/koverVerify/assembleDebug SUCCESSFUL. New tests mutation-verified.

title: Climate and seat controls showed states the car never entered
description:
## Problem

Six vehicle controls showed the driver a state the CAR NEVER ENTERED.

The climate temperature stepper, the fan stepper, and both seat heat/cool cycles
applied their new value optimistically, sent the command, and discarded the
outcome:

    Future<void> incTemp() async {
      _setpointC += 1;
      notifyListeners();
      try {
        await _vehicleService.setClimate(...);
      } catch (_) {}          // <- and no check of the response either
    }

Two independent failures, both silent:

1. `catch (_) {}` swallowed a THROWN error, leaving the optimistic value.
2. Nothing checked the response's success flag. **The daemon answers HTTP 200
   with `success:false` when it REFUSES a command**, so nothing throws — the
   catch never runs even in principle, and the refusal path is the NORMAL one for
   an unavailable control, not an edge case.

So: tap +, see 25 C, car stays at 24. Tap seat heat, see level 1, seat stays off.
No error, no revert, no way to tell.

This is precisely the defect BladeWatch-p7vi fixed on the SoH writes -- "save()
and reset() checked only for a THROWN error, but the daemon answers HTTP 200 with
success:false, so every refused write was reported to the user as a success". It
was fixed there and left in place here, three methods away from
`toggleMaxCooling`, which does it correctly.

## Why it survived: the tests asserted the bug

    test('incTemp increases and sends set_temp', () async {
      rpc.stubJson('VehicleService', 'SetClimate', {'success': false});   // REFUSED
      await c.incTemp();
      expect(c.setpointC, 25);                                           // "correct"
    });

That test stubs a refusal and asserts the value STAYS. Two more were named
outright: "a throw from incTemp/decTemp is swallowed (no crash, no revert)" and
"a throw from cycleSeatHeat/Cool is swallowed". The behaviour was not overlooked,
it was pinned.

A fourth, 'nowMs defaults to the real wall clock when not injected', leaned on it
incidentally: it called incTemp() with an UNSTUBBED rpc and asserted the value
survived the resulting throw. Its real subject is the debounce clock; the setpoint
assertion was a proxy that only worked because failures were swallowed.

## Fix

All six now mirror `toggleAc`/`toggleMaxCooling`: check `_mapCommand(resp).ok`,
REVERT on failure, and return the message. Signatures changed from `Future<void>`
to `Future<String?>`, and the screen surfaces the message -- the steppers were
bare `VoidCallback`s, which is why they had no way to report even if they had
known.

The climate steppers share one `_stepClimate` helper (apply / revert / request)
rather than four copies of the same try-catch.

The seat cycles snapshot ALL FOUR seat fields before mutating, because turning
heat on clears vent and vice versa -- reverting only the pressed field would leave
the other one wrong. That is covered by its own test.

## Tests

- Corrected the test that stubbed `success:false` and expected the value to stick.
- Rewrote the three "is swallowed" tests to assert revert + report, each carrying a
  comment naming what the old assertion claimed.
- Repointed the wall-clock test at what it actually tests: that the call got past
  the debounce and attempted the RPC.
- Added refusal coverage: a refused set_temp reverts, a refused set_fan reverts,
  and a refused seat command reverts every seat field.

MUTATION-VERIFIED: changing `if (!result.ok)` to `if (false)` makes the suite fail.

## Verification

- flutter analyze clean; flutter test 1439 passed, 0 skipped.
- Dart coverage 99.97%. Kover green.
- `./gradlew validateArbCatalogs validateAndroidStrings test koverVerify
  assembleDebug assembleRelease`: SUCCESSFUL.
- NOT verified on the head unit: the display was asleep. Worth a look with a
  control the car will refuse -- the refusal path is the one that was broken and
  the one nobody exercises deliberately.

Nothing committed.

2. Nothing checked the response's success flag. **The daemon answers HTTP 200
   with `success:false` when it REFUSES a command**, so nothing throws — the
   catch never runs even in principle, and the refusal path is the NORMAL one for
   an unavailable control, not an edge case.

So: tap +, see 25 C, car stays at 24. Tap seat heat, see level 1, seat stays off.
No error, no revert, no way to tell.

This is precisely the defect BladeWatch-p7vi fixed on the SoH writes -- "save()
and reset() checked only for a THROWN error, but the daemon answers HTTP 200 with
success:false, so every refused write was reported to the user as a success". It
was fixed there and left in place here, three methods away from
`toggleMaxCooling`, which does it correctly.

## Why it survived: the tests asserted the bug

    test('incTemp increases and sends set_temp', () async {
      rpc.stubJson('VehicleService', 'SetClimate', {'success': false});   // REFUSED
      await c.incTemp();
      expect(c.setpointC, 25);                                           // "correct"
    });

That test stubs a refusal and asserts the value STAYS. Two more were named
outright: "a throw from incTemp/decTemp is swallowed (no crash, no revert)" and
"a throw from cycleSeatHeat/Cool is swallowed". The behaviour was not overlooked,
it was pinned.

A fourth, 'nowMs defaults to the real wall clock when not injected', leaned on it
incidentally: it called incTemp() with an UNSTUBBED rpc and asserted the value
survived the resulting throw. Its real subject is the debounce clock; the setpoint
assertion was a proxy that only worked because failures were swallowed.

## Fix

All six now mirror `toggleAc`/`toggleMaxCooling`: check `_mapCommand(resp).ok`,
REVERT on failure, and return the message. Signatures changed from `Future<void>`
to `Future<String?>`, and the screen surfaces the message -- the steppers were
bare `VoidCallback`s, which is why they had no way to report even if they had
known.

The climate steppers share one `_stepClimate` helper (apply / revert / request)
rather than four copies of the same try-catch.

The seat cycles snapshot ALL FOUR seat fields before mutating, because turning
heat on clears vent and vice versa -- reverting only the pressed field would leave
the other one wrong. That is covered by its own test.

## Tests

- Corrected the test that stubbed `success:false` and expected the value to stick.
- Rewrote the three "is swallowed" tests to assert revert + report, each carrying a
  comment naming what the old assertion claimed.
- Repointed the wall-clock test at what it actually tests: that the call got past
  the debounce and attempted the RPC.
- Added refusal coverage: a refused set_temp reverts, a refused set_fan reverts,
  and a refused seat command reverts every seat field.

MUTATION-VERIFIED: changing `if (!result.ok)` to `if (false)` makes the suite fail.

## Verification

- flutter analyze clean; flutter test 1439 passed, 0 skipped.
- Dart coverage 99.97%. Kover green.
- `./gradlew validateArbCatalogs validateAndroidStrings test koverVerify
  assembleDebug assembleRelease`: SUCCESSFUL.
- NOT verified on the head unit: the display was asleep. Worth a look with a
  control the car will refuse -- the refusal path is the one that was broken and
  the one nobody exercises deliberately.

Nothing committed.

title: Setup Guide must say daemons will not start without BYD autostart
description:
## Problem

If the user does not enable BladeWatch in BYD's app-start management
(com.byd.appstartmanagement), NO DAEMON STARTS ON A COLD BOOT and nothing tells
them. The dashcam silently records nothing until someone opens the app by hand.

Proven on the head unit 2026-09-14 (BladeWatch-5rew): with autostart off, a real
reboot produced 3 minutes 38 seconds of zero BladeWatch activity and no daemons;
with autostart on, all three daemons came up by t+75s and t+90s across two
consecutive reboots with nothing touched.

Note the mechanism, because it is counter-intuitive: BOOT_COMPLETED stays
suppressed either way (BYD logs "ssc_skip reciever for uid 10073 ...
broadcast=android.intent.action.BOOT_COMPLETED"). BootReceiver runs via one of
its OTHER registered actions (QUICKBOOT_POWERON / LOCKED_BOOT_COMPLETED), which
BYD does not skip. The autostart gate decides whether the app may run at boot at
all. Do not "fix" this by chasing ssc_skip.

## Current state of the Setup Guide

app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/overlay/SetupGuideDialog.java and its
layout res/layout/dialog_setup_guide.xml already have an autostart step
(setup_autostart_* strings in res/values*/strings.xml, pointing at
com.byd.appstartmanagement). What it does NOT say is the consequence: that
recording will not start on its own without it. It reads as an optional
optimisation rather than a requirement.

## What to do

1. Reword the autostart step so the consequence is explicit and unmissable --
   something to the effect of: without this, BladeWatch will not start recording
   when the car is switched on, and you will have to open the app every time.
   Keep it to one short sentence; this is an in-car dialog.
2. Make sure the step is clearly distinguishable now that there are TWO rows in
   BYD's dialog: the user must enable **BladeWatch Service**
   (net.bladewatch.app), not only **BladeWatch** (net.bladewatch.flutter). The
   service host is the one that runs the daemons. See BladeWatch-8h7m, which gave
   the two packages distinct labels.
   Decide whether to tell the user to enable BOTH (simplest, and harmless) or
   only the service host, and verify on device which is actually sufficient.
3. Translate any new/changed string into all 17 locales.
   `./gradlew validateAndroidStrings` enforces key parity and WILL fail the build
   if a locale is missing the key.
4. Consider whether the guide should be re-shown when autostart is detected as
   off. Only if there is a reliable way to READ that state -- investigate before
   promising it; a wrong "you have not set this up" prompt is worse than none.
   If it cannot be read reliably, say so here and skip it.

## Constraints

- Do NOT add a launcher intent-filter to the service host. ServiceHostManifestTest
  pins that it has none.
- Do NOT chase ssc_skip or try to force BOOT_COMPLETED delivery; it is suppressed
  by design on this firmware and is not the working path.
- Do NOT add in-car UI strings to res/values*/strings.xml beyond what the Setup
  Guide itself renders -- that catalog was pruned to 30 keys deliberately and its
  header comment lists every surviving key's consumer. Update that comment if you
  add a key.
- Do NOT commit.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The Setup Guide's autostart step states the consequence of skipping it, in
      one sentence, in plain language.
- [ ] It names which entry/entries to enable, unambiguously, matching the labels
      the user actually sees ("BladeWatch" and "BladeWatch Service").
- [ ] All 17 locales carry any new key; `./gradlew validateAndroidStrings` passes.
- [ ] `./gradlew test koverVerify assembleDebug assembleRelease` pass, and
      ServiceHostManifestTest still passes.
- [ ] The guide was opened on the head unit and read at the real display density
      with no clipping or overflow, in at least English plus one long-word locale
      (de or ru).
- [ ] Whether a re-prompt on detected-off autostart is feasible is answered here
      either way, with the evidence.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the
build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is
ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
notes:
STATUS 2026-09-14: strings done and building clean. ONE criterion outstanding --
the on-device render check -- because the head unit's panel went back to standby.

## Done

setup_autostart_body rewritten in ALL 17 locales. It now:
- states the consequence explicitly: recording does NOT start when you switch the
  car on, and you have to open the app every time;
- names BOTH entries to uncheck, matching the labels the user now actually sees
  after BladeWatch-8h7m ("BladeWatch" and "BladeWatch Service"), with the "both"
  emphasised in each language;
- keeps the existing warning that BYD wipes the setting on every install.

Fixed a mistranslation found while editing: values-fr said "Trouvez BladeWatch
dans la liste et DEMARREZ la case" (start the box) where it must be "decochez"
(uncheck). Same bad bulk-translation pass that produced the settings_about_*_url
hallucinations already recorded in docs/build-and-operations.md.

`./gradlew validateAndroidStrings` passes: 16 locales, full key parity (30 keys),
valid XML, matching format slots, no unescaped apostrophes. Full gate run
(validateArbCatalogs, test, koverVerify, assembleDebug, assembleRelease) green.

## Answered: can the guide re-prompt when autostart is off?

NOT via BYD. Investigated on device:
- com.byd.appstartmanagement exposes NO content provider (dumpsys package
  providers has no match), so there is nothing to query.
- It holds android.permission.ACCESS_APPOPSDATA, which is signature-level and not
  grantable to us, so whatever it reads we cannot.
- `cmd appops get net.bladewatch.app` shows no autostart-specific op. The
  plausible candidates are RUN_IN_BACKGROUND / RUN_ANY_IN_BACKGROUND, both
  currently "allow" with autostart ENABLED -- but that is unverified, because the
  setting can only be changed through BYD's own UI on the car, so I could not
  observe the disabled state to confirm the op actually flips.

There IS a reliable provider-independent alternative, which does not depend on
BYD at all: have the app record whether BootReceiver fired since the CURRENT
boot, and prompt when it did not. That is a direct measurement of the thing the
user actually cares about ("did the boot path work"), not a proxy for a vendor
setting, and it is entirely within our control. It is a behaviour change rather
than a documentation change, so it is not in this task's scope -- filed
separately if wanted.

## Outstanding

- [ ] Open the Setup Guide on the head unit and read it at the real display
      density in English plus a long-word locale (de or ru) -- de is now ~265
      chars and ru ~249, up from ~200, in a fixed dialog. This is exactly the case
      that could clip. The dialog DOES scroll (confirmed earlier when
      BladeWatch-cny7 was closed as NOT A BUG), so the risk is awkward wrapping
      rather than unreachable text -- but it must be looked at, not assumed.

NOT DEPLOYED. The car is parked unattended with the daemons and sentry running;
a service host reinstall drops surveillance for several minutes, which is not a
trade worth making for a string change. Deploy alongside the next real change,
with the car awake, then do the render check.

Nothing committed.
close_reason:
Done and verified on the head unit.

## A mistake I made and corrected

The first pass edited ONLY `app/src/main/res/values*/strings.xml`. That backs the
SERVICE HOST's own `dialog_setup_guide.xml`. The guide the DRIVER actually opens is
a different one: `flutter_ui/lib/screens/dialogs/setup_guide_dialog.dart`, reached
from the About rail destination, and it renders `l10n.setup_autostart_body` from
the ARB. So the user-visible text was still the old wording.

Caught while trying to verify on device -- the acceptance criterion that required
opening the real dialog is what exposed it. Both catalogs now carry the text: 17
Android locales and all 19 ARB catalogs.

## What it says now

"Tap below to open BYD Auto-Start, then uncheck BOTH BladeWatch and BladeWatch
Service. Without this, recording does not start when you switch the car on — you
have to open the app every time. BYD wipes this on every install, so redo it after
updates."

- states the consequence explicitly, which is the point: this is silent data loss;
- names BOTH entries, which only became possible once BladeWatch-8h7m gave the two
  packages distinct labels;
- keeps the existing warning that BYD wipes it on every install.

Translated into all 17 locales in both catalogs. Fixed a mistranslation found while
editing: values-fr said "Trouvez BladeWatch dans la liste et DEMARREZ la case"
(start the box) where it must be "decochez" (uncheck).

## Verified on device

Opened the real dialog on the head unit at 1920x1080 with the display awake:

- **English**: the step-2 body wraps over two lines inside the card, no clipping,
  no overflow, buttons unaffected.
- **German** (the long-word case, ~265 chars vs ~200 before): renders
  "...entfernen Sie die Haken bei BladeWatch UND BladeWatch-Dienst. Ohne dies
  startet die Aufnahme beim Einschalten des Fahrzeugs nicht — Sie müssen die App
  jedes Mal öffnen." Also two lines, also no clipping. The longest locale fits, so
  the rest do.

Language was switched via the in-app picker and restored to Auto/English
afterwards. Screenshots taken but NOT committed -- they carry the Wi-Fi SSID and
device id.

## Answered: can the guide re-prompt when autostart is off?

NOT via BYD. Investigated on device:
- `com.byd.appstartmanagement` exposes NO content provider, so nothing to query.
- It holds `android.permission.ACCESS_APPOPSDATA`, signature-level and not
  grantable to us.
- `cmd appops get net.bladewatch.app` shows no autostart-specific op. The
  candidates are RUN_IN_BACKGROUND / RUN_ANY_IN_BACKGROUND, both "allow" with
  autostart ENABLED -- unverified, because the setting can only be changed through
  BYD's UI on the car, so the disabled state could not be observed.

There IS a reliable alternative that does not depend on BYD: record whether
BootReceiver fired since the CURRENT boot and prompt when it did not. That measures
the thing the user actually cares about rather than proxying a vendor setting. It
is a behaviour change, not a documentation change, so it is out of scope here.

## Deployment

Deployed alongside BladeWatch-c2h1 in one trip. The service host reinstall used the
key-preservation recipe from CLAUDE.md and needed ZERO taps on the car:
"ADB connection established successfully", "Auth no longer pending", 0 fresh
"ADB auth pending" errors. Local key copies deleted immediately.

After deploy: all daemons running, 8080/19876/19877 listening, 0 FATAL /
ClassNotFound / NoClassDefFound in logcat.

## Gates

- `./gradlew validateArbCatalogs validateAndroidStrings validateI18nCatalogs test
  koverVerify assembleDebug assembleRelease`: SUCCESSFUL.
- flutter analyze clean; flutter test 1411 passed, 0 skipped.
- Dart coverage 7004/7006 = 99.97%. Kover green.

Nothing committed.

title: Trunk open lost its unlock-first interlock when BYD cloud was removed
description:
## Problem

Two vehicle-control behaviours silently changed when the BYD cloud path was
removed in commit 61b4d7f. Neither is surfaced to the user, and one can set off
the car alarm. Found 2026-09-14 while correcting stale comments (BladeWatch-w4xn).

### 1. Trunk open lost its unlock-first safety interlock

Trunk open used to be: cloud unlock, then SDK tailgate, with the router firing
the tailgate motor ONLY if the unlock leg returned SUCCESS. That gate is gone.
VehicleCommandRouter.executeTrunkOpen() now calls
BydDataCollector.getInstance().openTailgate() unconditionally.

The router's own javadoc states the consequence plainly:

    "Trunk open via the local tailgate motor. There is no remote-unlock
     pre-step, so on locked vehicles the body controller may decline the
     motor or trip the alarm -- the local primitive is invoked as-is."

So this was a known consequence, not an unnoticed regression. What is missing is
anything telling the USER. The Flutter Vehicle screen and the Angular vehicle page
both still offer trunk open, and on a locked car the outcome may be the alarm
going off in a car park.

### 2. Close-all-windows no longer works while the car is asleep

area=0 + command=2 used to route through the cloud CLOSEWINDOW command, which
worked with the head unit asleep. It now calls the local primitive
BydDataCollector.setAllWindowsCommand(2) (see
VehicleCommandRouter.CloseAllWindowsCommand), which needs the head unit awake and
the SDK reachable. Remote "close my windows, it is raining" no longer works the
way it did. Nothing says so.

## What to decide (this is a product call, not a mechanical fix)

For the trunk:
1. Gate it. Read the lock state -- BydDataCollector already polls all five lock
   areas (see the "all locked" derivation around BydDataCollector.java:2436) --
   and refuse or warn when the car is locked, rather than firing the motor.
2. Or warn at the UI: a confirm step on trunk open saying it may be declined or
   trip the alarm if the car is locked.
3. Or accept it and document it, but then say so where a user can see it, not
   only in a router comment.

For the windows: decide whether the capability loss needs surfacing, and whether
the UI should stop implying the command works remotely.

## Constraints

- BYD vehicle control APIs ACTUATE A PHYSICAL CAR. Test conservatively, and do
  not test trunk open on a locked vehicle just to see whether the alarm fires.
- Do NOT reintroduce the BYD cloud path. It was removed deliberately.
- Do NOT change the lock/unlock RPCs' NOT_SUPPORTED behaviour.
- Any read of lock state must go through the existing BydDataCollector accessors;
  do not add a new reflection path.
- Do NOT commit.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A decision is recorded here for the trunk: gated, warned, or accepted-and-
      documented -- with the reasoning.
- [ ] Whatever is chosen is implemented and covered by a unit test that would fail
      if the behaviour regressed (for a gate: a locked-state fixture that must not
      reach openTailgate).
- [ ] The windows capability change is either surfaced in the UI or explicitly
      recorded as accepted.
- [ ] No comment anywhere still claims the unlock-first interlock exists.
- [ ] ./gradlew test and koverVerify pass; flutter test passes with zero skipped.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the
build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is
ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
close_reason:
Both decisions taken by the owner and implemented.

## Trunk: REMOVED (owner's call: "remove it")

Not gated, not warned -- removed. Gone: `TrunkOpenCommand`, `executeTrunkOpen()`,
the `open` action, and the previous default-to-open on a missing action. `POST
/api/vehicle/trunk` now accepts only `{"action":"close"}` or `{"action":"stop"}`;
anything else answers NOT_SUPPORTED with the same localized string the router
produces (new `VehicleCommandRouter.notSupportedMessage()`, so the wording cannot
drift).

`BydDataCollector.openTailgate()` is deliberately KEPT -- it is the BYD SDK
surface a future implementation with a real lock-state interlock would need. What
is pinned is that NOTHING CALLS IT.

Trunk close and stop are untouched: neither opens anything and both map to real
local primitives.

## Also removed (owner: "also remove byd cloud dependencies and related code")

Six commands that could only ever answer NOT_SUPPORTED after 61b4d7f deleted the
BYD cloud -- dead surface that read like a capability:

- Lock, Unlock, FindCar, FlashLights, BatteryHeat, ChargeSchedule

Removed at all three layers:
- `VehicleCommandRouter`: the 6 command classes (+ TrunkOpenCommand).
- `VehicleControlApiHandler`: `handleLock`, `handleUnlock`, `handleFindCar`,
  `handleBatteryHeat`, `handleFlash`, `handleChargingSchedule`,
  `handleGetChargingSchedule`, and their 7 route branches.
- `VehicleServiceImpl`: 7 Connect registrations and their 7 handler methods.

**The .proto was NOT touched**, deliberately. Regenerating stubs writes into
`web/src/gen`, and `web/` is out of scope by standing instruction. So the wire
contract is unchanged for any existing client; the daemon simply no longer
registers those methods. Verified first that this breaks nobody:
- `web/` removed the Lock/Unlock/Flash CONTROLS by decision already --
  `web/src/app/pages/vehicle/vehicle.component.ts:12` says so. Its remaining
  `lock` references are a read-only status pill, not a command.
- The Flutter UI has zero references to any of the 7 outside generated code.
- `VehicleServiceClient.kt` is `// Code generated by connect-kotlin. DO NOT EDIT.`
  and still declares them, which is correct -- it mirrors the proto.

## Windows: surfaced in the UI (owner's call)

New ARB key `vehicle_window_awake_note` in ALL 19 catalogs, rendered as a caption
under the all-windows row on the Flutter Windows tab (key
`vehicle.window.awakeNote`): "Works only while the car is awake." Close-all used
to run through the cloud CLOSEWINDOW command, which worked with the car asleep;
it is now the local `setAllWindowsCommand(2)`, which is not. Without the note a
remote tap just looks like it silently did nothing.

## The guard, and it is mutation-verified

New `NoUngatedTrunkOpenTest` (3 tests):
- nothing outside `BydDataCollector.java` may CALL `openTailgate()`;
- `TrunkCloseCommand` / `TrunkStopCommand` must stay wired, so the regression it
  guards is a silently reintroduced OPEN, not a removed endpoint;
- `class TrunkOpenCommand` must not reappear.

I did not trust it until I broke it: reinserting
`BydDataCollector.getInstance().openTailgate()` into `handleTrunk` made
`nothingCallsTheTailgateOpenPrimitive` FAIL (exit 1), then restored the file. A
guard that cannot fail is worse than no guard.

## Vacuous tests found and fixed

`./gradlew test` passed GREEN immediately after deleting six routes -- because
`VehicleApiAuthTest` and `AuthMiddlewareTest` assert on `AuthMiddleware.checkAuth`,
which matches by path PATTERN and neither knows nor cares whether a route exists.
Six tests were exercising endpoints that no longer existed and would have kept
passing forever.

- Deleted the 6 tests whose only subject was a removed route.
- Kept the 3 genuine auth tests (cookie JWT, missing JWT, tampered JWT) but
  repointed them from `/api/vehicle/unlock` to `/api/vehicle/trunk`, which is
  still live, and renamed them `vehicleControl*` so the name does not promise a
  route that is gone. Same for `AuthMiddlewareTest`'s 2 fixtures.

## Docs

- `docs/byd-integrations.md` -- "Commands with no local primitive" rewritten as
  "Commands removed with the BYD cloud", plus two new sections: why trunk open was
  removed rather than left ungated, and that close-all-windows now needs the car
  awake.
- `docs/http-api-reference.md` -- the six endpoints are now "route removed", not
  "not supported", and the trunk route documents that only close/stop are accepted.

## Verification

- `./gradlew validateAndroidStrings validateArbCatalogs test koverVerify
  assembleDebug assembleRelease`: SUCCESSFUL.
- flutter analyze clean; flutter test **1404** passed (was 1403), 0 skipped.
- Dart coverage 7004/7006 = 99.97%, not lower. Kover green.
- The compiler found every orphan: removing the command classes first surfaced
  `handleFlash` and the charging-schedule pair as "cannot find symbol", which is
  why they were caught rather than left behind.

NOT deployed to the head unit. The car is parked unattended with the daemons and
sentry running, and a service host reinstall drops surveillance for several
minutes. This is a daemon-side change and MUST be verified on device before it is
trusted -- specifically that trunk close/stop still work and that the Windows tab
renders the new caption without clipping in a long-word locale. Deploy with the
car awake, together with BladeWatch-zie8 which is also built and waiting.

Nothing committed.

title: Clean reinstall needs a physical ADB-auth tap before daemons can start
description:
## Context

Every clean reinstall of net.bladewatch.app requires someone to physically tap
"OK" on the head unit's USB-debugging authorization dialog before any daemon can
start. This is not documented in CLAUDE.md's deploy procedure, and it silently
blocks verification whenever the car's display is asleep.

Why it happens: AdbShellExecutor.getOrCreateAdbKeyPair() stores the app's ADB
RSA key pair in context.filesDir --
app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/launcher/AdbShellExecutor.kt lines
323-352, constants ADB_KEY_FILE / ADB_PUB_KEY_FILE at lines 20-21. Uninstalling
wipes /data/data/net.bladewatch.app, so the next launch generates a NEW key,
which the device has never authorized. dadb's connect to 127.0.0.1:5555 then
fails with "ADB auth pending - waiting for user to accept" and the system shows
com.android.systemui.usb.UsbDebuggingActivity.

Observed 2026-09-14 while verifying BladeWatch-81g9.3: the service host launched
and DaemonStartupManager ran, but every AdbShellExecutor command failed with
"ADB auth pending", so CameraDaemon / SentryDaemon / AccSentryDaemon never came
