The ADB Console needs to talk raw ADB protocol to adbd on 127.0.0.1:5555 — there is no `shell`
IPC command (removed as an RCE fix, TcpCommandServer.java's uy93.2 comment) and this class of
shell-execution capability was deliberately walked back elsewhere in this codebase. Presented 3
options (pub.dev ADB package / defer the whole screen / hand-roll a minimal Dart client); the
user chose to hand-roll it. Delivered as scoped: the wire protocol (framing, connect/auth/
shell state machine, socket I/O) is 100% hand-rolled Dart with zero third-party ADB packages;
the ONE piece not hand-rolled is the ADB/mincrypt public-key struct format (Montgomery-
precomputed, not meaningfully "protocol logic"), reused from dadb (a library already vetted and
shipped in the main app) rather than risk an unverifiable-without-a-device bug in a from-scratch
reimplementation of that specific format.

## Scoping decisions (deliberate, not oversights)

- **LogsPanelFragment is dead code, not ported.** This task's own file list named
  LogsPanelFragment.kt/LogsViewModel.kt/LogsAdapter.kt/LogEntry.kt/LogLevel.kt, but a full-repo
  grep for LogsPanelFragment/logsPanelFragment finds zero references anywhere outside the
  class's own file — no nav graph destination, no <fragment> tag, no programmatic
  instantiation. Both fragment_diagnostics.xml files' own header comments still describe an
  older two-column design with an embedded "Live event log" card; the body of both files
  already removed it (their own inline comment says so) — stale comments, not current
  behaviour. Even if reachable, LogsViewModel's data is in-memory/app-process-local with no
  daemon backing, so it would be unreachable from the Flutter APK regardless. Verified via the
  filesystem, not assumed from the task description.
- **Tunnel state is a 2-way approximation of native's 3-way status.** DaemonChannel.
  processStatus() only reports running/not-running, not native's STARTING/RUNNING/STOPPED.
  "Connecting" here means the tunnel daemon process is up but no URL has been minted yet (via
  the still-open BladeWatch-m1po gap), not literally adbd's STARTING value.
- **Performance polls via the typed GetPerformance RPC, not a second raw-HTTP GET** — the RPC
  already wraps the exact handler native's raw HttpURLConnection hits, so no reason to
  duplicate transport. connect()/disconnect()/heartbeat DO need raw HTTP (RawHttpSender, same
  transport ConnectClient itself uses) since PerformanceApiHandler's on-demand client-
  registration endpoints have no RPC equivalent — and skipping them isn't optional (verified by
  reading PerformanceMonitor.java: no registered client means isRunning() never becomes true,
  every poll returns the "no_data" wrapper forever).
- **Diagnostics' own periodic refresh is simplified to one unified cycle** rather than native's
  split cadence (a 5s SSID-only timer plus separate refresh-on-Fragment-resume for the more
  expensive Storage/Camera/Battery probes). Flutter has no exact equivalent of Android's
  Fragment onResume without a lifecycle observer, and since Storage now goes through
  StorageService's RPC (daemon-computed) rather than a local filesystem walk, the "expensive
  probe" concern that motivated native's split cadence doesn't apply to this port the same way.
  (Diagnostics' own 4-tile refresh() runs once on screen entry — no periodic timer at all,
  since a human visiting this screen and tapping Retry/re-entering is adequate for a diagnostics
  hub.)
- **The native `%1$.0f`-style SOH percent format** was bulk-imported into the ARB catalog with
  an untyped placeholder (`{arg1}`, no numeric format). The screen rounds to an int before
  calling the format string rather than relying on the placeholder to format it, to match
  native's whole-percent display (caught by a widget test expecting "90%" and getting "90.0%").

  already filed (UnifiedConfigManager's public "camera" section). DiagnosticsController's
  injected cameraConfigSource defaults to probedCameraId=-1/manualOverride=false, which is also

- `adb.getPublicKey`/`adb.sign` — Flutter-APK-local RSA key material (AdbKeyChannel.kt), no
  daemon/IPC involvement. Backs the hand-rolled Dart ADB client's AUTH exchange.
- `network.current` — Flutter-APK-local ConnectivityManager/WifiManager probe
  (NetworkInfoChannel.kt), no daemon/IPC involvement.
- No changes to TcpCommandServer.java, PeerCredentials.java, or any daemon-side code — the ADB

  reused already-existing RPC surface (SurveillanceService.SetConfig, SystemService.

- flutter_ui's AndroidManifest.xml gained ACCESS_WIFI_STATE (Network tile) and

  app's app/build.gradle.kts already carries for the same reason).

## A real bug found and fixed via a widget test

Camera Selection dialog's "Auto" RadioListTile originally used `null` as its Radio value.
Since the controller's own default state also starts at "Auto", the first widget test that
tapped "Auto" silently did nothing — Radio doesn't fire onChanged when tapping the
already-selected option (standard radio-button semantics, not a Flutter bug). Fixed by using a
non-null sentinel for "Auto" in the dialog (converting to/from selectCamera's real int? at the
call boundary) and rewriting the test to start from a genuinely different selection. Same class
of lesson as BladeWatch-yz1e.3's SettingsAppearanceController missing notifyListeners() — a
widget test catches what a controller-only test structurally cannot.

## A tooling gotcha discovered (saved to memory for future sessions)

Writing a `�`-style Dart escape sequence (needed for ADB's NUL-terminated connect/auth-
payload strings) through the Write tool landed as a literal raw NUL byte in 3 files instead of
the intended 6-character escape text. Dart compiles/runs it identically either way (silent —
no analyzer or test signal), but `grep`/`file` correctly flag the file as binary. Caught only
because a routine grep printed "binary file matches" instead of the line. Fixed with a byte-
level find-and-replace across the affected files (lib/adb/adb_client.dart and 2 test files);
verified zero raw NUL bytes remain project-wide afterward.

## Tests

TDD throughout for every controller/client file except adb_protocol.dart, whose wire-format
design needed to be nailed down through documented reasoning (AOSP protocol.txt, manual hex
derivation of the 4 command codes, independently cross-checked in the test itself) before its
first test could be meaningfully written — immediately followed by 17 tests covering every
encode/decode/reader branch. Every other file (adb_client.dart, diagnostics_controller.dart,
performance_controller.dart, adb_console_controller.dart) had its test file written first.

100% line coverage on every new file, individually verified via lcov (not just in aggregate):
adb_protocol.dart (56/56), adb_client.dart (59/59), adb_key_channel.dart (4/4, Dart wrapper),
network_channel.dart (9/9), diagnostics_controller.dart (105/105), diagnostics_models.dart
(1/1), performance_controller.dart (61/61), performance_models.dart (6/6),
adb_console_controller.dart (29/29), adb_console_models.dart (1/1) — and, though not a strict
requirement, every screen widget file too: diagnostics_screen.dart (251/251),
performance_screen.dart (95/95), adb_console_screen.dart (115/115).

adb_client.dart's own test suite (32 tests) runs against a REAL local loopback TCP server (a
minimal, independently-written fake adbd — deliberately does NOT import adb_client.dart's own
packet handling, only adb_protocol.dart's primitives, so a bug in AdbClient's usage of those
primitives can't hide behind the test sharing the same broken logic) — covers: unavailable (
nothing listening), connected without auth, connected after signature accepted, connected after
pubkey-then-retry accepted, authPending (timeout / unexpected final packet / connection dropped
mid-handshake), runCommand success (single and multi-chunk WRTE), runCommand timeout (idle and
disconnected-mid-command), re-entrant runCommand rejection, close(). No real device, no real
adbd, anywhere.

AdbKeyChannelTest.kt (Kotlin/JVM, 7 tests) proves the RSA signing scheme correct independently:
signs a token, reconstructs the public key from the private key file's own CRT parameters (not
by parsing the ADB/mincrypt format), and verifies via NONEwithRSA over the manually-built SHA1

wrong here would have meant BladeWatch-yz1e.4's entire ADB Console silently failing every real

Performance's full/partial/empty-snapshot rendering, ADB Console's connecting/unavailable/
authPending/connected states plus execute/clear/preset-tap/re-entrant-execute-ignored.

The Flutter UI is a **separate APK** (`net.bladewatch.flutter`) sharing a UID with `net.bladewatch.app`. Its Kotlin lives in `flutter_ui/android/app/src/main/kotlin/`; the main app's Kotlin is never called directly from Dart.

- settings_recording_controller.dart/_models.dart/_screen.dart — the controller behind BOTH of
  native's Recording-settings entry points (see "two entry points" note below). 4 tabs: Status,
  Capture (mode + segment limit), Quality, Storage (type/limit slider + format-drive and
  sync-catalog sub-flows, both fully implemented, not simplified).
- settings_overlay_controller.dart/_screen.dart — the 2 status-pill visibility toggles.
- settings_daemons_controller.dart/_models.dart/_screen.dart — daemon list (running/stopped from
  daemon.processStatus) + Zrok token configure/reset (fully capable via the existing config.*
  channel).
- settings_privacy_controller.dart/_screen.dart — storage summary (reused StorageService, same
  RPC the Recording Storage tab uses) + reset-data entry point + 2 developer-logging toggles.
- settings_about_controller.dart/_screen.dart — version/license/setup-guide row (native's actual
  scope) + "Check for updates" via the already-built update.* channel (a DIFFERENT, wider scope
  than native's About fragment — see below). Reachable via its own top-level rail destination
  (BwRoutes.settingsAbout), not the sub-rail, matching BwRoutes' own doc comment.
- flutter_ui/lib/platform/prefs_channel.dart + MainActivity.kt's new prefs.* group — plain
  SharedPreferences local to net.bladewatch.flutter, for themeMode/driveSide only. Not IPC, not
  shared with the main app (PreferencesManager.kt's file lives under a different package's
  app-private storage even though the two APKs share a UID).
- Added package_info_plus (flutter pub add) for About's own version/build display — reads the
  Flutter APK's own package identity, no custom native code needed.
- AppShell gained settingsScreen/settingsAboutScreen slots (same optional-default-null shape as
  yz1e.2's dashboardScreen slot); main.dart wires the real screens in.

## Scoping decisions (deliberate, not oversights)

- **Landscape sub-rail only, no portrait "SOTA hub".** BladeWatch targets fixed-landscape BYD
  head units; the portrait branch is unreachable on the actual target hardware. Documented in
  build-and-operations.md.
- **"Two entry points, one shared controller"** (Recording, per the task's own explicit note):
  built the controller once, mounted only from the Settings sub-rail. BwRoutes has no slot for a
  standalone destination without its own rail icon, and native's standalone
  recordingSettingsWebFragment isn't reachable from the main nav rail either (not one of the 9
  NavRailItems) — inventing new top-level shell/routing infrastructure for a destination with no
  clear Flutter-side equivalent surface was judged out of scope for this task. Documented as a
  gap, not silently dropped.
- **About's real scope vs. the task description's**: `SettingsAboutFragment.kt` (native) only
  shows version/build/license/setup-guide — no source link, no support links, no "Check for
  Updates". Several `settings_about_*` ARB keys for those features exist but are referenced by
  no current native code or resource (grepped app/src/main and app/src/main/res fully) — a
  leftover from a richer About page that was never built. Ported exactly what native's fragment
  does; did not invent the unused features. Separately, DID add "Check for updates" — not because
  native's About has it, but because the already-built `update.*` channel (BladeWatch-ncbb.2)
  exists specifically to update the Flutter APK itself, a distinct concern from native's
  ADB-based whole-app AppUpdater.java.
- **Daemons debug-only log download** (`DaemonsFragment.onDownloadLogClicked` — ADB `tail` +
  `FileProvider` share, gated to `BuildConfig.DEBUG`) deliberately not ported: a developer
  convenience, not a release end-user feature.
- **Zrok "reset environment" simplified**: native also calls `ZrokController.disableEnvironment()`
  (removes zrok's own local environment files via shell, unreachable from the Flutter APK). This
  port stops the tunnel (when a start capability is available) and deletes the saved token — the
  part that actually matters to the user, since re-enabling needs a fresh token either way.

## Architectural gaps discovered and filed (neither blocks this task)

- **BladeWatch-hygs** (P2) — no IPC path reaches `UnifiedConfigManager`'s public (non-secret)
  config sections (only the daemon-owned *secret* store is reachable via `ConfigChannel`).
  Blocks real persistence for Overlay's 2 toggles and Privacy's 2 developer-logging toggles.
  Both use an injected `loadSettings`/`persist` function pair (same shape as
  `DashboardController.tunnelUrlSource`/BladeWatch-m1po) defaulting to native's own fallback
  values and a no-op write; toggling still updates in-memory UI state for the session.
- **BladeWatch-abcx** (P2) — no IPC path starts/stops an individual daemon *process* (only
  camera-recording on/off within the already-running camera daemon exists). Blocks Daemons'
  per-service switches; `SettingsDaemonsController`'s injected `setDaemonEnabled` defaults to
  always reporting "not supported" — an honest, visible message, not a silent failure or a fake
  success.

Also traced but NOT re-litigated (already filed before this task, from BladeWatch-yz1e.2):
BladeWatch-b195 (JwtMinter auth-store mismatch — already fixed this session) and BladeWatch-m1po
(tunnel URL, still open, unrelated to Settings).

## New IPC/channel surface added this task (all narrow, self-contained)

- `prefs.getThemeMode`/`setThemeMode`/`getDriveSide`/`setDriveSide` — Flutter-APK-local
  SharedPreferences, no daemon/IPC involvement at all. Fully implemented and working (not a gap).
- No changes to `TcpCommandServer.java`, `PeerCredentials.java`, or any daemon-side code this
  task — everything else reused already-existing RPC/channel surface
  (`SettingsService`/`StorageService`/`RecordingsService`/`SystemService` RPCs,
  `daemon.processStatus`, `config.get/put/delete`, `update.checkForUpdate/downloadAndInstall`).

## Tests

TDD throughout — every controller's test file was written before its implementation. 100% line
coverage on every new controller AND model file (verified individually via lcov, not just in
aggregate): settings_appearance_controller.dart (17/17), settings_appearance_models.dart (14/14),
settings_overlay_controller.dart (22/22), settings_privacy_controller.dart (43/43),
settings_daemons_controller.dart (20/20), settings_daemons_models.dart (1/1),
settings_recording_controller.dart (141/141), settings_recording_models.dart (10/10). Every
screen widget file also reached 100% (not a strict requirement, but achieved): all 7 screens plus
the hub. Every reachable state (loading/loaded/empty/error, every interactive control, every
dialog branch) has a widget test — 145 new tests across screens/settings/, covering things like:
Recording's format-drive confirm/cancel/success/failure and sync-catalog success/failure/dismiss;
Daemons' Zrok save/delete/reset-with-confirmation and the "unsupported" toggle message; Overlay
and Privacy's toggle persistence (both with and without an injected capability); Appearance's
theme/drive-side selection and caption text for all states including "auto" detection.

Caught and fixed one real bug via a widget test, not just the controller test:
`SettingsAppearanceController.setDriveSide()` updated `ShellController`'s state (which notifies
ITS OWN listeners) but never called `notifyListeners()` on itself, so the Appearance screen never
rebuilt after a drive-side tap even though the underlying state had changed. The controller-only
test couldn't have caught this (it only asserted on `ShellController.driveSide` directly); the
widget test, which asserts on what's actually rendered, did.

Also discovered along the way: a `json_name` proto annotation
(`storage.proto`'s `recordings_size_bytes` serializes as `"recordingsSize"`, not the naive
camelCase `"recordingsSizeBytes"`) that had to be matched exactly in test JSON stubs — the same
class of trap as the Dashboard task's earlier `recordingsSize`/`recordingsSizeBytes` discovery,
worth remembering for future RPC-stubbing work: check the .proto file for `json_name` overrides
before assuming naive camelCase.

## Verification

- `flutter analyze`: clean, whole project.
- `flutter test`: 542/542 passing, 0 skipped.
- `flutter test --coverage` (tools/check_flutter_coverage.sh, lib/gen/** excluded): **99.91%
  (2227/2229 lines)** — up from 99.85% (BladeWatch-yz1e.2). The only 2 uncovered lines are
  main.dart's `void main()` (pre-existing, documented, not unit-testable).
- `cd flutter_ui/android && ./gradlew test koverVerify assembleDebug`: BUILD SUCCESSFUL, 100%
  Kover gate unchanged (package_info_plus's native Android code lives in its own Gradle module,
  outside this app module's report).
- `./gradlew test assembleDebug` (main app, repo root): BUILD SUCCESSFUL, no regressions.
- `./gradlew validateArbCatalogs`: 19 catalogs valid, full key parity with app_en.arb (689 keys —
  added ~55 new keys this task across Recording settings, Daemons, and About; all 19 locales
  translated for the ~10 highest-traffic strings, English-fallback for the rest, matching the
  established convention from earlier tasks this epic).
- `git status` confirms every native Settings-related fragment/layout/adapter/controller file
  (`SettingsFragment.kt`, `settings/*.kt`, `DaemonsFragment.kt`, `DaemonAdapter.kt`,
  `recording/*.kt`) and everything under `web/` are untouched by this task.

## Acceptance criteria — status

- [x] Every control, tab, menu and dialog present in the native screen exists and is wired —
      with the documented, narrow exceptions above (portrait hub, standalone Recording route,
      debug-only log download) and the 2 filed IPC gaps (Overlay/Privacy persistence, Daemons
      start/stop), all explicitly called out rather than silently dropped.
- [x] Loading, empty and error states match, including "daemon not running" (Daemons' processStatus
      failure → all 4 rows shown stopped, not a crash).
- [x] Renders correctly in light and dark theme — dedicated dark-theme widget test per screen.
- [x] No hardcoded user-facing strings — ~55 new ARB keys added, all 19 locales validated.
- [x] flutter analyze clean; assembleDebug succeeds (both Gradle projects + main app); native UI
      unchanged.
- [x] Tests written before implementation for every controller.
- [x] flutter test passes, 0 skipped.
- [x] 100% line coverage of every controller and model file (individually verified).
- [x] Every reachable screen state has a widget test.
- [x] Tests run green with no device and no daemon attached.
- [x] Coverage percentage recorded above and not lower than the previous task's (99.91% vs
      99.85%).

## Screenshot correspondence for Phase 3

`screenshots/native/08_settings.png`, `08c_settings_surveillance.png` (entry row only — full
surveillance settings are yz1e.8), `08d_settings_daemons.png`, `08e_settings_status_overlay.png`,
`10_about.png` — all landscape sub-rail shots; there is no portrait-hub equivalent to reproduce
per the scoping decision above.

title: Port Dashboard screen to Flutter
description:
> **CODE ONLY — do not touch the head unit in this task.**
> This project deliberately writes *all* Flutter code before any device work. Everything here
> is built and tested on the dev machine against the shared fakes from `BladeWatch-ncbb.5`,
> with no device and no daemon attached. On-device bring-up, screenshots, the render go/no-go
> and parity sign-off all live in **Phase 3** (`BladeWatch-imh6`).
> If you believe something genuinely cannot be verified without hardware, note it in the task
> notes for Phase 3 to pick up — do not reach for adb.

## Context

Port the Dashboard — the main landing screen and the largest single layout in the app.

## Native source

- `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/fragment/DashboardFragment.kt` (1,086 LOC — the biggest fragment)
- `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/dashboard/DashboardInsight.kt`
- `app/src/main/res/layout/fragment_dashboard.xml` (35.1 KB — the biggest layout)

Read all 1,086 lines before starting. This screen aggregates data from several services, so map every data source to its RPC before writing widgets.

## Notes

- The dashboard is a stats/connect hub. The live camera feed was deliberately MOVED OUT of the dashboard to the Live screen — do not put a video player back on the dashboard. (The Angular SPA has the same split; see the comment in `web/src/app/pages/live/live.component.ts`.)
- Insight cards come from `DashboardInsight`; port its logic, not just its rendering.
- The daemon connection status and tunnel URL surface here — those come from the `daemon.*` channel and SystemService.

## How every screen task works

1. Read the native fragment AND its controller/client/models files FULLY before writing any Dart. The controllers hold the real behaviour; the fragment is often just wiring.
2. Port the layout to Dart widgets using the shared M3 ThemeData built in Epic 1. Do not invent new styling.
3. Call the SAME RPCs via the generated Dart client, or the SAME platform-channel methods. Never add a new endpoint or a new channel method without saying why in the notes.
4. All user-facing text comes from the ARB catalogs. No hardcoded literals except the brand name BladeWatch.
5. Do **not** capture screenshots here — `BladeWatch-imh6.1` captures the whole set on the device in Phase 3. Note in your task notes which `screenshots/native/` shot this screen corresponds to, so Phase 3 knows what to reproduce.

## Universal constraints

- Do NOT delete or modify the native fragment, layout, adapter or view you are porting FROM. Both UIs must keep working — the native shell stays the default until Epic 4.
- Do NOT modify anything under `web/` (the Angular SPA), the daemon, the Connect server, or the `.proto` files.
- Do NOT commit. Leave changes in the working tree.
- **No device.** Do not run adb, do not install anything, do not capture screenshots. Build and test locally: `cd flutter_ui && flutter analyze && flutter test`. Phase 3 (`BladeWatch-imh6`) does all on-device work.
- Use the shared RPC fake and channel fake from `BladeWatch-ncbb.5`; tests must pass with no device and no daemon attached.

## Conventions for this refactor (decided — do not deviate)

**Where Dart code goes.** Mirror the native structure one-to-one, so each port is a translation rather than a redesign:

The Flutter UI is a **separate APK** (`net.bladewatch.flutter`) sharing a UID with `net.bladewatch.app`. Its Kotlin lives in `flutter_ui/android/app/src/main/kotlin/`; the main app's Kotlin is never called directly from Dart.

```
flutter_ui/lib/
  gen/                  generated protobuf — never hand-edited, excluded from coverage
  rpc/                  Connect transport + the 12 typed service clients
  platform/             Dart wrappers over the platform channels
  l10n/                 ARB catalogs
  theme/                ThemeData built from the Android M3 tokens
  shell/                nav rail, toolbar, routing
  screens/<name>/       <name>_controller.dart, <name>_models.dart, <name>_screen.dart
flutter_ui/test/        mirrors lib/ exactly
```

**State management: plain `ChangeNotifier` controllers. No Riverpod, no BLoC, no new state dependency.**
This mirrors the existing native Controller pattern (`app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/fragment/vehicle/VehicleController.kt`, `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/fragment/trips/TripsController.kt`, `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/fragment/surveillance/SurveillanceSettingsController.kt`), so porting is a direct translation.

- The controller is a **pure Dart class: it must not import `package:flutter/material.dart`.** It holds state, calls the RPC client and the platform channels, and calls `notifyListeners()`.
- The screen widget only renders controller state and forwards user intent. **No business logic in widgets.**
- This split is exactly what makes 100% coverage reachable — controllers are tested directly with no widget pump.

**No golden tests.** Visual parity is verified on the device in Phase 3 against `screenshots/native/`. Do not add `matchesGoldenFile` or `golden_toolkit`; they churn on every theme tweak and differ between host machines.

## Tests (TDD — required)

**Write the failing test first**, then the implementation, then refactor. Tests are not a closing chore — the test defines the behaviour.

- **Controller and model logic: 100% line and branch coverage.** These are pure Dart with no Flutter imports, so there is no excuse for a gap: every RPC-response-to-view-model transform, every formatter, every validation, every error branch.
- **Widget tests for every state the screen can reach**: loading, loaded, empty, error (including the "daemon not running" case), plus each interactive control. Assert on *behaviour* — that the right call was made with the right arguments — not merely that a widget rendered.
- Use the shared RPC fake and channel fake from `BladeWatch-ncbb.5`. Do not write your own.
- Tests must run green with `flutter test` on the dev machine with **no device and no daemon attached**.
- Run `flutter test --coverage`; `flutter_ui/lib/gen` is excluded from the denominator. Record the percentage in the task notes; it must not be lower than the previous task's figure.
- Anything uncovered is listed line-by-line in the notes with a concrete reason. **"Hard to test" is not a reason** — it means the logic belongs somewhere testable.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every control, tab, menu and dialog present in the native screen exists and is wired in the Flutter screen.
- [ ] Loading, empty and error states match — including the "daemon not running" case.
- [ ] Renders correctly in light and dark theme.
- [ ] No hardcoded user-facing strings; all keys resolve in at least en plus one CJK locale.
- [ ] `flutter analyze` clean; `./gradlew assembleDebug` succeeds; the native UI still works unchanged.
- [ ] Tests were written before the implementation, not retrofitted.
- [ ] `flutter test` passes with zero skipped tests.
- [ ] 100% line and branch coverage of controllers and models, or every gap justified line-by-line in the notes.
- [ ] Every reachable screen state (loading / loaded / empty / error) has a widget test.
- [ ] Tests run green with no device and no daemon attached.
- [ ] `flutter test --coverage` percentage recorded and not lower than the previous task's.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.

## What was built

Ported the Dashboard screen (DashboardFragment.kt, 1,086 LOC, the biggest native fragment +
fragment_dashboard.xml, 35.1 KB, the biggest layout) to Flutter, following the same
controller/models/screen split as BladeWatch-yz1e.1 (Startup):

- flutter_ui/lib/screens/dashboard/dashboard_models.dart — TripStatsState, RecordingsMetricState,
  DaemonsSummaryState, TunnelState/TunnelPhase, VehicleTileState, AccessCodeState,
  VehicleModelEntry, VehicleDialogState, modelDisplayName().
- flutter_ui/lib/screens/dashboard/dashboard_controller.dart — DashboardController
  (ChangeNotifier), aggregates TripsService.ListTrips, RecordingsService.ListRecordings,
  SystemService.GetStatus/GetSohNominal/GetSelectedModel, daemon.processStatus, and the
  AuthChannel access-code methods. Also exposes `deviceId` (from GetStatus, for the Connect
  card) — added this task.
- flutter_ui/lib/screens/dashboard/vehicle_dialog_controller.dart — VehicleDialogController
  (ChangeNotifier), a separate controller for the battery-capacity dialog: loads
  GetSohNominal/GetSohStatus/GetModelsManifest/GetSelectedModel in parallel, supports
  selectModel() (auto-fills capacity from the manifest), setCapacityText(), save() (8.0-120.0
  kWh validation, matching the native dialog's positive-button handler exactly), and reset()
  (SetSohNominal with no value set — NOT the unrelated ResetSoh RPC, which backs a different,
  bulk-reset dialog in MainActivity.kt).
- flutter_ui/lib/screens/dashboard/dashboard_screen.dart — DashboardScreen + its dialogs
  (regenerate confirmation, set-password, vehicle capacity). Renders every control from the
  native fragment: hero trip-stats card + hero chips (tunnel/services/recording), 4 metric
  tiles (recordings/tunnel/daemons/vehicle), Connect card (QR via qr_flutter + placeholder +
  device id + access code row with toggle/copy/regenerate/set-password), and the Live quick
  action.
- AuthChannel/JwtMinter.kt/MainActivity.kt: getAccessCode/regenerateAccessCode/
  setCustomAccessCode (built earlier this task, before this compaction).
- Wired into the app: AppShell gained an optional `dashboardScreen` slot (null by default, so
  every other route/test is unaffected) and main.dart builds the real DashboardController +
  DashboardScreen from a shared ConnectClient/AuthChannel and passes it in.
- Added qr_flutter ^4.1.0 via `flutter pub add` (pre-approved by the Phase 1 epic's own text).
- Added 4 new ARB keys (vehicle_dialog_soh_source_{live,calibration,oem,nominal}) across all
  19 locale files — the native dialog's SOH-source suffixes ("(live)"/"(from last
  charge)"/"(vehicle)"/"(nominal)") are hardcoded, non-localized literals in
  DashboardFragment.kt itself, but this task's own "no hardcoded strings" acceptance criterion
  is stricter than native, so these got real ARB entries instead of being copied verbatim.
  `./gradlew validateArbCatalogs` confirms full key parity (636 keys × 19 locales).

## Native fidelity notes / deliberate deviations

- **DashboardInsight.kt is dead code** (confirmed via grep — referenced nowhere outside its own
  file). The task description names it as a logic source; the live Dashboard's own header
  comment ("SOTA Dashboard") and its actually-used inline logic is what this port follows
  instead. Already noted in dashboard_controller.dart's doc comment from earlier this task.
- Today's recording count comes from `RecordingsService.ListRecordings(date: today).total` over
  RPC, not a local directory walk (RecordingScanner) — no filesystem access from the Flutter
  APK. Recording-in-progress and device id come from `SystemService.GetStatus()`'s
  `recording`/`deviceId` fields rather than native's ADB/SharedPreferences-based
  RecordingViewModel/DeviceIdGenerator.
- Model-selection pre-fill fidelity: a `GetSelectedModel` result is only honored if that model
  id is actually present in the loaded manifest (matches native's `idx >= 0` guard in
  `showVehicleCapacityDialog()` exactly) — covered by its own test.
- The vehicle-capacity dialog's model picker is a row of `ChoiceChip`s, not native's
  `MaterialAutoCompleteTextView` dropdown — visual parity is explicitly Phase 3's job per this
  task's own notes; BYD's model list is short enough that chips need no menu/overlay.
- Native's `regenerateToken()`/`InvalidateAuthCacheRequest` cache-invalidation RPC (which
  proactively logs out *other* already-connected sessions and picks between 4 toast variants
  depending on its outcome) was deliberately NOT ported. `JwtMinter`'s Kotlin methods already
  bump the state version on success, which is what actually makes `ConnectClient` drop its
  cached JWT immediately (the correctness-critical part); the extra RPC only affects other
  sessions' logout timing. Dashboard shows one generic success/failure message per action
  instead of native's 4-way branching. Noted here as a deliberate scope decision, not an
  oversight.
- Copy-to-clipboard is fire-and-forget (`Clipboard.setData` not awaited before showing the
  confirmation) — Android's ClipboardManager is synchronous; Flutter's Clipboard API is
  Future-based only because of the platform-channel round trip, and (found empirically) that
  Future never resolves inside `flutter_test`'s environment regardless of `pump()`/
  `pumpAndSettle()` count, since nothing schedules a frame while it's pending. Not awaiting is
  both correct UX (instant confirmation, matching native's perceived synchronicity) and
  resolved the test hang.

## Architectural gaps discovered and filed (do not block this task)

- **BladeWatch-b195 (P0)** — `JwtMinter.mintJwt()` can never succeed on a real device:
  `AuthManager.writeToConfig()` persists `deviceId`/`tokenEpoch` to `UnifiedConfigManager`,
  never to the `SecretConfigStore` section `secret_get_section("auth")` reads from, so every
  Flutter-side RPC call goes out with no `Authorization` header. Filed with full trace and two
  proposed fixes before this compaction. Does not block Dashboard's own access-code feature
  (only needs `deviceSecret` alone, confirmed present) but does mean the trip/recording/vehicle
  RPC tiles will show their "unavailable" states on a real device until fixed.
- **BladeWatch-m1po (P2)** — no IPC/RPC path exists for the Zrok tunnel URL. Filed before this
  compaction, mirroring BladeWatch-1xt9's pattern. `DashboardController`'s `tunnelUrlSource`
  constructor parameter is injected specifically so this can be wired in later without touching
  the controller; its default always reports "no tunnel."

## Verification

  - dashboard_screen.dart: 346/346 (100%)

- `./gradlew validateArbCatalogs`: 19 catalogs valid, full key parity with app_en.arb (636 keys).

description:
> **CODE ONLY — do not touch the head unit in this task.**
> This project deliberately writes *all* Flutter code before any device work. Everything here
> is built and tested on the dev machine against the shared fakes from `BladeWatch-ncbb.5`,
> with no device and no daemon attached. On-device bring-up, screenshots, the render go/no-go
> and parity sign-off all live in **Phase 3** (`BladeWatch-imh6`).
> If you believe something genuinely cannot be verified without hardware, note it in the task
> notes for Phase 3 to pick up — do not reach for adb.

## Context

Set up the test harness and the coverage gates FIRST, before any other Phase 1 foundation task writes code. Every subsequent task in this refactor is test-driven and must report a coverage number — this task is what makes that possible and, more importantly, **enforceable**.

The other four Phase 1 tasks (`BladeWatch-ncbb.1` through `.4`) are blocked on this one.

## Why an enforced gate and not a convention

This project has shipped breakage twice that a passing test suite did not catch:

- Angular AOT silently fell back to JIT on an unsupported `@else if` alias — **no build error** — and the page rendered blank. Fixed by adding a check that fails.
- Corrupt locale JSON (smart-quote delimiters, unescaped quotes in CJK values) shipped because nothing validated the catalogs. Fixed by adding `validateI18nCatalogs`, which **fails the build**.

Both were solved by a build-failing check, not a warning. Do the same here: the coverage gates must fail the build, not print a number someone ignores.

## What to build

### 1. Dart test harness

- Test dependencies in `flutter_ui/pubspec.yaml`: `flutter_test` plus a mocking approach. **Prefer hand-written fakes over a code-generating mock framework** — this repo already has three codegen pipelines (Java, Kotlin, TypeScript protobuf), and a fake implementing the client interface is easier to read at 3am than a generated mock.
- `flutter_ui/test/` mirrors `flutter_ui/lib/` exactly.

### 2. The two shared fakes — the most reused code in this refactor

Design these once, carefully; roughly 20 downstream tasks depend on them:

- **A fake ConnectRPC client** so screen tests run with no daemon. It must let a test stub any of the 12 services' responses, assert which RPC was called with which request message, and simulate a Connect error and a timeout.
- **A fake platform-channel layer** so screen tests run with no device. Same requirements for the 7 method groups (`auth`, `daemon`, `update`, `storage`, `config`, `logs`, `device`), including failure simulation — shell call failed, daemon not up, permission denied.

Each gets a one-paragraph usage note so the other tasks reuse them instead of writing their own.

### 3. Dart coverage gate

- `flutter test --coverage` producing `lcov.info`, with `flutter_ui/lib/gen` **excluded from the denominator** (generated protobuf is never hand-written and would inflate the number).
- A small script under `tools/` that prints the percentage and **exits non-zero below the configured threshold**.

### 4. Kotlin coverage gate (Kover)

- Add `org.jetbrains.kotlinx.kover` to `gradle/libs.versions.toml` and `app/build.gradle.kts`. It is Kotlin-native and works with the project's Kotlin 2.0.21 / AGP 8.13.2 setup.
- Configure `koverVerify` with a threshold. **Baseline it against the existing suite first** — there are already ~20 test files / ~3,100 LOC under `app/src/test/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/`, so measure what that currently covers and set the initial threshold there rather than at zero or at 100.
- Exclude generated protobuf (`net.bladewatch.app.grpc.**`) and the BYD SDK stubs in `android.hardware.*` / `android.os.*` — those are compile-time stubs never instantiated at runtime, so they are not testable by design.

### 5. Threshold ratchet policy

Both thresholds start at whatever the first real measurement gives and **may only ever be raised**. Record the current values somewhere a human will see them, and say in the notes where that is.

### 6. Wire into Gradle

The Flutter UI is a **separate Gradle project** (`flutter_ui/android/`), so the main app's `./gradlew test` does not reach it. Wire the Dart gate into `flutter_ui/android/app/build.gradle.kts` instead, and add Kover to the main app's `app/build.gradle.kts`. If you also add a convenience task in the main project that shells out to `flutter test`, it must not make the main app's build depend on the Flutter toolchain being installed — the daemon APK has to stay buildable on its own. Follow the hook pattern of the existing `validateI18nCatalogs` and `buildAngularWebUI` tasks rather than inventing a new one.

## Conventions for this refactor (decided — do not deviate)

- Dart lives under `flutter_ui/lib/` with `screens/<name>/` holding a pure-Dart `ChangeNotifier` controller, models, and the screen widget. Controllers must not import `package:flutter/material.dart` — that separation is what makes 100% coverage reachable.
- Kotlin lives under `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/`, declaring `package net.bladewatch.app.*` (the directory path and package name deliberately differ in this project — do not "fix" it).
- **No golden tests.** Visual parity is verified on the device in Phase 3 against `screenshots/native/`. Do not add `matchesGoldenFile` or `golden_toolkit`.

## Constraints

- Do NOT modify anything under `web/`, including its Playwright suite.
- Do NOT weaken, bypass or reorder the existing `validateI18nCatalogs` task.
- Do NOT lower any threshold to make a build pass.
- **Keep the harness simple.** No custom test framework, no fixture factory, no DSL — `flutter test` plus plain fakes. If the harness is bigger than the thing it tests, it is wrong.
- Do NOT commit. Leave changes in the working tree.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `cd flutter_ui && flutter test` runs green, even with an almost-empty suite.
- [ ] `flutter test --coverage` produces `lcov.info` with `lib/gen` excluded from the denominator.
- [ ] The Dart coverage script exits non-zero below threshold — **prove it** by temporarily setting the threshold above the current figure, observing the failure, then restoring.
- [ ] `./gradlew koverVerify` passes, and fails when the threshold is temporarily raised above the current figure — prove it the same way, then restore.
- [ ] Kover excludes generated protobuf and the `android.hardware.*` / `android.os.*` BYD stubs.
- [ ] The Kotlin baseline figure for the existing ~20-file suite is measured and recorded in the notes.
- [ ] `./gradlew koverVerify` gates the main app, and the Dart gate runs for the Flutter project.
- [ ] The main app still builds and tests **without** the Flutter toolchain installed.
- [ ] The RPC fake and the channel fake each have a one-paragraph usage note, and each can simulate a success, a Connect/channel error, and a timeout.
- [ ] Both initial threshold values, and where they are recorded, are written into the notes.
- [ ] `./gradlew assembleDebug` still succeeds and the existing test suite still passes.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.

  - `./tools/check_flutter_coverage.sh 99` → FAILED, printed "92.31% is below the required 99%", exit 1.
  - lib/gen exclusion proven with a throwaway `lib/gen/fake_generated.dart` (6 lines, 5 exercised by a throwaway test) — NOTE: had to import it as `package:bladewatch_ui/gen/fake_generated.dart` rather than a relative `../lib/...` path, because `flutter test --coverage`'s collector only attributes coverage to files reached via their own package: URI; a relative-path import compiles fine but the file silently never appears in lcov.info at all. Worth remembering for BladeWatch-ncbb.1: the real generated Dart protobuf code must be reachable via `package:bladewatch_ui/gen/...` for its (excluded) coverage entries to even show up for verification that the exclusion is doing something. With the throwaway file reachable that way, unfiltered total would have been 29/32=90.6% but the gate still reported 24/26=92.31% — proving the exclusion is real, not a no-op. Both throwaway files deleted immediately after, tree confirmed clean (`flutter_ui/lib/` contains only main.dart; `git status` shows no stray diff).

title: Port M3 design tokens to Dart ThemeData and build the nav shell
description:
> **CODE ONLY — do not touch the head unit in this task.**
> This project deliberately writes *all* Flutter code before any device work. Everything here
> is built and tested on the dev machine against the shared fakes from `BladeWatch-ncbb.5`,
> with no device and no daemon attached. On-device bring-up, screenshots, the render go/no-go
> and parity sign-off all live in **Phase 3** (`BladeWatch-imh6`).
> If you believe something genuinely cannot be verified without hardware, note it in the task
> notes for Phase 3 to pick up — do not reach for adb.

## Context

Port the Material 3 design tokens to a Dart `ThemeData` and build the Flutter navigation shell, so every screen ported in Epic 2 looks identical to its native counterpart by default rather than by hand-matching.

`docs/ui-ux-design-language.md` documents the **Android layer as the current M3 source of truth**. Read that document before starting — it is 409+ lines and explains the role mapping.

## Source files to port from

- `app/src/main/res/values/themes_bladewatch.xml` — M3 roles + widget styles
- `app/src/main/res/values/colors_m3.xml` and `app/src/main/res/values-night/` — light + dark palettes
- `app/src/main/res/values/dimens_bladewatch.xml` — shape + spacing scale
- `app/src/main/res/layout/activity_main_new.xml` — the shell: `shellRoot`, `shellContainer`, `navigationRailScroll`, `navigationRail` with 8 `railDest*` includes, toolbar, URL/status bar
- `app/src/main/res/layout/item_rail_destination.xml` and `app/src/main/res/layout/rail_header.xml` — rail item styling
- `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/MainActivity.kt` — `applyDriveSide()` (line ~952) and `isMainRailOnRight()` (line ~985)

## The 9 rail destinations — it is NINE, not eight

Ground truth is the `RailItem(...)` list in `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/MainActivity.kt` (around line 773), cross-checked against the `railDest*` include IDs in `app/src/main/res/layout/activity_main_new.xml`:

| # | Rail id | Navigates to |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `railDestDashboard` | `dashboardFragment` |
| 2 | `railDestLocation` | `locationFragment` |
| 3 | `railDestLive` | `liveViewFragment` |
| 4 | `railDestRecordings` | `recordingsFragment` |
| 5 | `railDestVehicle` | `vehicleControlFragment` |
| 6 | `railDestTrips` | `tripsFragment` |
| 7 | `railDestDiagnostics` | `diagnosticsFragment` |
| 8 | `railDestSettings` | `settingsFragment` |
| 9 | `railDestAbout` | `settingsAboutFragment` |

**`railDestAbout` is the one that gets missed.** In `app/src/main/res/layout/activity_main_new.xml` (lines 106-119) it sits *below a hairline divider* — a `View` of 40dp x 1dp, `?attr/colorOutlineVariant`, 6dp vertical margin — separating the eight primary destinations from the About meta-entry. That is a deliberate M3 grouping of action items apart from info items. Reproduce **both** the ninth item and the divider; a rail with eight items is a parity failure.

## Steps

1. Build a Dart `ThemeData` for light and dark from the colour/shape/type tokens. The app also adopts **Material 3 Expressive** refinements (tighter type tracking, tonal active indicators) tuned for a large in-car display — `docs/ui-ux-design-language.md` describes these; carry them over rather than accepting Flutter's stock M3 defaults.
2. Build the Dart nav shell with all 9 destinations (including the divider above About), the toolbar, and the URL/status bar.
3. **Implement drive-side mirroring.** The rail moves to the right-hand side for right-hand-drive cars. This is real shipped behaviour (`applyDriveSide()` / `isMainRailOnRight()`), it is easy to forget, and it is on the Epic 3 verification checklist.
4. Use the ARB strings from the i18n task for all rail labels — no hardcoded literals. The native rule is "use @string/getString, NOT hardcoded literals"; the same applies here. The only literal allowed is the brand name BladeWatch.
5. Add route stubs for all 11 screen groups so Epic 2 tasks just fill in a screen.

## Constraints

- Do NOT modify the native theme XML, layouts, or `MainActivity` — this task only READS them.
- Do NOT modify `web/`.
- Screen content is out of scope. Stubs only.
- Do NOT commit.

## Conventions for this refactor (decided — do not deviate)

**Where Dart code goes.** Mirror the native structure one-to-one, so each port is a translation rather than a redesign:

The Flutter UI is a **separate APK** (`net.bladewatch.flutter`) sharing a UID with `net.bladewatch.app`. Its Kotlin lives in `flutter_ui/android/app/src/main/kotlin/`; the main app's Kotlin is never called directly from Dart.

```
flutter_ui/lib/
  gen/                  generated protobuf — never hand-edited, excluded from coverage
  rpc/                  Connect transport + the 12 typed service clients
  platform/             Dart wrappers over the platform channels
  l10n/                 ARB catalogs
  theme/                ThemeData built from the Android M3 tokens
  shell/                nav rail, toolbar, routing
  screens/<name>/       <name>_controller.dart, <name>_models.dart, <name>_screen.dart
flutter_ui/test/        mirrors lib/ exactly
```

**State management: plain `ChangeNotifier` controllers. No Riverpod, no BLoC, no new state dependency.**
This mirrors the existing native Controller pattern (`app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/fragment/vehicle/VehicleController.kt`, `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/fragment/trips/TripsController.kt`, `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/fragment/surveillance/SurveillanceSettingsController.kt`), so porting is a direct translation.

- The controller is a **pure Dart class: it must not import `package:flutter/material.dart`.** It holds state, calls the RPC client and the platform channels, and calls `notifyListeners()`.
- The screen widget only renders controller state and forwards user intent. **No business logic in widgets.**
- This split is exactly what makes 100% coverage reachable — controllers are tested directly with no widget pump.

**No golden tests.** Visual parity is verified on the device in Phase 3 against `screenshots/native/`. Do not add `matchesGoldenFile` or `golden_toolkit`; they churn on every theme tweak and differ between host machines.

## Tests (TDD — required)

**Write the failing test first**, then the implementation, then refactor. Tests are not a closing chore — the test defines the behaviour.

- **Controller and model logic: 100% line and branch coverage.** These are pure Dart with no Flutter imports, so there is no excuse for a gap: every RPC-response-to-view-model transform, every formatter, every validation, every error branch.
- **Widget tests for every state the screen can reach**: loading, loaded, empty, error (including the "daemon not running" case), plus each interactive control. Assert on *behaviour* — that the right call was made with the right arguments — not merely that a widget rendered.
- Use the shared RPC fake and channel fake from `BladeWatch-ncbb.5`. Do not write your own.
- Tests must run green with `flutter test` on the dev machine with **no device and no daemon attached**.
- Run `flutter test --coverage`; `flutter_ui/lib/gen` is excluded from the denominator. Record the percentage in the task notes; it must not be lower than the previous task's figure.
- Anything uncovered is listed line-by-line in the notes with a concrete reason. **"Hard to test" is not a reason** — it means the logic belongs somewhere testable.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Light and dark themes both defined; no colour has its only definition inside one mode.
- [ ] All 9 rail destinations render with correct icons and localised labels.
- [ ] The hairline divider above the About entry is present and matches the native spacing.
- [ ] Drive-side mirroring works and matches the native behaviour when toggled.
- [ ] Theme token values are asserted in unit tests against the values parsed from the Android XML, so drift is caught without a device. Visual side-by-side comparison happens in `BladeWatch-imh6.1`.
- [ ] All 11 route stubs are reachable.
- [ ] `flutter analyze` clean, `./gradlew assembleDebug` succeeds.
- [ ] Tests were written before the implementation, not retrofitted.
- [ ] `flutter test` passes with zero skipped tests.
- [ ] 100% line and branch coverage of controllers and models, or every gap justified line-by-line in the notes.
- [ ] Every reachable screen state (loading / loaded / empty / error) has a widget test.
- [ ] Tests run green with no device and no daemon attached.
- [ ] `flutter test --coverage` percentage recorded and not lower than the previous task's.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.

## What was built

flutter_ui/lib/theme/ — ThemeData from the Android M3 tokens:
- color_tokens.dart: BwColorTokens.light/.dark, every M3 role + the 4 status colors,
  ported from colors_m3.xml / values-night/colors_m3.xml.
- dimens_tokens.dart: BwDimens, ported from dimens_bladewatch.xml (radii, page padding,
  gaps, icon sizes) plus the 2 ShapeAppearance.BladeWatch.* corner sizes from themes.xml.
- type_tokens.dart: BwTypeTracking, the 8 em-relative letterSpacing overrides from the
  TextAppearance.BladeWatch.* styles in themes_bladewatch.xml, plus the M3 spec font sizes
  needed to convert em → Flutter's logical-pixel letterSpacing (see Verification).
- bladewatch_theme.dart: BladeWatchTheme.light()/.dark() — ColorScheme from the tokens above,
  TextTheme = the M3 stock scale with only the 8 overridden roles getting fontWeight.w500 +
  the converted tracking (body roles untouched, matching how the Android theme leaves them
  unset too).

flutter_ui/lib/shell/ — the nav shell, ported from BOTH `activity_main_new.xml` and
`layout-land/activity_main_new.xml` (see the discovery below):
- drive_side.dart: DriveSide enum (left/right/auto).
- shell_controller.dart: ShellController (ChangeNotifier, no Flutter imports) — drive-side
  resolution mirroring applyDriveSide()'s exact branches, and the selected route.
- rail_destination.dart: the 9 RailDestination entries, ground truth = RailItem(...) in
  MainActivity.kt (~line 758). Icons use Flutter's built-in Material Icons by the same
  semantic name as each native icon's Material Symbol (e.g. Icons.monitor_heart for
  ic_diagnostics/monitor_heart) — not pixel-identical to Material Symbols Rounded, which
  Flutter doesn't bundle; noted in docs/ui-ux-design-language.md as a Phase-1 approximation,
  pixel sign-off is Phase 3.
- route_stubs.dart: BwRoutes, the 11 stub routes matching Epic 2's (BladeWatch-yz1e) 11 child
  tasks 1:1, plus a 12th extra route (settingsAbout) — see below.
- nav_rail.dart: NavRail (9 items + the hairline divider before About) and NavRailItem.
- app_shell.dart: AppShell — toolbar (title + accent stripe + status pill) + NavRail +
  content stage, ordered by ShellController.railOnRight.

lib/main.dart was rewired to a real BladeWatchApp (MaterialApp + BladeWatchTheme + AppShell),
replacing the untouched `flutter create` counter-app template that had sat there since
BladeWatch-ncbb.1. test/widget_test.dart now smoke-tests the real app instead of the counter.

## Discovery: the task's file list only covers half the shell — landscape is a different layout

The task lists `app/src/main/res/layout/activity_main_new.xml` as a source file. Reading it
fully (as instructed) surfaced that there is a SEPARATE `layout-land/activity_main_new.xml`
(and `layout-land/rail_header.xml`) that differs in more than orientation:
- Landscape shows a language-picker button at the TOP OF THE RAIL (`layout-land/
  rail_header.xml`); portrait removed that button entirely and moved it into the toolbar's
  end-cluster instead (`toolbarLanguageButton`) — confirmed by MainActivity.kt's
  `languageClick` listener, which binds whichever of the two buttons is actually present.
- Landscape toolbar is a fixed compact 48dp with TitleMedium; portrait uses the default
  ?attr/actionBarSize with TitleLarge.
- Landscape's About-divider margin is 4dp vertical, portrait's is 6dp; landscape's rail
  bottom padding is 12dp, portrait's is 16dp.

Since the target device is explicitly "rotatable" (docs/ui-ux-design-language.md describes
both a landscape and a portrait target size), I built AppShell/NavRail to branch on
`MediaQuery` orientation and reproduce both variants faithfully, rather than picking one and
silently dropping the other. Covered by dedicated tests (app_shell_test.dart's landscape/
portrait cases, nav_rail_test.dart's compact-divider-margin case).

## Route stubs: 11 per Epic 2, plus a 12th for a real 9th rail item

Epic 2 (BladeWatch-yz1e) has exactly 11 child tasks (startup, dashboard, settings hub,
diagnostics, trips, location, recordings, surveillance, vehicle, live view, dialogs) — BwRoutes
matches these 1:1. But the native rail has 9 destinations, and the 9th (About,
settingsAboutFragment) is its own distinct nav destination in MainActivity.kt, separate from
Settings (settingsFragment) — even though Epic 2 builds it as one of the "7 sections" inside
the Settings-hub task, not as its own task. So About needs its own route for the rail's
selection state to tell it apart from Settings, but it isn't one of the "11" Epic-2 counts
against. Added as BwRoutes.settingsAbout, documented in the class's own doc comment, and
tested separately from `all` (which stays at exactly 11).

## Verification

- flutter analyze: No issues found (clean).
- flutter test: 243/243 pass, 0 skipped (up from 191 at ncbb.3; +52 new tests across theme/
  shell/main).
- flutter test --coverage + tools/check_flutter_coverage.sh: 636/638 lines = 99.69% (up from
  99.49% at ncbb.3, per the "must not be lower" requirement). The 2 uncovered lines are
  lib/main.dart's `void main() { runApp(...); }` — the same category of gap already justified
  at ncbb.1/ncbb.2/ncbb.3 (the app entry point itself, not meaningfully unit-testable, not
  covered by convention in Flutter apps); it just moved from the placeholder counter-app's
  main() to the real one's, since this task replaced that file.
- Theme token values are asserted against the real Android XML, not hand-copied and trusted:
  color_tokens_test.dart parses colors_m3.xml + values-night/colors_m3.xml with a regex and
  compares every BwColorTokens.light/.dark field; dimens_tokens_test.dart does the same
  against dimens_bladewatch.xml (plus themes.xml's 2 ShapeAppearance corner sizes);
  type_tokens_test.dart does the same against themes_bladewatch.xml's letterSpacing values.
  bladewatch_theme_test.dart then asserts the *built* ThemeData's ColorScheme/TextTheme
  actually uses those token values (fontWeight.w500 + correctly-converted pixel
  letterSpacing on the 8 overridden roles, body roles untouched). This whole chain was
  proven correct empirically, not assumed — see the em→pixel conversion note below.
- `cd flutter_ui/android && ./gradlew assembleDebug` — BUILD SUCCESSFUL (run directly, not
  just via `flutter build apk`, to match the acceptance criterion literally).
  `flutter_ui/android: ./gradlew test koverVerify` — unaffected (100%, 161/161, unchanged; no
  Kotlin touched this task).
- Main app regression: `./gradlew test koverVerify validateArbCatalogs validateAndroidStrings
  validateI18nCatalogs` — BUILD SUCCESSFUL, all UP-TO-DATE, confirming this task's changes
  (isolated to flutter_ui/) didn't affect the main app.
- `git diff --stat` against every native file this task was only allowed to READ
  (themes_bladewatch.xml, colors_m3.xml, values-night/, dimens_bladewatch.xml,
  activity_main_new.xml + its layout-land/ counterpart, item_rail_destination.xml,
  rail_header.xml, MainActivity.kt, web/) — empty; none touched.
- No golden tests added, per the explicit constraint.

## A real Flutter API gotcha worth recording

`Typography.material2021(...).black/.white` and even `ThemeData(useMaterial3: true).textTheme`
return TextStyle objects with `fontSize: null` — Flutter resolves concrete M3 type-scale sizes
lazily, only once a TextTheme is read through `Theme.of(context)` inside an actual widget tree
(confirmed empirically with a throwaway testWidgets probe). Since BladeWatchTheme needs a
concrete pixel size *at theme-build time* to convert Android's em-relative letterSpacing, it
pins the well-known M3 spec sizes (36/32/28/24/22/16/14/12) as BwTypeTracking constants —
verified to exactly match what a real widget tree resolves to, not guessed.

- Theme token values asserted in unit tests against values parsed from Android XML: yes, see

- All 11 route stubs reachable: yes — BwRoutes.all has exactly 11 unique entries, each
  produces a real StubScreen (tested for all 11 individually, plus the extra settingsAbout).
  Only 8 of the 11 are reachable via a rail tap in this task's shell (dashboard, settings,
  diagnostics, trips, location, recordings, vehicle, live view) — startup/surveillance/dialogs
  aren't rail destinations in the native app either (startup precedes the shell, surveillance
  is drilled into from Settings, dialogs are modal overlays), so this matches native reality

- flutter analyze clean, ./gradlew assembleDebug succeeds: yes.
- Tests written before implementation: yes for shell_controller.dart, nav_rail.dart,

  above was discovered mid-implementation — the test file existed and was run (failing) before
  the fix, but the token files themselves were sketched first; noting this honestly rather

- flutter test passes, zero skipped: yes, 243/243.

  branch-coverage claim above is a manual audit of every conditional path against its own
  test, not a tool-reported percentage; noting this limitation rather than fabricating a

- Tests run green, no device, no daemon: yes, confirmed throughout.
- flutter test --coverage percentage recorded, not lower than previous: yes, 99.69% vs 99.49%

No mistakes found on re-verification; all figures above were regenerated fresh this turn.

title: Port strings.xml to Flutter ARB for all 17 locales with parity check
description:
> **CODE ONLY — do not touch the head unit in this task.**
> This project deliberately writes *all* Flutter code before any device work. Everything here
> is built and tested on the dev machine against the shared fakes from `BladeWatch-ncbb.5`,
> with no device and no daemon attached. On-device bring-up, screenshots, the render go/no-go
> and parity sign-off all live in **Phase 3** (`BladeWatch-imh6`).
> If you believe something genuinely cannot be verified without hardware, note it in the task
> notes for Phase 3 to pick up — do not reach for adb.

## Context

Port the Android string catalogs to Flutter ARB so the Flutter UI is fully localised from day one, with key names preserved 1:1 so parity checking against the native UI is mechanical.

## Current state

- `app/src/main/res/values/strings.xml` — 624 translatable base keys.
- 17 locales total: `values/` (en) plus `values-de`, `values-es`, `values-fr`, `values-hi`, `values-it`, `values-ja`, `values-ko`, `values-nb`, `values-nl`, `values-pt-rBR`, `values-ru`, `values-th`, `values-tr`, `values-vi`, `values-zh-rCN`, `values-zh-rTW`.
- There are currently **zero gaps** across all 17. Keep it that way.
- `values-night/` is theme colours, NOT strings — do not treat it as a locale.

Note there is a SEPARATE web catalog at `app/src/main/assets/web/i18n/*.json` (1598 keys) used by the Angular SPA. **Do not touch it and do not merge into it** — the decision on this refactor was to port strings.xml to ARB, keeping the two catalogs independent.

## Steps

1. Write a conversion script (put it under `tools/i18n/`, alongside the existing `tools/i18n/generate_vehicle_strings.py`) that reads each `values*/strings.xml` and emits `flutter_ui/lib/l10n/app_<locale>.arb`.
2. Map Android locale dir names to ARB locale codes: `values-pt-rBR` to `app_pt_BR.arb`, `values-zh-rCN` to `app_zh_CN.arb`, `values-zh-rTW` to `app_zh_TW.arb`, the rest are straightforward.
3. **Keep key names identical to the Android names** (e.g. `rail_dashboard`, `settings_section_surveillance`). Do not rename or namespace them.
4. Handle Android-specific syntax correctly: positional args (`%1$s`, `%2$d`) become ARB placeholders; escaped apostrophes (`\'`) and `&` must be unescaped; `<string-array>` and `<plurals>` entries need explicit handling — find them first and decide per case.
5. Wire `flutter_localizations` + `intl` and enable `gen-l10n` in `flutter_ui/pubspec.yaml` / `l10n.yaml`.
6. Add an ARB key-parity Gradle check next to the existing `validateI18nCatalogs` task in `app/build.gradle.kts`. That task exists because LLM edits previously introduced smart-quote delimiters and unescaped quotes into locale JSON and shipped broken — the same failure mode applies to ARB. The check must FAIL the build on invalid JSON or a missing key versus `app_en.arb`.

## Constraints

- Do NOT modify `app/src/main/assets/web/i18n/*.json` or anything under `web/`.
- Do NOT delete `res/values*/strings.xml` in this task — the native UI still uses them until Epic 4.
- Do NOT hand-translate. Every locale's values come from the existing XML.
- Do NOT commit.

## Conventions for this refactor (decided — do not deviate)

- Kotlin source lives under `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/`. **Note the directory path and the package name differ in this project**: files under `com/loabletech/bladewatch/` declare `package net.bladewatch.app.*`. Match the surrounding files; do not "fix" this.
- JVM tests go in `app/src/test/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/`, mirroring the main source layout.
- Kotlin coverage is measured by **Kover** with a verify gate (set up in BladeWatch-ncbb.5). Run `./gradlew test koverVerify`.
- Dart state management for this refactor is plain `ChangeNotifier` controllers — no Riverpod, no BLoC. Relevant if this task touches any Dart.
- **No golden tests** anywhere in this refactor.

## Tests (TDD — required)

`values/strings.xml` has 624 `<string>` tags (matching the task's "624 translatable base keys")

632 as one flat key space (ARB has no separate "plurals" concept — a `<plurals>` becomes one
ICU-syntax string value under its own key). This is additive, not a shortfall.

## Deliberate exclusion (documented per the acceptance criteria)

Every translated locale's `strings.xml` has 631 `<string>` tags, not 624 — 7 more than the
English template: `rail_integrations`, `integrations_hero_title`, `integrations_hero_subtitle`,
`integrations_status_configured`, `integrations_status_not_set_up`, `integrations_status_unknown`,
`integrations_configure_button`. These don't exist in `values/strings.xml` at all — stale
leftovers from a removed/renamed screen. The task's "there are currently zero gaps across all
17" claim is about the *existing* `validateAndroidStrings` check, which is one-directional
(only catches a locale *missing* something the template has — see
`parseStrings()`/`missing = masterKeys - parsed.keys` in `app/build.gradle.kts`); it was never
checking the reverse direction, so this 7-key asymmetry existed undetected. `xml_to_arb.py`
only ever looks up template keys per locale, so these 7 are naturally never copied (reported
on stdout as "skipped N orphan key(s)", not treated as an error) — every ARB ends up with
exactly the template's 632-key set, satisfying "every ARB has exactly the same key set as
app_en.arb — 0 missing, 0 extra."

## A second, more serious discovery: pre-existing native-app bug, filed separately

4 keys in `values/strings.xml` are `translatable="false"` (plain URLs: ko-fi/GitHub links).
Despite that marker, a past bulk/LLM translation pass translated them anyway in most locales,
and — having no real content to translate — hallucinated unrelated sentences. Confirmed by
direct inspection: 8 locales (de, es, fr, it, ja, nl, zh-rCN, zh-rTW) have completely unrelated
garbage text instead of a URL (e.g. `values-de`'s `settings_about_source_url` is "Das ist ein

today, completely unrelated to and unfixed by this task (`values*/strings.xml` is out of scope
here) — filed as **BladeWatch-hiw1** for the native side. The Flutter port is NOT affected:
`xml_to_arb.py` pins all 4 of these keys to the English template's value for every locale ARB
regardless of what the source locale XML says (see `non_translatable_keys()` in the script),
so the new Flutter UI will show the correct URLs in every locale from day one.

`pt_BR`, `zh_CN`, `zh_TW` are region-qualified locales with no bare-language counterpart in
this Android catalog (no `values-pt` or `values-zh` directory exists). `flutter gen-l10n`
refuses to generate unless a bare-language ARB (`app_pt.arb`, `app_zh.arb`) also exists as a
fallback. The script synthesizes these two extra files (copies of `app_pt_BR.arb` and

title: Build the privileged-operations layer over loopback IPC
description:
> **CODE ONLY — do not touch the head unit in this task.**
> This project deliberately writes *all* Flutter code before any device work. Everything here
> is built and tested on the dev machine against the shared fakes from `BladeWatch-ncbb.5`,
> with no device and no daemon attached. On-device bring-up, screenshots, the render go/no-go
> and parity sign-off all live in **Phase 3** (`BladeWatch-imh6`).
> If you believe something genuinely cannot be verified without hardware, note it in the task
> notes for Phase 3 to pick up — do not reach for adb.

## Context

Build the privileged-operations layer inside the Flutter APK — everything the UI needs that is **not** a ConnectRPC call.

Because the Flutter UI is a **separate APK** (`net.bladewatch.flutter`) sharing a UID with `net.bladewatch.app`, a Dart `MethodChannel` cannot reach the main app's process. Channels still work, but they call **new Kotlin inside the Flutter APK's own `android/` source set**, which then talks to the daemon over the existing loopback IPC.

This keeps the new Kotlin surface small: the daemon already runs privileged and already exposes the operations we need as IPC commands. **Do not duplicate `AdbDaemonLauncher`, `StorageManager`, or `UnifiedConfigManager` into the Flutter APK** — go through IPC instead.

## The transport

`app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/TcpCommandServer.java` on `127.0.0.1:19876`, authenticated by the shared token in `/data/local/tmp/bladewatch_ipc_token` (644, world-readable) **and** gated by peer UID via `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/PeerCredentials.java`. The shared UID is what lets the Flutter APK through — verified in `BladeWatch-7965.2`.

**Port the client from `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/config/SecretConfigBridge.kt`** — that is the existing app-side IPC caller and the reference for the wire format, token handling and error cases. Read it fully before writing anything.

## Command set actually available over IPC — verified against the source, not the docs

Read the `case` labels in `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/TcpCommandServer.java` directly; several docs are stale about this.

`start`, `stop`, `status`, `ping`, `shutdown`, `getFrame`, `setOutput`, `setStreamMode`, `getStreamMode`, `enableSurveillance`, `disableSurveillance`, `surveillanceStatus`, `setAccState`, `setRecordingMode`, `getRecordingMode`, `setBitrate`, `setCodec`, `setRecordingsStorageType`, `setRecordingsLimitMb`, `getQualitySettings`, `auth_invalidate`, `secret_get`, `secret_get_section`, `secret_put`, `secret_delete`.

From `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/SurveillanceIpcServer.java` (19877): `UPDATE_GPS` (line 276).

### There is NO `shell` command — do not design around one

`shell` (free-form `sh -c` over IPC) was **deliberately removed** as a security fix: it was remote code execution as UID 2000. `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/TcpCommandServer.java:485-486` records the removal. Two places still refer to it and are **stale**: the comment at `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/TcpCommandServer.java:98-99`, and `docs/ipc-auth-and-secrets.md`. Do not reintroduce it, and do not treat those references as evidence it exists.

## What to build in `flutter_ui/android/app/src/main/kotlin/`

| Dart channel group | Implementation |
|---|---|
| `ipc.*` | the IPC client itself — token read, TCP connect, command/response, typed errors |
| `auth.*` | JWT minting. `secret_get` the device secret, then sign HMAC-SHA256 locally. **Port the token format and signing from `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/auth/AuthManager.java`** — device token is `deviceId + "-" + secret`; the JWT must be one the daemon accepts. Mirror the 4-minute cache keyed to the auth state version. |
| `daemon.*` | `start` / `stop` / `status` over IPC — for the Daemons settings screen |
| `config.*` | `secret_get` / `secret_put` / `secret_delete` — for the Zrok token dialog and similar |
| `update.*` | OTA. This one genuinely cannot go over IPC because it needs Android's `PackageInstaller`. Port the download/verify/install flow from `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/updater/AppUpdater.java`. Decide and record in the notes **which APK this updates** — the Flutter APK, the main APK, or both. |

## Explicitly NOT needed in the Flutter APK

- **A `shell.*` channel.** There is no `shell` IPC command (removed as an RCE fix). The ADB Console screen runs its commands through **dadb over ADB**, exactly as the native UI does — see `BladeWatch-yz1e.4`. That is a plain TCP client to adbd and needs no special permission and no shared UID, but it does require ADB to be up.

- **Daemon launching at boot.** `DaemonStartupManager` and `AdbDaemonLauncher` stay in the main APK, which keeps its boot receiver. The UI only needs `start`/`stop`/`status`.
- **QR generation** — use the Dart `qr_flutter` package.
- **Anything already available over ConnectRPC.** If the data is on port 8080, use the RPC, not a channel. Check before adding a channel method.
- A shared Gradle library module between the two APKs. The surface here is small enough that extracting one is not worth refactoring the working app; revisit only if duplication actually grows.

## Constraints

- **Never log a secret value.** `/data/local/tmp/bladewatch_secrets.json` holds device tokens, tunnel tokens and cloud credentials — see the Security Notes in `CLAUDE.md` and `docs/ipc-auth-and-secrets.md`. The `auth.*` group returns a short-lived JWT, never the raw secret.
- **Do NOT change permissions** on `/data/local/tmp/bladewatch_ipc_token` (must stay 644) or `/data/local/tmp/bladewatch_secrets.json` (must stay 600).
- **Do NOT modify `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/PeerCredentials.java`, `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/TcpCommandServer.java`, `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/SurveillanceIpcServer.java`, or anything under `app/src/test/`.** If IPC is refused, fix the manifests or signing — never widen the UID gate.
- Do NOT modify the daemon, the protos, or `web/`.
- Do NOT commit.

## Conventions for this refactor (decided — do not deviate)

- Kotlin source lives under `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/`. **Note the directory path and the package name differ in this project**: files under `com/loabletech/bladewatch/` declare `package net.bladewatch.app.*`. Match the surrounding files; do not "fix" this.
- JVM tests go in `app/src/test/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/`, mirroring the main source layout.
- Kotlin coverage is measured by **Kover** with a verify gate (set up in BladeWatch-ncbb.5). Run `./gradlew test koverVerify`.
- Dart state management for this refactor is plain `ChangeNotifier` controllers — no Riverpod, no BLoC. Relevant if this task touches any Dart.
- **No golden tests** anywhere in this refactor.

## Tests (TDD — required)

**Write the failing test first**, then the implementation, then refactor.

The existing suite is ~20 files / ~3,100 LOC — read the closest neighbours first: `app/src/test/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/connect/ConnectWireParityTest.java` (proto/JSON wire parity), `app/src/test/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/auth/AuthManagerTest.java`, `app/src/test/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/AuthMiddlewareTest.java`, `app/src/test/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/IpcRoundTripTest.java`, `app/src/test/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/IpcTokenManagerTest.java`, `app/src/test/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/logging/SecretRedactorTest.java`, and the `vehicle/` suite (`app/src/test/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/vehicle/VehicleClientMapTest.kt`, `app/src/test/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/vehicle/VehicleFormattersTest.kt`, `app/src/test/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/vehicle/TyreTierTest.kt`, `app/src/test/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/vehicle/VehicleI18nParityTest.kt`). **CLAUDE.md's Testing section lists only four of these and is stale — trust the filesystem.**
- **100% coverage of every method you add, including every error path.** On this head unit the real failures are: the daemon is not up yet, the IPC token is unreadable, the command is rejected, the socket times out. Each needs a test proving the right error reaches the caller rather than being swallowed.
- Test argument marshalling in **both** directions. A dropped or mistyped field across a platform channel produces a bug that only appears on the car.
