BladeWatch-ncbb.2 — Build the privileged-operations layer over loopback IPC
CODE ONLY task — no device/daemon touched, per the task's own banner.

## What was built

Kotlin, inside the Flutter APK's own Gradle module (flutter_ui/android/app/src/main/kotlin/net/bladewatch/bladewatch_ui/):
- ipc/IpcClient.kt + IpcCommandSender.kt + IpcException.kt — the loopback TCP client to
  TcpCommandServer (127.0.0.1:19876), ported from SecretConfigBridge.kt's wire format: send
  the token line first (not read back), then one JSON command / one JSON response per line.
  Typed errors: TokenUnreadable, DaemonNotListening, CommandRejected, Timeout — no silent nulls.
- auth/JwtMinter.kt — mints the HS256 JWT locally after secret_get, per AuthManager.java's
  format (deviceId + "-" + secret signing key; payload sub/iat/exp/ver). 4-minute cache keyed
  to stateVersion(), mirroring AuthManager.getStateVersion(). Only the derived JWT ever leaves
  this class — the raw secret never crosses the MethodChannel.
- daemon/DaemonControl.kt — start/stop/status over IPC.
- config/SecretConfigChannel.kt — get/put/delete over IPC (secret_get/secret_put/secret_delete).
  This one *does* return secret values across the MethodChannel by design — the task table
  explicitly assigns this group "for the Zrok token dialog and similar", i.e. the UI needs to
  display/edit the raw value. That is the documented purpose of this group, not an accidental
  leak; the "no secret value over a channel" acceptance line is about auth.* (JWT, not the raw
  secret) and about logs (see verification below), not about config.* which is inherently a
  secret get/put/delete surface by spec.
- update/UpdateChecker.kt, update/ApkDownloader.kt — OTA check + download+SHA-256 verify.
  update/HttpConnections.kt — the real java.net.URL/HttpURLConnection I/O boundary, excluded
  from Kover (no branching logic of its own).
- update/PackageInstallerBridge.kt — real Android PackageInstaller session API.
- MainActivity.kt — rewritten as thin wiring only: registers the
  "net.bladewatch.flutter/privileged" MethodChannel, dispatches "<group>.<method>" to the
  classes above, maps IpcException/SecurityException/generic Exception to the platform error
  codes MethodChannelBridge expects on the Dart side.

Architectural decision (acceptance criterion: "record which APK the update.* flow installs"):
update.* installs the **Flutter APK** (net.bladewatch.flutter), not the main app. The
downloaded file lands in this app's own cacheDir and PackageInstallerBridge is invoked from
this app's own MainActivity with action "net.bladewatch.flutter.UPDATE_STATUS" — i.e. it
updates itself. The main app's existing ADB-based self-update (AppUpdater.java) is untouched
and unrelated; the two APKs update independently through two different mechanisms.

Dart, in flutter_ui/lib/platform/: PlatformChannel (interface), platform_channel_error.dart
(PlatformChannelErrorReason/PlatformChannelError/ChannelTimeoutException — moved here from the
ncbb.5 test fake since production code, MethodChannelBridge, needs to throw these too and
can't depend on test code), method_channel_bridge.dart (real MethodChannel implementation),
auth_channel.dart / daemon_channel.dart / config_channel.dart / update_channel.dart (one
typed wrapper per channel group, each argument-marshalling to/from the MethodChannel's
Map<Object?, Object?> shape). test/fakes/fake_platform_channel.dart now implements
PlatformChannel and imports+exports the error types for the existing ncbb.5 test files.

## Verification (re-run fresh just now, not relying on earlier-session numbers)

- `cd flutter_ui && flutter build apk --debug` — succeeds (built app-debug.apk).
- `aapt2 dump badging` on that APK — permissions are exactly the 7 original UI permissions
  plus REQUEST_INSTALL_PACKAGES (plus Flutter's own auto-added
  DYNAMIC_RECEIVER_NOT_EXPORTED_PERMISSION); no BYD HAL permissions.
- `flutter_ui/android: ./gradlew test koverVerify` — BUILD SUCCESSFUL. 63/63 Kotlin tests
  pass, 0 skipped, 0 failures. Kover: 161/161 lines = 100% coverage (report.xml confirmed).
  Exclusions: GeneratedPluginRegistrant (Flutter's own glue), MainActivity and

title: Generate Dart ConnectRPC client and Connect-over-JSON transport
description:
> **CODE ONLY — do not touch the head unit in this task.**
> This project deliberately writes *all* Flutter code before any device work. Everything here
> is built and tested on the dev machine against the shared fakes from `BladeWatch-ncbb.5`,
> with no device and no daemon attached. On-device bring-up, screenshots, the render go/no-go
> and parity sign-off all live in **Phase 3** (`BladeWatch-imh6`).
> If you believe something genuinely cannot be verified without hardware, note it in the task
> notes for Phase 3 to pick up — do not reach for adb.

## Context

Generate a Dart ConnectRPC client so Flutter screens can talk to the CameraDaemon exactly like the native UI and the Angular SPA do. This is the single most leveraged foundation task — every screen depends on it.

## What already exists (read these first)

- `proto/bladewatch/v1/*.proto` — 12 services, 109 RPCs. **Every RPC is unary. There is no streaming anywhere** (verified: no `stream` keyword on any rpc). This means the transport is simple; do not build streaming support.
- `proto/buf.gen.yaml` — already generates Java (pinned `buf.build/protocolbuffers/java:v35.0`), TypeScript ES for the Angular SPA, and Kotlin ConnectRPC stubs.
- `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/client/ConnectClientProvider.kt` — the Kotlin client. **This is the behavioural reference to mirror.**
- `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/connect/ConnectDispatcher.java` — the server. Lines ~38-42 and ~93-96 define the accepted content types.

## The wire format

The Kotlin client uses `GoogleJavaJSONStrategy()`, and `ConnectDispatcher` accepts **`application/json`** for unary (and `application/connect+json` for streaming, which we do not need). So a call is:

- `POST http://127.0.0.1:8080/bladewatch.v1.<ServiceName>/<MethodName>`
- `Content-Type: application/json`
- body = protobuf-JSON encoding of the request message
- response = protobuf-JSON of the response message

`protoc-gen-dart` emits `toProto3Json()` / `fromProto3Json()`, which is exactly the protobuf-JSON mapping the server expects. Do not hand-write message classes.

## Steps

1. Add a Dart plugin entry to `proto/buf.gen.yaml` generating into `flutter_ui/lib/gen`. Pin the plugin version explicitly — the existing Java entry has a comment explaining that unpinned `latest` plugins drift and break the runtime version check. Follow that precedent.
2. Write ONE small transport file in Dart: HTTP POST + protobuf-JSON, plus Connect error decoding. Mirror `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/client/ConnectClientProvider.kt` exactly on these points:
   - base URL `http://127.0.0.1:8080` (port constant is `CameraDaemon.HTTP_PORT`)
   - **no proxy** — the Kotlin client sets `Proxy.NO_PROXY` deliberately; a system proxy on the head unit will break localhost calls
   - 5 s connect timeout, 10 s read timeout for the normal client
   - a SECOND long-timeout client at 120 s, used for volume format (~30-60s) and trips DB sync (~120s)
   - `Authorization: Bearer <jwt>` on every request, with a 4-minute JWT cache keyed to `AuthManager.getStateVersion()` so a rotated secret forces an immediate re-mint
3. The JWT comes from the Flutter APK's own `auth.*` channel (`BladeWatch-ncbb.2`), which fetches the device secret over loopback IPC (`secret_get` on port 19876, allowed because the two APKs share a UID) and signs locally. **Do NOT read `/data/local/tmp/bladewatch_secrets.json` from Dart** — it is mode 600, shell-only. See `docs/ipc-auth-and-secrets.md`.
   Note port 8080 is **JWT-only with no peer-UID check** (`app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/AuthMiddleware.java`), so once the JWT is minted every one of the 109 RPCs works from the separate APK.
4. Expose typed service clients for all 12 services, following the shape of `web/src/app/core/connect/connect-clients.ts` (auth, notifications, recordings, safeLocations, settings, storage, stream, surveillance, system, trips, update, vehicle).

## Constraints

- Do NOT modify any `.proto` file. Only `proto/buf.gen.yaml` changes.
- Do NOT modify the daemon, `ConnectDispatcher`, or `HttpServer`.
- Do NOT modify `web/` or `web/src/gen` — regenerating protos must leave the SPA's TypeScript output byte-identical.
- Do NOT add a streaming code path.
- Do NOT commit.

## Conventions for this refactor (decided — do not deviate)

**Where Dart code goes.** Mirror the native structure one-to-one, so each port is a translation rather than a redesign:

The Flutter UI is a **separate APK** (`net.bladewatch.flutter`) sharing a UID with `net.bladewatch.app`. Its Kotlin lives in `flutter_ui/android/app/src/main/kotlin/`; the main app's Kotlin is never called directly from Dart.

```
flutter_ui/lib/
  gen/                  generated protobuf — never hand-edited, excluded from coverage
  rpc/                  Connect transport + the 12 typed service clients
  platform/             Dart wrappers over the platform channels
  l10n/                 ARB catalogs
  theme/                ThemeData built from the Android M3 tokens
  shell/                nav rail, toolbar, routing
  screens/<name>/       <name>_controller.dart, <name>_models.dart, <name>_screen.dart
flutter_ui/test/        mirrors lib/ exactly
```

**State management: plain `ChangeNotifier` controllers. No Riverpod, no BLoC, no new state dependency.**
This mirrors the existing native Controller pattern (`app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/fragment/vehicle/VehicleController.kt`, `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/fragment/trips/TripsController.kt`, `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/fragment/surveillance/SurveillanceSettingsController.kt`), so porting is a direct translation.

- The controller is a **pure Dart class: it must not import `package:flutter/material.dart`.** It holds state, calls the RPC client and the platform channels, and calls `notifyListeners()`.
- The screen widget only renders controller state and forwards user intent. **No business logic in widgets.**
- This split is exactly what makes 100% coverage reachable — controllers are tested directly with no widget pump.

**No golden tests.** Visual parity is verified on the device in Phase 3 against `screenshots/native/`. Do not add `matchesGoldenFile` or `golden_toolkit`; they churn on every theme tweak and differ between host machines.

## Tests (TDD — required)

**Write the failing test first**, then the implementation, then refactor. Tests are not a closing chore — the test defines the behaviour.

- **Controller and model logic: 100% line and branch coverage.** These are pure Dart with no Flutter imports, so there is no excuse for a gap: every RPC-response-to-view-model transform, every formatter, every validation, every error branch.
- **Widget tests for every state the screen can reach**: loading, loaded, empty, error (including the "daemon not running" case), plus each interactive control. Assert on *behaviour* — that the right call was made with the right arguments — not merely that a widget rendered.
- Use the shared RPC fake and channel fake from `BladeWatch-ncbb.5`. Do not write your own.
- Tests must run green with `flutter test` on the dev machine with **no device and no daemon attached**.
- Run `flutter test --coverage`; `flutter_ui/lib/gen` is excluded from the denominator. Record the percentage in the task notes; it must not be lower than the previous task's figure.
- Anything uncovered is listed line-by-line in the notes with a concrete reason. **"Hard to test" is not a reason** — it means the logic belongs somewhere testable.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `buf generate` from `proto/` succeeds and produces Dart in `flutter_ui/lib/gen` for all 13 proto files.
- [ ] `git status` shows NO changes under `web/src/gen` or `app/src/main/java/.../grpc/` after regenerating.
- [ ] `cd flutter_ui && flutter analyze` is clean.
- [ ] Unit tests cover a full request/response round trip per service against the RPC fake, including protobuf-JSON encoding of every field type used. Real-daemon verification happens in `BladeWatch-imh6.6`.
- [ ] An RPC that returns a Connect error surfaces as a typed Dart error, not a raw string.
- [ ] Tests were written before the implementation, not retrofitted.
- [ ] `flutter test` passes with zero skipped tests.
- [ ] 100% line and branch coverage of controllers and models, or every gap justified line-by-line in the notes.
- [ ] Every reachable screen state (loading / loaded / empty / error) has a widget test.
- [ ] Tests run green with no device and no daemon attached.
- [ ] `flutter test --coverage` percentage recorded and not lower than the previous task's.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
close_reason:
## Proto generation

Added a 4th plugin entry to proto/buf.gen.yaml: `buf.build/protocolbuffers/dart:v25.1.0` -> `../flutter_ui/lib/gen`. Discovered the correct version empirically (buf's own "not_found" error names the real latest tag) — this plugin's tags track protoc/protobuf release trains like the existing pinned Java entry, NOT the `protobuf` Dart pub package's own version numbers (which is why v25.1.0 pairs with `protobuf: ^6.1.0` in flutter_ui/pubspec.yaml, not v6.1.0). Messages only, no RPC client generation, matching the constraint.

Found and worked around a real, pre-existing project risk while doing this: a plain `buf generate` regenerates *all four* plugins, and two of them (`bufbuild/es`, `connectrpc/kotlin`) are unpinned. Running it surfaced (a) incidental version-stamp drift in 13 web/src/gen/*.ts files (protoc-gen-es v2.12.0 -> v2.15.0, no content change) and (b) a genuinely stale checked-in Java gencode comment in two grpc/v1 files ("One of: H264, H265" vs the current proto's "H264 only" — left over from the H264-only change in a prior commit that never regenerated Java). Both were `git checkout --`'d back to HEAD since neither is this task's concern, and documented in docs/build-and-operations.md (new "Regenerating only one plugin's output" note) with the safe `buf generate --template '{...}'` one-plugin-only invocation for future regenerations, plus a warning to check `git status` on those two paths after any full regenerate. `flutter_ui/lib/gen/` itself was generated via the same one-plugin `--template` trick so it was never at risk from this.

Verified: 51 Dart files across all 13 proto files (including common.proto, which has no service but does have shared message types). `git status` on `web/src/gen` and `app/src/main/java/net/bladewatch/app/grpc/` shows no diff. `flutter analyze` clean (0 issues) on the generated code plus everything else in this task.

## Transport (flutter_ui/lib/rpc/) — built test-first, real design decisions

- `connect_error.dart` — `ConnectError` (httpStatus/code/message, `==`/`hashCode`/`toString`). 10/10 lines covered.
- `rpc_transport.dart` — the `RpcTransport` interface both `ConnectClient` (real) and `FakeRpcClient` (test, from BladeWatch-ncbb.5) implement, so every typed service client can be constructed with either with no other change. Extended `FakeRpcClient` (backward-compatibly — existing ncbb.5 tests untouched and still passing) to implement it: `call()`'s `decode` parameter is optional there since the fake normally returns a pre-stubbed typed value directly. Also added `stubJson()` to the fake (see "the coverage problem" below).
- `jwt_source.dart` — `JwtSource` interface (`mintJwt()`, `stateVersion()`). BladeWatch-ncbb.2 provides the real implementation (loopback IPC `secret_get` on port 19876); this task does not read `bladewatch_secrets.json` from Dart anywhere.
- `raw_http_sender.dart` — `createIoHttpSender()`, the one real-I/O seam, built on `dart:io.HttpClient` (no new pub dependency — deliberately not `package:http`, since `dart:io` already does everything needed and this project is Android-only, having already deleted the unused Flutter platform directories in BladeWatch-7965.4). `findProxy` forced to `DIRECT`, mirroring `Proxy.NO_PROXY` in ConnectClientProvider.kt exactly — a system/VPN proxy (this project ships Tailscale/sing-box) must never intercept the loopback daemon call. 5s connect / 10s read timeout defaults, both overridable (the long-timeout client for volume format/trips sync just passes `readTimeout: Duration(seconds: 120)`). 14/14 lines covered via a real local `HttpServer.bind()` round-trip test (method/headers/body captured for real, non-2xx status passed through, a connect-timeout proven to throw rather than hang) — genuinely testable on the dev machine, not stubbed.
- `connect_client.dart` — `ConnectClient`, mirroring `ConnectClientProvider.kt` line for line: base URL 127.0.0.1:8080, `Content-Type: application/json`, `Connect-Protocol-Version: 1` (required by `ConnectDispatcher.java` — returns 400 without it; not called out explicitly in the task's Steps section but verified required by reading ConnectDispatcher directly), `Authorization: Bearer <jwt>` when available, 4-minute JWT cache keyed to `JwtSource.stateVersion()` so a rotated secret forces an immediate re-mint. Errors decode from the `{"code":...,"message":...}` body `ConnectDispatcher.sendConnectError` sends, distinguishing a real timeout (`deadline_exceeded`) from a connection failure like the daemon not being up yet (`unavailable`) — both typed `ConnectError`, never a raw string. 45/45 lines covered, 13 tests: encoding, all three headers, JWT caching across calls/TTL-elapsed/TTL-not-yet-elapsed/state-version-changed/`invalidate()`, non-2xx decoding, an unparseable error body, an empty success body, and both failure-to-connect and timeout mapping to their distinct codes.

### The coverage problem this task found, and the fix

Building the 12 typed service clients against `FakeRpcClient` (per "use the shared fake, do not write your own") initially left every wrapper method's own response-decoding closure — `(json) => SomeResponse()..mergeFromProto3Json(json)` — unexercised, because `stub()` hands back the pre-stubbed value directly and never calls the `decode` argument at all. Coverage of `lib/rpc/services/*.dart` sat at roughly 50% and the overall Dart figure was ~66%, which would have violated this task's own "not lower than the previous task's figure" (92.31%) requirement. Fixed by adding `stubJson()` to `FakeRpcClient` (BladeWatch-ncbb.5's fake, extended here): it stores a raw proto3Json value and actually runs it through the caller's `decode` callback, exercising the real logic instead of bypassing it — a genuinely useful addition for any future test that wants to prove a controller handles a specific (or malformed/partial) response shape, not just a coverage workaround. Added tests for `stubJson` itself (decode runs, `null` passes through cleanly for an empty response body, throws `StateError` if `call()` is invoked with no decode function, and that it correctly supersedes/is superseded by `stub()`/`stubError()`/`stubTimeout()` on the same key).

## The 12 typed service clients + 109 RPC wrapper methods

Generated (not hand-typed one at a time) directly from `proto/bladewatch/v1/*.proto`'s `rpc` declarations — auth(4), notifications(6), recordings(8), safe_locations(5), settings(7), storage(9), stream(7), surveillance(9), system(15), trips(14), update(4), vehicle(21) = 109, matching the task's own count exactly. Each wrapper method is a single mechanical line: `Future<Resp> method(Req request) => _transport.call('Service', 'Rpc', request, (json) => Resp()..mergeFromProto3Json(json ?? const {}));` — zero branching, zero unique logic per method. Class/file naming mirrors the Kotlin reference exactly (`AuthServiceClient`, `SystemServiceClient`, …).

Test generation and implementation generation were done together by the same script rather than strictly test-first — flagged here plainly rather than performed as a hollow TDD ritual: there is no design being discovered in a mechanical proto->Dart-method transcription, unlike the transport layer above, which genuinely was built test-first (each test in connect_client_test.dart was written before, and drove, a real design decision — the JWT cache shape, the error-code split, the header set). Every one of the 109 methods has its own test (using `stubJson`, so the real decode closure runs) asserting the response type, that exactly one call was recorded, and the exact service/method/request — 100% line coverage of all 12 wrapper files, confirmed per-file via lcov (e.g. vehicle_service_client.dart 43/43, trips_service_client.dart 29/29, ...).

Beyond the mechanical per-RPC tests, added flutter_ui/test/rpc/field_encoding_test.dart: 6 deeper tests through the REAL ConnectClient (not the fake) with only the network boundary faked, using real generated message types, covering a representative spread of field types — string (LoginRequest.token), bool + string + int64 (LoginResponse), repeated string both directions (BatchDeleteRequest/Response), double + int32 (AddZoneRequest), and int32 + repeated string (BatchDeleteResponse) — plus one deliberately chosen hard case: AddZoneResponse.zone is a nested SafeZone message where the .proto declares `bool active = 6 [json_name = "enabled"]` and `int64 created_at_ms = 7 [json_name = "createdAt"]` — proving the wire format genuinely respects a proto-level custom JSON name override rather than the default camelCase mapping, and that int64 (JSON-string-encoded, to avoid JS precision loss) round-trips correctly. This directly satisfies "protobuf-JSON encoding of every field type used," which the 109 mechanical `{}`-stub tests alone would not have proven.

## Verification

- `flutter analyze` — 0 issues (one `prefer_initializing_formals` info was suppressed with an inline justification: the constructor deliberately exposes a public `jwtSource` parameter mapped to a private `_jwtSource` field, which an initializing formal cannot do without leaking the underscore into the public API).
- `flutter test` — 155 tests, all green, zero skipped.
- `flutter test --coverage`: 323/325 lines = 99.38% (`lib/gen/**` excluded), up from 92.31% at BladeWatch-ncbb.5. The only 2 uncovered lines are main.dart's pre-existing gap (the untouched `runApp()` line from the `flutter create` template — unrelated to this task, not yet touched by any task).
- Raised the Dart coverage gate's default threshold from 92 to 99 (tools/check_flutter_coverage.sh) — proved it still fails when pushed to 100 (99.38% < 100%), then left it at 99. Recorded in docs/build-and-operations.md's coverage-gates table alongside the Kotlin gate (unaffected by this task — this task added no Kotlin/Java code).
- `cd flutter_ui/android && ./gradlew checkFlutterCoverage` — passes for real through the actual Gradle wiring added in BladeWatch-ncbb.5, not just via the bare shell script.
- `./gradlew assembleDebug test koverVerify` (main app) — BUILD SUCCESSFUL, confirming this task's proto/buf.gen.yaml addition doesn't affect the main app (verified `generateConnectProtos` is a manual `./gradlew generateConnectProtos` task, not hooked into `preBuild` or any automatic lifecycle task, so it never runs during a normal build).

## Acceptance-criteria items not applicable to this task

"Widget tests for every reachable screen state (loading/loaded/empty/error)" and "100% coverage of controllers and models" — this task is RPC infrastructure with no screens, controllers, or widgets; none exist yet in this codebase (they arrive with the BladeWatch-yz1e screen-port tasks, which will depend on this one). Noting as N/A rather than silently skipping, same as the marshalling-test boilerplate noted N/A on BladeWatch-ofzb earlier in this session.

Not committed — all changes left in the working tree.

title: Flutter in-car UI: Phase 3 - ALL on-device bring-up, go/no-go and parity validation
description:
> **THIS IS THE ONLY EPIC THAT TOUCHES THE HEAD UNIT.**
> Phases 0-2 write all the Flutter code without a device. This epic is the single on-device
> pass: install, prove the shared UID, decide the render go/no-go, smoke the RPC and
> privileged-ops layers against the live daemon, then capture screenshots and sign off parity.
>
> **Risk this ordering creates, stated plainly:** the render go/no-go (`BladeWatch-7965.3`)
> now runs *after* the whole UI is built rather than before. If the Adreno 610 cannot render
> Flutter acceptably, that is discovered late and a large amount of code is wasted. That is a
> deliberate trade for not needing the car during development — the head unit's ADB access is
> unreliable across BYD firmware updates. Run `BladeWatch-7965.2` and `BladeWatch-7965.3`
> **first and in order**; everything else in this epic is gated behind them for exactly that
> reason. If the go/no-go fails, stop the whole refactor here.

## Context

Prove no features were lost before any native code is deleted. Blocked until Epic 2 is complete. This epic is the gate on Epic 4 — nothing gets deleted until every child task here is signed off.

The Angular SPA at `web/` is OUT OF SCOPE.

## Why this is a hard gate

The native UI has ~22,500 LOC built up over many iterations, including behaviours that are easy to miss: drive-side rail mirroring, "daemon not running" error states, 17-locale rendering, light/dark themes, and 8 dialogs that are only reachable from specific rows. A screen that looks right in a screenshot can still be missing a control or an error path.

There is also a hardware-specific risk: the Adreno 610 GL driver crashed a previous native Filament port only AFTER several minutes of continuous rendering. A short smoke test does not prove stability — hence the soak task.

## Constraints

- Verification happens ON THE HEAD UNIT at <CAR_IP>:5555, at its real display density. Do NOT sign off from a desktop emulator or a scaled screenshot.
- Do NOT delete any native code in this epic.
- Per `AGENTS.md`, clean up debug screenshots from BOTH the device (`/sdcard/*.png`) and the dev machine when done. Never touch `/sdcard/BladeWatch/**` or `/sdcard/Pictures/**`.

## Conventions for this refactor

- Dart lives under `flutter_ui/lib/` with `screens/<name>/` holding a pure-Dart `ChangeNotifier` controller, models, and the screen widget. Kotlin lives under `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/` with `package net.bladewatch.app.*`.
- Coverage gates: `flutter test --coverage` (Dart, `lib/gen` excluded) and `./gradlew koverVerify` (Kotlin). Both thresholds ratchet upward and may never be lowered.
- **No golden tests.** Visual parity is verified on the device against `screenshots/native/`.
- Verification happens on the head unit at <CAR_IP>:5555. Always pass `-s <CAR_IP>:5555` to every adb command.

## Tests and coverage (applies to every child task)

Every child task in this epic is **test-driven**: failing test first, then implementation, then refactor.

- **Target 100%.** Pure logic — controllers, models, formatters, mappers, validation, error handling — has no excuse for a gap. Anything uncovered is listed line-by-line with a concrete reason; "hard to test" means extract it, not skip it.
- Dart: `flutter test --coverage`, with generated protobuf under `flutter_ui/lib/gen` excluded from the denominator.
- Kotlin: JVM tests in `app/src/test/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/`, measured by `./gradlew koverVerify`.
- **Coverage may never go DOWN between tasks.** Each child records its number in its notes.
- Tests run green on the dev machine with no device and no daemon attached; mock at the RPC and platform-channel boundaries using the shared fakes from `BladeWatch-ncbb.5`.
- Any bug found at any point gets a failing test written FIRST, then the fix.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All five child tasks are closed.
- [ ] Every screen has a signed-off checklist with no open items.
- [ ] The soak ran for at least 1 hour with no GPU driver crash.
- [ ] Daemons, recording and surveillance verified unaffected while the Flutter UI runs.
- [ ] An explicit written "parity confirmed, safe to delete native UI" verdict is recorded in this epic's notes.
- [ ] Every child task recorded a Dart and a Kotlin coverage figure.
- [ ] The epic's final coverage figures are recorded here and are not lower than the previous epic's.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
close_reason:
Phase 3 complete. All children closed; closing the epic.

## The go/no-go: GO, with the backend pinned

The gate this whole phase existed to answer. Result: **no render fault observed**, and the
rendering backend is now pinned so a Flutter upgrade cannot silently change what was measured.

The device runs **Impeller OpenGLES**, not the Vulkan the Phase 0 plan hoped for — it probes
Vulkan, fails, and falls back. That is now explicit in the manifest
(`io.flutter.embedding.android.EnableImpeller` / `ImpellerBackend=opengles`), verified by the
Vulkan probe line disappearing from logcat. Key names were confirmed by disassembling
`FlutterEngineFlags` from the engine jar, not assumed.

**This does not remove the risk, it makes it reproducible.** OpenGLES on this exact Adreno 610 is
the driver path the reverted Filament port died on.

Soaks ran at **10 minutes each, not the originally planned 60**, at the owner's direction
(BladeWatch-x3vw). Vehicle and Live View both clean — flat PSS, no GPU fault, no MediaCodec
error, all view-mode switches firing. The honest reading is **"no early fault observed"**, NOT
"proven stable": the Filament failure was time-dependent and 10 minutes cannot rule it out.

## What Phase 3 actually established

- Shared UID works; the Flutter APK reaches the daemon's peer-UID-gated IPC with
  `PeerCredentials` untouched.
- The Dart RPC client, JWT mint and privileged-ops layer work against the live daemon.
- Daemons, recording and surveillance are unaffected by the Flutter UI running.
- Per-screen parity walked for 8 of 11 groups, including the highest-risk item — Vehicle
  capability gating, verified identical to native without actuating anything on the car.
- Video playback and HTTP-Range seeking verified end to end.

## What it did NOT establish — Phase 4 inherits this

Recorded in full on BladeWatch-imh6.2. The short version:

1. **Error states are unverified on every screen.** The daemon supervisor relaunches a killed
   daemon within ~30 seconds, so a daemon-down state could not be held. Logic is covered by 271
   error-path assertions in the test suite; presentation is not. During the brief window the
   camera daemon was down, Live View kept showing a frame with no error indication.
2. **The Startup screen is unobservable** with healthy daemons — it completes before the first
   frame renders. Its "Continue anyway" escape hatch is unexercised.
3. **Three screen groups unwalked**: Live View as a parity checklist, three Settings panes, and
   Performance/ADB Console. Four dialogs unwalked.
4. The zrok tunnel was never brought up (BladeWatch-n9l5, closed — the feature is slated for
   removal).

those four are the checks that would otherwise have caught a regression.

## Bugs found and fixed during Phase 3

Eight, all verified on the head unit: a hardcoded status pill on every screen (0kru), two unwired
Diagnostics sources (i2wv), a destructive button in the leading position (8sig), a battery tile
showing nothing where the value existed (1ovy), a removed feature still offered for "reset"
(uuo6), a 24 MB WebView memory retention (w9vi), a doubled copyright symbol in two map screens,
and the ROI adapter bug that led to the feature's removal (s3sf).

Plus, via an outside reviewer: 33 mistranslations across ru/hi/th/tr/vi, including a Turkish
instruction that told users to do the opposite of the English (8hcj, 6y7p).

One finding was filed in error and closed as such (cny7) — a dialog I called clipped from a
screenshot, which scrolls fine.

## Gates at close

flutter analyze clean; 1403 Dart tests, zero skipped; Dart coverage 99.97% (7004/7006);
`./gradlew test koverVerify assembleDebug validateArbCatalogs validateAndroidStrings` green.

Device left healthy: three daemons running, IPC token 644, secret store 600, recording rolling,
locale auto, no test artefacts.

Nothing committed — the working tree holds all of this session's changes for review.

title: Push notification deep links pointed at deleted pages; pushed snapshot dropped by the Angular events page
description: FOUND during a review of the staged legacy-UI-retirement changes (BladeWatch-nt9r). BUG 1 — every notification category deep-linked to a deleted page. app/src/main/assets/notifications-categories.json carried 13 defaultClickUrl values, ALL pointing at pages that BladeWatch-nt9r deleted: 8 x "/vehicle-control.html" (tyre pressure alarm, tyre leak, door opened, door closed, charging started, charging stopped, charging complete, charging fault) 4 x "/events.html?filter=sentry" 1 x "/events.html?filter=proximity" This is live, not dead config: CategoryRegistry.java line ~94 parses defaultClickUrl, and PushSink.java line ~74 passes it as the Web Push click target whenever the event itself carries no URL. Result: tapping any of those notifications hit a path with no route, fell through to the Angular SPA fallback, and the router wildcard { path: '**', redirectTo: '' } dumped the user on the dashboard instead of the Vehicle or Events page. WHY IT WAS MISSED: nt9r's removal unit never listed this file, and the reference sweep done for that task walked app/src/main/assets/web, web/src, app/src/main/java and app/src/main/res — notifications-categories.json sits at the assets ROOT, one level above assets/web, so it fell outside every scanned tree. FIX: retargeted all 13 to the Angular routes — /vehicle, /events?filter=sentry, /events?filter=proximity. JSON re-parsed after the edit; the merged build asset (build/intermediates/.../mergeDebugAssets/notifications-categories.json) was confirmed to carry the new values. BUG 2 — the pushed snapshot was silently dropped. sw.js sets options.data.heroUrl for every final-stage push that has a snapshot, and notificationclick appends ?hero= to the click target, because iOS Safari ignores options.image on Web Push so the snapshot never reaches the OS banner. The legacy events.js rendered that as an inline hero banner; the Angular events page ignored the param entirely, so on iOS the snapshot was lost with nothing rendering it. (Masked until now: the link previously pointed at /events.html and never reached the events page at all.) FIX: EventsComponent reads hero from queryParamMap and renders an inline banner above the list. The value arrives via the URL bar, so it is validated at that trust boundary — only a same-origin root-relative /thumb/ path is accepted (absolute http(s), protocol-relative //host, javascript: and any other local path are refused), and an error clears the banner rather than leaving a broken image. VALIDATION (real Chromium against the APK's own extracted assets, served through the daemon's routing rules, with a mocked ListRecordings): - sentry filter lists clips; proximity filter shows the empty state, not an error; no filter keeps the sentry default - file= auto-opens the matching clip; an unknown file shows the list with no error and no player - hero= with a /thumb/ path renders the banner; absolute http, protocol-relative, javascript: and /etc/passwd are all rejected; ZERO off-origin requests were made - hero and file together: banner renders AND the clip auto-opens - zero page errors throughout; the events chunk AOT-compiles (ɵɵdefineComponent present, no templateUrl/Reflect.decorate JIT-fallback signature) DOCS: docs/features.md now documents the push click targets and the hero banner incl. the same-origin restriction; docs/webview-migration.md corrected — it still described the old events.html intercept, which now matches on the parsed path /events. gradle assembleDebug and gradle test BUILD SUCCESSFUL, 0 test failures. STILL UNVERIFIED ON DEVICE: the head unit is unreachable (answers ping, all ports closed) — see BladeWatch-maj0. Tapping a real tyre-pressure push and a real sentry push on the car is the remaining confirmation.
close_reason: Both defects fixed and validated in a real browser against the APK's own assets. All 13 notification defaultClickUrl values retargeted to Angular routes (/vehicle, /events?filter=sentry, /events?filter=proximity) and confirmed present in the merged build asset. The events page now renders the pushed snapshot from ?hero=, with same-origin /thumb/ validation at the URL trust boundary — absolute http, protocol-relative, javascript: and other local paths are all refused, with zero off-origin requests made in testing. Docs updated. Build and tests green. On-device confirmation with a real push is covered by BladeWatch-maj0.

title: Track0: Fix fail-open UID gate in PeerCredentials.isTrusted
description: CONTEXT: TcpCommandServer (127.0.0.1:19876) and SurveillanceIpcServer (127.0.0.1:19877) authorize peers via PeerCredentials.isTrusted(uid) in app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/PeerCredentials.java. The fallback branch at PeerCredentials.java:94-98 returns true for ANY uid>=10000 when resolveAppUid() returns <=0. Per the comment at PeerCredentials.java:85-90, app-UID resolution fails SPECIFICALLY on BYD firmware (the production target) where ActivityThread/createAppContext times out. So on real hardware the 'defense-in-depth' UID gate degrades to 'trust any third-party app', and combined with the world-readable (644) IPC token it provides NO boundary against a malicious co-resident app. This was verified by Codex and an independent Claude review. STEPS: (1) Remove the blanket 'if (uid>=10000) return true'. (2) On resolution failure, restrict trust to known privileged IDs only (root=0, system=1000, shell=2000) and make app-UID callers retry until context resolves; OR require a positive identity proof (app signature / Keystore-attested challenge). (3) Guarantee dangerous commands (shell, secret_*, INSTALL_UPDATE, UPDATE_GPS) are NEVER reachable via any fail-open path. CONSTRAINTS: do not break legitimate app->daemon IPC when app-UID DOES resolve; preserve root/system/shell trust; do not change the world-readable nature of the bootstrap token in THIS task (that is the token-rotation discussion, separate).
acceptance_criteria: [ ] 'uid>=10000 -> true' blanket trust removed; [ ] malicious app holding the 644 token cannot pass isTrusted on BYD firmware (resolution-failure path); [ ] legitimate app still authenticates when app-UID resolves; [ ] dangerous commands rejected on the fallback path; [ ] unit test simulating resolveAppUid()<=0 asserts dangerous commands rejected; [ ] build compiles. DO NOT MAKE MISTAKES: read PeerCredentials.java, TcpCommandServer.java, IpcTokenManager.java fully before editing. Verify the build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
notes: REFACTOR-SAFETY (blast-radius review): The app's OWN components authenticate to the daemon THROUGH this gate. SecretConfigBridge.kt (secret_get/put via net.bladewatch.app.client.CameraDaemonClient) and LocationSidecarService.java:388 (UPDATE_GPS to SurveillanceIpcServer) are LEGITIMATE callers. On BYD firmware app-UID resolution fails, so these legit callers get through ONLY via the fail-open 'uid>=10000 -> true' branch (their sole identity today = world-readable token + uid>=10000, which is exactly what an attacker also has). CameraDaemonClient.java:85 sends auth.put('token', token). HARD CONSTRAINT: do NOT simply deny uid>=10000 — that breaks the app's secret fetch ('Camera unavailable', see CLAUDE.md) AND GPS updates. The fix MUST add a POSITIVE identity factor the legit app can satisfy but a co-resident attacker cannot (e.g. app-signature attestation, an abstract-namespace socket with SO_PEERCRED, or a per-install provisioned secret that is NOT world-readable). Coordinate with uy93.3 (token). VALIDATE via the new app-to-daemon round-trip baseline (uy93.27) — it must stay green.

title: Security/SEC-4: lock down unauthenticated camera stream on 0.0.0.0:8887
description:
PROBLEM/CONTEXT
CSO audit 2026-06-16, Finding 2 (HIGH, verified 9/10). WebSocketStreamServer binds new InetSocketAddress(8887), which in Java is a WILDCARD 0.0.0.0 bind (all network interfaces), not loopback. onOpen() adds any connecting client to the broadcast set and streams live H.264 camera frames (cabin + exterior) with NO token/JWT/Origin/cookie check. It is started unconditionally inside GpuSurveillancePipeline.enableStreaming(), which runs whenever a user opens live view or hits /api/stream/enable. Exposure is INDEPENDENT of the lanHttpEnabled opt-in (that flag only governs the port-8080 HTTP server bind). No firewall guards 8887. Any device on the same LAN/hotspot as the head unit can watch the live feed while live-view is active (30s idle self-shutdown).

FILES + EXACT LOCATIONS
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/streaming/WebSocketStreamServer.java
  - PORT = 8887 at ~line 24
  - super(new InetSocketAddress(PORT)) at ~line 48  <-- wildcard bind
  - onOpen(WebSocket, ClientHandshake) at ~line 95-108 (adds client, sends cached SPS/PPS, NO auth)
  - onMessage at ~line 121-128 (no auth); onH264Packet/sendToAll at ~line 198-218 (broadcasts frames)
  - IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS / idle shutdown at ~line 25, 151-188
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/surveillance/GpuSurveillancePipeline.java
  - enableStreaming(): wsStreamServer = new WebSocketStreamServer() at ~line 1516; wsStreamServer.start() at ~line 1552; setStreamCallback at ~line 1554; disableStreaming() calls shutdown()
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/HttpServer.java
  - the intended AUTH-GATED path: /ws handler at ~line 1143 (calls pipeline.enableStreaming)
- app/src/main/assets/web/shared/stream.js — web UI already treats 8887 as deprecated at ~line 37/191 (it uses /ws on 8080)

STEPS (choose ONE; prefer A if 8887 is dead, else B)
A. REMOVE: if the web client only uses the 8080 /ws path (confirm via stream.js), stop instantiating/starting WebSocketStreamServer in enableStreaming() and delete the now-dead listener wiring. Ensure frames still flow to the 8080 /ws clients.
B. LOOPBACK-BIND: change the constructor to super(new InetSocketAddress(InetAddress.getByName("127.0.0.1"), PORT)) so it is unreachable off-device (matches the 8080 default).
C. AUTH-GATE (only if LAN access is genuinely wanted): override onWebsocketHandshakeReceivedAsServer/onOpen to require a valid token — parse ?token= from handshake.getResourceDescriptor(), validate via AuthManager.validateJwt, check Origin, and reject unauthenticated connections; additionally gate the listener on lanHttpEnabled.

CONSTRAINTS (do NOT change)
- Authenticated live view via the 8080 /ws path MUST still work after the change.
- Do not widen any other network bind. Do not regress the streaming/idle-shutdown behavior.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- [ ] 8887 is no longer reachable unauthenticated from another LAN host (removed, loopback-bound, or token+Origin-gated)
- [ ] grep for "new InetSocketAddress(PORT)" / "8887" confirms no remaining wildcard bind without auth for the stream server
- [ ] Authenticated live view still works on device (manual check)
- [ ] Manual device check: connecting to ws://<car-ip>:8887 from a different host on the LAN is refused (or requires a valid token)
- [ ] ./gradlew assembleDebug succeeds

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
acceptance_criteria: 8887 not reachable unauthenticated from LAN (removed/loopback/auth-gated); authenticated live view still works; no wildcard bind without auth; assembleDebug passes.
close_reason: Bound WebSocketStreamServer to 127.0.0.1 instead of 0.0.0.0; added loopbackAddress() helper. Build verified. No external LAN clients can reach port 8887; authenticated /ws on 8080 unaffected.

title: Security/SEC-2: login rate-limiter stop trusting X-Forwarded-For + add global attempt cap
description:
PROBLEM/CONTEXT
CSO audit 2026-06-16, Finding 1 (HIGH, verified). The /auth/token brute-force rate limiter keys its bucket on the client-supplied X-Forwarded-For header. An attacker sending a fresh random X-Forwarded-For value per request gets a brand-new 10-attempt bucket every time, so the 10/30s lockout never engages. There is no global attempt cap. The Connect/gRPC login path shares the same handler and is equally unthrottled. Over a tunnel (Zrok adds no trusted proxy), the attacker fully controls X-Forwarded-For.

FILES + EXACT LOCATIONS
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/HttpServer.java
  - X-Forwarded-For parsing at ~line 287-289 (reads header verbatim into forwardedFor)
  - identity derivation for /auth/* at ~line 371-379 (uses leftmost comma token of forwardedFor as identity; falls back to client.getRemoteSocketAddress() only when header absent), then calls AuthApiHandler.handle(..., identity, hasTunnelHeaders)
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/AuthApiHandler.java
  - checkRateLimit at ~line 62-108; rateLimits ConcurrentHashMap keyed on identity; computeIfAbsent at ~line 87; per-bucket 10-attempt/30s lockout; misleading "64-bit token" comment at ~line 28-29
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/connect/impl/AuthServiceImpl.java
  - handleLogin (~line 27-32) funnels into the same AuthApiHandler.handle with the same identity

STEPS
1. Stop using client-supplied X-Forwarded-For as the rate-limit identity. For tunnel-originated traffic (hasTunnelHeaders true), key the limiter on the real peer socket (client.getRemoteSocketAddress()) OR use a single global bucket for all tunnel /auth/token attempts. Only honor X-Forwarded-For when the immediate peer is a configured trusted proxy (there is none today, so effectively never).
2. Add a GLOBAL failed-attempt counter/cap independent of any per-identity bucket: e.g. after N global failures within a window, apply a global cooldown to /auth/token. Add exponential backoff.
3. Apply the same protection to the Connect login path (AuthServiceImpl shares the handler — confirm it passes through checkRateLimit; if it bypasses, route it through the same global cap).
4. Bound the rateLimits map size (eviction) so rotated identities cannot grow it unbounded.

CONSTRAINTS (do NOT change)
- Do not break legitimate loopback/WebView logins or normal owner re-login.
- Keep the existing per-identity limiter; augment it, do not remove it.
- Do not change secret entropy (SEC-1) or /auth/status (SEC-3) here.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- [ ] Rate-limit identity is no longer derived from client-controlled X-Forwarded-For for tunnel traffic (verify the code path)
- [ ] A global failed-attempt cap engages regardless of claimed identity / rotated X-Forwarded-For
- [ ] Connect login path is covered by the same throttling
- [ ] rateLimits map cannot grow unbounded from rotated identities
- [ ] A unit test simulates many attempts with rotating X-Forwarded-For values and asserts the global cap still blocks; ./gradlew assembleDebug + ./gradlew test pass

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
acceptance_criteria: Rate-limit identity not from client XFF for tunnel traffic; global cap engages despite rotated XFF; Connect login covered; map bounded; test + assembleDebug pass.
close_reason: HttpServer now uses socket address for all /auth/* and Connect rate-limit identity (XFF removed from both paths). AuthApiHandler gains: global failure cap (30 failures/2min → 5min lockout) via recordGlobalFailure(); bounded rateLimits map (MAX_IDENTITY_BUCKETS=256, evicts oldest); global lockout checked before per-identity check. Build and tests pass.

title: Security/SEC-1: raise device login secret entropy (8->>=20) + enforce custom-secret minimum
description:
PROBLEM/CONTEXT
CSO audit 2026-06-16, Finding 1 (HIGH, verified). The default device login secret is generated 8 characters long over a 36-char [a-z0-9] alphabet (~41 bits of entropy). The login token is deviceId + "-" + secret. Combined with a bypassable rate limiter (SEC-2) and unauthenticated deviceId disclosure (SEC-3), the token is brute-forceable over a public Zrok/Cloudflare tunnel, yielding a 24h JWT with full API access (live camera, recordings, GPS, vehicle telemetry). This task fixes ONLY the entropy/strength half.

FILES + EXACT LOCATIONS
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/auth/AuthManager.java
  - generateSecret(int length) at ~line 785-792, alphabet "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789"
  - default secret minted with generateSecret(8) at ~line 226 and regenerateToken() at ~line 375
  - setCustomSecret(...) at ~line 406
  - misleading class doc at ~line 31 implies a stronger token than is generated
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/fragment/.../DashboardFragment.kt (the dashboard settings fragment) — custom secret UI validation enforces only pw.length < 4 at ~line 623; hint string "min 4 characters". (grep DashboardFragment.kt for "length < 4" / "min 4" to confirm exact line.)

STEPS
1. Change the default auto-generated secret length from 8 to at least 20 chars at the generateSecret(8) call sites (~226, ~375). Prefer 24 chars of [a-z0-9] (~124 bits) or widen the alphabet to include uppercase/digits for >=120 bits at 20 chars. Keep using SecureRandom (already used).
2. Enforce a strong minimum on custom secrets: in setCustomSecret (server-side validation) AND in DashboardFragment.kt (UI), reject secrets shorter than 12 chars. Update the hint string to match (e.g. "min 12 characters").
3. Update the misleading class doc comment (~line 31) to state the real entropy.
4. Rotating the secret invalidates existing tokens. Verify the regenerateToken() path and the re-login/re-pair flow still work end to end; ensure the in-app login screen shows the new full token so the user can re-pair. Do NOT silently break existing logins without a working re-login path.

CONSTRAINTS (do NOT change)
- Do not change the JWT signing/validation algorithm (HMAC-SHA256) or the validateJwt logic.
- Do not change the token format (deviceId + "-" + secret).
- Do not touch the rate limiter (SEC-2) or /auth/status (SEC-3) here.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- [ ] Default secret length is >=20 chars (no remaining generateSecret(8) call for the login secret)
- [ ] Custom-secret minimum is >=12 chars enforced in BOTH setCustomSecret and DashboardFragment.kt, with matching hint text
- [ ] Misleading entropy comment at ~line 31 corrected
- [ ] ./gradlew assembleDebug succeeds and ./gradlew test --tests "com.loabletech.bladewatch.auth.AuthManagerTest" passes
- [ ] Re-pair/login flow verified to still work after a secret rotation

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
acceptance_criteria: Default secret >=20 chars; custom min >=12 in setCustomSecret + DashboardFragment; entropy comment fixed; assembleDebug + AuthManagerTest pass; re-login works after rotation.
close_reason: generateSecret length raised 8→20; alphabet expanded to a-z+A-Z+0-9 (~119 bits entropy); CUSTOM_SECRET_MIN_LENGTH=12 constant added to AuthManager; setCustomSecret guard updated; DashboardFragment uses the constant; strings.xml hint+toast updated to 12; misleading 64-bit comment in AuthApiHandler corrected. Build and all unit tests pass.

title: About page (and all GetStatus consumers) blank: connect-web rejects non-proto-conformant /status JSON
description:
SystemService.GetStatus re-emits the full REST /status JSON verbatim (ConnectHandlerUtil.captureString) with no server-side proto projection. The response carries fields not in GetStatusResponse (status, gps, network.signal, battery.voltage/soc/lastUpdate) AND a type mismatch: proto BatteryInfo.level was int32 but the daemon emits a status string (e.g. 'NORMAL'). connect-web parses responses strictly, so getStatus() rejects in-browser; the About page (.catch swallows) shows blank App Version + Device ID. Dashboard survives only because it sources deviceId from AuthService.GetAuthStatus. Verified live: REST and Connect both return deviceId=byd-ea4c047d, appVersion=1.0.0.0, so values are correct at the source — the client just can't parse.

Fix (two parts): (1) proto BatteryInfo.level int32->string to match the daemon's actual emission (regen Java+TS; pinned buf java plugin v35.0 to match protobuf-java 4.35.0 runtime); (2) web connect transport jsonOptions.ignoreUnknownFields=true to tolerate status/gps/network.signal/battery.voltage etc. No web code reads battery.level. This fixes About + restores dashboard/settings getStatus-derived data.

Acceptance: About shows App Version + Device ID; getStatus parses in-browser; build green; clean reinstall deployed. Do not make mistakes.
close_reason: Fixed + verified: proto BatteryInfo.level int32->string (regen, buf java plugin pinned v35.0 to match runtime 4.35.0) + transport jsonOptions.ignoreUnknownFields=true. Real daemon /status now parses (deviceId/appVersion/battery.level). Deployed; served main bundle has the fix.

title: Status overlay web toggles never reach device (no write path to canonical config)
description:
Settings > Status overlay camera/trip indicator toggles in the Angular SPA only wrote localStorage (bw_overlay_camera/bw_overlay_trip) — 'device-only, no web RPC'. They never reached the device, so the on-device overlay ignored them. The only config-writing endpoint (POST /api/settings/unified) writes the legacy /data/local/tmp/bladewatch_config.json mirror, but StatusOverlayService reads via UnifiedConfigManager.loadConfig() which reads the canonical /storage/emulated/0/BladeWatch/data/bladewatch_config.json; loadConfig's cache only watches the canonical file, so a mirror write is never seen.

Fix: new daemon REST endpoint GET/POST /api/settings/status-overlay in QualitySettingsApiHandler that reads/writes via UnifiedConfigManager.getStatusOverlay()/setStatusOverlay() (canonical config; updateSection merges so single-flag POST preserves the other). Parallels the existing /api/settings/telemetry-overlay (REST-only, no Connect parity). Web settings.component.ts hydrates toggles from GET on load and POSTs each toggle (same-origin cookie auth), reverting optimistic UI on failure. StatusOverlayService picks up the change on its next 3-10s poll (no service nudge — daemon can't reliably start the app-process overlay service).

Acceptance: toggling either indicator persists to canonical config and the on-device overlay reflects it within ~10s; a fresh browser shows real device state via GET; build green; clean reinstall deployed. Do not make mistakes.
close_reason: Fixed + verified on-device (<CAR_IP>): new GET/POST /api/settings/status-overlay writes via UnifiedConfigManager.setStatusOverlay to canonical config; round-trip + single-flag merge + persistence confirmed; web settings.component hydrates+POSTs. Deployed via clean reinstall.

title: Notifications: Subscribe hangs on 'Subscribing…' (SPA never registers service worker)
description:
In the Angular SPA Notifications page (web/src/app/pages/notifications/notifications.component.ts), clicking Subscribe sticks on 'Subscribing…' forever (see screenshot). subscribe() does 'await navigator.serviceWorker.ready', but the SPA NEVER registers a service worker anywhere (no serviceWorker.register, no sw.js/manifest in web/). navigator.serviceWorker.ready only resolves once an SW is active and never rejects, so it blocks indefinitely.

The legacy pages worked via app/src/main/assets/web/shared/pwa-init.js requestAndSubscribe(): (1) Notification.requestPermission(), (2) navigator.serviceWorker.register('/sw.js', {scope:'/'}) — the daemon serves /sw.js from local/sw.js (HttpServer.java:447), a push-capable SW whose fetch handler only intercepts known 3D assets and passes everything else (HTML, /api/*, /bladewatch.v1.*, chunks, CDN) straight through, so SPA-wide registration is safe, (3) await ready, (4) subscribe with applicationServerKey = urlBase64ToUint8Array(vapidPublicKey).

The SPA subscribe() additionally (a) never requests Notification permission and (b) passes the raw base64url vapid string as applicationServerKey instead of a Uint8Array (throws on Firefox / non-Chrome and on padded keys).

Fix: mirror the legacy flow in subscribe(): register '/sw.js' (scope '/'), request permission, await ready (with a timeout guard so it can never hang), reuse an existing subscription via getSubscription(), and convert the VAPID key with a urlBase64ToUint8Array helper. Keep using the Connect notifications.subscribe RPC to post the subscription.

Files: web/src/app/pages/notifications/notifications.component.ts (subscribe()).

Acceptance criteria:
- [ ] Clicking Subscribe over a secure context (zrok https tunnel or localhost) registers the SW, prompts for permission, creates a push subscription, posts it, shows 'Push notifications enabled', and lists the subscription — never stuck on 'Subscribing…'.
- [ ] If the SW can't become ready, the button returns to 'Subscribe' with a visible error (timeout guard), not an infinite spinner.
- [ ] VAPID key passed as Uint8Array; works in non-Chrome browsers.
- [ ] Send Test still works after subscribing.
- [ ] cd web && npm run build succeeds.

Do not make mistakes. Read pwa-init.js and the existing component fully before editing. Verify the build compiles before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
close_reason: Fixed + deployed: subscribe() now registers /sw.js, requests Notification permission, converts VAPID key to Uint8Array, ready-timeout guard. /sw.js served + push-capable on device. Full flow confirm pending user in secure-context browser.

title: Trips detail map: tiles load partially (black gaps) + fragile leaflet CSS import
description:
The Angular SPA Trips trip-detail route map (web/src/app/pages/trips/trips.component.ts) renders only a partial band of OSM tiles with large black gaps (see user screenshot). Two root causes:

1) Map is created from a constructor effect() via queueMicrotask(() => ensureMap()), which runs BEFORE the @if-rendered detail overlay is laid out. Leaflet computes a too-small tile grid for the not-yet-sized .route-map container, then drawRoute()'s fitBounds() zooms against that wrong size, so only a partial set of tiles is ever requested. The Location map avoids this by initializing in ngAfterViewInit (post-layout). Fix: call map.invalidateSize() once layout settles (requestAnimationFrame) AND attach a ResizeObserver to the host so later overlay/viewport resizes recompute the grid, then re-fit the route bounds.

2) Leaflet CSS is pulled via SCSS '@import "leaflet/dist/leaflet.css"' (trips.component.scss line 2). location.component.scss explicitly documents that Sass cannot resolve that node_modules path under this Vite + @analogjs build, which is why Location uses a TS side-effect import (import 'leaflet/dist/leaflet.css') instead. So trips only renders correctly if Location was opened first. Fix: add the TS side-effect import to trips.component.ts and remove the dead SCSS @import.

Files: web/src/app/pages/trips/trips.component.ts, web/src/app/pages/trips/trips.component.scss.

Acceptance criteria:
- [ ] Opening a trip detail shows a fully-tiled OSM map with no black gaps, route polyline + start/end dots, fitted to the route bounds.
- [ ] Works even when Trips is the first page visited in a fresh session (no dependency on Location loading leaflet.css).
- [ ] No regression to dark-mode invert (.bw-map-dark) or the 'No route data' empty state.
- [ ] cd web && npm run build succeeds; cd web && npx tsc -p tsconfig.app.json --noEmit clean.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
close_reason: Fixed + deployed: invalidateSize+ResizeObserver+refit after layout, leaflet.css via TS side-effect import (dropped dead SCSS @import). New trips chunk with invalidateSize served on device; full visual confirm pending user in-browser.

title: Zrok reserve 401 shareUnauthorized wedges tunnel — no recovery from stale environment.json
description: ZrokLauncher treats existence of /data/local/tmp/.zrok/environment.json as 'already enabled' (checkEnableAndLaunchPublic, ~L726) to avoid burning device registrations. But that file can outlive server-side trust (token rotated, env deleted, or a new enable token entered while the stale file short-circuits enable). Then 'zrok reserve public http://localhost:8080' returns [POST /share][401] shareUnauthorized and executeAutoReserve.onError only retried on timeout/connection — so the tunnel permanently wedged and the Angular webapp (served at 127.0.0.1:8080) was unreachable externally. Observed on device <CAR_IP>:5555 with environment.json dated 2026-05-25. FIX: added isZrokUnauthorized() detection in both reserve onSuccess(output) and onError(error); added recoverRevokedZrokEnvironment() that wipes environment.json+identities+metadata and re-runs zrok enable with the saved token (which chains back into checkReserveAndLaunch), guarded by one-shot zrokReEnableAttempted (reset per launchZrok) so a genuinely bad token fails with a clear 'Reset Zrok Environment + fresh token' message instead of looping. title: Filament spike + VehicleHeroView: render GLB in native Vehicle hero (replaces placeholder ImageView only)
description:
## Context
The native Vehicle tab hero shows a placeholder drawable instead of the 3D car. This task integrates Google Filament and replaces ONLY the placeholder ImageView with a 3D renderer. Old WebView reference implementation: app/src/main/assets/web/shared/vehicle-control.js (initThreeJS lines ~283-374, addLighting lines ~398-424, addGroundGrid lines ~425-433, animate lines ~725-764, _detectPerformanceProfile lines ~260-282, loadModel lines ~434-502, _loadModelFromPath lines ~578-677, _disposeCarModel lines ~503-532).

## Steps
1. Add Gradle deps to app/build.gradle.kts (pin all three to the SAME version, latest stable):
   com.google.android.filament:filament-android, gltfio-android, filament-utils-android.
   Note: app is arm64-v8a only via splits.abi (line ~282); minSdk 25; Filament requires GLES 3.0.
2. Create app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/fragment/vehicle/VehicleHeroView.kt: a class owning a SurfaceView + filament-utils ModelViewer (or hand-rolled Engine/Scene/View if ModelViewer is too rigid).
   - Load GLB bytes for the spike from APK assets: app asset path "web/shared/models/destroyer.glb" (bundled models ship inside the APK; do NOT read /data/local/tmp/web — those files are shell-owned mode 600 and unreadable from app UID).
   - Scene parity with vehicle-control.js addLighting(): key directional light, fill, cool back light (0x6644aa @ 0.3 intensity), plus an IndirectLight built from uniform spherical-harmonics (no KTX asset exists; without an IBL the PBR car renders nearly black).
   - Ground grid parity with addGroundGrid(): subtle grid under the car, opacity ~0.15. If a Filament grid mesh is disproportionate effort, the hero region ALREADY has a native GridView background (TyreOverlay.kt lines 22-37) — transparent clear color over it is acceptable parity.
   - Camera: frame the car like the old hero view; touch orbit via Manipulator.Mode.ORBIT; slow idle auto-rotation like the old animate() loop.
   - Frame pacing: Choreographer-driven render loop; cap to the perf profile like _detectPerformanceProfile (target 30fps is fine on the head unit).
3. In TyreOverlay.kt (app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/fragment/vehicle/TyreOverlay.kt) replace ONLY lines 75-82 (the "Car silhouette" ImageView) with VehicleHeroView, same FrameLayout slot/gravity, sized to fill the hero region behind the tyre cards. Add lifecycle hooks: VehicleController.onResume/onPause/onDestroy (app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/fragment/vehicle/VehicleController.kt — TyreOverlay is built at line ~123) must start/stop the render loop and destroy the Filament engine. Keep R.drawable.vehicle_hero_placeholder as the error/loading fallback image.
4. Robustness parity with loadModel(): monotonic load-generation counter so a stale async load can't overwrite a newer one; 60s hard load timeout; on failure show the placeholder again (full error overlay + retry comes in the model-picker task); dispose previous asset's resources on swap (_disposeCarModel parity — gltfio AssetLoader.destroyAsset).
5. Build ./gradlew assembleDebug, then clean-reinstall on the head unit per BladeWatch/CLAUDE.md "Build Commands" (device is at <CAR_IP>:5555 — NOT the .0.251 address in CLAUDE.md), screencap and verify the destroyer GLB renders.

- Do not modify the web assets or the daemon.

title: Native 3D vehicle hero: Filament GLB rendering + model/color selection (WebView parity)
description:
## Problem
The native Android Vehicle tab (VehicleFragment) replaced the old WebView vehicle page, but its hero region shows a static 2D drawable (R.drawable.vehicle_hero_placeholder in app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/fragment/vehicle/TyreOverlay.kt lines 75-82) instead of the 3D GLB car. Model selection and paint color selection do not exist in the native UI at all. The old WebView implementation (app/src/main/assets/web/shared/vehicle-control.js + ev-card-3d.js) rendered the user-selected GLB via three.js + GLTFLoader + DRACOLoader with runtime paint tinting.

## Goal
1:1 parity with the old WebView vehicle page for EXACTLY three things: (1) the 3D car rendering in the hero region, (2) model selection, (3) paint color selection. NOTHING else in the native Vehicle UI may change (tyre cards, grid background, panels, buttons all stay as-is).

## Technology decision
Use Google Filament: com.google.android.filament:filament-android + gltfio-android + filament-utils-android.
- gltfio = GLTFLoader equivalent (loads .glb directly via AssetLoader/ResourceLoader)
- gltfio has built-in Draco decoding = DRACOLoader equivalent. REQUIRED: all 11 bundled GLBs in app/src/main/assets/web/shared/models/ use KHR_draco_mesh_compression (verified), plus KHR_materials_clearcoat/specular/transmission.
- filament-utils ModelViewer/Manipulator = OrbitControls equivalent.
- App constraints: minSdk 25, arm64-v8a only, Filament needs GLES 3.0 (BYD DiLink v3 head unit must be verified in the spike task).

## Child tasks
Spike/renderer -> ModelStore client -> color picker -> model picker -> hardening/docs, plus a Draco re-encode contingency task.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Vehicle tab hero shows the selected 3D GLB car, tinted with the persisted color, on the BYD head unit (<CAR_IP>:5555)
- [ ] Model + color choices persist via the daemon (GET/POST /api/models/selected) and survive app restart and are shared with phone web UI
- [ ] No regressions in any other native Vehicle UI element

title: VEH E3b: UX minimums — pressed feedback, in-place poll updates, pending states, honest unknowns, preset snap, 44dp, poller hardening, success flash
description:
## Problem / Context
The native screen has zero pressed feedback (bare TextViews), rebuilds the entire view tree every 3s poll (applyStateToViews → rebuildTabBar+renderTabContent, ~L257-259), renders fake defaults (22°C/fan 3) before first data, highlights window presets only on exact percent match, has sub-44dp touch targets, and its poll loop can die silently (uncaught exception in a scheduleAtFixedRate lambda cancels the task forever; fetchState has no try/catch) plus a pause/resume race can leak a second poller. Successful commands show nothing until the next poll.

## Files (package note: declared package is net.bladewatch.app...; panels/factory exist after the decomposition task)
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/fragment/vehicle/VehicleController.kt + VehicleViewFactory.kt + panel files

## Steps (read every file fully first; depends on tasks VEH E3a and VEH E2 closed)
1. Pressed feedback: every clickable gets a StateListDrawable (pressed state darkens/lightens the GradientDrawable ~12%) or a RippleDrawable wrapping it. Factory-level change so all controls inherit.
2. In-place updates: applyStateToViews() must NOT rebuild the tree. Panels expose update(state) that mutates retained view refs (text, active-state backgrounds, visibility). Full rebuild only on tab switch and configuration change. Device-free proxy check: a counter/log assertion test or a debug counter proving renderTabContent is NOT called from the poll path.
3. Per-control pending: while an action key is in flight, that control alpha 0.5 + not clickable; restored on completion (uses the per-key inFlight map from E3a).
4. Honest unknowns: before first successful poll, climate shows "—" for temp/fan (no 22°C/3), window rows show "–%", lock pill grey + "—". Implement as pure formatter functions (e.g. formatTemp(Int?): String) in a new VehicleFormatters.kt with JUnit tests.
5. Preset snap: highlight nearest preset within ±10% (47%→none, 24%→25%). Pure function presetFor(current: Int): Int? in VehicleFormatters.kt + tests for boundaries (-1, 0, 10, 14, 15, 24, 35, 47, 90, 100).
6. Touch targets: every control ≥44dp in both dimensions (minWidth/minHeight on factory builders). 44dp ALWAYS wins over pixel parity (binding plan decision).
7. Poller hardening: wrap the scheduled lambda body in try/catch (log + count as failure, task survives); create the executor synchronously in onResume (or generation token) so rapid pause/resume cannot leak a second poller. Action-thread root.post gains an isAlive/running guard.
8. Success flash: on VehicleCommandResult.ok, the actioned control flashes its accent color ~300ms (ValueAnimator on the background) — the M1 stand-in for the WebView VFX.
9. ./gradlew test green (formatters, presetFor, poller-survival unit where feasible); assembleDebug compiles.

## Constraints
- No color-palette changes (theming is a later task) — pressed states derive from existing colors.
- Polling cadence stays 3s; debounce stays 600ms.
- Never run git add/commit.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] All controls have visible pressed feedback and ≥44dp targets
- [ ] Poll tick mutates views in place — proxy check proves no tree rebuild from poll path
- [ ] Unknown values render as "—"/"–%" until first data
- [ ] presetFor ±10% snapping with boundary unit tests
- [ ] Poller survives a thrown exception (test or log-verified) and pause/resume spam leaves exactly one poller
- [ ] Success flash on ok=true
- [ ] ./gradlew test green

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
close_reason: Pressed feedback (RippleDrawable on all buttons), 44dp minimums, in-place poll updates (applyStateToViews calls updateTabContent not renderTabContent), PanelResult updaters per tab, honest unknowns (formatTemp/formatFan dash until loaded), presetFor ±10 snap with 14 unit tests, poller hardening (generation token + try/catch), success flash via animate(). 19 new formatter+command-result tests pass, assembleDebug clean.

title: VEH E2: command result fidelity — surface server outcome/message, route window commands through doVehicleAction
description:
## Problem / Context
VehicleClient.vehicleCommand() collapses every command response to a Boolean and swallows exceptions (catch (_: Exception) { false }), so the user sees generic failure text while the server already returns a localized message + outcome (success/failed/not_supported). title: VEH G2: fetchChargeCap ignores optional-field presence — CHARGING panel wrongly shows 'not supported'
description:
## Problem / Context
proto GetChargeCapResponse declares percent/enabled/supported as `optional` precisely so the client can distinguish "not yet probed" (absent) from real false/0. But VehicleClient.fetchChargeCap() reads m.enabled / m.percent / m.supported directly without the has*() accessors, so an unprobed charge cap collapses to supported=false and VehicleController (~line 590) renders "Charge cap is not supported by this vehicle." for vehicles where it IS supported but not yet probed. Same bug class as the lights/ADAS wire defects.

## Steps

2. In fetchChargeCap(): use m.hasSupported() ? m.supported : null, m.hasEnabled() ? m.enabled : null, m.hasPercent() ? m.percent.coerceIn(50,100) : null. Adjust ChargingCapInfo field types to nullable where needed.

title: VEH E1a: lights/ADAS handlers reject ConnectRPC requests — add proto field parsing as pure testable functions
description:
## Problem / Context
The native app sends ConnectRPC JSON {"action":"dayTimeLight","on":true} to POST /api/vehicle/lights (and {"action":"speedLimitWarning","on":true} to /api/vehicle/adas), but the handlers only read the legacy field names "target"/"enable" and reject everything else — so the native DRL and Speed Limit Warning toggles ALWAYS fail. Additionally optBoolean("enable", true) defaults to TRUE when the boolean is absent, which would turn a feature ON when asked to turn it OFF.

## Files (NOTE: directory paths do NOT match package names — code under app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ declares `package net.bladewatch.app...`. Never guess packages; copy from the file you edit.)
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/VehicleControlApiHandler.java — handleLights (~line 690), handleAdas (~line 721)
- app/src/test/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/connect/ (new test class here or sibling dir)

## Steps
1. Read handleLights and handleAdas fully. Read the existing proto-fallback pattern in the SAME file: handleWindow (~L501: `req.has("windowIndex") ? ... : req.optInt("area",...)`) and handleSetClimate (~L576-618). Copy that pattern's style.
2. Extract the parsing into pure static package-visible functions, e.g. `static LightsRequestParse parseLightsRequest(JSONObject req)` returning either {target, enable} or an error string. Rules:
   - Accept proto names first: "action" (string), "on" (boolean) — then fall back to legacy "target"/"enable".
   - If NEITHER boolean key is present ("on" nor "enable"): return an error ("lights requires 'on'") — never default to true. Mirror handleChargeCap's has() style (~L847-852).
   - Validation unchanged: target/action must equal "dayTimeLight" (lights) / "speedLimitWarning" (adas); otherwise the existing localized unsupported-target error.
3. handleLights/handleAdas call the parse function; on error emit {"success":false,"error":...} exactly like existing error paths.

5. New JUnit test class covering, for BOTH lights and adas: proto shape on=true; proto shape on=false (must parse enable=false — this is the 2am-Friday case); legacy shape {"target":...,"enable":true} (regression guard — must still route identically); missing boolean → error; wrong target → error.
6. Run: ./gradlew test — all green.

## Constraints
- Do NOT change VehicleCommandRouter, AuthMiddleware, or any other endpoint's behavior.
- Do NOT touch proto files in this task (that is VEH E1b).
- Legacy REST callers keep working: the only legacy behavior change is absent-boolean now errors instead of defaulting true (decided in plan review EF10; the legacy web UI always sends enable explicitly — verify by grepping app/src/main/assets/web/shared/vehicle-control.js for "enable").

title: Fix IPC token mismatch (Unauthorized) after app install/daemon restart
description:
ROOT CAUSE: IpcTokenManager.generate() (called unconditionally at CameraDaemon.java:377 on every daemon startup) mints a NEW random token each boot and overwrites /data/local/tmp/bladewatch_ipc_token. Both daemon and app cache the token in a process-local static 'cachedToken' that is never re-read. On install/reinstall a stale detached daemon survives (not bound to package manager) and/or the app process keeps the old cached token, while the freshly-booted daemon writes a new token -> server isValid() rejects with 'Unauthorized' -> app->daemon secret fetch (auth.deviceSecret) fails -> AuthManager cannot mint JWT -> Dashboard trip card stuck on 'Loading...' and 'Camera unavailable'.

FIX 1 (idempotent generate): IpcTokenManager.generate() reuses an existing well-formed on-disk token instead of rotating it; only mints when the file is missing/empty/malformed. Token lives in /data/local/tmp (survives uninstall) so all processes converge across restarts. Single source of truth for token creation+read stays in IpcTokenManager.

FIX 2 (client recovery): add IpcTokenManager.reload() (drop cache + re-read disk). SecretConfigBridge read/write IPC loops detect an 'Unauthorized' response and call reload() before the next retry so a long-lived app self-heals without a process restart.

ACCEPTANCE:
- [ ] generate() does NOT rotate token when a valid token file already exists
- [ ] generate() still mints+persists (644) when file missing/malformed
- [ ] reload() clears cache and re-reads disk
- [ ] SecretConfigBridge reloads token + retries on Unauthorized (read AND write loops)
- [ ] IpcTokenManager remains the only reader/writer of the token file
- [ ] ./gradlew assembleDebug compiles
- [ ] On device: trip card shows trip count, not 'Loading...'

Do not make mistakes. Read referenced files fully before editing. Verify build compiles before closing.

1. Token idempotent — daemon generate() ran at 17:33, 17:49 (new build), 17:51; token stayed 7NpTb1oLLQRpL1YKcmZ91MUjgM8AVvlf across all 3 daemon starts (old build rotated it every boot). Persisted across uninstall (/data/local/tmp).
2. Zero Unauthorized/deviceSecret IPC failures since reinstall (logcat count=0) — previously continuous 'IPC read failed after 3 attempts for auth.deviceSecret: Unauthorized' spam.
3. Trips RPC healthy: /api/trips returns 2 trips incl fresh testdrive trip id=65; auth-gated live view + 117 recordings render (same JWT path as trip card).
Live dashboard screenshot not captured — head unit panel powered down after testdrive (ACC off). Trip-card mechanism (listTrips RPC + JWT mint via deviceSecret IPC) is proven working end-to-end; visual confirm pending next drive.
