title: Sunroof: 25% and 75% chips do nothing sensible (hardware only has close / half / open)
description:
## Problem (owner report, 2026-09-25)

In-car UI, Vehicle -> Windows -> Sunroof: the 25% and 75% chips "do not work"; only 0%, 50% and 100% behave properly.

## Cause
The hardware cannot do 25% or 75%. app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/byd/BydDataCollector.kt moveWindowToPercent() (~line 4087): for area >= 5 (5 = sunroof, 6 = sunshade) there is no usable position feedback (getSunroofPosition() reads 0 throughout travel), so it skips the closed-loop controller and sends BYD one-touch commands instead: targetPercent >= 75 -> full open (1), <= 25 -> full close (2), otherwise half (4). So 25% silently fully CLOSES and 75% fully OPENS. Supported sun-window commands (setWindowCommand / setSunWindowCommand ~line 3960-3990): 1 open, 2 close, 3 stop, 4 half, and 5 "breath" (tilt/vent, sunroof only).
The UI offers the side-window presets for it: flutter_ui/lib/screens/vehicle/vehicle_screen.dart ~line 942-947 builds the sunroof (and sunshade) cell with the generic _windowCell(..., 5, w.sunroof), i.e. the 0/25/50/75/100 chips from vehicle_models.dart _kWindowPresets.

## Fix
- Sunroof and sunshade cells offer ONLY what the hardware does: Close (0), Half (50), Open (100). Do not show 25/75 for areas 5/6. Side windows keep 0/25/50/75/100.
- Optional, ask the owner first: a "Tilt" chip for the sunroof using command 5 (breath). Do not add it without the owner's yes.
- Highlight: position feedback for the sunroof is unreliable (reads 0 in travel); if the displayed percentage/highlight is wrong after a move, derive the state from getSunroofState (discrete) where possible, and note what was measured.
- Server: keep moveWindowToPercent's mapping, but document on the handler that areas 5/6 accept only 0/50/100 semantics.
- Check the web page and companion do not offer sunroof 25/75 (as of 2026-09-25 neither shows a sunroof control).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Sunroof/sunshade rows show only Close/Half/Open; side windows unchanged (widget test).
- [ ] cd flutter_ui && flutter analyze && flutter test; coverage gate holds.
- [ ] On the head unit: each sunroof chip moves the roof to that state, and the highlight follows.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
notes:
Fixed 2026-09-25 (uncommitted): kSunPanelPresets [0, 50, 100] + presetsForArea(area) -- areas 5/6 (sunroof, sunshade) offer and light only close / half / open; side windows keep 0/25/50/75/100. Server mapping unchanged (moveWindowToPercent: <=25 close, >=75 open, else half). Tests: presetsForArea + sun-panel presetFor unit tests; widget test 'the sunroof offers only close / half / open'. On the head unit (GetState caps sunroof=true, sunroof 0%): the Windows tab shows the Sunroof row with 0% / 50% / 100% only, 0% lit. PENDING (moves the roof, owner at the car): tap 50% and 100% and 0%, confirm the roof moves and the highlight follows. Tilt (command 5 'breath') NOT added -- owner decision.
Measured 2026-09-25: getSunroofPosition reads 0 always (also documented at BydDataCollector.moveWindowToPercent). getSunroofState: 3 while opening, 4 while closing, 1 at rest whether closed or half open. The one-touch half command did open the sunroof 50 percent (owner confirmed) but the UI kept showing 0 percent because the position never changes. Fix: show the last commanded sunroof target instead of the unreadable position.
Implemented 2026-09-25, NOT yet installed on the head unit (installing resets BYD Auto-Start, which the owner had just re-allowed with the car off). All gates green: ./gradlew test koverVerify, flutter_ui 1469 tests / 99.59 percent, companion 98.57, bladewatch_rpc 100, web typecheck + templates + unit. Remaining: install both APKs with the owner in the car, check on screen, then close. Change: GetState windows.sunroof = stop of the last successful sunroof command unless the car ever reported a non-zero position. Check: tap 50 then 100 then 0; the chip follows each tap.
close_reason: Verified on the head unit 2026-09-26: owner confirmed the sunroof chips follow 50, 100 and 0. GetState reports the stop of the last successful sunroof command, since this car never reports a resting position (getSunroofState 1 at rest, 3 opening, 4 closing); a car that ever reports a non-zero position is believed instead.

title: Vehicle Windows: after Vent 12% the Rear Right row highlights no position (the others show 25%)
description:
## Problem (owner report with screenshot, 2026-09-25)

In-car UI, Vehicle -> Windows. After pressing "Vent 12%", the rows read Front Left (16%), Front Right (15%), Rear Left (15%), Rear Right (14%). The first three highlight the 25% chip; Rear Right highlights NOTHING. The same action on four windows shows two different states.

## Cause
flutter_ui/lib/screens/vehicle/vehicle_models.dart presetFor() (~line 217): highlights the nearest of _kWindowPresets [0, 25, 50, 75, 100] only when within +/-10 (returns null otherwise). 16/15 are within 10 of 25; 14 is 11 away -> null. The vent action (vehicle_screen.dart ~line 924, c.ventAllWindows(12)) lands windows at 14-16%, right on that boundary, so vented windows flip between highlighted and not. The +/-10 gap is deliberate and pinned by flutter_ui/test/screens/vehicle/vehicle_models_test.dart group 'presetFor' ("returns null when farther than 10 from every preset": 12, 38, 62 -> null) -- that expectation changes with this fix.

## Fix (rule)
A window's row always shows a state, consistently:
- unknown (-1 / negative) -> no highlight (unchanged);
- closed (0-2%) -> the 0% chip;
- any open window (> 2%) -> the NEAREST opening preset of [25, 50, 75, 100] (ties go to the higher preset), so an open window never shows "0%" and a vented window always shows 25%.
Keep the row label's exact percentage ("Rear Right (14%)") -- it already tells the owner the real position. Update presetFor's doc comment and the tests: vent-band values (12, 14, 15, 16) -> 25; 38 -> 50; 62 -> 50 (tie 62.5 not reachable with ints; 63 -> 75); 1-2 -> 0; 3 -> 25.

Scope: in-car UI only (the companion has Close/Vent/Open buttons, no per-window presets; the web page has no presetFor).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Unit tests for the new rule (including 14, 15, 16 -> 25 and 0-2 -> 0), and a widget test that four windows at 16/15/15/14 all highlight 25%.
- [ ] cd flutter_ui && flutter analyze && flutter test; coverage gate holds.
- [ ] On the head unit: Vent 12% -> all four rows highlight the same chip.

Tests: vehicle_models_test (vented 3/12/14/15/16/25 -> 25; 37->25, 38->50, 62->50, 63->75, 88->100), widget test 'four vented windows all light the same preset' with the car's exact 16/15/15/14. flutter_ui analyze clean, 1461 tests, coverage >= 99%. title: Vehicle view inside temperature reads 33 C when the cabin is below 30 C
description:
## Problem (owner report, 2026-09-25)

The Vehicle view's inside (cabin) temperature reads 33 C while the owner says the actual cabin temperature is below 30 C.

Measured on the head unit 2026-09-25 12:37 (BYD Seal 5 DM-i, ACC on, climate OFF: acOn=false, setpoint 24):
- VehicleService/GetState -> climate.insideTempC = 33.
- VehicleService/GetAcDiagnostics -> acDevice.getTemprature(position): pos0 = -2147482645 (the SDK's unavailable sentinel, Int.MIN_VALUE + 1003), pos1 = 24, pos2 = 24, pos3 = 24, pos4 = 33, pos5/pos6 = sentinel.
- The value comes from app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/byd/BydDataCollector.kt ~line 1600: BydDeviceHelper.callGetter(acDevice, "getTemprature", AC_TEMP_POS_CABIN) with AC_TEMP_POS_CABIN = 4 (constant ~line 5392; its doc says pos4 is NOT outside temperature, which comes from instrumentDevice.getOutCarTemperature() in collectInstrument ~line 1453). Served by VehicleControlApiHandler ~line 211 (ClimateTemps / cachedInsideC) as climate.insideTempC; shown by the in-car UI, companion and web Vehicle pages.

## What to find out (device work, car in the sun vs. shade, climate off and on)
1. Is pos4 really the cabin air sensor? Compare it over time against: instrumentDevice.getOutCarTemperature() (outside), a thermometer in the cabin (owner), and BYD's own climate UI if it shows a cabin value. Log all positions every minute for ~20 min, including after the AC runs.
2. Look for another cabin getter on this firmware (e.g. named getters on BYDAutoAcDevice / BYDAutoInstrumentDevice / body device that return an inside/in-car temperature); record what each returns.
3. Decide: use the correct source; or, if pos4 is a sun-loaded/duct sensor with no better source, label it honestly (or hide it) rather than presenting it as cabin air. Do NOT add an arbitrary offset without measurements that justify it.

## Acceptance criteria

title: In-car Dashboard never refreshes while open: Remote access stays Online after the car loses its network
description:
## Problem

The in-car Dashboard loads its tiles once, in DashboardScreen.initState (flutter_ui/lib/screens/dashboard/dashboard_screen.dart, widget.controller.refresh()), and never again while it stays on screen. Measured on the head unit 2026-09-25: with the dashboard open and then ALL networking cut, pearStatus went reachable=false but the "Remote access" tile kept saying "Online" with its reachable dot; it only changed when the page was re-entered. The same staleness applies to "Today's recordings", the services count and the recording/idle chips. The Services screen had exactly this bug and got a 5 s poll (BladeWatch-dh1r); the dashboard never did, and since rdtj.17 put Pear reachability on it, a stale "Online" is now actively misleading.

## Fix

Add a Timer.periodic in _DashboardScreenState (cancel in dispose) that calls widget.controller.refresh() every 15 s. DashboardController.refresh() already replaces state without resetting loading flags and notifies once, so tiles do not flicker. Do not add loading spinners on the periodic refresh.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Widget test: after the first load, a changed pearStatus stub shows on the tile after 15 s of pumped time, without re-entering the page; the timer is cancelled on dispose (no pending timers).
- [ ] cd flutter_ui && flutter analyze && flutter test pass; coverage gate holds.
- [ ] On the head unit: dashboard left open, networking cut, tile turns Offline without navigation.

title: In-car Services: an unreachable Pear peer is shown in success green
description:
## Problem

In the in-car UI, Settings -> Services, the "Remote access (Pear)" row renders its whole subtitle in the success colour. title: byd_cam_daemon restarts itself during camera warmup ~3 in 11 starts (GL thread blocked 10 s watchdog)
description:
## Problem

byd_cam_daemon sometimes kills itself during camera warmup at startup:
"PanoramicCameraGpu: CRITICAL: GL thread blocked for 10004ms - forcing process restart (during camera warmup)".
The wrapper restarts it 10 s later, and the second start succeeds.

Seen on the head unit 2026-09-24, in 3 of the last 11 daemon sessions in /data/local/tmp/cam_daemon.log (11:50, 19:06, 19:23). Each followed a fresh launch; two were right after an APK install. Cost per occurrence:
- About 25-35 s more before the car records or answers.
- 127.0.0.1:8080 and the Pear pump refuse connections in that window, so the companion shows "reconnecting" and a throughput run fails with ECONNREFUSED.
- If it happened at ACC ON, the start of a drive could go unrecorded.

Found while verifying BladeWatch-1996 (an rpc run hit ECONNREFUSED; the daemon's PID had changed). NOT caused by that change: it touches NetworkMonitor only, off the GL thread, and the same event appears earlier in the log.

## Where
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/camera/PanoramicCameraGpu.kt: the GL-thread watchdog (around line 1805-1845). It uses GL_THREAD_WARMUP_TIMEOUT_MS until firstFrameReceived, then exits with code 0, which the DaemonLauncher wrapper restarts.
- The comment there already notes the BYD panoramic HAL can take 5-8 s to deliver the first frame, and that I/O contention (MediaScanner) can stall the heartbeat.

## What to find out (device work)
1. What the GL thread is blocked on when the watchdog fires. Log the GL thread's stack from the watchdog thread, via Thread.getAllStackTraces or the GL thread reference, before exiting. The stack says which HAL or EGL call hangs.
2. Whether it correlates with PermissionGranter, which runs for about 18 s at every daemon start ("Done in 18633ms") and overlaps camera warmup, or with MediaScanner.
3. Then decide: raise the warmup timeout, move the blocking call, or sequence warmup after the permission grant. Do NOT simply raise the timeout without knowing the blocking call: a real hang must still recover.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The blocking call is identified from a captured stack (quoted in the notes).
- [ ] The fix makes 10 consecutive fresh daemon starts on the head unit finish warmup without a watchdog restart. Grep cam_daemon.log for "GL thread blocked".
- [ ] A genuinely hung GL thread still triggers the restart (a unit or fault-injection check).
- [ ] ./gradlew test and koverVerify pass.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
close_reason:
Root cause, captured on the head unit 2026-09-24 (ACC off): NOT a blocked GL call. Instrumented build logged, in the failing session: 22:15:54.313 PanoramicCameraGpu.stop() with running=false, called from main via RecordingModeManager.onAccStateChanged <- CameraDaemon.onAccStateChanged <- CameraDaemon.main (the ACC-off hardware-probe recovery, which stops the pipeline it just started); 22:15:54.722 the FIRST start's GL init post then completed (quitSafely still runs already-posted messages), set running=true and started a watchdog; 22:16:04.750 "CRITICAL: GL thread blocked for 10016ms ... glThread=null renderLoopAlive=true" -- the orphaned watchdog of the stopped start, with no GL thread to beat for it, killed the healthy daemon the second start() had built. No stack could exist because the watched thread had already quit. Before the fix this hit 7 starts on 2026-09-24 (20:37 21:45 21:53 21:56 22:04 22:09 22:16), including every post-install start. debuggerd -j needs root on this unit, hence the in-process instrumentation (removed again).

Fix (PanoramicCameraGpu): an AtomicInteger generation bumped by start() and stop(); the GL init post returns before opening EGL/camera if stopped, and after startCamera closes the camera it opened and returns without setting running or starting the render loop/watchdog; the watchdog takes its start's generation and exits (SUPERSEDED) once it is stale, via the pure watchdogVerdict(gen, currentGen, sinceHeartbeat, timeout). A genuinely hung GL thread of the current start still returns HUNG and exits: GlWatchdogVerdictTest (3). The CRITICAL line now also logs the GL thread stack.

Verified on the head unit, ACC off: 10 consecutive fresh camera-daemon starts (22:21-22:33: 3 after install -r, 7 after killing wrapper+daemon and letting the service host relaunch) with zero "GL thread blocked" and exactly one "Starting CameraDaemon" per run; all three daemons up; after StreamService/Enable a live still returned 200 image/jpeg (36388 bytes, ffd8ff) in 2 s, so the surviving pipeline owns a working camera. testDebugUnitTest + testReleaseUnitTest 942/942, koverVerify, assembleDebug pass. Docs: daemons-and-processes.md Camera Daemon "GL watchdog".

title: Debug builds give every co-resident app the full HTTP API without credentials, vehicle control included (Tier 2 loopback bypass)
description:
## Problem

On DEBUG builds -- the build that goes on the car, because preserving the ADB key across a reinstall needs run-as -- ANY app installed on the head unit gets the full HTTP API with no credential, vehicle control included. `AuthMiddleware.checkAuth` Tier 2 (app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/AuthMiddleware.kt, the `trust == ListenerTrust.LOCAL_APPS && isLoopbackBypassAllowed() ...` block) trusts any 127.0.0.1 caller on the 8080 listener, and `AuthMiddleware.isLocalAppCaller` exempts the same callers from the vehicle-action second factor. Android loopback is shared by every app. Measured on the head unit 2026-09-24 (BladeWatch-rdtj.16) with an invalid JWT on 127.0.0.1:8080: SystemService/GetStatus 200, VehicleService/SetChargeCap 200 (reached the handler; a real body would actuate), RecordingsService/ListRecordings 200, /video/ range download served, /ws live view streamed 39 frames. The IPC ports are protected against exactly this by UID (`PeerCredentials.isTrustedPeer`, pinned by CoResidentAttackerTest); the HTTP bypass is not.

## Fix direction

Require the peer to be a trusted UID for Tier 2 and for the vehicle second-factor exemption: resolve the connecting socket's UID with the same `PeerCredentials` lookup the IPC server uses (app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/PeerCredentials.kt) and allow only the BladeWatch app UID, shell and system. That needs the Socket (or its peer UID) passed into checkAuth / HttpServer's second-factor check instead of only the SocketAddress. Do NOT widen PeerCredentials, and do not change CoResidentAttackerTest.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A test: a LOCAL_APPS loopback caller whose UID is not trusted gets 401 with the bypass on, and is not exempt from the vehicle second factor.
- [ ] A test: the BladeWatch app UID still gets the bypass on debug.
- [ ] On the head unit (debug build): the in-car UI works; a request from another UID (e.g. `adb shell run-as` of another debuggable app, or a test APK) gets 401 on 8080.
- [ ] ./gradlew test and ./gradlew koverVerify pass; CoResidentAttackerTest unmodified.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
notes: Fixed offline 2026-09-24: HttpServer.handleClient now derives the connection's trust first thing via AuthMiddleware.effectiveTrust(listener) { PeerCredentials.isTrustedPeer(client) } -- LOCAL_APPS only for a trusted peer UID (BladeWatch app UID, shell, system, root), otherwise REMOTE (JWT required, no Tier 2, vehicle action token required); the lookup runs only on the 8080 listener. AuthMiddleware and PeerCredentials otherwise unchanged; CoResidentAttackerTest unmodified (9/9). LocalAppPeerTrustTest (4): untrusted local app -> 401 + no vehicle exemption with bypass forced on; BladeWatch keeps it; REMOTE never looks up; source guard that handleClient applies it before anything reads the trust. Mutation (ignore the peer) fails. docs/networking-and-tunnels.md Listener trust updated. REMAINING (next install): on the head unit the in-car UI still works (incl. a vehicle control through the UI's own path) and a shell-UID caller on 8080 is still local-trusted; an untrusted-UID negative check needs another debuggable app, otherwise rely on the unit test.
close_reason: Verified on the head unit 2026-09-24 with the debug build (fix from the notes, plus u43d). Foreign UID: installed a code-less debuggable probe package (net.bladewatch.probe, UID 10067, inet group) only to get a non-BladeWatch UID via run-as, then uninstalled it (pm list shows only the two BladeWatch packages). From UID 10067 on 127.0.0.1:8080: SystemService/GetStatus 401 with no JWT and with a bogus JWT, RecordingsService/ListRecordings 401, /ws upgrade 401, /video range 401 -- every surface measured open in rdtj.16 is now closed. Trusted callers unchanged: shell (adb shell curl) GetStatus without JWT 200, /video 404 (past auth); UID 10073 via run-as net.bladewatch.flutter GetStatus without JWT 200. Vehicle second-factor exemption for the app UID: VehicleService/SetChargeCap from UID 10073 with an undecodable body passed the gate (no 403) and stopped at decode ("cannot be converted to JSONObject"), so nothing actuated. In-car UI running (pid present) with an ESTABLISHED connection to 8080 owned by UID 10073, no 401/Unauthorized/exception in logcat after bringing it forward (panel asleep, so no screenshot). Unit side as in notes: LocalAppPeerTrustTest 4/4, CoResidentAttackerTest unmodified 9/9, testDebugUnitTest + testReleaseUnitTest 939/939, koverVerify passes.

title: GetStatus stalls ~700 ms whenever a periodic cache refresh lands on the request (worse during live view)
description:
## Problem

`SystemService/GetStatus` intermittently takes ~700 ms instead of ~2-6 ms. The in-car dashboard polls it, so the status tiles occasionally freeze for most of a second, more often while live view is open.

Measured on the head unit, 2026-09-24, loopback (127.0.0.1:8080), MEDIUM quality, with `tools/throughput/Throughput.java` (see docs/throughput-harness.md):

| Condition | Calls | p50 | p95 | p99 | max |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| back to back, 0.3 s total | 200 | 1.4 ms | 1.8 ms | 2.1 ms | 2.4 ms |
| paced 0.5 s apart for 60 s, no video | 120 | 5.7 ms | 50.6 ms | 702.8 ms | 713.0 ms |
| paced 0.5 s apart during live view | 111 | 5.6 ms | 654.8 ms | 747.3 ms | 777.2 ms |
| control: `StreamService/GetQuality` during live view | 120 | 4.8 ms | 9.9 ms | 14.1 ms | 18.2 ms |

So the server itself is responsive; the stall belongs to GetStatus's own work, and it recurs on a period (the back-to-back burst is too short to hit one).

## Suspects (start here)

`HttpServer.statusJson()` (app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/HttpServer.kt, around line 834), which SystemService.GetStatus returns. It calls, inline on the request thread:
- `BatteryMonitor.getBatteryInfo()` -- refreshes via `fetchBatteryInfo()` when the cached value is older than 30 s.
- `VehicleDataMonitor.getInstance().getChargingState()` / `getBatterySoc()` -- BYD SDK reads over reflection.
- `SafeLocationManager.getInstance()`.
- `TcpCommandServer.getRecordingCameras()` etc. -- read GPU pipeline flags (`isRecordingMode`, `isRecording`, `isRunning`); check whether any is synchronized on something the streaming/encoder threads hold, which would explain the higher rate during live view.

## Steps

1. Time each call in statusJson (temporarily, local build only -- do not commit enabled logging) to find the ~700 ms one.
2. Move that refresh off the request path: refresh on a background schedule and serve the cached value, so a request never waits for it.
3. Re-measure with the harness: `rpc --count 120 --every 0.5` with and without `video` running.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The slow call is identified and named in the close reason.
- [ ] Paced GetStatus p99 under 50 ms on loopback, with and without live view (harness numbers in the close reason).
- [ ] No behaviour change in the values GetStatus reports (existing tests pass; staleness bounded by the same refresh interval as today).

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
notes: Slow call identified: BatteryMonitor.getBatteryInfo -> fetchBatteryInfo, a synchronous IPC round trip to the surveillance daemon (GET_VEHICLE_DATA on 127.0.0.1:19877, 3 s timeout) made inline whenever the cache was >30 s old; worse, a FAILED fetch never advanced lastBatteryUpdate, so every GetStatus then retried inline. The other statusJson calls (VehicleDataMonitor via BydDataCollector's in-process cache, SafeLocationManager, the pipeline flags) are in-memory. Fix: refresh on a single-flight background thread at most once per 30 s whether or not it succeeds; only the very first call fetches inline, so reported values are unchanged. BatteryMonitorTest (3): first call inline then none within 30 s; a stale refresh never blocks the caller (and no second refresh while one runs); a failing refresh is not retried per call. Mutation (refresh inline again) fails the test. REMAINING: on-car harness numbers (rpc --count 120 --every 0.5, with and without video) -- batched with the next install.
close_reason: Fixed and verified on the head unit 2026-09-24. Two refreshes ran on the GetStatus request. The first was the battery IPC (BatteryMonitor, fixed earlier). The second, found on the device after that fix, was NetworkMonitor.getNetworkInfo refreshing inline every 10 s (the shell fallback runs dumpsys wifi): a 600-850 ms stall every ~11 s, per-call timing via adb forward. Both now refresh single-flight in the background; only the first call ever fetches inline. NetworkMonitorRefreshTest has 3 tests, and the inline-refresh mutation is killed. Throughput harness on the car, loopback, 120 calls paced 0.5 s: before, p50 6.7 / p95 86.7 / p99 663 / max 665 ms; after, p50 6.2 / p95 19.5 / p99 64 / max 68 ms. 200-call burst: 583 calls/s, p50 1.4 ms. docs/throughput-harness.md updated. While verifying, found an unrelated startup watchdog restart and filed it as BladeWatch-honj.

title: Pear from mobile data failed on one hotspot network (consistent NAT both sides) and passed on another -- cause unknown
description:
## Problem

Pear from mobile data to the car on home Wi-Fi failed 2/2 in one session and passed in the next, 2026-09-24, with the same builds (car: debug build with the BladeWatch-ekbp pear-end fix; companion: `companion/integration_test/car_e2e_test.dart` on macOS, flutter_pear 0.4.2).

- FAILED (12:50 and 12:52): Mac on a phone hotspot at 192.168.4.x. The DHT lookup found the car's announcement (45 swarm "connecting" updates per run) but no connection ever formed: `swarm failed CONNECT_TIMEOUT`, `findCarOverPear` gave up. HyperDHT measured this network as firewalled=true, randomized=false.
- PASSED (13:14 and 13:18): Mac on a hotspot at 10.101.x, HyperDHT firewalled=true, randomized=true. A plain HyperDHT dial to the car opened in 3.7 s; the companion's Pear route came up in 14.8 s with pinned TLS and a 401 through it.
- Home network (car side): firewalled=true, randomized=false.

Two consistent NATs are the easiest case to hole-punch, yet that is the pairing that failed. What differed between the two hotspot sessions is unknown (the owner was asked). Candidates: a different phone or tethering mode, a carrier that filters UDP on that path, or stale announcements from earlier companion runs crowding out the car (each run leaves an ephemeral announcement for ~20 min; four were seen at once).

## How to diagnose (no app changes needed)

A Node script using pear-end's own hyperdht (`packages/flutter_pear/pear-end/node_modules/hyperdht` in the flutter_pear repo): `new DHT()`, `await dht.fullyBootstrapped()`, print `dht.firewalled` / `dht.randomized`; `for await (const r of dht.lookup(topic))` to collect announcer public keys; then `dht.connect(key)` for each and log `open` or the error's `code` (e.g. HOLEPUNCH_ABORTED, HOLEPUNCH_DOUBLE_RANDOMIZED_NATS, PEER_CONNECTION_FAILED). Take the topic from a pairing QR payload (`pearTopic`). Print codes and counts only -- never the topic, keys or addresses. Run it from the failing network and from home.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The failing network is identified (phone, tethering mode, carrier) and reproduced.
- [ ] The dial probe's error code from that network is recorded.
- [ ] Either a fix, or a documented limitation in docs/networking-and-tunnels.md with what the companion shows the user in that case.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
notes:
READY 2026-09-26: a NAT probe (scratch natprobe.cjs, flutter_pear 0.4.4's own hyperdht, no app code) prints this network's firewalled/randomized classification, then looks up the car's topic and dials each announcer, recording open time or error code. Smoke on the home network: firewalled=true randomized=false; 5 announcers, 1 opened in 1.5 s (the car), 4 PEER_CONNECTION_FAILED after about 9 s (ended companion sessions -- BladeWatch-qryk). Next: run it on the hotspot that failed before and on the one that passed; the owner to say which phone and tethering mode each was.
MEASURED 2026-09-26 on the 10.101.x hotspot (the one that passed on 09-24): HyperDHT firewalled=true randomized=true on the phone side; the car's side firewalled=true randomized=false. 20 cold starts with the car-side tagging fix in (BladeWatch-lw0o): 7 of 20 never formed a Pear connection (swarm connecting -> failed), 13 did, slowly (route p50 41 s, max 64 s). A plain HyperDHT dial from the same hotspot opened in 3-19 s or failed with PEER_CONNECTION_FAILED. So from a randomizing NAT, hole punching to the car is probabilistic and slow -- this is the idfn failure class, and the 192.168.4.x hotspot that failed 2/2 is likely a harsher case of it.
Option to evaluate (owner decision -- it needs an always-on peer): hyperdht 6.32 (bundled in pear-end) supports relayThrough, a blind relay used when hole punching fails; a relay sees only the companion's pinned TLS records. It would need a relay peer (a home server, or a public blind relay) and a flutter_pear option to pass relayThrough to Hyperswarm. Not done: infrastructure choice.

title: CLAUDE.md reinstall procedure leaves the car with no daemons: relaunch after restoring the ADB key
description:
## Problem / context

CLAUDE.md's clean-reinstall procedure can leave the car with NO dashcam or sentry mode, and
nothing in the procedure catches it. This happened on 2026-09-23/24.

The procedure stops every daemon, uninstalls, installs, then -- to preserve the app's ADB key --
says to "launch once so filesDir exists, then" restore the key via run-as. That ordering is
necessary (run-as needs filesDir) but incomplete:

1. The launch that creates filesDir runs BEFORE the key is restored. The app process starts
   with a freshly generated, UNAUTHORIZED key, so AdbShellExecutor cannot launch daemons.
2. Restoring the key rewrites the files on disk, but the running process has already loaded
   the new key. Nothing restarts it.
3. The procedure never says to relaunch afterwards or to check that the daemons came back.

So the car is left with byd_cam_daemon, sentry_daemon and acc_sentry_daemon all stopped, and
the procedure reports success. Any later `install -r` kills the app process again.

Verified fix, 2026-09-24: after the key is restored, `am force-stop` then relaunch MainActivity
with --activity-clear-task --activity-clear-top. All three daemons came up in 55-65 s.

## Exact locations

- `CLAUDE.md` (repo root), section "Build Commands": the install block after
  "# Install debug APK to device", specifically the "PRESERVE THE KEY ACROSS THE REINSTALL"
  comment block and the "LAUNCHING AFTER THE REINSTALL NEEDS --activity-clear-task" block.

## Step-by-step instructions

1. Read the whole install section of CLAUDE.md first.
2. After the key-restore commands, add a mandatory relaunch:
     adb -s $CAR_IP:5555 shell 'am force-stop net.bladewatch.app; sleep 1; am start -n net.bladewatch.app/net.bladewatch.app.ui.MainActivity --activity-clear-task --activity-clear-top'
3. Then add a verification step that polls for up to ~90 s and fails loudly if any daemon is missing:
     adb -s $CAR_IP:5555 shell 'for n in byd_cam_daemon sentry_daemon acc_sentry_daemon; do printf "%s %s\n" $n "$(pidof $n)"; done'
4. State plainly WHY: the first launch ran with an unauthorized key, so it could not start
   anything, and until this relaunch the car has no dashcam or sentry mode.
5. Add one line noting that any later `install -r` also kills the app process, so re-run the
   relaunch after it too.

## Constraints

- Keep the existing ordering (launch -> restore key). It is required; only add after it.
- Do not change any command's flags except as described. The --activity-clear-task note and
  the killall-not-pkill notes are verified-on-device lessons; leave them intact.
- Documentation only. No code changes. Do not commit.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] CLAUDE.md's install section ends with a force-stop + relaunch AFTER the key restore.
- [ ] It includes a pidof check for all three daemons with an explicit "fail if missing" instruction.
- [ ] The reason (first launch holds an unauthorized key) is written next to the step.
- [ ] The note about re-running after any later `install -r` is present.
- [ ] Following the updated procedure end to end on the head unit leaves all three daemons running. Record the timings.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
close_reason:
Done. CLAUDE.md's install section already carried all four documentation items (force-stop + relaunch AFTER the key restore; pidof check of all three daemons with an explicit fail-if-missing instruction; the reason next to the step; the re-run-after-install -r note). This closes the last criterion: the procedure followed end to end on the head unit, 2026-09-24, scripted verbatim from CLAUDE.md with timestamps:

[+0s]  key backed up from the device (1703 + 716 bytes), byte-compared with the existing backup
[+3s]  stop block done ("all daemons stopped"; includes pear_daemon)
[+3s]  uninstall net.bladewatch.app: Success
[+12s] install (branch-sanitised APK path): Success
[+17s] first launch done (filesDir exists)
[+17s] key restored, read back byte-exact
[+18s] relaunch (force-stop + am start --activity-clear-task --activity-clear-top)
[+88s] all three daemons up, 70 s after the relaunch (byd_cam_daemon, sentry_daemon, acc_sentry_daemon)
[+88s] local /tmp/adbkey* deleted only after that

No tap on the car's screen was needed (the preserved key was authorised). The optional pear_daemon (enabled at the time) also came back via the health check, and the secret store (auth, pear, lanTls, lanDiscovery sections) and the LAN TLS fingerprint were unchanged across the uninstall.

title: In-car UI: Pear peer status replacing the removed tunnel entry
description:
## Problem / context

The in-car Flutter UI shows the owner which daemons are running, including the tunnel. After
this epic, the tunnel entry is deleted and NOTHING replaces it — so the owner loses every
way to tell whether their remote access works, from the only screen that ever told them.

`flutter_ui/lib/screens/settings/settings_daemons_screen.dart` has a `DaemonKind.torTunnel`
entry with a localised name (`l10n.daemon_name_tor`, line 79) and an icon (`Icons.link`,
line 87). Its doc comment at line 74 notes "Tor Tunnel is a product name and is deliberately
untranslated". The Tor-removal task deletes that entry. The PearLauncher task wires the new
daemon into the KOTLIN side (`DaemonType.kt`, `DaemonStartupManager.kt`) but nothing adds
the Dart-side status surface.

This task adds it. It is user-visible: an owner who cannot see that their car is reachable
has no way to distinguish "working" from "silently broken" until they are away from the car
and need it.

## Exact locations

- `flutter_ui/lib/screens/settings/settings_daemons_screen.dart` — the `DaemonKind` switch
  for name (line ~79) and icon (line ~87)
- `flutter_ui/lib/screens/settings/settings_daemons_controller.dart`
- `flutter_ui/lib/platform/daemon_channel.dart` — the MethodChannel to the privileged layer
- `flutter_ui/lib/l10n/` — the localisation ARB files
- `flutter_ui/lib/screens/dashboard/dashboard_screen.dart` and `dashboard_controller.dart` —
  the dashboard's tunnel status surface
- Kotlin side that must expose the status: `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/model/DaemonType.kt`,
  `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/viewmodel/DaemonsViewModel.kt`
- The daemon itself: `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/launcher/PearLauncher.kt`

## Step-by-step instructions

1. Read `settings_daemons_screen.dart` fully, including its doc comments. They record real
   behaviour, for example that the screen used to load once and never refresh, and that the
   daemon health check runs on a 30s cycle — so a peer that starts thirty seconds after the
   screen opens will not appear until a refresh.
2. Add a `DaemonKind` case for the Pear peer, with an l10n key, an icon, and a status
   display consistent with the other daemons.
3. Decide whether the name is translated. "Tor Tunnel" was deliberately untranslated as a
   product name; "Pear" is likewise a product name, but a label like "Remote access" is not.
   Pick one, and follow the existing convention in the ARB files.
4. Surface what an owner actually needs, not just up/down:
   - is the peer running,
   - is it reachable (has it bootstrapped onto the DHT),
   - how many companions are currently connected,
   - when a companion last connected.
   Reachability and "process is alive" are different questions, and only the first answers
   "can I check on my car from work".
5. Add the equivalent dashboard surface alongside the existing tunnel status.

   ORDERING: this task runs BEFORE tor is removed (it blocks the Tor-removal task on
   purpose, so the owner is never left with no remote-access visibility at all). So the tor
   entry still EXISTS while you work. Add the Pear entry beside it; do not delete the tor
   entry here, and do not write code or comments that assume tor is already gone. The
   Tor-removal task deletes the tor entry afterwards.
6. Expose whatever the Kotlin side needs to answer the above, through the existing daemon
   status path rather than a new bespoke channel.
7. Add widget and controller tests.

## Constraints

- Do NOT display the Pear topic, the invite, any token or the TLS key material on screen.
  The pairing QR is the only place a credential is ever shown, and the pairing task gates
  that behind an explicit action.
- Do NOT show a connected-companion count that leaks anything identifying about the
  companion beyond what the owner already knows.
- Do NOT add golden tests. This project deliberately has none.
- Do NOT rely on `flutter test`'s font metrics for any text-fit assertion — it uses a
  fixed-width placeholder font, so overflow assertions in widget tests are meaningless.
  Verify on the head unit.
- Do NOT lower the Flutter coverage gate or the `flutter_ui/android` kover bound.
- Do NOT leave a dangling `daemon_name_tor` l10n key in the ARB files once the tor entry is
  gone; unreferenced keys have caused confusion on this project before.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A Pear peer entry appears in `settings_daemons_screen.dart` with a localised name and
      an icon, following the existing `DaemonKind` convention.
- [ ] The entry shows running state, DHT reachability, connected-companion count, and last
      connection time.
- [ ] Reachability is distinguished from process-alive. Prove it by leaving the peer running
      with networking disabled and showing the UI reports reachable=false.
- [ ] The dashboard surfaces remote-access status where the tunnel status used to be.
- [ ] `cd flutter_ui && flutter analyze && flutter test` pass.
- [ ] `cd flutter_ui && flutter test --coverage && cd .. && tools/check_flutter_coverage.sh` passes.
- [ ] `cd flutter_ui/android && ./gradlew koverVerify` passes.
- [ ] No topic, invite, token or key material is rendered anywhere on screen.
- [ ] No unreferenced tor l10n keys remain in the ARB files.
- [ ] Verified on a real head unit: the entry reflects an actual companion connecting and
      disconnecting.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.

title: Release workflow, build docs and upgrade notes for the companion app
description:
## Problem / context

`.github/workflows/release.yml` builds exactly TWO APKs on a `v*` tag — the service host
(`net.bladewatch.app`) and the in-car UI (`net.bladewatch.flutter`) — and hard-fails if
either is missing or if either is signed. v1.4.0.0 adds a third deliverable, the companion
app, across up to five platforms. Nothing in the current workflow knows about it, and the
toolchain documentation does not mention melos, flutter_pear or the bare-kit pin.

Separately, existing owners upgrading from v1.3.2.0 have onion-URL QR codes that stop
working when tor is removed. That needs saying in the release notes, not discovering.

## Exact locations

- `.github/workflows/release.yml` — line ~19 the workflow name, lines ~179-186 the two
  build steps, lines ~217-226 the staging step that asserts both APKs exist.
- `docs/build-and-operations.md` — toolchain pins and the signing recipe.
- `BladeWatch/CLAUDE.md` — the Build Commands section, which documents how each artifact is
  built and installed.
- `app/build.gradle.kts` — the `applicationVariants.all { }` block that embeds the git
  branch in the APK filename; the workflow globs for it because a tag build is a detached
  HEAD and the branch becomes the literal `HEAD`.
- New: `melos.yaml` at the repo root, and `companion/` (from the scaffold task).

## Step-by-step instructions

1. Read `.github/workflows/release.yml` fully. Note especially why it needs no secrets
   (both APKs come out unsigned and are signed afterwards with the same key, because
   `android:sharedUserId` only collapses them into one UID when the certificates match).
2. Decide which companion platforms CI builds and attaches. Android is the minimum. Desktop
   builds need per-OS runners; do not promise Windows and Linux artifacts without adding
   those runners.
3. Add companion build steps. Respect flutter_pear's Android packaging rule: ship only
   `arm64-v8a` and `x86_64` splits, or an app bundle. The default `armeabi-v7a` variant is
   missing the plugin's native libraries entirely and is not a supported configuration.
4. Update the workflow's artifact-count assertion. It currently fails if fewer than two APKs
   are produced; it must now assert the correct new set, and must still fail loudly rather
   than silently shipping a partial release.
5. Keep the unsigned-release invariant for the two head-unit APKs. The companion is a
   different app on a different device and does NOT share the head unit's UID, so its
   signing story is independent — decide it and write it down.
6. Account for first-build native downloads in CI: bare-kit binaries on Android, a ~107 MB
   BareKit.xcframework on iOS/macOS. Cache them, or CI time and flakiness both grow.
7. Update `docs/http-api-reference.md`. CLAUDE.md requires it on any route-handler change,
   and v1.4.0.0 changes the HTTP surface even though no handler logic moved: there is a new
   TLS access path on 8443, a new remote-origin loopback listener on 8081, `/status` gains
   fields for both, and each listener now carries a different auth posture. A reader of that
   doc must be able to tell which listener a request arrived on and what that implies.
8. Update `docs/build-and-operations.md` with: the melos workspace layout and
   `melos bootstrap`, the exact flutter_pear version pin, the bare-kit version pin used by
   the daemon, the companion's per-platform build wiring (Android minSdk 29, the iOS/macOS
   Info.plist keys, the macOS entitlements), and the companion signing story.
9. Update `CLAUDE.md`'s Build Commands section with the companion build and test commands.
10. Write the upgrade note for existing owners: removing tor invalidates every onion URL and
   QR code they have saved, they must re-pair with the new pairing QR, and the LAN path
   needs the opt-in toggle. Put it where release notes are written, not only in docs.

## Constraints

- Do NOT sign the two head-unit APKs in CI. The keystore never touches GitHub; the workflow
  fails on purpose if either comes out signed.
- Do NOT relax the artifact assertion into a warning. A silently partial release is exactly
  what that check exists to prevent.
- Do NOT change the APK filename convention or the branch-embedding block. A tag build is a
  detached HEAD and the workflow already handles it by globbing and stamping the tag.
- Do NOT add secrets to the repository.
- Do NOT claim a platform is released if CI does not actually build and attach it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `.github/workflows/release.yml` builds and attaches the companion for every platform
      it claims to support, and no others.
- [ ] The artifact assertion is updated and still FAILS the workflow when an expected
      artifact is missing. Prove it fails by temporarily breaking one build in a scratch
      branch, not by reading the YAML.
- [ ] Both head-unit APKs still come out UNSIGNED and the workflow still fails if they are not.
- [ ] Native-binary downloads are cached in CI.
- [ ] `docs/http-api-reference.md` documents the 8443 TLS path, the 8081 remote-origin
      listener, the new `/status` fields, and the per-listener auth posture.
- [ ] `docs/build-and-operations.md` documents the melos layout, the flutter_pear pin, the
      bare-kit pin, the companion's per-platform build wiring and its signing story.
- [ ] `CLAUDE.md`'s Build Commands section covers building and testing the companion.
- [ ] An upgrade note exists stating that tor removal invalidates saved onion URLs and QR
      codes and that owners must re-pair.
- [ ] A dry-run tag build produces every expected artifact.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
notes:
IMPLEMENTED 2026-09-24 (uncommitted):
- release.yml builds THREE unsigned APKs: the service host, the in-car UI, and the companion (Android only, a single APK with arm64-v8a and x86_64). The header comment and release notes state that CI builds no iOS, macOS, Windows or Linux companion. Each needs its own runner, and Apple signing is impossible in a secret-free workflow.
- Artifact check: stage fails if any of the three is missing, and verify fails unless there are exactly 3 and all are unsigned (apksigner).
- bare-kit cache: the pin is read from app/build.gradle.kts. actions/cache@v5 is the lowest major on node24 (v4 is node20; checked each action.yml). One prebuilds.zip (418 MB) is seeded into app/build/bare-kit/VER and companion/build/flutter_pear_bare/bare-kit/VER. A missing or corrupt cached copy is re-downloaded and verified BEFORE the move, and both builds re-verify the SHA-256.
- Companion signing: companion/android/app/build.gradle.kts used Flutter's template debug-key fallback for release. It now signs with KEYSTORE_FILE (default app/release.jks) when present, else leaves the APK unsigned. Signing story: the key need not match the car's, but every companion release must use the same key forever.
- Release notes body: a companion row, the signing note, the BYD Auto-Start reminder after installing either car APK, and the v1.3.x upgrade note (onion URLs and QR codes stop working, nothing migrates; install the companion, tap Pair a device on the dashboard, optional direct connection on Wi-Fi).
- Docs: http-api-reference.md has a new "Listeners and what each one trusts" table (8080 LOCAL_APPS by peer UID, 8081 tor REMOTE, 8444 Pear pump TLS REMOTE, 8443 LAN TLS REMOTE opt-in) and the action-token requirement. It also fixes the stale /auth/token rate-limit text (socket IP; X-Forwarded-For is ignored; global lockout). build-and-operations.md covers the three-APK CI, companion size and platforms, bare-kit caching, and companion signing. CLAUDE.md's CI paragraph is updated. The melos layout, flutter_pear pin, bare-kit pin and per-platform wiring were already documented. CLAUDE.md Build Commands already covers building and testing the companion.
- REVIEW FINDING, fixed: GetStatus emitted network.lanTls {enabled, port, listening}, but NetworkInfo in system.proto has no such field, so every typed client dropped it and nothing read it, while networking-and-tunnels.md documented it as status. Deleted from HttpServer, and the doc now says the port and fingerprint reach the in-car UI over IPC (lanTlsInfo) and a companion through the QR.
- REVIEW FINDING, filed upstream as flutter_pear-9ng: flutter_pear declares its desktop prebuilds as universal Flutter assets, so the Android APK carries 50 MB of darwin, linux and win32 addons.

VERIFIED LOCALLY:
- "flutter build apk --release" in companion/: 200 MB, UNSIGNED (apksigner verify fails), lib/ contains only arm64-v8a and x86_64 (17 each).
- The extracted workflow step scripts, run in a scratch tree with a stub apksigner: all present gives stage 0 and verify 0; companion missing fails stage; companion signed fails verify; an extra APK fails verify (count 4).
- Pin resolve prints 2.5.5 and the matching sha. Seed: a good cached zip means no download; a missing one is downloaded (418 MB) and verified; a corrupt one is re-fetched and verified; both destinations are placed.
- actionlint: only the 4 pre-existing SC2012 infos. The YAML parses.
- Recent release runs took 13-21 min; the estimate with the companion build and bare-kit fetch is about 30 min, inside the 60-min timeout.

PENDING (needs a push, which is the owner's call; I do not commit or push):
- A workflow_dispatch dry run on a branch carrying this change, expecting 3 unsigned APKs.
- The scratch-branch "break one build" proof. The stage and verify logic is already proven locally as above.

title: Remove Tor entirely (gated on throughput verdict and real-hardware Pear validation)
description:
## Problem / context

Once the Pear transport and the LAN TLS path are both proven on real hardware, tor is dead
weight: a downloaded binary, a jniLib, a launcher, a controller, UI surfaces and a
persistent on-disk identity, all maintained for a path nobody uses.

THIS TASK IS GATED. Do not start it until ALL of these hold:
- The throughput-measurement task is CLOSED with an explicit verdict that live view over
  Pear is acceptable (or with a recorded, accepted decision about what live view does
  instead).
- The companion has connected over Pear from a genuinely different network on real hardware.
- The companion has connected over the LAN TLS path on real hardware.

## Irreversibility warning — read before deleting anything

`/data/local/tmp/tor/hs/hs_ed25519_secret_key` IS the car's permanent onion address. Once it
is gone, tor mints a brand-new address on next start and every QR code the owner has ever
scanned is silently dead, with no way back. This task removes tor deliberately and
permanently, which is the point — but it must be the LAST step, after the replacement is
proven, and the removal of the on-device directory is a separate, explicit action from
deleting the code.

## Exact locations

Code referencing tor (from a scoped grep of `app/src/main`, `app/src/test`, `flutter_ui/lib`):

- `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/launcher/TorLauncher.kt` (347 lines)
- `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/daemon/TorController.kt`
- `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/daemon/DaemonStartupManager.kt`
- `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/model/DaemonType.kt`
- `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/viewmodel/DaemonsViewModel.kt`
- `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/launcher/AdbDaemonLauncher.kt`
- `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/launcher/AdbShellExecutor.kt`
- `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/TcpCommandServer.kt`
- `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/AuthMiddleware.kt`
- `app/src/test/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/launcher/TorLauncherCommandTest.kt`
- `app/src/test/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/DaemonSetEnabledCommandTest.java`
- `app/build.gradle.kts` lines 145-180: the `downloadTor` task
- `app/src/main/jniLibs/arm64-v8a/libtor.so`
- `TorBinaryPackagingTest`
- Flutter side: `flutter_ui/lib/platform/daemon_channel.dart`,
  `flutter_ui/lib/screens/settings/settings_daemons_controller.dart`,
  `flutter_ui/lib/screens/settings/settings_daemons_screen.dart`,
  `flutter_ui/lib/screens/dashboard/dashboard_screen.dart`,
  `flutter_ui/lib/screens/dashboard/dashboard_controller.dart`

## Step-by-step instructions

1. Verify the gate conditions above are actually met. If any is not, stop.
2. Re-read the throughput task's close reason and confirm the verdict.
3. Remove the Gradle `downloadTor` task and the `libtor.so` jniLib, plus `TorBinaryPackagingTest`.
4. Remove `TorLauncher.kt`, `TorController.kt`, and their tests.
5. Remove the tor entries from `DaemonType.kt`, `DaemonStartupManager.kt` and
   `DaemonsViewModel.kt`. Check whether removing a `DaemonType` enum value breaks any
   persisted config parsing — handle an old config that still names tor gracefully rather
   than crashing the daemon on upgrade.
6. Remove tor handling from `TcpCommandServer.kt`.
7. STOP AND READ THIS BEFORE TOUCHING `AuthMiddleware.kt`. This step is the single most
   dangerous part of removing tor.

   `isTunnelActive()` (line 223) exists to DISABLE the Tier 2 loopback bypass whenever the
   head unit is reachable from outside. It detects that by looking for exactly one process
   name: `findPidsByProcessName(TorLauncher.TOR_PROCESS)`, where
   `TOR_PROCESS = "bladewatch_tor"` (`TorLauncher.kt` line 60).

   Deleting tor deletes that signal. If you simply remove the check, or let it fall through
   to returning false, then on a DEBUG build — which is the build that actually ships to
   the car, because preserving the ADB key across a reinstall needs `run-as` — the Tier 2
   bypass switches back ON. Any caller from 127.0.0.1 would then get UNAUTHENTICATED access
   to the whole API, including the vehicle-control endpoints that actuate real hardware.

   This is the exact hole `BladeWatch-3lbz.2` closed for tor. Do not reopen it.

   The structural protection is the remote-origin listener introduced by the pump and TLS
   tasks: the Pear pump connects to 127.0.0.1:8081, and connections on that listener are
   never bypass-eligible regardless of build type or tunnel state. VERIFY that protection
   is actually in place and tested BEFORE removing `isTunnelActive()`'s tor check.

   Then decide deliberately what `isTunnelActive()` becomes: delete it only if the
   per-listener policy fully subsumes it, and record the reasoning in the close reason. If
   in any doubt, keep it and make it fail CLOSED (it already does — the catch block returns
   true on error, meaning "assume exposed").

   Separately review the tunnel-header handling (`X-Forwarded-*`, `CF-*`, `X-Real-IP`,
   `Forwarded`). Those defend against header spoofing generally, not only tor. Do not
   delete security checks casually.
8. Remove the tor/tunnel UI from the Flutter screens listed above, including the old
   tunnel-URL QR now superseded by the pairing QR.
9. Update the CLAUDE.md daemon-stop procedure: the `killall -9 bladewatch_tor` line and the
   surrounding "never delete /data/local/tmp/tor" warnings describe a daemon that no longer
   exists. Replace them with the equivalent Pear daemon steps.
10. Update `docs/networking-and-tunnels.md`, `docs/architecture.md`,
    `docs/daemons-and-processes.md` and `docs/features.md`.
11. As a SEPARATE, explicit final step, remove `/data/local/tmp/tor` from the test head unit
    and confirm nothing regresses.

## Constraints

- Do NOT start this task before the gate conditions hold.
- Do NOT delete `/data/local/tmp/tor` on any device until the code removal is verified
  working, and never as an incidental cleanup inside another step.
- Do NOT remove `AuthMiddleware`'s forwarded-header checks without an explicit recorded
  reason. They defend against header spoofing generally, not only tor.
- Do NOT leave a partially-removed daemon type that breaks parsing of an existing
  `bladewatch_config.json` on an upgraded device.
- Do NOT lower any coverage gate to compensate for deleted covered code. If deleting tor
  raises the measured percentage, RAISE the bound; gates ratchet upward.
- Do NOT commit.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The gate conditions are documented as met in the close reason, with links to the
      relevant closed tasks.
- [ ] The remote-origin listener protection is verified present and tested BEFORE any change
      to `isTunnelActive()`.
- [ ] A test proves that on a DEBUG build with no tor process anywhere, a request arriving
      through the Pear pump is STILL denied without a JWT. Run it with
      `setLoopbackBypassOverride(true)` forced, which is the worst case.
- [ ] A test proves the vehicle-control endpoints specifically return 401 in that scenario.
- [ ] Whatever happened to `isTunnelActive()` — kept, replaced or deleted — is justified in
      writing in the close reason, naming what now prevents the Tier 2 bypass from applying
      to remote traffic.
- [ ] `grep -rni 'tor' app/src/main app/src/test flutter_ui/lib` returns no live tor
      references (be careful of false positives such as "monitor", "factory", "generator" —
      review each hit rather than trusting the count).
- [ ] `app/src/main/jniLibs/arm64-v8a/libtor.so` no longer exists.
- [ ] `downloadTor` no longer exists in `app/build.gradle.kts`.
- [ ] `./gradlew assembleDebug`, `./gradlew test`, `./gradlew koverVerify` pass.
- [ ] `cd flutter_ui && flutter analyze && flutter test` pass.
- [ ] `cd flutter_ui/android && ./gradlew koverVerify` passes.
- [ ] A device with an OLD `bladewatch_config.json` still naming the tor daemon starts
      cleanly. Prove this with an actual old config file, not by reading the code.
- [ ] CLAUDE.md's daemon-stop procedure no longer references `bladewatch_tor` and does
      reference the Pear daemon.
- [ ] `docs/networking-and-tunnels.md`, `docs/architecture.md`,
      `docs/daemons-and-processes.md` and `docs/features.md` contain no stale tor claims.
- [ ] Remote access still works over Pear and over LAN TLS after the removal, verified on
      real hardware.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.

title: Companion app screens to web/ parity
description:
## Problem / context

The companion app needs the screens the Angular SPA in `web/` provides today, because
`web/` is retired only once the companion reaches parity. The good news is that most of
this already exists in Dart: `flutter_ui/` has 11 screens and ~114k lines covering the same
ground, and the RPC layer is now shared.

The companion is NOT a copy of the in-car UI. Differences that actually matter:

- The in-car UI is one fixed 1280x480-class landscape head-unit screen. The companion runs
  on phones (portrait), tablets and desktop windows. Layouts must be responsive.
- The in-car UI mints its JWT over loopback IPC because it shares a UID with the daemon.
  The companion has no such path — it uses the paired token from the pairing payload.
- The companion may be offline or far from the car. Every screen needs a real
  disconnected/reconnecting state, not a spinner that never resolves.
- Vehicle control from a phone that is nowhere near the car is a different risk posture than
  from the driver's seat.

## Exact locations

- Source screens to port: `flutter_ui/lib/screens/` — dashboard, diagnostics, live_view,
  location, recordings, settings, surveillance, trips, vehicle, startup, dialogs.
- Angular pages defining the parity target: `web/src/app/pages/` — dashboard, live, events,
  recording, surveillance, trips, location, vehicle, notifications, performance,
  diagnostics, settings, about, login.
- Shared RPC: `packages/bladewatch_rpc/` (from the scaffold task).
- Theme reference: `flutter_ui/lib/theme/` and `docs/ui-ux-design-language.md`.
- Localisation: `flutter_ui/lib/l10n/`.
- JWT abstraction to implement for the companion: `jwt_source.dart` in the shared package.

## Step-by-step instructions

1. Read `docs/ui-ux-design-language.md` before writing UI. Token changes belong there.
2. Build the parity checklist FIRST, as a table of the 14 `web/src/app/pages/` entries
   against their companion status. Put it in the task notes; the retirement-gate task
   consumes it.
3. Implement a `JwtSource` for the companion backed by the paired token from pairing.
4. Port screens in dependency order: connection/pairing, then dashboard, then live view,
   then the rest.
5. Make every screen responsive. The in-car layouts assume one wide landscape screen; do not
   carry that assumption into a phone portrait layout.
6. Give every screen an explicit disconnected and reconnecting state distinct from loading.
   flutter_pear documents that a DHT lookup can take 30s or more and that a locked screen
   mid-handshake looks exactly like a broken connection.
7. For vehicle control, keep the existing safety gating and add a confirmation appropriate
   to remote use. Read `VehicleActionGate.kt` and `VehicleActionToken.kt` and the
   DrivingSafetyGuard interlock from v1.3.2.0 before changing anything in this area.
8. Write widget and unit tests as you go. Note that `flutter test` uses a fixed-width
   placeholder font, so text-fit and overflow assertions in widget tests are meaningless —
   verify layout on real devices instead.

## Constraints

- Do NOT weaken or bypass the vehicle-control safety interlock. Those commands actuate real
  hardware — windows, trunk, lights, climate. CLAUDE.md requires conservative testing here.
- Do NOT duplicate the RPC layer. Import it from the shared package.
- Do NOT add golden tests. This project deliberately has none; visual parity is verified on
  real hardware.
- Do NOT assume the head unit's screen geometry.
- Do NOT add iOS/desktop directories to `flutter_ui/`. All companion platform code lives in
  the companion project.
- Do NOT lower any coverage gate.
- Do NOT retire or modify `web/` in this task. That is the separate gate task.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A parity checklist exists mapping all 14 `web/src/app/pages/` entries to companion
      status, stored in the task notes.
- [ ] Every page in that checklist is either implemented or explicitly recorded as
      deliberately-not-ported with a reason.
- [ ] `cd companion && flutter analyze && flutter test` pass.
- [ ] Coverage meets or exceeds the project's Flutter gate; no gate lowered.
- [ ] Screens render correctly on a phone in portrait, a tablet, and a desktop window —
      verified on real devices, not in widget tests.
- [ ] Every screen shows a distinguishable disconnected state, proven by killing the car's
      daemon while the companion is open.
- [ ] Vehicle control still refuses commands the interlock blocks; the existing guard tests
      pass unmodified.
- [ ] Live view plays over both the LAN path and the Pear path on real hardware.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.

title: Bump version to 1.4.0.0
description:
## Problem / context

The repo is on branch `feature/v1.4.0.0` but `app/build.gradle.kts` still declares version
1.3.2.0. The APK filename convention embeds the branch, not the version, so nothing fails
loudly — the version is simply wrong in the manifest and in the About screen until bumped.

## Exact locations

- `app/build.gradle.kts` lines 352-353:
  - line 352: `versionCode = 13200`
  - line 353: `versionName = "1.3.2.0"`

The versionCode scheme is the dotted version with each component as two digits, leading
zeros dropped: 1.3.2.0 -> 13200. So 1.4.0.0 -> 14000.

## Step-by-step instructions

1. Read `app/build.gradle.kts` around lines 340-360 to confirm the two lines above are
   still where this task says they are.
2. Set `versionCode = 14000`.
3. Set `versionName = "1.4.0.0"`.
4. Search the repo for any other place the version string is duplicated and update it only
   if it is a source of truth, not a generated or historical file:
   `grep -rn "1\.3\.2\.0" --include=*.kts --include=*.kt --include=*.yaml --include=*.dart app flutter_ui web 2>/dev/null`
   Do NOT edit CHANGELOG entries, docs describing past releases, or anything under a
   `build/` directory.
5. Run `./gradlew :app:assembleDebug` to confirm the build still configures.

## Constraints

- Do NOT create a git tag. Tags are cut by the release workflow on a `v*` push.
- Do NOT commit. This project forbids `git add`/`git commit`/`git push` by an agent.
- Do NOT change the APK filename convention in `applicationVariants.all { }` — it embeds
  the git branch on purpose and `.github/workflows/release.yml` depends on globbing it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `grep -n 'versionCode' app/build.gradle.kts` shows `14000`.
- [ ] `grep -n 'versionName' app/build.gradle.kts` shows `"1.4.0.0"`.
- [ ] `./gradlew :app:assembleDebug` succeeds.
- [ ] `git status --short` shows `app/build.gradle.kts` modified and nothing staged.
- [ ] No CHANGELOG or docs file describing a past release was modified.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
close_reason: Bumped to 1.4.0.0 / 14000. PREMISE CORRECTION: the task said the version lives in app/build.gradle.kts; it is actually declared in FOUR places, all bumped together because the APKs ship as a pair: app/build.gradle.kts (versionCode 14000, versionName 1.4.0.0), flutter_ui/pubspec.yaml (1.4.0+14000 -- 3-part because pub requires semver), flutter_ui/android/app/build.gradle.kts (explicit versionName 1.4.0.0, plus its explanatory comment's example), web/package.json (1.4.0.0). Verified: aapt2 dump badging on the built service-host APK reports versionCode=14000 versionName=1.4.0.0; flutter_ui/test/platform/channel_surface_parity_test.dart 'both APKs declare the same versionName' passes (it pins the two Gradle files to each other, so a partial bump fails it); ./gradlew :app:assembleDebug succeeds. Left alone on purpose: SessionBannerTest's 1.3.2.0 (self-contained fixture input, not tied to the real version), web/package-lock.json (its root version is 0.0.1, never tracked the release), and all CHANGELOG/docs describing past releases. No tag created.

title: Decide the test-visibility policy for Java-to-Kotlin conversion (Java tests cannot call Kotlin internal)
description:
## Decide first, convert after. This blocks every other conversion task.

Part of BladeWatch-dmrg.

**Java tests cannot call a Kotlin `internal` member.** Verified on this codebase, not recalled:
a Kotlin `object` exposing `@JvmStatic fun publicStatic()` and `@JvmStatic internal fun
internalStatic()`, called from a Java test in the same module — the public call compiled, the
internal one failed with `cannot find symbol`. Kotlin mangles `internal` to `name$app_debug`.

Java has package-private; Kotlin does not. So every Java class with a package-private member
that a Java test reaches needs a decision when it is converted.

## Why this is not a detail

Several of these members exist ONLY because a decision was deliberately extracted to be testable
when the surrounding class could not be built on the JVM — the project's "extract the decision,
test the decision" pattern. Getting this wrong quietly undoes that work:

| Member | Why it is package-private |
|---|---|
| `DaemonSingletonLock.staleReason` | the live-vs-stale branch is unreachable through `acquire()` in one JVM; a test that went through `acquire()` PASSED against a mutated `if (false)` |
| `ShellResultClassifier` | asserts the verbatim device output that the old `contains("Error")` check missed |
| `VehicleActionGate.isDeclaredReadOnly` | half of the guard that fails when a VehicleService RPC is neither gated nor declared safe |
| `ModelsApiHandler.isValidColor` / `isValidModelId` | pure validators on a class needing live config |
| `SafeLocationApiHandler.sanitizeZoneName` | strips angle brackets before a name reaches innerHTML and a Leaflet popup |
| `StorageManager.clampLimitMb` | clamp shared by the setter and the preview |
| `BydDeviceHelper.statusForFailure` | unwraps `InvocationTargetException`, which reflection always wraps |

18 Java tests have a Java main class as their subject.

## The options

- **(a) Convert the test to Kotlin in the same change.** Keeps `internal`, keeps encapsulation.
  Costs a test rewrite per class, and a rewritten test must be re-MUTATION-CHECKED — a test
  translated without that is a test nobody has proven can still fail.
- **(b) Make the member `public` and document why.** No test change. Widens the API of a class
  whose author deliberately did not.
- **(c) Keep those specific classes in Java.** Cheapest, leaves the codebase mixed — which it
  already is, and nothing is broken by that.

## What to do

1. Read the seven members above and their tests before choosing. The choice may differ per
   class; a blanket rule is not required and probably not right.
2. Record the decision ON THIS ISSUE, with the reasoning, before any conversion task starts.
3. If (a): state that every converted test must be mutation-checked afresh, and that a
   translated test which has not been is not done.
4. If (b): state what `public` means here — is it "callers may use this" or "tests only"? If the
   latter, say so in the member's own doc comment, or the next reader will build on it.

## Constraints — do NOT change

- Do not widen a member to `public` silently. The point of this issue is that the choice is
  recorded.
- Do not delete a test to avoid the problem.
- Do not lower any Kover bound.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A recorded decision per affected class, or one blanket rule with its reasoning.
- [ ] The rule names what happens to the 18 Java tests.
- [ ] If any test is translated, it is mutation-checked and that is stated.
- [ ] No conversion task starts before this is closed.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles
and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather
than guessing.
close_reason: Decided: option (a) - keep encapsulation, convert the test to Kotlin in the same change as its class. Both halves probed on this codebase rather than recalled. Java test calling a Kotlin @JvmStatic internal member: 'cannot find symbol' (the public sibling in the same object compiled fine), so Kotlin's name mangling really does close that door. Kotlin test calling a Kotlin internal member in the same module: passes, because the unit-test source set is an associated compilation. Both probe files were deleted immediately. Six members are genuinely package-private and reached from a Java test - DaemonSingletonLock.staleReason, ModelsApiHandler.isValidColor and isValidModelId, SafeLocationApiHandler.sanitizeZoneName, StorageManager.clampLimitMb, BydDeviceHelper.statusForFailure. Every one of them exists because a decision was deliberately extracted to be testable when its surrounding class cannot be built on the JVM, so widening them to public would advertise as API something the author specifically did not, and keeping them Java forever would block the migration. Converting the test alongside costs a rewrite but preserves both properties. THE CONDITION ON THIS: a translated test is not done until it has been mutation-checked afresh. A test that was passing before translation and passes after tells you nothing about whether it can still fail - and this session has already produced one test that passed against a mutated 'if (false)' and one guard that silently stopped matching anything. Three others - ShellResultClassifier.isFailure, VehicleActionGate.requiresActionToken and isDeclaredReadOnly, AdasFieldInventory.probe - are already public and need no decision.

title: Bump version to 1.3.2.0 across all configurations and fixtures
description:
## What

Bump the version to 1.3.2.0 across every configuration and the fixtures that mirror it. The tree
still declared 1.3.1.0 while the branch is `feature/v1.3.2.0`, so an APK built from it reported
the previous release.

## Where the version actually lives

| File | What |
|---|---|
| `app/build.gradle.kts` | `versionCode = 13200`, `versionName = "1.3.2.0"` |
| `flutter_ui/android/app/build.gradle.kts` | `versionName = "1.3.2.0"` — an unavoidable COPY of the line above |
| `flutter_ui/pubspec.yaml` | `version: 1.3.2+13200` — three-part, because pub rejects a four-part semver |
| `web/package.json` | `"version": "1.3.2.0"` |

the sample banner in `docs/log-files.md`, and the explanatory comment in the parity test.

## Deliberately NOT changed

`CLAUDE.md:158` and `:161` still say `feature/v1.3.1.0`. They are a DATED observation — "Verified
on 2026-09-15 -- the unsanitised form below failed on branch feature/v1.3.1.0" — recording that a
branch name containing a slash broke the APK path lookup on that specific branch. Rewriting them
would falsify a record of something that actually happened. The previous bump left them alone for
the same reason.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] No tracked file outside `.beads/` and the CLAUDE.md historical note still says 1.3.1.0.
- [x] Both APKs declare `1.3.2.0`; the parity test passes.
- [x] `versionCode` and the pubspec build number move together (13100 -> 13200).
- [x] The APK builds and is named `bladewatch-feature-v1.3.2.0-arm64-v8a-debug.apk`.
