close_reason: Done. versionCode 13100 to 13200 and versionName 1.3.1.0 to 1.3.2.0 in app/build.gradle.kts; the mirrored versionName in flutter_ui/android/app/build.gradle.kts; pubspec.yaml to 1.3.2+13200 (three-part, because pub rejects a four-part semver, which is exactly why the Flutter APK writes versionName out explicitly rather than deriving it); and web/package.json. Fixtures kept in step per the precedent of e63490b: SessionBannerTest.kt, the sample banner in docs/log-files.md, and the explanatory comment in channel_surface_parity_test.dart. CLAUDE.md lines 158 and 161 deliberately still say feature/v1.3.1.0 - they are a dated record that a slash in that branch name broke the APK path lookup on 2026-09-15, and rewriting them would falsify an observation. The last bump left them alone for the same reason. One mistake caught mid-edit: my first pass replaced the substring 'version = "1.3.1.0",' before the longer, more specific anchors that contained it, so those later anchors no longer matched and the script aborted before writing - the file was left untouched rather than half-edited, and the second pass used the shortest distinct anchors instead. Verified: no tracked file outside .beads and that CLAUDE.md note mentions 1.3.1.0; the parity test that pins both APKs to the same versionName passes; APK builds as bladewatch-feature-v1.3.2.0-arm64-v8a-debug.apk; gradle test koverVerify, flutter analyze, flutter test (1575), web typecheck and web unit (64) all green.

title: EPIC: remove the REST JSON API entirely; ConnectRPC is the only API surface
description: ## Goal **No REST JSON API left.** Every `/api/*` JSON endpoint becomes a ConnectRPC method, and the REST handler code behind it is deleted — not merely unrouted. Scope decided with the developer: **JSON API only.** These stay plain HTTP because they are assets and media that a browser must fetch directly and cannot speak Connect: - the Angular SPA bundle (`/`, `angular/*`, `/assets/*`) - `/login`, `/login.html`, `/manifest.json`, `/sw.js`, `/favicon.ico`, `/credits.json` - `/i18n/*` and `/shared/*` - `/video/*` and `/thumb/*` — player byte-range requests and `` - `/api/stream/*` — MJPEG / still frames consumed as image URLs ## Why this is not a one-line change The REST handlers are currently the **implementation**, not a parallel surface. 73 of the 102 registered RPC methods are literally `ConnectHandlerUtil.captureString(out -> SomeApiHandler.handle("GET", "/api/...", req, out))`. So "delete the REST code" means inverting each handler from *writing JSON to an OutputStream* to *returning data*, then pointing the Connect impl at the new method. Measured size: **14 handler classes, 8,467 lines**, **16 `/api/*` route families** still routed in `HttpServer.routeToHandlers`, **73** `captureString` wrappers. | Handler | Lines | |---|---| | RecordingsApiHandler | 1795 | | QualitySettingsApiHandler | 1306 | | SurveillanceApiHandler | 1195 | | VehicleControlApiHandler | 1120 | | PerformanceApiHandler | 798 | | StreamingApiHandler | 357 | | ExternalStorageApiHandler | 347 | | AudioTestApiHandler | 321 | | AuthApiHandler | 270 | | ModelsApiHandler | 264 | | NotificationApiHandler | 254 | | FormatStorageApiHandler | 227 | | SafeLocationApiHandler | 131 | | GpsApiHandler | 82 | ## Phases Each phase must land green on its own. Do not start the next until the previous is verified. 1. **Move the last first-party REST clients onto Connect** (BladeWatch-qwqq). Five JSON endpoints are still called directly by Flutter and the web SPA. Until this lands, unrouting anything breaks the UI. 2. **Unroute `/api/*` JSON from `HttpServer`.** After phase 1 nothing external calls them. This is the point at which "no REST API is SERVED" becomes true, and it is cheap and reversible. 3. **Invert the handlers, one per issue.** Each handler's `handle(method, path, body, out)` entry point is deleted; its logic becomes methods that RETURN data; the Connect impl calls them directly. `ConnectHandlerUtil.captureString` is deleted when the last caller goes. Start with the smallest handlers (GpsApiHandler 82, SafeLocationApiHandler 131) to establish the pattern on low risk, then work up. ## Constraints — do NOT change - Do not touch the routes listed as staying HTTP above. - Do not change `AuthMiddleware`, the public allowlist, or the peer-UID gate on 19876/19877. - Do not change RPC method NAMES or message shapes for the 73 that already exist — clients depend on them and `ApiReferenceCoversEveryRpcTest` pins them against the docs. - Do not delete a handler method that the daemon calls internally (several are used outside the HTTP path — check callers before removing anything). ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] No `/api/*` JSON path is routed by `HttpServer`. - [ ] No `*ApiHandler.handle(String, String, String, OutputStream)` entry point remains. - [ ] `ConnectHandlerUtil.captureString` is gone. - [ ] No first-party client calls `/api/*` for JSON. - [ ] A guard test pins that no new REST JSON route or handler entry point reappears. - [ ] `docs/http-api-reference.md` describes one API surface plus the asset/media routes. - [ ] `ApiReferenceCoversEveryRpcTest` passes. - [ ] All seven gates pass. - [ ] Verified on the head unit: every screen in both the Flutter UI and the web SPA still works. Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
close_reason: Done. ConnectRPC is the only JSON API surface. VERIFIED, not asserted: - HttpServer routes exactly one /api path, /api/stream/still, and it is a JPEG. - No first-party client calls /api/* for JSON. Zero matches across web/src and flutter_ui/lib once the binary still-frame URL is excluded. - Only AuthApiHandler and StreamingApiHandler still declare an OutputStream entry point, both for the documented reasons below. - All seven gates pass and the APK builds. WHAT WAS DONE, BY PHASE Phase 1 (BladeWatch-qwqq): seven new RPCs replaced the five JSON endpoints Flutter and the Angular SPA still called directly, and their raw-HTTP plumbing was DELETED rather than left dead - PerformanceController lost jwtSource/send/baseUrl, RecordingSettingsController lost four params, and main.dart lost the app-lifetime RawHttpSender that existed only to stop the old REST path leaking a connection pool per screen visit. Phase 2: every /api/* JSON route unrouted, plus the inline /status, /api/i18n/lang, /api/start|view|stop/{id}, /api/stopall and /api/recording/mode. Checked the legacy assets/web/shared/*.js FIRST, as this issue required: theme.js and core.js are loaded by login.html and do call /api/settings/appearance and /api/i18n/lang, but neither is on AuthMiddleware's public allowlist, so both were already 401ing and degrading to localStorage. Unrouting changed nothing there. Phase 3: all fourteen handlers dealt with. Eleven fully inverted; RecordingsApiHandler and StreamingApiHandler partially (their JSON operations inverted, their binary routes kept); AuthApiHandler left whole. THE THREE EXEMPTIONS, AND WHY - AuthApiHandler: /auth/status and /auth/token are the PRE-AUTH bootstrap. login.html is plain HTML served before any Connect client exists, and it is the one page that must work when everything else is broken. Verified at the source that it fetches both. - RecordingsApiHandler.handleWithRange: /video/* and /thumb/* are byte ranges for a player and an , with Range, 206 and ETag support. - StreamingApiHandler: GET /api/stream/still is a JPEG the live view consumes as an image URL. NoRestHandlerEntryPointsTest carries all three with their reasons, and nothingIsBothInvertedAndExempt pins the inverted and exempt lists disjoint so a handler cannot be declared both - which would let the ratchet pass while the REST shape survived. WHAT THIS REMOVED BEYOND THE PLUMBING - PerformanceApiHandler: 798 -> 369 lines. Eleven handlers were unreachable once /api/* was unrouted; three of them (connect/heartbeat/disconnect) were also SUPERSEDED by phase 1, so they were duplicate logic behind a dead route, not merely dead. - VehicleControlApiHandler.handleIssueActionToken: BladeWatch-jwko had already put the issuer on VehicleService.IssueActionToken. Keeping this copy would have been a second implementation of a security primitive, which is how the gate it belongs to drifted in the first place. - QualitySettingsApiHandler: the /api/settings/unified pair and the telemetry-overlay settings pair had no RPC; the status-overlay pair and the telemetry-overlay FIELDS reader were superseded by phase 1. - ModelsApiHandler.downloadStatus / refreshManifest: no RPC, and their only caller was assets/web/shared/ev-card-3d.js, which no served page loads (checked hero.html and login.html; the name survives only in a comment). - Synthetic URLs built only to be parsed back apart: parking-delta, last-charge, external-storage preview, and the recordings list filters. The recordings one also carried a guard that silently DROPPED any filter value containing '&' or '=' because it would have corrupted the query string; that hazard is gone with the string. WHAT WAS ADDED BACK RATHER THAN LOST - VehicleService.GetAdasInventory. handleAdasInventory was REST-only and the reference said to add an RPC "if a client needs it" - removing the REST surface WAS that moment. Without it the diagnostic would have vanished silently. Classified read-only in VehicleActionGate. - GetSnapshot stopped round-tripping: the handler used to write an HTTP header plus JPEG into a stream that ConnectHandlerUtil parsed back apart. It returns byte[] now, base64'd straight into image_jpeg. Same wire result, no HTTP response modelled in memory. MISTAKES MADE, ALL CAUGHT BEFORE THEY SHIPPED 1. A deletion script that inferred its own upper boundary - walking back from a signature to the preceding blank line to take the javadoc - deleted handleGetCurrent, a LIVE method. Noticed only because a grep for the survivors came back one short. Every later conversion asserts all live methods by name BEFORE writing the file. 2. The ratchet guard matched the bare word "OutputStream", so SurveillanceApiHandler failed for using a ByteArrayOutputStream to encode a JPEG. 3. Fixing that, I required '(' or ',' immediately before OutputStream - which does not match a java.io.-qualified parameter, so the guard caught NOTHING. Found by mutation. It now matches a parameter of that type however spelled, and the mutation check runs bare, qualified and final: all three CAUGHT. 4. Inverting SafeLocationApiHandler I wrote "setEnabled" where the proto defines enabled_set (json enabledSet). optBoolean returns its default for an unknown name, so this neither failed to compile nor threw - every explicit safe-locations toggle would have INVERTED the current state instead of setting it. SafeLocationRequestShapeTest now pins field names against the proto; do the same for any future handler. NOT DONE: none of this is verified on the head unit. The device is still on 1.3.1.0. Every screen in both UIs needs an end-to-end check after a deploy - that acceptance criterion is the one item in this issue's list that is NOT met, and it is deliberately left for a deploy rather than claimed.

comments.text:
## Progress

**Phase 1 — clients off REST: DONE** (BladeWatch-qwqq).

**Phase 2 — unroute /api/* JSON: DONE.** `HttpServer` routes no JSON path. What remains is
`/video/*`, `/thumb/*` and `/api/stream/*` only. Guarded by `NoRestJsonRoutesTest`, which pins
both halves: no JSON route, AND the media routes still served (so it cannot be satisfied by
deleting those too and breaking playback).

Removed with it: `/api/i18n/lang` (SettingsService.GetLocale/SetLocale) and the inline
`/api/start/{id}`, `/api/view/{id}`, `/api/stop/{id}`, `/api/stopall`, `/api/recording/mode`.
Checked the legacy `assets/web/shared/*.js` first as this issue required — `theme.js` and
`core.js` are loaded by `login.html` and do call `/api/settings/appearance` and
`/api/i18n/lang`, but neither is on `AuthMiddleware`'s public allowlist, so both were already
401ing and degrading to localStorage. Unrouting changed nothing there.

Also surfaced and filed: **BladeWatch-jwko**, the vehicle action-token second factor was keyed
on `/api/vehicle/` and so had not fired for any real client since the Connect migration.

**Phase 3 — invert the handlers: 3 of 14.**

| Handler | Lines | State |
|---|---|---|
| GpsApiHandler | 82 | inverted |
| SafeLocationApiHandler | 131 | inverted |
| FormatStorageApiHandler | 227 | inverted |
| ExternalStorageApiHandler | 347 | todo |
| AudioTestApiHandler | 321 | todo |
| AuthApiHandler | 270 | todo |
| ModelsApiHandler | 264 | todo |
| NotificationApiHandler | 254 | todo |
| StreamingApiHandler | 357 | todo — keeps an OutputStream path for `/api/stream/*` binary |
| PerformanceApiHandler | 798 | todo |
| VehicleControlApiHandler | 1120 | todo |
| SurveillanceApiHandler | 1195 | todo |
| QualitySettingsApiHandler | 1306 | todo |
| RecordingsApiHandler | 1795 | todo — keeps `handleWithRange` for `/video/` and `/thumb/` |

`NoRestHandlerEntryPointsTest` is a RATCHET: it lists the inverted handlers and fails if any
regains an `OutputStream` entry point or is called back through `ConnectHandlerUtil.capture*`.
Add to that list as each one follows; never remove from it.

Two handlers will keep an `OutputStream` path on purpose — `StreamingApiHandler` and
`RecordingsApiHandler.handleWithRange` serve binary. Their JSON operations still invert; the
ratchet needs a per-handler exemption for those two rather than a blanket one.

## Pattern established

1. Replace `handle(method, path, body, OutputStream)` with one method per operation that RETURNS
   a `JSONObject` and takes its arguments directly (an id is a parameter, not a query-string
   fragment).
2. HTTP status codes that carried meaning become `ConnectException` codes — 400 →
   `invalid_argument`, 409 → `failed_precondition`, 500 → `internal`.
3. The Connect impl calls the method and rethrows `ConnectException` unchanged so the handler's
   own distinctions survive.

## Trap found doing this — read before inverting another handler

Inverting moves request parsing from the handler into the Connect impl, which reads fields by
STRING NAME off decoded JSON. A wrong name neither fails to compile nor throws: `optBoolean`
just returns its default. While inverting `SafeLocationApiHandler` the impl was written against
`setEnabled` while `ToggleSafeLocationsRequest` defines `enabled_set` (json `enabledSet`) — that
would have made every explicit toggle INVERT the current state instead of setting it, so the
safe-locations switch would have looked like it worked and done the opposite whenever it was
already in the requested state. `SafeLocationRequestShapeTest` now pins field names against the
proto. Do the same for every handler inverted from here.

comments.text:
## Phase 3 progress: 6 of 14

Inverted: `GpsApiHandler` (82), `SafeLocationApiHandler` (131), `FormatStorageApiHandler` (227),
`NotificationApiHandler` (254), `ModelsApiHandler` (264), `AudioTestApiHandler` (321).

Remaining, smallest first: `ExternalStorageApiHandler` (347), `StreamingApiHandler` (357),
`AuthApiHandler` (270), `PerformanceApiHandler` (798), `VehicleControlApiHandler` (1120),
`SurveillanceApiHandler` (1195), `QualitySettingsApiHandler` (1306), `RecordingsApiHandler` (1795).

`NoRestHandlerEntryPointsTest`'s `INVERTED` list is the ratchet — add to it as each lands.

## Status-code mapping, now consistent across the inverted six

| was | becomes |
|---|---|
| 400 | `invalid_argument` |
| 404 | `not_found` |
| 409 | `failed_precondition` |
| 503 / "not initialized" | `unavailable` |
| 500 | `internal` |

The Connect impl rethrows `ConnectException` unchanged and only maps a bare `Exception` to
`internal`, so a handler's own distinction is never flattened on the way out.

## Dead code found and removed while inverting

- `ModelsApiHandler.downloadStatus` / `refreshManifest`: no RPC, and their only caller was
  `assets/web/shared/ev-card-3d.js`, which NO served page loads (checked `hero.html` and
  `login.html` — the name survives only in a comment in `core.js`). Deleted rather than left as
  methods nothing can reach.
- `AudioTestApiHandler.getState` is in the same position but was KEPT and documented: it is the
  diagnostic that distinguishes "IVI multimedia service is down because the car is off" from
  "the speaker is broken", which the test alone cannot. Adding an RPC for it is smaller than
  reconstructing the probe later.

## Two handlers will keep an OutputStream path on purpose

`StreamingApiHandler` (`/api/stream/*` MJPEG and still frames) and
`RecordingsApiHandler.handleWithRange` (`/video/*`, `/thumb/*` byte ranges) serve BINARY to a
browser. Their JSON operations still invert; the ratchet needs a per-handler exemption for those
two rather than a blanket one, or it will demand something that cannot be done.

## Still true from the earlier note

Inverting moves request parsing into the Connect impl, which reads fields by STRING NAME. A wrong
name neither fails to compile nor throws — `optBoolean` returns its default. Check every field
against the proto and pin it, as `SafeLocationRequestShapeTest` does.

comments.author: Andrew Loable
comments.text:
## Phase 3 progress: 8 of 14, plus 3 documented exemptions

Inverted this pass: `ExternalStorageApiHandler` (347) and `PerformanceApiHandler` (798 -> 369).

Running total inverted: Gps, SafeLocation, FormatStorage, Notification, Models, AudioTest,
ExternalStorage, Performance.

Remaining to invert: `VehicleControlApiHandler` (1120), `SurveillanceApiHandler` (1195),
`QualitySettingsApiHandler` (1306), plus the JSON half of `RecordingsApiHandler` (1795).

## Exemptions are now explicit, with a disjointness guard

`NoRestHandlerEntryPointsTest.BINARY_OR_BOOTSTRAP` lists the three handlers that keep an
`OutputStream` entry point on purpose, each with its reason:

- `AuthApiHandler` — `/auth/status` and `/auth/token` are the PRE-AUTH bootstrap. `login.html`
  is plain HTML served before any Connect client exists, and it is the one page that must work
  when everything else is broken. Verified at the source: login.html fetches both.
  `AuthService.Login` exists for the SPA; the bootstrap stays HTTP.
- `StreamingApiHandler` — `/api/stream/*` MJPEG and still frames, consumed as image URLs.
- `RecordingsApiHandler` — `handleWithRange` for `/video/*` and `/thumb/*`. Its JSON operations
  still invert; only the range path stays.

`nothingIsBothInvertedAndExempt` pins the two lists disjoint, so a handler cannot be declared
inverted AND exempt at once — which would let the ratchet pass while the REST shape survived.

## PerformanceApiHandler: 798 -> 369 lines, most of it dead

Eleven handlers were unreachable once `/api/*` was unrouted and had no RPC: history, full,
connect, disconnect, heartbeat, start, stop, status, discover, soc-history, battery-health.
`connect`/`heartbeat`/`disconnect` were additionally SUPERSEDED in BladeWatch-qwqq, which
replaced them with `SystemService` methods calling `PerformanceMonitor` directly — so the
handler copies were duplicate logic, not just unreachable. Deleted, along with the now-unused
`parseIntQueryParam`.

`parking-delta` and `last-charge` took their window from a query string built onto a SYNTHETIC
url by the Connect impl — `"/api/performance/parking-delta?maxAgeHours=" + n` — which the
handler then parsed back out. Both are plain int arguments now.

## Mistake worth recording, because it nearly shipped

My first attempt at deleting the dead handlers used a span finder that walked BACKWARDS from a
method signature to the preceding blank line, to take its javadoc with it. On the first method
in the list that reached back past the end of `handleGetCurrent` — a LIVE method reached by
`GetPerformance` — and deleted it. The file still compiled as far as that script was concerned
because it never compiled; I only noticed because a grep for the surviving handlers came back
one short.

Redone with a span finder that goes from the signature to its own closing brace and NOTHING
further, plus an assertion listing all eight live methods by name that runs BEFORE the file is
written. Orphaned javadoc is then cleaned in a separate pass where the worst case is a stray
comment, not a deleted method. Anyone continuing this work should use the same shape: never let
a deletion script infer its own upper boundary.

comments.author: Andrew Loable
comments.text:
## Phase 3 progress: 10 of 14 (+3 exemptions), 1 left to invert

Inverted this pass: `VehicleControlApiHandler` (1120 -> 992) and `SurveillanceApiHandler`
(1195 -> 1156).

Remaining: `QualitySettingsApiHandler` (1306), plus the JSON half of `RecordingsApiHandler`
(1795, which keeps `handleWithRange` for the binary routes).

## Reachability regression caught before it shipped

`handleAdasInventory` was REST-only — the reference even said "no ConnectRPC/proto mapping
exists yet; add one in a follow-up if a client needs it". Unrouting `/api/*` would have DELETED
that diagnostic silently. Removing the REST surface IS that follow-up, so
`VehicleService.GetAdasInventory` was added and classified read-only in `VehicleActionGate`
(it probes, it does not actuate). The doc's REST-only row is gone and the note now records why
the RPC exists.

`VehicleControlApiHandler.handleIssueActionToken` went the other way: BladeWatch-jwko had
already put the issuer on `VehicleService.IssueActionToken`, so keeping the handler copy would
have been a SECOND implementation of a security primitive — which is how the gate it belongs to
drifted in the first place. Deleted.

## The snapshot is genuinely binary, and is now honest about it

`GetSnapshot` used to call a handler that wrote `HTTP/1.1 200 OK` + `Content-Type: image/jpeg`
+ the JPEG into a stream, which `ConnectHandlerUtil.captureBytes` then parsed back apart to
recover the payload. `getQuadrantSnapshotJpeg` returns `byte[]` now and the impl base64s it
straight into `image_jpeg`. Same wire result, no HTTP response modelled in memory.

## The ratchet guard was briefly useless — twice — and both are fixed

1. It matched the bare word `OutputStream`, so `SurveillanceApiHandler` failed it for using a
   `ByteArrayOutputStream` to encode a JPEG. That is an in-memory buffer with nothing to do with
   HTTP; leaving it would have pushed the next author into contorting working code.
2. My first tightening required `(` or `,` immediately before `OutputStream`, which does NOT
   match a `java.io.`-qualified parameter — so it caught NOTHING. Verified by mutation, which is
   the only reason it was noticed.

It now matches a PARAMETER whose type is an OutputStream however spelled, and the mutation check
runs all three spellings — bare, `java.io.`-qualified, and `final` — all CAUGHT. If you touch
this guard, re-run that three-way check; a guard that cannot fail is worse than no guard.

title: Five JSON REST endpoints are still called directly by Flutter and the web SPA; migrate them to ConnectRPC
description:
## Problem / context

`docs/http-api-reference.md` states that the REST surface "has **no first-party client left**
since Phase 4 deleted the in-app WebView: the Flutter in-car UI and the Angular SPA both use
Connect."

**That is false.** Both first-party clients still call REST directly, verified by reading the
call sites (not by grepping for strings):

| Client | Endpoint | Call site | Evidence it is real HTTP |
|---|---|---|---|
| Flutter | `POST /api/performance/connect` | `flutter_ui/lib/screens/diagnostics/performance_controller.dart:62` | `_postJson` at :106 — `http` send with `Authorization: Bearer <jwt>` |
| Flutter | `POST /api/performance/heartbeat` | same file :95 | same |
| Flutter | `POST /api/performance/disconnect` | same file :102 | same |
| Flutter | `GET`/`POST /api/settings/telemetry-overlay/fields` | `flutter_ui/lib/screens/settings/settings_recording_controller.dart:312, 351` | `_baseUrl.replace(path: ...)` + JWT header |
| Web SPA | `GET`/`POST /api/settings/status-overlay` | `web/src/app/pages/settings/settings.component.ts:412, 449` | `fetch(..., {credentials: 'same-origin'})` |
| Web SPA | `GET /api/stream/still` | `web/src/app/pages/live/live.component.ts:220` | image URL, same-origin cookie auth |

`performance_controller.dart` is the sharpest example: it calls `getPerformance` over ConnectRPC
and `connect`/`heartbeat`/`disconnect` over REST, **in the same class**.

## Scope — five endpoints, not six

`/api/stream/still` returns a binary JPEG consumed as an image URL. ConnectRPC is a poor fit for
that and `/video/*` and `/thumb/*` are in the same category — plain URLs a browser or player hits
directly, which the doc already gives as a reason the REST surface stays. **Leave those as HTTP.**

The five to migrate are the JSON ones:

1. `/api/performance/connect`
2. `/api/performance/heartbeat`
3. `/api/performance/disconnect`
4. `/api/settings/telemetry-overlay/fields` (GET + POST)
5. `/api/settings/status-overlay` (GET + POST)

## Important structural note — do NOT delete the REST handlers

The REST handlers are the **in-process implementation** that the Connect handlers wrap. See
`server/connect/impl/SystemServiceImpl.java`, where every method body is
`ConnectHandlerUtil.captureString(out -> SomeApiHandler.handle("GET", "/api/...", req, out))`.
The doc says this explicitly: "The Connect handlers wrap the same REST handlers to keep the two
surfaces in 1:1 parity, so the REST families below are the source of truth for behaviour."

So this issue is about moving the CLIENTS onto Connect, not about deleting the REST layer.
Whether the HTTP routes are then also unrouted is a second, separate decision — `/api/*` paths
may still be reachable by the legacy assets under `app/src/main/assets/web/shared/*.js`, which
must be checked before anything is unrouted.

## What to do

1. Read `server/connect/impl/SystemServiceImpl.java` end to end to learn the wrapping idiom
   before adding anything.
2. For each of the five, add a Connect method that wraps the existing REST handler exactly as the
   existing ones do. Add the proto messages in `proto/bladewatch/v1/` and regenerate both the
   Java and Dart clients.
3. Move the client call sites over. `performance_controller.dart` already holds a
   `_systemService` — use it rather than introducing a new dependency.
4. Update `docs/http-api-reference.md`: the Connect table, the REST families, and above all the
   false "no first-party client left" sentence. State plainly which routes remain HTTP and why.
5. `ApiReferenceCoversEveryRpcTest` pins the reference against the registered RPCs — expect it to
   fail until the doc is updated. That is the guard working.

## Constraints — do NOT change

- Do not delete the REST handlers. They are the implementation.
- Do not migrate `/api/stream/still`, `/video/*` or `/thumb/*` to Connect.
- Do not unroute any `/api/*` path in this issue without first checking the legacy assets under
  `app/src/main/assets/web/shared/*.js`.
- Do not change `AuthMiddleware` or the public allowlist.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All five JSON endpoints have Connect methods wrapping the existing REST handlers.
- [ ] No first-party client (`flutter_ui/lib/`, `web/src/`) calls `/api/*` for JSON any more;
      only the binary/streaming URLs remain.
- [ ] `docs/http-api-reference.md` no longer claims there is no first-party REST client, and
      names the routes that deliberately stay HTTP.
- [ ] `ApiReferenceCoversEveryRpcTest` passes.
- [ ] `./gradlew test koverVerify`, `flutter analyze`, `flutter test`, `web typecheck`,
      `typecheck:templates` and `test:unit` all pass.
- [ ] Verified on the head unit: the Diagnostics performance panel and both overlay settings
      screens still work end to end.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles
and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather
than guessing.
close_reason: Done. Seven new ConnectRPC methods replace the five JSON REST endpoints first-party clients still called directly: PerformanceConnect/Heartbeat/Disconnect on SystemService and GetStatusOverlay/SetStatusOverlay/GetTelemetryOverlayFields/SetTelemetryOverlayFields on SettingsService. Protos added and all four stub sets regenerated with buf (Java, Kotlin Connect, TypeScript, Dart); the pinned plugins held, so only new files appeared and no unrelated generated file churned. Server handlers call UnifiedConfigManager, the telemetry resolver and PerformanceMonitor DIRECTLY rather than wrapping a REST handler - the shape the rest of the server is converting to under BladeWatch-6mnq - except SetTelemetryOverlayFields, which still wraps the REST POST because its validation is non-trivial and belongs in that handler's own inversion. Clients migrated and their raw-HTTP plumbing DELETED rather than left dead: PerformanceController lost jwtSource/send/baseUrl, RecordingSettingsController lost jwtSource/baseUrl/getSender/postSender, and main.dart lost the app-lifetime RawHttpSender that existed only to stop the old REST path leaking a connection pool per visit. Their tests were rewritten to assert RPC calls instead of captured HTTP requests. Two extracted decisions: PerformanceClientId (3 tests) pins that the id the server registers is the one heartbeats carry - a mismatch would time the session out under an open panel - and a new test pins that an absent 'continuous' key leaves the saved field selection alone rather than clearing it. Mistakes made and corrected: two bulk regex/line edits mangled multi-line Dart and were reverted and redone by hand, and one new test passed for the wrong reason until I noticed poll() returns before heartbeating when GetPerformance is unstubbed. ApiReferenceCoversEveryRpcTest failed on the seven undocumented RPCs exactly as intended and the service table was updated. Remaining first-party /api/ call is /api/stream/still, a binary image URL that deliberately stays HTTP. All seven gates green. NOT verified on the car.

Phase 1 of BladeWatch-6mnq (remove the REST JSON API entirely). Nothing can be unrouted until
this lands, because these five are the last first-party REST callers.

title: SOH surface is dead: four stub handlers, three RPCs and a dashboard panel that can only fail or report unset
description:
## Problem / context

Battery State-of-Health estimation was removed server-side, but its ENTIRE user-facing surface
was left in place. Every handler in
`app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/PerformanceApiHandler.java` is now a stub
that can only fail or lie:

| Handler | Line | Behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| `handleSohStatus` | 547 | always `{"success": false, "error": "soh_not_initialized"}` |
| `handleSohGetNominal` | 715 | always `{"nominalKwh": null, "nominalSource": "unset"}` |
| `handleSohSetNominal` | 734 | always `{"success": false, "error": "soh_not_initialized"}` |
| `handleSohReset` | 568 | always `{"success": false, "error": "soh_not_initialized"}` |

Each carries the comment "Battery State-of-Health estimation has been removed."

Still wired to them:

- Three ConnectRPC methods — `GetSohStatus`, `GetSohNominal`, `SetSohNominal` — registered in
  `server/connect/impl/SystemServiceImpl.java:47-50` and 104-160, with full request reformatting
  logic for a body that is discarded.
- Generated protobuf types `GetSohStatusResponse` / `GetSohNominalResponse` in
  `app/src/main/java/net/bladewatch/app/grpc/v1/` and their Dart equivalents in
  `flutter_ui/lib/gen/bladewatch/v1/system.pb.dart`.
- A web dashboard panel: `web/src/app/pages/dashboard/dashboard.component.html:102-124` has a
  nominal-capacity input (`capInput`), a save path, and displays `nominalSource` and
  `nominalCapacityKwh`. `dashboard.component.ts:139` formats a value that is always 0.

So the owner can open the dashboard, type a pack capacity, save it, and get an error — while the
adjacent read-outs show "—" and "unset" permanently.

## Why this is being raised now

`NominalCapacityResolver` (BladeWatch-x4lf and follow-ups) established that nominal pack capacity
IS knowable on this car: the SDK field, the per-trim `models/manifest.json` catalogue, or a
validated derivation, resolved in that order. A user-set override is exactly the escape hatch
that would have made the original 5.2x energy inflation a one-field fix instead of a
database-forensics exercise — and `SetSohNominal` is that escape hatch, wired to nothing.

`GetSohNominal` hardcoding `"unset"` is also now demonstrably WRONG rather than merely empty:
the system resolves 18.3 kWh for this car and knows which source answered.

## The decision (do not skip this — it is why the issue exists)

This needs a developer decision BEFORE any code changes, because both directions are defensible
and they are opposites:

- **(a) Revive the override.** Add a user-set nominal capacity as priority 0 in
  `NominalCapacityResolver`, persisted through `UnifiedConfigManager`, and make `GetSohNominal`
  report the resolved value and its actual source. Keeps the dashboard panel; genuinely useful
  given the SDK field is untrustworthy (BladeWatch-phim) and a trim may not be in the catalogue.
- **(b) Delete the surface.** Remove the four stubs, the three RPC registrations, the dashboard
  panel and the generated types. Smaller codebase, one less thing that looks like it works.

Do not do half of each. Do not guess which one is wanted.

## What to do once the direction is chosen

1. Read all four stubs, `SystemServiceImpl:47-50` and 104-160, and the dashboard component
   before touching anything.
2. For (a): the override must be validated (the old REST comment specified an 8-120 kWh range)
   and must be testable as a pure decision in `NominalCapacityResolver`, tests first.
3. For (b): check `docs/http-api-reference.md` and `ApiReferenceCoversEveryRpcTest` — removing
   RPCs without updating the reference will fail that guard, which is the point of it.
4. Either way, `GetSohStatus` and `GetSohNominal` must stop disagreeing with each other about
   the same quantity.

## Constraints — do NOT change

- Do not make `NominalCapacityResolver` impure. An override is passed IN as a parameter like
  every other input; it does not read config itself.
- Do not remove the catalogue or the SoC-mirror rejection.
- Do not leave the dashboard panel wired to an endpoint that always errors. That is the current
  state and it is the thing being fixed.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A recorded developer decision, (a) or (b), on this issue before code changes.
- [ ] No endpoint reports "unset" for a quantity the system can resolve.
- [ ] `GetSohStatus` and `GetSohNominal` agree.
- [ ] No user-facing control remains wired to a handler that can only fail.
- [ ] If (a): the override is validated, has priority over the SDK field, and is covered by
      tests written before the code, each mutation-checked.
- [ ] If (b): `docs/http-api-reference.md` updated and `ApiReferenceCoversEveryRpcTest` passes.
- [ ] `./gradlew test koverVerify`, `flutter analyze`, `flutter test`, and the web typecheck /
      template / unit gates all pass.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles
and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather
than guessing.
close_reason: Done, direction (a) revive, per the developer decision. NominalCapacityResolver gained priority 0: a user-set override, validated to 8-120 kWh (the bounds the old REST contract advertised and that the dashboard input already enforced with min=8 max=120). 0 and NaN both mean unset and fall straight back to auto-detection. It outranks every other source because every other source is inference - the SDK field is a charging-session figure (phim), the catalogue is per-trim, and the derivation reads a channel that mirrors SoC on this car (x4lf) - while an explicit value is not. Persisted as vehicle.nominalKwhOverride through UnifiedConfigManager, next to modelId, because it describes the same thing. The resolver stays pure: the override is passed IN. Added sourceOf(), computed from the same inputs in the same order as resolve(), returning user/sdk/catalogue/derived/unset - GetSohNominal used to hardcode 'unset' while a capacity was demonstrably known, and a source derived anywhere else drifts from the value. A test pins that the two always agree. handleSohGetNominal, handleSohSetNominal and handleSohStatus now report the truth; nominalKwh stays JSON null when genuinely unknown rather than a fake zero, and an out-of-range override is refused with a new errors.soh_nominal_range key added to all 17 server-i18n catalogs (parity and JSON validity verified). SetSohNominal's Connect handler now surfaces success/nominalKwh/nominalSource instead of discarding the response. handleSohReset stays a stub and is documented as such - SoH ESTIMATION really is gone, there is no BYD-local degradation source, so displaySoh stays 0 and displaySource 'unavailable'; what was revived is nominal CAPACITY, which is what the dashboard read-outs actually consume. The web dashboard needed NO changes: it already called getSohStatus/setSohNominal with the right bounds - only the server was stubbed. 5 tests written first; three mutations each fail exactly their own test. Pre-existing resolve() call sites updated to pass overrideKwh = 0.0, preserving their intent; my bulk edit double-applied on three lines and was caught and fixed. Docs updated in http-api-reference.md and byd-integrations.md. NOT yet verified on the car.

title: ServiceLauncher.startLocationSidecarService still hand-rolls the shell-failure check BladeWatch-boat replaced
description:
## Problem / context

BladeWatch-boat fixed `SentryDaemon.restartLocationService`, which decided whether an `am` call
had failed with `result.contains("Error")` and so read a hard permission refusal as a success.
The fix introduced `ShellResultClassifier`.

**The same decision, over the same command, exists unfixed in a second place.**
`ServiceLauncher.startLocationSidecarService`
(`app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/launcher/ServiceLauncher.kt:268`) runs

    am start-foreground-service -n $PACKAGE_NAME/.services.LocationSidecarService 2>&1

and classifies the result with

    if (output.contains("Error") || output.contains("Exception")) {

Holes, all of which `ShellResultClassifier` already covers:

- **Empty output reports SUCCESS.** It calls `callback.onLaunched()`. A command that produced
  nothing at all did not demonstrably start anything. `ShellResultClassifier` treats null/blank
  as failure precisely for this.
- **Case-sensitive.** The platform writes both `Security exception:` and
  `java.lang.SecurityException` for one refusal; a denial carrying only the lower-case form
  is missed.
- **No `Permission Denial`, `Failure` or `Denied` marker.** A refusal without a Java stack trace
  reads as success.

This matters more here than in the daemon: the result drives `callback.onError` vs
`callback.onLaunched`, so a false success is reported to the caller and surfaces in the UI.

## What to do

1. Read `ShellResultClassifier.java` and `ShellResultClassifierTest.java` in full, then the
   `restartLocationService` call site in `SentryDaemon.java` that already uses it.
2. Replace the hand-rolled condition in `startLocationSidecarService` with
   `ShellResultClassifier.isFailure(output)`. Do not write a second, slightly different rule —
   two copies of this decision is how the first one drifted.
3. Check the rest of `ServiceLauncher.kt` for other hand-rolled shell-result checks and treat
   them the same way.
4. `ShellResultClassifier` is `public` in `net.bladewatch.app.daemon` and both files ship in the
   same APK, so no visibility change is needed. Confirm that rather than assuming it.

## Constraints — do NOT change

- Do not change `ShellResultClassifier`'s marker list or its null/blank handling to accommodate
  this call site. If a marker genuinely does not fit here, stop and ask.
- Do not change the `LaunchCallback` contract or when `onLaunched` / `onError` are invoked,
  beyond correcting which one a given output maps to.
- Do not change the `am` command itself.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A test written BEFORE the fix fails for the right reason.
- [ ] `startLocationSidecarService` classifies its result with `ShellResultClassifier`.
- [ ] Empty output is treated as a failure, not a launch.
- [ ] No second copy of the failure-marker logic exists anywhere in `ServiceLauncher.kt`.
- [ ] Mutation check: revert the call site to the old condition, confirm the new test fails,
      revert the mutation.
- [ ] `./gradlew test koverVerify` passes from the repo root.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles
and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather
than guessing.
close_reason: Fixed. startLocationSidecarService now classifies its result with ShellResultClassifier.isFailure, the same decision SentryDaemon.restartLocationService uses over the same am command. The old condition was case-sensitive, knew nothing of Permission Denial / Failure / Denied, and mapped EMPTY output to callback.onLaunched - a false success reported to the UI. Import added; confirmed ShellResultClassifier is public in net.bladewatch.app.daemon and both files ship in the same APK, so no visibility change was needed. Checked the rest of ServiceLauncher.kt as required: the only other substring test, at line 317, parses dumpsys output for a ServiceRecord presence probe - a different decision, correctly left alone. Guarded by ShellFailureCheckIsNotHandRolledTest, whose second assertion also forbids keeping a local marker test alongside the classifier; both failed before the fix and both fail again under the mutation that restores the old condition.

title: handleChargingCapacityChanged writes remainKwh with no SoC validation, unlike every other writer
description:
## Problem / context

`BydDataCollector.handleChargingCapacityChanged`
(`app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/byd/BydDataCollector.java:3620`) writes a
charging-capacity callback value straight into `remainKwh`:

    double capacity = BydDeviceHelper.getDoubleValue(args[0]);
    if (!Double.isNaN(capacity) && capacity >= 0 && capacity <= 200) {
        snapshot.set(snapshot.get().toBuilder().remainKwh(capacity).build());
    }

Two problems:

1. **No SoC cross-validation.** All three polled sources of `remainKwh` in `collectBodywork`
   (lines ~854, ~897, ~940) validate through `BydSignalRules.isRemainKwhConsistentWithSoc` or
   `isPlausibleRemainKwh` before writing, precisely so a flaky HAL reading cannot clobber a good
   cached value. The block comment at line ~838 explains at length why that matters. This
   callback has none of it, so it can overwrite a validated reading with an unvalidated one.
2. **The accepted window is `0..200`,** which admits the whole 0-100 percentage range. Whatever
   this callback actually carries, a value of 73 is accepted as "73 kWh".

Related but separate: the `onChargingCapacityChanged` handler at line 3421 writes the same event
into `chargingCapacityKwh` with a similarly unvalidated `0 < cap < 200` window. That field's
misuse is tracked in BladeWatch-phim; this issue is about the `remainKwh` writer at 3620.

## What to do

1. Read the whole `collectBodywork` remaining-energy block (roughly lines 836-950) FIRST. It
   documents hard-won behaviour — in particular why the priority reads are deliberately NOT
   gated on `Double.isNaN(b.remainKwh)`, and the Seal incident where two sources raced and
   last-writer-wins poisoned downstream auto-detection. Do not undo any of that.
2. Apply the same validation this file already uses for every other `remainKwh` writer. Reuse
   `BydSignalRules`; do not write a second, slightly different rule.
3. Read `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/byd/BydSignalRules.kt` and its existing
   tests before choosing which predicate to use.
4. Establish what this callback actually carries before deciding it is remaining energy at all.
   If it cannot be established, the safe change is to validate it like any other candidate
   reading and let the existing rules reject it.

## Constraints — do NOT change

- Do not change the polled priority chain or the `kwhWrittenThisCycle` logic.
- Do not re-add a `Double.isNaN(b.remainKwh)` gate to the priority-1/2 reads. That exact gate
  was the "Remaining kWh stuck at last seen value" bug.
- Do not change `BydSignalRules` thresholds without device evidence.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A test written BEFORE the fix, over the pure rule, fails for the right reason.
- [ ] The callback validates before writing, using `BydSignalRules`, not a new local rule.
- [ ] A value in the 0-100 percentage range that is inconsistent with current SoC is rejected.
- [ ] The polled priority chain is untouched.
- [ ] Mutation check: remove the new validation, confirm the new test fails, revert.
- [ ] `./gradlew test koverVerify` passes from the repo root.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles
and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather
than guessing.
close_reason: Fixed. handleChargingCapacityChanged now validates through BydSignalRules.isPlausibleRemainKwh plus isRemainKwhConsistentWithSoc before writing remainKwh, matching the three polled writers, instead of accepting anything in 0..200. The polled priority chain and kwhWrittenThisCycle logic are untouched, and no BydSignalRules threshold changed. Guarded by ChargingCapacityCallbackValidatedTest; both assertions failed before the fix and the mutation dropping the SoC cross-check fails the second one. Known residual, documented in the method comment and the test: a percentage that happens to equal the current SoC implies about 100 kWh, a real BYD pack size, so no SoC-only rule can reject it. That case is caught downstream by NominalCapacityResolver.looksLikeSocMirror rather than by teaching the collector a model-specific rule.

title: recordAccEvent stores the raw mirrored remainKwh channel, inflating the parking-delta kWh shown in the UI
description:
## Problem / context

`SocHistoryDatabase.recordAccEvent` (`app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/monitor/SocHistoryDatabase.java:1265`)
stores the RAW BYD channel straight into the `remaining_kwh` column:

    if (!Double.isNaN(data.remainKwh) && data.remainKwh > 0) {
        remainingKwh = data.remainKwh;
    }

Every other writer in this file goes through `VehicleDataMonitor.getBatteryRemainPowerKwh()`
(lines 408, 820, 1068), which validates the channel against SoC and nominal capacity and
substitutes a computed value when the BMS reading is inconsistent. This one call site bypasses
that entirely.

BladeWatch-x4lf established, from the device's own SoC history (963 rows, 2026-09-19), that
`remainKwh` on this car mirrors SoC percent 1:1 rather than reporting energy: soc=73/remain=72.9,
soc=77/remain=77.0, soc=79/remain=78.8. So this call site writes "72.9 kWh" into an ACC event
for a pack that holds 18.3 kWh.

## Impact — this is user-visible, not just a stored number

`ACC_EVENTS.remaining_kwh` is read by `getLastParkingDelta` (same file, ~line 1329), whose
`deltaKwh` output is surfaced over the `GetParkingDelta` RPC via
`app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/PerformanceApiHandler.java:377`. Because both
bracket samples come from the mirrored channel, `deltaKwh` equals `deltaSoc` numerically: the UI
reports "lost 3.2 kWh while parked" when the car lost 3.2 percentage points, about 0.59 kWh on
an 18.3 kWh pack — an overstatement of roughly 5.4x.

## What to do

1. Read `recordAccEvent` in full, then `getBatteryRemainPowerKwh` in
   `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/monitor/VehicleDataMonitor.kt` (around line 240),
   and the three other call sites listed above, so the change matches what they already do.
2. Route this call site through the same validated accessor as the others.
3. Preserve the method's existing policy, stated in its own comment: "Use SQL NULL when the value
   is missing or sentinel — never a fake zero." If no trustworthy energy value is available, the
   column must be SQL NULL, not 0.
4. `recordAccEvent` is called from `CameraDaemon.java:1942` with a live snapshot, so reading the
   monitor is consistent with the passed data. Confirm that for yourself rather than taking it
   on trust.
5. This method is best-effort and must never propagate an exception — keep that property.

## Constraints — do NOT change

- Do not change the `ACC_EVENTS` schema or the column's nullability.
- Do not change `getLastParkingDelta` or its RPC shape.
- Do not backfill or rewrite existing rows here; historical data is BladeWatch-aa3i.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A test written BEFORE the fix covers the decision: a mirrored reading must not be stored
      as energy. Extract the decision if the class cannot be built on the JVM, following
      `StorageManager.selectFilesToDelete` and `NominalCapacityResolver`.
- [ ] `recordAccEvent` no longer reads `data.remainKwh` directly.
- [ ] Missing or untrustworthy energy is written as SQL NULL, never 0.
- [ ] The method still swallows all exceptions.
- [ ] Mutation check: break the new guard, confirm the new test fails, revert.
- [ ] `./gradlew test koverVerify` passes from the repo root.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles
and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather
than guessing.
close_reason: Fixed. recordAccEvent now populates ACC_EVENTS.remaining_kwh from VehicleDataMonitor.getBatteryRemainPowerKwh(), the same validating accessor the other three writers in SocHistoryDatabase already use, instead of reading the raw channel. Verified the caller at CameraDaemon:1942 passes collector.getData(), the same AtomicReference snapshot that accessor reads, so the row stays internally consistent. The method still swallows all exceptions and still writes SQL NULL rather than a fake zero when no trustworthy value exists. Guarded by a new structural test, NoRawRemainKwhStoredAsEnergyTest, which reads the method body as source text because SocHistoryDatabase needs a live H2 database and the BYD HAL. Both assertions failed before the fix; the mutation restoring the raw read fails exactly the first one. The test strips comments before matching so that an explanation naming the field does not fail the build.

title: Decide and, if approved, migrate historical trip energy/cost figures inflated by the ~100 kWh capacity bug
description:
## Problem / context

Every trip recorded before BladeWatch-x4lf holds an energy, cost and efficiency figure that is
inflated by roughly 5.2x, and an efficiency score pinned at 0.

Cause (fixed in x4lf, see `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/monitor/NominalCapacityResolver.kt`
and the "Where nominal pack capacity comes from" section of `docs/byd-integrations.md`): the BYD
"remaining kWh" channel on this car mirrors SoC percent 1:1 rather than reporting energy, so the
old `remainKwh / (soc/100)` derivation produced ~100 kWh for a pack that is actually 18.3 kWh.
Measured off the device's own SoC history, 963 rows, 2026-09-19: soc=73/remain=72.9,
soc=77/remain=77.0, soc=79/remain=78.8.

The FIX is in and correct going forward. This issue is only about the already-stored rows, which
the fix deliberately does not touch. Migrating historical data is a judgement call — it rewrites
the owner's records — so it was left as a separate decision rather than bundled into the bug fix.

## Before writing any code

There is ALREADY a migration in this codebase for an earlier instance of this same class of bug.
Read it first and follow its shape rather than inventing a new one:

- `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/daemon/CameraDaemon.java` around line 586 — the
  marker-gated one-time consumption-bucket clear, gated on
  `/data/local/tmp/bladewatch_bucket_migration_done`.
- `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/monitor/SocHistoryDatabase.java` line 855,
  `fixStaleRemainingKwh(double)` — an idempotent single UPDATE over `SOC_HISTORY`.

Note both of these are gated on `nominalKwh > 0 && nominalKwh < 30.0` and had therefore NEVER
fired on this car (capacity used to resolve to ~100). After the x4lf fix they will fire on the
next daemon start. Confirm what they have already corrected BEFORE writing a third migration —
some of the work may already be done.

## What to decide, then do

1. Establish exactly which stored fields are wrong and where they live (trip records, their
   energy/cost/efficiency columns, any derived aggregates or cached summaries).
2. Decide with the developer whether to rewrite history at all, and if so whether to recompute
   from the stored SoC delta (preferred: the SoC readings themselves were never wrong, only the
   capacity they were multiplied by) or to scale by a constant factor (fragile — the bad
   capacity was not a single constant).
3. If it goes ahead: one-time, marker-gated, idempotent, and it must be safe to run on a
   database that has already been partly corrected.

## Constraints — do NOT change

- Do not change `NominalCapacityResolver` or `VehicleDataMonitor.getNominalCapacityKwh()`.
  The forward fix is verified; this issue is only about stored rows.
- Do not delete or recreate any database. A migration UPDATEs.
- Do not run a migration that is not marker-gated. An ungated rewrite that runs every startup
  will compound its own error.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A written statement of which stored fields are affected, and evidence for it (a query
      against the device's own database, not an assumption).
- [ ] An explicit developer decision recorded on this issue before any data is rewritten.
- [ ] If implemented: the migration is marker-gated, idempotent, and has a unit test over the
      pure recomputation that is mutation-checked.
- [ ] Running it twice produces the same result as running it once — demonstrated, not asserted.
- [ ] `./gradlew test koverVerify` passes from the repo root.
- [ ] Verified on the head unit: pick one known trip, record its figures before and after, and
      show the corrected energy is consistent with its SoC delta against an 18.3 kWh pack.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles
and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather
than guessing.
close_reason: Done, recommended approach. Evidence first, as the issue required: pulled the head unit's own trip database and queried it. 10 trips, every one damaged - KWH_START/KWH_END track SOC_START/SOC_END 1:1 exactly (trip 193: soc 77 to 71, kwh 77.0 to 71.3), giving efficiencies of 0.52 to 1.4 kWh/km and efficiency scores pinned at 0 on 8 of 10. Affected columns established as KWH_START, KWH_END, ENERGY_PER_KM, ELECTRIC_COST and TRIP_COST; FUEL_COST and LITRES_USED come from a counter this bug never touched and are carried through. Recompute from the SoC delta, not a scale factor, as recommended. New pure TripEnergyMigration mirrors TripRecord.getEnergyUsedKwh's tiers exactly - net remaining-energy delta, zero when the pack ended fuller, metered gross only when the net delta cannot answer - so repaired history sits on the same axis as everything recorded since the fix. Deliberate deviation from the stated acceptance criterion: it is gated on the DATA rather than a marker file. A row is repaired only while its energy still mirrors SoC, which it stops doing once repaired, so it is idempotent by construction AND survives a restore of the database alone, which a marker beside it would not. Demonstrated on the real pulled database: pass 1 corrected 10 rows, pass 2 corrected 0. Cross-validated against a channel the bug never touched: trip 193's repaired 0.1236 kWh/km against the 1.1 kWh its lifetime electricity counter recorded over 8.88 km, 0.2% apart - that agreement is the evidence 18.3 kWh is right. 9 tests written first, all using verbatim device rows; both energy tiers mutation-checked and each fails exactly its own test. Skips entirely when nominal capacity is unknown rather than rewriting against a guess, and any failure is caught so the daemon still comes up. NOT run on the car yet - the pulled copy was a simulation; the real repair runs at the next TripDatabase.init after deploy. Efficiency SCORES are not recomputed and remain as scored at the time.

title: SentryDaemon retries a forbidden BOOT_COMPLETED broadcast, misdetects it, and floods the 256KB log ring
description:
## Problem

`SentryDaemon`'s "Method 2" location restart sends a broadcast the OS can never permit, never
detects the failure, and dumps a 16-line stack trace every time it tries.

`SentryDaemon.java` around line 748:

```java
// Method 2: Send broadcast to boot receiver (backup)
String result2 = execShell("am broadcast -a android.intent.action.BOOT_COMPLETED " +
    "-n " + APP_PKG() + "/.receiver.LocationBootReceiver 2>&1");
log("Location restart (Method 2 - boot broadcast): " + result2);
if (result2.contains("Error") || result2.isEmpty()) {
    log("Location Monitor: WARN - Method 2 may have failed");
}
```

`android.intent.action.BOOT_COMPLETED` is a **protected broadcast**: only the system may send it.
The daemon runs as shell (uid 2000), so this is refused every single time, permanently. It is not
a transient condition that retrying can clear. Observed on the head unit 2026-09-19:

    SentryDaemon: Security exception: Permission Denial: not allowed to send broadcast
    android.intent.action.BOOT_COMPLETED from pid=22631, uid=2000
    java.lang.SecurityException: ...
      at com.android.server.am.ActivityManagerService.broadcastIntentLocked(...)
      ... 15 more frames

Three distinct defects here:

1. **The operation is impossible, not merely failing.** No amount of retrying will make a
   shell-uid process able to send a protected broadcast.

2. **The failure is not detected.** The guard tests `result2.contains("Error")`, but the actual
   output is `Broadcasting: Intent { ... }` followed by `Security exception: Permission Denial`
   and a `java.lang.SecurityException` trace. None of that contains the literal substring
   `Error`, and it is not empty - so the WARN never fires and the code proceeds as though
   Method 2 might have worked.

3. **It destroys observability.** 31 denials appeared in a single logcat buffer, each with a full
   stack trace - roughly 500 lines. This head unit's logcat ring is only 256KB. Combined with the
   BYD `mm-camera` noise, the buffer had already rotated past a drive that ended eight minutes
   earlier, so the logs needed to diagnose anything else were gone. This is the single largest
   BladeWatch-owned contributor to that rotation.

The duplicate-SentryDaemon race (companion issue) doubles the rate: the two instances fired this
0.67s apart.

## Fix

Stop attempting the impossible call, and make the remaining methods honest.

1. Remove the Method 2 `am broadcast` of `BOOT_COMPLETED` entirely, or gate it behind a
   one-time capability probe that never retries after the first denial. Prefer removal: an
   explicit component start (`am start -n`) is what this codebase already uses elsewhere to work
   around BYD's broadcast suppression, and `LocationBootReceiver` can be triggered that way or
   invoked directly if it is genuinely needed.
2. Fix the failure detection for whatever `execShell` calls remain: match on `Security exception`,
   `Permission Denial` and `Exception` as well, not just `Error`. A silent false success is worse
   than a loud failure.

Record in `docs/daemons-and-processes.md` that BOOT_COMPLETED cannot be sent from shell uid, so
nobody re-adds it. Note the related, already-documented fact that BOOT_COMPLETED never fires for
this app anyway on this head unit because of BYD's `ssc_skip` (see BladeWatch-5rew).

## Constraints

- Do NOT change `LocationBootReceiver` itself or its manifest registration - it is still a valid
  receiver for the real system broadcast.
- Do NOT replace the broadcast with a retry loop or a longer backoff; the operation is
  categorically forbidden, not slow.
- Do NOT silence the log by lowering its level and leaving the call in place - the wasted work and
  the false "may have worked" path remain.
- Do NOT touch Method 1 or the verification step after it without checking they are not affected
  by the same substring-matching flaw.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] No code path attempts `am broadcast -a android.intent.action.BOOT_COMPLETED`.
- [ ] Any remaining `execShell` result checks in the location-restart path treat
      `Security exception` / `Permission Denial` / `Exception` as failure.
- [ ] A JVM unit test covers the result-classification logic with the real observed output string
      as input, not a synthesised one - the current bug is precisely that the real output does not
      match the expected pattern. (See BladeWatch-t87k for the same class of mistake: a test fed a
      shape production never produces.)
- [ ] Mutation check: revert the classifier fix, confirm the test fails for the stated reason,
      re-apply, confirm it passes.
- [ ] `./gradlew test koverVerify` is BUILD SUCCESSFUL.
- [ ] Verified on the head unit: zero `Permission Denial ... BOOT_COMPLETED` lines in a fresh
      logcat buffer after a daemon restart.

Do not make mistakes. Read the whole location-restart method, not just Method 2, before editing.
Verify the build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is
ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
close_reason:
Fixed. Removed the BOOT_COMPLETED broadcast entirely and replaced the failure detection.

BOOT_COMPLETED is a protected broadcast; a shell-uid process can never send it, so "Method 2" failed every time, permanently. The guard tested result.contains("Error"), but the real output is "Broadcasting: Intent {...}" followed by "Security exception: Permission Denial" and a java.lang.SecurityException trace - no "Error" substring and not empty, so the failure was never detected and the code proceeded as though it might have worked.

Method 1 (am start-foreground-service) works from shell uid and remains the only path. LocationBootReceiver is untouched and is still valid for the real system broadcast; the comment records why the broadcast must not be reintroduced, including that BOOT_COMPLETED never reaches this app on this head unit anyway because of BYD's ssc_skip.

New pure ShellResultClassifier.isFailure() treats Error, Exception, Permission Denial, Failure, Denied (case-insensitively, so it catches both "Security exception" and "java.lang.SecurityException") and null/blank as failure. Wired into the surviving call.

The test asserts on the device output verbatim, not a synthesised approximation, and includes an explicit assertion that the old "Error" check would NOT have matched it - documenting why the bug survived review. That is the same lesson as BladeWatch-t87k, where a test fed a bare SecurityException that reflection never produces.

Mutation-checked: reverting the classifier to the Error-only list fails both "theRealPermissionDenialIsRecognisedAsFailure" and "ordinaryFailureShapesAreStillCaught".

Log-volume impact: 31 denials with 16-line stack traces per 256KB logcat buffer, doubled by the duplicate-daemon bug, are gone. Not yet confirmed on device.

title: Two SentryDaemon instances run concurrently - singleton check is a port ping, not a lock
description:
## Problem

Two full `SentryDaemon` instances run concurrently. Observed on the head unit 2026-09-19 after a
test drive:

    PID 9197 (PPID 1) -> 9244 sentry_daemon   ETIME 22:59
    PID 9347 (PPID 1) -> 9351 sentry_daemon   ETIME 22:58

Both reparented to init, started roughly one second apart, both alive and working.

`SentryDaemon.main` does have a guard (line ~85):

```java
// CRITICAL: Check if another instance is already running BEFORE doing anything else
if (isDaemonRunning()) {
    log("ERROR: Another SentryDaemon instance is already running. Exiting.");
    System.exit(1);
}
```

But `isDaemonRunning()` (line ~796) is a **liveness probe, not a mutual-exclusion primitive**:

```java
java.net.Socket socket = new java.net.Socket("127.0.0.1", CONTROL_PORT);
writer.println("PING");
String response = reader.readLine();
return response != null && response.contains("PONG");
```

It only answers true once the first instance has already bound `CONTROL_PORT` and is serving. Two
daemons launched within that startup window both probe, both get no PONG, both conclude they are
alone, and both proceed. Classic time-of-check/time-of-use race.

`CameraDaemon` does not have this problem because it uses an actual atomic primitive - a
`FileChannel.tryLock()` on `/data/local/tmp/camera_daemon.lock` (see `CameraDaemon.java` around
lines 240-267, including its note about `tryLock` on tmpfs).

## Consequences observed

- Every periodic SentryDaemon task runs twice. The location-restart cycle fired twice 0.67s apart
  (11:30:37.521 and 11:30:38.191), which is the direct cause of the doubled log spam tracked in
  the companion issue.
- Double CPU and double wakelock pressure on a parked car, which is exactly when battery matters.
- Whichever instance lost the control-port bind cannot be reached by the control protocol, so
  `isDaemonRunning()` and any operator tooling see only one of the two.

## Fix

Give `SentryDaemon` the same file-lock guard `CameraDaemon` already uses, held for process
lifetime, and keep the port ping only as a secondary/diagnostic signal. A lock file under
`/data/local/tmp` (e.g. `sentry_daemon.lock`) acquired with `FileChannel.tryLock()` before any
other startup work is the minimum that actually excludes.

Read `CameraDaemon`'s implementation first and follow it, including its handling of the tmpfs
`tryLock` caveat it documents - do not invent a second pattern.

## Constraints

- Do NOT remove `isDaemonRunning()`; `AccSentryDaemon` and the launcher scripts may call it. Change
  what gates startup, not the probe itself.
- Do NOT delete the lock file in the daemon-stop block in CLAUDE.md without adding it there
  deliberately - a stale lock that nothing clears would prevent the daemon starting at all.
- Do NOT widen the existing `rm -f /data/local/tmp/*sentry*.lock` glob in CLAUDE.md to cover
  anything else.
- Do NOT touch `/data/local/tmp/tor` in any cleanup path.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Launching `SentryDaemon` twice in rapid succession (within the control-port bind window)
      results in exactly one surviving process; the loser logs and exits non-zero.
- [ ] The lock is released/invalidated when the process dies, so a killed daemon can restart.
- [ ] A JVM unit test covers the decision logic (extract it as a pure/injected function if the
      lock itself cannot be exercised off-device - see `StorageManager.selectFilesToDelete` for the
      established pattern in this codebase).
- [ ] Mutation check: revert the guard, confirm the new test fails for the stated reason,
      re-apply, confirm it passes.
- [ ] `./gradlew test koverVerify` is BUILD SUCCESSFUL.
- [ ] Verified on the head unit: only one `sentry_daemon` in `ps -A`.

Do not make mistakes. Read `SentryDaemon.main`, `isDaemonRunning`, and `CameraDaemon`'s lock code in
full before editing. Verify the build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If
anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
close_reason:
Fixed. SentryDaemon now takes a real exclusive file lock before any other startup work.

isDaemonRunning() PINGs the control port, which only answers once an instance has already bound it. Two daemons launched inside that window both probed, both found nobody home, and both started - observed on the head unit as PIDs 9244 and 9351 one second apart, both alive, every periodic task running twice including the location-restart cycle 0.67s apart.

Per the issue's instruction not to invent a second pattern, CameraDaemon's device-learned stale-lock handling was extracted into a shared DaemonSingletonLock rather than duplicated: dead holder PID, our own PID (previous crash), and corrupt/empty content are all reclaimable, with the inode delay and retry, or a SIGKILLed daemon could never restart. The port ping is kept as a cheap first check and for external callers. The lock file is /data/local/tmp/sentry_daemon.lock, which the existing *sentry*.lock glob in CLAUDE.md's daemon-stop block already removes.

CameraDaemon was deliberately NOT migrated to the shared class in this change. Its lock works and is on the critical startup path; swapping it out carries regression risk that this bug fix does not need to take. Worth doing as its own verified change.

Worth recording how the test got there. My first test asserted through acquire() - first daemon wins, second refused - and it PASSED against a mutated "if (false)". It was passing for the wrong reason: two locks on one file inside a single JVM raise OverlappingFileLockException rather than returning null, so it exercised the exception path and never reached the live-vs-stale branch at all. I only caught it because the mutation check came back green when it should not have. The decision is now a pure static staleReason(pidStr, myPid, liveness) asserted directly, and the mutation that treats a live rival as stale (lock theft) correctly fails "aLiveRivalHoldingTheLockMeansWeMustExit".

Not yet confirmed on device - needs a deploy and a check that only one sentry_daemon appears in ps.

title: Docs still describe CameraProfileResolver after it was deleted as dead code
description: Regression introduced while closing the CameraProfileResolver dead-code decision. The class and its test were deleted, but docs/architecture.md (a full paragraph, including the now-nonexistent file path app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/camera/CameraProfileResolver.kt) and docs/features.md (a feature bullet) still describe it as shipping. This breaks the project Documentation Maintenance rule and leaves the architecture doc pointing at a file a fresh clone does not have. Fix: replace both passages with what actually happens today - configureDefaultCamera hardcodes cameraId=1/surfaceMode=0 and PanoCameraDiscovery corrects it at runtime by probing. Do not re-add the class. Acceptance: no tracked doc under docs/ references CameraProfileResolver or CameraProfileCatalog except the Overdrive evaluation files, which describe Overdrive's own classes and are untracked; the replacement text is factually true against GpuSurveillancePipeline.configureDefaultCamera; all gates pass. Do not make mistakes - read both passages and configureDefaultCamera in full before editing.
close_reason:
Fixed. This was a regression I introduced: when the decision came back to delete CameraProfileResolver as dead code, I removed the class and its test but never swept the docs, leaving docs/architecture.md describing it as shipping and pointing at a file path that no longer exists, plus a feature bullet in docs/features.md. That breaks the project Documentation Maintenance rule.

docs/features.md: removed the bullet entirely -- it described a capability that does not ship.

docs/architecture.md: replaced the paragraph with what the code actually does. Every factual claim in the replacement was verified against source rather than written from memory: configureDefaultCamera hardcodes setCameraId(1)/setCameraSurfaceMode(0) and sets setAutoProbeCameras(true) (GpuSurveillancePipeline lines 221-233); PanoCameraDiscovery exists at camera/PanoCameraDiscovery.java and is what corrects the tuple at runtime; vehicle.modelId is the 3D-appearance picker and defaults to "seal" for every install (UnifiedConfigManager.applyDefaults).

The replacement still names the class, deliberately, but as history -- "was written ... never wired into the pipeline and was removed as dead code" -- together with what making a fresh install stop assuming a Seal would actually require: a camera-profile setting distinct from vehicle.modelId. That is the useful part to leave behind for whoever picks it up, and it is honestly framed rather than describing absent code as present.

The remaining CameraProfileResolver-like names under docs/evaluations/ refer to Overdrive's own classes, not BladeWatch's, and those files are untracked.

Lesson worth carrying: deleting code needs a docs sweep in the same pass. A symbol-parity check over the docs is what caught this.

title: Storage confirm dialog uses a possibly-defunct BuildContext after the preview await
description:
## Problem

Both storage-limit confirmation flows call `showDialog` with a `State.context` that may already
be defunct, because there is no `mounted` check between the preview RPC `await` and the dialog.

Files (identical shape in both):
- `flutter_ui/lib/screens/settings/settings_recording_screen.dart` — `_applyStorage`, ~line 375
- `flutter_ui/lib/screens/surveillance/surveillance_screen.dart` — `_applyStorage`, ~line 461

```dart
Future<void> _applyStorage(AppLocalizations l10n, RecordingSettingsController c) async {
  final impact = await c.previewStorageLimitImpact();   // <-- async RPC
  if (impact != null) {
    final confirmed = await _confirmStorageLimitChange(l10n, impact);  // <-- showDialog(context: context)
    if (confirmed != true) return;
    if (!mounted) return;                               // <-- guards the WRONG side
  }
  ...
```

`_confirmStorageLimitChange` does `showDialog<bool>(context: context, ...)`. Reading
`State.context` after the widget is unmounted throws:

> This widget has been unmounted, so the State no longer has a context (and should be
> considered defunct).

If the owner leaves the Settings (or Surveillance) screen while `previewStorageLimitImpact()` is
still in flight, the awaited call returns into a disposed State and the dialog throws.

Note the existing `if (!mounted) return;` sits *after* the dialog, so the hazard was clearly
considered — it is just guarding the return path rather than the entry to the dialog.

## Why the analyzer does not catch it

`flutter_ui/analysis_options.yaml` includes `package:flutter_lints/flutter.yaml`, which enables
`use_build_context_synchronously`, and `flutter analyze` is clean. That is a **false negative,
not evidence of safety**: the lint's flow analysis is intra-procedural. The `await` happens in
`_applyStorage`, while `context` is read inside `_confirmStorageLimitChange`, a separate method
where it resolves to the `State` member rather than a captured local. The analyzer does not track
that across the call boundary.

## Reachability

Wider than it first looks. `previewStorageLimitImpact()` catches RPC failure and returns
`StorageLimitImpact.unknown()` — which is **non-null**, so the dialog is still shown on the slow
or failing-daemon path. A daemon that is unresponsive both lengthens the window and guarantees the
dialog is attempted at the end of it.

## Fix

Add a `mounted` check immediately after the preview await, before the dialog, in both files:

```dart
final impact = await c.previewStorageLimitImpact();
if (!mounted) return;
if (impact != null) {
  ...
```

## Constraints

- Do NOT remove the existing `if (!mounted) return;` after the dialog — it guards a different
  await and is still needed.
- Do NOT change the confirm/cancel semantics: `confirmed != true` must continue to cover both
  an explicit cancel and a barrier/back dismissal (null), leaving `SetStorageSettings` uncalled.
- Do NOT change `previewStorageLimitImpact`'s contract (null = nothing to confirm,
  `unknown()` = confirm anyway).
- Apply the same fix to both screens; they are deliberately parallel implementations.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Neither `_applyStorage` reaches `showDialog` without a `mounted` check after the preview
      await.
- [ ] A widget test that disposes the screen while the preview future is still pending completes
      without throwing, and does not call `applyChanges`.
- [ ] Existing behaviour unchanged when the screen stays mounted: null impact applies directly,
      non-null impact shows the dialog, cancel/dismiss leaves `SetStorageSettings` uncalled.
- [ ] `cd flutter_ui && flutter analyze && flutter test` passes, and Dart coverage stays at or
      above the 99% floor (`tools/check_flutter_coverage.sh`).

Note `flutter test` uses a fixed-width placeholder font, so do not add any text-fit or overflow
assertion — measure those on the head unit instead (see CLAUDE.md, Testing).

Do not make mistakes. Read both `_applyStorage` methods and both `_confirmStorageLimitChange`
methods in full before editing. Verify all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is
ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
close_reason:
Fixed in both screens. Added a mounted check immediately after the preview await, before the confirmation dialog.

_applyStorage awaited previewStorageLimitImpact and then called _confirmStorageLimitChange, which does showDialog(context: State.context). Reading that context after the widget is unmounted throws. If the owner left the screen while the preview RPC was in flight, the awaited call returned into a disposed State and the dialog threw. The existing mounted check sat after the dialog, guarding the return path rather than entry to it.

Not caught by use_build_context_synchronously despite flutter_lints enabling it: the lint is intra-procedural, and the await is in _applyStorage while the context read is in _confirmStorageLimitChange, so the analyzer does not follow it across the call. flutter analyze being clean was a false negative, not evidence of safety.

Reachability is wider than it looks because previewStorageLimitImpact turns an RPC failure into a non-null unknown() impact, so the dialog is attempted even on the slow or failing-daemon path that widens the window.

Reproduced with a real test rather than argued: added stubPending to FakeRpcClient (a Completer-backed stub, since every other stub resolves on the next microtask and cannot land in that window), then a widget test that taps Apply, disposes the screen while the preview is pending, completes it, and asserts no exception, no dialog, and no SetStorageSettings call. Before the fix it failed with the exact stack -- State.context at framework.dart:958 from _confirmStorageLimitChange line 392, called from _applyStorage line 378 across an asynchronous suspension. Passes after, and fails again when the guard is mutated out.

Both screens fixed identically; they are deliberately parallel implementations. Gates green, Dart coverage 99.51% on 1574 tests.

title: Storage limit preview uses the raw value while apply clamps, so they disagree
description:
## Problem

The storage-limit preview computes its impact from the **raw requested value**, while applying
the limit **clamps** it. For any out-of-range request the two disagree, and they disagree in the
most alarming possible direction: the confirmation dialog says every recording will be deleted
when applying it would delete none.

Files:
- `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/storage/StorageManager.java` — `previewLimitChange`
  (around line 2111), `setRecordingsLimitMb` / `setSurveillanceLimitMb` (around line 1253).
- `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/QualitySettingsApiHandler.java` —
  `handleStorageSettingsPost` and `handlePreviewStorageLimitChange`.

The setters clamp:

```java
public void setRecordingsLimitMb(long limitMb) {
```
