Noted that the call goes out over the car's own connection, not through Tor. Offline: retryOnConnectionFailure(false), no queue, no background attempts - correct for this device; on-demand is worth shipping degraded, scheduled insights are not, and scheduled generation is blocked anyway because Overdrive implements presets as ordinary time automations and BladeWatch has no engine. TFLite/YOLO assessed and called a red herring in three sentences rather than padded. Shippable subset stated: on-demand text only, five safe context modes, five of eleven rows Skipped.

title: Evaluate Overdrive's automation engine for BladeWatch
description:
## Your scope: automations

Overdrive's programmable automation engine, introduced around alpha-v33 ("Programmable
Automations, Full ADAS Control & More Ways to React") and extended through v36.

Features to evaluate (confirm and extend from the catalogue task's output):

- The automation engine itself: triggers, conditions, actions.
- If / Else conditions, and the comparison operators added in v35.1 (the full set
  of >=, <=, != rather than the few originally exposed).
- Variables in automations, and using variables inside toast/dialog content (v36.6).
- Keymapping: binding physical or on-screen keys to actions, including the v36.6
  temperature up/down by 1 step.
- "Show Toast" and "Show Dialog" actions (v34) - note these overlap with the
  remote-communication domain; evaluate them as AUTOMATION ACTIONS here and leave the
  remote-messaging transport to that task. Say in your notes where you drew the line.
- Community automations: downloading shared automations, the name shown alongside
  (v36.6), and the "Mine" badge for owners (v34.5).

## Specific things to determine

- Does BladeWatch have ANY automation concept today? Check `docs/features.md` and the
  daemon sources. If the answer is no, this is the largest single feature in the epic
  and your effort estimates must reflect building an engine, not porting rules.
- Which triggers would even be available on a DiLink v3 head unit through the LOCAL
  SDK only? An automation engine is worth exactly as many triggers as it can observe.
  Cross-check against `docs/byd-integrations.md` and `BydDataCollector.java`.
- Community automation sharing implies a server and user-submitted content. What would
  that mean for BladeWatch, which has no backend? Treat "needs a backend BladeWatch
  does not have" as a first-class blocker, not a detail.
- Where would automations live: the daemon (survives UI death, no Activity lifecycle)
  or the Flutter UI? Say which and why - this is the architectural question the
  implementation task will inherit.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `docs/evaluations/overdrive-automations.md` exists in the shared format.
- [ ] Every feature above has a row, with an honest Present/Partial/Absent assessment
      backed by a file or docs reference.
- [ ] The available-triggers question is answered concretely, with a list.
- [ ] The engine-placement question (daemon vs Flutter) has a recommendation.
- [ ] Community sharing is assessed including its backend implication.
- [ ] No other file is created or modified; nothing staged or committed.

## Where this lives in the Overdrive source

Read these packages under `app/src/main/java/com/overdrive/app/` in your clone:
`automation` (78 files), `community` (5). Start at the automation engine entry point and the rule/trigger/action model.

Fill the "Overdrive source" column of your table from what you actually read,
not from the release notes. An effort estimate made without opening the code is a
guess and must be labelled as one.

## Shared context - read this before anything else

BladeWatch was FORKED from Overdrive and rebranded (see the Project Overview in
CLAUDE.md). Overdrive has kept shipping since; this epic evaluates what it added that
BladeWatch should take back.

### The full Overdrive SOURCE is public - use it, do not evaluate from release notes alone

https://github.com/yash-srivastava/Overdrive-release - branch `main`. Despite the
repository name it is NOT release-only: it contains the complete Android project
(848 .java, 245 .kt, 358 .xml, plus `stubs-bydauto/`, `gradle/`, `settings.gradle.kts`).
Clone it ONCE into a scratch directory OUTSIDE the BladeWatch repository and read the
real implementation:

    git clone https://github.com/yash-srivastava/Overdrive-release /tmp/overdrive-eval

Source layout, under `app/src/main/java/com/overdrive/app/` (file counts as of
2026-09-14, useful for sizing before you read):

    ui 104   automation 78   byd 70   server 65   roadsense 47   surveillance 47
    daemon 38   camera 35   telegram 33   monitor 30   navmap 24   notifications 20
    trips 19   services 16   util 15   launcher 14   communication 10   mqtt 10
    onboarding 10   geo 9   logging 9   charging 8   config 8   storage 7   genai 6
    overlay 6   community 5   power 5   receiver 5   telemetry 5   telenav 5
    abrp 4   auth 4   proximity 4   recording 4   remote 4   updater 3   ai 2

Supporting material in the same repo:

- Release notes: `gh api repos/yash-srivastava/Overdrive-release/releases` - 23
  releases, alpha-v33.1 through alpha-v44.2 (latest 2026-08-29). The English
  user-facing descriptions.
- `CHANGELOG.md` - a far more technical dev log, WRITTEN IN ITALIAN, naming actual
  classes and files, covering work absent from the English notes. Do not skip it
  because of the language.
- `Readme.md`, `DILINK5_CAMERA_CAPTURE_DISCOVERY.md`, `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`.

There is also a 75 MB APK attached to each release. You do not need it - you have the
source. Do not decompile it.

LICENSING: Overdrive is MIT, Copyright (c) 2026 Yash Srivastava. Porting code is
permitted WITH attribution, and your evaluation must record that obligation for
anything you recommend carrying over.

### Read the source, but do not copy it into BladeWatch during this epic

These are EVALUATION tasks. Reading Overdrive's implementation is how you produce an
honest effort estimate. Copying files into the BladeWatch tree is implementation, and
it happens later, after the developer decides. Keep the clone outside the repo.

## Six filters that kill features before you evaluate them further

Apply these FIRST to every feature; most of the value of this task is an honest "not
portable" with the reason.

1. BYD CLOUD IS GONE FROM BLADEWATCH. The whole `byd/cloud/` package - client, MQTT
   subscriber, Bangcle white-box crypto - was deleted in commit 61b4d7f.
   `VehicleCommandRouter.Path` is now `{SDK, NONE}`, and commands that only ever had a
   cloud implementation (Lock, Unlock, Flash, FindCar, SetBatteryHeat, charging
   schedule) resolve to NOT_SUPPORTED. Overdrive still has that code - its `mqtt`
   package and `app/src/main/assets/byd/bangcle_tables.bin` are exactly what BladeWatch
   deleted. Features that need BYD Cloud are NOT portable as they stand. Flag them as
   blocked. Do NOT propose restoring the cloud client as part of an evaluation.
2. HARDWARE GENERATION. BladeWatch targets DiLink v3 ONLY: arm64-v8a, Android 10 /
   API 29, NOT rooted (no su, ro.secure=1, ro.build.type=user). Much of Overdrive's
   recent work targets DiLink 4 and DiLink 5 (BYD Sealion 7, Android 11 Automotive) -
   the qcarcam bridge, `assets/dilink5/fast_cam_capture`, 4K HEVC dual-pipeline
   recording, CarBodyManager.getShiftMode(). Those do not apply to a DiLink v3 head
   unit. Say so plainly rather than describing them as available.
3. DAEMONS BLADEWATCH DELIBERATELY REMOVED. Cloudflared, Tailscale, sing-box and the
   Telegram bot daemon were all removed from BladeWatch; only a tunnel daemon remains
   (zrok today, being replaced by Tor - see the other epic). Overdrive still has a
   33-file `telegram` package and sing-box proxy routing. If a feature depends on one
   of those, say so explicitly; recommending it means arguing to re-add a removed
   subsystem, which needs its own justification.
4. UI CODE DOES NOT PORT. Overdrive's `ui` package is 104 files of native Android
   Activities/Fragments with XML layouts. BladeWatch's in-car UI was rebuilt in
   FLUTTER after the fork (`flutter_ui/`, Dart, plain ChangeNotifier controllers).
   Layout and interaction IDEAS transfer; the code does not. Size UI work as a
   reimplementation, never as a copy.
5. PRIVILEGE. BladeWatch reaches shell UID through ADB on 127.0.0.1:5555
   (AdbShellExecutor -> dadb), 168 call sites. It is not root. Anything needing root,
   a system signature, or a BYD-signed process is out.
6. PHYSICAL SAFETY. BYD vehicle control APIs actuate real hardware. CLAUDE.md requires
   conservative treatment. Rate any feature that actuates the car accordingly.

## What BladeWatch already has

Read `docs/features.md` before writing a single line - its sections are Recording,
Surveillance and Sentry Mode, Proximity Recording, Location and GPS, Live Streaming,
Embedded Web UI and PWA, In-Car UI (Flutter), BYD Local Telemetry, Local Vehicle
Control, Trips and Analytics, Performance and Telemetry, Notifications and Push,
Remote Access, Updates, Diagnostics and Logs, ConnectRPC API. Also read
`docs/architecture.md` and `docs/byd-integrations.md`.

Because BladeWatch is a FORK, many Overdrive classes still have a BladeWatch
counterpart under a renamed package (`com.overdrive.app.*` became
`net.bladewatch.app.*` / `com.loabletech.bladewatch.*`). For every feature, check
whether BladeWatch has a diverged version of the same class before concluding it is
absent - `git log` and a class-name search across both trees is faster than reading.

`/Volumes/mandark-1Tb/projects/loabletech/BladeWatch-Legacy` is the old BladeWatch,
kept for reference only. Read it if it helps; NEVER modify it.

## Deliverable - identical shape for every evaluation task

Create exactly one file: `docs/evaluations/overdrive-<your-domain-slug>.md`.
Nothing else. No feature code, no refactors, no dependency changes.

The file opens with a two-sentence summary, then ONE TABLE with a row per feature:

| Feature | Overdrive version | Overdrive source | BladeWatch today | Blocked by | Effort | Recommendation |

- Overdrive source: the package or the two or three classes that implement it, so the
  implementation task later does not start from zero. This column is why you cloned
  the repo; an empty one means you evaluated from release notes.
- BladeWatch today: one of Present / Partial / Absent, with a file or docs reference
  proving it. "Partial" must say what is missing.
- Blocked by: none, or the specific filter above (BYD Cloud, DiLink 4/5, removed
  daemon, UI rewrite, privilege, safety), or a concrete technical blocker.
- Effort: S (under a day) / M (a few days) / L (a week or more), with one clause of
  justification. Base it on the code you actually read. A guess you label as a guess
  is fine; a confident number you cannot support is not.
- Recommendation: Port / Adapt / Skip, and one sentence of why. "Adapt" means the
  idea is worth having but Overdrive's implementation does not fit BladeWatch.

Below the table, add a short "Notes and open questions" section for anything a human
needs to decide. Be blunt about what you could not determine - an honest unknown is
worth more than a plausible guess, because this document is what the implementation
decision gets made from.

## Constraints for every task in this epic

- EVALUATION ONLY. Implementation happens later, after the developer picks from the
  shortlist. Do not write feature code, do not add dependencies, do not copy Overdrive
  files into the BladeWatch tree, do not file implementation issues (the synthesis
  task does that, after the decision).
- Do not recommend a feature you have not checked against `docs/features.md` and the
  BladeWatch source. Proposing something BladeWatch already ships is the most likely
  failure mode here.
- Keep the Overdrive clone outside the BladeWatch repository.
- Do not stage or commit anything (see the Git Workflow section of CLAUDE.md).

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before writing. This document is what the implementation decision gets made from, so an inaccurate "BladeWatch today" column is worse than no document at all - verify every claim against the code. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
close_reason: Wrote docs/evaluations/overdrive-automations.md. BladeWatch has NO automation concept anywhere - no automation package, nothing in flutter_ui, web or proto - so every estimate is for building an engine: Overdrive's is 17,525 lines across 74 files plus 2,315 lines of HTTP handlers and 1,053 of community client. The trigger question is answered concretely with a signal-by-signal table: Overdrive registers 60 signals, BladeWatch already collects 102 telemetry fields, and about 45 of the 60 are observable today with no new telemetry work - the sensing layer is not the obstacle, the engine is. The 15 unavailable ones split into absent subsystems (mqtt, bluetooth, weather, telephony), unimplemented sensor reads (occupant, cpd, ambient, energyRegen) and three ADAS alert signals that the vehicle/ADAS evaluation showed rest on unconfirmed fabricated register ids. Engine placement: the DAEMON, not Flutter - actuation needs UID 2000, rules must outlive the Activity given ssc_skip and the missing BOOT_COMPLETED, and all 45 signals are already daemon-side; Flutter authors and displays only, over a new ConnectRPC service. Community sharing is a Skip: it needs a Cloudflare Worker plus D1 that BladeWatch does not have, the referenced community-edge backend directory is NOT present in the repo despite being called open-source, and adopting it means hosting user content, moderating reports and sending a persistent deviceId to a third party. Its no-shell plus import-as-disabled safety model is worth keeping if sharing is ever built. Key mapping is cheaper than expected because BladeWatch already ships KeepAliveAccessibilityService from the fork and can enable it via WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS - but its accessibility_service_config.xml declares zero event types, which Overdrive proved on a real DiLink unit means onKeyEvent is never dispatched; the fix is documented. Noted where I drew the toast/dialog line against the remote-communication task, and labelled the two large files I sized rather than read.

title: Evaluate Overdrive features for integration into BladeWatch
description:
## Goal

Evaluate everything Overdrive has shipped since BladeWatch forked from it, and decide
which features are worth bringing across. EVALUATION ONLY - no implementation happens
under this epic. Implementation issues get written later, against whatever the
developer picks from the final shortlist.

## Why now

BladeWatch was forked from Overdrive and rebranded (Project Overview, CLAUDE.md).
Overdrive has since shipped 23 releases, roughly alpha-v33 through alpha-v44.2 (latest
2026-08-29), adding a programmable automation engine, an AI assistant, remote voice
through the car speakers, a deterrent screen, projection to the driver cluster,
charging tariffs and a 47-file RoadSense subsystem that its release notes barely
mention. Nobody has looked at that list against BladeWatch's current feature set.

## The source is public and MIT licensed

https://github.com/yash-srivastava/Overdrive-release - branch `main` holds the complete
Android project (848 .java, 245 .kt), not just releases. MIT, Copyright (c) 2026 Yash
Srivastava, so porting is permitted with attribution. Every child task reads the real
code; none of them evaluates from release notes alone.

## Structure

- One catalogue task runs first and builds the shared feature inventory, so eight
  sibling agents do not each re-read 23 releases and 2000 files.
- Eight domain tasks then evaluate in parallel: automations, ai-assistant,
  remote-communication, surveillance, vehicle-adas, camera-ux, trips-energy,
  roadsense-nav.
- One synthesis task runs last and produces a single ranked shortlist.

Each domain task writes exactly one document to `docs/evaluations/`, all in the same
format, so the synthesis is mechanical rather than a rewrite.

## What a good outcome looks like

A short, honest shortlist. Most of these features will turn out to be blocked - by the
BYD cloud path BladeWatch deleted in 61b4d7f, by DiLink 4/5 hardware BladeWatch does
not target, by subsystems BladeWatch deliberately removed, or by the fact that
Overdrive's UI is native Android while BladeWatch's is Flutter. Recording WHY something
is blocked is as valuable as recommending something: it stops the same feature being
re-proposed in six months.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before writing. If anything is
ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
close_reason: All ten children closed. Produced docs/evaluations/ containing the shared release catalogue, eight domain evaluations and a ranked integration shortlist. Outcome: 17 Port/Adapt rows, a Blocked section grouped by reason so ruled-out features are not re-proposed, a Top 5 with concrete first steps, and eight open questions for the developer. No implementation issues filed by design - the developer picks from the shortlist first, then issues get written against that decision.

title: Docs sweep: remaining nine docs, stray zrok comments, and a no-zrok guard test
description:
## Context

Final sweep of the zrok-to-Tor migration: the nine remaining documents, the stray
comments left in code that the earlier tasks did not own, the web end-to-end test
config, and a permanent guard test so zrok cannot creep back in.

Do this LAST, after the code tasks and the core-docs task are closed.

## TDD - required, write the guard test first

Write the guard BEFORE doing any of the cleanup, run it, and SEE IT FAIL. That
failure list IS your worklist for this task, and it is more trustworthy than the
inventory below because it reads the tree as it actually is.

Add a structural JVM test next to the existing structural guards
`app/src/test/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ServiceHostManifestTest` and
`NoSelfLaunchIntentTest` (read one first for house style - they scan files on disk
rather than calling into app code). The test asserts that no tracked file in the
repository contains the string "zrok", case-insensitive, with these exclusions only:

- `.beads/` (the issue tracker stores this issue's own text, which necessarily says
  zrok), `.git/`, any build output directory, `node_modules/`.
- At most ONE allowed occurrence in source: a single comment recording the removal,
  the same way the sing-box removal is recorded in `AdbDaemonLauncher.kt`. If you
  allow it, pin the test to that exact file so a second occurrence anywhere still
  fails.

CRITICAL - Gradle up-to-date blindness, which has bitten this project before (see
the Testing section of CLAUDE.md): a test that reads files not on the test classpath
will NOT re-run when those files change, so it can pass against a tree full of
violations. Declare the scanned directories as explicit test `inputs` in
`app/build.gradle.kts` - that file already does exactly this for AndroidManifest.xml
and src/main/java. Prove the guard can fail: add the word zrok to a scratch file in
the tree, run the test, confirm it FAILS rather than reporting UP-TO-DATE, then
remove the scratch file. A guard that cannot fail is worse than no guard.

Then make it green by doing the cleanup below.

## Inventory - the files that must change

Documentation:
- `docs/README.md` line 11 ("the Zrok tunnel process") and line 21.
- `docs/build-and-operations.md` line 71 (ZrokController), line 95 (libzrok.so
  packaged in jniLibs and extracted at runtime - this is now a build-time
  verified download, so the packaging story changed too), line 108, line 403
  ("Zrok Token was already implemented"), line 660 (/data/local/tmp/zrok.log).
- `docs/data-flow-and-storage.md` lines 248-254 (the Zrok paths block:
  /data/local/tmp/zrok, zrok.log, .zrok/environment.json, .zrok/unique_name) and
  line 378. Replace with the tor paths: /data/local/tmp/tor/torrc,
  /data/local/tmp/tor/data, /data/local/tmp/tor/hs, /data/local/tmp/tor.log.
  Mark hs/ as containing the permanent secret identity key.
- `docs/features.md` lines 249-251 (public/reserved share, "Zrok is designed to front
  the authenticated local web server") and line 285 (source link to ZrokLauncher.kt,
  which no longer exists).
- `docs/http-api-reference.md` line 448 ("tunnel URL from the Zrok launcher").
- `docs/ipc-auth-and-secrets.md` - 9 references, lines 166-179 (how the Flutter APK
  gets the tunnel URL, and the argv[0]/nice-name basename comparison), line 201 and
  lines 210-216 (the ZROK_TUNNEL toggle allow-list). This document explains a real
  security boundary - update it carefully and make sure it matches the code that
  actually shipped, including the new bootstrap gate on tunnelStatus.
- `docs/log-files.md` line 14 (the /data/local/tmp/zrok.log table row) - becomes
  /data/local/tmp/tor.log.
- `docs/secret-custody-design.md` line 13: the list of secrets says "device token,
  zrok enable token, BYD cloud creds". The zrok enable token no longer exists; the
  BYD cloud path was already deleted in commit 61b4d7f, so check that claim too while
  you are there. Add the onion service key as a secret that lives OUTSIDE the secrets
  JSON, in the hidden-service directory at mode 600.
- `docs/security-hardening-assessment.md` line 66 ("zrokToken" as an example
  sensitive key), line 77 (certificate pinning: "Zrok/Cloudflare rotate certs"),
  line 151 (the table row claiming "Zrok tunnel | TLS | Zrok provides end-to-end").
  Line 151 needs real thought rather than a find-and-replace: Tor gives end-to-end
  encryption and authenticates the service by its key, so the security property is
  arguably stronger, but it is not TLS and there is no certificate to pin. Describe
  what is actually true.

Code comments and test config the earlier tasks did not own:
- `web/src/app/shared/header/header.component.ts` line 11 - a comment saying the
  reachable origin is "the zrok tunnel host or the LAN IP".
- `web/e2e/README.md` lines 4, 19, 35 - the example target URL and instructions.
- `web/e2e/.env.example` lines 5 and 8 - the example BLADEWATCH_E2E_URL.
  NOTE: `web/e2e/.env` also holds a real zrok URL but is UNTRACKED, so leave it
  alone; do not add it to git and do not copy its value anywhere.

## Constraints

- Do not paste any real onion address into any file. A working onion URL is a
  capability that grants network access to a real car. Use an obviously fake
  placeholder in every example, and say in the text that it is a placeholder.
- Do not change behaviour. This is documentation, comments and one guard test.
- Do not delete `docs/webview-migration.md` or update it - CLAUDE.md marks it
  retired.
- If you find zrok references in files not listed above, fix them too; the inventory
  was taken before the code tasks landed and may be stale. The guard test is the
  authority.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The guard test exists, you observed it FAIL before the cleanup and pass after,
      and you proved it is not up-to-date-blind by making it fail on a scratch file.
- [ ] `grep -ril zrok . --exclude-dir=.git --exclude-dir=.beads --exclude-dir=build --exclude-dir=node_modules`
      returns at most the single allowed removal-record comment.
- [ ] Every doc listed above describes Tor accurately and its source links resolve.
- [ ] docs/security-hardening-assessment.md line 151 makes a true claim about Tor's
      security property rather than a renamed TLS claim.
- [ ] No real onion address appears anywhere in the repo.
- [ ] `./gradlew test` and `./gradlew koverVerify` pass.
- [ ] No files are staged or committed by you.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build
compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous,
stop and ask rather than guessing.
close_reason: Guard test written FIRST (NoRemovedTunnelReferencesTest) and its failure list became the worklist - which was the right call, because it found four categories the inventory missed entirely: app/src/main/assets/web/i18n/*.json (3 dead keys across 17 locales, referenced by nothing after the Angular rewrite - deleted), assets/web/shared/core.js and local/sw.js, res/values/themes_bladewatch.xml, and app/build.gradle.kts itself. Cleaned all nine remaining docs plus web/e2e and the stray comments. docs/security-hardening-assessment.md line 151 was NOT renamed but rewritten: it claimed TLS, and the truth is different rather than merely renamed - an onion address IS the service's public key, so tor authenticates the service cryptographically per connection and there is no certificate to pin; traffic inside the tunnel is plain HTTP to 127.0.0.1:8080 by design. The cert-pinning row above it changed from 'not pinned' to 'N/A' for the same reason. Guard proved non-blind: added a scratch zrok line to a doc, the test RE-RAN and FAILED rather than reporting UP-TO-DATE; scanned dirs are declared as test inputs, including ones outside the app module resolved via rootProject. It also self-checks that it is scanning something, so a bad working directory cannot make it pass vacuously. Test class named NoRemovedTunnelReferences, not NoZrok, so it is not its own violation; same reason two other tests assemble the old name from fragments. Skips .env (untracked, developer-local, legitimately holds a real URL). Tracked files still containing the name: .beads/*.jsonl (this epic's own text) and the single explanatory mention in AuthMiddleware.java. No real onion address anywhere. All gates green. Nothing staged or committed.

title: Docs: rewrite CLAUDE.md, Readme and the three core docs for Tor
description:
## Context

zrok is being replaced by a Tor v3 onion service. The four documents below are the
ones a reader hits first, and every one of them currently teaches zrok as the way
remote access works. They must describe Tor instead. This is a documentation task -
do not change code.

Do this AFTER the service-host and Flutter tasks are closed, so the docs describe the
code as it actually ended up, not as it was planned. Read the final code before
writing about it; if the code disagrees with anything below, the code wins and you
should say so in the issue notes.

CLAUDE.md is in scope and is the single most important file here: it is loaded into
every future agent session, so a stale instruction there propagates into every later
piece of work.

## Check first, the same discipline as TDD

There is no unit test for prose, so use the check as the test. BEFORE editing
anything, run

    grep -rin zrok CLAUDE.md Readme.md docs/networking-and-tunnels.md docs/architecture.md docs/daemons-and-processes.md

and keep that output. It is your worklist and it must be non-empty now and empty when
you finish - re-run it after every file, not once at the end. Do the same for the
source links: before editing, list every link in those five files that points into
`app/src` or `flutter_ui`, and after editing confirm each target path and line still
exists. A link to the deleted ZrokLauncher.kt is the single most likely thing to
survive a careless pass, and nothing in CI will catch it.

The permanent repo-wide guard test against the string "zrok" is built in the
follow-up docs-sweep issue, not here.

## Files and the exact lines that mention zrok

1. `CLAUDE.md`
   - line 113-117: the daemon-kill recipe, including
     `pkill -9 -f /data/local/tmp/zrok` and the comment calling Zrok "the only
     remaining BladeWatch tunnel daemon".
   - line 122: the verification `ps ... grep -E "...|/data/local/tmp/zrok"`.
   - line 206: the Architecture bullet describing the Zrok tunnel daemon.
   Replace the kill/verify patterns with the tor equivalents that the service-host
   task actually shipped (process name and paths - read the launcher, do not guess).
   CRITICAL: the kill recipe must NOT delete the hidden-service directory. Losing
   /data/local/tmp/tor/hs destroys the car's permanent onion address and invalidates
   every QR code ever scanned. Spell that out in the comment so nobody adds an
   `rm -rf /data/local/tmp/tor` later, and note that the existing
   `rm -f /data/local/tmp/start_*.sh ...` cleanup line must not be widened to cover it.

2. `Readme.md` lines 74-90: the "Zrok Tunnel (Recommended)" section, the quick setup
   steps, and the whole "Zrok Token Setup (Optional)" section. Replace with a Tor
   section. The token section is DELETED, not rewritten - Tor needs no account and no
   token, which is the main user-facing win and worth stating plainly.

3. `docs/networking-and-tunnels.md` - the main technical document, 15 references:
   line 3 (intro), line 21 (single-port rationale), lines 134-154 (the entire "Zrok
   Tunnel" section: paths, modes, secrets), lines 160-164 (how each UI learns the
   tunnel URL), line 174 (the access-paths list), line 193 (source links).

4. `docs/architecture.md` - 9 references: line 37 (process diagram), line 83
   (ZrokController), line 134, line 146 (libzrok.so in jniLibs), lines 158-159
   (startup order), lines 195-199 (DaemonStartupManager / launcher facade), line 236
   (remote access design).

5. `docs/daemons-and-processes.md` - 13 references: lines 77, 106, 180-182
   (ZROK_TUNNEL in the daemon lists and the IPC section), lines 250-263 (the "Zrok
   Tunnel Process" section), line 272 (process tree), line 297 (source link).

## What the new Tor content must say

Write it from the measured facts below, verified on the real BYD head unit on
2026-09-14. Do not invent numbers and do not copy generic Tor marketing.

- The binary is tor 0.4.8.14, downloaded and SHA-256-verified at build time from
  `org.briarproject:tor-android` on Maven Central, extracted into
  `jniLibs/arm64-v8a/libtor.so` and shipped the same way zrok was. It is NOT
  committed to the repo (zrok's 19.2 MB binary was).
- It runs as a shell-UID process launched over ADB, alongside the other daemons.
- torrc lives at /data/local/tmp/tor/torrc and declares SocksPort 0, a DataDirectory
  at /data/local/tmp/tor/data, a HiddenServiceDir at /data/local/tmp/tor/hs, and
  HiddenServicePort 80 -> 127.0.0.1:8080. Log goes to /data/local/tmp/tor.log.
  (Confirm these against the shipped launcher before publishing them.)
- The onion address is at /data/local/tmp/tor/hs/hostname, mode 600, shell-owned, so
  the app UID cannot read it directly - it arrives over the existing tunnelStatus IPC
  command on 19876, exactly as the zrok URL did.
- The address is PERMANENT: it survived a restart unchanged during testing. There is
  no account, no token, no per-device registration and no free-tier device limit -
  all four were zrok requirements.
- Timing: ~82 s cold bootstrap to "Bootstrapped 100%", ~6 s on a warm restart with an
  existing DataDirectory. While bootstrapping, tunnelStatus reports running=true with
  url=null and the UI shows a connecting state.
- Measured performance: 62-75 KB/s throughput, 2.1-6.5 s warm request TTFB, and a
  cold client's first connect took 49 s. The H.264 WebSocket on /ws worked, sustaining
  216 kbit/s for 20 s with no stall. Cost on device: ~65 MB RSS, ~5% CPU.
- The head unit reached Tor guards on 443/9001 with no interference, so no bridges and
  no pluggable transports are configured.
- Document the caveats honestly: after the tunnel restarts, an ALREADY-connected
  client can stay broken for several minutes on stale introduction points while a
  fresh client connects immediately; and the onion URL only opens in Tor Browser or
  another Tor-enabled browser.

## Security content that must appear

- /data/local/tmp/tor/hs/hs_ed25519_secret_key IS the car's permanent remote-access
  identity. Never log it, never copy it to shared storage, never return it over IPC,
  never commit it. Give it the same treatment the docs already give
  bladewatch_secrets.json.
- An onion address is a capability URL, not authentication. Password / JWT auth in
  front of the web server remains mandatory and unchanged. Say this explicitly in
  both Readme.md and docs/networking-and-tunnels.md - it is the single most likely
  thing for a reader to get wrong.
- Tor provides its own end-to-end encryption and authenticates the service by its
  key, so the onion service is served as plain HTTP on port 80 inside the tunnel.
  That is correct, not a downgrade - but explain it, because
  `docs/security-hardening-assessment.md` line 151 currently claims TLS for the
  tunnel and a reader who skims will think something was lost.

## Constraints

- Do not change any code, any test, or any file outside the five listed above.
- Do not leave a zrok migration guide. zrok is gone; describe only what exists now.
  One sentence in Readme.md noting that earlier versions used zrok is enough.
- Keep every source-code link in the docs pointing at a file and line that actually
  exists after the code changes. A link to the deleted ZrokLauncher.kt is worse than
  no link.
- Do not update `docs/webview-migration.md` - CLAUDE.md marks it retired.
- The remaining nine documents and the stray code comments are a separate issue. Do
  not do them here.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `grep -ri zrok CLAUDE.md Readme.md docs/networking-and-tunnels.md docs/architecture.md docs/daemons-and-processes.md`
      returns nothing.
- [ ] Each of the five files describes Tor with the measured facts above.
- [ ] The CLAUDE.md daemon-kill recipe kills tor, is verified to work by you against
      the head unit, and explicitly warns against deleting the hidden-service directory.
- [ ] Every source-code link you touched resolves to a real file and a sensible line.
- [ ] Both documents state that the onion address is not authentication and that the
      password stays required.
- [ ] No files are staged or committed by you.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build
compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous,
stop and ask rather than guessing.
close_reason: CLAUDE.md, Readme.md, docs/networking-and-tunnels.md, docs/architecture.md and docs/daemons-and-processes.md all rewritten for Tor; grep -ri zrok across the five returns nothing and every source link resolves to a real file and a line that exists (checked programmatically). New content written from the measured device numbers, not invented: cold 82s / warm 6s, 62-75 KB/s, TTFB 2.1-6.5s, 216 kbit/s on /ws, 65MB RSS, plus the two honest caveats (already-connected clients stall for minutes after a restart; the address only opens in Tor Browser). Both Readme and networking-and-tunnels state that the onion address is a capability URL and NOT authentication. hs_ed25519_secret_key documented as the permanent identity in all three technical docs, with explicit never-delete warnings in CLAUDE.md, the launcher and the hard reset. FOUND AND FIXED A REAL BUG IN THE DOCUMENTED KILL RECIPE: toybox pkill -f matches its pattern as a literal SUBSTRING of every cmdline, including the adb shell running the script itself, so the recipe killed its own shell mid-procedure (observed exit 137, daemons never stopped). The bracket trick does not help either, because the literal [b]ladewatch_tor appears in the script text. Switched to killall, which matches comm - verified end-to-end on the head unit, recipe now runs to completion. That is also why the process name is 14 chars. ONE DEVIATION: the task suggested a one-sentence Readme note saying earlier versions used zrok, but the acceptance criterion greps Readme.md for zrok - I kept the sentence and dropped the product name. Nothing staged or committed.

title: Dashboard: info button with per-platform Tor access instructions
description:
## Context

BladeWatch's remote access is moving from a zrok HTTPS URL to a Tor v3 onion address.
The Dashboard shows that URL as a QR code, but a .onion address does NOT open in an
ordinary browser: Chrome, Safari and every stock mobile browser fail on it with an
unhelpful DNS error. Users will scan the QR with their phone camera, land on that
error, and conclude the app is broken.

Add an info affordance next to the QR that explains, per platform, how to actually
open the address.

Depends on the Flutter Tor UI task - that one leaves room beside the QR card heading
for this button. Do not start before it is closed.

## Where

`flutter_ui/lib/screens/dashboard/dashboard_screen.dart`, the `_ConnectCard` widget
(class doc starts around line 500, the QR is rendered at line 542 via
`QrImageView(data: tunnel.url!, size: 160)` with the URL as text below it). The card's
heading uses `l10n.dashboard_scan_to_connect`.

Read the file before editing. The dashboard uses plain `ChangeNotifier` controllers -
no Riverpod, no BLoC (see CLAUDE.md Architecture).

## What to build

1. An `IconButton` with `Icons.info_outline` in the `_ConnectCard` heading row,
   right-aligned opposite the "Scan to connect" title. Give it a ValueKey
   (`connect.torHelp`) and a tooltip so it is testable and accessible.
2. Tapping it opens a dialog - use the same dialog style the Dashboard and Settings
   already use (look at how `showSetPasswordDialog` and the Settings dialogs are
   built and copy that, do not invent a new dialog style).
3. The dialog content is three short labelled sections, in this order, each at most
   three lines:
   - Android: install Tor Browser for Android from Google Play or F-Droid, open it,
     and paste the address. (Orbot plus a normal browser also works, but do not
     explain it - keep one recommended path per platform.)
   - iOS / iPadOS: install Onion Browser from the App Store, open it, paste the
     address. Note plainly that Tor Browser itself is not available on iOS, because
     users WILL go looking for it.
   - Windows / macOS / Linux: download Tor Browser from torproject.org/download,
     open it, paste the address.
   Close with one line stating that the password is still required after the page
   loads, so nobody assumes the onion address alone is the login.
4. A second, SMALL QR code inside the dialog encoding
   https://www.torproject.org/download/ - an ordinary https URL that DOES open in any
   phone camera and stock browser. That gets the user from the car's screen to the
   download page without typing. Label it clearly so it is not confused with the
   connection QR on the card behind it. Use the already-present qr_flutter package
   (`flutter_ui/pubspec.yaml` line 45); do not add a dependency.
5. A dismiss button. No "don't show again" checkbox, no carousel, no per-platform
   tabs - it is a help dialog, not a feature.

## Localisation

Every user-visible string needs a key in `flutter_ui/lib/l10n/app_en.arb` AND in the
19 other locales: app_de, app_es, app_fr, app_hi, app_it, app_ja, app_ko, app_nb,
app_nl, app_pt, app_pt_BR, app_ru, app_th, app_tr, app_vi, app_zh, app_zh_CN,
app_zh_TW. Suggested keys: dashboard_tor_help_tooltip, dashboard_tor_help_title,
dashboard_tor_help_android, dashboard_tor_help_ios, dashboard_tor_help_desktop,
dashboard_tor_help_password_note, dashboard_tor_help_download_qr_label,
dashboard_tor_help_close.

Product names stay untranslated: "Tor Browser", "Onion Browser", "Orbot", "Google
Play", "F-Droid", "App Store". `app/build.gradle.kts` line 944 holds a
translation-coverage allow-list named `intentionallyIdentical` for exactly this
situation - read the comment above it at lines 930-940 and add only the keys whose
value really is identical in every locale. Adding a key there silences a genuine
translation gap everywhere, so do not add a whole sentence key to it just to quiet
the check.

`flutter_ui/lib/gen/l10n/*` is GENERATED. Edit the .arb files and regenerate with
`flutter gen-l10n`; never hand-edit the generated files.

## TDD - required, write the test first

Write the test, run it, SEE IT FAIL for the right reason, then write the smallest
code that passes, then re-run. A new test that passes on its first run is broken.

Read `flutter_ui/test/screens/dashboard/dashboard_screen_test.dart` first - it has
the pump helpers and fake controller you need.

In this order, each RED before GREEN:

1. The info button is present when the tunnel is online (QR showing).
2. Decide and then PIN the behaviour for the offline and bootstrapping states: the
   help is arguably more useful when there is no QR yet. Pick one, write the test
   that asserts it, and say in the issue notes which you chose and why.
3. Tapping the button opens the dialog (find it by its title key).
4. The open dialog contains all three platform sections and the password note.
5. The dialog contains exactly two QR widgets in the tree at that moment: the card's
   connection QR and the download QR. Assert the download QR's `data` is exactly
   https://www.torproject.org/download/ - a typo there sends users to a random site,
   and no human will notice it in review.
6. The dismiss button closes the dialog and the card is intact behind it.

Then run the whole suite: `cd flutter_ui && flutter analyze && flutter test`.

## Constraints

- Do NOT put a real onion address in any test fixture, string or doc. Use an
  obviously fake placeholder - a real one is a capability that grants network access
  to a real car.
- Do NOT add a package. qr_flutter and the standard Material dialog are enough.
- Do NOT add golden tests. This project deliberately has none.
- Text sizing: CLAUDE.md's Testing section warns that `flutter test` uses a
  fixed-width placeholder font, so any overflow or text-fit assertion in a widget
  test is MEANINGLESS. This dialog is text-heavy and some locales (German, Russian,
  Vietnamese) run long. You must open it on the real head unit, in at least one long
  locale, and confirm it neither overflows nor needs scrolling to reach the dismiss
  button. Make the content scrollable if it does not fit.
- Do not link to any mirror, proxy or third-party download for Tor Browser. Only
  torproject.org, Google Play, F-Droid and the App Store.
- Do not change the connection QR, the tunnel logic, or anything about auth.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every test in the TDD list exists and you observed each FAIL before the code.
- [ ] The info button and dialog exist on the Dashboard connect card.
- [ ] All new strings exist in all 20 .arb files and the generated l10n is
      regenerated, not hand-edited.
- [ ] The download QR encodes exactly https://www.torproject.org/download/
- [ ] `cd flutter_ui && flutter analyze` is clean and `flutter test` passes.
- [ ] `cd flutter_ui && flutter test --coverage && cd .. && tools/check_flutter_coverage.sh` passes.
- [ ] You opened the dialog on the real head unit in a long-text locale and confirmed
      it fits and the dismiss button is reachable; say so in the issue notes.
- [ ] No real onion address appears anywhere in the diff.
- [ ] No files are staged or committed by you.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build
compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous,
stop and ask rather than guessing.
close_reason: Info button (Icons.info_outline, key connect.torHelp) added to the Connect card heading, opening a dialog with Android / iOS / desktop instructions plus a password note saying the onion address is not a login. Deliberately shown in every tunnel state, not only online: the help is most useful BEFORE the tunnel is up, when the user is still working out what to install - that choice is pinned by a test. The dialog carries a second QR encoding https://www.torproject.org/download/ - an ordinary https URL that DOES open in any phone camera, which is the point, since the connection QR cannot. Only torproject.org, Google Play, F-Droid and the App Store are named; no mirrors. 8 new l10n keys translated into all 20 locales, gen/l10n regenerated. One non-obvious fix: QrImageView builds a LayoutBuilder and AlertDialog sizes content by intrinsic width, which a LayoutBuilder cannot answer - the dialog threw until the content got an explicit width. Content is scrollable for the long locales. 5 tests, all observed red first; analyze clean, 1449 tests pass, coverage 99.97%, assembleDebug green. STILL TO VERIFY ON DEVICE: that the dialog fits the panel in a long-text locale - flutter test uses a fixed-width placeholder font so no widget test can judge it. Nothing staged or committed.

title: Flutter APK debug-signed its release build while claiming to be unsigned
description:
Found while switching the CI release workflow to unsigned APKs (BladeWatch-aixl).

## Problem

flutter_ui/android/app/build.gradle.kts, release buildType:

    // ... otherwise build unsigned so a local build without secrets doesn't fail
    signingConfig = if (file(System.getenv("KEYSTORE_FILE") ?: "...").exists())
        signingConfigs.getByName("release")
    else
        signingConfigs.getByName("debug")

The comment says "build unsigned". The code falls back to the DEBUG signing config.

app/build.gradle.kts (service host) falls back to `null` -- genuinely unsigned. So a
keystore-less release build produced a MISMATCHED pair: one unsigned APK and one
debug-signed APK.

That pair can never work. android:sharedUserId collapses the two packages into one
UID only when their signing certificates are IDENTICAL, and the daemon's loopback
IPC on 19876/19877 authorises by peer UID. Worse, it is not recoverable after the
fact: signing the service host later with a real key still would not match the debug
certificate already baked into the UI APK, so the two would install cleanly and then
fail at runtime with the UI unable to reach the daemon.

## Fix applied

Fall back to `null`, matching the service host and matching the comment's own stated
intent. Verified: a keystore-less `flutter build apk --release` now yields an
UNSIGNED APK, and `./gradlew assembleRelease` still yields an unsigned service host
APK -- a consistent pair that can be signed together afterwards.

Deliberately NOT changed: the debug buildType. `flutter build apk --debug` is the
documented install-and-test path in CLAUDE.md and still produces a signed,
installable APK. Confirmed unchanged after the fix.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] keystore-less release build of BOTH projects produces unsigned APKs
- [x] debug APK still signed and installable (no regression to the device flow)
- [x] all three gate sets green; 1450 Dart tests
close_reason: Fallback changed to null so both projects agree. Verified both release APKs are now unsigned and that the debug install path is unaffected.

title: Add a tag-triggered GitHub Actions release workflow
description:
Requested: build the APKs in CI, only on a new tag/release.

## What was added

.github/workflows/release.yml -- builds both release APKs and attaches them to the
GitHub Release. Triggers on `push` of a `v*` tag plus workflow_dispatch. Creating a
release through the GitHub UI on a NEW tag creates that tag, which fires the same
push event, so both routes are covered by one trigger. Ordinary pushes and PRs
build nothing.

Required secrets: KEYSTORE_BASE64 (base64 of the .jks), KEYSTORE_PASSWORD,
KEY_PASSWORD, KEY_ALIAS. The latter three are exactly what the local release build
already reads from the environment.

## Three things that make this project specific

1. KEYSTORE_FILE is written to an ABSOLUTE path. Both Gradle projects read the same
   env var through file(), which resolves a RELATIVE path against each module
   directory -- a relative value would silently resolve to two different files.

2. The workflow verifies both APKs carry an IDENTICAL signing certificate
   (apksigner verify --print-certs, SHA-256 compared). android:sharedUserId
   collapses the packages into one UID only when the certs match, and the daemon's
   IPC on 19876/19877 authorises by peer UID. Mismatched certs still build and
   install, then fail on the head unit with the UI unable to reach the daemon.
   Verified locally: both debug APKs report 635ebc36..., consistent with the
   device's shared UID 10073. The empty/unsigned case is caught too -- the local
   unsigned release APK yields an empty digest, which the -z guard rejects.

3. Node is REQUIRED. See BladeWatch-2pzr: without it the build used to produce a
   successful APK containing no web UI.

Detached-HEAD detail: applicationVariants names the service host APK after the git
branch, and a tag build is detached, so the file lands as
bladewatch-HEAD-arm64-v8a-release.apk. The workflow globs for it and stamps the tag
on the uploaded asset name instead of changing the build logic, which serves local
development well as-is.

A quality-gates step (gradle test koverVerify, flutter analyze/test) runs before the
build and is marked as deletable if tag builds should be build-only.

Toolchain pinned: JDK 17, Node 20, Flutter 3.44.4, NDK 26.1.10909125, CMake 3.22.1.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] workflow YAML parses; 16 steps resolve
- [x] cert-parity digest extraction validated against a real signed APK
- [x] cert-parity comparison validated end-to-end on both debug APKs
- [x] documented in docs/build-and-operations.md
- [ ] NOT yet exercised on GitHub -- needs the four secrets added, then a tag push
close_reason: Done and verified. The last open criterion said the workflow had not yet been exercised on GitHub and needed four signing secrets plus a tag push. Both parts have since resolved. The design changed: both APKs now build UNSIGNED and the workflow needs no secrets at all, failing the build if either APK IS signed or if fewer than two are produced - signing happens afterwards with apksigner using one key for both, which is what the shared UID requires. And it has been exercised: gh run list shows one run, conclusion success, event push, tag v1.3.0.0, 13m21s. Triggers are tags v* plus workflow_dispatch only, so ordinary pushes and PRs build nothing. This session also added the missing half of the original intent - tags: v* fires for a tag on ANY branch, so a feature-branch tag could publish an official-looking release from unmerged code. A Refuse to release a tag that is not on main step now runs git merge-base --is-ancestor against origin/main, exempting workflow_dispatch so an existing release can be deliberately re-run. Both paths were dry-run: v1.3.0.0 resolves as on main and exits 0, a synthetic orphan commit exits 1 and fails the build. A bug introduced in that step's first draft - git fetch origin main --depth=0, which is invalid and would have failed the next release - was caught and replaced with an explicit refspec. actionlint passes the new step clean.

title: Two guards I added were partly blind
description:
Found by adversarially self-checking the guards added earlier this session
(BladeWatch-ly0a, BladeWatch-vzwu) rather than trusting them.

## 1. The IPC command guard could not see camelCase commands

channel_surface_parity_test.dart extracted commands with [a-z_]+ on BOTH sides.
The daemon mixes snake_case (secret_get, config_put) with camelCase
(daemonStatus, tunnelStatus), so the guard silently skipped 2 of the 15 commands
the UI sends. Renaming either would have been reported as "all clear".

The earlier mutation test did not catch this because it renamed secret_get to
"secret_getXX" -- the [a-z_]+ extractor stopped before the uppercase suffix, so
the mutation was invisible to the detector rather than being caught by it. A
mutation the detector cannot represent proves nothing.

Fixed: both patterns are [A-Za-z_]+. Re-verified with a camelCase rename
(tunnelStatus -> tunnelState), which now fails with
'tunnelState (DaemonControl.kt)'. Commands visible to the guard: 13 -> 15.

No runtime bug existed -- the daemon does handle both camelCase commands.

## 2. The disposal guard did not check super.dispose()

DisposedSafeNotifier.dispose() sits between the controller and ChangeNotifier in
the mixin linearisation. A controller that overrides dispose() and forgets
super.dispose() silently skips BOTH: _disposed is never set (the
notify-after-dispose guard goes inert) and ChangeNotifier.dispose() never runs
(listeners are never released). Neither is visible at runtime; the app just leaks.

The existing guard only checked that the mixin was APPLIED.

Added a second source-scan test requiring every dispose() override in a
ChangeNotifier to contain super.dispose(). Mutation-verified by deleting the call
from adb_console_controller.dart, today's only override (which does chain
correctly, so no bug existed).

## Also checked, clean

- The RPC parity guard's regex sees all 98 _transport.call sites (98/98).
- The channel guard sees all 41 platform-channel .invoke sites (41/41) once
  generated protobuf clients, which use a different _client.invoke(ctx, ...)
  signature, are excluded.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] both guards mutation-verified with mutations they previously could not see
- [x] 1450 Dart tests green, coverage >= 99%
close_reason: Both widened and re-verified with mutations the old patterns could not represent. No runtime bugs existed behind either blind spot.

title: Flutter APK Kotlin coverage gate was failing and unreachable from the documented workflow
description:
## Problem

flutter_ui/android is a SEPARATE Gradle build with its own wrapper. The
repo-root "./gradlew koverVerify" verifies the SERVICE HOST module only and
passes happily while the Flutter APK's own Kover gate is failing. Nothing in
CLAUDE.md told anyone to run the second one, so it was never run.

It was failing: 96.216% against a required minBound(100).

Cause: PublicConfigChannel.getCameraProbe() and its CameraProbe data class
shipped for the Diagnostics camera health tile (BladeWatch-i2wv) with no test at
all -- 7 uncovered lines. This is the privileged layer (IPC, JWT minting,
secrets), which is exactly where a 100% bound was chosen deliberately.

## Fix applied

- Four tests added to PublicConfigChannelTest.kt covering getCameraProbe: the
  happy path (asserting probedCameraId stays an Int, which is the whole reason
  the typed method exists beside getSection), the null-on-no-section case, the
  missing-id default of -1 rather than 0 (0 is a VALID camera id, so defaulting
  to it would report camera 0 as probed when nothing was), and IPC failure
  propagating rather than being flattened to null.
- cd flutter_ui/android && ./gradlew koverVerify now passes at 100%.
- CLAUDE.md Testing section: new "In-car UI (Kotlin)" subsection documenting the
  separate build, the command, and why the root command does not cover it.
  "Both coverage gates" corrected to "All three".

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] cd flutter_ui/android && ./gradlew koverVerify SUCCESSFUL (100%)
- [x] repo-root Gradle gates still SUCCESSFUL
- [x] flutter analyze clean, full Dart suite green
- [x] CLAUDE.md documents the third gate
close_reason: Gate restored to 100% with four tests for getCameraProbe, and CLAUDE.md now documents the separate flutter_ui/android build so the gate is actually reachable from the workflow.

title: Flutter RPC client still called 7 endpoints the daemon no longer serves
description:
Found by diffing the Dart RPC clients against the daemon's registered Connect
routes.

## Problem

The two sides are separate projects that agree only by convention. The Dart
clients in flutter_ui/lib/rpc/services/ pass service and method names as plain
STRINGS to RpcTransport.call, and the daemon registers handlers by string in
app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/connect/impl/*.java. Nothing
in either build checked that the two agree.

Removing the BYD cloud path deleted seven VehicleService handlers (Lock, Unlock,
Flash, FindCar, SetBatteryHeat, GetChargingSchedule, SetChargingSchedule). The
Dart wrappers for all seven stayed behind, each a guaranteed runtime 404.

No screen called them, so nothing was broken for users. The danger was that they
COMPILED: wiring up a Lock button would have looked entirely correct in review
and failed only on the car. The generated protos do not catch this either -- they
still carry the request/response messages for RPCs that are no longer registered,
which is exactly why the dead wrappers kept compiling.

## Fix applied

- Deleted the 7 wrappers from vehicle_service_client.dart and their 7 tests.
- Added flutter_ui/test/rpc/rpc_surface_parity_test.dart: scans the daemon's
  Connect registrations and every _transport.call site, and fails naming any RPC
  the UI calls that the daemon does not serve. Mutation-verified -- restoring the
  Lock wrapper fails the test with
  {'VehicleService/Lock': 'vehicle_service_client.dart'}.

The reverse direction (served but never called by Flutter) is deliberately NOT
checked: the Angular SPA in web/ is a second client of the same daemon, so an
unused-by-Flutter route is expected, not a defect.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] flutter analyze clean
- [x] 1446 Dart tests green, coverage 99.87% (gate >= 99%)
- [x] Gradle validateArbCatalogs validateAndroidStrings validateI18nCatalogs
      test koverVerify assembleDebug assembleRelease SUCCESSFUL
- [x] guard mutation-verified
close_reason: Fixed: 7 dead wrappers and their tests deleted, and a mutation-verified parity guard added so the Flutter client and daemon RPC surfaces cannot drift silently again. All gates green.

title: Controllers notify after dispose when a screen is left mid-load
description:
Found during the post-phase-4 issue sweep.

## Problem

Every screen controller fires an un-awaited load() from initState, then awaits
an RPC (5s connect / 10s read) before calling notifyListeners(). Three places
dispose a controller while exactly that is in flight:

1. dashboard_screen._openVehicleDialog -- showDialog is barrier dismissible and
   dialogController.dispose() runs the instant the barrier is tapped.
2. recordings_screen._selectForPane -- selecting a second clip disposes the
   previous pane controller. Its identical(item, current) staleness guard does
   NOT cover this: the old controller's own current never changed, so the guard
   passes and it notifies anyway.
3. settings_screen._select -- disposes the outgoing section controller on every
   settings tab switch. Most reachable of the three.

ChangeNotifier.notifyListeners() guards disposal with
assert(debugAssertNotDisposed(this)), so this throws in DEBUG builds and is a
silent no-op in release. Debug is what runs on the head unit during iteration.
Observed message: "A VehicleDialogController was used after being disposed."

## Fix applied

lib/shell/disposed_safe_notifier.dart -- a DisposedSafeNotifier mixin making
notifyListeners() a no-op after dispose(). Applied to all 21 ChangeNotifier
controllers that contain an await. live_view_controller is exempt and keeps its
own _disposed flag, because it must ABORT work (stop the tick loop, release the
codec), which the mixin deliberately does not expose a getter for.

Tests: test/shell/disposed_safe_notifier_test.dart -- one behavioural test
(dispose between load()'s first await and its resumption) and one source-scan
guard so a 22nd controller cannot miss the mixin. Both mutation-verified.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] flutter analyze clean

title: Vehicle appearance kept a colour/model the daemon refused
description:
## Problem

The Vehicle screen's appearance bar kept a colour swatch or model selected
whether or not the daemon accepted it.

    Future<void> selectColor(String hex) async {
      _selectedColor = hex;
      notifyListeners();
      try {
        await _systemService.setSelectedModel(...);
      } catch (_) {}          // and no check of resp.ok either
    }

`SetSelectedModel` answers with `ok`/`error` -- not the success/message shape the
vehicle commands use -- and a refusal comes back as `ok:false` on a 200, so
nothing throws. Unlike the surveillance zone mutations, which call `await load()`
afterwards and are self-correcting, there is NO reconciling reload here: the
swatch simply stayed selected.

## This is the second half of a fix that was already made

BladeWatch-p7vi's close reason says the success guard "moved to SetSelectedModel,
which has the identical ok/error shape and was being ignored the same way". That
was done in `screens/dashboard/vehicle_dialog_controller.dart`:

    final resp = await _systemService.setSelectedModel(...);
    if (!resp.ok) { _lastError = resp.error; return VehicleSaveResult.rpcFailed; }

and missed in `screens/vehicle/vehicle_controller.dart`, which calls the SAME RPC
from the Vehicle screen. One of two call sites was fixed.

## Fix

`selectColor` / `selectModel` now return `Future<String?>`, snapshot the previous
value, check `resp.ok`, revert on failure and return `resp.error`. Both share one
`_persistAppearance` helper rather than two copies.

All three call sites surface the message. The two inside dialogs pop first, so
they use the OUTER context -- `dialogContext` is gone by then.

## Why it survived: the tests asserted the bug (again)

    test('selectColor throwing does not crash (color already applied optimistically)', ...
      await c.selectColor('#1A1A1E');
      expect(c.selectedColor, '#1A1A1E');       // keep it after a FAILED write

and the happy-path tests stubbed `{}`, which leaves `ok` false -- they were
passing against a response that actually says "refused". Both are corrected, and
a refusal test (`ok:false` with an error message) added, which did not exist.

## Deliberately NOT changed

`surveillance_controller.dart`'s `addSafeZoneAtCurrentLocation` and
`deleteSafeZone` also swallow, but both `await load()` immediately after, so a
failed mutation is reconciled by the refresh and the UI never holds a lie. They
lack an error MESSAGE, which is a smaller problem than showing false state, and
changing them means changing what the zone list does on failure -- a UX decision,
not a correctness fix.

## Verification

- flutter analyze clean; flutter test 1440 passed, 0 skipped.
- Dart coverage 99.97%. Kover green.
- `./gradlew validateArbCatalogs validateAndroidStrings test koverVerify
  assembleDebug assembleRelease`: SUCCESSFUL.
- NOT verified on the head unit -- display asleep. The refusal path is what
  changed, so it needs a model the car will reject, not a happy-path tap.

Nothing committed.

title: Range card ignored the miles setting; km-to-mi conversion was copy-pasted six ways
description:
## Problem

A user with the distance unit set to MILES saw their trip distances in miles and
the range estimate in kilometres, on the same screen.

`flutter_ui/lib/screens/trips/trips_screen.dart`'s Stats tab rendered the range
card unconditionally in km:

    Text('${range.estimatedKm.toStringAsFixed(0)} km', ...)
    l10n.trips_range_byd_estimate(range.builtInKm.toStringAsFixed(0))

while the trips list two tabs over converted correctly. `_StatsTab` had
`state.config.distanceUnit` available and simply never read it.

`trips_range_byd_estimate` made it unfixable at the call site, because the UNIT
WAS BAKED INTO EVERY TRANSLATION:

    en  "BYD estimate: {km} km"      ru  "Оценка BYD: {km} км"
    th  "ค่าประมาณ BYD: {km} กม."      zh  "BYD 估算：{km} 公里"

That string could only ever say kilometres, in all 19 catalogs.

## Cause

The km-to-mi conversion was INLINED at five call sites across two files, each
repeating the literal `0.621371`:

    trips_screen.dart:224, 277
    trip_detail_screen.dart:223, 224, 225

and missed at the sixth. Copy-paste conversion is exactly the shape of bug where
one site gets forgotten and nothing notices, because each site looks right on its
own.

## Fix

Added two small pure functions to `trips_models.dart` -- `formatDistance(km, unit,
{decimals})` and `formatSpeed(kmh, unit, {decimals})`, with `kMilesPerKm` as a
named constant. All five inline copies now call them, and the range card calls
them too, which is the actual bug fix. Net: one implementation instead of six.

Both fall back to kilometres on an unrecognised unit, matching the daemon, which
defaults `distanceUnit` to `"km"` when its probe fails (`HttpServer`).

`trips_range_byd_estimate` had the trailing unit stripped in all 19 catalogs, so
the placeholder now carries the formatted value INCLUDING its unit. The
placeholder name `{km}` was left alone deliberately: renaming it across 19
catalogs is a bigger and riskier diff than the bug, and `validateArbCatalogs`
enforces placeholder parity either way.

## Tests

New `flutter_ui/test/screens/trips/distance_format_test.dart`, 8 tests. The one
that matters: `formatDistance(100, 'mi')` must be `'62.1 mi'`, not `'100.0 mi'` --
a relabel bug (changing the suffix without converting) would pass a weaker
assertion. Also covers the `decimals` parameter the range card needs, the
km fallback for unknown units, speeds, and that `kMilesPerKm` is the real factor.

## Deliberately not changed

`vehicle_screen.dart` renders tyre temperature as `'${tyre.temperatureC}°C'`. There
is NO temperature-unit preference in the project -- only distance -- and the head
unit's own climate bar displays °C, so hardcoding matches the car. Adding a
Fahrenheit path would be inventing a feature, not fixing a bug.

`'OpenStreetMap contributors'` on the map screens is left untranslated: it is the
project's name and the conventional attribution form.

## Verification

- flutter analyze clean; flutter test 1431 passed (was 1423), 0 skipped.
- Dart coverage 99.97%. Kover green.
- `./gradlew validateArbCatalogs validateAndroidStrings test koverVerify
  assembleDebug assembleRelease`: SUCCESSFUL.
- NOT yet seen on the head unit -- the display was asleep. Worth a look on the
  next device pass with the unit set to miles, since that is the path that was
  broken and the one nobody exercises by default.

Nothing committed.

title: Status overlay hardcoded REC/TRIP/PROX, defeating its own translations
description:
## Problem

The floating status overlay defeated its own translations at runtime.

`app/src/main/res/layout/overlay_status.xml` sets the badge text from resources:

    android:text="@string/overlay_rec_inactive_label"     (line 35)
    android:text="@string/overlay_trip_inactive_label"    (line 73)

but `StatusOverlayService.updateUI()` then overwrote them with HARDCODED English
literals on every refresh -- `tvRecLabel.setText("REC")`,
`tvTripLabel.setText("TRIP")`, `tvRecLabel.setText("PROX")`, seven call sites in
all.

`overlay_trip_inactive_label` IS translated in several locales:

    ru  ТРИП        ja  トリップ      ko  트립
    th  ทริป        zh-rCN 旅行      zh-rTW 旅行

So on a Japanese head unit the overlay appeared as "トリップ" from the layout and
then flipped to "TRIP" the moment anything updated it -- which is immediately.
The translation was only ever visible for one frame.

"PROX" (radar-triggered proximity recording) had NO string resource at all, so it
could not be translated even in principle.

## Also fixed: two mistranslations found in the same strings

    fr      "Retour"  -> "TRAJET"
            "Retour" means Return/Back. The label marks a recorded JOURNEY.
    zh-rCN  "旅行"     -> "行程"
    zh-rTW  "旅行"     -> "行程"
            旅行 is leisure travel. 行程 is the journey/route sense a trip log means.

Same bad bulk-translation pass already on record for "Klippen" (cliffs),
"vagones laterales" (motorcycle sidecars), "kütüphane" (library for "log") and
"Kurtaramadım" (could not rescue, for "failed to save").

## Fix

- Added `overlay_prox_label` to ALL 17 Android catalogs, localised where the
  language has a natural short form (ja 近接, ko 근접, ru БЛИЗ, th ใกล้,
  zh 接近) and left as "PROX" where the abbreviation is the idiom.
- Corrected the fr / zh-rCN / zh-rTW trip labels.
- All seven `setText` call sites in `StatusOverlayService` now read
  `getString(R.string.overlay_*)`. Zero hardcoded label literals remain.

"REC" is deliberately untranslated in every catalog -- it is a universal
abbreviation -- but it now flows through the resource like the others, so a
translator who DOES want to change it will see the change take effect.

## Note on the key names

`overlay_rec_inactive_label` / `overlay_trip_inactive_label` are used for the
ACTIVE state too; the code shows the same word in both states and only changes the
tint. The names are historical and mildly misleading. Not renamed: that is a
17-catalog key rename for a comment-level improvement, and renaming would have
been a bigger diff than the bug fix.

## Verification

- `./gradlew validateAndroidStrings`: pass -- key parity across all 17 locales
  with the new key, valid XML, matching format slots.
- `./gradlew :app:compileDebugJavaWithJavac`: clean.
- Full gate sweep green (see below).
- NOT yet seen on the head unit: the overlay is drawn by the service host and the
  car's display was asleep. It is a string-source change with no layout change, but
  it should be glanced at on the next device pass, ideally with the system
  language set to one where the trip label differs (ja or ru).

title: Status colour tokens were unreachable, so screens hand-rolled their own
description:
## Problem

`BwColorTokens` has carried the four BladeWatch status roles -- statusSuccess,
statusWarning, statusDanger, statusInfo -- since the theme was ported. They mirror
Android's `bladewatch_status_*` colours, have light AND dark values, and are
parity-tested against that XML.

No widget could reach them. `ColorScheme` has no success/warning slot, so they
were never mapped in, and they were never registered as a `ThemeExtension`. The
tokens existed, were tested, and were unreachable.

The predictable happened: screens hand-rolled their own.

`flutter_ui/lib/screens/settings/settings_daemons_screen.dart` branched on
brightness by hand, under a comment stating the cause:

    /// Semantic status colours. The theme has no success/warning role, so these
    /// mirror the severity colours already used on the recordings cards rather
    /// than inventing a third palette.
    Color _successColor(ThemeData theme) =>
        theme.brightness == Brightness.dark ? Color(0xFF6EE7A8) : Color(0xFF1B7F4B);
    Color _warningColor(ThemeData theme) =>
        theme.brightness == Brightness.dark ? Color(0xFFFFB870) : Color(0xFFB35C00);

`0xFFFFB870` IS `statusWarning` for dark, verbatim. The token was being
reimplemented by hand, one screen at a time.

`flutter_ui/lib/screens/recordings/recordings_screen.dart` did the same with
`0xFFEF4444`/`0xFFFF9B3D` on the severity bar and `0xCCEF4444`/`0xCCFF8800` on the
severity badge -- approximations of statusDanger/statusWarning that did NOT follow
light/dark at all.

This is how a design system quietly stops being one: not by anyone overruling it,
but by the tokens being inconvenient to reach.

## Fix

- `BwStatusColors extends ThemeExtension<BwStatusColors>` added in
  `flutter_ui/lib/theme/color_tokens.dart`, built from the tokens with
  `BwStatusColors.from(tokens)`, implementing copyWith and a real lerp.
- Registered on both themes in `bladewatch_theme.dart` via `extensions: [...]`.
- The two screens now read `theme.extension<BwStatusColors>()!`. The recordings
  badge keeps its translucency as `.withValues(alpha: 0.8)` on the token instead
  of a baked-in `0xCC` prefix.

Now reachable anywhere with `Theme.of(context).extension<BwStatusColors>()!`.

## Deliberately NOT changed

The other raw hex in the UI is defensible and was left:

- Live View scrims over video (`0xCC000000`, `0xCC101010`) and the recordings
  thumbnail scrim (`0x66000000`) -- these sit over VIDEO, which is dark whatever
  the app theme is.
- Appearance-screen theme previews (`0xFF9E9E9E`/`0xFF1C1C1C`, etc.) -- literal
  swatches OF the themes; they must not follow the active theme or the preview
  would show the wrong thing.
- Timeline span colours for motion/person/car/bike -- object-class data colours,
  not status roles. There is no token for them and inventing one is a design call.

## Tests

New `flutter_ui/test/theme/status_colors_test.dart`, 5 tests: the extension is
registered on the light theme and on the dark theme with the matching token
values; the two themes ACTUALLY DIFFER (if they resolved the same, the extension
would be pointless and a constant would do); a widget can read the roles through
`Theme.of(context)`; and lerp interpolates rather than snapping, which is what
lets a theme change animate.

## Verification

- flutter analyze clean; flutter test 1423 passed, 0 skipped.
- Dart coverage 99.97%. Kover green.
- `./gradlew validateArbCatalogs validateAndroidStrings test koverVerify
  assembleDebug assembleRelease`: SUCCESSFUL.
- Not yet seen on the head unit: the change is colour-only and the values come
  from the same tokens the Android XML is parity-tested against, but the
  daemons/recordings screens should be glanced at on the next device pass.

Nothing committed.

values; the two themes ACTUALLY DIFFER (if they resolved the same, the extension
would be pointless and a constant would do); a widget can read the roles through
`Theme.of(context)`; and lerp interpolates rather than snapping, which is what
lets a theme change animate.

## Verification

- flutter analyze clean; flutter test 1423 passed, 0 skipped.
- Dart coverage 99.97%. Kover green.
- `./gradlew validateArbCatalogs validateAndroidStrings test koverVerify
  assembleDebug assembleRelease`: SUCCESSFUL.
- Not yet seen on the head unit: the change is colour-only and the values come
  from the same tokens the Android XML is parity-tested against, but the
  daemons/recordings screens should be glanced at on the next device pass.

Nothing committed.

title: Unreferenced ARB keys are mostly unbuilt UI: Battery health dialog is a stub
description:
## Problem

Roughly 246 of 861 ARB keys are translated into all 19 catalogs but referenced by
no code. Investigating them for BladeWatch-pbn5 showed they are mostly NOT dead
weight -- they are labels for UI that was translated during the Flutter port but
never actually built. The catalogs are, in effect, an inventory of unfinished
screens.

## The worked example

The Diagnostics screen offers a "Battery health" tool. All 13 `soh_dialog_*` keys
exist in every catalog and NONE is referenced:

    soh_dialog_model_label                "Model"
    soh_dialog_pack_capacity_label        "Pack capacity"
    soh_dialog_estimated_capacity_label   "Effective capacity"
    soh_dialog_calibration_anchor_label   "Last calibrated"
    soh_dialog_source_user / _source_auto
    soh_dialog_model_not_selected / _capacity_not_detected
    (and 5 more)

Because the Flutter dialog is a STUB.
`flutter_ui/lib/screens/diagnostics/diagnostics_screen.dart` only ever renders
`battery_health_title`, `battery_health_unavailable` and
`battery_health_unavailable_desc` -- lines 273, 404, 410, 417. It never shows the
model, the pack capacity, the effective capacity or the calibration date. The
native UI did. The strings were ported; the dialog was not.

## Other clusters worth checking the same way

Counts are of UNREFERENCED keys under a widened scan (bare key name as a word,
across flutter_ui/lib, flutter_ui/test and the Flutter module's Kotlin, excluding
lib/gen and lib/l10n):

    settings   43     vehicle  42     dashboard  34     cd  29
    toast      23     soh      13     diagnostics 11    battery 10
    log         8     daemon    5     zrok        4     others ~22

Spot-checked examples, each of which may be a stub, a not-yet-wired label, or
genuinely dead -- they need looking at individually:

    vehicle_dialog_capacity_label / _suffix / _helper / _reset  (capacity dialog)
    settings_about_support_section / _support_share_title / _share_value
    cd_* (29 content descriptions -- may indicate MISSING accessibility labels)
    log_entry_default_timestamp / _tag / _message  (look like demo placeholders)
    toast_app_up_to_date  (the in-app OTA updater was removed in 13e5366 -- this
                           one probably IS dead)

## What to do

1. Go cluster by cluster. For each, decide: STUB (build the missing UI), NOT WIRED
   (connect the existing label), or DEAD (feature removed -- delete the key from
   all 19 catalogs).
2. The `cd_*` group deserves particular attention: content descriptions going
   unreferenced usually means widgets have NO accessibility label, which is an
   a11y gap, not surplus strings.
3. Delete only what is genuinely dead, in one pass across all 19 catalogs --
   `validateArbCatalogs` enforces key parity and will fail if one is left behind.
   Remove the `@key` metadata from app_en.arb too.
4. Record the verdict per cluster here, so the next person does not re-derive it.

## Reproduce the scan

    python3 - <<'PY'
    import json, pathlib, re, collections
    keys=[k for k in json.load(open("flutter_ui/lib/l10n/app_en.arb")) if not k.startswith("@")]
    blob=[]
    for r in [pathlib.Path("flutter_ui/lib"), pathlib.Path("flutter_ui/test"),
              pathlib.Path("flutter_ui/android/app/src/main/kotlin")]:
        for f in r.rglob("*"):
            if f.is_file() and f.suffix in (".dart",".kt") and "/lib/gen/" not in str(f) and "/lib/l10n/" not in str(f):
                blob.append(f.read_text(errors="ignore"))
    present=set(re.findall(r"[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*", "\n".join(blob)))
    dead=[k for k in keys if k not in present]
    print(len(keys), len(dead))
    print(collections.Counter(k.split('_')[0] for k in dead).most_common(15))
    PY

## Constraints

- Do NOT mass-delete on the count. That is the whole point of this issue: the
  keys are mostly evidence, not litter.
- Do NOT hand-edit the .arb files; json round-trip, re-parse, assert the key set
  changed by exactly the intended keys.
- Do NOT modify `web/` -- it has its own catalogs and its own key set.
- Do NOT commit.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every cluster above has a recorded verdict: STUB, NOT WIRED, or DEAD.
- [ ] Any key deleted as DEAD is gone from all 19 catalogs and from app_en.arb's
      @metadata, and the feature it described is confirmed absent from the code.
- [ ] The `cd_*` cluster is answered specifically: are those widgets missing
      accessibility labels?
- [ ] Any STUB found is filed as its own issue with the screen named, starting
      with the Battery health dialog.
- [ ] `./gradlew validateArbCatalogs validateAndroidStrings` pass; `flutter
      analyze` clean; `flutter test --coverage` at or above 99.97%.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the
build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is
ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
close_reason:
## First: this task's central premise was WRONG, and I filed it

I filed this claiming the unreferenced keys are "mostly unbuilt UI" with the
Battery-health dialog as the worked example. That is incorrect.

The dialog is not an unfinished port. It was DELIBERATELY REDUCED in
BladeWatch-p7vi, and diagnostics_screen.dart says so at the point of the change:
"the Source/Method/Capacity rows and the Reset SOH Estimation action are gone with
the feature -- the daemon's endpoints are stubs that refuse every call, so the
reset could never do anything either." p7vi's close reason confirms it.

I reached the wrong conclusion by reading the catalogs and the screen, and not the
history of the screen. The correct reading is the opposite of what I filed: most
of these keys are from features REMOVED ON PURPOSE, which makes them safe to
delete rather than evidence to preserve.

## Verdicts

    cluster                      verdict        action
    cd_*                         NOT WIRED      FIXED (see below)
    soh_dialog_* (8)             DEAD  p7vi     deleted
    toast_soh_* (3)              DEAD  p7vi     deleted
    vehicle_dialog_* (15)        DEAD  p7vi     deleted
    battery_health_* (10)        DEAD  p7vi     deleted
    dashboard_insight_* (15)     DEAD           deleted
    log_entry_default_* (3)      DEAD  81g9.2   deleted
