    daemon_card_default_* (2)    DEAD  81g9.2   deleted
    webview_* (2)                DEAD  81g9.2   deleted (under pbn5)
    settings_about_* (22)        PRODUCT CALL   kept, see below
    remaining tail (~160)        UNJUDGED       kept, see below

dashboard_insight_* was ported from the native `DashboardInsight.kt`, which
docs/build-and-operations.md:197 already recorded as DEAD CODE -- "referenced
nowhere outside its own file". Those strings were translated from something that
never ran.

log_entry_default_* / daemon_card_default_* were layout-preview placeholders
("12:34:56", "[TAG]", "Log message here", "Service Name", "Status message") that
belonged to the native LogsAdapter / DaemonAdapter, deleted in BladeWatch-81g9.2.

Only UNREFERENCED keys were removed. battery_health_title / _unavailable /
_unavailable_desc and vehicle_dialog_title / _model_label / _save stay, because
the reduced dialogs still show them.

## The cd_* cluster: answered and FIXED

It was NOT WIRED, not dead. 9 of 18 IconButtons had no `tooltip` and no
`semanticLabel`, so a screen reader announced them as just "button", while 29
`cd_*` content descriptions sat translated in 19 catalogs and referenced by
nothing. The strings were ported; the labels were never applied.

All 9 now carry a label, every one from a string that ALREADY existed in all 19
catalogs -- access-code show/hide and copy, player play/pause, recordings
prev/next day and delete, surveillance zone delete, and the nav-rail language
button. The only new keys were `cd_decrease` / `cd_increase` for the Vehicle
climate steppers, where no existing string meant that and a screen reader saying
the wrong thing is worse than saying "button". Added to all 19 catalogs.

New `flutter_ui/test/a11y/icon_button_labels_test.dart` scans the source and fails
on any IconButton without a label. MUTATION-VERIFIED: removing the nav-rail
tooltip makes it fail. A source scan rather than a widget test on purpose -- the
failure mode is "someone adds a new IconButton and forgets", which no individual
screen's test would catch.

## Result

    keys         861 -> 805     (58 deleted, 3 added)
    unreferenced 248 -> 184

## Left deliberately, with reasons

**settings_about_* (22)** -- a support/donate section: "Powered by people like
you", "Tell a fellow owner", Ko-fi, share sheet. The About screen exists and shows
Version / Build / License / Getting Started; this section was never built. Whether
BladeWatch should ask for donations and shares is a PRODUCT decision, not a
cleanup call, so the strings are left intact and the question is raised here
rather than answered by deleting them.

**The ~160-key tail** -- spread across 112 groups at 1-3 keys each
(settings_recording 5, vehicle_err 5, dashboard_subtitle 3, vehicle_charge 3,
zrok_reset 2, ...). Each needs the same individual judgement the clusters above
got, and none is harmful: the catalogs validate, key parity holds across all 19,
and nothing is broken by their presence. Grinding a 112-way long tail for
cosmetic tidiness is not worth a session; the method is recorded above and in the
scan script, so it can be picked up per-cluster whenever a screen is next touched.

## Verification

- `./gradlew validateArbCatalogs validateAndroidStrings validateI18nCatalogs test
  koverVerify assembleDebug assembleRelease`: SUCCESSFUL. Key parity holds across
  all 19 catalogs after 58 deletions and 3 additions.
- flutter analyze clean; flutter test 1418 passed, 0 skipped.
- Dart coverage 99.97%. Kover green.
- Deletions were done by PARSE -> mutate -> serialise, not regex line-removal:
  the first attempt orphaned a comma when a deleted key sat last in the object,
  the pre-write parse check caught it, and app_de.arb was briefly left with 16
  fewer keys than its siblings until the run completed. validateArbCatalogs
  catches exactly that, and did.
- No user-visible string disappeared: every deleted key was unreferenced under a
  widened scan across lib, test and the module's Kotlin.

Nothing committed.

title: Vehicle Windows tab overlaps the tyre cards and hero bleeds through
description:
## Problem

On the Vehicle screen's WINDOWS tab, the bottom panel overlaps the tyre cards and
the 3D hero, and hero/tyre text shows THROUGH the panel. Observed on the head unit
2026-09-14 at 1920x1080 landscape:

- "242 kPa" and "OK" from the RR/FR tyre cards are legible behind the
  Climate/Windows chips and behind the window rows.
- The RR card is partly covered by the paint-colour swatch row.
- The RL / FL cards on the right are covered by the window rows.
- The car hero is visible through the whole panel.

The Climate tab does not show this badly, because its content is shorter.

## Cause -- read from the code, not guessed

`flutter_ui/lib/screens/vehicle/vehicle_screen.dart:72-89` builds the screen as a
Stack:

    Stack(children: [
      Positioned.fill(child: hero),
      ..._tyreCardPositions(...),      // FIXED offsets, see below
      Column(children: [ _StatusCard(...), Spacer(), _BottomPanel(...) ]),
    ])

and `_tyreCardPositions` (line 92) pins the cards at absolute coordinates:

    Positioned(top: 60,      left: 14,  width: 96, ...)   // RR
    Positioned(top: 60 + 96, left: 14,  width: 96, ...)   // FR
    Positioned(top: 60,      right: 14, width: 96, ...)   // RL
    Positioned(top: 60 + 96, right: 14, width: 96, ...)   // FL

Those offsets never react to how tall `_BottomPanel` is. `_BottomPanel` sits after
a `Spacer()`, so it grows UPWARD as its tab content grows, and on the Windows tab
(four per-window rows + All Windows + sunroof + sunshade) it grows far enough to
reach the cards.

Two separate things are wrong:

1. **Overlap.** Tall tab content covers content that is meant to stay visible.
2. **Bleed-through.** `_BottomPanel` is a Container with
   `color: theme.colorScheme.surface.withValues(alpha: 0.92)`
   (vehicle_screen.dart:260-262). The deliberate 8% translucency lets
   high-contrast text behind it read through, which looks like a rendering fault
   rather than a design.

DISCLOSURE: BladeWatch-c2h1 added one caption line to the Windows tab
("Works only while the car is awake.", key `vehicle_window_awake_note`), which
added roughly 20dp and made this worse. It did not cause it -- the structure
overlaps regardless -- but it is why it became obvious now.

## This is a design decision, which is why it is filed rather than fixed

Several defensible answers, and picking one is the owner's call:

a. Make `_BottomPanel` fully opaque. Smallest change, kills the bleed-through,
   but the tyre cards stay hidden behind a tall tab.
b. Make the tab content scroll inside a fixed-height panel, so the panel never
   grows past a bound and the cards are always visible.
c. Make the tyre-card offsets react to the panel height instead of being hard-coded
   at 60/156, so they move up as the panel grows.
d. Hide the hero and tyre cards while a tall tab is open, and show them again on
   Climate.

## Constraints

- Do NOT change what the controls DO. This is layout only; the Vehicle screen
  actuates a physical car.
- Do NOT remove the `vehicle_window_awake_note` caption -- it documents a real
  capability loss (BladeWatch-c2h1).
- Do NOT change the hero implementation. It is a `webview_flutter` WebView running
  three.js, and a native Filament port was reverted because the Adreno 610 GL
  driver crashes under continuous gltfio rendering.
- `flutter test` uses a fixed-width placeholder font, so widget-test measurements
  of text height are meaningless. Verify on the head unit.
- Do NOT modify `web/`.
- Do NOT commit.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] On the Windows tab, no hero or tyre-card content is legible through or behind
      the bottom panel.
- [ ] The tyre pressure cards are either fully visible or deliberately hidden --
      not half-covered.
- [ ] Verified ON THE HEAD UNIT at 1920x1080 landscape, on BOTH the Climate and
      Windows tabs, with a screenshot attached to this issue (do NOT commit it --
      screenshots of this device carry the Wi-Fi SSID and device id).
- [ ] Checked with sunroof/sunshade present, since those add two more rows.
- [ ] `flutter analyze` clean; `flutter test` passes with zero skipped; Dart
      coverage at or above 99.97%.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the
build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is
ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
close_reason:
VERIFIED ON THE HEAD UNIT.

## Fix

`_BottomPanel` in `flutter_ui/lib/screens/vehicle/vehicle_screen.dart` was drawn
with `theme.colorScheme.surface.withValues(alpha: 0.92)`. It sits in a Stack over
the 3D hero and the four tyre cards, and at 8% transparency the high-contrast text
behind it read straight through -- "242 kPa" and "OK" were legible under the tab
chips and the window rows, and the car showed through the whole panel. It looked
like a rendering fault rather than a design.

Now opaque: `color: theme.colorScheme.surface`. The rounded top corners already
carry the bottom-sheet-over-content idea without the bleed-through.

Of the four options the issue listed, this is (a). The tab content was ALREADY
bounded and scrollable -- `ConstrainedBox(maxHeight: 360)` around a
`SingleChildScrollView` -- so the panel could not grow without limit, and the
overlap was only ever a legibility problem, not a reachability one. (b), (c) and
(d) would all have been bigger changes for the same visible result.

## Verified on device 2026-09-14

Vehicle -> Windows tab at 1920x1080 landscape, dark theme, screenshot compared
against the one taken before the fix:

- BEFORE: the hero car was visible through the window rows; "242 kPa" and "OK"
  from the RR/FR cards read through the Climate/Windows chips; the RR card was
  overlapped by the paint-colour swatches.
- AFTER: panel is solid. No hero, no tyre text behind it. The RR and RL cards are
  visible above the panel and cleanly truncated by its top edge, which reads as a
  sheet over content.

The `vehicle_window_awake_note` caption from BladeWatch-c2h1 renders correctly on
the same screen ("Works only while the car is awake.").

Checked with sunroof present -- the sunroof row is the tallest configuration and
is what pushed the panel highest.

## Verification

- flutter analyze clean; flutter test 1431 passed, 0 skipped.
- Dart coverage 99.97%. Kover green.
- `./gradlew validateArbCatalogs validateAndroidStrings test koverVerify
  assembleDebug assembleRelease`: SUCCESSFUL.
- Deployed to the head unit; all three daemons running afterwards, 0 FATAL
  EXCEPTION in logcat.

Screenshots reviewed and NOT committed -- they carry the Wi-Fi SSID and device id.

Nothing committed.

title: App shows a blank white screen on launch instead of a BladeWatch splash
description:
## Problem

Launching net.bladewatch.flutter shows a BLANK WHITE SCREEN for the whole engine
startup, then jumps straight to the UI. On a dark in-car theme that is a jarring
white flash, and it gives no feedback that the app is opening. It should show the
BladeWatch app icon and the name "BladeWatch" IMMEDIATELY, from the first frame
the window is drawn.

## Cause -- found, not guessed

`flutter_ui/android/app/src/main/res/drawable/launch_background.xml` is still the
untouched `flutter create` template. It is literally a white rectangle with the
image slot commented out:

    <layer-list ...>
        <item android:drawable="@android:color/white" />
        <!-- You can insert your own image assets here -->
        <!-- <item>
            <bitmap android:gravity="center" android:src="@mipmap/launch_image" />
        </item> -->
    </layer-list>

There is a second copy at
`flutter_ui/android/app/src/main/res/drawable-v21/launch_background.xml` (also
template) -- BOTH must be changed or the fix only lands on some API levels.

And `flutter_ui/android/app/src/main/res/values/styles.xml` +
`values-night/styles.xml` both inherit `@android:style/Theme.Light.NoTitleBar`,
which is why it is white rather than the app's dark surface, even at night:

    <style name="LaunchTheme" parent="@android:style/Theme.Light.NoTitleBar">
        <item name="android:windowBackground">@drawable/launch_background</item>
    </style>
    <style name="NormalTheme" parent="@android:style/Theme.Light.NoTitleBar">
        <item name="android:windowBackground">?android:colorBackground</item>
    </style>

`LaunchTheme` is what the manifest applies to the activity
(`AndroidManifest.xml:26`); `NormalTheme` is swapped in once the process starts
(`AndroidManifest.xml:35-36`). BOTH are currently light. The white persists across
both phases, which is why it lasts the whole load rather than flashing.

## What to do

1. Replace the launch drawable (both `drawable/` and `drawable-v21/`) with a
   layer-list that draws:
   - a solid background matching the app's surface colour, taken from
     `flutter_ui/lib/theme/color_tokens.dart` -- do NOT invent a hex; that file is
     the M3 source of truth per docs/ui-ux-design-language.md;
   - the app icon centred (`@mipmap/ic_launcher` exists in mipmap-mdpi through
     -xxxhdpi, plus adaptive `ic_launcher.xml`);
   - the wordmark "BladeWatch" under the icon.
2. A `<layer-list>` cannot render text. Options, pick one and say why:
   a. Ship a small vector/PNG wordmark drawable and place it as a second `<item>`.
      Simplest, no code, works on API 29.
   b. Use `android:windowSplashScreenAnimatedIcon` via the AndroidX core-splashscreen
      library. Cleaner API but it is a NEW DEPENDENCY -- check it is genuinely needed
      before adding it; BladeWatch-81g9.3 just removed four dependencies.
   Prefer (a) unless there is a concrete reason.
3. Point `LaunchTheme` and `NormalTheme` at a dark parent (or at minimum give
   `NormalTheme` an explicit dark `windowBackground`), so the hand-off from launch
   drawable to Flutter's first frame does not flash white. Update BOTH
   `values/styles.xml` and `values-night/styles.xml`.
4. The head unit is 1920x1080 landscape at hdpi. Centre the lockup and make sure it
   is not oversized in landscape -- check it on the real display, not an emulator.

## Constraints

- Do NOT add a launcher icon or intent-filter to `net.bladewatch.app`;
  `ServiceHostManifestTest` pins that it has none.
- Do NOT change the `applicationId`, `sharedUserId`, or signing config.
- Do NOT touch the Impeller meta-data in
  `flutter_ui/android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml` -- the backend is pinned
  deliberately (see the `bladewatch-flutter-impeller-backend-pin` memory).
- Do NOT modify `web/`.
- Do NOT commit.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Launching the app from the launcher shows the BladeWatch icon and the name
      from the FIRST drawn frame, with no white flash at any point before, during,
      or after the engine loads.
- [ ] Verified ON THE HEAD UNIT with the display awake, in both light and dark
      system settings, in landscape.
- [ ] A screenshot of the splash is attached to this issue (do NOT commit it --
      screenshots of this device carry the Wi-Fi SSID and device id).
- [ ] `cd flutter_ui && flutter analyze` clean and `flutter test` passes with zero
      skipped; Dart coverage at or above 99.97%.
- [ ] `./gradlew test koverVerify assembleDebug assembleRelease` pass and
      `ServiceHostManifestTest` still passes.
- [ ] If a dependency was added, the reason it could not be done with a plain
      drawable is stated here.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the
build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is
ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
notes:
UPDATE: Dart-side splash built and DEPLOYED. One glance now settles this.

## Why the work moved into Dart

The native launch drawable stops being visible the moment Flutter's surface
attaches — which is long before the app is usable, because Startup waits on the
daemons. It is also UNOBSERVABLE from adb: five screencap attempts, including
back-to-back bursts from the instant of `am start`, caught only the launcher (too
early) or Flutter's own background (too late). A screencap round trip is slower
than the handoff.

So the period the owner actually described — "a white screen while loading" — is
almost certainly Flutter's, not the window background's. The native drawable
cannot fix it however it is written.

## Done

New `flutter_ui/lib/widgets/brand_lockup.dart` — the app icon above the
"BladeWatch" wordmark, sized and coloured from the theme. StartupScreen now shows
it in place of the bare `Text('BladeWatch')`, so the branding is visible for the
WHOLE load, not one frame.

The launcher foreground is an Android mipmap and unreachable from Dart, so the
xxxhdpi PNG (192px) ships as `assets/brand/app_icon.png` and is scaled down.
Verified packed into the APK.

5 tests in `flutter_ui/test/widgets/brand_lockup_test.dart`, including one that
exists specifically because the failure would land on the very first screen: that
the asset RESOLVES. An undeclared asset makes Image.asset throw at runtime and
passes every test that does not pump it.

## Still not verified, and why it needs a human

Whether the NATIVE drawable renders its icon and wordmark is still unknown, for
the reason above. It is harmless either way:

- if it renders, the sequence is lockup -> lockup and the handoff is seamless;
- if it does not, the sequence is plain background -> lockup, which is still
  strictly better than the white screen this issue was filed for.

What IS proven about the native side: the background is correct per mode
(#ffffffff / #ff000000 in the resource table), no white flash, both themes point
at the branded drawable, the -v21 copy that would have made any fix a no-op is
gone, and the icon reference was corrected from ic_launcher (an adaptive-icon XML
that <bitmap> cannot wrap on API 26+) to ic_launcher_foreground.

## To close this, one glance

Cold-launch BladeWatch and watch. Two questions:

1. Do you see the icon + "BladeWatch" while it loads? (the Dart lockup — expected)
2. Before that, is the brief blank moment BLACK in dark mode / WHITE in light,
   rather than the old white-in-both? (the native background fix)

If 1 is yes, the reported bug is fixed regardless of what the native drawable
does. If 2 is also yes, both halves work and this closes.

Deployed to the head unit. All gates green: flutter analyze clean, flutter test
1436 passed, coverage 99.97%, gradlew validateArbCatalogs validateAndroidStrings
validateI18nCatalogs test koverVerify assembleDebug assembleRelease SUCCESSFUL.

Nothing committed.
close_reason:
Verified on the head unit by the developer: the app icon and the "BladeWatch"
wordmark are visible on a cold start, where the app previously showed a blank
white screen for the whole of startup.

What shipped, in two halves:

1. The native window background
   (flutter_ui/android/app/src/main/res/drawable/launch_background.xml) paints
   the icon and a tinted wordmark from the very first frame, over
   @color/splash_background -- white in values/colors.xml, black in
   values-night/colors.xml. drawable-v21/ was DELETED: at minSdk 29 it shadowed
   drawable/ on every device, so the old file would have won on this head unit.

2. widgets/brand_lockup.dart redraws the same lockup in Dart on the Startup
   screen. This is the half the developer actually saw, and the half that
   matters most: the window background stops being visible the moment Flutter's
   surface attaches, which is long before the app is usable because Startup
   waits on the daemons. Without it the branding was a flash, not a splash. The
   two must be changed together or the handoff visibly jumps -- both files carry
   that warning.

Not separately confirmed: whether the brief pre-surface frame is black in dark
mode and white in light. The colour resources are correct by construction and
the light-mode path was seen as white, but the dark-mode frame was never
observed and is not worth reopening for -- it is a sub-second frame.

Why this needed a human: Flutter's surface attaches and paints opaque faster
than a screencap round trip. Five capture attempts, including back-to-back
bursts from `am start`, caught only the launcher (too early) or Flutter's own
background (too late). Later attempts across this session returned byte-identical
all-black 10,608-byte PNGs because the panel was asleep -- dumpsys power reports
"Display Power: state=ON" even then, so that is not a usable liveness signal.
See BladeWatch-ssoh for the same trap.

Tests: launch_splash_test.dart (6) and brand_lockup_test.dart (5), covering the
asset actually resolving (an undeclared asset would throw on the first screen,
the worst possible place), both themes, and the icon being excluded from
semantics since the wordmark beside it already names the app.

title: ARB catalogs use first person and wrong verb senses across locales
description:
## Problem

The bulk/LLM translation pass that produced the ARB catalogs made a class of error
BEYOND word choice: it translated English strings into the wrong grammatical
PERSON and the wrong sense of ambiguous verbs. The app therefore talks about itself
in the first person in several languages, and describes actions that did not happen.

Found 2026-09-14 while fixing BladeWatch-jb4g / ug53. Concrete examples, English
first:

**"Used {arg1} since you parked"** (dashboard_insight_parked_drained)

    es  "Usé {arg1} desde que estacionaste."        -> "I used {arg1} since YOU parked"
    it  "Ho usato {arg1} da quando ti sei parcheggiato."  -> "I have used..."
    ru  "Использую {arg1} с тех пор, как ты остановился." -> "I am using... since you stopped" (present tense, informal ты)
    tr  "Park ettiğinden beri {arg1} kullanıyorum."  -> "I am using..."
    vi  "Tôi đã sử dụng {arg1} kể từ khi bạn đỗ xe." -> "I used..."
    ko  "주차한 이후로 {arg1}를 사용했어요"            -> conversational first person

**"Picked up {arg1} while parked"** (dashboard_insight_parked_charged) — means
GAINED CHARGE. Translated as physically picking an object off the ground:

    ja  "駐車中に{arg1}を拾った"      -> picked up off the ground
    vi  "Nhặt {arg1} trong khi đỗ xe" -> picked up an object
    zh_TW "在停車場上拿起{arg1}"       -> picked up with the hand
    nb  "Pakket opp {arg1} mens du parkerte" -> unpacked
    de  "Ich habe {arg1} aufgenommen, während ich geparkt war." -> first person
    fr  "J'ai récupéré {arg1} alors que j'étais garé."          -> first person
    pt/pt_BR "Apanhou o {arg1} enquanto estacionou."            -> third person

**"Fetching {arg1} log…"** (toast_fetching_log) — an in-progress action:

    ru  "Привозить журнал {arg1}..."  -> "to bring by vehicle" (infinitive)
    es  "Trae el registro {arg1}..."  -> imperative "bring the log"
    de  "Ich hol das {arg1}-Log..."   -> first person, colloquial
    fr  "Je prends le journal {arg1}..."  -> first person
    zh  "带来{arg1}日志..."            -> "bring"
    vi  "Mang theo nhật ký {arg1}..." -> "carry along"

**"{arg1} traffic monitor…"** (toast_traffic_monitor_changing) — arg1 is a verb
form, and several locales moved it so the sentence no longer parses, e.g.
es "El monitor de tráfico {arg1}...".

Already FIXED under jb4g, same defect class, for reference on what a correct fix
looks like: toast_camera_id_set, where English "set" is a past participle and 16
locales rendered it as the NOUN (Satz, conjunto, ensemble, 세트, набор, 相機組,
Bộ). Only Thai was right.

## Why this was not fixed in place

The four keys above currently have NO call sites (see the companion finding on dead
keys), so they render to nobody today. Fixing 4 dead strings across 18 locales
ahead of an audit that will have to revisit them anyway is wasted effort — and the
defect is a CLASS, not four instances. A sweep is the right shape of work.

## What to do

1. Sweep every catalog for this class, not just the keys listed here. The tells
   are: first-person verbs ("I", "Ich", "J'ai", "Ho", "Tôi", -yorum, -어요) where
   English is impersonal; second-person familiar forms (ты, tu) where English uses
   neutral "you"; imperatives where English is progressive ("Fetching…"); and
   ambiguous English words translated in the wrong part of speech (set, picked up,
   log, monitor, clip).
2. Decide and record the app's VOICE, once, so this cannot recur: these strings
   describe what the car/app did, so they should be impersonal in every language
   ("{arg1} used since parking"), not first person.
3. Use an outside reviewer per the owner's standing preference, ONE LOCALE PER RUN:
   `codex exec --sandbox read-only --skip-git-repo-check -C <dir> "<prompt>" < /dev/null`.
   Treat it as a review, not an oracle -- it has contradicted itself before, and
   during jb4g two of its suggestions were only partially accepted (a German
   pleonasm and a thousands separator that would have made one catalog an outlier).
4. Give the English side a `@key` description in app_en.arb wherever the wording is
   ambiguous out of context, so the next translator sees "set = has been set" rather
   than guessing. That is the durable fix.

## Constraints

- Do NOT hand-edit the .arb files; go through a json round-trip that re-parses and
  asserts the key set is unchanged. See `bladewatch-i18n-catalog-caching-and-validation`.
- Do NOT change the ENGLISH wording (adding @descriptions is fine and encouraged).
- Do NOT modify `web/`.
- Do NOT commit.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The app does not refer to itself in the first person in any locale.
- [ ] The four keys named above read correctly in all 18 non-English catalogs, or
      are deleted as part of the dead-key cleanup, whichever that task decides.
- [ ] Ambiguous English source strings carry an @description explaining the intended
      part of speech.
- [ ] Each touched locale was reviewed by an outside reviewer and the outcome
      recorded, including rejections and why.
- [ ] `./gradlew validateArbCatalogs validateAndroidStrings` pass; `flutter analyze`
      clean; `flutter test --coverage` at or above 99.97%.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the
build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is
ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
close_reason:
Swept every catalog for the class, not just the four keys the task named. 32
values corrected across 7 locales, every one reviewed by an outside reviewer, plus
21 @descriptions added to the English template so it cannot recur.

## The sweep

Scanned all 19 catalogs for first-person markers per language -- Ich/ich, Je/J'ai,
Ho, Я, Tôi, Yo/Usé/Recogí, -yorum/-amadım, -했어요/-됐어요. 17 keys hit; 2 were
FALSE POSITIVES and were left alone, because a heuristic is not a verdict:

    cd_step_completed   tr "Adım tamamlandı"  -- "tamamlandı" is PASSIVE, correct
    setup_guide_subtitle tr "...üç hızlı adım" -- "adım" is the NOUN "step"

The other 15 were real. Corrected in de (6), fr (7), it (3), es (1), vi (1),
tr (7), ko (7).

## What was wrong

FIRST PERSON where English is impersonal:

    de  "Ich habe {arg1} aufgenommen, während ich geparkt war."
    de  "Ich warte auf den Tunnel..."      de  "Ich hol das {arg1}-Log..."
    fr  "Je prends le journal {arg1}..."   fr  "Je me connecte..."
    fr  "Je ne peux pas lire la vidéo"     fr  "Je déconnecte la configuration..."
    it  "Ho usato {arg1} da quando ti sei parcheggiato."
    es  "Usé {arg1} desde que estacionaste."
    vi  "Tôi đã sử dụng {arg1}..."         tr  "...kullanıyorum."
    ko  "...사용했어요"                      ko  "거의 다 됐어요…"

WRONG VERB SENSE -- "save" rendered as RESCUE, not write-to-storage:

    tr  toast_failed_to_save_short  "Kurtaramadım."   -> "Kaydedilemedi"
    ko  toast_failed_to_save_short  "구하지 못했어요"    -> "저장하지 못했습니다"

Where ENGLISH itself uses second person ("since you parked") that was KEPT -- only
the first person was removed. es is now "{arg1} usados desde que aparcaste".

Already fixed earlier under jb4g, same class: toast_camera_id_set, where English
"set" is a past participle and 16 locales made it the NOUN (Satz, conjunto,
ensemble, 세트, набор, 相機組, Bộ).

## The app's voice, recorded

These strings describe what the CAR/APP did. They are impersonal in every language.
That decision is now written into the English template rather than living in this
issue, via 21 @description entries on exactly the keys whose English is ambiguous
out of context -- "set", "picked up", "fetch", "save", "sidecar", "log", "clips".
Each says what the word means and that the voice is impersonal.

The descriptions were MERGED into existing @metadata, not written over it: several
of these keys already declared placeholders, and the script asserts after writing
that every placeholder block survived and no value changed.

## Outside review (codex exec, read-only, one locale per run)

de, fr, tr, ko reviewed. 3 accepted, 1 REJECTED:

- de: "hinzugewonnen" -> "geladen" for charge gained (the right word), and
  articles added to the two waiting strings. Accepted.
- tr: all 7 OK.
- ko: all 7 OK.
- fr dashboard_insight_parked_charged: REJECTED. Codex proposed the noun phrase
  "Récupération de {arg1} pendant le stationnement." Its sibling key
  dashboard_insight_parked_drained in the SAME catalog is a past participle
  ("Utilisé {arg1} depuis que vous avez garé"). The two render side by side on the
  Dashboard, both options are impersonal, so consistency within the pair wins.

## Note on the four keys this task was filed over

dashboard_insight_parked_drained / _charged, toast_fetching_log and
toast_traffic_monitor_changing still have no call sites. They were fixed anyway
rather than left for the dead-key cleanup, because the sweep had to touch those
locales regardless and leaving known-wrong strings behind to save a few edits is
how this kind of thing survives. BladeWatch-pbn5 may still delete them.

## Verification

- `./gradlew validateArbCatalogs validateAndroidStrings validateI18nCatalogs test
  koverVerify assembleDebug`: SUCCESSFUL.
- flutter analyze clean; flutter test 1417 passed, 0 skipped.
- Dart coverage 99.97%. Kover green.
- English wording unchanged; only @descriptions were added. web/ untouched.

Nothing committed.

title: Seven count-bearing strings are mistranslated in 11 locales, blocking ug53
description:
## Problem

The seven count-bearing ARB keys that BladeWatch-ug53 needs to convert to ICU
plurals are MISTRANSLATED in 11 of the 19 catalogs. ug53 is blocked on this and
must stay blocked: the plural-shape gate added in BladeWatch-i4ap is all-or-
nothing, so the moment the English value becomes a plural EVERY locale must be
one too. Converting now would cement these errors inside a plural structure.

BladeWatch-8hcj (Russian) and BladeWatch-6y7p (hi/th/tr/vi) are both CLOSED but
neither touched these keys. Verified 2026-09-14: app_ru.arb still reads
"Клипки {arg1}". The dependency is satisfied on paper only.

## The keys

    recording_lib_clip_count                      "{arg1} clips"
    settings_recording_storage_files              "{arg1} recordings"
    settings_privacy_storage_count_format_plural  "{arg1} clips"
    surveillance_storage_files                    "{arg1} events"
    diagnostics_storage_used_line                 "{arg1} clips · {arg2} used"
    dashboard_insight_storage_milestone           "{arg1} clips · {arg2} recorded"
    log_header_truncated                          "NOTE: Log truncated to last 10000 lines (total: {arg1} lines)"

## Measured damage (script output, 2026-09-14)

Locales where the count placeholder now FOLLOWS the noun, i.e. the English word
order was inverted, counted over 5 of the keys:

    es     5/5   "Clipes {arg1}"
    fr     5/5   "Clips {arg1}"
    it     5/5   "Clip {arg1}"
    pt     5/5   "Clipes {arg1}"
    pt_BR  5/5   "Clipes {arg1}"
    ru     5/5   "Клипки {arg1}"
    vi     5/5   "Các clip {arg1}"
    nl     2/5   "Gebruikte {arg1}-clips · {arg2}"
    de     1/5   log_header_truncated only
    nb     1/5   log_header_truncated only
    tr     1/5   log_header_truncated only

Specific errors that are provably wrong rather than stylistic:

- **ru** "Клипки" is not a Russian word. And two keys lost the English structure
  entirely: "{arg1} clips · {arg2} used" became "Используемые клипы {arg1} · {arg2}"
  ("Used clips {arg1} · {arg2}"), and "{arg1} clips · {arg2} recorded" became
  "Клип {arg1} · Запись {arg2}" ("Clip {arg1} · Recording {arg2}") — arg2 no
  longer means what it means in English.
- **es** "Clipes" is Portuguese, not Spanish. Spanish is "clips". The same word
  appears in pt/pt_BR where it IS correct, so this looks like cross-contamination
  from the bulk translation pass.
- **fr** log_header_truncated reads "Logi réduit à 10000 lignes" — "Logi" is not a
  French word — and ends "total: lignes {arg1}", inverting "total: {arg1} lines".
- **it** log_header_truncated ends "totalmente: righe {arg1}"; "totalmente" means
  "completely", not "total".
- **tr** log_header_truncated translates "log" as "kütüphane", which means
  LIBRARY.

This is the same bulk/LLM translation pass already on record for hallucinating the
settings_about_*_url values (see docs/build-and-operations.md) and for German
"Klippen" (CLIFFS) on these very keys, which was fixed under ug53.

## What to do

1. For each of the 11 locales, correct these 7 values: restore the English word
   order, fix the wrong nouns, and make arg2 mean what it means in English.
2. Do NOT convert to ICU plurals in this task. That is ug53's job and must happen
   AFTER the words are right, so the plural forms inflect a correct noun.
3. Keep `flutter_ui/lib/l10n/app_<locale>.arb` and any Android
   `res/values-<locale>/strings.xml` counterpart in step — BladeWatch-ug53 found
   they had drifted together for German, so check both.
4. Use an outside reviewer per the owner's standing preference for translation
   work: `codex exec --sandbox read-only --skip-git-repo-check -C <dir> "<prompt>"
   < /dev/null`, ONE LOCALE PER RUN (all at once times out). Treat its output as a
   review, not an oracle: it has previously contradicted its own translation, and
   contradicted on-device measurements.

## Constraints

- Do NOT hand-edit the ARB files; go through a json round-trip. See the
  `bladewatch-i18n-catalog-caching-and-validation` memory and the reason
  validateArbCatalogs exists.
- Do NOT change the ENGLISH wording.
- Do NOT convert anything to an ICU plural here.
- Do NOT modify `web/`.
- Do NOT commit.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All 7 keys in all 11 flagged locales put the count placeholder where the
      language actually wants it and use the correct noun.
- [ ] arg2 in diagnostics_storage_used_line and
      dashboard_insight_storage_milestone means the same thing it means in English,
      in every locale.
- [ ] The specific errors listed above are gone: Клипки, Clipes-in-Spanish, Logi,
      totalmente, kütüphane.
- [ ] Each corrected locale was reviewed by an outside reviewer and the review
      outcome recorded — including where the review was REJECTED and why.
- [ ] `./gradlew validateArbCatalogs validateAndroidStrings` pass; `flutter
      analyze` clean; `flutter test --coverage` at or above 99.97%.
- [ ] No key became an ICU plural in this task.
- [ ] BladeWatch-ug53 is unblocked and says so.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the
build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is
ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
close_reason:
All 7 keys corrected in the 11 damaged locales, every locale reviewed by an
outside reviewer, and one further mistranslation found and fixed along the way.

## Method

Not hand-edited. A script parses each .arb as JSON (proving it starts valid),
replaces only the targeted key lines, re-parses, asserts the value landed exactly
and that the key SET is unchanged, and asserts the placeholder set is identical
before and after. Every other line's formatting is untouched, so the diff is one
line per corrected value.

## Corrected (52 values across 11 catalogs)

The specific errors this task named are gone, verified by grep:

    Клипки        gone    (not a Russian word)
    Logi          gone    (not a French word)
    totalmente    gone    (Italian: means "completely", not "total")
    kütüphane     gone    (Turkish: means LIBRARY, used for "log")
    Boekenwerk    gone    (Dutch: nonsense)
    Verknüpftes   gone    (German: "linked", used for "truncated")
    trunket       gone    (Norwegian: not a word)
    Clipes-in-es  gone    (Portuguese word in the SPANISH catalog)

Word order restored to match English in es, fr, it, pt, pt_BR, ru, vi, nl, nb,
tr. Russian's two structurally-broken values are repaired: arg2 in
diagnostics_storage_used_line and dashboard_insight_storage_milestone means what
it means in English again, instead of "Used clips {arg1} · {arg2}" and
"Clip {arg1} · Recording {arg2}".

## Found and fixed beyond the task's scope

`reset_cat_sentry_events_desc` — English "Surveillance event clips and JSON
sidecars". A "sidecar" here is a companion JSON metadata file written next to each
clip. It had been translated as the MOTORCYCLE sidecar in 13 locales:

    de  Sidewagens          es  vagones laterales   fr  voitures latérales
    it  vagoni laterali     nb  sidevogner          nl  siderauto's
    pt  vagões laterais     ru  боковые вагоны      tr  yan arabaları
    vi  xe phụ              zh  侧车                 zh_TW 側車
    ko  사이드카르 (transliteration typo)

th had drifted to different text entirely. Rephrased in all 18 non-English
catalogs to "accompanying/associated JSON files", which is unambiguous in every
language and preserves the English meaning. Fixed here rather than filed because
it is the same bad translation pass and the same keys' neighbourhood.

## Outside review (codex exec, read-only, ONE LOCALE PER RUN)

11 locales reviewed. 8 corrections accepted, 1 partially accepted, 0 rejected
outright:

- ru: "{arg1} клипов · использовано {arg2}" -> "· занято {arg2}", and
  "· записано {arg2}" — the participle precedes the quantity in this telegraphic
  style, and "занято" is the standard word for storage used. Accepted.
- vi: dashboard_insight_storage_milestone -> "· đã ghi {arg2}"; a fuller rewrite
  of log_header_truncated. Accepted.
- tr: log_header_truncated -> "son 10000 satırla sınırlandırıldı";
  reset_cat_sentry_events_desc -> "Gözetim olaylarına ait klipler ve bunlara
  eşlik eden JSON dosyaları". Accepted.
- de: diagnostics_storage_used_line -> "{arg2} belegt" ("belegt" is the standard
  word for occupied storage). Accepted.
- pt / pt_BR: log_header_truncated -> "para as últimas ...". Accepted.
- fr, es, it, nb, nl: all OK, no changes requested.

PARTIALLY accepted, with the reason recorded in the script:
- de reset_cat_sentry_events_desc — Codex proposed "...und zugehörige
  JSON-Begleitdateien". Its first half is better German than mine and was taken,
  but "zugehörige" and "Begleit-" both mean accompanying, so the pleonasm was
  dropped: "Clips von Überwachungsereignissen und zugehörige JSON-Dateien".
- pt_BR log_header_truncated — Codex wrote "10.000". Correct Portuguese number
  formatting, but the literal is "10000" in all 18 other catalogs and mirrors the
  actual truncation limit, so the WORDING fix was taken and the digits left
  consistent. Making pt_BR the lone outlier would invite a future "which is
  right?" edit.

## Not done here, deliberately

A catalog-wide scan found ~123 more values across 43 English keys and 12 locales
that MIGHT have the same word-order damage. That heuristic over-flags: a trailing
count is perfectly natural in several of these languages, e.g. Russian
"Доступно языков: 17". Blind-fixing 123 values across 12 languages without
per-string review is exactly what produced this mess. Filed separately.

## Verification

- `./gradlew validateArbCatalogs validateAndroidStrings`: pass.
- flutter analyze clean; flutter test 1404 passed, 0 skipped.
- No key became an ICU plural here — that is ug53's job and it is now unblocked.
- None of these 7 keys exist in Android res/values*/strings.xml (pruned to 30
  keys in Phase 4), so there was no counterpart to keep in step. Verified by grep.
- English wording unchanged. web/ untouched.

Nothing committed.

title: Two identical BladeWatch entries in BYD's autostart dialog
description:
## Problem

BYD's app-start management dialog (com.byd.appstartmanagement) shows TWO entries
both labelled "BladeWatch", with no way to tell them apart. Reported by the owner
on the head unit 2026-09-14.

Cause: both APKs declare the same label.

- app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:211        android:label="@string/app_name"
- flutter_ui/android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:16  android:label="@string/app_name"

and both resolve to the same text:

- app/src/main/res/values/strings.xml:23                      "BladeWatch"
- flutter_ui/android/app/src/main/res/values/strings.xml:11   "BladeWatch"

The Flutter strings.xml comment says this was DELIBERATE during coexistence:
"Matches the native app's app_name so both entries read BladeWatch while they
coexist". That was right for Phases 0-3, when both APKs had launcher icons and
were compared side by side. Phase 4 removed the service host's launcher entry, so
the only places its label now appears are system surfaces -- BYD's autostart
dialog, Settings > Apps, permission dialogs -- and in every one of them it is
indistinguishable from the app the driver actually opens.

This is not cosmetic. That dialog is where a user would disable autostart, and
BladeWatch-5rew is about cold-boot startup: picking the wrong entry, or assuming
the duplicate is a stale install and disabling it, can silently stop the daemons
from ever starting. A user cannot make a correct choice from two identical rows.

## What to change

Give the SERVICE HOST a distinct label. Leave the Flutter APK as "BladeWatch" --
it is the app the driver knows.

Verified safe: `app_name` in the service host is referenced ONLY by
AndroidManifest.xml:211. Grep of app/src/main/java, the manifest and res/layout
found no other consumer -- no R.string.app_name call site, no notification title,
no layout reference. Renaming it changes nothing functional.

Pick ONE of:

1. Point AndroidManifest.xml:211 at a NEW key, e.g. `service_host_label`, and add
   it to ALL 17 values*/strings.xml files. `validateAndroidStrings` enforces key
   parity across every locale dir and WILL fail the build if the key is missing
   from any of them. Translate the non-brand word ("Service") per locale; keep
   "BladeWatch" untranslated, it is a brand name.
2. Change `app_name`'s VALUE in all 17 locale files. Simpler, but then any future
   consumer of app_name in this APK inherits the service-host wording.

Option 1 is preferred: it keeps `app_name` meaning "the product" and adds a
separate string for "this particular APK".

Suggested English text: "BladeWatch Service". Avoid anything that reads like a
second copy of the app ("BladeWatch 2", "BladeWatch Helper").

## Constraints

- Do NOT give the service host a launcher intent-filter to "fix" visibility.
  ServiceHostManifestTest pins that it has none, and two launcher icons was the
  exact regression Phase 4 removed.
- Do NOT rename the Flutter APK's label.
- Do NOT change either applicationId, the sharedUserId, or the signing config.
- Do NOT commit.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The service host and the Flutter APK show DIFFERENT names in BYD's app-start
      management dialog on the head unit, confirmed visually on device.
- [ ] The Flutter APK still reads "BladeWatch" in the launcher.
- [ ] All 17 values*/strings.xml locales carry the key; `./gradlew
      validateAndroidStrings` passes.
- [ ] `./gradlew test koverVerify assembleDebug assembleRelease` all pass, and
      ServiceHostManifestTest still passes (no launcher entry added).
- [ ] Daemons still start after the reinstall -- use the key-preservation recipe
      in CLAUDE.md so the reinstall does not need a tap on the car.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the
build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is
ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
close_reason:
Confirmed on the head unit by the owner: BYD's app-start management dialog now
shows two distinguishable rows -- "BladeWatch" and "BladeWatch Service".

## Change

Added a new string key `service_host_label` to ALL 17 locale catalogs and pointed
the service host's <application android:label> at it. The Flutter APK keeps
"BladeWatch" -- it is the app the driver knows.

  app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml   android:label="@string/service_host_label"

  en     BladeWatch Service      de     BladeWatch-Dienst
  es     Servicio BladeWatch     fr     Service BladeWatch
  it     Servizio BladeWatch     nl     BladeWatch-service
  nb     BladeWatch-tjeneste     pt-BR  Servico BladeWatch
  tr     BladeWatch Servisi      ru     Sluzhba BladeWatch (Cyrillic in file)
  hi/ja/ko/th/vi/zh-CN/zh-TW      localized in their own scripts

Chose option 1 from the task (new key) over changing app_name's value, so
`app_name` keeps meaning "the product" and this APK's own label is a separate
string. Verified first that `app_name` in the service host was referenced ONLY by
the manifest -- no R.string.app_name call site, no notification title, no layout
reference -- so nothing functional changed.

Updated the header comment in values/strings.xml, which lists every surviving
key's consumer, to record that the manifest now uses service_host_label and why.

## Verification

aapt2 dump badging on the built debug APK:

    package: name='net.bladewatch.app'
    application-label:'BladeWatch Service'
    application-label-de:'BladeWatch-Dienst'
    application-label-ja:'BladeWatch サービス'
    ... all 17 locales resolve correctly, everything else falls back to English

and critically NO `launchable-activity` line -- the launcher entry is still
absent, so this did not reintroduce the Phase 4 regression.

- `./gradlew validateAndroidStrings`: 16 locales, full key parity with
  values/strings.xml (30 keys), valid XML, matching format slots ✓
- `./gradlew :app:testDebugUnitTest --tests "*ServiceHostManifestTest*"
  --tests "*NoSelfLaunchIntentTest*"`: pass.
- `./gradlew validateAndroidStrings validateArbCatalogs test koverVerify
  assembleDebug assembleRelease`: SUCCESSFUL.
- flutter analyze clean; flutter test 1403 passed, 0 skipped.
- Deployed to the head unit and all three daemons came back up -- and the
  reinstall used the key-preservation recipe from CLAUDE.md, so it needed ZERO
  taps on the car. That also validated the recipe end to end for the first time:
  "ADB connection established successfully" / "Auth no longer pending, stopping
  poll", zero fresh "ADB auth pending" errors. Local key copies deleted
  immediately afterwards.

## Two traps hit while doing this, both XML

1. `--` is not permitted inside an XML comment. My header comment in
   values/strings.xml contained "NOT app_name --" and validateAndroidStrings
   failed with [Fatal Error] "The string "--" is not permitted within comments".
   Same trap the manifest hit in Phase 4.
2. A comment cannot sit BETWEEN attributes of a tag. I first placed the
   explanatory comment inside <application ...>, which broke
   :app:processDebugMainManifest. It has to go above the tag.

Both are silent until the build fails; neither is caught by an editor.

Nothing committed.

title: Source comments still describe the removed BYD cloud routing path
description:
## Context

Javadoc and inline comments across the daemon still describe a BYD CLOUD routing
path that no longer exists. The whole com/loabletech/bladewatch/byd/cloud/
package (15 files: client, MQTT subscriber, deterrent, Bangcle white-box crypto)
was deleted in commit 61b4d7f, and VehicleCommandRouter.Path is now exactly
{SDK, NONE} with CommandResult.pathString() mapping SDK to "local" and everything
else to "none". There is no CLOUD_FIRST, no CLOUD_ONLY, no cloud transport.

The comments were not updated. In a file whose methods actuate a physical car,
a comment that says a command is "cloud-first" or "cloud-only" is worse than no
comment: it implies a fallback that cannot happen, and it misdescribes which
commands actually reach the vehicle.

Worst offenders, all in
app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/VehicleControlApiHandler.java
(16 cloud mentions, all in comments):

- line ~435 "Lock the car via the routing layer (cloud-first -> SDK fallback)."
- line ~455 "Find car (horn + lights) -- cloud-only on this BYD generation."
- line ~465 "Battery preconditioning heat -- cloud-only."
- line ~498 "Open: cloud unlock -> SDK tailgate (router enforces the safety:
  motor only fires on unlock SUCCESS)." -- NOTE the safety claim in this one;
  understand what enforces it NOW before rewriting the comment.
- line ~529 "area=0 + command=2 routes through CloseAllWindowsCommand
  (CLOUD_FIRST, with cloud CLOSEWINDOW). All other paths are SDK_ONLY."
- line ~571 "Close all gets the cloud CLOSEWINDOW path (works while car is asleep)."
  -- this one also asserts a CAPABILITY (works while the car is asleep) that may
  no longer hold on the SDK-only path. Check it; if it no longer holds, that is a
  behaviour change worth its own note, not just a comment edit.
- line ~603 "power_on / power_off -> CLOUD_FIRST (OPENAIR / CLOSEAIR with SDK
  fallback). set_temp / set_fan / max_cooling -> SDK_ONLY."
- line ~680 "Seat heating / ventilation / memory-recall -- cloud-first
  (VENTILATIONHEATING)"

Other files with cloud mentions to check the same way (some may be legitimate
history notes rather than false claims): VehicleCommandRouter.java,
BydDataCollector.java, AccSentryDaemon.java, AdbDaemonLauncher.kt,
AuthManager.java, NativeMotion.java, MotionPipelineV2.java.

## What to do

For each mention: decide whether it is (a) a false description of current
routing -- rewrite it to describe the SDK-only reality, or (b) a deliberate
historical note -- keep it but mark it explicitly as removed, naming commit
61b4d7f. Do not simply delete the word "cloud" and leave a sentence that now says
something different from what it meant.

Two of these comments carry more than routing information -- the tailgate safety
interlock and the "works while car is asleep" capability. For those, verify the
CURRENT behaviour in code before touching the comment, and if the behaviour
actually changed when the cloud path was removed, raise that as a separate bug
rather than quietly editing the comment to match.

## Constraints

- COMMENTS AND DOCS ONLY. Do not change any vehicle-control logic in this task.
- Do NOT modify web/ or the protos. The cloud-only RPCs stay declared for API
  compatibility -- docs/byd-integrations.md already documents that they resolve
  to NOT_SUPPORTED.
- Do NOT weaken any safety interlock or the comment describing it.
- Do NOT commit.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] No comment in app/src/main/java claims a cloud routing path, cloud
      fallback, CLOUD_FIRST or CLOUD_ONLY strategy as current behaviour.
- [ ] Every retained historical mention names commit 61b4d7f (or the relevant
      commit) so a reader can tell history from present tense.
- [ ] The tailgate unlock interlock and the "works while car is asleep" claim
      were each checked against current code, and the finding is stated -- in the
      comment if unchanged, in a new bug if changed.
- [ ] ./gradlew test and koverVerify pass; flutter test passes with zero skipped.
- [ ] No behavioural change: git diff shows comment-only edits.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the
build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is
ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
close_reason:
No comment in app/src/main/java claims a BYD cloud routing path, cloud fallback,
CLOUD_FIRST or CLOUD_ONLY strategy as current behaviour any more.

## Rewritten (all in VehicleControlApiHandler.java unless noted)

- handleLock -- was "cloud-first -> SDK fallback". Now says NOT SUPPORTED: no
  local lock primitive, cloud removed in 61b4d7f, LockCommand declares no SDK
  path, router returns NOT_SUPPORTED with path=NONE.
- handleFindCar, handleBatteryHeat -- "cloud-only" -> NOT SUPPORTED, naming 61b4d7f.
- handleTrunk -- the false safety claim. See the finding below.
- handleWindow javadoc and the inline "Close all" comment -- CLOUD_FIRST /
  cloud CLOSEWINDOW replaced with the local primitive that actually runs.
- handleClimate -- CLOUD_FIRST / SDK_ONLY replaced with "every action is local
  SDK", noting power_on/power_off is what used to be the fallback leg.
- handleSeat -- "cloud-first with SDK fallback" corrected, and the full-state
  payload explained as a leftover of the stateful cloud command rather than
  something the SDK path needs.
- handleChargingSchedule -- CLOUD_ONLY -> NOT SUPPORTED, with the payload shape
  kept because the RPC/REST contract still declares it.
- routedResponse javadoc -- `path` documented as "local" or "none", matching
  CommandResult.pathString(), instead of the four old values including "cloud".
- BydDataCollector.java (~2436) -- the five-area lock poll is now described as
  the ONLY lock source, not a fallback for when cloud is unconfigured.
- AccSentryDaemon.java (~990) -- "cloud listener" dropped from CameraDaemon's
  ACC-ON cleanup list, noted as removed with the cloud.

Left as correct: VehicleCommandRouter.java:269,306 already said "WAS a cloud-only
feature" in the past tense. AdbDaemonLauncher.kt's note about removed tunnels is
accurate. AuthManager.java names Cloudflare only as a generic tunnel example.
NativeMotion / MotionPipelineV2 mean weather clouds.

## The two load-bearing comments -- checked, and one was FALSE

**Trunk unlock-first interlock: GONE.** The handler claimed "router enforces the
safety: motor only fires on unlock SUCCESS". It does not.
VehicleCommandRouter.executeTrunkOpen() calls openTailgate() unconditionally, and
the router's OWN javadoc already says so: "There is no remote-unlock pre-step, so
on locked vehicles the body controller may decline the motor or trip the alarm --
the local primitive is invoked as-is." So it was a known consequence of removing
the cloud, recorded at the router and never propagated to the handler. The
comment now states the interlock is gone and says not to describe the route as
safety-gated.

**Close-all-windows "works while car is asleep": ALSO FALSE.** That came from the
cloud CLOSEWINDOW command. CloseAllWindowsCommand now calls the local
setAllWindowsCommand(2), which needs the head unit awake.

Per this task's own instruction not to quietly edit a comment to match a changed
behaviour, both are raised as **BladeWatch-c2h1** (P1 bug): a trunk-open route
that can trip the car alarm on a locked vehicle with no user-facing warning, and
a silently lost remote capability. That is a product decision about a physical
car, so it is filed rather than decided here.

## Verification

- git diff over the three touched files, non-comment lines only: EMPTY. The
  change is comment-only, as required.
- ./gradlew test koverVerify assembleDebug assembleRelease: SUCCESSFUL.
- flutter test: 1403 passed, 0 skipped. Dart coverage 7004/7006 = 99.97%,
  unchanged. Kover green.
- Nothing committed.

title: Docs reference removed subsystems: BYD cloud, OTA updater, tunnel launcher
description:
## Context

Several docs and CLAUDE.md still describe subsystems whose code was removed in
earlier work, unrelated to the Flutter refactor. A link-resolution sweep on
2026-09-14 (during BladeWatch-81g9.4) found these targets do not exist anywhere
under app/src/main:

- BydCloudClient.java, BydCloudMqttSubscriber.java, and the whole
  com/loabletech/bladewatch/byd/cloud/ package
- UpdateApiHandler.java (referenced from docs/features.md,
  docs/http-api-reference.md, docs/security-smoke-test.md,
  docs/build-and-operations.md)
- TunnelLauncher.kt (docs/daemons-and-processes.md)
- BydConstants.java (docs/byd-integrations.md)
- app/src/main/assets/web/shared/app-shell.css (docs/ui-ux-design-language.md,
  two references)

The dead BydCloud entry in CLAUDE.md's Key Source Locations was already removed.
Everything else was left alone deliberately: some of these are load-bearing
SAFETY text, not just pointers. CLAUDE.md's Security Notes still say "BYD cloud
vehicle control APIs affect the physical car -- test conservatively", and
CLAUDE.md's Architecture section still lists "BYD cloud, MQTT" as CameraDaemon
responsibilities and "optional BYD cloud deterrent" in the surveillance pipeline.
Deciding whether BYD cloud is genuinely gone -- versus moved, renamed, or
reachable through another path -- must be a deliberate check, not a guess made
while fixing a link.

## What to do

1. Determine for each item whether the subsystem was REMOVED or MOVED/RENAMED.
   Use git log / git show on the deleting commit; do not infer from the current
   tree alone.
2. For MOVED: repoint the link at the new path.
3. For REMOVED: delete the reference, or keep the prose with an explicit
   "removed in <commit/task>" note where the behaviour is still worth recording.
4. Decide specifically whether BYD CLOUD VEHICLE CONTROL still exists in any
   form. If it does not, CLAUDE.md's Security Notes line and docs/byd-integrations.md
   must say so plainly. If it does, repoint at the real implementation.
   **If this is ambiguous, STOP AND ASK.** Do not delete a safety constraint
   about commands that move a physical car on the strength of a missing file.
5. Re-run the sweep and confirm every relative link in docs/*.md and CLAUDE.md
   resolves, except the ones in docs/webview-migration.md, which is explicitly
   retired and whose dead links are expected.

## Constraints

- Do NOT modify web/.
- Do NOT weaken or delete any security/safety instruction without positive
  evidence the subsystem it guards is gone.
- Do NOT commit.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every relative link in docs/*.md and CLAUDE.md resolves, except within
      docs/webview-migration.md.
- [ ] Each removed subsystem is either deleted from the docs or marked as removed
      with the task/commit that removed it.
- [ ] The BYD cloud question is answered explicitly, with the evidence stated.
- [ ] No safety constraint was removed without that evidence.
- [ ] ./gradlew test and flutter test both pass with zero skipped tests.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the
build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is
ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
close_reason:
Every relative link in docs/*.md and CLAUDE.md now resolves, except inside
docs/webview-migration.md, which is explicitly retired and whose dead links the
acceptance criteria exempt.

## The BYD cloud question -- ANSWERED, with evidence

BYD cloud vehicle control is GONE. Evidence, not inference:

- Commit 61b4d7f deleted the entire com/loabletech/bladewatch/byd/cloud/ package
  -- BydCloudClient (1145 lines), BydCloudConfig, BydCloudDataProvider,
  BydCloudDeterrent, BydCloudMqttSubscriber, BydCloudSession, BydCloudTransport,
  SmartChargeCache, VehicleCloudSnapshot, and crypto/ (BangcleBlockCipher,
  BangcleCodec, BangcleTables, BydCryptoUtils, CredentialCipher) -- plus
  assets/web/local/byd-cloud.html. The same commit removed SingboxLauncher,
  TailscaleLauncher, TelegramDaemonLauncher and TunnelLauncher.
- VehicleCommandRouter.Path is now exactly {SDK, NONE}, and
  CommandResult.pathString() maps SDK to "local" and everything else to "none".
  There is no cloud branch to take.
- No BydCloud / bangcle reference remains in app/src, flutter_ui/lib, web/src or
  proto (only generated protobuf classes for the still-declared RPCs, plus the
  i18n strings for the not-supported messages).
- docs/byd-integrations.md ALREADY documented this correctly and needed no change.

Because of that evidence I did edit CLAUDE.md's safety line -- but I did not
delete it. "BYD cloud vehicle control APIs affect the physical car -- test
conservatively" became a statement that BYD VEHICLE CONTROL affects the physical
car, naming the local SDK commands that still actuate hardware (climate, windows,
seats, trunk, lights, ADAS, charge cap) and saying explicitly that the cloud path
being gone is not a reason to relax the rule. The constraint is unchanged in
force; only its false premise was corrected.

## Fixed

- **CLAUDE.md** -- removed "BYD cloud, MQTT" from CameraDaemon's
  responsibilities; replaced the BYD-cloud-via-MQTT/Bangcle sentence with the
  local-SDK-only reality and the NOT_SUPPORTED command list, citing 61b4d7f;
  dropped "optional BYD cloud deterrent" from the surveillance pipeline;
  corrected the tunnel-daemon list to Zrok only (Cloudflared / Tailscale /
  sing-box / Telegram are gone); "cloud credentials" removed from the secrets
  file description; two Documentation Maintenance triggers reworded from "cloud"
  to "vehicle"; the Security Notes line reworded as above.
- **docs/http-api-reference.md** -- the window route no longer claims
  CLOUD_FIRST/SDK_ONLY strategies; the `path` field documented as "local" or
  "none" instead of the four old values including "cloud".
- **docs/build-and-operations.md, features.md, http-api-reference.md,
  security-smoke-test.md** -- UpdateApiHandler links removed; the smoke-test entry
  now says plainly that the in-app OTA updater was removed in 13e5366 and the
  item has no implementation left to exercise.
- **docs/daemons-and-processes.md** -- TunnelLauncher dropped from the
  AdbDaemonLauncher coordination list and from Source References; ZrokLauncher
  links kept, since Zrok is the surviving tunnel.
- **docs/byd-integrations.md** -- BydConstants.java repointed at BydFeatureIds.java,
  noting the removal commit 8e98aaf.
- **docs/ui-ux-design-language.md** -- both app-shell.css links repointed at
  flutter_ui/lib/shell/app_shell.dart, noting the file was retired with the legacy
  static pages in c970b59.

## Filed rather than fixed

**BladeWatch-w4xn** -- the same falsehood survives in SOURCE comments, 16
mentions in VehicleControlApiHandler.java alone ("cloud-first -> SDK fallback",
"cloud-only", "CLOUD_FIRST, with cloud CLOSEWINDOW"). Deliberately out of scope
here: this task is documentation, and two of those comments carry more than
routing information -- a tailgate unlock safety interlock, and a claim that
close-all-windows "works while car is asleep". Both need the current behaviour
verified in code before the comment is touched, and if the behaviour actually
changed when the cloud path went away, that is a bug, not a comment edit. Not
something to do while tidying links.

## Verification

- Link sweep over every relative link in docs/*.md and CLAUDE.md: 7 remaining,
  all inside docs/webview-migration.md, all expected.
- ./gradlew test koverVerify assembleDebug: SUCCESSFUL.
- flutter analyze: no issues. flutter test: 1403 passed, 0 skipped.
- Documentation only; no test was added, changed or deleted.
- Nothing committed.

title: Observe a live surveillance motion event with the Flutter UI installed (post-ROI-removal)
description:
## Problem

Split out of BladeWatch-n9l5, which the owner closed because the zrok tunnel feature is slated
for removal after the Flutter refactor. That decision settles the tunnel half of n9l5. It does
NOT settle this half, which has nothing to do with zrok, so it is preserved here rather than
dropped alongside it.

**Motion detection has not been observed firing since the Flutter UI was installed.**

What is established:
- `SentryDaemon` and `acc_sentry_daemon` run.
- The Surveillance pane reports "Running" and, at last check, 131 events today in the
  Recordings screen's Surveillance segment.
- The pipeline has plainly worked recently: 38 events on 2026-09-11, 72 on the 12th, 21 on the
  13th — each a `.mp4` + `.jpg` + `.json` triple under the SD card's `BladeWatch/surveillance`.

What is NOT established: that a NEW event fires and lands correctly with the Flutter UI in place.
Nothing fired during the verification sessions because the car is parked and motion cannot be
created remotely.

So "motion detection still fires" currently rests on history plus a live process, not on an event
observed after the refactor. That is a reasonable inference, not a verification — and the
surveillance pipeline is the product's core function, so it deserves the real check before Phase 4
deletes the native UI.

Worth noting BladeWatch-s3sf removed the per-quadrant detection-zone feature from the C++ motion
pipeline (`blockRoiMask` / `hasCustomRoi` and the per-block skip on the hot path). The engine was
rebuilt and the daemon starts clean, but no motion event has been observed since that change
either. That makes this check more valuable than it was when n9l5 filed it.

## What to do

1. With surveillance armed and the car parked, walk in front of it.
2. Confirm a new event triple appears under `/storage/E3B7-10F2/BladeWatch/surveillance/` with
   today's date.
3. Confirm it appears in the Flutter Recordings screen's Surveillance segment, and that the clip
   plays.
4. Confirm the event's quadrant is correct for the side you approached from — that is the part
   the s3sf C++ change could plausibly have disturbed.
5. Record the result here, including the event's JSON sidecar contents (quadrant, threat level).

## Constraints

- Do NOT modify daemon, surveillance, camera or BYD code to make this pass. A failure here is a
  real regression — file it.
- Do NOT weaken detection thresholds to force an event.
- Do NOT commit.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A new surveillance event triple with today's date exists on the SD card.
- [ ] It appears in the Flutter Recordings screen's Surveillance segment and plays.
- [ ] The recorded quadrant matches the side the motion actually came from.
- [ ] The result is recorded here either way.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles
and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather
than guessing.
close_reason:
Closed on the owner's confirmation that surveillance motion detection is already working.

**Basis: the owner's word, not an observation I made.** Recording that plainly so nobody later
reads this as a verified check. I never saw a live event fire — the car was parked throughout and
motion cannot be created remotely.

What I did establish independently, which is consistent with the owner's confirmation:
- `SentryDaemon` and `acc_sentry_daemon` running throughout the session.
- The Surveillance pane reporting "Running" with 131 events today.
- 618 surveillance files on the SD card, and a history of 38 / 72 / 21 events on 2026-09-11 / 12
  / 13 respectively, each a `.mp4` + `.jpg` + `.json` triple.
- The daemon starting clean and recording continuing to roll after BladeWatch-s3sf rebuilt the
  native motion pipeline.

The specific thing that remains unobserved is the one this issue was filed for: a NEW event
firing after BladeWatch-s3sf removed the per-quadrant ROI mask from the C++ hot path
(`blockRoiMask` / `hasCustomRoi` and the per-block skip), and its quadrant being attributed
correctly. The owner reports detection working, which covers it.

If a quadrant ever turns out to be mis-attributed on an event after this date, s3sf's C++ change
is the first place to look.

Nothing committed.

title: Diagnostics Battery tile shows 'Not available'; show the charge percentage instead
description:
## Problem

The Diagnostics screen's Battery health tile reads **"Not available"** on the head unit. The
user asked for it to show the battery percentage instead, which is reasonable: the Vehicle screen
displays "Charge: 61%" on the same device at the same moment, so the number plainly exists.

The current state is not a bug so much as a dead end left by a removal:

    // BladeWatch-p7vi: SoH estimation was removed from the daemon.
    // `handleSohGetNominal`/`GetSohStatus` are stubs that answer nothing, so
    // this used to leave the battery card pending forever. Nothing is fetched
    // any more and the card says the feature is unavailable instead.
    Future<void> _refreshBattery() async {}

`_refreshBattery` in `flutter_ui/lib/screens/diagnostics/diagnostics_controller.dart` is an empty
method, and `_batteryHealthTile` in `diagnostics_screen.dart` hardcodes
`l10n.battery_health_unavailable` with a neutral outline dot.

**Important distinction:** what was removed is state of HEALTH (SoH) — how degraded the pack is.
What the user is asking for is state of CHARGE (SoC) — how full it is right now. Those are
different numbers and the second one is available; do not "restore SoH" to satisfy this.

Native is no guide here. `DiagnosticsFragment.kt` line 47 says so itself: "The Camera and Battery
tiles still show placeholders (out of scope)." Native shows "Pending data", which is no better.
So this is a deliberate improvement over native, not a parity fix.

## Where the number comes from

`VehicleService.GetVehicleState` -> `battery.soc` (and `battery.rangeKm`). Ground truth is
`flutter_ui/lib/screens/vehicle/vehicle_controller.dart` around line 137:

```dart
battery: BatteryInfo(soc: m.battery.soc.toInt(), rangeKm: m.battery.rangeKm),
```

`DiagnosticsController` does not currently hold a `VehicleServiceClient`; it will need one
injected, following the same constructor-seam pattern every other source on that controller uses
so the new path stays unit-testable without a device.

## What to do

1. Inject a vehicle-state source into `DiagnosticsController` as an injectable function seam
   (match how `tunnelUrlSource` / `cameraConfigSource` are done — they are function seams
   precisely so tests need no device).
2. Implement `_refreshBattery()` to fetch the SoC and expose it as state.
3. Render the percentage in `_batteryHealthTile`. Keep "Not available" as the FALLBACK for when
   the read fails or the vehicle reports nothing — do not show a bare "0%", which is
   indistinguishable from a flat pack.
4. The card is a shortcut to the Battery health dialog; leave `onTap` alone.
5. Decide the dot colour deliberately and say why in the close reason. A charge percentage is not
   a health signal, so colour-coding it red at low charge would be inventing meaning — the
   neutral/primary dot is probably right.

## Strings

There is an existing `diagnostics_battery_value_soh` = `"{arg1}%"`, but the key name says SOH and
this is SOC, so reusing it would leave a lie in the catalog. Prefer a new key.

A bare `"{arg1}%"` is LETTERLESS, which means `validateArbCatalogs` REQUIRES it to be
byte-identical in all 19 catalogs — so adding it is mechanical and needs no translation. Add it
programmatically via a json round-trip, never by hand.

## Constraints

- Do NOT reinstate SoH estimation; it was deliberately removed in BladeWatch-p7vi.
- Do NOT hand-edit ARB catalogs.
- Do NOT show "0%" when the read fails — fall back to the unavailable string.
- Do NOT modify `web/`.
- Do NOT commit.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The Diagnostics Battery tile shows the live charge percentage on the head unit, and it
      agrees with what the Vehicle screen shows at the same moment.
- [ ] A failed or absent read still shows "Not available", verified by a test.
- [ ] A failing test was written first for both the value and the fallback.
- [ ] `./gradlew validateArbCatalogs validateAndroidStrings` pass.
- [ ] `flutter analyze` clean; `flutter test --coverage` at or above the current gate (99.97%).
- [ ] The dot colour decision is recorded.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles
and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather
than guessing.
close_reason:
Done. The Diagnostics Battery tile now reads the live charge percentage, verified against the
Vehicle screen on the head unit.

## What it shows now

    Diagnostics -> BATTERY   60%
    Vehicle     -> Charge: 60%

Captured seconds apart on the same device. They agree because they now read the SAME source —
`VehicleService.GetState` -> `battery.soc`, the one `VehicleController._fetchState()` already
used — rather than two independent paths that could drift.

## What was actually wrong

`_refreshBattery()` was an empty method and the tile hardcoded "Not available". That was a dead
end left by BladeWatch-p7vi, which removed state of HEALTH (how degraded the pack is) from the
daemon. The user was asking for state of CHARGE (how full it is), which is a different number
that was available all along — the Vehicle screen was displaying it on the same screen-full.

SoH was NOT reinstated. The existing test asserting that a `GetSohStatus` stub must not surface a
health reading is kept and retargeted, so a future change cannot quietly bring it back through
this tile.

Native was no guide: `DiagnosticsFragment.kt` line 47 says "The Camera and Battery tiles still
show placeholders (out of scope)" and it shows "Pending data". So this is a deliberate improvement
over native, not a parity fix.

## Decisions worth recording

- **Dot colour stays neutral outline.** A charge percentage is not a health signal. Colouring it
  red at low charge would invent meaning — it only says the car is due a plug. The dot that could
  have earned a colour was the SoH reading, and that is gone.
- **Null, never 0%.** The proto default for `soc` is 0, so a sleeping vehicle or a failed read
  would otherwise render "0%" — indistinguishable from a flat pack. `BatterySocSource` returns
  null for <= 0 and for > 100, and the tile falls back to "Not available". Tested both ways.
- **`BatterySocSource` is a class, not a closure in `main.dart`.** Same reason as
  `CameraProbeSource`: putting it in the composition root dropped Dart coverage 99.97% -> 99.90%,
  because `main.dart` is not covered and a branch must not hide there. Moving it restored 99.97%.

## The string

New `diagnostics_battery_value_charge` = `"{arg1}%"`, added to all 19 catalogs programmatically.
Deliberately NOT reusing `diagnostics_battery_value_soh`, which is also `"{arg1}%"` but whose key
name says SOH — reusing it would have left a lie in the catalog. A bare `"{arg1}%"` is letterless,
so `validateArbCatalogs` REQUIRES it byte-identical everywhere; no translation was needed or
invented.

## A test that earned its keep

The first version of the `BatterySocSource` tests stubbed `VehicleService/GetVehicleState`. The
real RPC method is `GetState`. Three of the five tests passed anyway — they assert null, and an
unstubbed call also yields null, so they were passing for the wrong reason. Only the positive test
("reads the charge percentage") failed and exposed it. Worth remembering: a suite of
negative-assertion tests can be entirely vacuous without one positive case to anchor it.

## Tests

- 4 controller tests: the value, null source, a throwing source (other probes still complete), and
  the injected default.
- 2 screen tests: renders "61%", and falls back to "Not available" with no "0%" anywhere.
- 5 `BatterySocSource` tests: the value, the `success:false` gate, zero-as-no-reading,
  out-of-range rejection, and a throwing transport.

## Gates

flutter analyze clean; 1402 Dart tests pass; Dart coverage 99.97% (7005/7007);
`./gradlew test koverVerify assembleDebug validateArbCatalogs validateAndroidStrings` all green.

Nothing committed.

title: Toolbar URL pill is hardcoded 'Connecting...' on every screen; native hides it when no tunnel
description:
## Problem

The toolbar URL/status pill in the Flutter shell is a hardcoded placeholder. It is on the app's
persistent chrome, so it is wrong on EVERY screen, in every screenshot taken during
BladeWatch-imh6.2's parity sweep.

`flutter_ui/lib/shell/app_shell.dart` (~line 240-275) builds it with no state at all:

```dart
Container(                                  // status dot
  decoration: BoxDecoration(color: colors.outline, ...),   // ALWAYS grey
),
Text(
  l10n.url_connecting,                      // ALWAYS "Connecting…"
  ...
),
IconButton(
  icon: const Icon(Icons.copy, size: 18),
  onPressed: null,                          // ALWAYS disabled
),
```

There is no tunnel URL input, no listener, no controller. It cannot ever change.

### What native does instead

`MainActivity.updateUrlDisplay()`:

```kotlin
val tunnelUrl = daemonsViewModel.zrokController.tunnelUrl.value
if (tunnelUrl.isNullOrEmpty()) {
    // No active tunnel URL — hide the pill entirely. The dashboard
    // connect card already surfaces the "No tunnel running" state.
    urlBar.visibility = android.view.View.GONE
    mainViewModel.setCurrentUrl(null)
} else {
    urlBar.visibility = android.view.View.VISIBLE
    tvCurrentUrl.text = tunnelUrl
    urlStatusDot.setBackgroundResource(R.drawable.status_dot_online)
    mainViewModel.setCurrentUrl(tunnelUrl)
}
```

So there are four separate divergences:

1. Native HIDES the pill when there is no tunnel. Flutter always shows it.
2. Flutter's text says "Connecting…", which is factually false — no tunnel is configured
   (Services shows "Zrok Tunnel — No token configured"), so nothing is connecting and nothing
   ever will. A permanent "Connecting…" is worse than showing nothing: it reads as the app being
   stuck.
3. Flutter never shows the actual URL when a tunnel IS running.
4. Flutter's copy button is permanently dead (`onPressed: null`); native's copies the URL.

Confirmed on device: native's toolbar shows no pill at all on any screen, Flutter's shows
"Connecting…" on every screen, with all three daemons healthy and no tunnel running.

## What to do

1. Give the shell the real tunnel URL. The plumbing ALREADY EXISTS — BladeWatch-m1po added
   `DaemonChannel.tunnelUrl` (Kotlin `DaemonControl.tunnelStatus`, reading zrok's own log and
   gating on the process being alive) and wired it into `DashboardController`. Reuse that source
   rather than adding a second path.
2. Mirror native's rule exactly: **no URL means hide the pill**, do not show a placeholder. The
   Dashboard connect card is already the place that says "No tunnel running".
3. When a URL is present: show it, use the online status-dot colour, and enable the copy button
   to copy that URL.
4. Note BladeWatch-i2wv is the sibling of this on the Diagnostics screen — the same
   `tunnelUrlSource` was left at its default there too. Consider doing both together; they share
   one source.

## Constraints

- Do NOT add a second tunnel-URL lookup path; reuse `DaemonChannel.tunnelUrl`.
- Do NOT leave a placeholder string in place of hiding — that IS the bug.
- Do NOT modify `web/`.
- Do NOT commit.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] With no tunnel running, the toolbar pill is ABSENT, matching native.
- [ ] With a tunnel running, the pill shows the real URL, an online dot, and a working copy
      button that puts that URL on the clipboard.
- [ ] A failing widget test was written first for each of the two states (the URL source is
      injectable, so no device is needed for the test).
- [ ] `flutter analyze` clean; `flutter test --coverage` at or above the current gate (99.97%).
- [ ] Verified on the head unit in both states, as BladeWatch-m1po did for the Dashboard (it
      used a stand-in process to simulate a live tunnel).

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles
and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather
than guessing.
close_reason:
Fixed and verified on the head unit. The pill is gone when there is no tunnel, matching native.

## What changed
