title: About has no Getting Started entry point, so the setup guide cannot be reopened after dismissal
description:
## Problem

The Flutter About screen has no way to reopen the Getting Started guide, so
once it is dismissed the user cannot get it back.

Found in BladeWatch-imh6.1 comparing screenshots/flutter/10_about.png against a
freshly re-captured screenshots/native/10_about.png.

Native About lists three rows:
  License        MIT - open source. Tap to view full text.      (check icon, chevron)
  Getting Started  Three quick steps to get the best experience:  (star icon, chevron)

The Flutter port has the License row but NOT the Getting Started row.

This matters because the guide is the only in-app place that explains the three
things the app genuinely needs from the head unit: picking a language,
disabling BYD's auto-start restriction, and allowing display over other apps.
The second is the important one -- the guide's own text says "BYD wipes this on
every install, you'll redo it after updates", so a user WILL need to reach it
again after a BYD update, exactly when the app has stopped working properly.

The guide itself is already ported and works: SetupGuideController exists and is
wired in flutter_ui/lib/main.dart (see _setupGuideController and
_maybeShowSetupGuideOnLaunch, which shows it automatically on first launch or
after a version change). Only the manual entry point from About is missing, so
this should be a small change -- add the row and call the existing dialog.

## Also on this screen (cosmetic, fix while you are here)

- Native wraps the app identity in a card with a circular app ICON beside the
  name, then Version and Build as rows inside that card. Flutter renders
  Version and Build as bare rows with no card and no icon.
- Native's page opens with the title "About BladeWatch" and the subtitle
  "Version, license, support development." The Flutter port has neither, and
  instead renders that same title/subtitle pair as a CARD lower down, which
  reads as a duplicate of the page itself.
- Native's rows carry leading icons (a check for License, a star for Getting
  Started) and trailing chevrons; Flutter's have neither. This overlaps
  BladeWatch-mrsc item 4 -- do whichever lands first, do not do it twice.

## Not a defect

Version reads 1.0.0 in the Flutter APK against 1.0.1.0 in the native one.
That is correct: they are separate packages with their own versionName
(flutter_ui/pubspec.yaml "version: 1.0.0+1" against app/build.gradle.kts
versionName "1.0.1.0"), and the screen reads the real value via
PackageInfo.fromPlatform(). Flag it to the owner if the product version should
be unified before the native UI is deleted in Phase 4, but do not "fix" it here.

## Constraints

- Reuse the existing SetupGuideController and its dialog; do NOT write a second
  setup-guide implementation.
- Do NOT change what the guide checks or the order of its steps.
- Do NOT touch the Android res/ files or web/.
- Do NOT commit.

## Tests (required)

- Widget test: the About screen renders a Getting Started row, and tapping it
  opens the setup guide dialog.
- Widget test: the row is present regardless of whether the guide has been
  dismissed before (it is a manual entry point, not a first-run prompt).
- flutter test and flutter analyze clean; coverage not lower than 99.97%.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] About shows a Getting Started row matching native's label and subtitle.
- [ ] Tapping it opens the existing setup guide dialog.
- [ ] The row works after the guide has already been dismissed.
- [ ] App identity renders in a card with the app icon, as native does.
- [ ] The page shows the "About BladeWatch" title and its subtitle once, not as
      a duplicate card.
- [ ] Fresh screenshots/flutter/10_about.png captured and compared at real
      device density.
- [ ] flutter test and flutter analyze clean; coverage not lower than before.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the
build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is
ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
close_reason:
Fixed and verified on device.

ROOT CAUSE WAS NOT WHAT THE ISSUE ASSUMED. The row was never missing: it
existed at settings_about_screen.dart with key 'about.setupGuide' and was
already wired to onShowSetupGuide. It was LABELLED WRONG -- it used
settings_about_row_title / settings_about_row_subtitle, which in the Android
source of truth mean "About BladeWatch" / "Version, license, support
development." Those are the strings for the Settings hub's About ROW, not for a
setup-guide entry. So on device the row read as a duplicate of the page header
and there was no discoverable way back into the guide. The correct keys,
setup_guide_title / setup_guide_subtitle, already existed in both catalogs.

Why it went unnoticed: the existing widget test only asserted that tapping the
row fired the callback. It never asserted the label, so the test agreed with the
implementation rather than with native. Same shape as the YYYYMMDD date bug
found in BladeWatch-imh6.6 -- a test that pinned the defect.

Changes:
 - settings_about_screen.dart now uses setup_guide_title/subtitle for that row.
 - Page header restored to match native: "About BladeWatch" title plus the
   one-line description, instead of a hardcoded, unlocalised 'BladeWatch'.
 - App identity grouped into one card with the app mark, as native does,
   instead of two bare rows.
 - License and Getting Started rows gained their native leading icons (check,
   star) and trailing chevrons -- the part of BladeWatch-mrsc item 4 that
   applies to this screen is therefore already done here.

Tests: added an assertion that the row is labelled as the setup guide and NOT
with the About page strings (fails before the fix). widget_test.dart's
"Getting Started" finder had to be scoped to the AlertDialog, because the row
behind it now legitimately carries the same label -- that is the fix working,
not a regression.

flutter analyze clean; flutter test 1283 passed, zero skipped; Dart coverage
unchanged at 99.97%. Verified on the head unit: About matches native's
structure and tapping Getting Started opens the guide with all three steps.
screenshots/flutter/10_about.png re-captured.

NOT fixed here, deliberately: version reads 1.0.0 against native's 1.0.1.0.
That is correct -- separate packages, real values read via
PackageInfo.fromPlatform(). Flagged for the owner to decide whether the product
version should be unified before Phase 4 deletes the native UI.

Not committed, per CLAUDE.md.

title: Settings and pushed sub-screens drop the native design system: no rail, titles, grouped cards, icons, theme previews
description:
## Context

Found in BladeWatch-imh6.1 comparing the Flutter set against a FRESHLY
re-captured native set (the committed baseline was stale and all 18 shots were
retaken from the current build first, so none of this is a theme-era artifact).

These are not one screen's problem. The same handful of design-system decisions
were dropped across Settings, its sub-pages, and every pushed sub-screen, so
they are collected here rather than filed one screen at a time. Individually
each is small; together they make the port read as a different, plainer app.

Colour tokens are NOT at issue -- the Dart primary 0xFF00677E matches
md_sys_color_primary_light exactly, and dark 0xFF3CD7FF matches. An earlier
suspicion of a green/teal mismatch came purely from the stale baseline.

Reference shots (all now current): screenshots/native/08_settings.png,
08e_settings_status_overlay.png, 07c_diagnostics_adb_console.png,
07e_diagnostics_performance.png, 10_about.png, against their
screenshots/flutter/ counterparts.

## Differences (native -> Flutter)

1. SUB-SCREENS HIDE THE NAV RAIL. Native keeps the 9-destination rail visible
   on pushed sub-screens (ADB Console, Performance) and puts a back arrow plus
   the screen name in the toolbar. The Flutter port pushes them FULL SCREEN
   with the rail gone and no toolbar title, so the user loses their place and
   the only way out is one back arrow. This is the most disorienting of the
   set on a head unit.

2. SECTION TITLES AND SUBTITLES DROPPED. Every native settings pane opens with
   a title and a one-line description, e.g. "Appearance / Theme, language, and
   visual preferences." and "Status overlay / Choose which segments of the
   floating status pill stay visible." The Flutter panes render the subtitle
   only, or nothing, and never the title.

3. GROUPED CARD CONTAINERS DROPPED. Native wraps each settings group in a
   rounded container (Theme in one, Navigation Side in another, the two status
   overlay toggles in a third, with a divider between them). Flutter renders
   bare rows on the page background with no grouping and no dividers.

4. LEADING ICONS DROPPED ON ROWS. Native's Status overlay rows carry a camera
   icon and a trip-arrow icon; About's rows carry a check and a star. The
   Flutter equivalents have no leading icons.

5. THEME PICKER REDUCED TO CHIPS. Native offers three large preview CARDS --
   an actual gradient/light/dark swatch with a selection pill and the label
   beneath -- plus the helper line "Auto follows your system theme." Flutter
   renders three small segmented chips with no preview and no helper text, so
   the user cannot see what they are choosing.

6. NAVIGATION SIDE LOST ITS SUBTITLES. Native's three options are cards with a
   title AND an explanatory subtitle: "Left / LHD . default", "Right / RHD
   vehicles", "Auto / Detect from vehicle". Flutter renders bare chips reading
   only Left / Right / Auto, dropping the explanation of what each means --
   which matters because this is the drive-side control.

7. CHEVRONS MISSING ON DRILL-DOWN ROWS. Native marks Recording and Surveillance
   in the settings list with a chevron because they open sub-pages. Flutter's
   rows look identical to the non-drill-down ones.

8. LANGUAGE ROW LOST ITS DETAIL. Native's row has a globe icon, the label
   "Display language", the CURRENT value as a heading ("Auto") and the count
   "17 of 17 languages available", plus a chevron. Flutter renders a bare
   "Display language >" row that shows neither the current language nor the
   count.

9. "SETTINGS" LIST HEADER MISSING above the section list.

10. ADB CONSOLE CHROME. Native groups the command field and presets in a card
    labelled "PRESET COMMANDS", with a filled "Run" button carrying a play
    icon, an uppercase "OUTPUT" label, an OUTLINED "Clear Output" button, and
    an outlined output box. Flutter has a bare field with a plain send arrow,
    sentence-case labels, a text-link Clear Output and a filled grey box.

## Explicitly NOT in scope here

- The Dashboard layout gap is BladeWatch-ya6f.
- The Recordings master-detail gap is its own bug (filed alongside this one).
- Diagnostics CAMERA reading "Probing..." where native reads "Camera 0" is NOT
  a layout bug: cameraConfigSource in flutter_ui/lib/main.dart:202 is stubbed
  at its default because no IPC path to UnifiedConfigManager's public sections
  exists. That is BladeWatch-hygs; this issue must not duplicate it.
- Health-card icon choices on Diagnostics (native traffic-light / pulse vs
  Flutter wifi / SD-card) are listed under item 4's spirit but are cosmetic;
  fix them with the icons if convenient, do not block on them.

## Constraints

- Do NOT touch the Android res/ files -- they are the reference and the native
  UI still ships until Phase 4.
- Do NOT modify web/.
- Do NOT change any controller's RPC behaviour; this is presentation only.
- Keep the drive-side mirroring behaviour intact when restoring the rail on
  sub-screens.
- Do NOT commit.

## Tests (required)

- Widget tests for the restored structure: rail present on a pushed sub-screen;
  section title and subtitle rendered; grouped containers present; leading
  icons present; theme options expose their preview and helper text;
  navigation-side options expose their subtitles; drill-down rows have
  chevrons; the language row shows the current value and count.
- Existing settings controller tests must pass UNCHANGED.
- flutter test and flutter analyze clean; coverage not lower than 99.97%.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Pushed sub-screens keep the nav rail and show a toolbar title with the
      back arrow, as native does.
- [ ] Every settings pane shows its title and description.
- [ ] Settings groups render in rounded containers with dividers where native
      has them.
- [ ] Status overlay and About rows carry their leading icons.
- [ ] Theme picker shows three preview cards plus the helper line.
- [ ] Navigation Side options show their subtitles.
- [ ] Recording and Surveillance rows show drill-down chevrons.
- [ ] The language row shows the globe icon, current value and
      "N of N languages available".
- [ ] The section list carries its "SETTINGS" header.
- [ ] ADB Console chrome matches native (grouped presets, labelled Run button,
      outlined Clear Output and output box).
- [ ] Fresh screenshots captured for each affected name and compared at real
      device density.
- [ ] flutter test and flutter analyze clean; coverage not lower than before.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the
build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is
ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
close_reason:
All ten items addressed and verified on the head unit.

1. SUB-SCREENS KEEP THE NAV RAIL. The shell's stage now hosts its own Navigator
   (app_shell.dart), so pushes from Diagnostics land INSIDE the stage instead of
   on the root navigator, which used to cover the rail. Verified on device: the
   ADB Console shows the rail, the main toolbar still reads "Diagnostics", and
   the sub-screen has its own back arrow plus a TITLE -- it previously pushed a
   bare, unlabelled AppBar.
   Two details worth knowing:
   - The stage Navigator is keyed by selected route, so switching rail
     destination discards any open sub-screen. Without that, leaving Diagnostics
     with the console open would keep showing it under the new title.
   - Dialogs are unaffected: showDialog defaults to useRootNavigator: true, so
     they still cover the whole window rather than being trapped in the stage.
2. PANE TITLES AND SUBTITLES restored via a shared header in the Settings hub.
   Privacy deliberately has none -- that pane opens with its own "On-device by
   default" heading in both UIs, so a generic header would duplicate it.
3. GROUPED CARD CONTAINERS restored on Appearance (Theme, Navigation Side) and
   Status overlay, with a divider between the two overlay toggles.
4. LEADING ICONS restored on the Status overlay rows. About's rows already got
   theirs in BladeWatch-vbew.
5. THEME PICKER is now three preview CARDS -- an actual gradient/light/dark
   swatch with a selection pill and label -- plus the "Auto follows your system
   theme." caption, instead of three bare chips.
6. NAVIGATION SIDE options regained their subtitles: LHD . default / RHD
   vehicles / Detect from vehicle. This one mattered most of the set: "Left" and
   "Right" alone do not tell you it is about drive side.
7. CHEVRONS restored on Recording and Surveillance only, matching native, where
   SettingsFragment.Section marks exactly those two navigates = true purely for
   the affordance.
8. LANGUAGE ROW now shows the globe, the CURRENT language (Auto, or the
   language's own name in its own script) and "N of N languages available".
9. "SETTINGS" list header restored above the section list.
10. ADB CONSOLE CHROME matches native: command field and presets grouped in one
    card under an uppercase PRESET COMMANDS label, a filled Run button with a
    play icon instead of a bare send arrow, uppercase OUTPUT, an OUTLINED Clear
    Output button, and an outlined output box instead of a filled grey slab.

EVERY STRING USED ALREADY EXISTED IN BOTH CATALOGS -- settings_appearance_subtitle,
settings_theme_active_auto_caption, settings_drive_side_{left,right,auto}_hint,
settings_language_count_format, settings_subrail_overline, action_run. They were
ported long ago and simply never wired up. No new keys were added, so the ARB
parity gate is untouched.

AN ACCESSIBILITY REGRESSION I INTRODUCED AND THEN FIXED: replacing ChoiceChip
with custom preview/subtitle tiles silently dropped the selected state that
ChoiceChip exposes to accessibility services. Both new tiles now wrap in
Semantics(selected:, button:). That also let the existing tests assert selection
without casting to a widget type -- they previously read ChoiceChip.selected,
which pinned the implementation class and broke on any presentation change while
proving nothing a user would notice.

SettingsHubDependencies gained localeController (two construction sites: main.dart
and the test helper) so the Appearance pane can show the current language. No
controller behaviour changed anywhere.

flutter analyze clean; flutter test 1300 passed, zero skipped; Dart coverage
99.97% (unchanged -- getting there needed a test for the non-auto language
branch, which nothing had exercised).

Screenshots re-captured: 08_settings, 08e_settings_status_overlay,
07c_diagnostics_adb_console.

Not committed, per CLAUDE.md.

title: Confirm the ADB Console unavailable state with wireless ADB genuinely off
description:
## Context

BladeWatch-imh6.6 required the ADB Console's ADB-unavailable state to be
confirmed with ADB genuinely down. Everything else in that task was verified;
this one check could not be, and it is NOT a matter of effort -- it is blocked
by the device.

The ADB Console (flutter_ui/lib/screens/diagnostics/, backed by
flutter_ui/lib/adb/adb_client.dart) talks to adbd on 127.0.0.1:5555 with a
hand-rolled pure-Dart ADB protocol client. AdbClient.connect() returns one of
three states; this task is about the first:

  unavailable  -- nothing is listening on the ADB port at all, e.g. the head
                  unit's wireless ADB was reset by a BYD firmware update
                  (see BladeWatch-ofzb)
  authPending  -- adbd is reachable but has not authorised this key
  connected    -- handshake complete

authPending and connected were BOTH verified on device in imh6.6: opening the
console raised the head unit's own "Allow USB debugging?" prompt, the screen
rendered the waiting-for-approval state correctly, and after approving, a real
command returned byd_cam_daemon / sentry_daemon / acc_sentry_daemon.

## Why it could not be done from the shell

adbd runs as uid 2000 (shell) -- the same uid our shell and the app have -- so
it looks killable. It is not. SELinux denies the signal:

    killall: pid 2390: Permission denied
    killall: adbd: Permission denied

This matches the stored memory that BYD gates TCP ADB behind its own
persist.sys.adb.wiress.enable property (note BYD's typo "wiress"), which shell
cannot write; service.adb.tcp.port is non-persistent and set by BYD's
wireless-ADB mechanism each boot.

So the only way to produce the state is to turn wireless ADB OFF on the head
unit itself, through BYD's own setting -- which needs a person at the car.

## What to do

Do this only when you are physically at the vehicle and able to turn wireless
ADB back on afterwards. Losing it may otherwise require a reboot or BYD's own
mechanism to restore, and the whole app depends on ADB (168 call sites via
AdbShellExecutor).

1. With ADB still up, open the app: Diagnostics > ADB Console, and confirm it
   reaches the connected state ("Ready for commands").
2. Turn wireless ADB off on the head unit via the BYD setting.
3. In the app, tap Retry (or re-enter the console).
4. Confirm the screen renders the UNAVAILABLE state -- not authPending, and not
   a raw exception. It must explain that ADB is not reachable and offer a
   retry, and it must NOT hang or show an empty console.
5. Turn wireless ADB back on, tap Retry, and confirm the console recovers to
   connected without restarting the app.

### Capturing evidence while ADB is down

You cannot screenshot over ADB while ADB is down -- screencap needs it. Drive
it from the device instead. A detached script survives the parent adb shell
dying:

    nohup sh /data/local/tmp/probe.sh >/dev/null 2>&1 &

with the script doing: sleep, then "input tap" to hit Retry, then
"screencap -p /data/local/tmp/adbdown.png". Pull the PNG once ADB is back.
That harness was written and confirmed working in imh6.6; only the kill step
was denied. Remove the script, the PNG and any log afterwards (AGENTS.md
cleanup; never touch /sdcard/BladeWatch/** or /sdcard/Pictures/**).

## Constraints

- Do NOT try to work around the SELinux denial, and do NOT attempt to root the
  device. If the state cannot be produced, say so and stop.
- Never write adb_enabled=0 (see the Security Notes in CLAUDE.md).
- Fix any defect in the DART side (adb_client.dart / the console screen), not
  in the daemon.
- Do NOT commit.

## Tests (required)

- The unavailable path is already unit-covered (a failed socket connect maps to
  AdbConnectionStatus.unavailable). If the on-device behaviour differs from
  what those tests assert, correct the TEST first to match reality, then fix
  the code -- that is the convention this refactor follows.
- flutter test and flutter analyze clean afterwards; coverage not lower.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] With wireless ADB off, the ADB Console renders its unavailable state,
      distinct from authPending, with a working retry and no hang.
- [ ] No raw exception text or stack trace is shown to the user.
- [ ] Turning wireless ADB back on and tapping Retry recovers to connected
      without an app restart.
- [ ] Evidence captured (screenshot pulled from the device) and attached.
- [ ] Any mismatch between the unit tests and real behaviour is reconciled,
      test first.
- [ ] All probe artifacts removed from the device.
- [ ] flutter test and flutter analyze clean; coverage not lower than before.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the
build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is
ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
close_reason:
Closed at the owner's direction: not needed.

This wanted the ADB Console's unavailable state confirmed with wireless ADB genuinely switched
off. It was never run, and the reason it stayed open is worth recording: turning wireless ADB off
severs the very connection every check in Phase 3 depends on, and on this head unit it is not
trivially reversible — `persist.sys.adb.wiress.enable` is a BYD-owned persistent property that
shell cannot write (SELinux denies the setprop), so restoring ADB would need BYD's own wireless-ADB
UI on the car.

So the cost of this check was a real risk of losing device access mid-refactor, against confirming
one empty-state screen. The owner's call that it is not needed is reasonable on that trade.

**Unverified as a result:** the Flutter ADB Console's behaviour when wireless ADB is off. The
screen exists and renders (seen in Diagnostics > Tools), but its unavailable path has not been
exercised on device. If it ever misbehaves in that state, this is the check that was skipped.

Nothing committed.

title: Enforce Android-only: fail the build if non-Android Flutter platform dirs reappear
description:
> **CODE ONLY — do not touch the head unit in this task.**
> Build-configuration and guard work only. Verify locally with `flutter`, `git`
> and `./gradlew`; no device, no adb.

## Context

BladeWatch's Flutter UI targets exactly one thing: an **arm64 Android head unit**
(BYD DiLink v3, Android 10 / API 29). iOS, macOS, Windows, Linux and web are not
targets and never will be — there is no BladeWatch on a desktop or a phone.

`flutter create` scaffolded all six platforms. Those directories have already
been deleted and are untracked (verified: `flutter_ui/ios`, `macos`, `windows`,
`linux`, `web` are all 0 tracked files; only `android`, `lib`, `test` and
`assets` remain). **So this task is not a cleanup — it is the guard that keeps it
that way.**

## Why a guard is needed rather than a one-off deletion

The directories regenerate. `flutter create .` in the project root, some
`flutter pub get` paths, adding a plugin that runs platform scaffolding, or a
developer following stock Flutter docs will all recreate them silently. They
then sit there inviting someone to "fix" an iOS build that should not exist,
and they add 103 files of dead scaffolding to every clone.

There is a second, sharper reason. A plugin that supports only the desktop or
web platforms will resolve and compile perfectly on a dev machine and fail only
at APK build time — or worse, pull a transitive dependency that changes
behaviour on Android. Declaring the supported platform set makes the intent
machine-checkable instead of tribal.

## Steps

1. **Declare the platform set in `flutter_ui/pubspec.yaml`.** Add a
   `flutter: platforms:` section listing only `android`. Confirm `flutter build
   apk` and `flutter test` still pass afterwards — this key is advisory for apps,
   so treat it as documentation plus a signal to tooling, not as the enforcement.
2. **Add the actual enforcement** as a check that fails the build. Put it next to
   the existing `validateAndroidStrings` / `validateArbCatalogs` tasks in
   `app/build.gradle.kts` and hook it into `preBuild` the same way, OR extend
   `tools/check_flutter_coverage.sh`'s pattern with a sibling script under
   `tools/`. It must fail, not warn, if any of `flutter_ui/ios`,
   `flutter_ui/macos`, `flutter_ui/windows`, `flutter_ui/linux` or
   `flutter_ui/web` exists.
3. The failure message must say what to do: delete the directory, this project is
   Android-only, and do not run `flutter create` in `flutter_ui/`.
4. **Keep the `.gitignore` belt-and-braces.** Even with the build check, add the
   five directories to `.gitignore` so a regenerated tree cannot be committed by
   an `git add` that sweeps them up. Note the existing screenshots rule uses the
   `path/*` + `!path/keep/` negation form — follow the file's existing style.
5. Record in `flutter_ui/README.md` (or wherever the project's Flutter notes
   live) that the UI is Android-only and why, so the next person does not
   "restore" the missing platforms thinking something is broken.

## Constraints

- Do NOT delete `flutter_ui/android`, `lib`, `test` or `assets`.
- Do NOT add a plugin or dependency solely to satisfy a non-Android platform.
- Do NOT modify `web/` (the Angular SPA) — it is a separate, browser-targeted
  project and is unrelated to Flutter's `web` platform directory.
- The main app (`net.bladewatch.app`) must still build without the Flutter
  toolchain installed; if the enforcement lives in `app/build.gradle.kts`, it
  must be a filesystem check only, with no `flutter` invocation.
- Use non-interactive flags for file operations (`rm -rf`, `cp -f`, `mv -f`) —
  some shells alias these to interactive mode and will hang.
- Do NOT commit. Leave changes in the working tree.

## Conventions for this refactor

- The Flutter UI is a separate APK (`net.bladewatch.flutter`) under `flutter_ui/`,
  arm64-v8a only, minSdk 29. Its Android project is `flutter_ui/android/`.
- Gradle logic for the main app lives in `app/build.gradle.kts`; there is no
  root-level Gradle build script.
- Coverage gates: `flutter test --coverage` (Dart, `lib/gen` excluded) and
  `./gradlew koverVerify` (Kotlin). Neither threshold may be lowered.

## Tests (required)

- Prove the check **fails**: create an empty `flutter_ui/web/` directory, run the
  build, confirm it fails naming that directory, then delete it and confirm the
  build passes again. A guard nobody has watched fail is not a guard.
- Do the same for at least one more platform directory, to prove the check is not
  hardcoded to a single name.
- `cd flutter_ui && flutter test` and `flutter analyze` still pass.
- `./gradlew assembleDebug` and `./gradlew test` still pass.
- If the check is a shell script, it gets the same treatment as
  `tools/check_flutter_coverage.sh`: non-zero exit on failure, proven by running it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `flutter_ui/pubspec.yaml` declares `android` as the only supported platform.
- [ ] A build-failing check rejects the presence of `flutter_ui/{ios,macos,windows,linux,web}`.
- [ ] The check was demonstrated failing for at least two different platform
      directories, then restored to passing.
- [ ] Its failure message tells the reader to delete the directory and not to run
      `flutter create` in `flutter_ui/`.
- [ ] The five directories are also in `.gitignore`, following the file's existing style.
- [ ] The Android-only decision and its reason are written down where a Flutter
      developer will see them.
- [ ] `flutter build apk --target-platform android-arm64 --debug` still succeeds.
- [ ] `flutter analyze` clean; `flutter test` and `./gradlew test` pass.
- [ ] The main app still builds without the Flutter toolchain installed.
- [ ] Changes left uncommitted in the working tree.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
close_reason:
Done. Code only; the head unit was not touched.

ENFORCEMENT: new `validateFlutterAndroidOnly` Gradle task in
app/build.gradle.kts, registered next to validateAndroidStrings /
validateArbCatalogs and hooked into preBuild the same way. It FAILS (not warns)
if any of flutter_ui/{ios,macos,windows,linux,web} exists. Deliberately a
filesystem check with no `flutter` invocation, so the main app still builds on a
machine without the Flutter toolchain.

The failure message names each offending directory and says what to do: delete
it, this project is Android-only, and do not run `flutter create` inside
flutter_ui/. It also warns that web/ at the REPO ROOT is the Angular SPA and is
unrelated, because that is the obvious way to misread the rule.

PROVEN FAILING, not assumed:
  flutter_ui/web       -> BUILD FAILED, "found flutter_ui/web"
  flutter_ui/ios + macos -> BUILD FAILED, BOTH listed (so it is not hardcoded to
                          one name)
  flutter_ui/linux     -> `./gradlew assembleDebug` itself FAILED on
                          :app:validateFlutterAndroidOnly, confirming the
                          preBuild wiring blocks a real build and not just the
                          standalone task
  each one deleted afterwards -> BUILD SUCCESSFUL again.

GITIGNORE: the five paths added to the repo .gitignore as belt-and-braces, so a
regenerated tree cannot be swept into a commit. Verified the scoping is right:
`git check-ignore` reports flutter_ui/web IS ignored while the repo-root web/
(the Angular SPA) is NOT.

ONE ACCEPTANCE CRITERION COULD NOT BE MET AS WRITTEN, and it is worth knowing
why. The task asked pubspec.yaml to declare `flutter: platforms: android:`,
expecting it to be advisory for apps. It is not advisory -- it is rejected.
`flutter pub get` fails outright with:
    Unexpected child "platforms" found under "flutter".
That key is valid for PLUGINS only; an application has no machine-readable way
to declare its platform set. I tried it, saw it break the build, and reverted.
pubspec.yaml now carries a prominent comment stating the platform target, the
reason there is no key, and where the real enforcement lives. That is the whole
substance of the criterion; the mechanism it named does not exist.

README: flutter_ui/README.md was still the stock `flutter create` boilerplate
("A new Flutter project"). Replaced with real orientation: the Android-only
rule and why, both guards, the "nothing is broken, do not restore them" note,
the repo-root web/ distinction, day-to-day commands, and a layout table.

Verification: ./gradlew assembleDebug BUILD SUCCESSFUL, ./gradlew test BUILD
SUCCESSFUL, flutter analyze clean, flutter test 1294 passed zero skipped.
flutter_ui still contains only android/ assets/ lib/ test/ plus config files.

Not committed, per CLAUDE.md.

title: Surveillance ROI (region-of-interest) motion-zone config has no client on either platform
description:
## Context

Discovered while implementing BladeWatch-yz1e.8 (Flutter port of the Surveillance settings screen). That task instructed porting app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/view/RoiDrawingView.kt (a generic touch-drawn, 3-8-point normalized-polygon View) to a Flutter CustomPainter, citing commit 1273df2 as evidence a "quadrant off-by-one" bug had shipped in this area before.

## What was actually found

RoiDrawingView.kt is confirmed dead code with no client anywhere, but the backend capability it would have driven is real:

- RoiDrawingView.kt has no fragment, layout, or call site anywhere in app/src/main/java/ or app/src/main/res/ besides its own file. git log on it shows only the original Overdrive-to-BladeWatch rename commits, nothing since.
- SurveillanceSettingsClient.kt (the RPC mapping for the Surveillance settings screen) has zero ROI/polygon/region calls. SurveillanceSettingsModels.kt has zero such fields.
- surveillance.proto's SurveillanceConfig message (29 fields) has no ROI field. Grepping the whole proto tree for "roi" (case-insensitive) returns nothing.
- Commit 1273df2, cited as the "quadrant off-by-one" precedent, touches only web/src/app/pages/surveillance/surveillance.component.ts and i18n catalogs -- no Kotlin surveillance-settings or ROI file is in its file list. Its actual fix was an unrelated 0-indexed-vs-1-indexed bug in the debug heatmap snapshot viewer (GetSnapshot, quadrant 1-4 display vs 0-3 daemon range).

However, docs/surveillance-implementation.md's own "ROI" section describes a real, working backend capability: the native motion pipeline supports per-quadrant block-mask ROI (SurveillanceEngineGpu.applyQuadrantRoi(), NativeMotion.setQuadrantRoi(), SurveillanceIpcServer's GET_ROI/SET_ROI commands on 127.0.0.1:19877, and a legacy SurveillanceApiHandler REST path). This is not fabricated -- it is real, wired, server-side functionality. It simply has no client anywhere:

- Grepping app/src/main/java/ for the ROI RPC/IPC call sites (SET_ROI, GET_ROI, applyQuadrantRoi, QuadrantRoi) turns up only SurveillanceEngineGpu/SurveillanceApiHandler/SurveillanceIpcServer themselves -- no fragment, activity, or view calls into this path.
- web/ has zero ROI references anywhere (grepped for roi/quadrantRoi/SET_ROI/GET_ROI across web/src/).
- The only "quadrant" concept either client actually uses is the fixed 4-way debug heatmap/snapshot viewer (GetHeatmap/GetSnapshot/GetFilterLog -- 3 of SurveillanceService's 9 RPCs), which is a completely different feature (a debug visualization of the 4 fixed camera-mosaic quadrants) from a user-drawn ROI polygon.

## Why this is out of scope for a porting task

BladeWatch-yz1e.8's own constraints forbid modifying the daemon, the Connect server, or any .proto file, and require calling "the SAME RPCs" native uses. Since the ConnectRPC SurveillanceConfig message has no ROI field, and native's own Settings screen never calls the legacy REST ROI endpoint or the IPC GET_ROI/SET_ROI commands either, there is no "same RPC" to mirror -- reviving ROI as a real user-facing feature would need a new proto field or RPC (a daemon/proto change) plus new client UI on both native Android and the Flutter port (native currently has none either, despite the dead RoiDrawingView.kt). That is a product decision -- whether ROI zone configuration should return as a feature at all, and if so what UI/UX it should have -- not a mechanical translation task.

## Suggested next step

If ROI-based per-quadrant motion masking is wanted as a real feature:
1. Add an explicit ROI field/RPC to surveillance.proto (e.g. a repeated polygon-points field on SurveillanceConfig, or a dedicated GetRoi/SetRoi RPC per quadrant).
2. Wire it server-side to the already-working SurveillanceEngineGpu.applyQuadrantRoi()/NativeMotion.setQuadrantRoi() path (no pipeline changes needed -- only the client-facing surface is missing).
3. Build a drawing UI on whichever platform(s) should get it first -- RoiDrawingView.kt's interaction model (tap to add points, drag to adjust, 3-8 points, normalized coordinates) is a reasonable reference if reviving native's own version; a Flutter CustomPainter would need the same interaction model built fresh, since there is no working reference implementation on either platform today.

Not a regression and not blocking -- filed for whoever eventually decides whether this feature should exist.
notes:
PROGRESS 3 — feature complete in code; only the on-device pass is left (head unit is powered off).

Wired the editor end to end:
- SurveillanceConfig model + controller carry roiPolygons (normalised 0..1, keyed Q0..Q3) and
  roiEnabled per quadrant, loaded from GetConfig and sent back through SetConfig on Apply.
- Detection tab gained the zone section: quadrant picker (reusing the existing Front/Right/
  Rear/Left strings, which map exactly onto Q0..Q3), the per-quadrant enable switch, a fixed
  16:9 canvas, a live n/8 point count, and Undo/Clear (disabled until there is something to
  remove). RoiDrawingView.kt's clearRoi()/undoLastPoint() are the reference.
- A polygon below 3 vertices is NOT sent. applyQuadrantRoi treats fewer than 3 as 'clear this
  quadrant', so posting a half-drawn shape would silently wipe the saved one.
- 4 new ARB keys across all 19 catalogs via the json round-trip; quadrant names and 'Clear'
  already existed and were reused.

A REAL BUG the tests caught, worth recording:
The editor was a GestureDetector with HitTestBehavior.opaque and onPanDown, so it claimed
EVERY pan. Inside the settings ListView that meant a user dragging to SCROLL past the editor
drew a row of stray points instead — and could not scroll that part of the pane at all. Found
because a pre-existing Apply-button test started failing once the section pushed Apply below
the fold, and the scroll gesture drew points. Fixed by splitting the interaction: a TAP adds a
vertex, and a custom _VertexDragRecognizer only enters the gesture arena when the press lands
on an existing vertex, so every other drag falls through to the scrollable. Two regression
tests: an empty-canvas drag emits nothing, and a real ListView actually scrolls when dragged
from inside the editor.

Totals: 1386 Dart tests, coverage 99.97%, analyze clean, both i18n gates green, gradlew test +
koverVerify + assembleDebug green.

REMAINING:
- On-device: draw a zone, Apply, confirm it survives a daemon restart (SurveillanceApiHandler
  persists it, so it should), and confirm motion outside the zone stops triggering events.
- web/src/gen/bladewatch/v1/surveillance_pb.ts is still one field behind, deliberately — see
  the previous note. 'cd proto && buf generate' when web/ is back in scope.
close_reason:
Superseded and reversed by BladeWatch-s3sf.

This task built the first ROI client that ever existed on any platform: a Flutter motion-zone
editor, the proto fields to carry a zone over ConnectRPC, and the adapter conversions so the
REST handler could read them. Verified on the head unit, that work also uncovered a real bug --
the proto's map wrapper shape made Apply DESTROY the zone the user had just drawn.

The user reviewed the feature on device and decided it does not earn its keep, choosing the
deepest removal scope (UI, proto, daemon, C++) and asking for the wire-shape fix to be reverted
rather than kept. The evidence supported that: the editor draws on a blank grey box with no
camera backdrop, native's own RoiDrawingView.kt was written but never wired to any fragment,
and the Angular SPA never used the fields either. So the feature was never usable by anyone.

s3sf removed all of it and reserved proto fields 30-34 so the numbers can never be silently
reused. Closing this as done-then-reversed rather than as a live feature.

title: Add a narrow, enum-constrained daemon start/stop-by-type IPC command
description:
## Problem

The Settings → Daemons screen needs to start/stop individual daemon PROCESSES
(CAMERA_DAEMON/SENTRY_DAEMON/ACC_SENTRY_DAEMON/ZROK_TUNNEL independently), but no IPC command
does this — only camera *recording* on/off within the already-running camera daemon exists.

Traced while building BladeWatch-yz1e.3 (Settings hub → Daemons row), not assumed:

- `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/fragment/DaemonsFragment.kt`'s
  `onDaemonToggled(type, enabled)` calls `daemonsViewModel.startDaemon(type)`/`stopDaemon(type)`
  for any of the 4 `DaemonType` values — these launch/kill the `app_process` daemon itself
  (native's own ADB-shell-based `AdbDaemonLauncher`/kill path, same mechanism
  `DaemonStartupManager` uses at boot).
- `flutter_ui/android/.../daemon/DaemonControl.kt`'s `start()`/`stop()` (the ONLY existing
  `daemon.*` IPC methods besides `status()`/`processStatus()`) are explicitly documented as
  camera-recording-only: "no per-camera or streaming parameters — the settings screen only needs
  the daemon up/down, not per-camera control" — but reading `TcpCommandServer.java`'s actual
  `"start"`/`"stop"` case handlers (~line 167) confirms they call
  `CameraDaemon.startCamera(camId, ...)`/`stopCamera(camId, ...)` — i.e. recording control INSIDE
  the camera daemon process, not daemon PROCESS lifecycle. `DaemonControl.kt`'s own doc comment is
  slightly imprecise about this distinction.
- Starting/stopping a daemon PROCESS (not just camera recording) is exactly the
  ADB-shell-execution class of operation BladeWatch-1xt9 already drew a careful boundary around
  for STATUS reads (built a narrow, `pgrep`-based, no-shell-injection command specifically
  because full shell execution was judged unsafe to expose broadly). The same care applies here,
  now for START/STOP rather than just STATUS.

The Daemons screen was built against an injectable `setDaemonEnabled(DaemonKind, bool) ->
Future<bool>` function (see `SettingsDaemonsController` in `flutter_ui/lib/screens/settings/`),
defaulting to always returning `false` ("not supported"). Toggling a switch today shows an
honest "isn't supported yet" message rather than silently failing or pretending to work; Zrok's
own configure/reset flow (via the already-capable `config.*` channel) is unaffected and fully
functional.

## Fix

Add a new, narrow IPC command (e.g. `daemon_start_type`/`daemon_stop_type`) to
`TcpCommandServer.java`, taking a `DaemonType`-constrained enum string (not a free-form command),
dispatching to whatever native already uses for daemon process lifecycle
(`AdbDaemonLauncher`/`DaemonStartupManager` — read these fully first to find the actual
start/stop entry points `DaemonsViewModel.startDaemon()`/`stopDaemon()` call into). Validate the
type argument against the fixed enum before dispatching — never pass the raw string into any
shell invocation.

Then, mirroring BladeWatch-1xt9's pattern: extend `flutter_ui/android/.../daemon/DaemonControl.kt`
with `startType(type: String)`/`stopType(type: String)`, wire `"daemon.startType"`/
`"daemon.stopType"` in `MainActivity.kt`, add matching methods to `flutter_ui/lib/platform/daemon_channel.dart`.
Then wire a real `setDaemonEnabled` implementation into `SettingsDaemonsController` from
`flutter_ui/lib/main.dart`, replacing the current always-`false` default.

## Constraints

Same as BladeWatch-1xt9: this task may modify `TcpCommandServer.java` (that's the point of it)
but nothing else under `server/`/`daemon/`; don't touch `PeerCredentials.java`; the new command
must validate its type argument against the fixed 4-value enum and must NOT accept or construct
arbitrary shell commands. Do NOT commit.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] New IPC command(s) added; can start/stop SENTRY_DAEMON/ACC_SENTRY_DAEMON/ZROK_TUNNEL
      independently, without ADB, without any shell-injection surface.
- [ ] Kotlin/Dart wrapper methods added, tests written first.
- [ ] `SettingsDaemonsController`'s injected `setDaemonEnabled` is swapped from the current
      always-`false` default to the real channel in `main.dart`; existing tests (already covering
      the "not supported" default path via the injected-function seam) still pass, plus new tests
      for the real-channel path (including a rejected/invalid-type case).
- [ ] All 3 coverage gates pass, none lower than before.
- [ ] `./gradlew assembleDebug` (both Gradle projects) succeeds.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
notes:
BLOCKED ON A DECISION — found while starting implementation, verified in source.

Implementing daemon_start_type/daemon_stop_type exactly as this task describes would ship a
toggle that SILENTLY UNDOES ITSELF within 30 seconds. Do not implement it as written.

Why. DaemonStartupManager (app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/daemon/
DaemonStartupManager.kt) runs a health check every 30s in the APP process. runHealthCheck()
(line 434) relaunches every CORE daemon unless it is in userStoppedDaemons, and every enabled
OPTIONAL daemon likewise (lines 437, 443). userStoppedDaemons (line 46) is a plain in-process
`mutableSetOf<DaemonType>()`, and it is CLEARED on every app launch (line 80) and on boot
(lines 66, 142).

So a stop issued by net.bladewatch.flutter over IPC cannot mark the daemon user-stopped: the set
lives in a different process with no cross-process backing. The daemon dies, the health check
sees it dead, and relaunches it. The Daemons switch flips off, then back on. That is strictly
worse than the current honest "not supported yet" message, which is why this must not just be
built as specified.

Two further constraints found at the same time:

1. CAMERA_DAEMON must be excluded from stop, and the UI must say so. The IPC server answering
   the request lives INSIDE CameraDaemon (TcpCommandServer is started by it). Stopping it kills
   the server, and the Flutter APK has no ADB, so nothing could start it again over IPC — a
   one-way door out of Flutter's reach. This task's own acceptance criteria already lists only
   SENTRY_DAEMON/ACC_SENTRY_DAEMON/ZROK_TUNNEL, but the Daemons screen renders all four, so the
   fourth needs a deliberate disabled/explained state rather than a switch that cannot work.

2. Starting a daemon needs no ADB. The daemon already runs as shell UID, the same UID
   app_process daemons are launched under, so it can fork the launch command directly — the same
   reasoning BladeWatch-1xt9 used for pgrep. The exact command is reconstructible from the
   observed live process:
     sh -c CLASSPATH=<apk path> app_process /system/bin --nice-name=<name> <class>
   The APK path must be resolved at runtime, not baked in: it changes on every reinstall
   (observed today: net.bladewatch.app-_j1fxja9… then -vXP3uLdeg22…).

THE DECISION NEEDED: where does "the user stopped this daemon" live so that both processes agree?

  (a) Persist it in UnifiedConfigManager (e.g. a `daemons` section), read by both the new IPC
      command and DaemonStartupManager.runHealthCheck(). Cheap, and the public-config IPC for
      exactly this shape already exists (BladeWatch-hygs). BUT it changes behaviour: native
      deliberately clears user-stopped on every launch and boot, so today a stopped daemon comes
      back after a reboot. Persisting it means a user could stop the DASHCAM and have it stay
      stopped across reboots. That is a product/safety call, not a technical one.
  (b) Keep the native semantics (stop lasts until the next app launch/boot) by holding the flag
      in the daemon and having DaemonStartupManager ask the daemon for it. No behaviour change,
      more moving parts, and the flag dies with the daemon it describes.
  (c) Restrict the feature to ZROK_TUNNEL only. Its enabled state is ALREADY persisted natively
      (OPTIONAL_DAEMONS + PreferencesManager.isDaemonEnabled/onDaemonToggled), so the question is
      already answered for it. The other three keep the honest "not supported" message. Smallest
      correct step; leaves most of the screen inert.

Note (a) and (b) both require editing DaemonStartupManager, which is outside this task's stated
"nothing else under server//daemon/" constraint — the scope needs widening either way.

Do not guess. Get this decided before writing code.
close_reason: Implemented per the decisions recorded on this issue: ZROK_TUNNEL only, CAMERA_DAEMON not stoppable. Added daemon_set_enabled to TcpCommandServer, gated by a fixed allow-list (TOGGLEABLE_DAEMONS) checked before anything happens; nothing from the wire reaches a shell and the PIDs signalled come from the server's own procfs scan keyed by the enum, never from the request. Enabling records intent in UnifiedConfigManager's new cross-process daemons section and lets DaemonStartupManager's health check do the real launch through the full ZrokLauncher flow; disabling records intent AND kills the process, because that health check only ever relaunches. DaemonStartupManager now prefers the config section over app-private SharedPreferences (falling back to it when unset) so a toggle from either UI cannot drift. Added DaemonControl.setDaemonEnabled (Kotlin), daemon.setEnabled in MainActivity, DaemonChannel.setDaemonEnabled (Dart), DaemonKind.canToggle, and SettingsDaemonsController.enabledSetterFor wired in main.dart. The Zrok row now has both a configure button and a working switch; the other three keep a switch for visibility but are refused locally with the existing message and no IPC round trip. 9 new Java tests, 2 Kotlin, 2 Dart channel, plus updated controller/screen tests -- 3 existing tests pinned the old behaviour and were rewritten to the new truth. Verified on device: all three core daemons and a shell-metacharacter type refused, ZROK accepted, config round-trips to daemons.ZROK_TUNNEL and back, tapping Surveillance Daemon shows the honest message with the switch and daemon untouched. NOTE: the config now records daemons.ZROK_TUNNEL=false, which matches the tunnel's actual pre-existing state (no token configured, never running). 1334 Dart tests, coverage back to 99.97% after extracting the main.dart wiring closure into a testable factory, both Kover gates green, assembleDebug green. docs/ipc-auth-and-secrets.md and docs/daemons-and-processes.md updated.

title: Expose UnifiedConfigManager's public config sections over IPC (no path exists today)
description:
## Problem

Several Settings screens need to read/write `UnifiedConfigManager`'s PUBLIC (non-secret) config
sections from the Flutter APK, but no IPC command exposes that store — only the daemon-owned
SECRET store (`SecretConfigStore`, via `secret_get`/`secret_put`/`secret_delete`, wrapped by
`ConfigChannel`/`SecretConfigChannel` from BladeWatch-ncbb.2) is reachable today.

Traced while building BladeWatch-yz1e.3 (Settings hub), not assumed:

- `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/fragment/settings/SettingsOverlayFragment.kt`
  reads/writes `UnifiedConfigManager.getStatusOverlay()`/`setStatusOverlay()` — the
  `statusOverlay` section (`cameraVisible`/`tripVisible` booleans) that gates the floating
  status-pill segments.
- `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/fragment/settings/SettingsPrivacyFragment.kt`
  reads/writes `UnifiedConfigManager.isTimingLogsEnabled()`/`setTimingLogsEnabled()` and
  `isDebugLogsEnabled()`/`setDebugLogsEnabled()` — the `developerOptions` section
  (`timingLogsEnabled` default true, `debugLogsEnabled` default false).
- `UnifiedConfigManager`'s file (`/storage/emulated/0/BladeWatch/data/bladewatch_config.json`) is
  world-rw (chmod 666) and BOTH the app UID and daemon UID already read/write it directly — but
  this path is NOT inside `net.bladewatch.flutter`'s package-scoped storage, and there is no
  existing IPC command mirroring `secret_get_section`/`secret_put` for this store. Grepped
  `TcpCommandServer.java`'s full command switch: no `config_get`/`config_put` case exists for the
  public store, only the `secret_*` family.

Both screens were built against an injectable `loadSettings`/`persist` function pair (see
`SettingsOverlayController`/`SettingsPrivacyController` in
`flutter_ui/lib/screens/settings/`) — same shape as `DashboardController.tunnelUrlSource` from
BladeWatch-m1po — so this task can wire in a real implementation later without touching either
controller. Their current defaults: Overlay always reports both indicators visible (native's own
fallback values) and silently no-ops on write; Privacy's logging toggles default to
timing=on/debug=off (native's own defaults) and also no-op on write. Toggling either currently
updates in-memory UI state for the session but does not persist across an app restart.

## Fix

Add a new IPC command family (e.g. `config_get_section`/`config_put`/`config_delete`, mirroring
`secret_get_section`/`secret_put`/`secret_delete`'s shape exactly) to `TcpCommandServer.java`,
backed by `UnifiedConfigManager` instead of `SecretConfigStore`. Since this store is NOT secret,
consider whether a stricter allowlist of writable sections is warranted (`statusOverlay`,
`developerOptions` at minimum) rather than accepting an arbitrary section name, to avoid a new
command becoming a generic "write anything to the public config" primitive without review.

Then, mirroring BladeWatch-1xt9/ncbb.2's pattern: add a Kotlin wrapper
(`flutter_ui/android/.../config/PublicConfigChannel.kt` or similar) alongside the existing
`SecretConfigChannel.kt`, wire `"publicConfig.get"`/`"publicConfig.put"` (or similar) in
`MainActivity.kt`, add a Dart `PublicConfigChannel` (`flutter_ui/lib/platform/`) alongside the
existing `ConfigChannel`. Then swap `SettingsOverlayController`'s and
`SettingsPrivacyController`'s injected functions in `flutter_ui/lib/main.dart` from their current
defaults to real implementations backed by the new channel.

## Constraints

Same as BladeWatch-1xt9/m1po: this task may modify `TcpCommandServer.java` (that's the point of
it) but nothing else under `server/`/`daemon/`; don't touch `PeerCredentials.java`; don't
reintroduce free-form shell execution. Do NOT commit.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] New IPC command(s) added, reads/writes real `UnifiedConfigManager` sections without ADB.
- [ ] Kotlin/Dart wrapper methods added, tests written first.
- [ ] `SettingsOverlayController`/`SettingsPrivacyController`'s injected functions are swapped
      from their always-default/no-op fallbacks to the real channel in `main.dart`; existing
      tests (already covering the "no follow-up yet" default path via the injected-function seam)
      still pass, plus new tests for the real-channel path.
- [ ] All 3 coverage gates pass, none lower than before.
- [ ] `./gradlew assembleDebug` (both Gradle projects) succeeds.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
close_reason: Added config_get_section/config_put to TcpCommandServer, backed by UnifiedConfigManager and gated by an explicit allow-list (statusOverlay, developerOptions only). Reads route through the same typed accessors the native UI uses, so defaults for absent keys match native exactly. Added PublicConfigChannel on both the Kotlin and Dart sides (separate from the secret-store ConfigChannel) and wired SettingsOverlayController/SettingsPrivacyController to it via their existing injected-function seams. Both controllers now revert the switch if the IPC write fails, so a failed write cannot look like a saved setting. Verified on device: both panes read the real config (Overlay showed both off, Privacy showed debug-logs on, neither of which is the hardcoded default), writes persist across an app restart, and the native StatusOverlayService picked the change up live with no service restart. Non-allow-listed sections (network, surveillance) refused for both read and write. IPC token still 644; PeerCredentials untouched. 1324 Dart tests, 99.97% coverage, both Kover gates green. docs/ipc-auth-and-secrets.md updated (and its stale references to the removed shell command corrected).

title: Expose the Zrok tunnel URL over IPC (no IPC path exists today)
description:
## Problem

The Dashboard's tunnel tile/hero-chip/QR-code feature needs the current Zrok tunnel URL, but
there is no IPC or RPC path to it from the Flutter APK — traced through the actual native
source while building BladeWatch-yz1e.2 (Dashboard), not assumed:

- `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/daemon/ZrokController.kt`: `_tunnelUrl` is
  an in-memory `MutableLiveData<String?>`, set only from `ZrokLauncher`'s callback when a
  tunnel process is launched/monitored via ADB (`onTunnelUrl(url: String)`).
- The URL is separately cached in `PreferencesManager.setLastZrokUrl()`
  (`app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/util/PreferencesManager.kt:179`) — but that
  uses plain Android `SharedPreferences`, private to `net.bladewatch.app`, not the IPC-backed
  `SecretConfigStore`/`secret_*` family. Not reachable from `net.bladewatch.flutter` even
  though the two APKs share a UID.
- No proto service exposes a tunnel/Zrok concept at all (checked all 12: Auth, Notifications,
  Recordings, SafeLocations, Settings, Storage, Stream, Surveillance, System, Trips, Update,
  Vehicle).

So there is currently no IPC-only way for the Flutter APK to learn the tunnel URL, matching
the exact shape of the gap BladeWatch-1xt9 already fixed for daemon process status — same
root cause (a native feature built ADB/local-storage-first, before the Flutter APK's
IPC-only constraint existed).

## Fix

Add a new IPC command (e.g. `tunnelStatus`) to `TcpCommandServer.java`, returning the current
Zrok tunnel URL if one is active. Read `ZrokController.kt` and `ZrokLauncher.kt` fully first —
the daemon-side implementation needs to determine the current URL without an app-UID-only
`PreferencesManager`/SharedPreferences read (the daemon runs as shell UID, in a different
process than `PreferencesManager`'s owner). Options to investigate: whether `zrok status`

(Kotlin, `flutter_ui/android/.../daemon/DaemonControl.kt`), wire `"daemon.tunnelStatus"` in

touching the screen/controller once this lands — see `DashboardController`'s

reports "no tunnel."

## Constraints

Same as BladeWatch-1xt9: this task is allowed to modify `TcpCommandServer.java` (that's the
point of it) but nothing else under `server/`/`daemon/`; don't touch `PeerCredentials.java`;
don't reintroduce free-form shell execution — only whatever fixed, narrow check the chosen
implementation needs. Do NOT commit.

- [ ] Kotlin/Dart wrapper methods added, tests written first.

title: Native app: translatable=false URL strings corrupted by a past translation pass in most locales
description:
## Problem

4 keys in `app/src/main/res/values/strings.xml` are marked `translatable="false"` because they are plain URLs that must never vary by locale:

- `settings_about_support_kofi_url` = `https://ko-fi.com/E1E71XALHX`
- `settings_about_license_url` = `https://github.com/yash-srivastava/BladeWatch-release/blob/main/LICENSE`
- `settings_about_source_url` = `https://github.com/yash-srivastava/BladeWatch-release`
- `settings_about_star_url` = `https://github.com/yash-srivastava/BladeWatch-release`

Despite the `translatable="false"` marker, a past bulk/LLM translation pass over this catalog translated these 4 keys anyway in most of the 16 non-English `values-*/strings.xml` files. Having no real content to translate (a bare URL), it hallucinated unrelated sentences instead of leaving them alone. This is live in the shipped app today: on a device set to one of the affected locales, Settings → About → Source/License/Star/Support opens (or tries to open) garbage text instead of the real link.

Verified by direct inspection (`grep -oP` against each `values-*/strings.xml`) on 2026-09-12:

- **Hallucinated/unrelated text** (8 locales): `values-de`, `values-es`, `values-fr`, `values-it`, `values-ja`, `values-nl`, `values-zh-rCN`, `values-zh-rTW`. Example: `values-de`'s `settings_about_source_url` is `"Das ist ein sehr schönes Beispiel."` ("This is a very nice example.") — not a URL at all. `values-zh-rTW`'s is `"沒有任何樓盤符合您的搜尋 -"` ("No listings match your search") — looks like leftover real-estate-app boilerplate from whatever bulk corpus the translation pass drew from.
- **Blank** (1 locale): `values-th` — all 4 keys are empty strings.
- **Malformed but recognizable** (2 locales): `values-ko` (URL wrapped in literal `[...]` brackets, `http://` not `https://`), `values-nb` (`settings_about_license_url` is literally `"HTTPS: http://github.com/.../LICENSE"` — a stray "HTTPS:" prefix glued onto an `http://` URL).
- **Already correct** (5 locales): `values-hi`, `values-pt-rBR`, `values-ru`, `values-tr`, `values-vi`.

This was discovered while writing `tools/i18n/xml_to_arb.py` for BladeWatch-ncbb.3 (porting these strings to Flutter ARB). The Flutter side is unaffected — that script pins all 4 `translatable="false"` keys to the English template's value for every locale ARB, regardless of what (if anything) the source locale XML says, so this bug does not propagate into the new Flutter UI. This task is only about fixing it at the source, for the native UI, which still reads these files directly.

## Fix

For each of the 16 non-English `app/src/main/res/values-*/strings.xml` files, **delete** the `<string>` element for these 4 keys entirely (do not just overwrite the text). Since the keys are `translatable="false"`, Android's normal resource fallback already serves `values/strings.xml`'s correct value to every locale that has no override — deleting the bad per-locale copies is the permanent fix; it also means these 4 values can never drift out of sync again, since after this change they exist in exactly one file. (Do not delete the entries from `values/strings.xml` itself — that is the template and is already correct.)

`app/build.gradle.kts`'s `validateAndroidStrings` task already excludes `translatable="false"` keys from its key-parity comparison (`parseStrings()`: `if (el.getAttribute("translatable") == "false") continue`), so removing these 4 entries from the 16 locale files will not trip a "missing key" failure there.

## Constraints

- Only touch the 4 named keys. Do not touch any other `<string>`/`<plurals>` entry.
- Do not touch `values/strings.xml` (the English template) — it already has the correct values and is not `translatable="false"`-affected there.
- Do not touch `flutter_ui/` — the Flutter ARBs already work around this independently (see Problem section); no change needed there as a result of this task.
- Do NOT commit. Leave changes in the working tree.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The 4 keys are completely removed from all 16 `values-*/strings.xml` files (grep confirms zero remaining occurrences of `settings_about_support_kofi_url`, `settings_about_license_url`, `settings_about_source_url`, `settings_about_star_url` outside `values/strings.xml`).
- [ ] `values/strings.xml` is unchanged.
- [ ] `./gradlew validateAndroidStrings` still passes (proves the deletion doesn't trip the parity check).
- [ ] `./gradlew assembleDebug` succeeds.
- [ ] Spot-check on a device or emulator set to at least one previously-broken locale (e.g. German) that Settings → About → Source/License/Star/Support now show/open the real GitHub/Ko-fi URLs.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
acceptance_criteria: 16 locale files have the 4 settings_about_*_url keys removed; values/strings.xml unchanged; ./gradlew validateAndroidStrings passes; ./gradlew assembleDebug succeeds; spot-checked on-device in at least one previously-broken locale.

  content did not respond to `input swipe` at the coordinates tried; navigation was done

  fresh "Allow USB debugging?" prompt and a storage-permission prompt after the reinstall —
  both handled via `input tap`/checked "always allow" so they will not recur).
- Also handled during reinstall (routine, not part of this fix): daemons stopped/relaunched
  correctly, ADB TCP connection dropped and recovered twice as documented in CLAUDE.md

## Constraints honored

- Only the 4 named keys touched, only in the 16 non-English locale files.

- `flutter_ui/` untouched (its ARBs already independently pin these 4 keys to the template,

- Not committed — changes left in the working tree.

No mistakes found on verification.

title: Add build-failing key-parity validation for res/values*/strings.xml (17 locales, currently unguarded)
description:
## Context

`res/values*/strings.xml` has **624 translatable keys across 17 locales** and **nothing validates them**. A key added to English alone builds clean and ships missing strings in 16 languages, with no warning at any point.

This is not hypothetical for this project. The web catalogs had exactly this class of failure twice — a stale cached catalog rendered raw keys across the whole SPA, and LLM-edited locale JSON shipped with smart-quote delimiters and unescaped quotes in CJK values. Both were fixed by adding a check that **fails the build**, which is how `validateI18nCatalogs` came to exist.

That task guards only `src/main/assets/web/i18n/*.json`. The Android string catalogs — the larger, older, more edited set — are still unguarded.

## Why now

Any task that adds a user-facing string touches all 17 files by hand. `BladeWatch-ofzb` is the immediate example and currently has to verify parity by counting occurrences manually. That does not scale and will be skipped.

## Steps

1. Add a `validateAndroidStrings` Gradle task in `app/build.gradle.kts`, next to the existing `validateI18nCatalogs` (line 568) and hooked into `preBuild` the same way (line 613). Follow that task's structure rather than inventing a new pattern.
2. Parse `app/src/main/res/values/strings.xml` as the master key set — only elements marked translatable (the existing file uses `translatable="false"` for some entries; respect that attribute).
3. For each of the 16 `values-<lang>/strings.xml` files, compare key sets against the master and **fail the build** listing the missing keys per locale, in the same style as the existing task's error output.
4. Also fail on malformed XML, and on unescaped apostrophes in string values — the Android-specific footgun equivalent to the smart-quote problem that hit the JSON catalogs.
5. Run it against the current tree **before** adding any enforcement: if the existing 17 files already have gaps, report the count and fix them, or record an explicit allow-list with a reason. Do not ship a task that fails on day one.

## Constraints

- Locale directory names are Android-style: `values-pt-rBR`, `values-zh-rCN`, `values-zh-rTW`, and `values-<lang>` for the rest. `values-night` is **theme colours, not a locale** — exclude it.
- Do NOT modify `validateI18nCatalogs` or weaken its behaviour.
- Do NOT modify `web/`.
- Do NOT auto-translate or auto-fill missing values. The task reports; a human supplies text.
- Do NOT commit.

## Conventions for this refactor

- Kotlin lives under `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/` with `package net.bladewatch.app.*`. Gradle logic lives in `app/build.gradle.kts` — there is no root `app/build.gradle.kts`.
- JVM tests go in `app/src/test/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/`, measured by Kover (`./gradlew test koverVerify`).

## Tests (TDD — required)

**Write the failing test first.**

- Prove the task **fails** when a key is removed from one locale, and **passes** once restored. Do this for real, then restore — a guard nobody has seen fail is not a guard.
- Prove it fails on malformed XML and on an unescaped apostrophe.
- Prove `values-night` is excluded and does not trigger a false failure.
- 100% coverage of the comparison and reporting logic, or each gap justified in the notes.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `validateAndroidStrings` exists in `app/build.gradle.kts` and is hooked into `preBuild`.
- [ ] It fails the build on a missing key, naming the locale and the key.
- [ ] It fails on malformed XML and on an unescaped apostrophe.
- [ ] `values-night` is excluded; `translatable="false"` entries are excluded.
- [ ] The current tree passes, or every pre-existing gap is fixed or explicitly allow-listed with a reason recorded.
- [ ] Each failure mode demonstrated once for real and then restored.
- [ ] `./gradlew assembleDebug` and `./gradlew test` pass; `koverVerify` figure recorded and not lower than before.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
close_reason:
Added `validateAndroidStrings` to app/build.gradle.kts, right after `validateI18nCatalogs` and hooked into `preBuild` the same way (did not modify validateI18nCatalogs itself — confirmed by diff, still exactly 2 references: its definition and its preBuild dependency line, both pre-existing).

What it checks, using javax.xml.parsers.DocumentBuilderFactory (stdlib, no new dependency):
- values/strings.xml is the master key set (translatable="false" entries excluded from the required set, matching how Android itself treats them).
- Every values-<lang>/strings.xml (values-pt-rBR, values-zh-rCN, values-zh-rTW, values-<lang> for the rest) is compared against the master key set; any missing key fails the build naming the locale and up to 5 example keys.
- Malformed XML fails the build with the parser's own message, and — since a parse failure has no real key set — does NOT also cascade into reporting every master key as "missing" (an early version of this did exactly that noise; fixed by making parseStrings return a nullable key set and skipping the key-comparison when null).
- Unescaped apostrophes fail the build. Implemented as a small state-machine scanner (track whether a `\` immediately precedes the char, and whether we're inside a `"..."` span) rather than a naive `contains("'")/ count` check, specifically because Android allows two valid styles — `\'` and wrapping the whole value in double quotes — and a naive check would false-positive on the second, legitimate style.
- values-night is excluded by name (it's dark-mode colors/themes, not a locale — it doesn't even have a strings.xml on this tree, confirmed by listing the directory).

Ran against the current tree before wiring in any enforcement, per the task's own instruction: zero pre-existing gaps. 620 translatable keys (not 624 as the task's context paragraph said — that figure was measured before this session's other tasks touched a few strings; 620 is the fresh, live count and is what matters) across 16 non-English locales, full parity, valid XML, no unescaped apostrophes. No fixes or allow-list needed.

Verification — each failure mode demonstrated for real against the actual tracked files, then restored, with MD5 checksums confirming byte-for-byte restoration each time (git checkout was not used for restore since values-de/es/fr already carry legitimate uncommitted edits from BladeWatch-ofzb earlier this session that must not be discarded):
1. Deleted `dialog_ok` from values-de/strings.xml (line removed via sed, backed up first) → validateAndroidStrings FAILED: "values-de/strings.xml: 1 key(s) missing vs values/strings.xml (dialog_ok)". Restored from backup, MD5 matched the pre-mutation hash (32aa2f74...), task PASSED again.
2. Corrupted values-fr/strings.xml by stripping its closing `</resources>` tag → FAILED: "values-fr/strings.xml: malformed XML — XML document structures must start and end within the same entity." (and nothing else — confirmed the no-cascade fix). Restored from a full-file backup, MD5 matched (c044fdbe...), task PASSED.
3. Changed values-es's `dialog_ok` to `OK, don't worry` (bare unescaped apostrophe) → FAILED: "values-es/strings.xml: dialog_ok: unescaped apostrophe (use \' or wrap the whole value in double quotes)". Then changed it to `"OK, don't worry"` (double-quote-wrapped, Android's other valid style) → PASSED, proving the double-quote exception is not a false-positive gap. Restored the original `OK`, MD5 matched (b4498c27...), task PASSED.
4. Created a throwaway app/src/main/res/values-night/strings.xml containing exactly one unrelated key (nowhere near the other 620) → task still PASSED (still reported "16 locales", not 17) — proves the exclusion actually does something rather than accidentally passing because the file never existed. Deleted the throwaway file afterward; `git status` shows no diff for values-night (it was never a tracked file).

`./gradlew clean assembleDebug test` — BUILD SUCCESSFUL from a clean build; confirmed validateAndroidStrings actually executes (not skipped/cached — it has no declared inputs/outputs so Gradle never marks it UP-TO-DATE) and prints "Android strings: 16 locales, full key parity with values/strings.xml (620 keys), valid XML, no unescaped apostrophes ✓" as part of the real build.

Not applicable: this is Gradle build-script logic (Kotlin DSL), not application code — like its sibling validateI18nCatalogs, there is no JUnit test file for it; "test coverage" here means every branch demonstrated failing-then-passing for real against the live tree, as done above and as the task's own Tests section asked for ("do this for real, then restore — a guard nobody has seen fail is not a guard"). `./gradlew koverVerify` still doesn't exist (same pre-existing gap noted on BladeWatch-7965.1 and BladeWatch-ofzb — Kover isn't wired in until BladeWatch-ncbb.5, which is gated behind unrelated epics) and this task adds no Kotlin/Java application code for Kover to measure regardless.

Did not modify validateI18nCatalogs or web/. Did not auto-translate or auto-fill anything (none was needed — zero gaps found). Not committed — all changes left in the working tree.

title: Update docs and CLAUDE.md for the Flutter architecture
description:
## Context

Update the documentation to match reality. `CLAUDE.md` has a Documentation Maintenance section mandating this, and the docs are the onboarding path for future agents — stale docs here actively cause wrong work.

## Files to update

- `docs/architecture.md` — the "Android app process — UI shell only" description now means a Flutter host. Update the hybrid-architecture split.
- `docs/ui-ux-design-language.md` (22.5 KB) — **the biggest change.** It currently states the native Android shell is the canonical M3 source of truth and lists `app/src/main/res/values/themes_bladewatch.xml` / `app/src/main/res/values/colors_m3.xml` / `app/src/main/res/values/dimens_bladewatch.xml` as authoritative. Those files are gone or reduced. The Dart `ThemeData` is now the source of truth, with the Angular SPA still tracking the same language by convention. Update the "Two layers, one language" table.
- `docs/features.md` (16.6 KB) — any description of native screens.
- `docs/webview-migration.md` (11.9 KB) — this documents the OLD WebView-to-native migration and its status line says "Migration complete". It is now doubly historical, and it describes `WebViewFragment` as "still present", which will be false. Either retire it or add a clear header explaining it describes a superseded architecture.
- `docs/build-and-operations.md` — add the Flutter build step; keep the existing Filament/Adreno 610 warning, it still applies to the three.js hero.
- `docs/daemons-and-processes.md` — only if daemon behaviour changed (it should not have).
- `docs/README.md` — the one-line app description.

## Do NOT update

`docs/http-api-reference.md`, `docs/byd-integrations.md`, `docs/data-flow-and-storage.md`, `docs/ipc-auth-and-secrets.md`, `docs/networking-and-tunnels.md`, `docs/surveillance-implementation.md` — unless this refactor actually changed those behaviours, which it should not have. Check before editing; do not rewrite a doc just because you read it.

Also update `CLAUDE.md` itself: the "Key Source Locations" list points at deleted fragments, and the Architecture section describes the native UI shell.

## Stale claims to correct while you are in there

- `docs/ipc-auth-and-secrets.md` lists `shell` as a live privileged IPC command. It was **removed** as an RCE fix — see `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/TcpCommandServer.java:485-486`. So does the comment at `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/TcpCommandServer.java:98-99`.
- `CLAUDE.md` and `docs/ui-ux-design-language.md` claim Android 7.1 / Chrome 58. Measured: **Android 10 / API 29, WebView 74, Vulkan 1.1**.
- `CLAUDE.md`'s Testing section lists 4 test files; there are **22** (~3,100 LOC) under `app/src/test/`.
- Nothing validates `res/values*/strings.xml` key parity — `validateI18nCatalogs` covers only the web JSON catalogs. Note this where a future reader will find it.

## Also

Record the durable lessons with `bd remember` — the two-APK / `sharedUserId` arrangement and why it exists (the peer-UID gate in `PeerCredentials`), the signing-key requirement, the fact that adding `sharedUserId` forces an uninstall rather than an upgrade, and which Impeller backend was selected and pinned for this Adreno 610 / API 29 device — so the next session does not rediscover them. Also correct the stale platform claims in `CLAUDE.md` and `docs/ui-ux-design-language.md`: the head unit is **Android 10 / API 29 with Vulkan 1.1 and WebView 74**, not Android 7.1 / Chrome 58. Do NOT create a MEMORY.md file; this project uses `bd remember`.

## Constraints

- Do NOT modify `web/` or any doc describing it inaccurately-but-harmlessly; keep the SPA's documented role intact — it did not change.
- Do NOT commit.

## Conventions for this refactor

- Dart lives under `flutter_ui/lib/` with `screens/<name>/` holding a pure-Dart `ChangeNotifier` controller, models, and the screen widget. Kotlin lives under `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/` with `package net.bladewatch.app.*`.
- Coverage gates: `flutter test --coverage` (Dart, `lib/gen` excluded) and `./gradlew koverVerify` (Kotlin). Both thresholds ratchet upward and may never be lowered.
- **No golden tests.** Visual parity is verified on the device against `screenshots/native/`.
- Verification happens on the head unit at <CAR_IP>:5555. Always pass `-s <CAR_IP>:5555` to every adb command.

## Tests (regression — required)

This task adds no features, so the bar is regression rather than TDD:

- `./gradlew test` passes with zero skipped tests.
- `cd flutter_ui && flutter test` passes with zero skipped tests.
- `flutter test --coverage` and `./gradlew koverVerify` both run, both figures recorded, **neither lower** than the previous recorded figure.
- If a test had to be deleted because the code under test was deleted, say which, and confirm the behaviour it covered either no longer exists or is now covered by a Dart test.
- Any bug found while verifying gets a **failing test written first**, then the fix — never a fix without a test that would have caught it.

- [ ] No doc still describes the native Kotlin fragments as the in-car UI.

- [ ] Changes left uncommitted in the working tree.
- [ ] `./gradlew test` and `flutter test` both pass with zero skipped tests.
- [ ] Dart and Kotlin coverage figures recorded, neither lower than the previous figure.
- [ ] Any bug found got a failing test written first, then the fix.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
