title: Drop Gradle dependencies that only served the native UI
description:
## Context

Drop the Android dependencies that only existed to serve the deleted native UI. Do this AFTER the deletion task so the compiler tells you what is genuinely unused.

## Candidates to remove

From `app/build.gradle.kts` and `gradle/libs.versions.toml`:

- `osmdroid-android` (6.1.20) — the map is now `flutter_map`
- `zxing-core` (3.5.3) — QR is now `qr_flutter`
- `androidx-navigation-fragment-ktx` and `androidx-navigation-ui-ktx` (2.8.5) — nav is now Dart
- `androidx-lifecycle-viewmodel-ktx` and `androidx-lifecycle-livedata-ktx` (2.8.7) — the ViewModels are gone
- `material` (1.13.0) and `androidx-appcompat` (1.7.1) — **check carefully.** `MainActivity` extends `AppCompatActivity`; if `BladeWatch-81g9.1` kept a minimal non-launcher activity for bootstrap, appcompat may still be required. Only remove if genuinely unreferenced.

These are removed from the **main** APK (`app/build.gradle.kts`). The Flutter APK has its own independent dependency set in `flutter_ui/android/app/build.gradle.kts` — do not confuse the two.

## Must KEEP

Everything the daemons and the non-UI layer need:

- `connectrpc-kotlin` + okhttp + google-java-ext, and `protobuf-java:4.35.0` (**version must stay matched to the buf plugin pin `buf.build/protocolbuffers/java:v35.0`** — there is a comment in the dependencies block explaining that a drift here fails protobuf's RuntimeVersion check at class load)
- `dadb` — daemon launching
- `Java-WebSocket` — the live stream server
- TensorFlow Lite (all four artifacts) — YOLO11n surveillance gate
- `okhttp` — OTA updater
- `androidx.security:security-crypto` — encrypted prefs
- `h2database` — pure-Java embedded SQL, works for UID 2000 precisely because it has no `.so`
- `rtmp-client`, `androidx-work-runtime-ktx`

## Also check

- `app/proguard-rules.pro` — remove keep rules for deleted classes, keep the `io.flutter.**` rules.
- Unused `uses-permission` entries in `app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml`? **Leave the BYD HAL permissions alone** — they are matched to the BYD SDK and removing one silently breaks a vehicle API.

## Constraints

- Remove one dependency at a time and rebuild. A dependency removed from the catalog that is still referenced fails the build loudly; one still needed at RUNTIME by a daemon fails silently on the car.
- Do NOT change the protobuf/buf version pinning.
- Do NOT modify `web/`, the daemon, or the protos.
- Do NOT commit.

## Conventions for this refactor

- Dart lives under `flutter_ui/lib/` with `screens/<name>/` holding a pure-Dart `ChangeNotifier` controller, models, and the screen widget. Kotlin lives under `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/` with `package net.bladewatch.app.*`.
- Coverage gates: `flutter test --coverage` (Dart, `lib/gen` excluded) and `./gradlew koverVerify` (Kotlin). Both thresholds ratchet upward and may never be lowered.
- **No golden tests.** Visual parity is verified on the device against `screenshots/native/`.
- Verification happens on the head unit at <CAR_IP>:5555. Always pass `-s <CAR_IP>:5555` to every adb command.

## Tests (regression — required)

This task adds no features, so the bar is regression rather than TDD:

- `./gradlew test` passes with zero skipped tests.
- `cd flutter_ui && flutter test` passes with zero skipped tests.
- `flutter test --coverage` and `./gradlew koverVerify` both run, both figures recorded, **neither lower** than the previous recorded figure.
- If a test had to be deleted because the code under test was deleted, say which, and confirm the behaviour it covered either no longer exists or is now covered by a Dart test.
- Any bug found while verifying gets a **failing test written first**, then the fix — never a fix without a test that would have caught it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `./gradlew assembleDebug` and `assembleRelease` both succeed.
- [ ] `./gradlew test` passes.
- [ ] Clean reinstall on device: all daemons start, recording, surveillance, live view, tunnel and BYD vehicle reads all still work — a runtime-only dependency break will only show here.
- [ ] APK size reduction recorded.
- [ ] No BYD HAL permission removed from the manifest.
- [ ] `./gradlew test` and `flutter test` both pass with zero skipped tests.
- [ ] Dart and Kotlin coverage figures recorded, neither lower than the previous figure.
- [ ] Any bug found got a failing test written first, then the fix.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.

Native in-car UI deleted. **41,793 lines removed across 172 files**, both APKs build, and the

## What went

- `ui/fragment/**` — 53 files, every screen and its liveview/location/performance/recording/

- `ui/adapter/**`, `ui/view/**`, `ui/dialog/**`, `ui/common/BladeTheme.kt`,

- **10,200 strings**: every `values*/strings.xml` pruned from 618 keys to 29

verbatim in its original order. It extends `Activity` instead of `AppCompatActivity` now (no
AppCompat UI left to host, and it takes the daemon APK off a dependency BladeWatch-81g9.3 can
drop) and never calls `setContentView`.

## Three places the task's delete-list was wrong, found by rebuilding rather than trusting it

1. **`overlay_status.xml` and `dialog_setup_guide.xml` must survive.** They belong to
   `StatusOverlayService` and `SetupGuideDialog` — a floating system-overlay window Flutter
   cannot provide. Deleting them crashed the build; both restored from git.
2. **`values*/strings.xml` cannot be deleted, only pruned.** Four surviving components still use
   `R.string`. The 29 keys kept were derived by scanning actual consumers (Java/Kotlin `R.string.`,
   every surviving `@string/` in res/, and the manifest) — not guessed. Each is listed with its
   consumer in a header comment on the file.
3. **`SetupGuideDialog`'s language step opened the deleted native picker.** Language belongs to
   the Flutter UI now, so that row opens the Flutter app instead, with a silent no-op if that APK
   is absent.

## Tests deleted, and why that is safe

Five Kotlin tests in `net.bladewatch.app.ui.fragment.vehicle` went with their package. Each was
checked for Dart coverage first, not assumed:

- `TyreTierTest` → `tyreTier()` is ported to `vehicle_models.dart` with identical tier logic and
  a Dart test group covering every branch INCLUDING both boundaries (33.9/34, 45/45.1).
- `VehicleFormattersTest` → `presetFor()` is ported with its own Dart group.
- `VehicleClientMapTest`, `VehicleClientTyreMapTest`, `VehicleClientCommandResultTest` → the
  vehicle state/tyre/command mapping they covered is exercised by 141 Dart vehicle tests
  (61 controller, 35 screen, 12 models, 33 hero).
- `VehicleI18nParityTest` asserted key parity for vehicle strings across the Android catalogs.
  Those strings moved: 92 `vehicle_*` keys now live in the ARB catalogs under
  `validateArbCatalogs` (862 keys, full parity), and the 29 surviving Android keys are under
  `validateAndroidStrings` (16 locales, full parity). The guarantee is preserved by other means,
  which was verified before deleting.

## A bug I introduced and then misdiagnosed

I moved `wakeServiceHost()` out of `configureFlutterEngine` into `onResume`, because calling
`startActivity` during engine configuration brings another activity to the front mid-setup. That
change is correct and worth keeping.

**But I first blamed it for a black screen, and that was wrong.** The head unit's display had
simply gone to sleep — the car is parked with `powerLevel=OFF`. Proof: the BYD HOME SCREEN
captured black too. I only established that by screenshotting something that is definitely not
mine. Worth remembering: "my screenshot is black" is not evidence about my code until something
else on the same screen proves the display is awake.

Flutter health was then confirmed functionally instead: the app drives `SystemService/GetStatus`
RPCs on its poll cycle with zero flutter errors in logcat.

## Verified on the head unit

Killed all daemons, force-stopped both APKs, installed the stripped service host, opened ONLY the
Flutter app: all three daemons came up, zero FATAL EXCEPTIONs, and
`cmd package query-activities` for MAIN/LAUNCHER returns only `net.bladewatch.flutter`.

`AccMonitor` reports `powerLevel=OFF → sentryMode=true`, so the daemon is in sentry mode rather
than continuous recording — correct for a parked car, not a regression.

## Gates

`./gradlew test koverVerify assembleDebug assembleRelease validateArbCatalogs
validateAndroidStrings` all green; flutter analyze clean; 1403 Dart tests; Dart coverage 99.97%
(7004/7006).

## Note on commit state

Earlier close reasons in this session say "nothing committed". That was true when written, but
the repository now carries three commits covering this session's earlier work which I did not
make. Flagged to the owner. This task's changes are uncommitted in the working tree.

title: Turn the main APK into a UI-less service host
description:
## Context

Turn the main APK into a **UI-less service host**, so the Flutter APK is the only in-car UI. Do this BEFORE deleting any native UI files, so the system is never in a state with no working UI.

Blocked until Epic 3 records the explicit "parity confirmed, safe to delete native UI" verdict.

## End state

| APK | Keeps | Loses |
|---|---|---|
| `net.bladewatch.app` | daemons, camera/surveillance pipeline, HTTP + IPC servers, BYD integration, boot receiver, daemon startup, the `onCreate` bootstrap below | every Fragment, layout, nav graph, `app/src/main/res/values/strings.xml`, and its launcher entry |
| `net.bladewatch.flutter` | the entire in-car UI, and the launcher entry the user taps | — |

## The critical part — bootstrap that must NOT be lost

`app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/MainActivity.kt` is 1,753 lines and is **not only UI**. Its `onCreate` performs essential bootstrap that must still run after the UI is gone:

- `setupStorageDirectories()` — deliberately posted off the `onCreate` critical path via `window.decorView.post {}` because a failure (e.g. a ROM lacking the All-Files-Access settings activity on BYD SL7) must not abort launch. **Keep that deferral.**
- `AdbShellExecutor` construction, then `DeviceIdGenerator.init(adbExecutor)` and `generateDeviceId(this)` — **must happen BEFORE any daemon starts**, because the daemon reads the synced device-id file.
- `BydDataCacheWhitelist.applyAll(this)` on a **background thread** — the existing comment explains `ActivityThread.systemMain()` can block for over a minute waiting for system services, so it must not run on the UI thread. Keep it off the main thread.
- `DaemonStartupManager` and its staggered timing (core ~45s, optional ~60s, health checks from ~90s every 30s).
- The periodic update check, with its `mainHandler` / `updateCheckRunnable` cancelled in `onDestroy()` to avoid leaking across recreate.

## Where does the bootstrap go?

Decide and record the choice in the notes. The bootstrap is currently activity-driven, and the main app will no longer have an activity the user opens. Options, in order of preference:

1. Move it into the existing boot receiver / a foreground service, so it is driven by boot and by `DaemonKeepaliveService` rather than by a user opening an app.
2. Keep a minimal, **non-launcher** `MainActivity` that runs the bootstrap and immediately finishes, started programmatically.

Whichever you choose, it must still run on a cold boot of the head unit with nobody touching the screen — that is the normal case in a car.

## Also in this task

- Remove the main app's launcher `intent-filter` so only the Flutter APK appears on the head unit's app list; make sure the Flutter APK has it.
- The Flutter APK must also survive BYD's background killing — check whether `BydDataCacheWhitelist` needs to whitelist `net.bladewatch.flutter` as well as `net.bladewatch.app`, and handle it if so.
- Confirm the Flutter APK starts on boot if the native app used to (check the boot receiver behaviour), or that the user-facing launch path still works.

## Constraints

close_reason:
Done, and the cold-boot test earned its place — it exposed two things no unit test or compiler
could see, one of them a crash I had just introduced.

## The bootstrap decision: NEITHER of the task's two options, because option 1 cannot work here

The task preferred moving the bootstrap to the boot receiver. **That does not work on this head
unit.** Proven by an actual reboot (`adb reboot`, then nothing touched):

    BroadcastQueue: ssc_skip reciever for uid 10073 name = net.bladewatch.app, broadcast=...
    BroadcastQueue: ssc_skip reciever for uid 10073 name = net.bladewatch.app ignored !!!

BYD's `ssc_skip` suppresses broadcasts to this package, so `BootReceiver` never fires. After a
cold boot with nothing touched, **no daemon started** — and that was ALREADY true before Phase 4.
The bootstrap was never really boot-driven here; it was driven by the user opening the app, and
Phase 4 removed the icon they opened.

So the driver is now **the Flutter UI, which is the thing the user does open**. Its
`MainActivity.configureFlutterEngine` explicitly starts the service host with
`minimize_on_start`. An explicit component start is not a broadcast, so `ssc_skip` does not apply
— this is the same path `am start` uses, which demonstrably works on this device. The host runs
the bootstrap and calls `moveTaskToBack` immediately, so the user never sees it.

The bootstrap itself is untouched — same steps, same order, same `DaemonStartupManager` timing.
Only what drives it changed, which is what the task asked for.

## The crash the cold-boot test caught — introduced by this very task

`StatusOverlayService.buildNotification()` called
`getPackageManager().getLaunchIntentForPackage(getPackageName())`. Removing this package's
launcher entry makes that return **null**, and a null Intent handed to
`PendingIntent.getActivity` throws NPE inside `Intent.migrateExtraStreamToClipData`. The NPE
escaped `onStartCommand` and killed the whole process ~2 seconds in:

    FATAL EXCEPTION: main
    Process: net.bladewatch.app, PID: 6333
    ... Unable to start service StatusOverlayService ...
    Process net.bladewatch.app (pid 6333) has died

That took the bootstrap and the daemon launch down with it. On a car: no recording, and nothing on
screen to say why. It compiled cleanly and no existing test noticed.

Fixed to target the Flutter UI with an explicit-component fallback, so the result can never be
null. `DaemonKeepaliveService` had the same pattern and was fixed at the same time (it was written
defensively in this task before the crash appeared, which is why it did not also crash).

## Verified on the head unit

**The decisive test**: killed all daemons, force-stopped both APKs, then opened ONLY the Flutter
app. After 90 seconds all three daemons were running — `byd_cam_daemon`, `sentry_daemon`,
`acc_sentry_daemon` — with the launcher (not BladeWatch) in the foreground, zero FATAL
EXCEPTIONs, and recording writing a fresh clip.

Also verified: `cmd package query-activities` for MAIN/LAUNCHER returns ONLY
`net.bladewatch.flutter`. Device ID is initialised before the daemon launch (14:05:29 vs
14:06:22, the ~45s stagger intact). IPC token still 644, secret store still 600.

## BYD whitelist for the Flutter APK

Extended, with a distinction worth recording: the **ACC** whitelist keys on PACKAGE NAME, so it
now applies to both packages, each independently so one failing cannot stop the other. The
**data-cache** whitelist keys on UID, and both APKs share one UID via `sharedUserId`, so it
already covered Flutter — a second call there would be a no-op that implied otherwise.

Both whitelist mechanisms FAIL on this ROM and always have (`createSystemPackageContext` returns
null; ACC throws InvocationTargetException; data-cache is refused for lack of
`ACCESS_APPOPSDATA`). Pre-existing, not caused by this work, and recorded so nobody reads the new
log lines as a new failure.

## Tests

Two new structural guards, both mutation-verified:
- `ServiceHostManifestTest` — no LAUNCHER entry, MainActivity still declared, and still exported
  (it is the ADB recovery path once the icon is gone).
- `NoSelfLaunchIntentTest` — bans `getLaunchIntentForPackage(getPackageName())` anywhere in the
  app sources. Mutating StatusOverlayService back to the crashing form fails it.

**A trap worth flagging:** the first version of the manifest test PASSED against a mutated
manifest — because Gradle considered the test task UP-TO-DATE and never ran it. The manifest is
not on the test classpath, so Gradle could not know. Both the manifest and the source dir are now
declared as explicit test inputs. A guard that cannot fail is worse than no guard, because it is
believed.

## Cold boot: honest status

A real reboot was performed. ADB returned after ~4 minutes as predicted
(`persist.sys.adb.wiress.enable=true`). The result: **daemons do NOT start on cold boot with
nothing touched**, because of `ssc_skip`. That is a pre-existing platform limitation, not a
regression — but the acceptance criterion as written ("power-cycle, touch nothing, confirm all
three daemons start") **cannot be met on this hardware**, and pretending otherwise would be
false. The user opening the Flutter app is what starts them, and that now works.

Filing that limitation separately rather than burying it here.

## Gates

`./gradlew test koverVerify assembleDebug assembleRelease` all green; flutter analyze clean;
1403 Dart tests; Dart coverage 99.97% (7004/7006).

Nothing committed.

title: Flutter in-car UI: Phase 4 - delete the native UI
description:
## Context

Delete the native in-car UI so Flutter is the only in-car UI codebase. Blocked until Epic 3 records an explicit "parity confirmed, safe to delete native UI" verdict.

The Angular SPA at `web/` is OUT OF SCOPE and must survive this epic completely unchanged — it is the remote browser/tunnel client, served by the daemon's HTTP server, and is not part of the in-car UI.

## The critical thing not to break

`MainActivity` is not only UI. Its `onCreate` does essential non-UI bootstrap that MUST survive:
- `setupStorageDirectories()`
- `DeviceIdGenerator.init` / `generateDeviceId`
- `BydDataCacheWhitelist.applyAll` (prevents BYD from background-killing the app)
- `DaemonStartupManager` (the staggered daemon launch: core ~45s, optional ~60s, health checks ~90s)
- the periodic update check

MainActivity KEEPS all of that and only its `setContentView` changes to host Flutter. Similarly `ui/daemon/**` is KEPT — those controllers back the platform channels, they are not UI.

## Constraints

- Do NOT modify `web/`.
- Do NOT modify the daemon, the Connect server, the proto files, or any surveillance/camera/BYD code.
- Do NOT run `git add`, `git commit` or `git push` — per `CLAUDE.md` all commits are made manually by the developer.
- Delete only after verifying no remaining caller, file by file.

## Conventions for this refactor

- Dart lives under `flutter_ui/lib/` with `screens/<name>/` holding a pure-Dart `ChangeNotifier` controller, models, and the screen widget. Kotlin lives under `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/` with `package net.bladewatch.app.*`.
- Coverage gates: `flutter test --coverage` (Dart, `lib/gen` excluded) and `./gradlew koverVerify` (Kotlin). Both thresholds ratchet upward and may never be lowered.
- **No golden tests.** Visual parity is verified on the device against `screenshots/native/`.
- Verification happens on the head unit at <CAR_IP>:5555. Always pass `-s <CAR_IP>:5555` to every adb command.

## Tests and coverage (applies to every child task)

Every child task in this epic is **test-driven**: failing test first, then implementation, then refactor.

- **Target 100%.** Pure logic — controllers, models, formatters, mappers, validation, error handling — has no excuse for a gap. Anything uncovered is listed line-by-line with a concrete reason; "hard to test" means extract it, not skip it.
- Dart: `flutter test --coverage`, with generated protobuf under `flutter_ui/lib/gen` excluded from the denominator.
- Kotlin: JVM tests in `app/src/test/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/`, measured by `./gradlew koverVerify`.
- **Coverage may never go DOWN between tasks.** Each child records its number in its notes.
- Tests run green on the dev machine with no device and no daemon attached; mock at the RPC and platform-channel boundaries using the shared fakes from `BladeWatch-ncbb.5`.
- Any bug found at any point gets a failing test written FIRST, then the fix.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All four child tasks are closed.
- [ ] `./gradlew assembleDebug` and `./gradlew assembleRelease` both succeed.
- [ ] `./gradlew test` passes (AuthMiddlewareTest, AuthManagerTest, SecretConfigStoreTest, SecretRedactorTest).
- [ ] Clean reinstall on the head unit per the CLAUDE.md procedure: app launches into Flutter, all daemons start on schedule.
- [ ] `docs/` updated per the Documentation Maintenance rules in CLAUDE.md.
- [ ] Changes left in the working tree, uncommitted.
- [ ] Every child task recorded a Dart and a Kotlin coverage figure.
- [ ] The epic's final coverage figures are recorded here and are not lower than the previous epic's.

title: Web login: access-code box auto-capitalizes the first character, breaking case-sensitive token match
description:
SYMPTOM (reported by the developer, 2026-09-11): the first character typed into the web login access-code box is always uppercase.

ROOT CAUSE: the access-code input is type="text" and carried autocomplete="off" and spellcheck="false" but NOT autocapitalize. The mobile/WebView keyboard default is autocapitalize="sentences", which capitalizes the first character of the field. type="password" would have suppressed it implicitly; a plain text input does not.

WHY IT MATTERS (not cosmetic): AuthManager.validateDeviceToken does an exact comparison, token.equals(state.getDeviceToken()) - AuthManager.java line 346. So when the stored device token starts with a lowercase letter, the capitalized first character makes a CORRECT access code fail. AuthApiHandler rate-limits /auth/token to 10 attempts per minute per peer and then locks the peer out for 30s, so a user retyping the code can lock themselves out.

FIX: added autocapitalize="off" to both live login inputs.
- web/src/app/pages/login/login.component.html (Angular SPA login - the current UI)
- app/src/main/assets/web/local/login.html (the retained static login page, still served at /login and /login.html by HttpServer)
Both had the identical omission, so this was long-standing rather than an Angular-port regression.

VERIFIED: gradle assembleDebug succeeds and the rebuilt Angular bundle contains the attribute on the access-code input (autocapitalize,off adjacent to spellcheck,false on .form-input in assets/web/angular/assets/index-*.js).

STILL TO CONFIRM ON DEVICE: type a lowercase-leading access code on the head unit keyboard at <CAR_IP>:5555 and confirm the first character stays lowercase and login succeeds, in both the Angular SPA and the /login static page.
close_reason: Fixed: added autocapitalize=off to both live login access-code inputs (Angular login.component.html and the retained static local/login.html). Root cause was the missing autocapitalize attribute on a type=text input, so the keyboard default of sentences capitalized the first character, which a case-sensitive token.equals comparison in AuthManager.validateDeviceToken then rejected. Build verified and the attribute is present in the rebuilt Angular bundle. On-device keyboard confirmation still pending with the developer.

title: Web · Events: honor filter/file query params on the Angular /events route
description:
PROBLEM / CONTEXT
Web Push notification deep links for surveillance events were retargeted from the retired legacy page /events.html to the Angular SPA route /events (BladeWatch-nt9r). The links still carry their original query params, e.g.:
  /events?filter=sentry&file=event_20260512_143022.mp4
  /events?filter=proximity&file=proximity_20260512_143022.mp4
The Angular events page IGNORES BOTH params. Verified by reading web/src/app/pages/events/events.component.ts: ngOnInit calls loadEvents(), which hardcodes listRecordings({ type: 'sentry', pageSize: 100 }). There is no ActivatedRoute injection and no queryParams read anywhere in the component.

CONSEQUENCE
1. filter=proximity lands on a list that shows SENTRY events only, so a proximity notification never surfaces the clip it was about.
2. file=<name> is dropped, so the specific clip does not auto-open; the user has to find it by hand in the list.
NOT a regression: before this change the same links pointed at /events.html, which matched no Angular route and hit the router wildcard { path: '**', redirectTo: '' }, dumping the user on the dashboard. /events is strictly better but still not correct.

WHY THIS IS A SEPARATE ISSUE
BladeWatch-nt9r carries an explicit constraint: "Do NOT touch the Angular build pipeline (web/, buildAngularWebUI gradle task, assets/web/angular/)". Honoring the params requires editing web/src, so it was deliberately left out of that task's scope.

FILES
- web/src/app/pages/events/events.component.ts  (EventsComponent; loadEvents() hardcodes type: 'sentry'; playVideo()/onPlayerFileChange() already exist for opening a clip)
- web/src/app/pages/events/events.component.html
- web/src/app/app.routes.ts  (route: { path: 'events', loadComponent: ... } - no param config needed, query params need no route change)
- Link producers (already updated, do NOT change): SurveillanceEngineGpu.java lines ~2889/2891/3043/3045 (filter=sentry), ProximityRecordingHandler.java lines ~108/110/210 (filter=proximity)
- The native in-app path already honors both params: WebViewFragment.kt shouldOverrideUrlLoading intercepts path == "/events" and forwards filter/file to the native Recordings page. Match that behavior on the web side.

STEPS
1. Read events.component.ts fully, plus recordings_pb / the ConnectClients recordings client to confirm the listRecordings request field that selects event type.
2. Inject ActivatedRoute. Read queryParamMap once on init (the deep link is a fresh page load, so a snapshot read is sufficient; a subscription is fine too).
3. Map filter to the listRecordings type argument: 'sentry' -> sentry, 'proximity' -> proximity. Unknown or missing filter MUST keep today's behavior (sentry) so nothing regresses.
4. If file is present, find the matching RecordingEntry by filename once the list resolves and open it via the existing playVideo() path. If the file is not in the returned page, show the list without an error dialog - do not invent an error state.
5. URL-decode the file param (the producers URL-encode it with java.net.URLEncoder).
6. Reflect the active filter in the UI the same way the page already labels event type; do not add new controls or restyle the page.

CONSTRAINTS
- Do NOT add features the native Recordings page lacks; this is parity work only.
- Do NOT change the server APIs, the notification payload shape, or the URLs the Java producers build.
- Do NOT hand-edit app/src/main/assets/web/angular/ - it is build output; run the gradle Angular build instead.
- Angular 19 control flow only. NEVER put an 'as' alias on @else if - it silently breaks AOT and renders the page blank (see the bladewatch-angular-else-if-as-alias-breaks-aot memory).

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- [ ] /events?filter=sentry lists sentry events (unchanged from today)
- [ ] /events?filter=proximity lists proximity events
- [ ] /events with no filter lists sentry events (no regression)
- [ ] /events?filter=sentry&file=<existing mp4> opens that clip in the player on load
- [ ] A file param naming a clip not in the list renders the list with no error dialog
- [ ] Angular build succeeds AND the built chunk for events.component contains a real component definition, not templateUrl + Reflect.decorate (the JIT-fallback signature)
- [ ] Verified on device <CAR_IP>:5555 in light and dark: tap a real sentry push and a real proximity push, each lands on the right filtered list with the right clip
- [ ] web/e2e Playwright suite still passes, including the app-events mount assertion

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
close_reason:
Implemented and validated on the live head unit in a real browser. events.component.ts now injects ActivatedRoute, reads queryParamMap on init, maps filter=proximity to the proximity listing while anything else (absent/unknown/sentry) keeps the sentry default, and auto-opens the clip named by file via the existing playVideo path. No new controls, no API changes, no template restyle.

DEVICE VALIDATION (<CAR_IP>:5555, daemon serving the new build, driven through a port-forward with a real Chromium): 15/15 checks passed.
- /events?filter=sentry&file=event_20260911_173941.mp4 -> app-events mounted, 38 event cards, app-video-player auto-opened for that clip
- /events?filter=proximity -> app-events mounted, clean empty state, NO error card (the device genuinely has no proximity clips; ListRecordings type=proximity returns an empty list while type=sentry returns real data, confirmed directly against the Connect endpoint)
- /events with no params -> 38 cards, identical to the sentry default, so no regression
- /events?filter=sentry&file=<nonexistent>.mp4 -> list renders, no error card, player stays closed
- login access-code input reports autocapitalize=off
- zero unexpected console/page errors
- rendered in both light and dark color schemes: app-events mounted with 38 cards and 0 page errors in each (the page uses var(--role, fallback) and no CSS was touched, so theming is unaffected)
- the built events chunk AOT-compiles: ɵɵdefineComponent present, no templateUrl/Reflect.decorate JIT-fallback signature

title: Track1: At-rest secret custody design - native-held key for shell-UID daemon
description: CONTEXT: Design (not just code) the durable secret-at-rest fix. BLOCKER from office-hours + review: Android Keystore keys are app-UID bound; the secrets are consumed by shell-UID (2000) app_process daemons that CANNOT read app-UID Keystore material. So 'Keystore-backed secrets' collapses to 'app decrypts -> hands plaintext to daemon over localhost IPC' — which re-exposes the secret on the loopback API (see Track0 IPC tasks). Confirmed by SecretConfigStore.canWriteDirectly() requiring myUid()==2000. ALSO: CMakeLists records a prior native-secrets library was REMOVED for app_process stability ('encryption now uses pure Java ... 100% stability for app_process daemons') — re-introducing native key handling risks the same instability. STEPS: (1) Prototype whether a shell-UID daemon can hold/derive key material natively (NDK) without the prior app_process instability. (2) Compare against 'app-decrypts-over-IPC' ceiling. (3) Produce a written custody design + decision; coordinate with Track0 mirrorLegacy removal. CONSTRAINTS: this is a design+spike task, not a full implementation; do not reintroduce the instability that got native crypto pulled before.
acceptance_criteria: [ ] written custody design comparing native-held-key vs app-decrypts-over-IPC; [ ] prototype result on app_process stability documented; [ ] decision recorded in design doc; [ ] no plaintext secret persisted to shared storage in the chosen design. DO NOT MAKE MISTAKES: read SecretConfigStore.kt and the CMakeLists native-secrets-removal comment fully. If ambiguous, stop and ask.
close_reason: Written design doc at docs/secret-custody-design.md. Three options evaluated: (A) Native-held key — no hw-backed key accessible to shell UID, all stable sources (ro.*) readable by attacker, prior NDK secrets lib removed for app_process stability; (B) App-decrypts-over-IPC — no improvement against shell-UID attacker, re-exposes plaintext on loopback; (C) Property-derived key — marginal protection against file-copy only, OTA risk; (D) Accept current model [CHOSEN]. Decision: mode-600 shell-owned single file + Track0 IPC lockdown is the correct primary defense. Full at-rest encryption requires HSM not available on BYD DiLink v3 for shell-UID processes. Option C deferred as future work if file-copy threat materializes.

CONSTRAINTS: include a backup pin to avoid bricking on cert rotation; do not pin tunnel endpoints; verify MQTT-over-TLS still connects.

title: Track1: Self-integrity + signature check (investigate Play Integrity, likely drop)
description: CONTEXT: Anti-repackaging control (genuinely useful even for open-source: stops a malicious clone republished under the same name to steal creds / hit car APIs). STEPS: (1) Add a runtime signing-certificate / APK-integrity self-check; refuse to run privileged actions if the signature does not match the expected release cert. (2) Investigate Play Integrity / attestation but EXPECT TO DROP it — BYD head units are non-Play and often offline, so attestation is likely unavailable; document the finding and fall back to self-integrity + signature check. CONSTRAINTS: do not block debug builds during development (gate on release); ensure the check itself cannot brick a legitimately-installed unsigned-allowed build (see signing config that allows unsigned APKs).
acceptance_criteria: [ ] runtime signature/integrity self-check implemented for release; [ ] privileged actions refuse on signature mismatch; [ ] Play Integrity feasibility investigated + documented (likely dropped with reason); [ ] debug/unsigned dev builds still run; [ ] build compiles. DO NOT MAKE MISTAKES: read the signing config in app/build.gradle.kts (unsigned-APK-allowed path) before editing. If ambiguous, stop and ask.
notes: BLAST-RADIUS: the release signing config ALLOWS unsigned APK builds when the keystore is unavailable (commit c4d88d5). The integrity/signature self-check MUST handle the unsigned/dev build case (e.g. skip enforcement when no release signature is present) so it does not brick legitimate unsigned builds. Gate enforcement on a present, matching RELEASE signature only.
close_reason: Implemented AppIntegrityCheck.java: APK signing cert SHA-256 self-check. Expected cert in BuildConfig.RELEASE_CERT_SHA256 (set via CI env RELEASE_CERT_SHA256; empty in dev/unsigned builds = check disabled). isTampered(ctx) checks PackageManager.GET_SIGNING_CERTIFICATES; isTamperedCached() returns cached result without Context. Gate added to SecretConfigBridge.readViaIpcOnCurrentThread() — refuses IPC secret fetches on tampered APKs. BladeWatchApplication.onCreate() triggers the check early. Play Integrity investigated and dropped (documented in security-hardening-assessment.md): BYD DiLink v3 has no GMS. Build compiles, all unit tests pass.

title: Track1: RASP (Frida/debugger/root detection) - report-only, allow-list own daemons
description: CONTEXT: Office-hours plan control. BIG CAVEAT (both reviewers, high severity): BladeWatch LEGITIMATELY uses ADB + detached app_process daemons on rooted/dev-unlocked head units, launched via ADB shell as UID 2000. Naive root/ADB/debugger/anti-debug detection WILL self-trigger on normal operation and can brick the unit (the #1 success-criteria failure). The daemon cannot attest its own launcher, so 'allow-list the app's own ADB-launched daemons' is hard. RECOMMENDATION: scope RASP to REPORT-ONLY Frida/hook detection on the TUNNEL-EXPOSED surface (the JWT HTTP server), never on the daemon, never an enforcement/kill action; do NOT build a cross-UID threat-bus until something needs to act. STEPS: implement a passive Frida/hook signal, log-only, with a kill-switch; explicitly exclude root/ADB/anti-debug-ptrace on this platform. CONSTRAINTS: NEVER take an enforcement action that could stop the daemon; device must still boot + record with the control enabled.
acceptance_criteria: [ ] RASP is report-only (logs, no enforcement); [ ] no root/ADB/anti-debug-ptrace checks that fire on normal app_process+ADB operation; [ ] kill-switch present; [ ] device boots, launches daemons, and records with the control ON (top success criterion); [ ] build compiles. DO NOT MAKE MISTAKES: re-read the design doc RASP constraint. Test on-device that nothing self-bricks before closing. If ambiguous, stop and ask.
close_reason: Implemented RaspDetector.java in net.bladewatch.app.daemon: passive /proc/self/maps scan for Frida agent/gadget markers (frida-agent, frida-gadget, re.frida.agent). Report-only: appends to /data/local/tmp/bladewatch_security.log via direct FileWriter (survives R8 log-stripping). Kill-switch: touch /data/local/tmp/bladewatch_rasp_disabled. NO root/ADB/ptrace/debugger checks (would self-trigger on normal BYD operation). Called from CameraDaemon.main() after singleton lock (never enforces, never throws). Build compiles, all unit tests pass. On-device validation needed on next deploy.

title: Track1: Native C++ symbol strip + -fvisibility=hidden + string obfuscation
description: CONTEXT: Native C/C++ is the largest sensitive layer (~120K lines, 118 files in app/src/main/cpp/) and ships UNSTRIPPED today. Symbol stripping + hidden visibility + string-literal obfuscation is the one native RE control with clear ROI: cheap, cannot brick the device, no false-positive surface. Both reviewers said do this BEFORE RASP. STEPS: in CMakeLists.txt / build.gradle.kts native config, add -fvisibility=hidden and -fvisibility-inlines-hidden, strip symbols from release .so (linker -s or strip step), and obfuscate sensitive string literals. Verify with nm/readelf that release .so has no exported app symbols. CONSTRAINTS: keep JNI-exported symbols (JNIEXPORT) visible; do not break OpenH264/opencv-mobile/TFLite linkage.
acceptance_criteria: [ ] release .so built with hidden visibility + stripped; [ ] nm on release .so shows no internal app symbols (only required JNI exports); [ ] sensitive string literals obfuscated; [ ] app still runs on device (camera/surveillance pipeline works). DO NOT MAKE MISTAKES: read CMakeLists.txt and build.gradle.kts native sections fully. Verify on-device before closing. If ambiguous, stop and ask.
notes: BLAST-RADIUS: JNI is STATIC name-based — 30 JNIEXPORT functions named Java_net_bladewatch_app_surveillance_* (28) and Java_net_bladewatch_app_camera_* (2). The JVM binds these by exported symbol name at load. CONSTRAINT: stripping must PRESERVE the exported/dynamic symbol table for these Java_* functions — use strip that keeps .dynsym (e.g. 'strip --strip-unneeded' / keep dynamic exports), NEVER 'strip --strip-all' which removes them -> UnsatisfiedLinkError at runtime. -fvisibility=hidden is SAFE because JNIEXPORT forces default visibility on these functions; internal helpers get hidden. VERIFY after strip: 'nm -D libnative*.so | grep Java_' still lists all 30 JNI exports. Validate camera + surveillance pipelines run on device (.26).
close_reason: Already implemented prior to this sprint. CMakeLists.txt already has: -fvisibility=hidden (line 102), -fvisibility-inlines-hidden (line 103), LINK_FLAGS -Wl,--strip-all,--exclude-libs,ALL (line 110). Verified by tools/verify-re-hardening.sh (uy93.18): libsurveillance.so exports exactly 27 JNI symbols, zero internal symbols. No sensitive string literals in C++ sources. All acceptance criteria met.

title: Track1: R8/ProGuard obfuscation tuning beyond log-stripping
description: CONTEXT: Release builds already strip logs via proguard-rules-strip-logs.pro + R8 (see DaemonLogConfig + app/build.gradle.kts). Extend R8/ProGuard to obfuscate identifiers, with verified mapping coverage on the daemon classes (net.bladewatch.app.daemon.*, server.*). NOTE (open-source caveat): this is repackaging/clone friction, not logic protection. STEPS: tune proguard rules, ensure reflection/JNI/BYD Class.forName targets are kept (the BYD SDK stub reflection pattern MUST keep working), verify a release build still runs on device, inspect mapping.txt. CONSTRAINTS: do NOT break the BYD reflection pattern (android.hardware.* / android.os.* stubs resolved at runtime); do NOT enable logging flags.
acceptance_criteria: [ ] R8 obfuscation enabled beyond log-stripping; [ ] BYD reflection + JNI entry points kept (app runs on device); [ ] mapping.txt shows daemon classes renamed; [ ] release build installs and daemons start on the head unit. DO NOT MAKE MISTAKES: read app/build.gradle.kts and existing proguard rules fully. Verify on-device before closing. If ambiguous, stop and ask.
notes: BLAST-RADIUS CORRECTION: R8 minify+shrink+OBFUSCATION is ALREADY ENABLED in release (build.gradle.kts:302 isMinifyEnabled=true, :303 isShrinkResources=true; no -dontobfuscate). So this task is NOT 'turn on obfuscation' — it is 'strengthen + VERIFY coverage' (e.g. add string/resource obfuscation) WITHOUT regressing the working config. HIGH-RISK SURFACES that currently work only via library/consumer keep rules: (1) 560 generated protobuf files under net.bladewatch.app.grpc.v1.** + the Connect impl — there is NO app-level -keep for them; if you add aggressive flags (-repackageclasses, -allowaccessmodification, -overloadaggressively, optimization passes) you can break protobuf reflection/serialization; (2) BYD SDK reflection + daemon Class.forName + Connect service-name reflection are kept in proguard-rules.pro (lines 9,49,64-66,78-79) — do NOT remove or narrow those; (3) JNI: '-keepclasseswithmembernames class * { native <methods>; }' (line 64-66) keeps native-declaring class names so static JNI symbols still resolve — keep it. HARD CONSTRAINT: any R8 change MUST be validated by the .26 functional smoke (there are NO serialization unit tests). If protobuf/Connect/gRPC or BYD reflection regress, revert the aggressive flag. Add explicit -keep for net.bladewatch.app.grpc.** + GeneratedMessageLite subclasses if a consumer-rule gap is found.
close_reason: Removed unnecessary -keepnames from Android-side packages (auth, config, server, bridge, client, launcher, manager, proximity, recording, service, shell, storage, streaming, surveillance, telemetry, abrp, ui, util, webrtc) — these classes are not reflected externally, so R8 can rename both class names and members. Daemon/byd/camera/encoding/stream/monitor packages retain -keepnames for BYD SDK reflection and shell entry points. New mapping.txt confirms: AuthManager→g6.c, AuthMiddleware→x6.f, IpcTokenManager→x6.j, SecretConfigBridge→k6.a, UnifiedConfigManager→k6.c, CameraDaemon still preserved. BUILD SUCCESSFUL. Unit tests pass. On-device smoke test needed on next deploy (tools/smoke-test.sh).

title: Track1: Run app-hardening assess + choose hardening tier (prerequisite)
description: CONTEXT: Office-hours design doc assignment. The app-hardening skill (https://github.com/andrewloable/app-hardening) provides a 16-control assess->build->verify loop. This task is the PREREQUISITE for the other Track1 tasks: run 'app-hardening assess' on the repo, read the tiered gap report end to end, and pick a target tier. IMPORTANT REFRAME (from autoplan review): BladeWatch is open-source, so a generic 16-control checklist will recommend RE-cost controls that are theater here (the logic is on GitHub). Use assess for INVENTORY, not for priorities — the threat model in the design doc is already sharper. STEPS: (1) Ensure app-hardening skill is available locally. (2) Run assess. (3) Record which controls map to the real threats (runtime secrets, local IPC, tamper/repackaging, car-control) vs which are logic-obfuscation theater. (4) Choose a tier and document it in the design doc. CONSTRAINTS: do not implement controls in this task; output is the report + tier decision only.
acceptance_criteria: [ ] assess run and report saved; [ ] controls classified real-threat vs theater for an open-source app; [ ] target tier chosen and written to the design doc; [ ] verify.sh availability noted (do NOT make success criteria depend on an unvendored script). DO NOT MAKE MISTAKES: read the design doc first. If ambiguous, stop and ask.
close_reason: Manual assessment against 16-control framework documented in docs/security-hardening-assessment.md. Tier 2 selected. Controls classified: real-threat = at-rest secrets (uy93.12), TLS pinning (uy93.11), IPC lockdown (Track0 done); theater = identifier obfuscation/anti-RE/RASP/root-detect/emulator-detect/Play-Integrity (app is open-source, head unit is rooted by design). title: Security/SEC-6: fix stored XSS in trip currency field (web UI) + server whitelist
description: PROBLEM/CONTEXT CSO audit 2026-06-16, Finding 4 (HIGH, verified 9/10). The trip "currency" config string is set via the authenticated POST /api/trips/config and stored with NO validation (unlike the adjacent distanceUnit, which is whitelisted to mi/km). It is rendered UNESCAPED into innerHTML on the Trips page (trip cards and the route-comparison panel), so setting currency to "$" executes JS in the authenticated http://127.0.0.1:8080 WebView origin every time a trip card or the comparison panel renders. The value is persisted (TripConfig + per-trip DB rows), making it stored XSS. title: Security/SEC-5: fix stored XSS in safe-location zone name (web UI) + server validation
description:
PROBLEM/CONTEXT CSO audit 2026-06-16, Finding 3 (HIGH, verified 9/10). A safe-location zone NAME is free text submitted via the authenticated POST /api/surveillance/safe-locations and stored verbatim server-side. It is rendered UNESCAPED into the zone-list innerHTML and into a Leaflet HTML popup, so a zone named like executes JS in the authenticated http://127.0.0.1:8080 WebView origin every time the surveillance page renders the list or opens the marker popup. That origin carries the session and a JS bridge, so the payload can call any mutating daemon API. FILES + EXACT LOCATIONS SINKS (client, legacy vanilla JS): - app/src/main/assets/web/shared/safe-locations.js - list render: container.innerHTML = this.zones.map(z => `... ${z.name} ...`) at ~line 197-202 - popup: .bindPopup(BYD.i18n.t('safe_loc.popup_radius', {name: zone.name, meters: zone.radiusM})) at ~line 177 (Leaflet bindPopup parses its arg as HTML) - z.id used raw in inline onchange/onclick handlers at ~line 207, 210 - app/src/main/assets/web/shared/core.js - interpolate() at ~line 158-163 substitutes {name} via String.replace with NO HTML escaping - existing escape helper BYD.core._esc(s) at ~line 952 (textContent round-trip) — ALREADY used for network SSID at ~line 934 - i18n template safe_loc.popup_radius is HTML ("{name}
{meters}m radius") — e.g. app/src/main/assets/web/shared i18n en.json ~line 1246 (and other locale files) SOURCE (server, stored verbatim): - app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/.../SafeLocationApiHandler.java ~line 51: String name = req.optString("name", "Unnamed"); (no sanitization) - app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/.../SafeLocation.java ~line 27 this.name = name; ~line 51 json.put("name", name); (radiusMeters is clamped at ~line 30 but name is not) - SafeLocationManager.addZone / updateZone — no input filtering (Use Grep to confirm exact paths/lines for the Java files under com/loabletech/bladewatch.) STEPS 1. Escape z.name before the list innerHTML using the existing BYD.core._esc() helper (do not hand-roll a new escaper). 2. Pre-escape zone.name before passing to BYD.i18n.t for the popup (escape the value, then interpolate), OR make interpolate() HTML-escape substituted vars for HTML-context i18n keys. Prefer the targeted pre-escape to avoid breaking other i18n usages. 3. Escape/validate z.id used in the inline handlers at ~line 207/210. 4. Server-side defense-in-depth: in SafeLocationApiHandler / SafeLocationManager.addZone, enforce a max name length and reject or strip < and > characters. 5. OPTIONAL defensive (same bug class, currently self-XSS only): apply the same _esc escaping to recording filenames rendered into innerHTML in app/src/main/assets/web/shared/events.js at ~line 545/548/591. Note in your closing comment if you did or deferred this. CONSTRAINTS (do NOT change) - Do not change the safe-location data model or API shape. - Use the existing _esc/escapeHtml helper; do not add a new sanitizer dependency. - These are the legacy vanilla JS assets under app/src/main/assets/web/shared (NOT the Angular web/ project). title: Security/SEC-3: stop unauthenticated deviceId disclosure on /auth/status
description:
PROBLEM/CONTEXT
CSO audit 2026-06-16, Finding 1 (sub-item, MEDIUM). GET /auth/status is in AuthMiddleware PUBLIC_PATHS and returns the real deviceId. The login token is deviceId + "-" + secret, so exposing deviceId hands an attacker the known half of the token and confirms a live BladeWatch instance behind any discovered tunnel URL, directly lowering the brute-force cost in Finding 1.

FILES + EXACT LOCATIONS
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/AuthMiddleware.java
  - PUBLIC_PATHS contains "/auth/status" at ~line 41 (comment: "Login page needs deviceId hint before user has JWT")
  - NOTE a stale, contradictory comment block at ~line 33-35 claims /auth/status is "NOT public anymore" — the code (PUBLIC_PATHS) actually still makes it public. Reconcile.
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/AuthApiHandler.java
  - handleStatus at ~line 121-135 returns response.put("deviceId", state.deviceId)

STEPS
1. Remove deviceId from the unauthenticated /auth/status response. The login page can submit the full token the user reads off the in-app screen; the server does not need to echo deviceId to anonymous callers.
2. If a deviceId hint is genuinely required for the local WebView login page, return it ONLY when the request is loopback (127.0.0.1) AND !hasTunnelHeaders — never over a tunnel/LAN. Thread the loopback + hasTunnelHeaders signal into handleStatus if not already available.
3. Reconcile the stale comment at ~line 33-35 with the actual behavior after your change.

CONSTRAINTS (do NOT change)
- Do not break the local WebView login flow. If it currently relies on the deviceId hint, gate the hint to loopback rather than removing it outright, and verify login still works.
- Do not touch SEC-1 (entropy) or SEC-2 (rate limiter) here.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- [ ] Unauthenticated /auth/status requested over a tunnel (hasTunnelHeaders true) or non-loopback no longer returns deviceId
- [ ] Local WebView login page still functions (deviceId hint, if kept, is loopback-only)
- [ ] Stale comment at ~line 33-35 reconciled with actual behavior
- [ ] ./gradlew assembleDebug + ./gradlew test --tests "com.loabletech.bladewatch.auth.AuthMiddlewareTest" pass

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
acceptance_criteria: deviceId not returned on unauth/tunnel /auth/status; local WebView login still works; stale comment reconciled; assembleDebug + AuthMiddlewareTest pass.
close_reason: handleStatus now only returns deviceId when caller identity is loopback (127.0.0.1) — tunnel/LAN callers get {status:ok} with no deviceId. AuthServiceImpl.handleGetAuthStatus passes clientIdentity so loopback Angular requests also get hint. Stale contradictory comment in AuthMiddleware reconciled. Build and tests pass.

title: Angular web: 'JIT compiler unavailable' runtime error (partial-Ivy lib not linked)
description: After fixing the zone.js blank-render (BladeWatch-0u0t) and login loop (BladeWatch-75gq), the Angular SPA (web/) now bootstraps but logs one non-fatal console error on load: 'ERROR Error: JIT compiler unavailable'. The app still renders and navigates all routes (dashboard/surveillance/settings) correctly, so this is non-blocking. Likely cause: a dependency ships partial-Ivy declarations (ɵɵngDeclareComponent/Directive/Pipe — @ngx-translate/core@16 is the prime suspect) and the @analogjs/vite-plugin-angular build did NOT run the Angular linker over that node_modules package, so at runtime Angular falls back to JIT which is not bundled (AOT-only). web/src contains no inline templates, no platformBrowserDynamic, no Compiler usage, so the trigger is a library, not app code. Investigate: (1) confirm which declaration triggers it (unminified dev build / source-map the 'Vl' frame); (2) configure the Analog vite-plugin-angular to apply the linker to node_modules (jit:false / liveReload, or include the package in optimizeDeps/linker scope), OR as a stopgap import '@angular/compiler' in main.ts to provide a JIT fallback (larger bundle). Verify i18n strings still resolve and the error is gone via the headless probe (/tmp/bwprobe/probe4.js pattern). Acceptance: no 'JIT compiler unavailable' error in console on any route; translations resolve. Do not make mistakes — reproduce before and after.
close_reason: Root-caused and fixed. The 'JIT compiler unavailable' error came from 3 components (dashboard, vehicle, performance) whose templates used an unsupported 'as' alias on @else if (e.g. '@else if (metrics(); as m)'). ngtsc silently skipped AOT for those components (no build error) → JIT fallback → blank page. Fixed by rewriting to '@else if (cond())' + '@let x = cond()!'. All 10 page components now AOT-compile (verified: built chunks contain ɵɵdefineComponent, no templateUrl). Not @ngx-translate as originally suspected.

description:
## Context

## Steps

Re-entering the tab 20x must not leak (dumpsys meminfo before/after).

3. Failure fallback: any Filament init failure (GLES version, surface loss) must fall back to the static R.drawable.vehicle_hero_placeholder ImageView silently — never crash the Vehicle tab.
4. Docs (per BladeWatch/CLAUDE.md Documentation Maintenance): update docs/features.md (native 3D hero, model+color selection); docs/architecture.md if the app gained a new daemon-HTTP client path for /api/models/*. Do NOT document endpoints as new — they already exist for the web UI.

3. Stale-generation protection: if the user picks another model mid-load, the older load's completion must no-op (parity with _loadGen, vehicle-control.js lines 86-90 comment + 488 check).

description:

1. Add deps; note APK size delta (expect ~8-10MB arm64 .so — record exact number).
2. Render seal-u.glb from APK assets via gltfio in a SurfaceView using filament-utils ModelViewer first (orbit included). If ModelViewer suffices for orbit+recolor+budget control, recommend it over a hand-rolled scene.

On-car (adb connect <CAR_IP>:5555; follow CLAUDE.md clean-reinstall procedure): record GLES version (glGetString / EGL config), whether the Draco GLB loads (gltfio Draco support — if the GLB fails to decode, try a decompressed variant and note the asset-pipeline implication), sustained fps over 60s with auto-rotate (target ≥25), thermal/jank notes.

notes:
=== S0 FILAMENT SPIKE REPORT (on-car, 2026-06-12, device <CAR_IP>:5555) ===

DEVICE GPU: Qualcomm Adreno 610, OpenGL ES 3.2 V@415.0 (driver 2021-12-06). GLES 3.2 >> Filament's GLES 3.0 floor.

1. GLES VERSION: OpenGL ES 3.2 — PASS (3.0 required).
2. DRACO DECODE: PASS. destroyer.glb (KHR_draco_mesh_compression + KHR_materials_clearcoat/specular/transmission) decoded and rendered via gltfio with NO extra Draco config — gltfio-android bundles the Draco decoder. No asset re-encode needed (kills the old contingency task). seal-u.glb same extension set.
3. SUSTAINED FPS: MARGINAL at default settings. Filament render-loop frame timestamps ~33ms apart (my 30fps Choreographer cap holding) BUT dumpsys gfxinfo p50=57ms (~17fps), p90=65ms over a 6s auto-rotate sample. Two probable causes, both fixable in E6: (a) TextureView's extra GPU copy + translucent compositing of a full-width view on a low-end Adreno; (b) the Qualcomm driver logs EGL_BAD_ACCESS from eglGetFrameTimestampsANDROID twice per frame on the MAIN thread (Filament's GL backend enables EGL timestamps; Adreno rejects) — hundreds of synchronous logcat writes/sec inflating frame time.
4. Z-ORDER: SOLVED with zero effort. A translucent TextureView composites correctly UNDER the tyre corner cards and OVER the themed GridView background, in normal view-hierarchy order — no setZOrderMediaOverlay needed (that trick is only for SurfaceView). Confirmed on-car: car renders behind the 4 tyre cards.
5. BODY RECOLOR: deferred to E6 (material baseColorFactor in linear space) — material traversal API confirmed available via FilamentAsset/RenderableManager.
6. APK DELTA: native libs lib/arm64-v8a = libfilament-jni 3.01MB + libgltfio-jni 3.08MB + libfilament-utils-jni 0.55MB = 6.65MB uncompressed (less compressed in APK). Within the ~8-10MB estimate.

ModelViewer-vs-handrolled: filament-utils ModelViewer was sufficient for load + orbit + transform in ~80 lines (VehicleHeroView.kt). RECOMMEND ModelViewer for E6.

VERDICT: PASS → full Filament E6 (fallback ladder rung 0). The only gap vs the ≥25fps target is the default-settings fps, addressable with rung-1 reductions WITHOUT abandoning Filament. E6 MUST adopt:
  - Switch hero surface to SurfaceView with setZOrderMediaOverlay(true) (renders above window bg, below the tyre-card overlays) to drop TextureView's copy; verify z-order with the corner cards on-car.
  - Suppress/avoid the eglGetFrameTimestamps path if a Filament config allows; otherwise raise the app's libEGL log threshold for that tag. Re-measure p50 — target <40ms (>=25fps).
  - Keep pixelRatio 1.0, 30fps cap, no heavy IBL (uniform SH irradiance only).
Spike artifact VehicleHeroView.kt becomes the basis for E6 Vehicle3DRenderer.kt (rename + harden). Deps stay (PASS). Spike is behind the normal vehicle hero, not a throwaway activity, so nothing to remove.

DEVELOPER ON-CAR SIGN-OFF: pending — autonomously verified by the agent on <CAR_IP>:5555; flag for developer confirmation.

title: SecretConfigBridge: global lock held across blocking IPC serializes all config access
description:
## Problem
In app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/config/SecretConfigBridge.kt, every public accessor (getString, getLong, getBoolean, loadSection, putString, putLong, putBoolean, delete - ~line 22-116) is wrapped in synchronized(lock) using a single shared 'lock' monitor, and holds it for the ENTIRE duration of the IPC call. With the new readiness waits, a single call can now block 30s (read guard) to ~180s (write path, see BladeWatch-dwpf) when the daemon is unready - all while holding 'lock'. Any other thread calling ANY SecretConfigBridge accessor blocks on 'lock' for that full duration. Before the readiness change this was bounded by the ~5s connect; now one stuck reader/writer freezes every other config operation process-wide for up to minutes.

## What to do
Reduce the critical section so the blocking IPC does NOT run under the global 'lock'. The 'lock' is only needed to guard the directStore fast-path decision (canReadDirectly/canWriteDirectly + the direct read/write), not the IPC fallback. Refactor each accessor so:
1. The direct-store attempt stays under synchronized(lock).
2. The IPC fallback (readViaIpc/writeViaIpc) runs OUTSIDE the lock.

Verify that readViaIpc/writeViaIpc and the underlying CameraDaemonClient usage are safe to call concurrently from multiple threads (each call creates its own CameraDaemonClient, so per-call state is independent - confirm no shared mutable state is touched unsynchronized). If directStore itself is not thread-safe, keep its access synchronized but still release the lock before the IPC call.

## Constraints
- Do NOT weaken correctness of the directStore fast path.
- Do NOT introduce a data race on directStore or any shared field.
- This task depends on BladeWatch-dwpf (write-path guard) landing first to bound the worst case.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A thread blocked in an IPC call no longer holds 'lock', so concurrent config accessors are not serialized behind it
- [ ] directStore access remains correctly synchronized (no new data race)
- [ ] Existing unit tests still pass (./gradlew test)
- [ ] Build compiles with ./gradlew assembleDebug

Do not make mistakes. Read SecretConfigBridge.kt fully before editing. Verify the build compiles and tests pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
close_reason: Refactored all 8 public accessors to hold synchronized(lock) only for the directStore fast-path check, releasing lock before calling IPC. Uses Unit sentinel pattern to distinguish null returns from 'no direct access'. Each IPC call creates its own CameraDaemonClient (no shared state). SecretConfigStoreTest passes.

title: CameraDaemon: confirm TCP:19876 is actually listening before writing ready sentinel
description:
## Problem
In app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/daemon/CameraDaemon.java, the TCP and HTTP servers are started fire-and-forget on detached threads at ~line 493-494: new Thread(tcpServer::start, 'TcpServer').start() and new Thread(httpServer::start, 'HttpServer').start(). Nothing joins or polls those threads to confirm a successful ServerSocket bind. The ready sentinel is written ~115 lines later (~line 612, after the 'Daemon ready' log). The original task BladeWatch-erkh required the sentinel be written ONLY after port 19876 is confirmed listening. In practice the elapsed work makes the bind likely, but it is not guaranteed: if TcpCommandServer.start() is slow to bind (e.g. port still in TIME_WAIT from a prior instance) or its thread hasn't been scheduled, the sentinel is written 'ready' while accept() is not yet listening. A client that passes waitUntilReady() then hits ConnectException on its first socket.connect(), defeating the sentinel's purpose.

## What to do
Before writing the sentinel (the READY_SENTINEL FileWriter block, ~line 606-617), add a bounded confirmation that port 19876 is actually accepting connections. Reuse the existing local-port probe pattern - CameraDaemon already has anyPortInUse() (~line 1208) which does a Socket().connect(127.0.0.1:port, 500). Add a small loop that waits (e.g. up to 5s, polling every 200ms) until a TCP connect to 127.0.0.1:TCP_PORT succeeds, then write the sentinel. If it never confirms within the timeout, log a warning but still proceed (do not block daemon startup indefinitely).

## Constraints
- Do NOT change server startup, timing, or the Looper.
- Do NOT block daemon startup forever; cap the confirmation wait (~5s).
- Keep the sentinel content (PID) and the world-readable chmod from BladeWatch-2x4e.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The sentinel is written only after a successful TCP connect to 127.0.0.1:19876 (or after a bounded ~5s timeout with a logged warning)
- [ ] Daemon startup is not blocked indefinitely if the bind fails
- [ ] A client passing waitUntilReady() can immediately connect without ConnectException under normal startup
- [ ] Build compiles with ./gradlew assembleDebug

Do not make mistakes. Read CameraDaemon.java (server start ~line 493, sentinel write ~line 606, anyPortInUse ~line 1208) fully before editing. Verify the build compiles before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
close_reason: Implemented together with BladeWatch-2x4e: 5s polling loop (200ms interval) using Socket().connect() probe on TCP_PORT before writing sentinel. Warns and proceeds if port never confirms within timeout.

title: DaemonReadinessChecker: verify sentinel PID is alive to avoid false-ready after kill -9
description:
## Problem
app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/client/DaemonReadinessChecker.java isReady() only checks new File('/data/local/tmp/camera_daemon.ready').exists() && length>0. It does NOT verify the PID written in the sentinel is a live process. When the daemon is killed with kill -9 (the documented manual cleanup path in CLAUDE.md), no shutdown hook runs, so CameraDaemon.releaseSingletonLock() (which deletes the sentinel) never executes and the file persists with a STALE PID. The app then sees isReady()==true while no daemon is listening on port 19876. readDaemonPid() already parses the PID but it is never used for a liveness check - effectively dead code. The startup delete in CameraDaemon (clearing stale sentinel) only helps once a NEW daemon launches; between a kill -9 and the next launch the app gets a false 'ready' signal and wastes the connect retry loop against a dead port.

## What to do
In DaemonReadinessChecker.isReady(), after confirming the file exists and is non-empty, read the PID via readDaemonPid() and verify the process is alive by checking new File('/proc/' + pid).exists(). Return true only if exists() && non-empty && pid > 0 && /proc/<pid> exists. Keep it cheap (no shell-out). If readDaemonPid() returns -1 (corrupt/empty), treat as NOT ready.

Mirror the liveness pattern already used in CameraDaemon.acquireSingletonLock() (it checks new File('/proc/' + pid).exists() to detect a dead lock holder).

## Constraints
- Keep isReady() cheap: only File.exists()/read + /proc check, no Process exec.
- Do NOT change waitUntilReady()'s polling interval or logging.
- readDaemonPid() signature stays the same.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] isReady() returns false when the sentinel exists but its PID has no /proc/<pid> entry (dead daemon)
- [ ] isReady() returns true when the sentinel exists and its PID is a live process
- [ ] isReady() returns false for a corrupt/empty PID
- [ ] Build compiles with ./gradlew assembleDebug

Do not make mistakes. Read DaemonReadinessChecker.java and CameraDaemon.acquireSingletonLock() fully before editing. Verify the build compiles before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
close_reason: isReady() now reads PID via readDaemonPid() and checks new File('/proc/'+pid).exists() before returning true. Stale sentinels from kill -9 return false. Build compiles.

title: SecretConfigBridge.runIpcBlocking: cancel abandoned executor task on 6s timeout
description:
## Problem
In app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/config/SecretConfigBridge.kt, runIpcBlocking() (~line 229) offloads work to a single-thread ipcExecutor and waits future.get(6, TimeUnit.SECONDS) when called on the main looper. When the daemon is unready, the submitted block is stuck in connect()/waitUntilReady for 30-180s. After 6s, get() throws TimeoutException and runIpcBlocking returns the default value - BUT the future is never cancelled, so the stuck block keeps the single-thread executor busy. Every subsequent main-thread SecretConfigBridge call queues behind the still-running task; each one also blocks the full 6s and returns its default (null/false) for minutes, even after the daemon recovers, until the original task finally finishes. A transient daemon outage thus degrades main-thread config reads to 'always default after 6s' for the duration of the longest stuck call.

## What to do
In runIpcBlocking(), capture the Future and cancel it on timeout. Change:
    ipcExecutor.submit<T> { block() }.get(6, TimeUnit.SECONDS)
to capture the future, and in the catch (or specifically on TimeoutException) call future.cancel(true) before returning defaultValue. Note: cancel(true) interrupts the worker thread; ensure the blocking calls in the chain (Thread.sleep in waitUntilReady / retry backoff, socket connect) respond to interruption - waitUntilReady's Thread.sleep already handles InterruptedException, and socket ops will throw on interrupt. Verify the executor thread actually unblocks after cancel(true).

Consider whether interrupting a write mid-IPC could corrupt a partial secret write; if so, prefer cancel(false) plus a note, or only cancel read operations. Document the choice.

## Constraints
- Do NOT change the 6s timeout value or the main-looper vs background-thread branching.
- Background-thread path (runs block directly) is out of scope for this task.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] After a main-thread IPC call times out at 6s, the executor is freed (not held for the full 30-180s)
- [ ] Subsequent main-thread config calls are not blocked behind an abandoned task once the daemon recovers
- [ ] No partial-write corruption is introduced (justify the cancel(true) vs cancel(false) choice in a comment)
- [ ] Build compiles with ./gradlew assembleDebug

Do not make mistakes. Read SecretConfigBridge.kt fully before editing. Verify the build compiles before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
close_reason: runIpcBlocking() captures future and calls future.cancel(true) on TimeoutException. cancel(true) chosen over cancel(false): IPC is atomic JSON lines, no partial-write risk. Executor freed after 6s instead of staying occupied for 30-180s.

title: CameraDaemonClient.sendCommand(): implicit reconnect now stalls up to 60s on waitUntilReady
description:
## Problem
In app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/client/CameraDaemonClient.java, sendCommand() (~line 105) calls connect() internally when !isConnected() (reconnect path). connect() now begins with DaemonReadinessChecker.waitUntilReady(60_000). So a long-lived client whose socket drops mid-session (e.g. daemon restarted, readLine() returned null setting connected=false) will, on its next sendCommand(), block up to 60s in waitUntilReady before even attempting the socket. Previously this reconnect failed in ~5s. This stalls live-preview/recording control and status polling on the UI's background camera thread for tens of seconds per dropped connection. sendCommandAsync runs on a single-thread executor, so one stuck reconnect serializes all queued async commands behind it.

## What to do
Decide and implement a bounded-reconnect strategy. Recommended: the readiness wait is appropriate for the FIRST cold-boot connect but not for mid-session reconnects where the daemon was already known up. Options (pick one, document why):
1. Add an overload connect(long readinessTimeoutMs) and have sendCommand()'s reconnect call it with a short timeout (e.g. 2000ms) instead of the implicit 60s, while the cold-boot caller keeps 60s.
2. Track a 'wasEverConnected' flag; once true, the reconnect path uses a short readiness timeout.

Keep the public connect() default at 60s for cold-boot callers (SecretConfigBridge, etc.).

## Constraints
- Do NOT change the auth token send, socket timeout, HOST/PORT, or the command read/write logic.
- Reconnect must still attempt the socket; just cap the readiness wait.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A mid-session sendCommand() reconnect after a dropped socket fails or recovers within a few seconds, not 60s
- [ ] Cold-boot connect() still waits up to 60s for the daemon to become ready
- [ ] Build compiles with ./gradlew assembleDebug

Do not make mistakes. Read CameraDaemonClient.java fully before editing. Verify the build compiles before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
close_reason: Added connect(long readinessTimeoutMs) overload. sendCommand() reconnect path calls connect(2_000) for short mid-session timeout; cold-boot connect() still uses 60s. Documented in code.

title: CameraDaemonClient.connect(): retry on SocketTimeoutException, not only ConnectException
description:
## Problem
In app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/client/CameraDaemonClient.java, connect() (~line 48) has a new 3-attempt retry loop, but the retry catch only matches java.net.ConnectException (connection refused). A SocketTimeoutException - thrown when socket.connect() exceeds CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS (5000ms) because the daemon is bound but slow to accept during startup - is a subclass of IOException, NOT ConnectException. It therefore falls into the generic 'catch (Exception e)' block, which logs and returns false IMMEDIATELY with zero retries. The new retry resilience only helps for connection-refused, not for connect-timeout (the common 'daemon slow to accept' case during the staggered startup window).

## What to do
In connect(), broaden the retry catch to also handle java.net.SocketTimeoutException (treat it the same as ConnectException: log 'connect attempt N/3 failed', close socket, null out fields, sleep 2000ms if attempt < 2, continue the loop). The simplest correct change is to catch java.io.IOException (superclass of both ConnectException and SocketTimeoutException) for the retry path, while still letting truly unexpected exceptions (e.g. RuntimeException from JSON/auth) fall through to the immediate-fail generic catch. Verify ConnectException and SocketTimeoutException are both IOException subclasses and that no auth/protocol error is an IOException that would now be wrongly retried.

## Constraints
- Do NOT retry on non-IO exceptions (auth/protocol/JSON errors must still fail fast).
- Do NOT change HOST/PORT, CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS, the auth token send, or sendCommand/ping.
- Keep the 3-attempt cap and 2000ms backoff.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A connect timeout (SocketTimeoutException) is retried up to 3x, same as connection-refused
- [ ] A non-IO exception (e.g. RuntimeException) still returns false immediately without retry
- [ ] Build compiles with ./gradlew assembleDebug

Do not make mistakes. Read CameraDaemonClient.java fully before editing. Verify the build compiles before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
close_reason: Changed retry catch from ConnectException to IOException (superclass of both ConnectException and SocketTimeoutException). Non-IO exceptions still fall through to immediate-fail catch. Build compiles.

title: Investigate H264CircularBuffer: 0 keyframes and oversized packet drops
description:
## Problem
The cam_daemon.log shows two recurring H264 buffer issues:

  H264CircularBuffer: Dropping oversized packet (size=527418 > 262144)
  H264CircularBuffer: Buffer state: 155 packets, 10.0 sec, 0 keyframes, pool=32 free

The buffer has 155 packets spanning 10 seconds but zero keyframes. Video saved during this state would not be seekable and may not decode correctly. Oversized packets (>262144 bytes) are being silently dropped.

## Root Cause to Find
- Locate H264CircularBuffer implementation (likely in app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ or camera/ subdirectory)
- Why are 0 keyframes occurring? Is the camera encoder not producing IDR frames at the expected interval? Check camera encoding config (keyframe interval / I-frame interval setting).
- Is the 262144 byte max packet size appropriate for the current bitrate/resolution? A single 527418-byte packet suggests a large I-frame is being dropped — which explains the 0 keyframes.
- Is there a relationship between the oversized packet drops and the 0-keyframe state? (i.e. the I-frame is being dropped because it is too large, so the buffer never gets a keyframe)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Root cause of 0 keyframes identified
- [ ] Packet size limit reviewed against actual encoder output sizes
- [ ] Fix proposed: either increase MAX_PACKET_SIZE or reduce encoder bitrate/resolution so I-frames fit
- [ ] After fix, buffer state shows >0 keyframes in logcat within 30 seconds of camera start

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
close_reason: Increased MAX_PACKET_SIZE from 256KB to 768KB in H264CircularBuffer.java:31. Root cause: camera configured at BITRATE=4Mbps, KEYFRAME_INTERVAL=2s, 5120x960@25fps produces I-frames up to 527KB which exceeded 256KB limit. Buffer dropped all I-frames as oversized, resulting in 0 keyframes. New 768KB threshold handles STANDARD-H.264 comfortably through PREMIUM typical I-frames. Pool ceiling 200 x 768KB = 150MB peak.

description:

title: Implement storage priority: SD card → USB → internal for recordings and settings
description:
## Context

BladeWatch currently defaults to internal storage for recordings and settings. The device may have an SD card or external USB drive attached. We should prefer external storage when available, both for capacity reasons and so that footage survives a head-unit reboot/crash without filling internal storage.

## What needs to be done

On daemon startup, implement a storage priority scan:

1. Check for an SD card mount point (e.g. `/storage/sdcard1`, `/mnt/media_rw/`, or any mount under `/storage/` that is not `emulated`)
2. If not found, check for an external USB drive (e.g. `/mnt/usb*`, `/storage/usb*`)
3. Fall back to internal storage (`/storage/emulated/0`)

For each candidate mount point:
- Verify it is mounted and writable
- Check if a `BladeWatch/` folder exists; if so, prefer that drive immediately
- If no `BladeWatch/` folder exists, create one before adopting that drive
- Once a drive is selected, persist the resolved base path in the unified config so all subsystems (recordings, surveillance, proximity, trips) use it

Update the following subsystems to use the resolved storage base path instead of the hard-coded internal path:
- Recording output paths in `CameraDaemon.java`
- Settings/config persistence paths in `UnifiedConfigManager.kt`
- Any other path constants referencing `/storage/emulated/0/BladeWatch`

Relevant files to read before editing:
- `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/daemon/CameraDaemon.java`
- `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/config/UnifiedConfigManager.kt`
- `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/config/SecretConfigStore.kt`
- `docs/data-flow-and-storage.md`

## Constraints

- Do NOT change the IPC token path (`/data/local/tmp/bladewatch_ipc_token`) or config/secrets paths under `/data/local/tmp/` — those must stay on tmpfs
- The scan must be fast (< 200 ms) so it does not delay daemon startup
- If no external storage is found, silently fall through to internal — no error, no crash
- If the selected drive is later unmounted mid-session, log a warning but do not crash; new recordings can fall back to internal
- This is a daemon-side change only; no UI work is required in this task

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] On startup with an SD card present containing a `BladeWatch/` folder, recordings go to the SD card
- [ ] On startup with an SD card present but no `BladeWatch/` folder, the folder is created and recordings go to the SD card
- [ ] With no SD card but a USB drive present, same logic applies to USB
- [ ] With neither SD nor USB, recordings go to internal storage as before
- [ ] `docs/data-flow-and-storage.md` is updated to document the new priority order
- [ ] Unit test or integration note documents the expected behavior

## Warning

Do not make mistakes. Read every referenced file fully before editing. Verify the build compiles (`./gradlew assembleDebug`) and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
close_reason: Added applyAutoStoragePriority() to StorageManager.java with USB drive discovery. Called from CameraDaemon.java startup after fixAllPermissions(). Runs unconditionally on every boot: SD card first, then USB, then internal. Docs updated in data-flow-and-storage.md. Build: SUCCESS.

title: Migrate remaining raw-HTTP/TCP screens to Connect gRPC (Dashboard, MainActivity, Diagnostics)
description:
Most of the Android UI was migrated REST to Connect/gRPC (Vehicle, Trips, Recording settings, Surveillance settings, Live view), but several screens were NOT migrated. They still use raw java.net.HttpURLConnection and/or the legacy TCP CameraDaemonClient and parse JSONObject(body) directly, bypassing the Connect clients.
