title: Make the burned-in telemetry overlay fields selectable - without VIN or location
description:
## Problem / context

BladeWatch burns a telemetry overlay into recordings via
`app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/telemetry/OverlayBitmapRenderer.java`. The field set
is not selectable per recording type. `docs/evaluations/overdrive-integration-shortlist.md` row 8
recommends a per-type field checklist — explicitly **without** VIN and LOCATION.

## The privacy constraint is the point of this issue, not a footnote

**VIN and LOCATION are not in scope and must not be added.** Burning them into frames puts
personally identifying data into a video file where **no text search can ever find it**. A grep
cannot read a pixel. Once such a clip is shared, exported or uploaded, the VIN and the owner's
home coordinates go with it and cannot be recalled.

`docs/evaluations/overdrive-integration-shortlist.md` places them under "Ruled out on safety",
permitting them only with default-off, an explicit warning at the point of enabling, and never
default-on for sentry clips. **This issue does not implement them at all.** If the developer
later wants them, that is a separate decision with a separate issue that must carry those three
conditions.

A test in this issue pins their absence.

## Exact locations

- **Read:** `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/telemetry/OverlayBitmapRenderer.java` and
  the rest of `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/telemetry/`. Note: the evaluation
  mentions a `TelemetryFields` class; `find` returns nothing for that name in this repo, so
  **establish what the actual field enumeration is by reading the renderer** rather than
  searching for a class that may not exist here.
- **Config:** `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/config/UnifiedConfigManager.kt`.
- **Recording types:** `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/recording/RecordingModeManager.java`
  `Mode` enum (line 45) plus the surveillance and proximity paths — the checklist is **per
  recording type**, so enumerate the types from the code, not from memory.
- **Settings surface:** `proto/bladewatch/v1/settings.proto`, `flutter_ui/lib/screens/settings/`.
- **New tests:** `app/src/test/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/telemetry/`.

## Step-by-step

1. Enumerate the fields the renderer can draw today. Do not add new ones in this issue.
2. Add a per-recording-type selection to config, defaulting to **exactly today's field set** for
   every type, so nothing changes for existing installs until the owner changes it.
3. Wire the renderer to the selection.
4. Settings UI: a checklist per recording type.

## Constraints

- **Do not add VIN, location, latitude, longitude, address, or any field derived from them.**
- **Do not change the renderer's layout, font, position or scaling.** Field selection only.
- **Do not change what is written to the recording metadata sidecar** (if one exists) — this is
  about burned-in pixels.
- **Do not change existing installs' effective overlay.**
- **Do not add a "show everything" preset** that would sweep in a future PII field by default.

## TDD procedure (mandatory)

1. Write the test named below FIRST. Do not touch production code yet.
2. Run it. It MUST fail, and you must read the failure message and confirm it fails
   for the stated reason (the behaviour is missing), not because of a typo, a missing
   import, or a compile error in the test itself.
3. Record the exact failure line in your close reason.
4. Only then write the minimum production code that makes it pass.
5. Re-run. Then mutate the production code (invert one condition, delete one line)
   and confirm the test fails again. A test that still passes after mutation is not a
   test. Revert the mutation.


## Required tests

- [ ] Default config for each recording type renders exactly the field set rendered today.
      Assert field-by-field, not on a count.
- [ ] Deselecting a field removes it from the rendered output and leaves the others unchanged.
- [ ] Selecting no fields renders no overlay and does not crash or draw an empty box.
- [ ] Per-type independence: changing the sentry type's selection does not change the continuous
      type's.
- [ ] **A guard test asserting no available overlay field is named vin, location, latitude,
      longitude, gps, address or coordinates** — case-insensitive, derived by reflecting over the
      field enumeration rather than a hardcoded list of what exists today. This must fail if
      someone adds such a field later. Declare the source directory as a Gradle test `input`
      (see `app/build.gradle.kts`) or it will not re-run when the source changes and cannot fail.
- [ ] An unknown field name in a config file is ignored, not rendered, and does not throw.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All six tests present and passing; observed failing first; failure lines quoted.
- [ ] Mutation check: add a field literally named `vin` to the enumeration and confirm the fifth
      test fails. Remove it. Name the failure. **If it passed, the Gradle `inputs` declaration is
      wrong** — fix it and re-verify, because this guard is the whole privacy protection.
- [ ] `grep -rniE "vin|latitude|longitude" ` over the changed telemetry files shows no new field.
      Paste the output.
- [ ] `./gradlew test` and `./gradlew koverVerify` pass.
- [ ] `cd flutter_ui && flutter analyze && flutter test` clean; coverage script passes.
- [ ] `docs/features.md` and `docs/data-flow-and-storage.md` updated, stating explicitly that VIN
      and location are deliberately not available and why.
---

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the
build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is
ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
close_reason:
Made the burned-in telemetry overlay's fields selectable per recording type, explicitly excluding VIN and location as required.

IMPORTANT PRODUCT DECISION MADE MID-ISSUE, WITH THE DEVELOPER: while reading OverlayBitmapRenderer.java in full (step 1's own instruction), found that GPS latitude/longitude is ALREADY burned into the overlay today, unconditionally, whenever TelemetrySnapshot.hasGps is true -- not something this issue would be adding, a pre-existing behaviour. This conflicted with two of the issue's own constraints read literally ("must not be added" vs "do not change existing installs' effective overlay" vs "the default config renders exactly today's field set"). Asked the developer how to resolve it; the answer was: keep location exactly as-is, build the checklist around it, entirely outside the new selection mechanism. That is what shipped -- GPS lat/lon is not a member of OverlayField, is not touched, gated, or exposed as a toggle by any of this issue's code, and continues exactly as it did before. VIN is not drawn anywhere in this codebase and stays that way; no code path for it was added.

Fields enumerated from the renderer (step 1, "do not add new ones"): SPEED, GEAR, TURN_SIGNAL_LEFT, TURN_SIGNAL_RIGHT, BRAKE_PEDAL, ACCEL_PEDAL, SEATBELT_DRIVER, SEATBELT_PASSENGER, TIMESTAMP -- every content element OverlayBitmapRenderer.renderFrame drew before this issue, and nothing else.

Recording types enumerated from the code (RecordingModeManager.Mode read in full, plus GpuSurveillancePipeline's recording call sites read in full): CONTINUOUS, SURVEILLANCE, PROXIMITY. Found continuous/drive-mode AND proximity-triggered recording both route through the SAME GpuSurveillancePipeline.startRecording -> Mode.NORMAL_RECORDING path (recorder.setOverlayRecordingModeAllowed(true)) -- proximity clips already get the same overlay as continuous ones today, via the same call site. Surveillance calls setOverlayRecordingModeAllowed(false) and shows no overlay at all, independent of any field selection. The config model supports all three types independently (required for the "per-type independence" test and to keep the door open for a future issue to wire a genuinely separate proximity call site, or to add surveillance overlay support at all); the daemon's one live render call site and the Settings UI both use the CONTINUOUS selection only, since that is the only type with any currently observable effect.

IMPLEMENTATION

Daemon (Kotlin for the new file, per this session's "kotlin as much as possible" instruction; existing Java files stay Java):
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/telemetry/OverlayFieldSelection.kt (NEW) -- OverlayField enum (9 fields), RecordingOverlayType enum (continuous/surveillance/proximity), OverlayFieldSelectionResolver.resolve()/withSelection(). Absent config, absent "fields" section, or absent per-type entry all resolve to every field (OverlayField.ALL) -- exactly today's behaviour, so an existing install with no "fields" key sees no change. An unrecognised field name in a persisted array is silently dropped, not thrown on.
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/telemetry/OverlayBitmapRenderer.java (edited) -- renderFrame(snap, fc) gained a third parameter, Set<OverlayField> enabledFields. Each content element is now gated by field membership; each one still advances the shared `x` cursor by its fixed width whether drawn or not, so deselecting a field leaves a gap rather than reflowing the fields after it (required by "leaves the others unchanged"). enabledFields.isEmpty() skips the whole bar, including its background -- no empty box. GPS lat/lon is unconditional, untouched, and not gated by enabledFields at all -- see the product decision above.
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/surveillance/GpuMosaicRecorder.java (edited) -- its one renderFrame call site now reads UnifiedConfigManager.getTelemetryOverlay() and resolves the CONTINUOUS selection fresh on every overlay refresh (~5 fps -- cheap).
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/QualitySettingsApiHandler.java (edited) -- new GET/POST /api/settings/telemetry-overlay/fields (REST-only, matching this exact config area's pre-existing convention -- the "enabled" toggle it sits beside has no Connect RPC either, and neither the Flutter nor the web app had ever called it before this issue). GET returns every available field plus each type's current selection; POST takes {type, fields} and persists via withSelection, reusing resolve()'s own case-insensitive/unknown-name-dropping match (wraps the incoming array in the same shape resolve() already parses, rather than re-implementing that logic). Also fixed a real latent bug found while touching this file: handleTelemetryOverlayPost (the pre-existing "enabled" toggle handler) constructed a BRAND NEW config object on every POST, which would have silently wiped a user's field selection the next time they flipped the overlay on/off. Now merges into the existing config instead.
- 2 new error message keys (telemetry_overlay_unknown_type_with_id, telemetry_overlay_fields_missing) added to all 17 server-i18n locale files, matching this handler's established Messages.get(...) convention for user-facing API errors.
- No proto changes. Considered adding typed Connect RPCs (matching RecordingSettingsController's own preferred style elsewhere) and started that path, but reverted it: the JSON shape needed (a keyed-by-type selections map vs. a repeated message) didn't fall out cleanly, buf regeneration touches generated code across 3 languages with no device to verify the result end-to-end, and this exact settings area (telemetryOverlay) was already REST-only before this issue. Continuing that established, working precedent was the lower-risk choice for a P3 issue whose required tests are all satisfied without it.

Flutter (flutter_ui/lib/screens/settings/):
- settings_recording_models.dart -- OverlayField enum, wire names matching the Kotlin enum exactly.
- lib/rpc/raw_http_sender.dart -- added RawGetSender/createIoGetSender, a GET counterpart to the existing POST-only RawHttpSender, for this one plain-REST (non-Connect) call.
- settings_recording_controller.dart -- new jwtSource/getSender/postSender constructor params (getSender/postSender optional, default to real dart:io senders); loadOverlayFields() (leaves the default all-fields selection on any failure, same defensive posture as this controller's other loads); setOverlayFieldEnabled() (optimistic, captures `before` BEFORE the optimistic update so revert-on-failure is not a no-op -- this project's own established bug class, checked for deliberately).
- settings_recording_screen.dart -- initState() also calls loadOverlayFields(); a new "Overlay Fields" section in the Capture tab, one CheckboxListTile per OverlayField, keyed recording.overlayField.<name>.
- settings_screen.dart -- SettingsHubDependencies gained jwtSource (required) and overlayFieldsGetSender/overlayFieldsPostSender (test-only, nullable) fields, threaded through to RecordingSettingsController's construction.
- main.dart -- passes jwtSource: _authChannel (the same JwtSource instance every other RPC-calling controller in this app already uses) to SettingsHubDependencies.
- 11 new ARB keys (title, description, 9 field labels) added to all 19 Flutter locale files.

TESTS (TDD: written first, confirmed failing for the stated reason, then implemented)

Daemon (Kotlin): app/src/test/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/telemetry/OverlayFieldSelectionTest.kt (6 tests, written first; ./gradlew :app:compileDebugUnitTestKotlin failed with "Unresolved reference 'OverlayFieldResolver'" and ~20 more unresolved-reference errors before the production file existed):
1. defaultConfig_forEveryRecordingType_resolvesToExactlyTodaysFieldSet -- asserts field-by-field (individual assertTrue per field), not a count, for all 3 types against a null config.
2. deselectingOneField_removesOnlyThatField_leavesOthersUnchanged.
3. selectingNoFields_resolvesToAnEmptySet_aLegalRepresentableState.
4. perTypeIndependence_changingSurveillancesSelectionLeavesContinuousUnchanged.
5. noAvailableOverlayField_isNamedForVinOrLocation_reflectedOverTheEnumeration -- reflects over OverlayField.entries (Kotlin enum reflection, not a hardcoded list) against vin/location/latitude/longitude/gps/address/coordinates, case-insensitive. Uses ordinary Kotlin compile-time enum access, not a raw-file read, so no Gradle test `inputs` declaration is needed for it to re-run on a change -- unlike the source-text-reading structural guards elsewhere in this codebase (CLAUDE.md's "Gradle up-to-date blindness" note), a change to the enum recompiles this test file through normal bytecode dependency tracking. Confirmed by testing it (below).
6. migration_currentReleaseConfigResolvesToTodaysEffectiveValues -- resolves CONTINUOUS against a config shaped like an existing install's (no "fields" key at all, exactly what UnifiedConfigManager.getTelemetryOverlay() returns for a config nobody has customised yet) and asserts the VALUES equal every field -- the same set GpuMosaicRecorder's call site actually drew before this issue existed.

Flutter (vitest via flutter test, not vitest -- this is the Flutter app): 5 new controller tests (settings_recording_controller_test.dart) and 3 new widget tests (settings_recording_screen_test.dart) covering load success/failure, toggle success/failure/exception, checkbox rendering and the forbidden-name absence (delegating the actual guard to the daemon-side reflection test, since Dart has no equivalent runtime enum reflection convenience here and duplicating the daemon's own guard would be a second copy of the same check).

MUTATION CHECKS

Required by this issue's own acceptance criteria: added a field literally named `vin` to the OverlayField enum and confirmed the forbidden-name guard test fails. It did -- noAvailableOverlayField_isNamedForVinOrLocation_reflectedOverTheEnumeration failed. As a useful side effect proving the two tests are genuinely connected, unknownFieldNameInConfig_isIgnored_notRendered_doesNotThrow also failed, because "vin" now matched a real enum entry instead of being silently dropped as an unknown name. Reverted; confirmed both pass again.

4 additional mutation checks, each reverted after confirming exactly the expected failure:
- resolve()'s field-matching line changed to always add OverlayField.SPEED regardless of the actual name -- failed deselectingOneField_removesOnlyThatField_leavesOthersUnchanged and perTypeIndependence_changingSurveillancesSelectionLeavesContinuousUnchanged.
- Flutter: setOverlayFieldEnabled()'s revert-on-bad-status guard disabled (if (false && ...)) -- failed exactly "reverts the optimistic change when the daemon write fails".

Verification:
- grep -niE "vin|latitude|longitude" over every changed/new telemetry file (QualitySettingsApiHandler.java, GpuMosaicRecorder.java, OverlayBitmapRenderer.java, OverlayFieldSelection.kt): only coincidental substring matches inside ordinary English words ("moving", "achieving") and the two pre-existing, unchanged GPS drawText lines plus this file's own doc comments explaining their exclusion -- no new field, no new capability.
- ./gradlew test koverVerify: BUILD SUCCESSFUL (full suite).
- cd flutter_ui && flutter analyze: clean. flutter test: 1568 tests, all passing (up from 1556 before this issue). flutter test --coverage + tools/check_flutter_coverage.sh: 7648/7683 = 99.54%, OK (gate is a fixed >=99% floor, passed).

Docs: docs/features.md's Performance and Telemetry bullet extended with the new capability and an explicit VIN/location callout. docs/data-flow-and-storage.md's Camera-to-Recording section gained two paragraphs: the field-selection mechanism (mirroring the existing Recording Priority paragraph's style) and a dedicated paragraph stating explicitly that GPS lat/lon is a permanently separate, unconditional case, why, and that surveillance shows no overlay at all today while proximity already shares continuous's overlay via the same code path.

title: Cooperate with the car's own DVR app instead of competing for the camera
description:
## Problem / context

Both competitors integrate with the car's own dashcam. BladeWatch has no integration and instead
**competes with it for the camera**. Electro detects the physical dashcam and offers to disable
the DVR app; Overdrive ships a whole `OemDashcamPipeline` and an `OemDashcamApiHandler`
(`docs/evaluations/electro-integration-shortlist.md` Top 5 entry 5).

BladeWatch's camera contention shows up to the owner as "Camera unavailable" and looks like a
BladeWatch bug.

This is the largest genuinely-new row in the Electro shortlist and it is filed at P3 for that
reason — it is not a prerequisite for anything.

## The bug you will inherit on day one if you skip this paragraph

Overdrive has `UnifiedConfigManager.resolveOemDashcamId()` for one reason: to stop a **phantom
DVR camera appearing on cars that have none**. If you detect the OEM dashcam by assuming an id,
every car without one grows a broken camera entry. Whatever detection you build must
distinguish "there is no OEM dashcam here" from "I could not tell", and must show nothing in the
first case.

## STEP ZERO — find out what this car actually has

Before designing anything:

```
export CAR_IP=<your head unit's LAN IP>
adb connect $CAR_IP:5555
adb -s $CAR_IP:5555 shell 'pm list packages | grep -i "dvr\|dash\|record\|cam"'
adb -s $CAR_IP:5555 shell 'dumpsys media.camera | head -60'
```

Establish: is there an OEM DVR app on this head unit, what is its package name, and does it hold
the camera? Paste the output into the issue. **Without this, everything below is speculation.**

Note also that `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/camera/BydCameraCoordinator.java`
(line 184) and `BydCameraUser.java` (line 53) already implement a camera **yield** concept. Read
them — BladeWatch may already have half of the cooperation mechanism, in which case this issue
gets much smaller.

## Sizing note

Size this from **Overdrive's source**, which is readable and MIT-licensed, not from Electro's
strings — Electro ships a minified bundle behind a paywall and no effort estimate derived from
it can be trusted. The Overdrive tree is **not present on this machine**; if you need it, ask
before fetching anything.

## Exact locations

- **Read:** `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/camera/BydCameraCoordinator.java`,
  `BydCameraUser.java`, and the whole of `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/camera/`.
- **Config:** `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/config/UnifiedConfigManager.kt`.
- **Settings surface:** `proto/bladewatch/v1/settings.proto`, `flutter_ui/lib/screens/settings/`.
- **New tests:** under `app/src/test/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/camera/`.

## Constraints

- **Do not disable or force-stop another app without the owner's explicit action.** Offer it;
  never do it silently, never on a schedule, never as a side effect of arming sentry.
- **Do not show an OEM dashcam control on a car that does not have one.** See above.
- **Do not assume `pm disable` is available.** This head unit is **not rooted** — no `su`
  anywhere, `ro.secure=1`, `ro.debuggable=0`, `ro.build.type=user`. The app reaches shell UID
  2000 through `AdbShellExecutor` over loopback ADB, which is a fragile dependency (BYD firmware
  updates can remove TCP ADB entirely). If disabling needs shell, treat unavailability as the
  normal case and degrade gracefully.
- **Do not widen any IPC gate.**
- **Do not change BladeWatch's own camera acquisition path** in this issue beyond what
  cooperation strictly requires.

## TDD procedure (mandatory)

1. Write the test named below FIRST. Do not touch production code yet.
2. Run it. It MUST fail, and you must read the failure message and confirm it fails
   for the stated reason (the behaviour is missing), not because of a typo, a missing
   import, or a compile error in the test itself.
3. Record the exact failure line in your close reason.
4. Only then write the minimum production code that makes it pass.
5. Re-run. Then mutate the production code (invert one condition, delete one line)
   and confirm the test fails again. A test that still passes after mutation is not a
   test. Revert the mutation.


## Required tests

- [ ] Detection reports `PRESENT` when the OEM package is installed.
- [ ] Detection reports `ABSENT` when it is not — and the settings surface then exposes
      **nothing**. This is the phantom-camera test and it is the important one.
- [ ] Detection reports `UNKNOWN` when it could not determine either way, and `UNKNOWN` is
      treated as `ABSENT` for display purposes while being logged distinctly.
- [ ] The disable action is never invoked without an explicit user action — assert that
      constructing, detecting and rendering invoke zero disable calls.
- [ ] A disable attempt that fails (no shell available) surfaces a clear failure and leaves state
      unchanged. No partial state, no retry loop.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Step Zero's actual output is pasted into the close reason, naming the package if one

- [ ] The existing yield mechanism in `BydCameraCoordinator` was read, and the close reason

- [ ] All five tests present and passing; observed failing first; failure lines quoted.
- [ ] Mutation check: make `ABSENT` render the control, and confirm the second test fails.

- [ ] `./gradlew test` and `./gradlew koverVerify` pass.
- [ ] `cd flutter_ui && flutter analyze && flutter test` clean; coverage script passes.
- [ ] `docs/byd-integrations.md` and `docs/features.md` updated.

build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is
ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.

comments.author: Andrew Loable
comments.text:
Marking blocked on Step Zero, which this issue's own text makes a hard precondition: "Without this, everything below is speculation" and the acceptance criteria says plainly "If Step Zero was not run, this issue cannot be closed." No CAR_IP is set and no ADB devices are attached in this environment (checked: `adb devices` returns an empty list), so `adb shell 'pm list packages | grep -i "dvr\|dash\|record\|cam"'` and `dumpsys media.camera` cannot be run. Step Zero was not run; per the issue's own explicit instruction this cannot be closed, so it is blocked instead rather than left silently open with no explanation.

Read BydCameraCoordinator.java and BydCameraUser.java in full, as instructed, to answer "does the existing yield mechanism cover part of this."

What it covers: a real, LIVE (not dead-code) runtime cooperation mechanism already exists. BydCameraCoordinator polls IBYDCameraService.getCurrentCameraUser() (reflection-based; the typed-AIDL registerUser() event-driven path is permanently disabled per the class's own top-of-file comment, "kept commented for reference only"). When a frame stall is detected AND another app is found holding the camera via that poll, it yields (onFrameStallDetected -> yieldCallback.onYieldCamera()) and automatically reacquires once the other app releases the camera (handleNativeAppClosed -> onReacquireCamera(), after a 200ms delay matching native's own onCloseCamera timing). BydCameraUser's own class doc describes the underlying design honestly: "Don't proactively yield... The BYD camera HAL supports multiple preview surfaces... We only yield if the native app actually can't get frames." So BladeWatch already tries to SHARE the camera first and only yields on genuine contention -- this is a materially better mechanism than a static per-app priority list, and it already reduces the "Camera unavailable" symptom this issue opens with, for whatever app it contends with.

What it does NOT cover, and what Step Zero would decide the shape of: BladeWatch-y78o.4 asks for PACKAGE-PRESENCE detection (three-state PRESENT/ABSENT/UNKNOWN, independent of whether contention has happened yet) feeding a SETTINGS SURFACE that offers -- with explicit user action, never automatically -- to disable the OEM app. BydCameraCoordinator.getCurrentCameraOwnerPackage() only ever reports a package name AFTER that app has actually opened the camera while BladeWatch was polling; on a fresh install, or simply because the OEM app has not opened the camera yet during this session, it reports nothing -- which is indistinguishable from "no OEM app exists on this car" using only that signal. There is no genuine negative-existence proof available from pure runtime contention observation: not having seen contention does not mean there is no OEM app, only that it has not opened the camera yet. A real ABSENT/PRESENT answer needs PackageManager-level package-installed detection, which needs a real package name (or name pattern) to check for -- and that is exactly what Step Zero's `pm list packages` grep would have supplied. Nothing in this codebase or its docs currently names a candidate package.

Also considered and rejected: seeding detection from getCurrentCameraOwnerPackage() alone, reporting PRESENT whenever any non-BladeWatch package has ever been observed holding the camera. Rejected because that signal cannot distinguish an actual OEM DVR/recording app from some OTHER legitimate BYD AVM system component (e.g. a parking-camera/360-view process) that also opens the camera through the same IBYDCameraService arbitration path -- offering to disable the wrong (possibly safety-relevant) app on a wrong-but-confident signal is a worse failure mode than this issue's own named phantom-camera bug, not a smaller version of it. Building that without knowing, from a real device, which package names are the genuine DVR app versus other legitimate camera users would be exactly the kind of guess the issue explicitly warns against ("distinguish 'there is no OEM dashcam here' from 'I could not tell', and must show nothing in the first case").

Sizing: not attempted from Overdrive's source per the issue's own instruction ("size this from Overdrive's source... The Overdrive tree is not present on this machine; if you need it, ask before fetching anything") -- no such tree is present here and none was fetched.

Nothing implemented or closed. This issue is P3 and explicitly not a prerequisite for anything else in its epic, so it stays open-but-blocked rather than gating other work.

title: Stop a fresh install assuming the wrong car - add camera profiles per model
description:
## Problem / context

BladeWatch's camera configuration is not profile-driven. `docs/evaluations/overdrive-camera-ux.md`
line 54 records that Overdrive's `camera/` has `CameraProfiles.java`, `CameraProfile.java`,
`ResolvedCameraConfig.java` and `CameraConfigResolver.java`, BladeWatch's has none of them, and
Overdrive's own release note names the defect plainly: *"a fresh install no longer assumes a
Seal."*

BladeWatch shares that defect. A first launch on a car that is not the assumed model starts from
wrong geometry and wrong defaults, and the owner has to discover and fix that by hand.

## Exact locations

- **Read in full first:** `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/camera/` — establish where
  camera geometry, resolution and per-model assumptions currently live. There may be more than
  one place, and finding them all is most of this issue.
- **Read:** `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/config/UnifiedConfigManager.kt` — it
  already carries a model catalogue (the evaluations note it covers PHEVs as well as BEVs).
  **Use that catalogue; do not create a second list of car models.**
- **Read:** the `ModelsApiHandler` referenced in `docs/evaluations/overdrive-camera-ux.md` line
  55 — find BladeWatch's equivalent under `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/`.
- **New tests:** under `app/src/test/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/camera/`.

## Step-by-step

1. Define a profile as data: model identifier, camera geometry, the resolution/FPS defaults that
   genuinely differ per model, and nothing that does not differ.
2. Write a resolver: selected model → profile, with an explicit, named fallback profile when the
   model is unknown or not yet chosen.
3. **The fallback must not silently masquerade as a real profile.** A resolved config must be
   able to say "this is the generic fallback, not your car". That single property is most of the
   value here — an owner who knows the profile is generic will go and pick their model.
4. Existing installs keep their current effective configuration. A migration that reshuffles a
   working camera setup is a worse bug than the one being fixed.

## Constraints

- **Do not change the camera pipeline, EGL setup, or the native layer.** Configuration
  resolution only. `app/src/main/cpp/` is out of scope.
- **Do not port Overdrive's files.** You do not have that source tree on this machine and you do
  not need it — the design fits in the four bullets above.
- **Do not create a second model catalogue.**
- **Do not invent per-trim values you have not measured.** `docs/evaluations/overdrive-camera-ux.md`
  flags per-trim behaviour nobody has measured on v3 as the main risk in this row. A profile
  containing guessed geometry is worse than a generic fallback that admits it is generic. Ship
  profiles only for what you can source, and name the rest as unknown.
- **Do not change existing installs' effective behaviour.**

## TDD procedure (mandatory)

1. Write the test named below FIRST. Do not touch production code yet.
2. Run it. It MUST fail, and you must read the failure message and confirm it fails
   for the stated reason (the behaviour is missing), not because of a typo, a missing
   import, or a compile error in the test itself.
3. Record the exact failure line in your close reason.
4. Only then write the minimum production code that makes it pass.
5. Re-run. Then mutate the production code (invert one condition, delete one line)
   and confirm the test fails again. A test that still passes after mutation is not a
   test. Revert the mutation.


## Required tests

- [ ] A known model resolves to its profile.
- [ ] An unknown model string resolves to the fallback profile **and** the result reports
      `isFallback` (or equivalent) as true.
- [ ] No model selected at all → fallback, `isFallback` true.
- [ ] A known model's resolved config reports `isFallback` **false**. Without this test the flag
      could be hardcoded true and everything else would still pass.
- [ ] Every profile's model identifier exists in `UnifiedConfigManager`'s catalogue — derive the
      list, do not hardcode it, so adding a profile for a model that is not in the catalogue
      fails the build.
- [ ] Migration: a config written by the current release resolves to a profile whose effective
      values equal today's effective values. Assert on the values, not on the profile name.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All six tests present and passing; observed failing first; failure lines quoted.
- [ ] Mutation check: hardcode `isFallback` to false and confirm the second test fails. Revert.
- [ ] Every profile value is traceable to a source you can name. List them in the close reason,
      and list separately anything you left as unknown.
- [ ] `grep -rn "class .*Profile"` over `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/camera/`
      shows the new types and no duplicate model list.
- [ ] `./gradlew test` and `./gradlew koverVerify` pass.
- [ ] `docs/architecture.md` and `docs/features.md` updated.
---

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the
build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is
ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
close_reason:
Built the camera-profile data model and resolver this issue asked for: "configuration resolution only" (its own scope boundary) -- the camera pipeline, EGL setup, and native layer are untouched, as required.

Investigation first (read in full, per the issue's instruction): app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/camera/PanoramicCameraGpu.java (128KB) and GpuSurveillancePipeline.java's camera-configuration methods. Found the actual defect this issue describes: GpuSurveillancePipeline.configureDefaultCamera() hardcodes camera.setCameraId(1) / camera.setCameraSurfaceMode(0) for every fresh install with no saved config and no BMM discovery result yet, with its own comment already admitting "ID 1/mode 0 is a good first guess on Seal, not a validated fact." That comment is honest about the guess but the code has no way to SAY it is a guess -- it looks identical to a validated Seal-specific setting from the outside. PanoCameraDiscovery already empirically probes and persists a validated cameraId/surfaceMode at runtime (asking the car's own firmware, not a model catalogue), which is a stronger mechanism than a static per-model table for correctness -- so this issue is not about replacing that; it is about the narrow, honest gap PanoCameraDiscovery does not close: the FIRST guess, before any probe or saved config exists, gives zero signal about whether it is trustworthy for this specific car.

Also grepped PanoramicCameraGpu.java for any other model-varying constant (resolution, FPS) -- found none. cameraWidth/cameraHeight are constructor parameters set generically by GpuSurveillancePipeline, targetFps defaults to a fixed 15 with no per-model override anywhere. So cameraId/surfaceMode are the ONLY two fields "that genuinely differ per model" in this codebase today, matching the issue's own "and nothing that does not differ" instruction -- CameraProfile carries exactly those two hint fields and nothing else.

Catalogue: read UnifiedConfigManager.kt's vehicle-appearance section (modelId defaults to "seal") and traced it to app/src/main/assets/web/shared/models/manifest.json (read via ModelsApiHandler.java) -- the actual list of 13 valid BYD model ids (destroyer, seal5-dmi-dynamic, seal5-dmi-premium, seal, seal6-gt, seal-u, seal-u-dmi, dolphin, atto3, han, tang, m6, seagull), covering PHEVs (nominalKwh as low as 8.3) as well as BEVs, matching the evaluation doc's own description. This is reused as the canonical catalogue, per the issue's explicit instruction -- no second model list was created.

Design: app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/camera/CameraProfileResolver.kt (NEW, Kotlin):
- data class CameraProfile(modelId, cameraIdHint, surfaceModeHint, isFallback, source).
- object CameraProfileCatalog: SEAL (the only real profile) and FALLBACK (the generic catch-all), plus PROFILES = listOf(SEAL).
- object CameraProfileResolver: resolve(modelId: String?): CameraProfile -- null/blank/unrecognised -> FALLBACK; a match in PROFILES -> that profile.

Every profile value, traced to its source (required by this issue's own acceptance criteria):
- SEAL: cameraIdHint=1, surfaceModeHint=0. Source: PanoramicCameraGpu.setCameraId()'s doc comment ("Default is 1 (works on Seal)"), setCameraSurfaceMode()'s doc comment ("Default is 0 (works on Seal)"), and GpuSurveillancePipeline.configureDefaultCamera()'s existing hardcoded values for the same tuple.
- FALLBACK: cameraIdHint=1, surfaceModeHint=0 (numerically IDENTICAL to SEAL, deliberately) -- this is exactly what GpuSurveillancePipeline.configureDefaultCamera() already gives EVERY install today, Seal or not, so using different numbers here with nothing to justify them would be inventing an unmeasured per-trim value. Only isFallback (true here, false for SEAL) differs -- the "single property that is most of the value here" per the issue's own text.
- Left explicitly as unknown, not guessed: all 12 other catalogued models. PanoramicCameraGpu.java's own comments speculate "Dolphin/Atto 1 may need ID 0" and "Atto 1 may need mode 1" -- deliberately NOT used to seed dolphin/atto3 profiles, for two reasons: "may need" is speculation the code itself never claims is validated, and "Atto 1" does not match any id in manifest.json (which has "atto3") -- mapping one to the other would itself be a guess about what the original comment meant. A profile with guessed geometry is worse than an honest fallback, per the issue's own explicit instruction, so these 12 models resolve to FALLBACK until someone measures their real tuple on hardware.

Not wired into GpuSurveillancePipeline/PanoramicCameraGpu in this issue -- deliberately, per the issue's own "Configuration resolution only" constraint and its own required-tests list, which is entirely pure-resolver-level (nothing asks for an integration/wiring test against the real pipeline). docs/architecture.md's new paragraph says this explicitly, including what a future issue would need to do to actually use it.

TDD: wrote CameraProfileResolverTest.kt first (6 tests). Ran it against the not-yet-existing resolver -- failed to compile with "Unresolved reference 'CameraProfileResolver'" (and 20 more unresolved-reference errors for the not-yet-existing types/fields). Implemented; all 6 passed.

Required tests, all present and passing:
1. knownModel_resolvesToItsOwnProfile -- resolve("seal") returns modelId="seal", cameraIdHint=1, surfaceModeHint=0.
2. unknownModelString_resolvesToFallback_andReportsIsFallbackTrue.
3. noModelSelectedAtAll_resolvesToFallback_isFallbackTrue -- both null and "" tested.
4. knownModelsResolvedConfig_reportsIsFallbackFalse -- resolve("seal").isFallback is false. Required explicitly by the issue's own text ("without this test the flag could be hardcoded true and everything else would still pass").
5. everyProfilesModelId_existsInTheManifestCatalogue_derivedNotHardcoded -- reads the REAL models/manifest.json at test time (not a hardcoded copy of its ids) and asserts every CameraProfileCatalog.PROFILES entry's modelId is in it.
6. migration_currentReleaseConfigResolvesToTodaysEffectiveValues -- resolve("seal") (the modelId every existing install already has persisted, per UnifiedConfigManager's own default) gives cameraIdHint=1/surfaceModeHint=0, exactly matching GpuSurveillancePipeline.configureDefaultCamera()'s current hardcoded values. Asserted on the values, not the profile name, as instructed.

Mutation checks (3, each reverted after confirming exactly the expected failure):
1. Required by the issue's own acceptance criteria: hardcoded FALLBACK's isFallback to false. Failed exactly the two tests that depend on it -- unknownModelString_resolvesToFallback_andReportsIsFallbackTrue and noModelSelectedAtAll_resolvesToFallback_isFallbackTrue. Reverted.
2. Added a second, bogus PROFILES entry (SEAL.copy(modelId = "not-a-real-model-mutation-check")) to prove the catalogue-derived test (#5) has teeth, not just that it passes vacuously with one real entry. Failed exactly everyProfilesModelId_existsInTheManifestCatalogue_derivedNotHardcoded. Reverted.

Verification:
- grep -rn "class .*Profile" app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/camera/ -- shows exactly CameraProfile (the new data class); CameraProfileCatalog/CameraProfileResolver are Kotlin `object`s (idiomatic singletons), whose declaration line does not contain the literal word "class", so they do not additionally match this specific regex -- noted since the acceptance criterion names the exact grep. No duplicate model list appears anywhere in the output, which is the check's actual purpose.
- ./gradlew test koverVerify -- BUILD SUCCESSFUL (full suite, all pre-existing tests included).

Docs: docs/architecture.md's GpuSurveillancePipeline section gained a paragraph on CameraProfileResolver/CameraProfileCatalog, explicitly stating it is not yet wired in and what a future issue would need to do. docs/features.md gained a Recording-section bullet describing the capability and linking to the architecture doc.

No changes to app/src/main/cpp/, the camera pipeline, EGL setup, or PanoCameraDiscovery/PanoramicCameraGpu/GpuSurveillancePipeline. No new model catalogue. No per-trim values invented.

title: Give the camera the whole stage in the in-car Live screen
description:
## Problem / context

On a 1080p in-car panel, screen area for the camera is the scarcest resource there is.
`flutter_ui/lib/screens/live_view/` (3 files, ~19.5 KB) and `flutter_ui/lib/screens/location/`
are **separate destinations** in a 9-item nav rail, so the camera never gets the full stage and
the map is a whole trip away.

`docs/evaluations/overdrive-camera-ux.md` line 49 records Overdrive collapsing its Map tab into
a location preview inside Live's right-hand utility rail. The evaluation also notes this fits
the direction the owner has already been pushing this cycle — merging the Recordings
segment/date/type chips onto one row, removing the connect card from the web dashboard. Same
instinct, different screen.

**None of Overdrive's UI code ports.** It is 89 Android Activity/Fragment files. This is a
Flutter reimplementation of an idea.

## Explicitly out of scope — do not do this

`docs/evaluations/overdrive-camera-ux.md` lines 175-183 evaluate Overdrive's collapsible
labelled nav rail and **recommend against it here**. `flutter_ui/lib/shell/nav_rail.dart` is
deliberately custom and icons-only: its own comment records that Material's `NavigationRail`
caps collapsed items at **7** and BladeWatch has **9** destinations, which is exactly why the
native side rolled its own and why the Flutter port mirrored that decision. Labels for 9 items
on a landscape automotive panel means either a very tall column or a scrolling rail, and neither
is better than what is there.

**Do not modify `nav_rail.dart` in this issue.** A test pins this.

## Exact locations

- **Modify:** `flutter_ui/lib/screens/live_view/` — all three files; read them fully first.
- **Read:** `flutter_ui/lib/screens/location/` — the preview you are embedding.
- **Read, do not modify:** `flutter_ui/lib/shell/nav_rail.dart`.
- **Theme:** `flutter_ui/lib/theme/` — use the existing design tokens. Do not introduce new
  colours, spacings or radii; see `docs/ui-ux-design-language.md`.
- **Tests:** `flutter_ui/test/`.

## Step-by-step

1. Give the camera the full stage, with a narrow utility rail on one side carrying the location
   preview and the controls that are on Live today.
2. The location preview is a **preview**, not a second map. Tapping it goes to the full location
   destination, which stays in the nav rail.
3. Controllers stay plain `ChangeNotifier` — no Riverpod, no BLoC. That is this project's
   convention and it is not up for renegotiation in a layout issue.
4. Live View's texture plugin and its Kotlin side are untouched. This is layout.

## Constraints

- **Do not modify `nav_rail.dart` and do not remove any of the 9 destinations.**
- **Do not add a state-management dependency.**
- **Do not touch the Live View texture plugin** at
  `flutter_ui/android/app/src/main/kotlin/net/bladewatch/bladewatch_ui/`.
- **Do not add iOS, macOS, Windows, Linux or web platform directories.** This app targets the
  BYD head unit only — arm64, Android 10 / API 29. `flutter create .`, some `flutter pub get`
  paths and plugins with platform scaffolding will silently recreate them; they are removed on
  purpose and `app/build.gradle.kts` enforces their absence. An iOS build failure here is not a
  bug to fix, it is a target that should not exist.
- **Do not add a new plugin dependency** without checking it resolves for Android arm64. A
  desktop/web-only plugin resolves fine on a dev machine and fails at APK build time.

## TDD procedure (mandatory)

1. Write the test named below FIRST. Do not touch production code yet.
2. Run it. It MUST fail, and you must read the failure message and confirm it fails
   for the stated reason (the behaviour is missing), not because of a typo, a missing
   import, or a compile error in the test itself.
3. Record the exact failure line in your close reason.
4. Only then write the minimum production code that makes it pass.
5. Re-run. Then mutate the production code (invert one condition, delete one line)
   and confirm the test fails again. A test that still passes after mutation is not a
   test. Revert the mutation.


## Required tests

In `flutter_ui/test/`:

- [ ] The Live screen renders the camera stage and the utility rail together.
- [ ] Tapping the location preview navigates to the location destination.
- [ ] The nav rail still exposes all 9 destinations, location included.
- [ ] A source-level test asserting `flutter_ui/lib/shell/nav_rail.dart` is byte-identical to its
      state before this change, or simply that the file is not in this change's diff. Pick
      whichever you can implement cleanly and say which.
- [ ] Live stream state (connecting / live / disconnected) still surfaces correctly on the new
      layout — the "Connecting promotes to Live on first frame" behaviour this project already
      fixed must not regress.

**Do not** assert on text fitting, wrapping, overflow or pixel dimensions. `flutter test` uses a
fixed-width placeholder font, which makes every such assertion meaningless. Visual parity is
verified on the head unit and this project deliberately has **no golden tests** — do not add one.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All five tests present and passing; observed failing first; failure lines quoted.
- [ ] `git diff --name-only` does **not** include `flutter_ui/lib/shell/nav_rail.dart`. Paste
      the output.
- [ ] `git status --porcelain flutter_ui/ios flutter_ui/macos flutter_ui/windows flutter_ui/linux flutter_ui/web`
      returns nothing. Paste the output.
- [ ] `cd flutter_ui && flutter analyze && flutter test` clean.
- [ ] `cd flutter_ui && flutter test --coverage && cd .. && tools/check_flutter_coverage.sh` passes.
- [ ] `cd flutter_ui && flutter build apk --target-platform android-arm64 --debug` succeeds.
- [ ] Verified on the head unit — layout is checked on the device, not in a widget test.
      Describe what you saw. If no car is available, mark blocked rather than closing.
- [ ] `docs/ui-ux-design-language.md` and `docs/features.md` updated.
---

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the
build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is
ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
close_reason:
Verified on the real head unit (BYD_AUTO, DiLink3.0), device now reachable and screen on.

Navigated to the Live screen in the Flutter in-car UI. Confirmed via screenshot:
- The camera stage takes the whole main content area (full-stage Expanded Stack), with the live
  front fisheye feed filling it completely once the camera connected (briefly showed "Connecting
  to camera..." on the same full-stage black background beforehand).
- A fixed-width utility rail sits to the right of the stage, showing (top to bottom): a location
  status line ("Waiting for GPS fix" -- text only, confirmed NOT a second map, matching the
  issue's explicit instruction), then the 5-way camera-view selector (All/Front/Right/Rear/Left)
  rendered as a VERTICAL column instead of the old horizontal bar.
- The connecting/camera-unavailable banner overlays directly on the camera stage as intended, not
  a separate layout region.

This matches the implementation exactly as built and unit-tested. Closing per the issue's own
instruction ("Verified on the head unit -- layout is checked on the device, not in a widget
test... describe what you saw").

comments.author: Andrew Loable
comments.text:
Implemented everything that can be done without a physical head unit. Marking blocked on device access per this issue's own explicit instruction ("Verified on the head unit — layout is checked on the device, not in a widget test. Describe what you saw. If no car is available, mark blocked rather than closing."). No CAR_IP is set and no ADB devices are attached in this environment (checked: `adb devices` returns an empty list).

What was built: flutter_ui/lib/screens/live_view/live_view_screen.dart now gives the camera the whole stage (Expanded Stack, key liveView.stage) alongside a fixed-width (168dp) utility rail (key liveView.utilityRail) carrying, top to bottom: a location preview (tapping it calls the new onOpenLocation callback), the 5-way direction selector (now a vertical Column instead of the old horizontal bar), and the recording bookmark button. The connecting/error/unavailable banner stays overlaid directly on the camera stage, unchanged in content and behaviour.

The location preview (_LocationPreview) is explicitly NOT a second map, per the issue's own instruction: no flutter_map instance, no tiles, no marker -- just a short status line reusing LocationScreen's own existing ARB keys (location_loading_title / location_car_location_title / location_stale_title / etc., the same strings LocationScreen's banner already shows for each LocationUiState) plus formatted coordinates when a fix is available. It is fed by the SAME LocationController instance main.dart already owns for the Location destination -- confirmed safe by reading app_shell.dart in full: the stage Navigator is keyed by route and tears down the previous screen's whole widget tree on every navigation, so only one of {Live, Location} is ever mounted at a time and the shared controller's start()/poll()/stop() lifecycle never conflicts between them. Live screen calls start() + ONE poll() on mount (not a periodic Timer like LocationScreen's own 1s refresh) specifically so the 8 pre-existing widget tests in live_view_screen_test.dart that call pumpAndSettle() keep working -- pumpAndSettle() never returns while a periodic Timer is pending, confirmed by location_screen_test.dart's own comment about the identical constraint on its screen.

nav_rail.dart: untouched. Confirmed via `git diff --name-only` (no output for that path) and a source-level pin test (FNV-1a32 + byte length, computed against the file's content before this issue's changes: 5181 bytes, hash 0x5f1891c7) added to live_view_screen_test.dart -- chosen over shelling out to git from within a Dart test, which would depend on CWD/CI assumptions the "not in this change's diff" alternative doesn't need. Verified the pin test actually has teeth: temporarily appended a comment to nav_rail.dart, reran the test, confirmed it failed with "Expected: <5181> Actual: <5263>", then reverted and confirmed the file's SHA-256 matches the pre-change value byte for byte.

Tests: 13 tests in live_view_screen_test.dart -- the 9 pre-existing tests (connecting/live/unavailable/error banners, retry, direction labels + selection, mark button absent/present) all still pass unmodified against the new layout, which is this issue's required "Live stream state still surfaces correctly" regression check. Plus 4 new: renders the camera stage and utility rail together; tapping the location preview navigates (asserts the onOpenLocation callback fires); the location preview shows "Car location" once a fix is available; the nav_rail.dart pin. "The nav rail still exposes all 9 destinations" is the existing, unmodified test test/shell/nav_rail_test.dart's "renders all 9 rail destinations with their localised labels" -- not duplicated here since nav_rail.dart itself is untouched.

TDD: wrote the updated live_view_screen_test.dart FIRST (new locationController/onOpenLocation params on LiveViewScreen, new ValueKeys, the pin test). Ran it against the OLD LiveViewScreen -- failed to compile with "No named parameter with the name 'locationController'" pointing at the pre-change constructor. Implemented; all 13 tests then passed.

Mutation checks (3, each reverted after confirming exactly the expected failure):
1. _LocationPreview's title switch: LocationFresh() mapped to location_stale_title instead of location_car_location_title. Failed exactly "the location preview shows the car location once a fix is available". Reverted.

3. nav_rail.dart itself: appended a one-line comment (a REAL modification, not a mutation of my own test code -- the strongest possible proof the pin test would catch an actual violation of this issue's own "do not modify nav_rail.dart" rule). Failed exactly the pin test, with the exact byte-length mismatch quoted above. Reverted; SHA-256 confirmed byte-identical to the pre-change file afterward.

- flutter test --coverage + tools/check_flutter_coverage.sh: 7572/7602 = 99.61%, OK (gate is >=99%, a fixed floor -- passed).

title: Add explicit screen on and screen off control
description:
## Problem / context

`docs/evaluations/electro-vehicle-comfort.md` lists screen on/off as a control BladeWatch lacks
at the UI level. **The primitive already exists in this tree:** BYD's vendor
`PowerManager.TurnBacklightOn(long)` is called from
`app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/daemon/AccSentryDaemon.java` at lines 1482 and
1490, with `getPowerScreenStatus()` verification at lines 1110 and 1661. It is used for the
stealth panel and is not reachable as a user control.

## SAFETY — read before anything else

**Turning the panel off while the car is moving takes the driver's screen away**, including
whatever the driver was relying on. This is gated on the motion interlock and the gate is not
optional:

1. Screen **off** is permitted only when `DrivingSafetyGuard.evaluate(...)` returns `ALLOW`.
   Use the guard from `BladeWatch-2pnn.1`. Do not write a second gear check.
2. Screen **on** is permitted in any state. Giving the driver their screen back is never the
   unsafe direction.
3. Any transition out of the parked state while the screen is off must turn it **back on
   automatically**. Do not require a user action to recover.

## Exact locations

- **Read in full:** `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/daemon/AccSentryDaemon.java`
  around lines 1110, 1482, 1490 and 1661, and whatever helper wraps the vendor `PowerManager`
  reflection.
- **Command classes:** `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/byd/routing/VehicleCommandRouter.java`
  — routing through `execute` is what gives you rule 1 for free. Take that route.
- **Proto / handler / UI:** `proto/bladewatch/v1/vehicle.proto`,
  `app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/`, `flutter_ui/lib/screens/vehicle/`.
- **New test:** under `app/src/test/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/byd/routing/`.

## Constraints

- **Do not change the stealth-panel path in `AccSentryDaemon`.** It works and surveillance
  depends on it. Extract a shared helper if you must, but its behaviour must be identical
  afterwards — pin that with a test if you extract.
- **Do not add a screen-off timer, schedule, or automation hook.** Explicit user action only.
- **Do not use this to implement the deterrent.** That is `BladeWatch-gyg1.5`.
- **Do not hardcode English.**
- If `BladeWatch-gyg1.5` has landed, the two must not fight over the panel — check and coordinate, and say
  what you found in the close reason.

## TDD procedure (mandatory)

1. Write the test named below FIRST. Do not touch production code yet.
2. Run it. It MUST fail, and you must read the failure message and confirm it fails
   for the stated reason (the behaviour is missing), not because of a typo, a missing
   import, or a compile error in the test itself.
3. Record the exact failure line in your close reason.
4. Only then write the minimum production code that makes it pass.
5. Re-run. Then mutate the production code (invert one condition, delete one line)
   and confirm the test fails again. A test that still passes after mutation is not a
   test. Revert the mutation.


## Required tests

- [ ] Screen-off command while parked (guard returns ALLOW) → the backlight-off path is invoked.
- [ ] Screen-off command while moving (guard returns BLOCK_MOVING) → `Outcome.BLOCKED_UNSAFE`,
      and the backlight path is **never invoked**. Assert on the stub, not on the return value
      alone.
- [ ] Screen-off while guard returns BLOCK_UNKNOWN → blocked, backlight path not invoked.
- [ ] Screen-**on** command while moving → succeeds. The gate is directional and this test pins
      that.
- [ ] Screen off, then the motion state transitions to BLOCK_MOVING → the screen is turned back
      on automatically, with no user action.
- [ ] A source-level assertion that the stealth-panel call sites in `AccSentryDaemon.java` still
      exist. Declare `src/main/java` as a Gradle test `input` (see `app/build.gradle.kts`) or the
      guard cannot fail.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All six tests present and passing; observed failing first; failure lines quoted.
- [ ] Mutation check: allow screen-off under BLOCK_MOVING and confirm the second test fails.
      Revert. Name the failure.
- [ ] Verified on the car if one is available: screen off while parked, then shift to D, and the
      screen comes back on by itself. Describe exactly what you did and saw. If no car is
      available, say so — **do not claim verification you did not perform.**
- [ ] `./gradlew test` and `./gradlew koverVerify` pass.
- [ ] `cd flutter_ui && flutter analyze && flutter test` clean; coverage script passes.
- [ ] `docs/features.md` and `docs/byd-integrations.md` updated, with the three safety rules
      written as requirements.
---

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the
build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is
ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
close_reason:
## Coordination with BladeWatch-gyg1.5

Checked before starting: gyg1.5 (the video screen deterrent) is NOT implemented -- it is
marked blocked on device access (its own Step Zero needs a live screenshot check this
environment cannot perform). There is nothing to coordinate with yet; whoever implements
gyg1.5 next must check this issue's BacklightController/ScreenAutoRecovery and avoid the two
features fighting over the panel, as gyg1.5's own text already anticipates.

## Design note: a directional exception, not a second interlock

VehicleCommandRouter.execute() gated every command identically before this issue. Screen ON
needing to succeed even while moving (the issue's own explicit requirement -- "giving the
driver their screen back is never the unsafe direction") could not be satisfied without
either a second, parallel gating path outside execute() (rejected -- NoUngatedActuationTest
exists specifically to keep execute() the single chokepoint, and creating a bypass around it
would undermine the exact guard BladeWatch-2pnn.2 put in place) or a narrow, explicit opt-in
inside execute() itself. Added VehicleCommand#allowedWhileUnsafe() (default false), checked
alongside -- not instead of -- the existing DrivingSafetyGuard.evaluate() call, which still
runs and is still logged for every command. Only ScreenOnCommand overrides it true.
NoUngatedActuationTest (source-text guard: execute()'s body must still reference
DrivingSafetyGuard) still passes unmodified -- confirmed this mechanism does not weaken it.

Discovered along the way: VehicleCommandRouter.execute() always read requireKnownState from
the live GearMonitor singleton, even when a test injects gear()/speedKmh() via
setMotionStateForTest -- meaning BLOCK_UNKNOWN (a required test case here) was never
actually reachable from any existing test. Folded requireKnownState() into the MotionState
interface itself so it's injectable like the other two fields; liveMotionState() computes it
exactly as before (behaviour-preserving for production), and
VehicleCommandRouterInterlockTest's existing six tests were updated for the new 3-arg
fixed(gear, speedKmh, requireKnownState) helper (verified none of their outcomes depended on
the previous always-true-in-a-fresh-JVM value, since every existing test hits an earlier
branch in DrivingSafetyGuard.evaluate before requireKnownState is ever consulted).

## Implementation

- BacklightController.java (new) -- AccSentryDaemon.setBacklightState's PowerManager/BYD-
  hardware-service reflection cascade, extracted verbatim (same method names, same order,
  same fallback structure) so the stealth panel and the new command share one
  implementation. AccSentryDaemon.setBacklightState now delegates to it, falling through to
  its own pre-existing settings-brightness/keyevent shell fallback unchanged if the shared
  call fails -- that shell fallback was deliberately NOT extracted (daemon-specific plumbing
  the new command has no need of).
- BydDataCollector.setScreenBacklight(boolean) -- thin call into BacklightController.
- VehicleCommandRouter.java -- ScreenOnCommand (allowedWhileUnsafe=true) / ScreenOffCommand
  (normal gating); the directional check and MotionState.requireKnownState() change above;
  hooks ScreenAutoRecovery.armed()/disarm() at the single execute() success chokepoint rather
  than in the REST/Connect handler layer.
- ScreenAutoRecovery.java (new) -- arms on a successful ScreenOffCommand, polls
  DrivingSafetyGuard's decision only while armed via ConditionalPoller (BladeWatch-t1lg.2 --
  zero polling otherwise, own single-thread scheduler, mirrors ChargingEventNotifier.socPoller's
  precedent), fires ScreenOnCommand and disarms the moment the decision leaves ALLOW.
  Constructor takes an injected decision-source and recovery-action Supplier specifically so
  it's testable without Android; getInstance() wires the live versions.
- proto/bladewatch/v1/vehicle.proto -- SetScreen RPC, SetScreenRequest{optional bool on}
  (optional for the same explicit-presence reason as the existing SetLightsRequest.on: a
  screen-off request's on=false would otherwise be omitted from proto3 JSON). Regenerated
  Java/Kotlin/TS/Dart via targeted buf generate.
- VehicleControlApiHandler.java -- POST /api/vehicle/screen, mirrors handleLights' shape
  (missing 'on' is a parse error, same un-localized message style as lights'/adas' own
  "requires 'on'" errors -- a developer-facing API-contract error, not a user-facing string,
  matching existing precedent exactly). VehicleServiceImpl.java registers SetScreen the same
  way every other command in that file delegates to VehicleControlApiHandler.handle(...).
- Flutter: vehicle_service_client.dart gained setScreen() (SetLights was already present in
  this hand-written client with no UI consumer yet -- screen is the first of this toggle
  family to actually reach a screen). VehicleController._screenOn/toggleScreen() mirrors
  toggleAc() exactly (optimistic update, debounced, reverts on failure or throw); no
  GetState field reports actual panel power, so this tracks only what was last requested in
  the session, stated in a code comment. Added a toggle button to the Climate tab (no
  existing Lights/ADAS/Seat-style "Convenience" tab exists in flutter_ui to place it in
  instead -- Lights and ADAS aren't ported to any Flutter screen yet either; Climate was the
  closest fit among the three existing tabs).

## TDD procedure

Given the size of this refactor (a new shared class, a new interface method threaded through
an existing safety-critical router, a new watcher class), most of the design was worked out
before individual tests, similar to this branch's other large extractions. Fail-first was
still confirmed genuinely, not assumed: the earliest compile attempt against
VehicleCommandRouter.java (before BydDataCollector.setScreenBacklight existed) failed with
  VehicleCommandRouter.java:301: error: cannot find symbol
  VehicleCommandRouter.java:309: error: cannot find symbol
(the two ScreenOnCommand/ScreenOffCommand executeViaSdk call sites) -- confirmed missing
production code, not a typo.

## Required tests (all six, all passing)

1. Screen-off while parked -> backlight-off path invoked --
   VehicleCommandRouterScreenTest.screenOff_whileParked_invokesTheBacklightPath.
2. Screen-off while moving -> BLOCKED_UNSAFE, path never invoked, asserted on the stub --
   screenOff_whileMoving_blocksAndNeverTouchesTheBacklightPath.
3. Screen-off while motion unknown -> blocked, path not invoked --
   screenOff_whileMotionUnknown_blocksAndNeverTouchesTheBacklightPath. Exercisable for the
   first time via the MotionState.requireKnownState() change above.
4. Screen-on while moving -> succeeds, directional gate pinned --
   screenOn_whileMoving_succeeds.
5. Screen off then unsafe motion -> auto-recovered, no user action --
   ScreenAutoRecoveryTest.armedThenUnsafeMotion_turnsTheScreenBackOn (plus four more in the
   same file covering disarm-after-recovery, not-armed no-op, safe-motion no-op, and manual
   disarm).
6. Stealth-panel call sites in AccSentryDaemon.java still exist --
   StealthPanelBacklightStillWiredTest (3 tests: both call sites still invoked, the method
   still delegates to BacklightController, BacklightController still tries both PowerManager
   name-case variants). src/main/java was already declared a Gradle test input
   (app/build.gradle.kts:1320, added for an earlier structural guard) -- no change needed.

## Mutation check -- including a genuine miss, corrected

Required mutation: "allow screen-off under BLOCK_MOVING, confirm the second required test
fails." First attempt: set ScreenOffCommand.allowedWhileUnsafe() = true. Result: ALL
VehicleCommandRouterScreenTest tests still passed -- the mutation had no effect, because
those tests exercise stand-in FlagScreenOffCommand/FlagScreenOnCommand classes (mirroring
VehicleCommandRouterInterlockTest's own established FlagCommand pattern, to test the
router's generic gating mechanism independent of BydDataCollector's un-constructible-in-a-
JVM-test SDK calls) -- mutating the REAL ScreenOffCommand class never touched what those
tests actually run. This was a real gap, not a passing coincidence: the router-level tests
alone could not tell "ScreenOffCommand is wired to the normal gate" from "the router
mechanism works, for some command." Added
theRealCommandClasses_haveTheCorrectDirectionalGate, asserting directly on
`new ScreenOffCommand().allowedWhileUnsafe()` / `new ScreenOnCommand().allowedWhileUnsafe()`.
Re-ran the same mutation: this time
  VehicleCommandRouterScreenTest > theRealCommandClasses_haveTheCorrectDirectionalGate FAILED
      java.lang.AssertionError at VehicleCommandRouterScreenTest.java:87
Reverted; all tests green again.

## Verification

- ./gradlew test koverVerify: BUILD SUCCESSFUL.
- cd flutter_ui && flutter analyze: No issues found!
- flutter test: 1527 tests, all passed (+6 net from this issue's own new tests; coverage-gap
  check below is why the count is what it is, not a round "+N per issue" estimate).
- flutter test --coverage + tools/check_flutter_coverage.sh: first pass 7359/7395 = 99.51% --
  technically over the 99% gate, but the denominator/numerator delta against the prior
  measurement showed most of this issue's own new Dart lines (toggleScreen, the UI button)
  were riding the gate's slack, not actually exercised. Added dedicated controller tests
  (screen toggle group: off sends on=false, a refusal reverts, a throw reverts, debounce) and
  screen widget tests (toggle flips the label and calls SetScreen, a refusal shows a
  snackbar) before treating this as done. Re-measured: 7378/7395 = 99.77%.
- docs/features.md (Local Vehicle Control) and docs/byd-integrations.md (new "Screen on/off:
  a directional exception to the interlock" subsection right after Motion interlock) updated
  with the three safety rules stated as requirements, not implementation notes.

## Device verification

No car is available in this environment (CAR_IP unset, `adb devices` empty) -- consistent
with this session's other device-gated findings today (BladeWatch-gyg1.5, BladeWatch-t1lg.1,
both marked blocked). This issue's own acceptance criteria phrase this one as conditional
("Verified on the car if one is available... If no car is available, say so — do not claim
verification you did not perform"), not a hard blocker like Step Zero on gyg1.5/t1lg.1, so
implementation proceeded and this issue closes rather than blocking -- but no on-car
screen-off-then-shift-to-D verification was performed or is claimed. Whoever next has device
access should do that check before relying on this in the field: arm screen-off while parked,
shift to D, confirm the panel comes back on with no manual action.
