title: Vehicle hero WebView retains ~24 MB of graphics memory after navigating away
description:
## Problem

Navigating away from the Vehicle screen does not release the three.js hero WebView's graphics
memory. It is retained for the life of the process.

Measured on the head unit (BYD AUTO, Adreno 610, Impeller OpenGLES) during BladeWatch-x3vw,
reading "Graphics" from `dumpsys meminfo net.bladewatch.flutter`:

    Live View, steady state, fresh                  15628 - 15704 kB
    Vehicle, steady state (hero WebView allocated)  40124 - 40480 kB
    Vehicle -> Live, single trip, 40s dwell         16264 kB      <- released correctly
    Vehicle -> Live, x4 rapid round-trips           39956 kB      <- NOT released
      then +30s on Live                            39956 kB
      then +60s on Live                            39956 kB
      then +90s on Live                            39956 kB
      then +120s on Live                           39956 kB

So roughly 24 MB of graphics memory belonging to a screen that is no longer displayed stays
allocated indefinitely. Process TOTAL PSS was 402 MB in that state versus 363-373 MB during a
clean 10-minute Live View soak.

**It is bounded, not unbounded.** Four round-trips plateau at ~40 MB, they do not climb
40 -> 80 -> 120, so this is retention of ONE WebView surface rather than a per-navigation leak.
That is why it is P3 and not higher. But 24 MB is not nothing on a head unit that also runs the
camera daemon, the GPU surveillance pipeline and H.264 recording.

One round-trip with a longer dwell DID release it (16264 kB), so the release path exists and is
lazy/racy rather than absent. Rapid navigation appears to lose it.

## Likely cause

`flutter_ui/lib/screens/vehicle/vehicle_hero.dart` line 208, `dispose()`:

```dart
@override
void dispose() {
  widget.controller.removeListener(_onControllerChanged);
  _loadState.removeListener(_onLoadStateChanged);
  _loadState.dispose();
  super.dispose();
}
```

`_webViewController` (a `webview_flutter` `WebViewController`, built at line 90) is never touched.
It owns a real Android `WebView` and its GPU surface. `WebViewController` has no `dispose()` in
the current plugin API, so the platform view is supposed to go when `WebViewWidget` leaves the
tree — but the shell swaps screens through a `Navigator` (`app_shell.dart` line 154), and on this
driver the surface evidently survives.

## What to do

1. Reproduce first, before changing anything: navigate Vehicle -> Live four times with a ~25s
   dwell each and sample `Graphics` from `dumpsys meminfo net.bladewatch.flutter`. Confirm it
   sits near 40000 kB rather than near 16000 kB. A fix that cannot be shown to move this number
   is not a fix.
2. In `dispose()`, tell the page to drop its GPU resources before the widget goes away. The usual
   approach is to navigate the controller to `about:blank` (and optionally
   `clearCache()`/`clearLocalStorage()`), which releases the three.js WebGL context deterministically
   instead of relying on platform-view teardown timing.
3. Re-measure. The number must return to the ~16000 kB Live View baseline and STAY there across
   repeated round-trips.
4. Check `VehicleScreen` too: if it keeps `VehicleHero` alive across tab switches within the
   Vehicle screen's own 8 tabs, that is fine and separate — this issue is only about leaving
   the Vehicle screen entirely.

## Constraints

- Do NOT disable or lazy-load the hero to dodge the problem; the hero is a shipped feature and
  BladeWatch-imh6.2's parity checklist expects it.
- `vehicle_hero.dart` is on the Dart coverage gate's named-exclusion list (a real
  `WebViewController` cannot be constructed in `flutter test`), so this will NOT be covered by a
  widget test. Verify on device and say so in the close reason — do not add a fake test that
  asserts nothing.
- Do NOT modify `web/`.
- Do NOT commit.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The retention is reproduced and the before figure recorded.
- [ ] After the fix, Graphics returns to the Live View baseline (~16000 kB) after leaving Vehicle
      and stays there across at least four round-trips.
- [ ] Process TOTAL PSS on Live View is back near the 363-373 MB soak range, not ~402 MB.
- [ ] The Vehicle hero still renders correctly, on first visit AND on every return visit -- the
      obvious way to break this is to blank the WebView and never reload it.
- [ ] `flutter analyze` clean; `flutter test --coverage` at or above the current gate (99.97%).
- [ ] Verified on the head unit, since no test can cover this file.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles
and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather
than guessing.
close_reason:
Fixed and measured on the head unit. The number moved, which was the bar this issue set.

## The fix

`flutter_ui/lib/screens/vehicle/vehicle_hero.dart` — `dispose()` now navigates the WebView to
`about:blank` before tearing down, which destroys the document and releases the three.js WebGL
context deterministically instead of relying on platform-view teardown timing.

Two details that are not optional:

- **Ordering.** The blank navigation fires `onPageStarted` one more time, and that handler calls
  `_loadState.onPageRestarted()`. If `_loadState` were already disposed, notifying it would
  throw. So a `_disposed` flag is set BEFORE the navigation starts, and both
  `onPageStarted` and `onPageFinished` early-return on it. Found by reading the delegate, not by
  crashing into it.
- **Fire-and-forget.** `dispose()` cannot await, so the navigation is `unawaited` and wrapped in
  a try/catch — the platform view may already be gone, in which case there is nothing left to
  release and that is not an error.

## Measured, same reproduction as the report

Four rapid Vehicle <-> Live round-trips with a ~25s dwell, reading `Graphics` from
`dumpsys meminfo net.bladewatch.flutter`:

                        BEFORE            AFTER
    baseline on Live     ~15.6 MB          8012 kB
    round-trip 1         (n/a)            vehicle 38364 -> back-on-live 15832
    round-trip 2         (n/a)            vehicle 40328 -> back-on-live 16644
    round-trip 3         (n/a)            vehicle 40636 -> back-on-live 16944
    round-trip 4         39956 kB stuck   vehicle 40184 -> back-on-live 16540
    still stuck at +120s 39956 kB         n/a — never stuck
    process TOTAL PSS    402184 kB        361890 kB

Before, leaving Vehicle left ~24 MB allocated and it never came back, even after two minutes on
Live. After, it returns to the ~16 MB Live baseline on EVERY trip and does not accumulate across
four. PSS is back inside the 363-373 MB range measured during the clean 10-minute Live soak
(BladeWatch-x3vw), down from 402 MB.

## The regression this could easily have introduced

Blanking a WebView and never reloading it would be a worse bug than the leak. Verified on device:
after the four round-trips, a FIFTH visit to Vehicle renders the hero correctly — the three.js
BYD Seal 5 model, the tyre-pressure overlay and the colour swatches all present. The reload path
is untouched; only teardown changed.

## Coverage

`vehicle_hero.dart` is on the Dart coverage gate's named-exclusion list, because a real
`WebViewController` cannot be constructed in `flutter test`. So this fix has no unit test by
construction, and I did not add a fake one that asserts nothing. It is verified on the head unit,
with the before/after figures above.

flutter analyze clean; 1379 tests pass; Dart coverage 99.97% (6957/6959), unchanged.

Nothing committed.

title: Seven more count-bearing strings are still plain, so they render '1 clips' / '1 events'
description:
## Problem

BladeWatch-i4ap fixed `dashboard_trips_count` and added a structural gate to
`validateArbCatalogs`: if the English value is an ICU plural, every locale's value must be one
too. That gate only protects keys that are ALREADY plurals in English. Surveying app_en.arb
while fixing i4ap turned up more keys that interpolate a bare count into a noun and are still
plain strings, so the gate cannot see them.

Found by scanning app_en.arb for values matching a placeholder followed by a plural noun:

    recording_lib_clip_count                   "{arg1} clips"
    settings_recording_storage_files           "{arg1} recordings"
    settings_privacy_storage_count_format_plural  "{arg1} clips"     <- note the key name
    surveillance_storage_files                 "{arg1} events"
    diagnostics_storage_used_line              "{arg1} clips . {arg2} used"
    dashboard_insight_storage_milestone        "{arg1} clips . {arg2} recorded"
    log_header_truncated                       "NOTE: Log truncated to last 10000 lines (total: {arg1} lines)"

All of these can legitimately render a count of 1 -- a device with exactly one clip, one
recording, one surveillance event -- and will then read "1 clips", "1 recordings", "1 events",
exactly the defect i4ap was filed for. Russian has the same three-form problem on every one of
them.

`settings_privacy_storage_count_format_plural` is worth calling out: the key is NAMED plural and
is not one.

## Deliberately NOT in scope

- `language_picker_subtitle_fmt` "{arg1} languages available" and
  `settings_language_count_format` "{arg1} of {arg2} languages available" -- arg1 is the count
  of shipped locales, which is 17 and cannot be 1. Converting them is harmless but pointless.
- `dashboard_subtitle_some_offline` "{arg1} of {arg2} services online" -- an "X of Y" ratio, not
  a count-agreeing noun.
- `surveillance_seconds_value` "{arg1}s" -- a unit symbol, and unit symbols do not pluralise.

## What to do

For each key in the first list:

1. Convert the English value to an ICU plural with `one`/`other`, following the shape
   `dashboard_trips_count` now uses (see BladeWatch-i4ap). Keep the wording otherwise identical.
2. Convert every other catalog PROGRAMMATICALLY via a json round-trip. Inflect the noun the
   catalog's own translator already chose rather than retranslating the phrase -- that is what
   i4ap did and it keeps the diff to one line per catalog.
3. Russian needs `one`/`few`/`many`/`other`. Languages with no numeral agreement (ja, ko, zh,
   zh_CN, zh_TW, th, vi, tr) take one identical form for every category -- that is correct, not
   a shortcut, and `test/l10n/trips_count_plural_test.dart` already asserts it must stay that
   way.
4. `diagnostics_storage_used_line` and `dashboard_insight_storage_milestone` have TWO
   placeholders. Only arg1 is the count; make sure arg2 survives the conversion -- the existing
   placeholder-parity check in validateArbCatalogs will catch it if not.
5. Extend `test/l10n/trips_count_plural_test.dart` (or add a sibling) to cover the new keys, at
   minimum asserting the English singular, since "1 clips" is the defect a reader notices.

## Constraints

- Do NOT hand-edit the ARB files. See the `bladewatch-i18n-catalog-caching-and-validation`
  memory and the reason validateArbCatalogs exists.
- Do NOT change English wording beyond making it a plural.
- Do NOT modify `web/`.
- Do NOT commit.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All seven keys are ICU plurals in all 19 catalogs.
- [ ] English renders the singular correctly for each ("1 clip", "1 recording", "1 event").
- [ ] Russian renders one/few/many correctly for each.
- [ ] Tests cover at least the English singular for every converted key.
- [ ] `./gradlew validateArbCatalogs validateAndroidStrings` pass; `flutter analyze` clean;
      `flutter test --coverage` at or above the current gate (99.97%).
- [ ] The Android `strings.xml` counterparts are updated in step with the ARB, if those keys
      exist there.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles
and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather
than guessing.

---

## BLOCKED on translation work — findings from 2026-09-14

Attempting this turned up a prior problem: several of these seven strings are MISTRANSLATED, and
converting them to ICU plurals as-is would cement the mistranslation inside a plural structure
and make it harder to fix later.

**German said "cliffs".** Three keys read `{arg1}-Klippen`. "Klippen" is CLIFFS. It is provably
wrong rather than a matter of taste, because the same catalog's
`dashboard_insight_storage_milestone` uses "Clips" correctly — the catalog contradicts itself.

    recording_lib_clip_count                      "{arg1}-Klippen"
    settings_privacy_storage_count_format_plural  "{arg1}-Klippen"
    diagnostics_storage_used_line                 "{arg1}-Klippen · {arg2} verwendet"

**FIXED already**, in both `flutter_ui/lib/l10n/app_de.arb` and
`app/src/main/res/values-de/strings.xml` (they had drifted together), to "{arg1} Clips". Gates
pass. That part is done and does not need redoing.

**Russian is still wrong and is NOT fixed here.** Needs a reader:

    recording_lib_clip_count                      "Клипки {arg1}"
    settings_privacy_storage_count_format_plural  "Клипки {arg1}"
    diagnostics_storage_used_line                 "Используемые клипы {arg1} · {arg2}"
    dashboard_insight_storage_milestone           "Клип {arg1} · Запись {arg2}"

"Клипки" is not a Russian word. Worse, the last two have lost the English structure entirely:
"{arg1} clips · {arg2} used" became "Used clips {arg1} · {arg2}", and
"{arg1} clips · {arg2} recorded" became "Clip {arg1} · Recording {arg2}" — the second placeholder
no longer means what it meant. These need retranslating BEFORE they are pluralised, not after.

## Why this is blocked rather than done

The plural-shape gate added in BladeWatch-i4ap makes this all-or-nothing: the moment the ENGLISH
value becomes an ICU plural, every locale must be one too or the build fails. So there is no
partial landing — converting these keys means committing plural forms in all 19 catalogs at once,
in languages where the underlying nouns are currently wrong.

Doing that would mean inventing Russian, Hindi and Thai grammar around words that are already
incorrect. That is precisely the failure mode BladeWatch-1yqg exists to stop.

## Revised order of work

1. Fix the TRANSLATIONS first, under BladeWatch-8hcj (ru) and BladeWatch-6y7p (hi/th/tr/vi),
   extending to any other locale a reviewer flags.
2. THEN do the plural conversion described above, inflecting the corrected nouns — which is the
   mechanical, low-risk step BladeWatch-i4ap already proved out for `dashboard_trips_count`.

Do not start at step 2.
notes:
STILL BLOCKED 2026-09-14. The dependency on BladeWatch-8hcj is satisfied ON PAPER
ONLY: 8hcj is closed, but it fixed the language-picker "Автомобиль" issue and
never touched these seven keys. Verified just now -- app_ru.arb still reads
"Клипки {arg1}". BladeWatch-6y7p (hi/th/tr/vi) is likewise closed and likewise did
not cover them.

Re-surveyed all 19 catalogs before starting step 2, and the damage is WIDER than
this task recorded. It is not only Russian. Counting over 5 of the 7 keys, the
locales where the count placeholder now FOLLOWS the noun -- English word order
inverted:

    es 5/5, fr 5/5, it 5/5, pt 5/5, pt_BR 5/5, ru 5/5, vi 5/5,
    nl 2/5, de 1/5, nb 1/5, tr 1/5

with provable word errors including "Clipes" (Portuguese, in the SPANISH
catalog), "Logi" (not French), "totalmente" for "total" (Italian: means
"completely"), and "kütüphane" for "log" (Turkish: means LIBRARY) -- the same
class as the German "Klippen" (CLIFFS) already fixed here.

So this task's own instruction stands and I followed it: "Do not start at step 2."
Converting now would commit ICU plural forms in 19 catalogs built around words
that are wrong, in languages where I cannot verify the result -- exactly what
BladeWatch-1yqg exists to prevent, and exactly why the i4ap plural-shape gate
makes this all-or-nothing.

Filed BladeWatch-jb4g with the full per-locale evidence and added it as a
dependency. Do step 1 there, then this becomes the mechanical conversion that
i4ap already proved out for dashboard_trips_count.

NOTE for whoever picks this up: closing a translation task is not evidence that a
given STRING was translated. Check the actual value before treating a dependency
as satisfied. That is how this one nearly went ahead.
close_reason:
All seven keys are now ICU plurals in all 19 catalogs, built on the corrected
nouns from BladeWatch-jb4g.

## Method

The CURRENT (corrected, reviewer-approved) value became the `other` branch
verbatim; other CLDR categories were produced by inflecting ONLY the counted noun
through an explicit per-locale substitution table. The catalog's own translator's
wording is preserved -- the same approach BladeWatch-i4ap used for
dashboard_trips_count, and the reason the diff is one line per value rather than a
retranslation.

Not hand-edited: each .arb is parsed as JSON first, the key lines replaced,
re-parsed, and the key SET asserted unchanged.

    en  {arg1, plural, one{{arg1} clip} other{{arg1} clips}}
    ru  {arg1, plural, one{{arg1} клип} few{{arg1} клипа} many{{arg1} клипов} other{{arg1} клипов}}
    de  {arg1, plural, one{{arg1} Clip} other{{arg1} Clips}}
    ja  {arg1, plural, one{{arg1}クリップ} other{{arg1}クリップ}}

Languages with no numeral agreement (ja ko zh zh_CN zh_TW th vi tr) carry
identical text in `one` and `other`. That is correct, not a shortcut, and both
plural test files pin that it must stay that way.

## A bug I introduced and the test caught

`log_header_truncated` contains the noun TWICE:

    "NOTE: Log truncated to last 10000 lines (total: {arg1} lines)"

The first is part of a fixed literal -- 10000 is the truncation limit, always
plural, independent of arg1. My first pass substituted blindly and produced
"last 10000 line", which is wrong at EVERY count, in all 11 inflecting locales.

Rebuilt so only the occurrence directly following {arg1} is inflected, and added a
test that asserts `contains('last 10000 lines')` across n = 1, 2, 5, 11, 21, 10000.

Then it failed AGAIN -- because I had repaired the .arb but not re-run
`flutter gen-l10n`, so the generated Dart still held the broken string. The test
caught that too. Both are exactly why the assertion is on rendered output rather
than on the .arb contents.

## Tests

New `flutter_ui/test/l10n/storage_count_plural_test.dart`, a sibling of
`trips_count_plural_test.dart`, 7 tests:

- English singular for all four count nouns (clip / recording / clip / event).
- The two-placeholder lines keep arg2 intact in both branches.
- Only the counted noun inflects, not the fixed 10000 limit (the bug above).
- Russian one/few/many by CLDR, including n=11 and n=21-22, which a hand-rolled
  `n < 5` rule gets wrong.
- Russian inflects the two-placeholder lines while keeping arg2.
- The no-agreement languages render ONE STABLE FORM across counts -- asserting a
  future "fix" that invents a singular there would be wrong.
- Every one of 16 locales renders every one of the 7 keys at n = 1, 2, 5 without
  throwing, actually interpolates the count, and does not drop arg2. A branch that
  silently lost arg2 would otherwise only surface on a device set to that language.

## Call sites

Only three keys have Dart call sites. gen-l10n changed their signatures from
`Object arg1` to `num arg1`, and all three already pass real counts
(`storage.surveillanceCount`, `c.storageClipCount`, `storage.recordingsCount`), so
`flutter analyze` stayed clean. None of the seven keys exist in Android
`res/values*/strings.xml` -- pruned to 30 keys in Phase 4 -- so there was no
counterpart to convert.

## Verification

- `./gradlew validateArbCatalogs validateAndroidStrings validateI18nCatalogs test
  koverVerify assembleDebug assembleRelease`: SUCCESSFUL. The i4ap plural-shape
  gate now covers all seven keys.
- flutter analyze clean; flutter test **1411** passed (was 1404), 0 skipped.
- Dart coverage 7004/7006 = 99.97%, not lower. Kover green.
- English wording unchanged apart from becoming a plural. web/ untouched.

Nothing committed.

title: Surveillance settings subtitle still advertises detection zones in all 17 locales
description:
## Problem

BladeWatch-s3sf removed the per-quadrant detection-zone (ROI) feature end to end, but the
Surveillance settings section still advertises it in its subtitle:

    settings_section_surveillance_subtitle = "Detection zones, schedule, motion sensitivity."

Verified on the head unit after the removal: Settings -> Surveillance still renders that line
under the "Surveillance" heading, while the screen no longer has any detection-zone control.
The other two clauses ("schedule, motion sensitivity") are still accurate; only the first is
stale.

## Why this was not fixed in s3sf

The string lives in 20 catalogs:

- `app/src/main/res/values/strings.xml` line 714 (English source)
- `flutter_ui/lib/l10n/app_en.arb` line 1411, plus all 18 other `app_*.arb` catalogs

Editing the English source alone leaves 17 locales advertising a feature that does not exist,
and hand-editing 17 translations is exactly the failure mode the `validateArbCatalogs` gates
and `tools/i18n/audit_catalogs.py` exist to catch (see the MT corpus-bleed work in
BladeWatch-1yqg). Dropping the leading clause is not a mechanical deletion in every locale --
clause order and grammar differ in zh/ja/ko/th/vi/hi, so it needs a real translation pass, not
a regex.

## What to do

1. Pick the replacement English text. Suggested: "Schedule, motion sensitivity, and detection
   objects." -- accurate to what the screen actually has now (General / Detection / Recording /
   Storage / Advanced tabs, with preset, sensitivity, and the Person/Car/Bike toggles).
2. Update `app/src/main/res/values/strings.xml` and every `values-*/strings.xml`.
3. Update `flutter_ui/lib/l10n/app_en.arb` and all 18 other ARB catalogs, via the json
   round-trip -- do NOT hand-edit ARB files.
4. Run `./gradlew validateArbCatalogs validateAndroidStrings` and
   `python3 tools/i18n/audit_catalogs.py`.
5. Verify on the head unit that Settings -> Surveillance shows the new subtitle.

Fold this into BladeWatch-6y7p (native-speaker review of hi/th/tr/vi) if that pass happens
first -- a human reviewer touching those catalogs may as well fix this line in the same sitting.

## Constraints

- Do NOT hand-edit ARB catalogs; use a json load/dump round-trip so formatting stays stable.
- Do NOT change the key name -- only the value.

title: dashboard_trips_count is not a plural, so English says '1 trips' and Russian cannot express few/many
description:
## Problem

Found during BladeWatch-imh6.3's locale sweep on the head unit.

`dashboard_trips_count` is a PLAIN string, not an ICU plural:

    en     "{arg1} trips"

So with one trip the Dashboard hero reads "1 trips" in English, and in languages with richer
plural rules it is worse. Russian has three forms (one / few / many) and the catalog can only
carry one, so it currently uses the "many" form everywhere:

    ru     "{arg1} поездок"

which renders "3 поездок" on the device. Russian requires "3 поездки" (few) for 2-4 and
"5 поездок" (many) for 5+. Screenshot shows "3 поездок · 21.0 km".

Polish/Czech-style rules are not in scope here (not shipped locales), but Russian is, and Arabic
would be if ever added.

## Why it was not caught

`validateArbCatalogs` checks key parity, placeholder parity, letterless values and mixed script.
None of those look at whether a COUNT-bearing string is declared as a plural — an ordinary string
with `{arg1}` in it is structurally valid.

The app already uses real ICU plurals elsewhere (`delete_recordings_message`,
`recordings_deleted_count`, `dashboard_insight_today_clips`), so the machinery is in place and
the pattern is established; this key just is not one of them.

## What to do

1. Convert `dashboard_trips_count` in `app_en.arb` to an ICU plural with `one`/`other`, matching
   the shape `delete_recordings_message` already uses, and give it an `@`-entry declaring
   `arg1` as `num`/`int` so gen-l10n emits the plural selector.
2. Translate into the other 18 catalogs PROGRAMMATICALLY (json round-trip). Give Russian its
   `one`/`few`/`many`/`other` forms; gen-l10n accepts the extra categories.
3. Check the neighbours while there — anything else that interpolates a bare count into a noun.
   `dashboard_trips_label_trips`, `trips_detail_*` and the Trips screen's own summary are the
   obvious candidates.
4. Consider extending `validateArbCatalogs`: if the English value is an ICU plural then every
   locale's value must be one too. That is a structural rule with no false positives, so it can
   fail rather than warn, like the four checks BladeWatch-1yqg added.

## Constraints

- Do NOT hand-edit the ARB files — a smart quote or stray comma there has shipped before, which
  is why `validateArbCatalogs` exists. See the `bladewatch-i18n-catalog-caching-and-validation`
  memory.
- Do NOT change the English wording beyond making it a plural.
- Do NOT modify `web/`.
- Do NOT commit.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `dashboard_trips_count` is an ICU plural in all 19 catalogs.
- [ ] English reads "1 trip" / "3 trips"; Russian reads "1 поездка" / "3 поездки" / "5 поездок",
      verified on device or by a widget test that pumps each count.
- [ ] A test asserting the singular, because "1 trips" is the bug a reader will actually notice.
- [ ] `./gradlew validateArbCatalogs` passes; `flutter analyze` clean; `flutter test --coverage`
      at or above the current gate.
- [ ] A decision recorded on whether the plural-shape check is added to validateArbCatalogs.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles
and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather
than guessing.
close_reason:
Fixed, gated so it cannot come back, and the neighbours filed rather than silently folded in.

## The fix

dashboard_trips_count is now an ICU plural in all 19 catalogs. English reads "1 trip" / "3
trips"; Russian carries all four categories and renders "1 поездка" / "3 поездки" / "5 поездок".

Translations were produced by INFLECTING the noun each catalog's own translator had already
chosen (Fahrten -> Fahrt, viajes -> viaje, trajets -> trajet, ...), not by retranslating the
phrase. That matters here: the existing plural entries in these catalogs are themselves visibly
MT-damaged -- app_de's recordings_deleted_count reads "Löschte Aufnahmen von {arg1}" and app_es
"Se suprimieron las grabaciones de {arg1}" -- so modelling new text on them would have spread
the corpus-bleed problem BladeWatch-6y7p exists to clean up. The diff is one line per catalog.

Languages with no numeral agreement (ja, ko, zh, zh_CN, zh_TW, th, vi, tr) get one identical
form for every category. That is the correct answer for those languages, not a shortcut, and the
new test asserts it must STAY that way so a future "fix" does not invent a singular.

## The gate (answering the "decision recorded" criterion: YES, added)

validateArbCatalogs now fails if the English value is an ICU plural and a locale's value is a
plain string. Rationale for failing rather than warning: it is structural, with no judgement in
it. gen-l10n builds each method signature from the TEMPLATE, so a locale supplying a plain
string still COMPILES -- it just renders that string verbatim and the count silently vanishes.
Nothing else in the build catches that.

It deliberately does NOT require matching CATEGORY sets: ru needs few/many where en does not,
and ja/zh/th correctly have none. Demanding identical categories would be wrong in both
directions.

Mutation-verified, not assumed: regressing app_ru.arb back to the plain "{arg1} поездок" makes
the build FAIL with the file and key named, and restoring it makes it pass.

## Tests

New test/l10n/trips_count_plural_test.dart, 4 tests:
- English singular first, because "1 trips" is the defect a reader actually notices.
- Russian one/few/many by real CLDR rules, including 11 -> many and 21 -> one, the cases a naive
  "n < 5" hand-rolled rule gets wrong.
- The no-agreement languages render one stable form across counts.
- Every shipped locale still interpolates the count in both branches -- a plural whose branch
  dropped {arg1} would render "trips" with no number.

## Verification

- flutter analyze clean; 1379 tests pass; Dart coverage 99.97% (6957/6959), unchanged.
- gradlew test koverVerify validateArbCatalogs validateAndroidStrings: all pass.
- ARB diff is exactly 19 files, 19 insertions, 19 deletions -- one line each, no reformatting.

## Filed, not folded in

BladeWatch-ug53: seven MORE count-bearing strings are still plain and will read "1 clips" /
"1 recordings" / "1 events" on a device that has exactly one. The new gate cannot see them,
because it only protects keys that are already plurals in English. Notably
settings_privacy_storage_count_format_plural is NAMED plural and is not one. Three other
candidates were examined and deliberately excluded there (language counts that can never be 1,
an "X of Y" ratio, and a unit symbol).

Nothing committed.

title: Russian rail_location clips in the nav rail (parity with native, but the last clipped label)
description:
## Problem

Found during BladeWatch-imh6.3's 17-locale sweep on the head unit.

The main navigation rail is a fixed ~120 logical px column. Two Russian labels do not fit and
ellipsise:

    Местоположение  ->  Местополо…      (rail_location)
    Диагностика         fits
    Автомобиль          fits

Every other locale fits, including the ones that looked riskiest: Thai (ตำแหน่ง, วิเคราะห์ระบบ),
Hindi (डैशबोर्ड, रिकॉर्डिंग), Italian (Registrazioni, Diagnostiche, Impostazioni — 13 chars) and
German (Einstellungen). Cyrillic is simply wider per character.

## This is parity, not a regression

Native's rail truncates the same way — its German rail shows "Einstellung…" for
`rail_settings`. So the Flutter port matches the behaviour it was ported from, and nothing got
worse. It is filed because imh6.3 requires every remaining clipped label to have an issue, not
because the Flutter port introduced it.

`rail_live` WAS a third offender in Russian: BladeWatch-vcur's pass corrected it from "Жизнь"
(life — a mistranslation) to "Прямой эфир", which then did not fit, and it is now "Эфир", which
does. So only `rail_location` remains.

## Options

- **Shorten the Russian.** No good short form: "Место" is vague, "Локация" is an anglicism and
  barely shorter. Not recommended — the word is correct, the column is what is too narrow.
- **Let the rail label wrap to two lines** the way the settings SUB-rail already does
  (Russian "Конфиденциальность и данные" wraps there and stays fully readable). This is the most
  promising: it changes one widget, not 17 catalogs.
- **Shrink the label font on overflow** (`FittedBox`/`AutoSizeText`). Keeps one line but makes
  one rail item visibly smaller than its neighbours.
- **Accept it.** It is what native does, and "Местополо…" is still recognisable in context next
  to a location pin icon.

## What to do

1. Look at the rail widget in `flutter_ui/lib/shell/` and decide between wrapping and accepting.
2. If wrapping: confirm the rail's fixed height still fits 8 destinations with a two-line label,
   at the head unit's real density — this is exactly the sort of thing a desktop window will not
   reproduce.
3. Re-run the 17-locale sweep (`tools/i18n/`-style walk, or by hand) and confirm no new clipping.

## Constraints

- Do NOT shorten a correct translation to fit a layout — imh6.3 says so explicitly, and the
  word is right.
- Do NOT modify `web/`.
- Do NOT commit.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A decision recorded here: wrap, shrink, or accept-as-parity.
- [ ] If changed: no clipped rail label in any of the 17 locales, verified on device.
- [ ] If changed: `flutter analyze` clean, `flutter test --coverage` at or above the current gate.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles
and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather
than guessing.
close_reason:
Decision: **accept as parity**. Verified on the head unit in Русский, and the survey found a
SECOND clipped label the original sweep missed.

## What the device actually shows

With the UI set to Русский, the main rail renders:

    Панель          fits
    Местополо…      CLIPPED   (rail_location = "Местоположение")
    Эфир            fits
    Записи          fits
    Автомобиль      fits
    Поездки         fits
    Диагностика     fits
    Настройки       fits
    О приложе…      CLIPPED   (settings_section_about = "О приложении")

So it is TWO labels, not one. `settings_section_about` clips as well, and imh6.3's sweep missed
it because the About entry is the 9th destination and sits BELOW THE FOLD -- the rail is a
`SingleChildScrollView` and About is only visible after scrolling it. Recording that here because
"only rail_location remains" is what this issue said, and it was not correct.

## Why accept rather than wrap

The rail already overflows vertically. Nine destinations do not fit the viewport at this screen
height -- About has to be scrolled to. Giving rail labels a second line would add roughly 16dp
per item to a column that is ALREADY too tall, pushing more destinations off-screen to fix a
cosmetic truncation. That trade is clearly the wrong way round.

The other options do not hold up either:
- Shortening the Russian is forbidden by imh6.3 and the words are correct.
- Shrinking the font on overflow makes two rail items visibly smaller than their seven
  neighbours, which reads as a rendering bug rather than a design.

And native does exactly the same thing: its German rail shows "Einstellung…". The Flutter port
matches the behaviour it was ported from, and both truncated labels stay recognisable next to
their icons (a location pin, a download/update glyph).

## A test was written for this and then deleted, deliberately

I built a widget test to measure every locale's rail labels against the 80dp column so the
clipped set would be a fact in CI rather than a note in an issue. It reported English
"Dashboard", "Location", "Settings" and most of the German and Spanish rail as clipping -- which
is false; they render fine on the device.

The cause: `flutter test` renders with a placeholder test font whose glyphs are all identical
fixed-width boxes. Any text-fit measurement taken in a plain `flutter test` is therefore
meaningless. Loading real Roboto into the harness would still not settle it, because the device
resolves Cyrillic, Thai and Devanagari through its own font fallback chain.

So rail label fit is only verifiable on the head unit, and the test was removed rather than
shipped. A measuring rig that cannot measure is worse than no rig, because the next person
believes it.

## Found while here, filed separately

- **BladeWatch-8hcj** (raised to P2): several confirmed Russian mistranslations, including
  `language_auto_title` rendering "Auto" as "Автомобиль" (car) in the LANGUAGE PICKER -- the
  screen a user needs to get back out of a language they cannot read -- and "Follow system" as
  "Следующая система" ("the next system").

Also confirmed on device while in Russian: BladeWatch-i4ap's plural fix renders correctly. The
Dashboard hero read "3 поездок" (the many form) before and now reads "3 поездки" (the correct few
form for 3).

## Not changed

No code, no catalogs, no layout. Both clipped labels are accepted as parity with native.

Nothing committed.

title: Native-speaker review of hi/th/tr/vi ARB catalogs
description:
## Problem

BladeWatch-1yqg corrected ~1,400 machine-translation defects across both i18n catalogs and added
four structural build gates. It did NOT finish the job for four locales.

For **hi, th, tr and vi** I fixed only what is unambiguous without reading the language fluently:
inverted states, dropped format placeholders, values left in English, training-corpus bleed, and
mixed script. I deliberately left PHRASING alone in those four, because a confident wrong "fix"
is worse than the machine translation -- it looks reviewed, so nobody checks it again.

The observed error rate justifies a real pass: of roughly 60 keys sampled at random across 8
locales, 11 were outright wrong (~18%), and every systematic probe run afterwards found more.

Two examples of what shipped before 1yqg, to calibrate how bad "wrong" got:
- `vehicle_tyre_fast_leak` in German read "Schnelle Auslieferung" -- *fast delivery* -- on a
  deflating-tyre warning.
- `dialog_keep_disabled` rendered "disabled" as a DISABLED PERSON in nine locales; Russian read
  "Оставайся инвалидом" (*remain an invalid*).

## What to do

1. Commission or perform a native-speaker review of `flutter_ui/lib/l10n/app_{hi,th,tr,vi}.arb`.
   That is the catalog set that survives Phase 4; `app/src/main/res/values-*/strings.xml` is
   deleted by BladeWatch-81g9.2, so do NOT spend review budget on it.
2. Give the reviewer the UI context, not just the strings. Nearly every 1yqg defect came from a
   short string translated with no idea what it labelled ("Run" as *flee*, "Clear" as
   *transparent*, "Current" as *electric current*, "Pick a date" as a *romantic date*). A key
   name plus a screenshot prevents the entire class.
3. Prioritise the same way 1yqg did: safety and destructive strings first (tyre pressure, battery
   health, reset data, delete recording, format drive), then short nouns and verbs, then prose.
4. Apply fixes PROGRAMMATICALLY (`json.load` / `json.dump` round-trip). Hand-editing these files
   previously shipped invalid JSON and is why `validateArbCatalogs` exists -- see the
   `bladewatch-i18n-catalog-caching-and-validation` memory.
5. Re-run `python3 tools/i18n/audit_catalogs.py` afterwards. It reports drift 0 and bleed 0 today;
   keep it that way. Its "dropped" (22) and "long" (5) hits are reviewed false positives --
   Chinese joins clauses with a comma rather than a full stop, and Thai is genuinely more verbose.

## Constraints

- Do NOT weaken the four gates in `validateArbCatalogs` / `validateAndroidStrings` (placeholder
  parity, format-slot parity, letterless values, mixed script). They all fail rather than warn
  because each is a hard structural rule with no false positives.
- Do NOT add keys to `intentionallyIdentical` to silence a problem. That set is a claim the key
  is correct in EVERY locale.
- Do NOT modify `web/`.
- Do NOT commit -- the developer commits manually.
- If you cannot read a language, say so in this issue rather than guessing.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] hi, th, tr and vi reviewed by someone who reads them, ARB side.
- [ ] Corrections applied programmatically and listed in this issue.
- [ ] `./gradlew validateArbCatalogs validateAndroidStrings` pass with no new warning.
- [ ] `python3 tools/i18n/audit_catalogs.py` still reports drift 0 and bleed 0.
- [ ] `flutter analyze` clean, `flutter test --coverage` passes, `tools/check_flutter_coverage.sh`
      still >= 99%.
- [ ] A recorded decision on whether the other 14 locales need the same treatment.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles
and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather
than guessing.
close_reason:
Reviewed by Codex as outside native-speaker reviewer (the owner's call), findings triaged, and
28 strings corrected across hi / th / tr / vi in both catalog families.

## The review

One `codex exec` run per language (gpt-5.6-luna, xhigh), each given the English source and the
current translation for 21 high-traffic keys — language picker, rail labels, settings section
titles and subtitles — with the in-car context, the 80dp rail width constraint, and an explicit
instruction to say so rather than guess if unsure.

A first attempt covering all five locales in one run exceeded its time budget before emitting a
report; splitting it one language per run worked.

    hi: 5 high, 3 medium
    th: 5 high, 3 medium
    tr: 4 high, 4 medium
    vi: 7 high, 2 medium

## The worst of it — labels that meant something else entirely

- **vi `settings_section_recording`: "Đăng ký"** = registration / subscription. The Recording
  settings section was labelled "Subscription".
- **vi `settings_section_privacy`: "Bảo mật"** = security, not privacy. On the privacy screen,
  where the distinction is the whole point.
- **vi `settings_section_appearance`: "Nhìn hình"** = looking at an image.
- **hi `settings_section_appearance`: "उपस्थिति"** = presence (as in attendance), not appearance.
- **hi `rail_diagnostics`: "निदान"** = diagnosis in the medical sense.
- **th `settings_section_overlay`: "แถบสถานะ"** = status BAR, not status overlay.
- **th `rail_vehicle`: "สถานะรถ"** = vehicle status, not vehicle.
- **tr `setup_autostart_body`: "kutuyu açın"** = "open the box" — the OPPOSITE of the English
  "uncheck the box". That instruction actively told a Turkish user to do the wrong thing.

## Applied: 28 strings

All high-severity findings, plus mediums that fix an actual error rather than a preference —
word order (vi `language_picker_subtitle_fmt`), a grammar rule (tr uses the singular after a
numeral), and malformed constructions (tr "Ön / sonrası").

    hi 5   th 7   tr 7   vi 9

Declined: mediums that were pure style or register preference, on the same principle applied to
Russian in BladeWatch-8hcj — the review is evidence, not instructions.

## Deliberately excluded

`settings_section_surveillance_subtitle` was flagged in hi, th and tr, and was NOT fixed here:
BladeWatch-o93h replaced that entire string in all 19 catalogs in the same session, because
BladeWatch-s3sf deleted the "detection zones" feature it described. Fixing the grammar of a
clause about to be deleted would have been wasted work and a merge conflict.

That interaction produced a useful cross-check, recorded on o93h: Codex's *translation* of the
new subtitle used "कार्यक्रम" for "schedule" in Hindi, while its own Hindi *review* had flagged
that exact word as wrong for schedule. The review won.

## Both catalog families

ARB and `values-{hi,th,tr,vi}/strings.xml` updated together, with Android format specifiers
(`%1$s`, `%1$d`) carried across from the existing values rather than leaving ARB-style `{arg1}`
in the XML.

## Honest limits

This is an LLM acting as a native speaker, not a native speaker. It is a large improvement over
untriaged machine translation — it found instructions that said the opposite of the English, and
section labels naming the wrong concept — but it is not a substitute for a human reviewer before
a public release. Anything a real speaker later disputes should be taken over this.

Not covered by this pass: the remaining ~600 keys per catalog. Only the 21 highest-traffic keys
were reviewed, chosen because a wrong navigation label costs more than an awkward sentence in
body text.

## Gates

`./gradlew validateArbCatalogs validateAndroidStrings` pass; flutter analyze clean; 1403 Dart
tests pass; Dart coverage 99.97% (7005/7007).

Nothing committed.

title: Native toasts/log-header still show hardcoded English daemon names (and a different set from the list)
description:
## Problem

BladeWatch-def0 localised the four service names in the Services LIST
(`DaemonAdapter.getDaemonDisplayName` and the Flutter Services pane) via the new
`daemon_name_*` resources. Three native call sites still print hardcoded English, and they
print a DIFFERENT set of words:

`app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/model/DaemonType.kt:8-12` declares
`enum class DaemonType(val displayName: String, ...)` with:

    CAMERA_DAEMON("Camera Daemon", ...)
    SENTRY_DAEMON("Sentry Daemon", ...)        <- list says "Surveillance Daemon"
    ACC_SENTRY_DAEMON("ACC Sentry", ...)       <- list says "ACC Surveillance"
    ZROK_TUNNEL("Zrok Tunnel", ...)

So native shows two different names for the same daemon depending on where you look. The
user-visible consumers:

- `ui/fragment/DaemonsFragment.kt:116` — `toast_no_config_needed` toast
- `ui/fragment/DaemonsFragment.kt:260` — `toast_fetching_log` toast
- `ui/fragment/DaemonsFragment.kt:294` — `log_header_title` in the downloaded log file
- `ui/fragment/DashboardFragment.kt:455` — `labelFor()`'s fallback for every non-Zrok daemon

(The `DaemonStartupManager.kt` uses at lines 359, 484 and 512 are log lines, not UI. Leave them.)

## THE TRAP — read this before changing anything

**Do NOT localise `DaemonType.displayName`.** It is not only a label:

    // DaemonsFragment.kt:258
    val daemonName = type.displayName.replace(" ", "_").lowercase()

That derives the FILENAME of the downloaded log. Localising the field would produce filenames
like `kamera-dienst`, `カメラサービス` or `บริการกล้อง` — non-ASCII, and `replace(" ", "_")` does
nothing useful for CJK/Thai/Hindi, which have no spaces to replace. Some of those characters are
also invalid on FAT32, which is what the SD card is formatted as.

`displayName` must stay an English, code-level identifier. Fix the CALL SITES instead.

## Fix

1. Change the four user-visible call sites above to resolve the name through the resources
   BladeWatch-def0 already added (`R.string.daemon_name_camera` /
   `daemon_name_surveillance` / `daemon_name_acc` / `daemon_name_zrok`), exactly as
   `DaemonAdapter.getDaemonDisplayName` now does. Consider extracting that mapping into a
   single helper both classes call, so there is one place that maps DaemonType -> resource id.
2. Leave `DaemonType.displayName` and `DaemonType.processName` untouched.
3. Leave `DaemonsFragment.kt:258`'s filename derivation reading `displayName`, and add a comment
   there saying why it must not be localised — that is the whole point of this task.
4. Decide whether `DaemonType.displayName`'s English values should be corrected to match the
   list ("Sentry Daemon" -> "Surveillance Daemon", "ACC Sentry" -> "ACC Surveillance"). That
   would change the downloaded log filename, so it is a deliberate choice, not a tidy-up. If you
   change it, say so in the issue and check nothing parses those filenames.

## Note on scope

`ui/fragment/**` and `ui/adapter/**` are on the Phase 4 deletion list (see the refactor plan),
so this is native-only work with a limited life. It is still worth doing while native ships,
but it should not be prioritised above Flutter-side parity work.

## Constraints

- Do NOT change the English wording of the `daemon_name_*` resources — they are byte-identical
  to what the docs and daemon logs use.
- Do NOT modify `web/`.
- Do NOT commit.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The four user-visible native call sites resolve their name from `daemon_name_*`.
- [ ] `DaemonType.displayName` is unchanged and still drives the log filename.
- [ ] A comment at the filename-derivation site explains why it must stay English.
- [ ] `./gradlew validateAndroidStrings test` passes and `assembleDebug` succeeds.
- [ ] Verified on device: switch the head unit to a non-English locale and confirm the toasts
      and the Dashboard fallback show translated names while the downloaded log filename stays
      ASCII.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles

title: Storage info rows lose their labels in Flutter (Storage Usage / Files show bare values)
description:
## Problem

Found during the BladeWatch-htel tab audit, by comparing both UIs on the head unit.

Native renders EVERY storage info row as a label/value pair, right-aligned
(`infoRow(label, value)` in both `RecordingSettingsController.renderStorage` and
`SurveillanceSettingsController.renderStorage`):

```
Storage Usage        17042.8 MB used / 90100 MB limit
Files                82 recordings
Path                 /storage/E3B7-10F2/BladeWatch/recordings
SD Card Free         94.0 GB
Internal Free        51.7 GB
```

Flutter drops the label on the first two and puts Path's value on a second line:

```
16827.9 MB used / 90100 MB limit      <- no "Storage Usage" label
81 recordings                         <- no "Files" label
Path
  /storage/E3B7-10F2/BladeWatch/...   <- subtitle, not right-aligned
SD Card Free                  94.0 GB <- correct
Internal Free                 51.7 GB <- correct
```

So a user scanning the pane sees two bare values with nothing naming them.

## Why this was not fixed in BladeWatch-htel

The value strings exist and are already translated:
- `settings_recording_storage_usage` = "{arg1} used / {arg2} limit"
- `settings_recording_storage_files` = "{arg1} recordings"
- `surveillance_storage_usage`, `surveillance_storage_files` (= "{arg1} events")

But there is NO label key for either row, in either screen. Grep confirms only
`*_storage_location_label`, `*_storage_limit_label`, `*_storage_path_label`,
`settings_recording_storage_sd_free_label` and `settings_recording_storage_internal_free_label`
exist. Adding "Storage Usage" and "Files" labels for both screens means 4 new keys × 19 ARB
catalogs = 76 strings, 72 of which need real translations. Inventing those is a quality risk
this project has already been bitten by (see the `bladewatch-i18n-catalog-caching-and-validation`
memory: LLM edits to locale catalogs previously shipped invalid JSON and had to be caught by a
new Gradle validator).

## Fix

1. Add 4 keys to `flutter_ui/lib/l10n/app_en.arb`:
   `settings_recording_storage_usage_label` ("Storage Usage"),
   `settings_recording_storage_files_label` ("Files"),
   `surveillance_storage_usage_label` ("Storage Usage"),
   `surveillance_storage_files_label` ("Files").
   Native's own literals are those exact English strings.
2. Translate into the other 18 catalogs. Do NOT hand-edit the JSON — write a script that
   `json.load`s each catalog, inserts the key, and `json.dump`s it back, so a smart quote or a
   stray comma cannot corrupt the file. `validateArbCatalogs` (app/build.gradle.kts, hooked to
   preBuild) fails the build on a key gap, so all 19 must be updated together.
3. In `flutter_ui/lib/screens/settings/settings_recording_screen.dart` and
   `flutter_ui/lib/screens/surveillance/surveillance_screen.dart`, change the Usage and Files
   rows from `ListTile(title: Text(<composed value>))` to
   `ListTile(title: Text(<label>), trailing: Text(<value>))`, matching the SD Card Free /
   Internal Free rows immediately below them that already have this shape.
4. Change the Path row from `title` + `subtitle` to `title` + `trailing` so it right-aligns like
   native's. Watch for overflow: the path is long and the pane is narrow — if it cannot fit,
   keep the subtitle form for Path ONLY and say so in a comment, because native's own row
   would ellipsise too.

## Constraints

- Do NOT modify `app/src/main/res/` or `web/`.
- Do NOT invent translations for languages you cannot verify; if unsure for a locale, say so in
  this issue rather than guessing.
- Do NOT commit.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All four rows in both Storage tabs render as label + right-aligned value, matching native.
- [ ] All 19 ARB catalogs contain the new keys and `./gradlew :app:validateArbCatalogs` passes.
- [ ] Every catalog is still valid JSON (parse each one as a check, not by eye).
- [ ] `flutter analyze` clean, `flutter test` passes, coverage gate not lower than before.
- [ ] Verified on device against the native pane side by side, with screenshots.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles
and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask rather
than guessing.
acceptance_criteria: Usage/Files/Path rows render as label + right-aligned value in both Storage tabs; 4 new keys present and translated in all 19 ARB catalogs with validateArbCatalogs passing; every catalog still parses as JSON; analyze/test/coverage gates pass; verified on device with screenshots.
notes:
CODE DONE — only the on-device screenshot comparison is outstanding (head unit powered off).

- Added settings_recording_storage_usage_label / _files_label and the surveillance pair to all
  19 ARB catalogs via the json round-trip. Translated per locale.
- Both Storage tabs now render Usage and Files as label + right-aligned value, matching
  native's infoRow(), so the column of values lines up as it does there.
- Path deliberately KEPT its subtitle form. The task suggested right-aligning it 'unless it
  cannot fit' — it is a long absolute path (/storage/E3B7-10F2/BladeWatch/recordings, seen on
  the device) and native's own right-aligned row ellipsises it at this pane width, so the
  subtitle shows more of it, not less.
- 3 tests asserting the labels exist and that the rows carry a trailing value rather than
  being title-only.

FOUND WHILE DOING THIS, filed as BladeWatch-aklv: most of this string family is UNTRANSLATED
English in most locales — validateArbCatalogs enforces key parity but never compares values, so
roughly 30 real prose strings per locale are still English. That is why the new labels will
briefly read as better-translated than their neighbours. It also means imh6.3 (verify 17
locales) will surface raw English rather than raw keys.

REMAINING: on-device side-by-side against the native pane, per this issue's last criterion.
close_reason:
DONE, verified on device against the native pane.

Side by side on the head unit, Recording > Storage, same live SD-card data:

    row             native                                  flutter
    Storage Usage   17296.9 MB used / 90100 MB limit        identical
    Files           84 recordings                           identical
    Path            /storage/E3B7-10F2/BladeWatch/recordings identical, right-aligned
    SD Card Free    93.7 GB                                 93.4 GB (live drift, recording)
    Internal Free   52.1 GB                                 51.9 GB (live drift, recording)
    Storage Limit   88.0 GB                                 88.0 GB

All five rows are now label + right-aligned value and the column of values lines up exactly as
native's does.

CORRECTION TO MY EARLIER NOTE. I had kept Path on a second line and justified it as "native's
own right-aligned row ellipsises it at this pane width". That was wrong, and the device shows
it: native right-aligns the full /storage/E3B7-10F2/BladeWatch/recordings with no ellipsis, and
the Flutter pane is actually the wider of the two. So Path now matches the other rows.

The value is capped at 520 logical px via bwPathValue() in lib/widgets/storage_limit.dart and
ellipsises past that, which is what native's TextView does when a path really is too long --
a bare Text in ListTile.trailing gets loose constraints and would overflow instead. The cap is
a fixed number rather than a measurement of the pane; the comment says so and names the upgrade
path, since the paths this app shows are a volume id plus a fixed suffix.

Acceptance criteria:
  [x] All four rows in both Storage tabs render as label + right-aligned value, matching native.
      Both tabs -- Recording and Surveillance -- confirmed on device.
  [x] All 19 ARB catalogs carry the new keys; ./gradlew validateArbCatalogs passes.
  [x] Every catalog parses as JSON (the validator does this, not an eyeball).
  [x] flutter analyze clean; 1391 tests pass; coverage 99.97%, not lower than before.
  [x] Verified on device against the native pane side by side, with screenshots.

Screenshots: screenshots/flutter/08f_settings_recording_storage.png,
screenshots/native/08f_settings_recording_storage.png,
screenshots/flutter/08i_settings_surveillance_storage.png.

2 new tests, both mutation-verified: reverting the Path row to the subtitle form fails
"the storage path is right-aligned like the other rows, not a subtitle".

No settings were changed on the device while testing.

title: Background-service display names are hardcoded English in both UIs, so they never localise
description:
## Problem

The four background-service display names are hardcoded English in BOTH UIs and
exist in no string catalog, so they stay English in all 17 locales.

Native: app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/ui/adapter/DaemonAdapter.kt,
getDaemonDisplayName():

    DaemonType.CAMERA_DAEMON     -> "Camera Daemon"
    DaemonType.SENTRY_DAEMON     -> "Surveillance Daemon"
    DaemonType.ACC_SENTRY_DAEMON -> "ACC Surveillance"
    DaemonType.ZROK_TUNNEL       -> "Zrok Tunnel"

Flutter: flutter_ui/lib/screens/settings/settings_daemons_screen.dart,
_daemonLabel(), which now hardcodes the same four strings.

## Why the port hardcodes them too

BladeWatch-b05u required the Services pane to match native's names exactly. The
port had been reusing the STARTUP screen's short labels (startup_daemon_camera
= "Camera", startup_daemon_sentry = "Sentry Mode", startup_daemon_parking =
"Parking Guard") -- different words for the same daemons, matching neither the
docs, the logs, nor CLAUDE.md.

Matching native meant taking native's strings, and native has no resource for
them. Inventing ARB-only keys would have made the two UIs diverge again the
moment anyone translated one side, so the port deliberately inherited the gap
rather than papering over it. This task is that debt, recorded rather than
hidden.

## What to do

1. Add four string resources to app/src/main/res/values/strings.xml, e.g.
   daemon_name_camera / daemon_name_surveillance / daemon_name_acc /
   daemon_name_zrok, with the exact current English values.
2. Point DaemonAdapter.getDaemonDisplayName at them.
3. Mirror the four keys into flutter_ui/lib/l10n/app_en.arb and point
   _daemonLabel at l10n instead of the hardcoded map.
4. Translate them across the other 16 Android locales and the other 18 ARB
   catalogs. "Zrok Tunnel" is a product name and should almost certainly stay
   as-is in every locale; the other three are descriptive and should be
   translated.

Both parity gates must stay green: validateAndroidStrings (17-locale key parity
for res/values*/strings.xml) and validateArbCatalogs (full key parity against
app_en.arb). Adding a key to only one catalog WILL fail the build, which is the
gate doing its job.

## Constraints

- Do NOT change the English wording. These names appear in docs and logs; this
  is a localisation task, not a renaming one.
- Do NOT drop the Flutter map until the ARB keys exist in all 19 catalogs, or
  the ARB gate fails.
- Do NOT modify web/.
- Do NOT commit.

## Tests

- ./gradlew validateAndroidStrings and validateArbCatalogs both pass.
- flutter test and ./gradlew test pass; flutter analyze clean.
- A widget test asserting the Services rows render the localised names (the
  existing b05u test asserts the English ones and should be updated to read
  from l10n rather than literals).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The four names come from string resources in both UIs; no hardcoded
      display names remain in DaemonAdapter.kt or settings_daemons_screen.dart.
- [ ] All 17 Android locales and all 19 ARB catalogs carry the keys.
- [ ] English wording is byte-identical to today's.
- [ ] Both i18n gates pass; flutter test, gradlew test and flutter analyze clean.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the
build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is
ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
close_reason: Added daemon_name_camera/_surveillance/_acc/_zrok to all 17 Android locales and all 19 ARB catalogs, and pointed DaemonAdapter.getDaemonDisplayName and the Flutter Services pane at them. English wording is byte-identical to before (verified by comparing the XML and ARB values directly). Translations were derived from each catalog's OWN existing vocabulary for camera/surveillance/service rather than invented in isolation, so they read consistently with the rest of that catalog; Zrok Tunnel stays verbatim everywhere as a product name. Both catalog sets were edited PROGRAMMATICALLY -- the ARB side via a json.load/json.dump round-trip, which cannot emit the invalid JSON that LLM hand-editing produced before (see the bladewatch-i18n-catalog-caching-and-validation memory); diff is 80 pure insertions with no reformatting churn. Updated the b05u test to read from l10n instead of English literals and added a test that pumps the German locale -- asserting the English strings alone would still pass against hardcoded text, so the non-English pump is what actually proves the fix. IMPORTANT FINDING, filed as BladeWatch-9rjg rather than fixed here: DaemonType.displayName is ALSO hardcoded English, carries a DIFFERENT set of names ('Sentry Daemon'/'ACC Sentry' vs the list's 'Surveillance Daemon'/'ACC Surveillance'), and reaches four user-visible native call sites. It must NOT simply be localised -- DaemonsFragment.kt:258 derives the downloaded log FILENAME from it via replace(' ','_').lowercase(), so localising it would produce non-ASCII filenames on a FAT32 SD card. That trap is documented prominently in the new issue. Both i18n gates green (validateAndroidStrings, validateArbCatalogs), gradlew test + koverVerify + assembleDebug green, 1378 Dart tests, coverage 99.97%, analyze clean.

title: Decide the selected-state style for segmented controls: native filled pill vs M3 check-mark chip
description:
## What differs

Every multiple-choice control in the app renders its SELECTED option
differently in the two UIs:

  native   a FILLED pill in the primary colour, white label, no check mark
  Flutter  a light tonal chip with a CHECK MARK and dark label

Seen on, at least: the Trips day filter (7/14/30 Days), the Trips bottom tabs
(Trips / Stats / Storage), Trip Storage's Distance Unit (km / mi) and Storage
Location (Internal / SD Card), the Recordings source segments (Dashcam /
Surveillance), the Vehicle Climate / Windows tabs, and the Surveillance tabs
(General / Detection / Recording / Storage / Advanced).

Reference pairs, both current: screenshots/native/06_trips.png and
06c_trips_storage.png against their screenshots/flutter/ counterparts.

## Why this is filed as a decision, not asserted as a bug

Flutter's appearance is what Material 3's SegmentedButton produces by default,
and the check mark is part of that spec. Native's filled pill is also valid M3,
just a different component. So this is NOT obviously wrong -- it is a choice
that was never consciously made, and it is the single most repeated visual
difference between the two UIs.

It matters for this refactor specifically because BladeWatch-81g9 deletes the
native UI on the strength of a 1:1 parity sign-off, and "every selector looks
different" is the kind of thing that is cheap to align now and awkward to argue
about later.

Decide one of:
  (a) match native -- give the shared selector a filled-pill selected state and
      drop the check mark;
  (b) keep the M3 SegmentedButton default and record the deviation explicitly
      in docs/ui-ux-design-language.md so the parity checklist
      (BladeWatch-imh6.2) does not keep re-raising it.

Either is defensible. What is not defensible is leaving it undecided while both
UIs ship.

## If (a) is chosen

There should be ONE shared widget, not per-screen styling. Find whatever the
screens currently share (or introduce it) under flutter_ui/lib/widgets/ and fix
it in one place, then re-capture the affected screenshots.

## Constraints

- Do NOT restyle by hand on each screen.
- Do NOT change any control's BEHAVIOUR or the values it selects.
- Do NOT touch the Android res/ files or web/.
- Do NOT commit.

## Tests (required)

- If (a): a widget test asserting the shared selector's selected state uses the
  primary colour and renders no check mark, plus existing screen tests passing
  unchanged.
- If (b): no code change; update docs/ui-ux-design-language.md and note the
  decision in BladeWatch-imh6.2 so the checklist records it as accepted.
- flutter test and flutter analyze clean; coverage not lower than 99.97%.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A decision is recorded, (a) or (b), with the reason.
- [ ] If (a): one shared selector widget changed, all listed screens verified,
      screenshots re-captured.
- [ ] If (b): docs/ui-ux-design-language.md records the deviation and
      BladeWatch-imh6.2 notes it as accepted.
- [ ] flutter test and flutter analyze clean; coverage not lower than before.

Do not make mistakes. Read the referenced files fully before editing. Verify the
build compiles and all acceptance criteria pass before closing. If anything is
ambiguous, stop and ask rather than guessing.
close_reason:
DECISION: option (a) -- match native. Single-choice options now render as a
FILLED primary pill with no check mark.

REASON. Both treatments are valid Material 3, so this was a genuine choice, not
a defect. It went native's way because BladeWatch-81g9 deletes the native UI on
the strength of a 1:1 parity sign-off (BladeWatch-imh6.2), and "every selector
in the app looks different" is cheap to settle now and awkward to argue about
after the reference implementation is gone. Option (b) -- keeping the M3 default
and documenting the deviation -- would have left the checklist re-raising it on
every screen.

IMPLEMENTATION. One shared widget, not per-screen styling:
lib/widgets/bw_choice_chip.dart, applied at all 21 call sites across Trips,
Surveillance, Recording settings, Vehicle and the Dashboard's vehicle dialog.

Three judgement calls worth recording:

1. It is a thin WRAPPER over ChoiceChip, not a hand-rolled control. A bespoke
   InkWell would silently drop the selected state, focus and keyboard handling
   that ChoiceChip provides -- exactly the mistake made and corrected earlier in
   this refactor on the Appearance theme tiles. A test pins that semantics
   survive.

2. onSelected is NULLABLE, mirroring ChoiceChip. Two call sites (a busy
   surveillance tab, an unavailable storage location) pass null to DISABLE the
   option; making the callback required would have silently re-enabled both.
   The analyzer caught this, and there is now a test for it.

3. The styling is scoped to this widget rather than the global chipTheme, and
   that is deliberate. A chipTheme would also strip the check mark from
   multi-select FilterChips (the Normal/Proximity type row, the actor/severity
   filters), where the check mark is MEANINGFUL -- it signals inclusion, not a
   single active choice. Those are untouched.

SegmentedButton needed separate handling and was nearly missed: the Recordings
source segments are a SegmentedButton, not a ChoiceChip, so the first pass left
them still showing the M3 check mark. Colours now come from a
segmentedButtonTheme in BladeWatchTheme, with showSelectedIcon: false at the two
call sites (it is a widget property, not a theme one). The theme IS the right
home there, because every SegmentedButton in the app is a single-choice
selector -- there is no multi-select variant whose check mark carries meaning.

VERIFIED ON DEVICE: the Trips day filter and bottom tabs, and the Recordings
source segments, all render as filled teal pills with white labels and no check
mark, matching the re-captured native shots. screenshots/flutter/06_trips.png
and 04b_recordings_surveillance.png updated.

flutter analyze clean; flutter test 1312 passed, zero skipped; Dart coverage
99.97% (unchanged). Five tests added for the shared widget covering the filled
selected state, the outlined unselected state, tap reporting, the disabled path
and semantics.

docs/ui-ux-design-language.md was NOT changed: that file documents the design
language, and this restores the documented native behaviour rather than
deviating from it. Option (b) was the branch that would have required a doc
entry.

Not committed, per CLAUDE.md.

title: CONTINGENCY: re-encode vehicle GLBs without Draco if Filament gltfio decode fails on BYD head unit
description:
## Context
All 11 bundled GLBs in app/src/main/assets/web/shared/models/ use KHR_draco_mesh_compression (verified via GLB JSON chunk extensionsUsed). Filament gltfio ships a Draco decoder, but this MUST be proven on the BYD DiLink v3 head unit in the spike task. This task activates ONLY if the spike finds Draco decode broken/unacceptably slow there.

## Steps (only if activated)
1. Re-encode every GLB with glTF-Transform (the models were generated with glTF-Transform v4.3.0): npx @gltf-transform/cli copy in.glb out.glb strips nothing by default — use "gltf-transform draco --decompress? " NOTE: actual command is: npx @gltf-transform/cli optimize --no-simplify --compress false OR simply: npx @gltf-transform/cli dedup in.glb out.glb after a decompress pass. Verify the output has NO KHR_draco_mesh_compression in extensionsUsed and identical visual output. Keep KHR_materials_* extensions intact.
2. Keep filenames and model ids IDENTICAL. Update sizeBytes and sha256 for every entry in app/src/main/assets/web/shared/models/manifest.json and bump manifest "version".
3. The GitHub release (manifest baseUrl models-v1) must be updated with the new files too — flag this for the developer; do not attempt to publish a release yourself.
4. Check APK size impact (Draco-stripped GLBs are larger); report before/after sizes.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] python3 GLB header check shows no KHR_draco_mesh_compression in any model
- [ ] All models render in the native hero AND still render in the legacy web vehicle page (three.js path must keep working for phone access)

title: SetRecordingMode RPC returns success=true on invalid mode (silent no-op)
description:
## Problem
SettingsService.SetRecordingMode (added in BladeWatch-pg0s) calls CameraDaemon.setRecordingMode(mode), which does Mode.valueOf(mode.toUpperCase()) and SWALLOWS IllegalArgumentException for unknown modes (CameraDaemon.java:2336 logs "Invalid recording mode" and returns). The Connect impl handleSetRecordingMode then still returns {success:true, mode}. So an invalid mode string is a silent no-op reported as success.

Low severity today: the UI only sends valid enum values (selectedMode.value), and this matches the old REST behavior. But it is a latent correctness gap.

## Files
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/connect/impl/SettingsServiceImpl.java (handleSetRecordingMode, ~line 101)
- app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/daemon/CameraDaemon.java (setRecordingMode, ~line 2325)

## Steps
1. Make setRecordingMode signal failure for an invalid mode (e.g. return boolean, or expose a validated setter / check against RecordingModeManager.Mode values), without breaking other callers.
2. In handleSetRecordingMode, validate the mode (against the Mode enum) and return success=false with error="invalid_mode: <mode>" (or throw ConnectException invalid_argument) when it does not apply.
3. Keep success=true only when the mode was actually applied.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] SetRecordingMode with a bogus mode returns success=false (or invalid_argument), not success=true.
- [ ] SetRecordingMode with a valid mode still applies and returns success=true.
- [ ] ./gradlew :app:compileDebugJavaWithJavac passes; add a small unit test if feasible.

Do not make mistakes. Read both files fully and check all callers of CameraDaemon.setRecordingMode before changing its signature. If anything is ambiguous, stop and ask.
close_reason: Added enum validation in SettingsServiceImpl.handleSetRecordingMode before calling CameraDaemon — invalid mode now throws ConnectException(invalid_argument) instead of silently returning success=true. compileDebugJavaWithJavac passes.

title: Connect parity STRUCTURAL: Surveillance status/heatmap/filterlog shapes
description:
## Problem
SurveillanceService Connect<->REST mismatches that json_name cannot cleanly fix. Audited under BladeWatch-s4k: GetSurveillanceConfigResponse fully MATCHES (no change needed); GetSnapshotResponse matches via captureBytes. The rest are structural/ambiguous.

Background: daemon ships REST JSON verbatim; client parses with JsonFormat.ignoringUnknownFields(). See epic BladeWatch-48b.

## Structural mismatches
1. GetSurveillanceStatusResponse (surveillance.proto ~101): proto = {pipeline_running, surveillance_active, active_cameras, error}. CameraDaemon.getSurveillanceStatus() (~2365) emits {initialized, enabled, active(=gpuPipeline.isRunning), recording, frameCount, ... 50+ keys}. AMBIGUOUS mapping: 'active'=pipeline isRunning, 'enabled'=surveillanceEnabled — so which maps to pipeline_running vs surveillance_active needs the original intent. active_cameras has NO emitter. Decide the intended field semantics, then either redesign the proto status message to the fields the client actually needs (with json_name) or adjust the emitter. Verify what SurveillanceSettingsClient.kt / Angular consume.
2. GetHeatmapResponse (surveillance.proto ~126): proto declares image_jpeg (bytes); SurveillanceApiHandler.sendHeatmap (~1091) emits a heatmap GRID structure {gridCols,gridRows,viewMode,quadrants[...]} — NOT a JPEG. Decide: model the grid in proto OR rename. (GetSnapshotResponse.image_jpeg is fine via Connect captureBytes.)
3. FilterLogEntry / GetFilterLogResponse (surveillance.proto ~144-152): proto FilterLogEntry = {timestamp_ms, reason, details}; emitter returns an array of PLAIN STRINGS (sentry.getFilterLogEntries()), plus an extra 'count'. Decide: emit structured objects OR model entries as repeated string.

## Constraints
- Do NOT break web UI (REST keys) or Angular TS client. Align proto to actual emitted JSON where possible; if restructuring, regenerate stubs (buf) and update Kotlin/TS consumers so the build compiles.
- Regenerate via ./gradlew generateConnectProtos; verify ./gradlew :app:compileDebugJavaWithJavac.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Each of the 3 areas resolved with a documented decision (esp. the status field-semantics).
- [ ] Stubs regenerated; consumers updated; compileDebugJavaWithJavac passes.

Do not make mistakes. Read surveillance.proto, CameraDaemon.getSurveillanceStatus(), SurveillanceApiHandler.sendHeatmap/sendFilterLog, and the consumers fully before editing. If ambiguous, stop and ask.

(1) GetSurveillanceStatusResponse: removed unpopulated/unread active_cameras (reserved 3); pipeline_running/surveillance_active match consumers (Kotlin SurveillanceSettingsClient, Angular surveillance.component). (2) GetHeatmapResponse: replaced bytes image_jpeg with the actual motion-grid shape the handler emits — grid_cols/grid_rows/view_mode + repeated HeatmapQuadrant{id,name,enabled,suppressed,mean_luma,active_blocks,confirmed_blocks,threat_level,component_size,confidence[]} (canonical camelCase names match emitter; impl already uses captureString pass-through). (3) GetFilterLogResponse: emitter returns plain string lines + count, so changed entries to repeated string + added count and removed FilterLogEntry (deleted orphan generated stubs). title: Connect parity STRUCTURAL: Trips telemetry/rollup/range/detail/gps shapes
description:
## Problem
TripsService Connect<->REST mismatches that json_name cannot fix (shape/type differences). Audited under BladeWatch-dkv: TripSummary, DnaScores, TripConfig, TripStorageInfo, SimilarTripsStats all MATCH already; the remaining issues are structural and need design decisions + consumer (Kotlin TripsClient.kt / Angular TS) updates.

Background: daemon ships REST JSON verbatim; client parses with JsonFormat.ignoringUnknownFields(); a field with the wrong TYPE/shape is dropped. See epic BladeWatch-48b. Emitters live in app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/trips/.

## Structural mismatches
1. TelemetrySample (trips.proto): proto models a sample as string field sample_json; TelemetrySample.toJson() emits an OBJECT with compact keys {t,s,a,b,bp,g,la,lo,al}. Whole telemetry array is silently lost. Decide: model the compact fields in proto (with json_name t/s/a/...) OR change emitter to emit a sample_json string.
2. WeeklyRollupEntry (GetSummaryResponse): proto models rollup_json string; WeeklyRollup.toJson() emits an OBJECT {year,weekNumber,tripCount,totalDistanceKm,...}. Decide similarly.
3. RangeEstimate (GetRangeResponse.range_json): proto field range_json (string); handler emits an OBJECT under key 'range' {predictedRangeKm,lowerBoundKm,...}. Decide: model RangeEstimate message + json_name='range', OR emit a range_json string.

title: Cleanup: fix dead code in ConnectHandlerUtil and ConnectDispatcher
description:
## Dead code to fix

Three distinct dead-code issues in the Connect layer:

### 1. ConnectDispatcher.sendConnectSuccess() — null guard on extraHeaders (always non-null)
File: app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/connect/ConnectDispatcher.java

In sendConnectSuccess(), the check 'if (extraHeaders != null)' is always true because ConnectResponse's constructor guarantees extraHeaders is always Collections.emptyList() or Collections.unmodifiableList(...), never null. Remove the null check; just iterate directly.

### 2. ConnectHandlerUtil.requireString() — v == null check is dead (line 176)
File: app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/connect/ConnectHandlerUtil.java

'JSONObject.getString(field)' either returns a non-null String or throws JSONException. It cannot return null. The '|| v == null' branch is unreachable and misleads readers. Remove the v == null check:
  if (v.isEmpty()) throw new Exception("empty");

### 3. ConnectHandlerUtil.captureString() — unnecessary parse+serialize round-trip
File: app/src/main/java/com/loabletech/bladewatch/server/connect/ConnectHandlerUtil.java (line 150-152)

captureString() currently calls capture() (which parses body as JSONObject) then calls .toString() (re-serializes). This is a pointless round-trip. Worse, it silently transforms the body: array-bodied responses get wrapped as {"items":[...]}, and non-JSON bodies become "{}". captureString should directly call captureRaw() and decode the body bytes to a UTF-8 string:

  public static ConnectResponse captureString(HandlerInvoker invoker) throws ConnectException {
      RawCapture raw = captureRaw(invoker);
      String body = new String(raw.bodyBytes, StandardCharsets.UTF_8).trim();
      if (body.isEmpty()) body = "{}";
      return ConnectResponse.of(body);
  }

NOTE: This change also means captureString will stop silently swallowing HTTP errors if issue BladeWatch-2oq is fixed first (which adds status checking to captureRaw/the capture helpers). Coordinate with BladeWatch-2oq.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] ConnectDispatcher: null guard on extraHeaders removed
- [ ] ConnectHandlerUtil: v == null check in requireString removed
- [ ] ConnectHandlerUtil: captureString uses captureRaw directly, no round-trip through JSONObject
- [ ] Build compiles with ./gradlew assembleDebug

Do not make mistakes. Read the relevant files fully before editing. Verify the build compiles before closing.
close_reason: Closed

title: LiveStreamClient enableStream()/setViewMode() swallow ConnectRPC failures before opening WebSocket
description:

title: ConnectDispatcher/capture leak raw exception messages to client
description:
Unhandled exceptions surface their raw message (and possibly internal paths) to the Connect client, which is risky for a tunnel-exposed daemon.
